articles.title: Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
articles.text:
A critical 16-year-old flaw in EDK II, the open-source code that most hardware makers use to build UEFI firmware, can allow an attacker to run code on a machine before its operating system loads, but only while the machine is booting over the network.
UEFI firmware is the software that runs first when a computer is switched on, before the operating system. An attacker who can reach the machine with a crafted network message during such a network boot can hang the boot, or, with work tailored to the exact firmware build, run their own code before Secure Boot and other startup defenses load.
An attacker needs no password and no existing access to the machine, but does need to reach it over the network during the short window when it is booting this way.
Red Hat and SUSE, which both ship the affected code, rated the flaw as one an attacker exploits from an adjacent network position rather than across the open internet.
TianoCore, the project behind EDK II, published an advisory on October 22 and rated the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, 9.5 out of 10. A code fix exists, but no stable release of EDK II contains it yet, and the advisory still lists no patched version, so most users have nothing to install today.
What the Flaw Lets an Attacker Do
The flaw is a buffer overflow in EDK II's network-boot code, known as PXE. During a PXE boot, a machine loads its startup image from the network instead of from a local disk.
As part of this, the PXE driver listens for ICMP error messages and the small status messages that network devices send back, and copies each one into a fixed 504-byte area of memory.
The size checks in that copy are wrong in both the IPv4 and IPv6 versions of the code, so a message longer than 504 bytes spills past the area and overwrites nearby memory with data the attacker chose.
To set this off, an attacker only has to send one crafted error message to the machine's address while it is in the middle of a network boot. No password or existing access to the machine is needed.
The simple result is a crash: the boot hangs, and the machine fails to start. Getting code to run is much harder and far less reliable. The advisory says that an attacker who knows the exact firmware build can plant a "counterfeit event" that causes the firmware to run the attacker's own code, so an exploit has to be built for a specific build.
When code runs, it executes within the firmware, before Secure Boot and other boot-time checks have verified anything. That timing is what makes the flaw serious.
Code planted this way runs only once and does not survive a reboot by itself. That single run is still enough to install other code that does start on every boot.
Who Is Affected
The bug sits in EDK II up to and including edk2-stable202608, the newest stable version, dated August 21. EDK II is the reference code that nearly every UEFI firmware vendor builds on, including the independent BIOS makers AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, as well as Microsoft's hardened fork, Project Mu.
The flawed copy loop has been in the code since a commit added in November 2010, The Hacker News found by tracing the project's history.
PXE network boot is turned on by default in EDK II's standard build. The flaw does not affect home or office users who boot only from a local disk. It applies to organizations whose machines boot over a network, primarily servers and data center equipment.
How many shipping products carry the vulnerable code is not known. Intel told Ars Technica that none of its "commercial products currently under security support" are known to be affected, and that it "does not include the affected EDK2 functionality in its reference code," though an OEM board vendor or system maker could add it.
Arm said the flaw "is not directly applicable to Arm's product portfolio." Both companies' own firmware draws on EDK II.
Linux distributions also ship the code. Red Hat lists its edk2 package in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10 as affected and not yet fixed, and SUSE and Debian mark their equivalent packages the same way.
AMD, Phoenix Technologies, AMI, Microsoft, and Amazon did not answer the tech news site's questions before publication, and TianoCore did not respond either, so the status of their products remains unclear.
Is There a Fix?
A fix has been merged into the EDK II source code. It rewrites the faulty copy so an oversized message is cut off at 504 bytes instead of spilling over, and it reached the main development branch on October 15.
No stable release of EDK II includes that fix yet. The Hacker News checked the project's release tags on October 28 and found the newest, edk2-stable202608, predates it, and the advisory still lists the patched version as "Not patched currently." Microsoft's Project Mu has already pulled the fix into its release branches, and cut tagged builds on October 26.
Even with the fix public in source, a server operator has nothing to install until the maker of their firmware ships a BIOS or UEFI update built from it. That step is at least straightforward, Jesse Michael, a principal researcher at the firmware security firm Eclypsium, told Ars Technica: unlike Secure Boot bypasses such as BootHole and BlackLotus, the flaw "can be fixed with a basic code fix" and does not require certificate or key revocations.
Until that update arrives, the advisory lists no workaround. Because the flaw can only be reached during a network boot, operators who do not need PXE can disable it to reduce exposure. Ars also advised watching boot-time network traffic and logs for signs of attempts.
How It Became Public
The flaw was found by Alex Matrosov of Anthropic and Dan Holmes-Mitra of Google, the advisory credits. A coordinated disclosure had been planned for January 2027.
That plan was overtaken on September 28, when a pull request to EDK II, signed off by an AMI engineer, publicly described the flaw by its CVE number and included the fix. Once the people who found it saw the post, TianoCore published its advisory on October 22, weeks before the planned date.
With the patch public, Ars noted that skilled attackers can study it to determine how the flaw is triggered and build working exploits.
There is no sign the flaw has been used in an attack. It was not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of its October 27 update, and no researcher has reported seeing it exploited.
The flaw is also not, on its own, a way into a network, Ars Technica reported after putting questions to several firmware researchers. The realistic attacker is an insider, or someone who has already gained a low-level foothold on the local network and wants to dig deeper.
"An attacker intent on compromising a nearby endpoint or server could use this bug to hijack program flow at a point where the boot process still has access to sensitive components, like the endpoint's TPM," said HD Moore, the creator of Metasploit and chief research officer at the security firm Dragos, in comments to Ars Technica.
"This could be used to break disk encryption for cases where an attacker has short-term network access (and it would be even easier in a theft scenario)."
It is not the first serious flaw in EDK II's network-boot code. In January 2024, researchers disclosed PixieFail, a set of nine flaws in the same part of EDK II, also reachable during PXE boot. Ars reported that fuzzing projects started after PixieFail to find more bugs in the code did not catch this one.

articles.title: Anthropic entra a la medicina: compra empresa biotecnológica que investiga la distrofia muscular y enfermedades raras
articles.text:
Anthropic adquirió Mithril Medicine, una empresa de biotecnología de una sola persona con sede en Cambridge, Massachusetts, que utilizaba Claude para coordinar experimentos, datos y logística con 11 laboratorios externos. La operación se concretó en julio y fue anunciada por la compañía el 27 de octubre.
El fundador de Mithril, Cody Tranbarger, dirigía a científicos consultores a tiempo parcial y a laboratorios subcontratados que producían anticuerpos, medían su unión a objetivos biológicos, realizaban ensayos celulares y llevaban adelante estudios con ratones.
Tras la adquisición, sus programas para dos formas raras de distrofia muscular se convirtieron en los primeros proyectos internos de desarrollo de fármacos de Anthropic.
La empresa trabaja en tratamientos para la distrofia muscular congénita relacionada con LAMA2 y la alfa-distroglicanopatía.
El primer programa busca reparar las conexiones debilitadas entre las fibras musculares y el tejido circundante mediante anticuerpos biespecíficos, diseñados para unirse a dos dianas y formar un puente molecular.
El objetivo de Anthropic con la adquisición
Anthropic incorporó Mithril como parte de una estrategia para ampliar el uso de Claude en todas las etapas del desarrollo de medicamentos: desde la identificación de dianas terapéuticas y el diseño de moléculas hasta la fabricación, la documentación regulatoria y la planificación de ensayos clínicos.
La compañía sostiene que los obstáculos para acelerar la creación de fármacos se distribuyen a lo largo de todo el proceso, no solo en el diseño inicial de nuevas moléculas.
Por eso, busca involucrar a Claude en programas reales de investigación y desarrollo, en distintas áreas terapéuticas y etapas de avance.
Además de Mithril, Anthropic colaboró con seis organizaciones que desarrollan medicamentos: BigHat Biosciences, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines y The Column Group.
Según la empresa, estas asociaciones le permiten evaluar las fortalezas y limitaciones de sus modelos en tareas científicas y operativas.
El sistema utilizado por Mithril recibió el nombre de “Pipeline-in-a-Person”. Durante una semana elegida por el equipo como ejemplo, Claude sintetizó un informe de producción de 341 páginas sobre 113 construcciones de anticuerpos en menos de ocho minutos.
Asimismo, revisó un plan experimental para incluir 89 de esas moléculas en cuatro minutos, después de que un integrante del equipo descartara una recomendación previa.
Sin embargo, el uso de la inteligencia artificial también produjo errores. El equipo revisó seis fallas de Claude y al menos tres llegaron a laboratorios externos mediante correos electrónicos editados y enviados por personas.
Una de ellas pedía menos material por tubo del requerido, aunque fue corregida antes de que comenzara el llenado; otras dos, vinculadas con datos de producción, pasaron inadvertidas durante más de cuatro días.
Qué medicamentos podrían adelantarse
El principal programa de Mithril está dirigido a la distrofia muscular congénita relacionada con LAMA2, una enfermedad causada por mutaciones en el gen que codifica la proteína laminina-α2. Estas alteraciones debilitan las conexiones entre las fibras musculares y el tejido que las rodea.
Anthropic afirmó que Mithril alcanzó una prueba de concepto en ratones en menos de 18 meses.
El informe técnico, aún pendiente de revisión por pares, detalla que siete ratones tratados con un formato de anticuerpo mostraron, aproximadamente a las seis semanas de edad, casi el doble de fuerza de agarre y fuerza máxima del tríceps que cuatro ratones que recibieron una solución de control.
Los resultados, no obstante, presentan limitaciones. Los investigadores asignaron el tratamiento por camada, sin aleatorización, y evaluaron al grupo que recibió anticuerpos entre 126 y 161 días después del grupo de control, con un traslado de colonia en el medio.
El propio informe recomienda repetir los experimentos de manera simultánea y a ciegas.
Mithril apunta a seleccionar candidatos a fármacos en 2027. Si el desarrollo posterior tiene éxito, el programa para LAMA2 podría comenzar ensayos clínicos en humanos a finales de 2028, mientras que el proyecto para la alfa-distroglicanopatía tiene como objetivo iniciar estudios clínicos en 2029.

articles.title: Une IA juge leur comportement au volant suspect, la police les arrête
articles.text:
Aux États-Unis, la police arrête des conducteurs qui n’ont commis aucun délit. Leur seul tort : avoir emprunté un trajet que l’intelligence artificielle (IA) juge suspect. Un petit air de Minority Report ?
Outre-Atlantique, des lecteurs automatiques de plaques d’immatriculation sont installés au bord des routes, et photographient chaque véhicule qui passe, accompagné du lieu et de l’heure. Le réseau de l’entreprise Flock Safety en compterait à lui seul plus de 335 000 et assure depuis juillet 2025 pouvoir signaler des itinéraires jugés inhabituels. Une pratique dont la police abuserait sciemment.
De nombreux cas recensés à travers le pays
Dans un rapport publié ce 26 octobre, l’American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), une grande association américaine de défense des libertés, étaye comment des policiers s’appuient sur l’IA pour cibler des automobilistes sans aucune preuve contre eux. Une fois la cible désignée, l’agent n’a plus qu’à relever une infraction mineure pour justifier le contrôle.
Elle cite notamment l’histoire de Grace Knowles, une jeune femme en road trip. En septembre 2025, elle a quitté La Nouvelle-Orléans en direction de la Floride quand un policier l’a arrêtée car elle serait restée trop longtemps sur la voie de gauche. Il l'a interrogée sur son itinéraire et, doutant de sa version, l'a invitée dans son véhicule. À l’écran, une carte des États-Unis retraçait ses déplacements, chaque point renvoyant à une photo de sa plaque.
Le policier lui a alors expliqué que les caméras sont « partout », y compris au dos des panneaux routiers. En réalité, c’était une IA qui avait signalé le véhicule de la jeune femme à l'officier. Et son cas est loin d’être isolé.
Au Texas, un jury a donné raison à un vendeur de matériel pétrolier, arrêté pour un prétendu écart de voie que les images de sa caméra embarquée contredisaient. Un centre fédéral avait alerté la police locale parce qu’il avait simplement fait l’aller-retour entre deux localisations, un trajet qui posait question au système de surveillance. Dans le même comté, des milliers d’autres conducteurs auraient subi le même traitement.
« Faux prétextes »
L’ACLU craint que ces algorithmes piègent bien plus d’innocents que de coupables, et redoute des dérives politiques, par exemple contre des personnes qui ont participé à des manifestations. » Même avant l’apparition des lecteurs de plaques d’immatriculation et de l’IA, les contrôles sous faux prétexte étaient malheureusement assez courants en tant que stratégie policière, raison pour laquelle l’ACLU se bat depuis des années pour les faire interdire », étaye l’organisme.
« Mais ce à quoi nous assistons aujourd’hui marque un changement radical par rapport à la manière dont la police a toujours fonctionné : celle-ci peut désormais utiliser la technologie pour nous surveiller tous en permanence, puis s’appuyer sur l’IA pour analyser les montagnes de données ainsi générées afin d’identifier des suspects, qui sont ensuite interpellés sous de faux prétextes », poursuit-elle.
Dans ce contexte, elle appelle à mettre fin à « la surveillance des plaques d’immatriculation, au suivi de localisation sous toutes ses formes et à la surveillance de masse en général ». En France, la lecture automatisée des plaques existe déjà pour la police, la gendarmerie et les douanes, sous le contrôle de la CNIL. Une loi de 2023 autorise même les douanes à tester, à titre expérimental, le repérage de véhicules qui circulent régulièrement ensemble.

articles.title: Razer Introduces Reclusa Mini 65% Magnetic Gaming Keyboard
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Razer Introduces Reclusa Mini 65% Magnetic Gaming Keyboard
Razer, the leading global lifestyle brand for gamers, today announced the Razer Reclusa Mini 65%, a wireless hot-swappable magnetic gaming keyboard for enthusiasts who care about how every key sounds, feels, and performs.
Built around the philosophy of "Your Board. Your Rules.", the Reclusa Mini 65% combines magnetic switch precision, refined acoustics, and deep customization in a compact 65% form factor that is rewarding from the very first keystroke.The Razer Reclusa Mini 65% joins the Reclusa line with Hall Effect magnetic switches, adjustable actuation, Rapid Trigger, and tri-mode connectivity, for players who want more control over how every key responds.
Barrie Ooi, Head of PC Gaming Division at Razer"We created the Reclusa line for enthusiasts who view their keyboard as something personal. With the Reclusa Mini 65%, we are bringing magnetic switch technology into the Reclusa experience while staying true to what makes the line unique: a great out-of-box experience, rewarding acoustics, enjoyable typing feel, and the freedom to make the board your own through hot-swappable magnetic switches and swappable keycaps."
Tuned Sound. Solid Feel.
Sound and feel come first. The Reclusa Mini 65% delivers from the first key press: a full, clean, clacky sound and a plush bottom-out, no modding required.Razer Hall Effect Magnetic Switches define the feel, while an IXPE switch foam sheet, PPS plate, lubricated stabilizers and dual-layer silicone dampening add fullness and reduce case resonance. The result is a keyboard that stays enjoyable through long gaming and typing sessions.
Rapid Response. Total Control.
The Reclusa Mini 65% puts the feel of every keystroke in the player's hands. Powered by Razer Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, it delivers a smooth, responsive typing experience, with adjustable actuation from 0.1 mm to 4.0 mm so users can tune each key to their own style. Set it light and fast for competitive gaming, or deeper and more deliberate for typing.Rapid Trigger delivers faster repeated inputs, while Advanced Input Control, including Razer Snap Tap, Razer Snap Flex, and Dual-Key press Priority, adds tighter control in fast-paced gameplay. Six onboard profiles keep each setup saved on the board.
Wired Speed. Wireless Freedom.
Ready to play the moment it is plugged in, and ready to adapt when the player is. Tri-mode connectivity lets players choose how to connect: game with low latency over Razer HyperSpeed Wireless (2.4 GHz), switch between up to three devices via Bluetooth, or go wired via USB Type-C for true 8,000 Hz polling.The multi-function dial puts essential controls within immediate reach, allowing players to make quick adjustments without interrupting their gameplay. Brightness, volume, and more can be adjusted without breaking flow, so the keyboard can be set up around how players play, work, and create.
Swap Freely. Make It Yours.
The Reclusa Mini 65% is built to be customized. Preferences change, and so does the way players play and type. The hot-swappable PCB makes it easy to swap in preferred magnetic switches to fine-tune the feel, with the included 2-in-1 keycap and switch puller making it simple.South-facing LEDs keep the keyboard compatible with a wider range of enthusiast keycaps without giving up RGB lighting, while doubleshot ABS keycaps in a tri-tone design stay crisp and fade-resistant. Per-key Razer Chroma RGB lighting with 16.8 million colors lets players match each key to their setup or mood, giving the board a distinctive identity from day one.
One Board. Zero Compromise.
Tuned Sound. Solid Feel: Razer Hall Effect Magnetic Switches for feel, IXPE switch foam for a fuller sound, plus a PPS plate, lubricated stabilizers, and dual-layer silicone dampening.

articles.title: Oman's Phaze Ventures launches two AI funds targeting over $75 million
articles.text: Oman-based Phaze Ventures has launched two venture capital funds targeting more than $75 million combined, securing over $40 million in investor commitments to date. The funds will invest in artificial intelligence and deeptech startups in Oman and international markets. Phaze Ventures Fund II is anchored by ITHCA Group, a subsidiary of Oman Investment Authority, as well as Ominvest and Oman LNG Development Foundation. The second vehicle, Phaze Ventures Oman Fund, is backed by Future Fund Oman and will focus on domestic AI-enabled businesses. Founded in 2018 by Abdullah Al Shaksy, Mohammed Al Wahaibi and Masoud Al Rawahi, Phaze Ventures invests in early-stage AI and deeptech companies, with a focus on the GCC and North America. The firm has offices or team members in Muscat, Dubai and Riyadh. The two funds have made 10 investments, including Arabic.AI, Sully.ai, Andromeda Surgical, Boardy.ai and Metal. Phaze Ventures manages capital for more than 50 investors, including sovereign entities, corporations and family offices across the Gulf and other markets. Press release: Oman-headquartered Phaze Ventures announced the launch of two new venture funds targeting over $75 million. Phaze Ventures Fund II, anchored by ITHCA Group (a subsidiary of Oman Investment Authority), Ominvest and Oman LNG Development Foundation, continues the firm’s global AI and deeptech investment mandate, while Phaze Ventures Oman Fund, anchored by Future Fund Oman, establishes a dedicated capital pool for homegrown AI-enabled businesses. Together, the two-fund venture platform has secured over $40 million in investor commitments, with ongoing discussions to grow the funds to $75 million. The announcement comes as Oman builds the International Financial Centre of Oman, a new hub for international companies and investors. “AI is the most disruptive technology shift of our generation. Oman and the Gulf can’t afford to be spectators, and our participation can’t be limited to playing catch-up through investments in hyperscalers, data centres and public market offerings. We need to invest in the founders disrupting industries at home and across the globe, and we need to be a part of that disruption early,” said Abdullah Al Shaksy, Co-founder and CEO of Phaze Ventures. The new funds’ first 10 investments include Arabic.AI, Sully.ai, Andromeda Surgical, Boardy.ai and Metal, with co-investors including a16z, 8VC, Standard Capital, Y Combinator and Baidu Ventures. “We back founders who combine domain expertise with strong engineering and learn from every real-world deployment,” said Masoud Al Rawahi, Co-founder and Partner at Phaze Ventures. Nour Al Hassan, Founder and CEO of Arabic.AI, said: “Getting to know the Phaze Ventures team convinced me they were the right partners. They shared our ambition to build AI our region can own and our long-term commitment to make it happen.” Arabic.AI develops Arabic-language enterprise AI, supported by investment from Saudi Arabia’s HUMAIN and a partnership with Qualcomm Technologies. Ahmed Omar, Co-founder and CEO of Sully.ai, said: “Phaze Ventures understood early how Sully could leverage AI to bring more capacity and real returns to the global healthcare system. They backed us every step of the way as we scaled globally, and were able to connect us with healthcare providers who could put our product to work.” NVIDIA highlighted Sully.ai in a case study showing a 90% reduction in inference costs and a 65% improvement in response times for medical workflows. That early conviction extends to Andromeda Surgical, which Phaze Ventures backed before its US$15 million Series A led by Standard Capital. Nick Damiano, Co-founder and CEO of Andromeda Surgical, said: “Phaze Ventures didn’t shy away from a frontier problem like building the autonomous AI-guided future of robotic surgery. They recognised our team’s rare combination of medical and autonomy expertise, backed us early, and have been proactive in opening doors through their regional network.” The new fund platform has backed players in the capital markets ecosystem, including Metal and Boardy.ai. Phaze Ventures invested in Metal’s seed round alongside Y Combinator and a16z. Metal’s AI fundraising platform helps hundreds of founders manage their capital raise uses AI to connect founders with investors, customers and talent. Usman Gul, Founder and CEO of Metal, said: “In today’s venture landscape, slow capital is expensive. I’ve raised from some of the world’s leading venture firms, and Phaze Ventures brings the same speed and foresight. They moved quickly to back us early and became committed partners as we rapidly scaled Metal’s AI-driven operating system for founders raising venture rounds.” A two-time founder, Usman previously raised US$120 million from investors including First Round Capital and 20VC. With team members in Muscat, Dubai and Riyadh, Phaze Ventures manages capital for over 50 investors, including sovereign entities, listed companies, corporates, family offices and business families across Oman, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, India and beyond. “Investors across Oman and the Gulf want a stake in the next generation of AI companies while they are still taking shape. This platform is our answer” said Mohammed Al Wahaibi, Co-founder and Partner at Phaze Ventures.

articles.title: This 20-year-old Nokia phone can now run ChatGPT and Gemini — but you’ll need to be somewhere that still has 2G
articles.text:
Your ancient Nokia can now run ChatGPT thanks to a vibe-coded app
An old phone with new features
- A vibe-coded app lets you access various AI chatbots on the Nokia 6300 and other ancient phones
- As long as the phone supports Java apps, it should, in theory, be able to run the app
- However, you have to buy credits to use it
Phones have come a long way since the Nokia 6300 launched back in early 2007 — that device had no touchscreen and no Wi-Fi capabilities. In fact, you were limited to 2G connectivity on the 6300 — something that the US and some other countries have now shut down. But thanks to a new vibe-coded app, the Nokia 6300 now has some very 2026 capabilities.
X user @EmirKarsiyakali has shared how they’ve created an app dubbed Aikon — that's 'Nokia' backwards — that allows you to access ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Grok on the Nokia 6300 or any other old phone that runs Java apps (notably, though, it was originally developed for the 6300 and has only been tested on Nokia Series 40 and Series 60 phones).
So if you’ve got one of these ancient handsets sitting in a drawer, you could dig it out and give this app a try — though you’re unlikely to want to ditch your smartphone.
Pricey and clunky
While the Aikon app does add some smart capabilities to old dumb phones, it’s not free, as you have to buy credits from the Aikon site to converse with it.
Also, while some effort has been made to provide a good user experience — the app supports multiple languages, saves messages for 30 days, and includes support for voice messages and image analysis — you’re still going to be working with a tiny, low-resolution screen and a keypad.
Not to mention the fact that, in the case of the Nokia 6300 and some other supported models, you might not even have access to any sort of data connection if you’re in a country that has shut down its 2G services.
Still, it’s impressive to see such a modern technology working on such ancient hardware, and it could be fun to at least dabble with the Aikon app if you have a supported handset.

articles.title: Así cotizan las principales criptomonedas del mundo digital este miércoles 28 de octubre
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 81.099,39 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de 0,364% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de 0,701% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 2.364,19 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de 0,02%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 748,21 dólares, con un cambio de 0,92%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 57.607 dólares, tras una variación de 1.6688619.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,08 dólares tras presentar un cambio de 3,05% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Criptomonedas en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: Wazuh and AI for Enhanced SOC Workflows
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of this decade's defining technologies. From healthcare and finance to manufacturing and education, organizations increasingly rely on AI to automate repetitive tasks, uncover patterns hidden within large datasets, and support faster decision-making. Cybersecurity has experienced a similar transformation. While attackers employ AI to automate cyberattacks and accelerate vulnerability discovery, defenders are adopting AI to improve threat detection and enhance incident response.
Security Operations Centers (SOCs) receive a high volume of alerts from endpoints, cloud workloads, network devices, identity providers, and business applications. Although SIEM and XDR platforms provide visibility into these environments, analysts often spend considerable time correlating alerts, searching documentation, and determining the next investigative steps. AI offers a practical way to augment analysts by providing contextual explanations, summarizing findings, and recommending remediation actions, rather than replacing human expertise.
Challenges facing modern SOCs
Modern SOCs are expected to detect and respond to sophisticated threats while processing millions of security events every day. High alert volumes contribute to analyst fatigue and increase the likelihood that critical events are overlooked. Investigations frequently require switching between dashboards, documentation, vulnerability databases, and threat intelligence feeds before a complete picture emerges. As infrastructures become increasingly distributed across on-premises and cloud environments, maintaining consistent situational awareness becomes more difficult. AI-assisted workflows help address these challenges by reducing repetitive analysis, adding context, and accelerating investigative decision-making.
Wazuh and artificial intelligence for enhanced SOC workflows
Wazuh promotes flexible AI adoption through the Wazuh AI Analyst available on the Wazuh Cloud and integrations with third-party AI providers. Organizations can leverage the Wazuh AI Analyst capability on the Wazuh Cloud for guidance on their environment's security posture. Organizations that self-deploy Wazuh can also leverage Wazuh integrations with AI providers. The following sections highlight further details:
The Wazuh AI Analyst
The Wazuh AI Analyst is automated and hands-off. It is an AI-powered security analysis service for Wazuh Cloud subscriptions that processes your security data through Amazon Bedrock and Anthropic’s Claude, delivering insights without any manual configuration. It periodically emails key indicators, a histogram of protected endpoints, alert volume, active vulnerabilities, and a posture summary with a full PDF report attached.
The reports are generated on your Wazuh Cloud subscription’s schedule and are periodically sent to your registered email address. You can also view them from the Wazuh Cloud console in the Environments > AI Reports page.
On privacy, subscription data is not shared with third parties and is not used to train AI models; it is processed only to generate your reports, with encrypted transmission, isolated processing, and no permanent storage. As with any AI output, the recommendations are advisory and should be validated against your own policies before you act.
Threat hunting and security operations with external AI integrations
Beyond the Wazuh AI Analyst, you can expand Wazuh capabilities using a self-hosted LLM and externally managed AI integrations tailored to your needs.
Self-hosted Llama 3 and Ollama
This integration keeps everything on your own network. Ollama runs the Meta open-source Llama LLM locally on the Wazuh server; a Python script decompresses the archived logs for a chosen period, vectorizes them into a FAISS store, and serves a LangChain-powered chatbot you can query. Nothing is sent to a cloud provider, which makes it well-suited to teams with strict privacy or data-residency requirements.
Full setup steps are in the Wazuh blog post: Leveraging artificial intelligence for threat hunting in Wazuh.
Externally managed integration with Claude 3.5 Haiku
This integration surfaces Anthropic’s Claude 3.5 Haiku, hosted on Amazon Bedrock, as a chat box inside the dashboard through the OpenSearch Assistant. Setup involves enabling the model in Bedrock, installing the relevant OpenSearch plugins, and creating an ML Commons connector, model, and conversational agent. The assistant can provide useful guidance on many common tasks, including what to do about a finding and how to configure certain settings.
Full setup steps are in the Wazuh blog post: Leveraging Claude Haiku in the Wazuh dashboard for LLM-powered insights.
Conclusion
Artificial intelligence is becoming an important capability in modern SOCs. Rather than replacing analysts, it can reduce repetitive work, accelerate investigations, and provide contextual support for detection, triage, and response activities. These capabilities can help security teams operate more efficiently while keeping analysts responsible for validation and consequential decisions.
For Wazuh Cloud users, the Wazuh AI Analyst provides automated, scheduled security reports covering key indicators, alert activity, endpoint coverage, active vulnerabilities, and overall security posture. Organizations can further tailor AI-enabled security operations through self-hosted LLM integrations for privacy-sensitive threat hunting or externally managed, cloud-hosted models, aligning adoption with their operational, privacy, and data-residency requirements.

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Reaches Nearly $2,000 Across U.S. Retailers
NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 5080 has seen a significant increase in its listed price over the past few weeks, with this high-end GPU now costing nearly $2,000. Due to price hikes throughout the supply chain and the GPU's 16 GB of GDDR7 memory, which is currently in short supply, the listing price has doubled its original MSRP. NVIDIA initially launched the GeForce RTX 5080 in early 2025 with an MSRP of $999. articles.title: Tailscale corrige ses failles SSH et confirme d'autres vulnérabilités permettant de prendre le contrôle de serveurs
articles.text:
Une connexion SSH pouvait être parfaitement autorisée et donner malgré tout accès à des fonctions réservées aux administrateurs. D'autres failles exposaient les services partagés ou risquaient d'interrompre toutes les connexions d'un serveur.
Quelques jours après la publication du rapport Tailworm d'Erica Windisch, Tailscale a déployé la version 1.104.4 de son client. Les travaux de la chercheuse avaient montré comment un appareil déjà compromis pouvait servir à obtenir les droits administrateur sur d'autres serveurs auxquels les règles du réseau autorisaient les connexions SSH. Quatre bulletins de sécurité détaillent désormais les vulnérabilités confirmées, leurs conditions d'exploitation et les modifications apportées au logiciel.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Des privilèges root aux connexions interrompues
Le correctif le plus important concerne les redirections de Tailscale SSH. Jusqu'ici, le processus tailscaled les exécutait avec les privilèges root du système, même lorsque le compte connecté disposait de droits bien plus limités. Depuis la version 1.104.4, ces opérations respectent les permissions de ce compte, empêchant ainsi d'accéder, par ce moyen, à des ressources réservées aux administrateurs.
Cette mauvaise séparation des privilèges concernait aussi Tailscale Serve, qui permet de partager des applications et des services locaux sur le réseau privé. Dans certaines configurations, une vérification insuffisante des sockets Unix pouvait exposer l'API d'administration locale du logiciel à des utilisateurs distants, jusqu'à permettre une prise de contrôle complète du serveur. Une autre faille touchait les connexions HTTP/2 : les autorisations destinées à une application pouvaient être transmises à une autre, donnant potentiellement accès à des ressources protégées. Les correctifs renforcent les vérifications des destinations et associent désormais les autorisations à chaque requête.
Une session SSH pouvait également servir à paralyser le réseau sans chercher à obtenir davantage de droits. En envoyant continuellement certains messages, une personne disposant déjà d'un accès pouvait saturer progressivement la mémoire de tailscaled, jusqu'à provoquer son arrêt et interrompre toutes les connexions Tailscale du serveur. La nouvelle version limite désormais la mémoire consommée par chaque session et libère les ressources correspondantes dès sa fermeture.
La version 1.104.4 à installer sans attendre
Les administrateurs utilisant Tailscale SSH ou Tailscale Serve doivent mettre à jour les machines concernées vers la version 1.104.4, ou une version ultérieure. Chaque serveur vulnérable doit recevoir le correctif, une mise à jour du seul poste depuis lequel on s'y connecte ne protégeant pas les autres machines du réseau.
Il est également nécessaire de revoir les règles d'accès SSH pour limiter les connexions aux comptes et appareils qui en ont réellement besoin. Sur les serveurs sensibles, le mode SSH check permet d'exiger une authentification supplémentaire avant l'ouverture d'une session, afin de réduire les possibilités d'exploitation depuis un appareil compromis.
Si une mise à jour immédiate est impossible, la désactivation des redirections SSH permet de bloquer temporairement plusieurs techniques d'exploitation. Pour cela, il suffit d'ajouter la variable TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 à l'environnement du service tailscaled, puis de le redémarrer. Les connexions SSH demeurent possibles, mais les redirections ne fonctionnent plus. Cette mesure ne protège toutefois pas contre toutes les vulnérabilités identifiées, notamment celles qui touchent Tailscale Serve et la gestion de la mémoire. Elle ne remplace donc pas l'installation des correctifs.
- Installation rapide
- Connexion sécurisée
- Gestion multiplateforme

articles.title: Egyptian climatetech NoorNation secures $1.05 million seed funding
articles.text: Egypt-based climatetech startup NoorNation has closed a $1.05 million seed funding round, backed by agribusiness group Linah Farms, along with climate tech investor Catalyst Fund and Saudi firm KBW Ventures. Founded in 2021 by Ragy Ramadan and Mohamed Khaled, NoorNation develops decentralised clean energy and water infrastructure for agricultural businesses and underserved communities. Its flagship product, LifeBox, provides solar-powered electricity and water solutions for off-grid operations. Linah Farms' investment follows projects involving solar-powered irrigation at its agricultural operations, renewable energy systems at its agricultural school and a solar installation at its Sultan Gardens Resort in Sharm El Sheikh. The investment comes as NoorNation develops pay-per-use solar irrigation solutions for Egyptian farmers, aiming to reduce reliance on diesel-powered pumping systems. Press release: Egypt-based climatetech startup NoorNation has closed a $1.05 million seed funding round, with agricultural group Linah Farms joining its shareholder base after deploying the startup's renewable energy solutions across several of its operations. The round saw participation from climate tech investor Catalyst Fund and Saudi firm KBW Ventures. The investment marks a shift in the relationship between the two companies, with Linah Farms moving from a commercial customer to an investor following projects involving solar-powered agricultural irrigation, an agricultural school and a hotel in Sharm El Sheikh. Founded in 2021 by Ragy Ramadan and Mohamed Khaled, NoorNation develops decentralised clean energy and water infrastructure for agricultural businesses, rural communities and other off-grid users in Egypt and Sub-Saharan Africa. Its flagship product, LifeBox, is a self-contained, solar-powered system designed to provide electricity and water for irrigation, desalination and other applications in areas with limited access to conventional infrastructure. The company has previously attracted investment from KBW Ventures , the investment firm founded by Saudi Prince Khaled bin Alwaleed, which backed NoorNation in 2024 for an undisclosed amount. From customer to investor NoorNation and Linah Farms have worked together on several renewable energy projects, including solar irrigation systems at agricultural operations in Egypt's Bahariya Oasis, a solar-and-battery installation at Linah's agricultural school and a solar power system at Sultan Gardens Resort in Sharm El Sheikh. According to NoorNation founder Ragy Ramadan, the solar-powered irrigation system at Linah Farms' Bahariya Oasis operations has generated more than EGP 3 million in diesel savings, while the installation at Sultan Gardens Resort has reduced electricity costs by more than EGP 2.2 million. The companies have also announced an agreement covering five additional solar installations with a combined capacity of approximately 1.13 MWp across the Bahariya Oasis and West Minya. The projects include solar irrigation systems and a hybrid power station. The agreement brings the combined capacity of projects delivered and under implementation for Linah Group to approximately 1.71 MWp, according to NoorNation. Expanding solar-powered irrigation The funding comes as NoorNation develops a pay-per-use solar irrigation model aimed at farmers who continue to rely on diesel-powered water pumps. Linah Farms is also expected to support financing for this model, extending the partnership beyond its existing energy installations. The approach seeks to make solar-powered irrigation more accessible to agricultural businesses while reducing their exposure to fuel costs. NoorNation's latest investment adds to growing interest in decentralised clean energy solutions for Egypt's agricultural sector, where access to affordable power and water remains a challenge for farms operating outside established infrastructure networks.

articles.title: Adobe Fixes 8 Critical Campaign Classic Flaws Allowing Code Execution and Security Bypass
articles.text:
Adobe has released patches to address multiple critical security flaws in Campaign Classic that, if successfully exploited, could result in arbitrary code execution, security feature bypass, and privilege escalation.
The list of eight vulnerabilities is as follows -
- CVE-2026-104351 (CVSS score: 9.9) - A code injection vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.
- CVE-2026-104353 (CVSS score: 9.9) - An operating system code injection vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.
- CVE-2026-105780 (CVSS score: 9.9) - An incorrect authorization vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.
- CVE-2026-105489 (CVSS score: 9.9) - An SQL injection vulnerability that could lead to security feature bypass.
- CVE-2026-105781 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An SQL injection vulnerability that could lead to security feature bypass.
- CVE-2026-104350 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that could lead to privilege escalation.
- CVE-2026-104354 (CVSS score: 9.1) - An SQL injection vulnerability that could lead to security feature bypass.
- CVE-2026-105779 (CVSS score: 9.1) - An SQL injection vulnerability that could lead to security feature bypass.
The issues affect Adobe Campaign Classic versions 7.4.4 build 9402 and earlier for Windows and Linux. They have been patched in version 7.4.4 build 9403.
Also resolved by Adobe is a critical code injection flaw in Adobe Connect Desktop and Mobile for Windows, macOS, and Android (CVE-2026-48360, CVSS score: 9.6) that could result in arbitrary code execution.
The vulnerability has been fixed in the following versions -
- 
    Adobe Connect Desktop - 
    
  - Windows: version 2026.9.61
  - macOS Silicon: version 2026.10.66
  - macOS Intel: version 2026.10.170
- Adobe Connect Mobile for Android version 4.5
Adobe said it's not "aware of any exploits in the wild for any of the issues" addressed in the update. Users are advised to update to the latest version for optimal protection.

articles.title: Japanese internet giant GMO tells customers to shut down and disconnect PCs from the internet following data breach and ransomware threat
articles.text:
Japanese internet giant GMO tells customers to shut down and disconnect PCs from the internet following data breach and ransomware threat
Hackers threatened to install ransomware on user devices
- GMO warned customers to back up data, disconnect devices, and shut down systems after a cyberattack
- Attackers allegedly stole customer data, leaked information, and threatened ransomware deployment
- Compromised trading-platform credentials and reports of unauthorized transactions raised concerns for affected users
Japanese internet giant GMO Group has told its customers to scan their computers for viruses, back up all of their data, disconnect the devices from the internet and then shut them down.
The announcement, which literally told customers, “unplug any cords connected to your PC," was made in response to a cyberattack it recently suffered, as well as the threats then made by the malicious actors.
GMO Group gets hit
GMO Internet Group is a large Japanese technology conglomerate whose business spans internet infrastructure, cybersecurity, online advertising, financial services, and more. It brings in billions of dollars every year, and operates a broad portfolio of subsidiaries, among which is Onamae Desktop Cloud, a popular VPS service provider.
Its main customers seem to be individual retail forex (FX) traders in Japan who run automated trading software. It provides a rented Windows desktop hosted on GMO’s servers, allowing customers to keep trading applications running, while being able to shut down their own computers.
On October 20, 2026, the company disclosed having suffered a cyberattack in which threat actors installed malware on some customer environments. Apparently, up to 26,739 servers were at risk, and the company responded by progressively shutting them down, launching an investigation, and cleaning them up.
“We have confirmed that unauthorized access by a third party occurred against Onamae.com Desktop Cloud and that unauthorized programs were installed in some customers’ server environments,” the company said at the time.
The investigation determined that the attackers walked away with sensitive customer data, although it wasn’t said how many customers were compromised, or what types of information were taken. It was also later reported that the unnamed attackers were demanding roughly $50 million in ransom, in exchange for deleting the data. They threatened to release the data on the dark web if the demands aren’t met. Onamae said it wouldn’t pay the attackers, and the data eventually did leak.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Despite the data leaking, no known entities claimed responsibility for the attack.
Condolences money
The attackers also threatened to install ransomware on devices belonging to Onamae customers, triggering the warning and the call for everyone to shut down and unplug their devices:
“1. Request for a full scan of your own device for virus checks 2. Request for backup 3. Request to disconnect network and power from customer PC. Before 12:00 PM on Tuesday, October 27make sure to back up, disconnect the network, turn off the power, and unplug any cords connected to your PC,” the warning, machine-translated from Japanese, reads.
It seems the attackers never acted on their threat, since no ransomware was found on customer servers.
Onamae said it would not pay the attackers, but would instead compensate each customer $30 for their troubles, regardless or not if they actually suffered any damage or not. Those that suffered more meaningful damage will be compensated separately, it was said. Replacement computers were also offered, BleepingComputer reports.
The company has continued its investigation of the attack and is currently analyzing the leaked data to see how many customers were affected, and what is at risk. It also warned the public and the media not to share the leaked information, threatening legal information against those who do.
In one of the updates, Onamae said login credentials and some account details from users of trading platforms MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5 were compromised. “Some customers have reported transactions in their trading accounts that they do not recognize,” it added, before urging customers to reset their passwords and terminate all active sessions.
The full scope of the attack, as well as material damages (which might be substantial), are yet to be seen.
