articles.title: OpenAI planea comprar chips Google para entrenar sus modelos de IA
articles.text:
OpenAI planea comprar chips de inteligencia artificial a Google, según The Information, que cita a una persona al tanto del asunto. La operación uniría a dos empresas que compiten en productos de IA y en buscadores, pero que cierran cada vez más acuerdos entre sí.
El reporte no divulgó condiciones financieras ni otros detalles de la operación. Según el resumen de Investing.com, los términos finales del posible acuerdo todavía no están definidos. OpenAI declinó hacer comentarios a la agencia Reuters, y Google no respondió de inmediato al pedido de la agencia, enviado fuera del horario habitual de oficina.
Los chips en cuestión son las unidades de procesamiento tensorial (TPU) de Google, diseñadas para entrenar y ejecutar modelos de IA. Funcionan como alternativa a las unidades de procesamiento gráfico (GPU) de Nvidia, que dominan este mercado. OpenAI es una de las mayores compradoras de esas GPU, que usa para crear y hacer funcionar sus modelos.
Cómo es la relación entre OpenAI y Google
El movimiento llega una semana después de que OpenAI anunciara que ofrecerá sus modelos más avanzados a través de Google Cloud, la plataforma de servicios en la nube de su competidor. Reuters ya había informado en junio de 2025 que OpenAI había empezado a alquilar chips de Google.
Google comenzó este año a vender sus TPU directamente a algunos clientes, según Reuters. Entre los compradores figura Anthropic, rival de OpenAI. La directora financiera de Alphabet, la empresa matriz de Google, Anat Ashkenazi, dijo antes que la compañía espera registrar una pequeña parte de los ingresos de esos contratos antes de que termine este año, y la gran mayoría en 2027.
El martes, Oracle también anunció que empezará a ofrecer por primera vez los TPU de Google a sus clientes de nube. La misma empresa amplió su acuerdo con Nvidia para llevarlo a una escala de “varios gigavatios” y sumará chips de Cerebras y SambaNova, según Reuters. Oracle no precisó cómo financiará esas compras.
OpenAI también fabrica su propio chip
OpenAI presentó en junio su primer chip propio de IA, diseñado junto con Broadcom, y dijo que planeaba ponerlo en funcionamiento antes de fin de año, como parte de un programa de varias generaciones de procesadores. La compra a Google se sumaría así a esa vía interna y a los pedidos a Nvidia.
La demanda de capacidad de cómputo explica el interés por varios proveedores a la vez. Reuters calculó que Amazon, Microsoft y Alphabet planean gastar en conjunto hasta USD 600.000 millones este año en infraestructura de IA, mientras los inversores cuestionan cuándo ese gasto se traducirá en retornos significativos.
Para Google, un cliente como OpenAI reforzaría su negocio de chips frente a Nvidia. Para OpenAI, comprar a un competidor directo implica depender de otra empresa con la que disputa usuarios. Ninguna de las dos compañías confirmó el reporte, y se desconoce cuántos chips incluiría la operación.
Alphabet presentará sus resultados trimestrales el miércoles 28 de octubre. Los inversores esperan ver en esos números si su fuerte inversión en IA sigue impulsando el crecimiento de su negocio de nube, según Reuters.
OpenAI presentó GPT-6.1 Terra, un modelo intermedio más barato y rápido
OpenAI lanzó GPT-6.1 Terra, un modelo de inteligencia artificial de gama media para trabajo de oficina, con precios un 50% menores que su antecesor. Combina razonamiento visual y uso de computadora para tareas como redactar propuestas o editar videos.
Cuesta USD 1 por millón de tokens de entrada y USD 5 de salida. Según pruebas de la propia empresa, supera a GPT-5.6 Terra en exámenes profesionales y programación, e iguala a GPT-6 Astra a un precio mucho menor.
Artificial Analysis confirmó mejoras de forma independiente, aunque menores a las que indica OpenAI. La compañía recomienda modelos superiores para programación compleja. Analistas externos señalan que Terra sirve sobre todo para tareas repetitivas, sin representar una gran novedad para usuarios habituales de ChatGPT.

articles.title: Moitié prix pour cette trottinette électrique d'Acer parfaite pour éviter les transports en commun
articles.text:
L'Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator 833 W est une trottinette complète avec son système de freinage à double disque, ses pneus tubeless et cet écran LCD pour suivre l'autonomie en temps réel. Sur le site de la Fnac, elle chute sous les 250 euros.
En 2022, Acer a sorti une première itération de sa ES Series 5 Advanced Predator. Un modèle qui présentait plusieurs défauts, dont un moteur qui manquait de puissance. Conscient de ce problème, Acer a revu sa copie et a sorti une nouvelle itération de cette trottinette en faisant évoluer le moteur avec une puissance maximale de 833 W. En ce moment, le bolide est vendu à moitié prix par la Fnac.
Au lieu de 552,99 euros, l'Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator 833 W est proposée à 249,99 euros par la Fnac
Pourquoi choisir l'Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator 833 W ?
- Un moteur plus puissant : Avec une puissance maximale de 833 W, cette trottinette électrique atteint plus rapidement sa vitesse de pointe tandis que la montée des pentes sera plus simple.
- Une autonomie qui assure plusieurs trajets quotidiens : Avec soixante minutes d'autonomie, l'Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator 833 W pourra assurer plusieurs trajets domicile-travail même si la recharge de huit heures peut sembler longue.
- Un double freinage et des pneus tubeless : Pour renforcer sa fiabilité, Acer a offert à son engin un système de double freinage ainsi que des pneus tubeless qui doivent limiter les risques de crevaison.
Acer a compris ses erreurs
Comme évoqué en préambule, la première version de l'Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator 833 W présentait quelques défauts, dont ce moteur qui manquait de puissance. Défaut corrigé par la marque qui offre désormais un moteur avec une puissance maximale de 833 W à sa trottinette. Concrètement, il sera plus facile de gravir des pentes et d'atteindre la vitesse de pointe de 25 km/h, la limite légale dans l'Union Européenne.
Ce nouveau moteur s'insère dans un design réussi. Acer livre un engin complet avec un deck qui devrait pouvoir accueillir vos deux pieds. Les détails ont aussi été soignés par la marque. D'abord, le guidon accueille un écran LCD pour vous donner votre vitesse ou encore le niveau d'autonomie restant. Des clignotants sont aussi présents, tout comme des feux avant et arrière.
Côté conduite, l'Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator 833 W emporte des pneus tubeless de 10 pouces qui visent à limiter les crevaisons. Un système de double freinage est présent alors que la première version ne contenait qu'un seul frein à disque à l'arrière.
Des défauts restent à corriger
Malgré tous ces progrès, Acer ne rend pas une copie parfaite. L'application reste imparfaite puisqu'elle se contente d'ajuster l'éclairage ou de suivre le niveau d'autonomie. À noter qu'il est possible d'activer ou de désactiver le verrou électrique.
Autre défaut : le poids de cette trottinette. Elle pèse un peu plus de 18 kg. Un problème si vous habitez dans un appartement sans ascenseur puisque vous devrez la porter à bout de bras. Ce souci est encore plus important au moment de la recharge puisque la batterie n'est pas amovible. L'Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator 833 W tient 60 minutes avec une seule charge. Pour une recharge complète, il faudra compter huit heures, ce qui est un poil long.
✅ Les points forts
- Un moteur de 833 W plus efficace en côtes
- Un double système de freinage pour un arrêt plus précis
- Des pneus tubeless pour limiter les crevaisons
❌ Les limites
- Une charge longue et une batterie inamovible
- Une application qui demande à être perfectionnée
L'Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator 833 W est désormais disponible pour 249,99 euros sur le site de la Fnac au lieu de 552,99 euros
L'Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator 833 W rend une meilleure copie que la première itération avec un moteur plus puissant et un système de freinage plus précis. Si des défauts sont encore à noter, ils sont très largement atténués par cette promotion de la Fnac.

articles.title: DPI Venture Capital closes Nclude Fund at over $112 million
articles.text: DPI Venture Capital has announced the final close of its Nclude Fund at over $112 million, to invest in technology startups across Africa and the Middle East. Established in Egypt in 2022, Nclude came under DPI Venture Capital's investment advisory management in 2025 following a restructuring. The fund focuses on fintech, financial inclusion, AI and technology-enabled businesses, investing between $500,000 and $10 million per company, from Seed to Series C. Egypt remains its core market, with 30% of the fund's investment mandate allocated to opportunities outside the country. Nclude has invested in 15 companies across Africa and the Middle East, including Egyptian startups Nawy, Paymob and Money Fellows, UAE-based FlapKap, Senegal-focused healthtech Kera and Accord Partners, which targets AI applications in accounting and auditing. The final close will support new investments and the regional expansion of portfolio companies, particularly businesses scaling between Egypt, the Gulf and other African markets. DPI Venture Capital is led by Managing Partner Ashley Lewis, alongside General Partner Mohamed Aladdin. Press release: DPI Venture Capital, Development Partners International’s venture capital platform, today announced the final close of the Nclude Fund at over $112 million, supporting its next phase of investment across Africa and the Middle East. Nclude was established in 2022 as a fintech-focused venture capital fund in Egypt. DPI became investment adviser to the fund in 2025 following a restructuring transaction, alongside the launch of DPI Venture Capital, its dedicated venture capital platform. Since then, DPI Venture Capital has selectively broadened the LP base with additional strategically aligned investors. Nclude’s strategy focuses on fintech, fintech-enabled businesses and financial inclusion, and supports companies at the intersection of fintech, AI and emerging technology. The fund invests from seed through Series C, with investments ranging from $500,000 to $10 million, allowing it to back businesses at different stages of their growth. Egypt is a core market for Nclude and a launchpad for businesses with the potential to scale across Africa and the Middle East. The fund also invests across the wider Africa region and the Middle East, with 30% of its mandate available for investment outside Egypt, backing businesses with the potential to expand between markets and build regional scale. To date, Nclude has invested in 15 companies across Africa and the Middle East. The portfolio includes: ● Nawy, the Egyptian proptech company that raised a $52 million Series A as it expands across MENA; ● Paymob, the Egyptian payments business with operations across the UAE and wider Gulf that raised $35 million in a pre-Series C round led by Mubadala and EBRD; ● FlapKap, a UAE-based fintech that raised $34 million in a pre-Series A round to support SME finance and GCC expansion; ● Money Fellows, which raised $13 million to support financial inclusion and expansion across North Africa, including Morocco; ● Kera, a health access AI company operating across Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire; ● Accord Partners, an AI roll-up venture focused on the accounting and auditing space with an immediate focus on Saudi Arabia and the broader MENA region. Ashley Lewis, Managing Partner and Head of DPI Venture Capital, said: “When we became adviser to Nclude, we took stewardship of an existing fund with a strong investment thesis, rooted in improving financial inclusion across Africa and the Middle East. We have grown a portfolio aligned with that central thesis and have built on those foundations by activating more of the fund’s mandate across the region. This has included expansion into themes such as affordable insurance and healthcare access, unlocking credit access for SMEs, and helping individuals save and invest for the future. At the same time, we have selectively broadened the fund’s investor base with additional strategically aligned LPs.” Lewis added: “At over $112 million, we believe Nclude is appropriately sized for today’s market, giving us the firepower to invest with discipline and support ambitious founders as they grow from strong local businesses into regional technology leaders.” Mohamed Aladdin, General Partner at DPI Venture Capital, said: “Across our portfolio, we are seeing ambitious technology businesses increasingly look beyond their home markets as they scale. The growing links between Africa and the Middle East create opportunities for companies to access new customers and markets, whether expanding from Egypt into the Gulf, across North Africa or into Egypt from elsewhere in the region. Companies including Nawy, Paymob, Money Fellows, and FlapKap demonstrate the potential to build regional technology leaders from these markets.” Sofiane Lahmar, Chief Executive Officer of Development Partners International, said: “As one of Africa’s leading investment firms, DPI has a long track record of backing high-growth African businesses through different stages of growth. By institutionalising venture capital as a core part of our platform, we can combine DPI Venture Capital’s specialist expertise with the networks, capabilities and investment experience of the wider firm. This strengthens our ability to support ambitious technology businesses as they scale across Africa and the Middle East and deliver strong returns for our investors while advancing financial inclusion across the region.”

articles.title: OpenAI prévoit d'acheter des puces TPU de Google, un affront à NVIDIA ?
articles.text:
OpenAI, l’un des plus importants clients de NVIDIA, regarde désormais du côté de Google pour s’approvisionner en puces. La firme de Mountain View place doucement ses pions pour grappiller des parts de marché, et ça marche.
OpenAI a constamment besoin de puissance de calcul supplémentaire pour alimenter ses très gourmands modèles. Et elle multiplie les pistes pour y parvenir : en juin, l’entreprise a dévoilé sa toute première puce maison conçue avec Broadcom et attendue en service d’ici la fin de l’année. En parallèle, elle a aussi ouvert ses modèles aux géants du cloud. Après Amazon Web Services (AWS), c’est Google Cloud qui les propose depuis la semaine dernière. Un premier signal.
Des puces taillées pour l’IA
Car selon The Information, OpenAI s’apprêterait à acheter des puces conçues par Google, et plus particulièrement des TPU, pour « Tensor Processing Units ». Contrairement aux GPU de NVIDIA, à l’origine pensés pour le graphisme, elles ont été taillées sur mesure pour l’intelligence artificielle (IA).
Le groupe les développe depuis plus de dix ans, d’abord pour accélérer son moteur de recherche, puis pour les calculs d’IA. Longtemps gardées pour un usage interne ou louées via son cloud, elles sont vendues directement à certains clients depuis avril, qui peuvent les installer dans leurs propres data centers.
Il s’agirait d’un réel virage pour OpenAI. Si elle a déjà loué des puces de Google en 2025, acheter est une autre affaire. D’autant que les liens entre les deux camps sont plus étroits qu’il n’y paraît : l’équipe chargée des puces d’OpenAI est dirigée par Richard Ho, un ancien de Google qui a travaillé sur les TPU.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code
Google monte en puissance
S’il s’agit d’un revers pour NVIDIA, ses GPU restent la référence absolue d’un marché qu’elle domine allègrement. En revanche, c’est une très bonne nouvelle pour le géant du Web : ses puces séduisent désormais les plus gros noms de l’IA, y compris ses concurrents directs. En février, Meta aurait signé en février un contrat de plusieurs milliards de dollars pour en louer, et discuterait d’en acheter dès 2027.
D’ailleurs, Oracle vient également d’annoncer qu’elle proposerait ces TPU à ses propres clients de cloud. La tendance est telle que les chercheurs de Google doivent patienter pour accéder aux processeurs.
Il lui faut désormais transformer l’essai. Alphabet s’attend à ne comptabiliser qu’une petite part des revenus liés aux TPU d’ici la fin de l’année, l’essentiel devant arriver en 2027. Mais il y a clairement une carte à jouer : les géants du cloud prévoient de dépenser jusqu’à 600 milliards de dollars cette année dans l’infrastructure IA.

articles.title: American Organizations Under Attack: Skyw4lker Device Code Phishing Campaign Exposed
articles.text:
Modern phishing campaigns can compromise American businesses without relying on traditional credential theft. Attackers can abuse legitimate cloud services, authentication mechanisms, and trusted business workflows to gain access to corporate accounts while leaving fewer obvious signs behind.
ANY.RUN's analysis of Skyw4lker, a device code phishing campaign primarily targeting U.S. organizations, shows how this works in practice. The campaign has focused on manufacturing, technology, and healthcare, using business-themed documents, Google-hosted infrastructure, and Microsoft authentication flows to facilitate account compromise.
For security teams, the investigation goes beyond identifying the initial lure. It requires tracing the authentication flow and supporting infrastructure, extracting reliable indicators, and turning those findings into detections that can protect the wider organization.
Device Code Phishing: A Growing Challenge for U.S. Organizations
The scale of phishing in the United States provides an important backdrop. The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center recorded 193,407 phishing and spoofing complaints in 2024, making it one of the most frequently reported categories of internet crime. In 2025, the FBI recorded more than 1 million internet crime complaints and $20.9 billion in reported losses, with reported losses increasing by 26% compared with the previous year.
Attackers are also adapting to organizations that have invested heavily in identity security and MFA.
Device code phishing is one example. Rather than collecting credentials through a fake login page, an attacker can initiate a legitimate device authorization flow and convince the victim to complete it. The resulting authentication tokens can then provide access to resources available to the compromised account.
How Skyw4lker Uses Legitimate Authentication to Compromise Accounts
How the Skyw4lker Campaign Works
Skyw4lker starts with a lure designed to resemble normal business correspondence, as observed in ANY.RUN’s Interactive Sandbox analysis.
| The Skyw4lker phishing kit identified in ANY.RUN’s Interactive Sandbox | 
Victims receive a password-protected document presented as a contract or service proposal. The scenario is credible in environments where employees routinely exchange vendor agreements, procurement documents, statements of work, and similar files.
From the document, the victim is directed toward a page hosted on sites[.]google[.]com, which eventually leads into a Microsoft authentication flow.
| Skyw4lker redirecting the victims to a Microsoft365 authentication page | 
The attacker does not need to reproduce Microsoft's login experience perfectly. The authentication itself can be legitimate; the deception is in convincing the victim to complete an authentication request initiated by the attacker.
Once the process is completed, the attacker can obtain access to the resulting Microsoft 365 tokens.
That makes the attack difficult to evaluate through identity telemetry alone. An organization may see a valid authentication event without immediately seeing the malicious context that caused it. Establishing what happened requires the security team to connect the document, web activity, authentication flow, and associated infrastructure.
The Infrastructure Behind the Skyw4lker Phishing Page
The web infrastructure used by Skyw4lker provides additional evidence of the campaign's operation.
ANY.RUN’s analysis identified obfuscated JavaScript and a PHP backend used to create a victim session, collect information such as IP address and geolocation, and repeatedly poll the backend while waiting for the authentication process to complete.
| Skyw4lker sample submissions in ANY.RUN’s Interactive Sandbox by country | 
A static inspection of the original document may reveal the starting URL, but it cannot fully explain what happens once the victim interacts with the page. The malicious behavior emerges through the combination of browser activity, JavaScript execution, backend communication, redirects, and authentication.
That makes behavioral analysis essential when the objective is to establish exactly what a phishing campaign is doing and which indicators can be trusted for follow-up detection.
View the Skyw4lker analysis in ANY.RUN’s Interactive Sandbox to see its complete attack chain and associated IOCs.
Reduce Tier 1 workload by up to 20% and give analysts more time to focus on critical threats.
Interactive Sandboxing Turns Suspicious Files and URLs into Actionable Evidence
An interactive sandbox lets security teams safely execute and interact with suspicious files, links, and documents, revealing behavior that static inspection can miss.
That matters in campaigns such as Skyw4lker, where the document is only the starting point. Analysts need to follow the attack through the browser, observe redirects and authentication activity, inspect network communication, and identify the infrastructure behind the phishing flow. All of this can be done in an isolated ANY.RUN Sandbox environment, with a result available in as little as 40 seconds.
| The Tier 1 report for the observed Skyw4lker sample available in ANY.RUN’s sandbox | 
Instead of stopping at a malicious/benign verdict, the investigation can produce URLs, domains, IP addresses, network activity, screenshots, behavioral evidence, and other IOCs. These findings give security teams the context needed to validate an alert, scope-related activity, and create detections from evidence gathered during a single investigation.
As a result, SOC and MSSP teams can reach a confident verdict faster without manually reproducing the attack across multiple tools, while the resulting intelligence can support threat hunting and detection across the wider environment. Moreover, the same workflow makes it easier for MSSPs to investigate new campaigns and turn findings from one customer case into intelligence that can be searched across other environments.
Turning Threat Intel into Earlier Detection
The value of an IOC increases when it can be used to detect another attack.
ANY.RUN Threat Intelligence Feeds (TI Feeds) provide malicious IPs, domains, URLs, and contextual information derived from sandbox investigations. 99% of unique, high-confidence IOCs are added to TI Feeds after validation, helping security teams work with intelligence that has already been reviewed.
| ANY.RUN TI Feeds provide live threat intelligence for real-time attack detection | 
ANY.RUN’s internal analysis found that up to 30% of unique malicious IOCs discovered in Interactive Sandbox sessions had already been observed by the company and were present in TI Feeds. When one of these indicators appears in customer telemetry, it can potentially be matched against existing intelligence before an analyst manually investigates the associated sample.
This creates a more efficient workflow: known malicious activity can be identified earlier, while sandbox analysis provides the behavioral evidence needed to investigate unfamiliar threats.
For internal SOCs, this can reduce time spent researching indicators that are already known to be malicious. For MSSPs, the same intelligence can help identify related activity across multiple customer environments. This is how the existing threat knowledge can be reused instead of reconstructed for every new alert.
Cut MTTR by 21 minutes and give your SOC more time to focus on critical threats.
Threat Intelligence Provides Context Behind the Alert
An indicator becomes more useful when security teams can understand the activity surrounding it.
ANY.RUN’s Threat Intelligence Lookup (TI Lookup) allows analysts to investigate a suspicious domain, IP address, or URL and examine its history and associated activity. In a Skyw4lker-related investigation, this context can help determine whether an indicator is connected to the campaign, has appeared in other malicious activity, or requires further investigation.
In addition, ANY.RUN’s Threat Intelligence Reports (TI Reports) provide a broader perspective by connecting indicators with campaigns, infrastructure, techniques, and observed behavior. This can reveal relationships that are difficult to see from individual alerts, such as multiple incidents sharing the same infrastructure or a suspicious domain belonging to a wider phishing operation.
When it comes to organizations in U.S. healthcare, manufacturing, and technology, those connections can be especially important. A compromised Microsoft 365 account can expose sensitive communications, intellectual property, operational information, and regulated data, making early identification of related activity critical.
How to Make Each SOC and MSSP Investigation More Valuable
A successful investigation should improve an organization's ability to detect the next attack.
For an MSSP investigating a suspicious contract sent to one American manufacturing customer, indicators associated with Skyw4lker can be searched across other customer environments and incorporated into monitoring. The same approach works within an internal SOC environment, where an IOC found after one employee reports a phishing document can be compared against historical telemetry to identify other potentially affected users.
ANY.RUN supports these workflows through API/SDK, STIX/TAXII, SIEM, TIP, and XDR integrations, allowing intelligence from investigations to feed into existing detection and monitoring processes.
The result is broader protection from the same investigation: an incident affecting one user can generate intelligence that helps identify related activity across a SOC or MSSP's wider customer base.
Uncover up to 58% more threats and gain broader visibility into emerging attacks.
Conclusion
Skyw4lker shows why modern phishing defense requires visibility beyond the initial lure or login page. By combining interactive sandboxing, threat intelligence, and contextual investigation, security teams can move faster from suspicious artifact to actionable intelligence and broader detection.
For organizations in the U.S., that means faster investigations, less repetitive manual work, and a better ability to identify related activity before it becomes a larger incident. The goal is not only to understand one attack, but to turn every investigation into protection against the next one.

articles.title: GTA 6 Tipped to Be a 210 GB Download on PS5
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
GTA 6 Tipped to Be a 210 GB Download on PS5
GTA 6 could take up around 210 GB on PlayStation 5, according to PlayStation Game Size, an X account that pulls data from the PlayStation Store backend. The same post lists the $79.99 Standard Edition, pre-loading from November 12, and a midnight release on November 19. Insider Gaming has reportedly corroborated the figure. However, Rockstar hasn't confirmed anything yet, so it's best to treat 210 GB as a rough estimate for now. It's also unclear whether that's the download alone or the full install footprint, and a day-one patch could push it higher. If accurate, that's a big chunk of a base PS5's storage. 
The original 825 GB model leaves roughly 667 GB for games, so GTA 6 alone would eat close to a third of it. Physical buyers aren't spared either, since the boxed edition ships with a download code instead of a disc. The Xbox Series X|S size hasn't surfaced yet. Interestingly, an earlier claim tied to leaker Cyberleek, who has threatened to release a playable build, put the game's development build at over 200 GB, though dev builds usually carry a lot of extra baggage. The PC version is reportedly due in Q1 2027, so PC players have some time before this becomes their problem. Console players, on the other hand, are advised to clear space or look into an M.2 expansion before pre-loading opens on November 12.

articles.title: 'We analyzed 119 million ear data points' — how Samsung builtGalaxy Buds Open, its first open-type earbuds
articles.text:
'We analyzed 119 million ear data points' — how Samsung built Galaxy Buds Open, its first open-type earbuds
Finding the fit that balances audio and awareness
- Samsung unveils its first open-ear buds
- Galaxy Buds Open feature twin drivers for open adaptive listening
- 9.5 hours of battery life
Staying connected to the real world is the hot new thing, or so it seems if you've been paying attention to the parade of new clip-on (or cuff-style) open earbuds arriving from Sony, Anker, and Bose, to name a few. The solution is so good when done well that you'll regularly see these buds occupying a healthy chunk of our best open earbuds buying guide. And now Samsung is joining the trend with its first pair: Galaxy Buds Open.
Unlike over-the-ear headphones or in-ear buds, open-ear options must deliver quality sound without the benefit of an audio seal betwixt your ear canal and the buds' driver housings, and all while not making you feel like you're wearing too-heavy ear cuffs (each earpiece here weighs 6.65g). As a Samsung exec told us, "Designing these buds is a complex challenge because of the unique anatomy of ears and the difficulty to find the perfect balance between a secure fit and a comfortable fit."
Part of that is acknowledging that every ear is different. Samsung told us it used AI and "analyzed 119 million ear data points to find the optimal fit for the widest range of users possible." Engineers used that information to optimize the components, including wire length, weight, bridge length, battery, speaker placement, and to select an alloy that flexes for the clip-on components but also stays secure. Samsung claims you could almost forget you're wearing them.
The sound of things
Samsung sounds confident in the fit, but it also had to do some fairly complex audio engineering to make these open earbuds capable of delivering high-quality audio that doesn't leak out to the person next to you.
One of the most interesting aspects of this audio design is the TwinBoost drivers that can be used to both enhance the open-ear audio quality and cut down on audio leakage. The way it works is the open earbuds project "matching reverse soundwaves" from the rear of the speaker, which could cancel out some of the escaping audio. It's a claim we obviously can't confirm until we test the Galaxy Buds Open. This is essentially like active noise cancellation, which these buds lack, but instead of the buds creating antiphase sound waves to counteract the noise leaking into your ears, it uses counteracting sounds to cut down on noise leaking from the speakers near your ears.
Galaxy Buds Open can't seal you off from outside sounds; in fact, they're designed not to, but they can help keep your calls clear. To manage call quality, the earbuds include three mics and a "voice pickup unit". Samsung claims the Galaxy Buds Open capture your voice through the mics and even "jaw movement" to help isolate your voice from other external noises. For those sounds that are not blocked by these audio features, Samsung added some machine learning to automatically cancel out recognized noises such as car horns and construction work.
The buds also support head gestures for accepting and rejecting calls, Gemini access, and Quick Voice Memos. More impressively, Samsung is rating the Galaxy Buds Open for 9.5 hours of audio playback and, with the charge case, a total of 38 hours of battery life. Battery life with calls is 5.5 hours and 25 hours with the charging cradle.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Galaxy Buds Open, which are only available in black, list for $229 (AU and UK pricing were unavailable at the time of writing) and in early November. That price puts them a touch cheaper than the excellent (and also noise-reducing) Shokz Openfit Pro, at $249, and makes them quite a bit more affordable than Bose Ultra Open ($299).
We'll have more to say about the actual fit, audio quality, external noise cancellation, and battery life when we get a chance to test out the new Galaxy Buds Open. But things are looking good on paper.

articles.title: Escritores de Stanford demandaron a Anthropic por usar sus libros pirateados para entrenar a Claude
articles.text:
Dos escritores de la Universidad de Stanford, Tobias Wolff y Chang-rae Lee, demandaron a Anthropic en mayo de 2026 por usar sus libros, descargados de bibliotecas piratas, para entrenar a Claude. Rechazaron el acuerdo colectivo de USD 1.500 millones y piden un juicio con jurado, según informó el diario universitario The Stanford Daily.
La demanda, llamada Cruz contra Anthropic, reclama el máximo legal de USD 150.000 por obra infringida. El acuerdo colectivo ofrecía unos USD 3.000 por obra. Los demandantes también piden una orden permanente que impida a Anthropic entrenar sus modelos con esos libros.
Wolff, profesor emérito de Inglés y ganador de la Medalla Nacional de las Artes, dice que diez de sus publicaciones se usaron sin permiso. Según The Stanford Daily, otros autores de la universidad cuyas obras se habrían usado son Abraham Verghese, Daniel Mason, Hayagreeva Rao y Myra Strober.
Qué decidió el juez y qué todavía no
La prensa internacional ha señalado que Anthropic entrenó a Claude de forma ilegal y que un juez así lo dictaminó. Los documentos judiciales citados por Reuters muestran un cuadro más matizado. El caso Cruz no tiene sentencia: lo que existe son acusaciones de los autores, que Anthropic no ha sido declarada culpable de ninguna en esa causa.
El fallo que sí existe es de otro caso, Bartz contra Anthropic. En junio de 2025, el juez William Alsup resolvió que entrenar a Claude con libros fue uso legítimo. Pero también dictaminó que copiar y guardar más de 7 millones de libros pirateados en una biblioteca central infringió los derechos de los autores.
Ese caso terminó en un acuerdo de USD 1.500 millones, el mayor conocido en un caso de derechos de autor en Estados Unidos. La jueza Araceli Martínez-Olguín lo aprobó de forma definitiva el 20 de julio de 2026, informó Reuters, que precisó que algunos autores y editoriales se excluyeron y siguen con causas separadas.
Autores que dicen que el acuerdo no alcanza
El acuerdo cubre a autores y editoriales de casi 500.000 obras registradas. Según The Stanford Daily, Wolff y otros 27 autores consideran que el monto es insuficiente. Cruz plantea que Anthropic descargó, reprodujo y distribuyó sus libros desde las bibliotecas clandestinas LibGen y PiLiMi, y que los almacenó en una biblioteca central.
“Poner mi trabajo a producir así, sin remuneración, es una forma de trabajo esclavo”, dijo Wolff al diario. También afirmó que el acuerdo “sigue dando a Anthropic bastante libertad” para tomar de la literatura lo que le resulte útil y rentable.
Paul Goldstein, especialista en propiedad intelectual de la Facultad de Derecho de Stanford y uno de los demandantes de la causa colectiva, planteó el problema desde otro lado. En un correo al diario, escribió que obtener licencias para millones de obras copiadas en un entrenamiento es “imposible en la práctica” para una plataforma.
Más de 70 demandas y una ley en discusión
Fuera de Bartz y Cruz, autores, artistas visuales y medios como The New York Times y Getty Images presentaron más de 70 demandas por infracción contra empresas de IA, según el diario universitario. El futuro legal del rastreo masivo de contenido para entrenar modelos de lenguaje sigue sin definirse.
La directora ejecutiva del gremio Authors Guild, Mary Rasenberger, dijo al diario que la organización impulsa otras demandas, entre ellas una contra OpenAI y Microsoft, y trabaja con el Congreso de Estados Unidos en una ley que obligue a licenciar los libros usados. El diario no informó una fecha para el juicio de Cruz.
El conflicto deja expuesta una tensión que la expansión de la inteligencia artificial todavía no ha resuelto: mientras las empresas sostienen que el entrenamiento de modelos requiere cantidades masivas de información, autores y editoriales reclaman control y remuneración por obras que forman parte de ese proceso.

articles.title: Anthropic's Unreleased AI Model Chains Flaws Into Working Chrome, Safari, Windows and Linux Exploits
articles.text:
An unreleased Anthropic AI model found security flaws in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux and chained them into working proof-of-concept exploits, the company said in its latest report.
The exploits were built in the lab after the model was prompted, not seen in any real attack, and Anthropic reported every flaw to the vendor first, so all of them are already patched. One proof of concept opened the Calculator app on a stock Mac running Chrome within seconds of a page loading, with no further clicks.
Anthropic's Frontier Red Team described five chains in a research post. The strongest claim is not any single bug, but that one model found several separate flaws and combined them into a working exploit, something the company says has until now been the work of a few specialist teams. That capability claim rests on Anthropic's own account.
The patches and the fact that Apple and Google credit Anthropic and its Claude model for specific fixes can be verified with the vendors.
What a reader cannot check is how much of each chain the model built on its own. Anthropic says the work needed only "initial prompting" and "little human involvement," but it does not break down what a person did at each step, and it does not name the model beyond calling it an unreleased, internal research model.
For the one flaw with its own public record, the Windows bug, the record names no finder at all. Here are the five chains, what each would do, the condition each needs, and where the fix landed.
| Platform | What the exploit does | Condition it needs | Fix | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Chrome | Runs code on the computer, outside the browser's sandbox, from one visit to a web page | One click or page load, stock Chrome on macOS | Chrome 156, October 20 | 
| Safari | Lets any website read data from other sites the user is signed in to, such as email or a bank account | One visit to a malicious page | iOS and iPadOS 26.5.2, June 29 | 
| Android | Copies photos and other data off a locked, stolen phone | Physical access to the phone, over USB | Anthropic says Google has fixed it; no public record was found | 
| Windows | Crashes a server over the network, and keeps it down by repeating | The server answers HTTP/3 requests | CVE-2026-33096, patched April 2026 | 
| Linux | Runs commands as root over the network, with no login and no user action | The server runs a multipath TCP listener | CVE-2026-98432, patched October 15 | 
In the Chrome chain, the model used four separate flaws in turn. A malicious page first corrupted memory in V8, Chrome's JavaScript engine.
A second flaw escaped V8's memory sandbox and took control of the part of Chrome that renders the page. A race condition in a feature called CacheStorage then let that code read memory it should not reach and learn the layout of the more privileged browser process.
A final use-after-free bug in FedCM, Chrome's sign-in feature, let the exploit run code outside the sandbox entirely. Anthropic says it reported 62 flaws to Google that were assigned CVEs and fixed as of Chrome 156, all rated critical or high, including 13 sandbox escapes.
Google's own release notes credit "Xinyang Ge of Anthropic, assisted by Claude" for specific Chrome fixes, though not for all 62.
The Safari chain is different because it never runs code at all. It chains flaws to obtain full read and write access to the browser's memory, then changes a single value to turn off the same-origin policy, the rule that prevents one website from reading another's data.
With that rule off, a malicious page can read a user's history and cookies and send signed-in requests to other sites. Apple fixed the use-after-free at the center of the chain in iOS and iPadOS 26.5.2 and credits "Milad Nasr and Nicholas Carlini with Claude, Anthropic" for it.
The Windows chain is the one with an independent paper trail, and it is also the narrowest. It is a denial-of-service attack: a few network packets crash the machine, and repeating them keeps it down, but it does not run code or steal data. Anthropic describes the flaw as an out-of-bounds read in the Windows kernel's QUIC handling.
The public record for the bug it points to, CVE-2026-33096, instead names HTTP.sys, Windows' built-in web request handler, and rates it 7.5 out of 10. No open source ties those two descriptions together as the same component. The CVE record credits no finder, so Anthropic's authorship of this one rests on its own post.
As of late October, the U.S. government's vulnerability enrichment marked the flaw as not exploited, and it was not in the CISA catalog of known exploited bugs.
The Linux chain is the most serious in terms of impact: it runs commands as root over the network without a login. It needs the target server to be running a multipath TCP listener. The model first leaks a kernel memory address to bypass a defense called KASLR, then reuses the same race-condition bug to redirect the program to code the attacker has already placed, resulting in a root shell.
Anthropic says its proof of concept took 48 minutes to leak the address and five more to reach the shell, and that a failed attempt does not crash the system, so an attacker can keep retrying.
The company ties this chain to CVE-2026-98432, a kernel use-after-free rated 9.8 and fixed upstream on October 15; the public record for that CVE describes an IPv4 TCP fix rather than a multipath TCP one, and the two are linked only by Anthropic's post.
Anthropic frames the work as help for defenders. It says it reported each flaw under a coordinated disclosure policy that gives developers 90 days to patch and 45 more before it discusses details beyond a public advisory, and it points security teams to its expanded Cyber Verification Program, which gives vetted professionals access to Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Mythos 5.1.
The reason the company gives for publishing is in its own words: "Now, it's something models can do with little human involvement, and then prove by producing a working exploit that anyone can run and verify."

articles.title: Amazon’s new Echo Show 16 feels like the future of Alexa, with a slimmer design and a smarter interface
articles.text:
Amazon’s new Echo Show 16 has a thinner design, a better screen, and a clever new way to organize Alexa conversations
It's pricey, though
- Amazon’s new Echo Show 16 starts at $499.99 and boasts a fresh design
- Alexa+ gets a redesigned interface with interactive Cards
- You can even get the 16-inch smart display with a NanoMatte finish
Amazon’s new Echo Show 16 looks like a big step forward for its smart displays. With a slimmer design, upgraded audio, and a redesigned Alexa+ interface, it feels like Amazon’s hardware and software are finally working in tandem.
It has a thinner, more modern look, almost mimicking that of an iMac, with a brighter, more vibrant display that can be treated with the special anti-glare NanoMatte coating. It also boasts a redesigned interface that feels tailor-made for the larger screen.
At $499.99 with a standard display and $579.99 with NanoMatte, the new Echo Show 16 is very much a premium smart display. It’s also only available in the United States for now and is up for preorder ahead of a mid-December launch. You can also save by preordering, with $100 off either finish.
Like the refreshed Echo Show 8 and Echo Show 11, this Echo Show 16 feels like Amazon’s device design team, led by Panos Panay, has hit its stride. I only spent a handful of minutes with it, but I can already see that the design and software are working in tandem, and this could be the template for future Echo Show smart displays.
Amazon has redesigned the entire build, including the internals, from the ground up, packing everything into an anodized aluminum frame that’s 40% slimmer than that of the Echo Show 15 or 21. The audio team has also built out eight custom micro-woofers on the sides and two tweeters for robust audio. In the demo space, it got pretty loud with no noticeable muddiness. It can also adjust playback in real time using the onboard microphones, sensors, and custom algorithms to ensure sound stays clear.
There are four microphones as well, so Alexa can clearly hear you when you make queries, but they also help if you’re on a video call, letting whoever you’re speaking to hear you without extra background noise. Two forward-facing microphones sit next to the wide-angle 13MP camera, and two are on the rear.
The 16-inch display is Full HD, and I’m especially loving the NanoMatte finish, particularly for a device that might be wall-mounted or used with the separately sold swivel stand. Either way, it could be exposed to varying degrees of natural sunlight, and glare can be an issue with smart displays.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Of course, Alexa — specifically Alexa+ — is central to this, and the Show 16’s new Cards, which organize your conversations with the assistant, offer a new way to interact with and revisit those conversations. Panos described the interface as a combination of user interface and AI, and explained how the two work together.
When you open a Card from a previous Alexa conversation, you’re presented with the original prompt, condensed, alongside jumping-off points on the right and more detailed information next to it. You can easily tap on those suggestions or pull up the original conversation. Alexa's new conversation design is also reminiscent of how conversations are organized in the Siri app. The new look is also rolling out to the Alexa mobile app.
The whole interface feels a bit cleaner, and you can finally choose between different Screen Styles for the Echo Show 16. These include a Family Organizer for calendars and family plans, a Smart Home view for controlling connected devices — think the Echo Hub on steroids — and a Photos option that turns the display into a digital picture frame.
A more focused Echo Show
After spending a little time with the Echo Show 16, I came away most impressed by the cohesive feel of the hardware and software. The slimmer frame, more capable audio setup, NanoMatte display option, and redesigned Alexa+ experience all serve the same goal: making a large smart display more useful in the home.
The new Cards could be particularly interesting as Alexa+ becomes more capable, giving conversations a life beyond the moment you ask a question. And with Screen Styles that cater to different household needs, the Echo Show 16 feels less like a screen that simply sits on a counter or wall and more like a hub for organizing your home.
I’ll need to spend more time with it to see how well those features work in everyday use, but my first impression is that Amazon has made a more considered, cohesive smart display. If the new Alexa+ experience delivers on its promise, the Echo Show 16 could be one of the more compelling examples of where Amazon wants its smart home devices to go next.

articles.title: Palit Denies GALAX GPU Factory Closure, Continues Business as Usual
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Palit Denies GALAX GPU Factory Closure, Continues Business as Usual
Palit issued a statement today to address and dismiss current industry rumors that GALAX GPU factories are winding down. The rumor suggested that GALAX and its European-focused KFA2 brand were experiencing supply issues with NVIDIA. However, Palit has clarified that these reports are inaccurate. As one of NVIDIA's largest add-in card partners, Palit sells a significant volume through its brands. The speculation that GALAX factories are shutting down due to supply problems with NVIDIA would imply a risk to NVIDIA's entire business with its AIC partners, which doesn't make much sense. Palit explained that since Palit and GALAX are now operating under one roof, they share some manufacturing facilities, and GALAX products continue to be sold.
Palit has also confirmed that the company is developing next-generation GALAX Hall-of-Fame (HOF) graphics cards, along with regular GALAX and KFA2-branded GPU models. While the current generation of GPUs remains available, the mention of next-generation GPUs in development is particularly intriguing. This indicates that the upcoming NVIDIA GeForce RTX 60-Series "Rubin" gaming GPUs will also be available in GALAX HOF and KFA2 variants, providing extreme overclockers with more HOF generations in the future.
PalitWe are aware of recent reports and speculation regarding GALAX's business operations. We would like to clarify that these claims are inaccurate.
GALAX continues to operate as usual. No manufacturing facilities have been shut down, and GALAX products remain available through our sales channels in both domestic and international markets.
As part of the same group, GALAX and Palit share manufacturing facilities, with production and business operations continuing as normal.
We remain fully committed to delivering high-quality products and supporting our customers, partners, and the global community.
For any further inquiries or clarification, please contact us at info@galaxytech.com.
We sincerely appreciate your continued trust and support.

Un peu plus d’un mois après leur sortie, la version la plus complète des écouteurs ouverts d’Apple tombe presque au prix du modèle de base. Amazon affiche les AirPods 5 avec boîtier de charge sans fil à 149,95 € au lieu de 169 €, un modèle noté 8/10 dans notre test, mais pensé avant tout pour l’iPhone.
Lancés le 18 septembre, les AirPods 5 reprennent la silhouette des AirPods 4 et étendent la réduction de bruit active à toute la gamme. Apple les décline en deux versions : 149 € pour le modèle standard, 169 € pour celui doté d’un boîtier de charge sans fil, d’un réglage du volume par balayage de la tige et d’une heure d’autonomie en plus.
Amazon vend cette seconde version à 149,95 € au lieu de 169 €, soit 11 % de remise et 19,05 € d’économie sur le prix conseillé. Elle s’adresse aux possesseurs d’iPhone que les embouts en silicone fatiguent, mais qui veulent atténuer le bruit ambiant.
Les Apple AirPods 5 avec boîtier de charge sans fil passent à 149,95 € chez Amazon, contre 169 € au prix conseillé, soit 19,05 € de moins sur la version la plus complète.
Pourquoi choisir les Apple AirPods 5 ?
- Une réduction de bruit en net progrès : Apple annonce jusqu’à 50 % de bruit éliminé en plus par rapport aux AirPods 4. Dans notre test, le gain s’entend surtout sur les voix graves et les bas-médiums.
- Le confort d’un écouteur ouvert : Sans embout à enfoncer dans le conduit auditif, ils se font oublier pendant des heures, un confort que nous avons jugé exemplaire. Écouteurs et boîtier sont par ailleurs certifiés IP57, contre IP54 pour les AirPods 4.
- Les atouts propres à cette version : Le boîtier se recharge sans fil et le volume se règle d’un glissement du doigt sur la tige. L’autonomie passe à 5 heures avec réduction de bruit, contre 4 heures pour le modèle standard.
Dans les transports, au bureau, en appel : ce qu’ils changent au quotidien
Le format ouvert laisse passer une partie de l’environnement, mais l’audio adaptatif dose désormais transparence et réduction de bruit selon le niveau sonore. Dans notre test des Apple AirPods 5, nous avons mesuré 5 h 30 d’écoute avec la réduction de bruit active, un peu plus que les 5 heures annoncées, et Apple promet jusqu’à 22 heures avec le boîtier. En appel, la captation de la voix se situe clairement dans le haut du panier, avec des bruits de fond bien atténués.
Ils vous conviendront si vous enchaînez trajets, open space et visioconférences avec un iPhone. Les fonctions récentes, comme la traduction en direct via Apple Intelligence ou le contrôle de Siri par des mouvements de tête, restent liées à l’écosystème Apple. Sur Android, ils assurent le service minimum : pas de multipoint, pas de codec avancé, pas d’appairage rapide Fast Pair. En avion, les très basses fréquences et les aigus traversent toujours la réduction de bruit.
Version standard, AirPods Pro 3 : où se situent-ils ?
Face à la version standard, vendue 149 € au prix officiel, l’arbitrage devient simple : moins d’un euro d’écart pour la charge sans fil, le réglage du volume sur la tige et une heure d’autonomie de plus. Si l’isolation prime, les AirPods Pro 3 restent techniquement supérieurs grâce à leur format intra, comme le relève notre test. Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs écouteurs sans fil, la génération précédente tient déjà la place des meilleurs écouteurs ouverts.
✅ Les points forts
- Réduction de bruit plus efficace sur les voix et les bas-médiums
- Confort exemplaire, sans embout intra-auriculaire
- Qualité d’appel dans le haut du panier
- Écouteurs et boîtier certifiés IP57
- Charge sans fil et volume réglable sur la tige
❌ Les limites
- Très basses fréquences et aigus encore mal filtrés
- Autonomie moyenne de 5 heures par charge avec réduction de bruit
- Service minimum sur Android, sans multipoint ni Fast Pair
- Imprécisions persistantes dans les extrêmes du spectre
Avant de valider, vérifiez sur la fiche Amazon qu’il s’agit bien du modèle avec boîtier de charge sans fil, affiché à 149,95 € au lieu de 169 €.
À 149,95 €, les AirPods 5 avec boîtier de charge sans fil coûtent 19,05 € de moins que leur prix conseillé, une remise modeste qui change pourtant l’arbitrage dans la gamme. Pour à peine plus que le prix officiel du modèle standard, vous obtenez la version complète, celle que nous avons testée et notée 8/10. Sans révolution face aux AirPods 4, ils progressent sur la réduction de bruit, le son et la résistance à l’eau.
Si vous utilisez un iPhone et que les intra vous fatiguent, cette offre mérite votre attention. Sur Android, vous paierez des fonctions inaccessibles : un modèle compatible Fast Pair et multipoint vous servira mieux. Pour le silence dans le métro ou en avion, les AirPods Pro 3 et leur format intra restent plus cohérents.

articles.title: Cómo dominar el algoritmo de Instagram y multiplicar su alcance
articles.text:
Instagram no funciona con un único algoritmo, sino con un conjunto de clasificadores que evalúan el contenido de forma distinta según la sección de la aplicación donde aparece. Dominar su funcionamiento exige abandonar la búsqueda de trucos puntuales y comprender un objetivo de fondo: la plataforma mide y recompensa todo aquello que mantiene al usuario dentro de la app el mayor tiempo posible.
A partir de esa lógica se puede construir una estrategia de contenido que multiplique el alcance real, basada en jerarquías de interacción, optimización de búsqueda y estructuras de video pensadas para la retención.
Cómo funciona el algoritmo de Instagram en cada sección
El comportamiento del usuario cambia según dónde navega, y por eso cada sección aplica reglas propias de clasificación. En el Feed y en las Historias, el sistema prioriza contenido de cuentas que ya se siguen y predice cinco acciones: el tiempo que alguien se detiene a mirar una publicación, si comenta, si da “me gusta”, si la comparte o si toca la foto de perfil.
La cercanía previa con una cuenta, medida a través de mensajes directos o búsquedas anteriores, pesa de manera considerable en esa predicción.
La sección Explorar responde a una lógica distinta, orientada al descubrimiento. Ahí Instagram muestra contenido de cuentas que el usuario no sigue, apoyándose en sus interacciones pasadas y en la velocidad con la que una publicación acumula interacciones apenas se publica.
Reels, por su parte, concentra la disputa por la atención masiva. La métrica decisiva es la tasa de finalización del video, es decir, si se reproduce hasta el final, junto con señales como el ingreso a la página del audio original para crear un clip propio o el envío del video por mensaje directo.
En síntesis, dominar el algoritmo de Instagram implica entender que no existe una fórmula única: el Feed premia la fidelidad con la audiencia propia, Explorar recompensa la popularidad inicial entre públicos nuevos y Reels exige retención completa del video para competir por alcance global.
Qué interacciones valen más para el algoritmo
No todas las acciones del usuario tienen el mismo peso dentro del sistema. Los compartidos, ya sea por mensaje directo o hacia Historias, constituyen la señal más fuerte, porque indican que alguien considera el contenido lo bastante relevante como para asociarse a él frente a su círculo social.
Los guardados ocupan el segundo lugar en la jerarquía. Esta acción suele asociarse a tutoriales, listas o contenido de inspiración, piezas que el usuario quiere conservar para revisar más adelante.
El tiempo de retención y las reproducciones completas también entran en la clasificación como señales de calidad. Un usuario que se detiene a leer un pie de foto extenso o que recorre un carrusel completo está enviando una señal de interés profundo, distinta a una reacción superficial.
Los comentarios generan comunidad y alargan la permanencia sobre una publicación, por lo que también suman valor. En el extremo opuesto se ubica el “me gusta”, la interacción de menor peso actual debido a la facilidad con la que se ejecuta sin un consumo real del contenido.
Estrategias de contenido para multiplicar el alcance en Instagram
Entender esta jerarquía permite diseñar publicaciones de forma deliberada. En lugar de pedir “me gusta”, conviene construir piezas que empujen al usuario hacia compartidos y guardados: los carruseles educativos que fragmentan información compleja en varias diapositivas aumentan el tiempo de pantalla y las guardas.
En tanto, los Reels con ganchos visuales de humor, opinión o situaciones cotidianas generan la reacción de enviarlo a otra persona porque “esto me representa”.
La estructura del video también determina el alcance en Reels. Los primeros tres segundos son determinantes: un texto en pantalla, un cambio de plano rápido o una afirmación intrigante evitan que el usuario deslice de inmediato.
Diseñar el final para que conecte de forma fluida con el inicio provoca reproducciones repetidas sin que el usuario lo note, lo que favorece la tasa de finalización.
La originalidad del material es otro factor determinante. El algoritmo reduce el alcance en Explorar y en Reels cuando detecta marcas de agua de otras plataformas, videos de baja calidad visual o contenido resubido por cuentas agregadoras.
SEO en Instagram: palabras clave y texto para posicionar contenido
Instagram se ha convertido progresivamente en un motor de búsqueda, y ese cambio exige tratar el perfil y las publicaciones con criterios de posicionamiento. Incluir palabras clave exactas en el nombre de usuario y en la biografía ayuda a que la cuenta aparezca en búsquedas relacionadas con su temática.
Los pies de foto cumplen una función similar: un texto rico en palabras clave naturales permite que el sistema identifique de qué trata la publicación y la recomiende en Explorar. A esto se suman los subtítulos integrados en los videos y el texto alternativo en las imágenes, elementos que refuerzan la categorización del contenido.
El papel de las Historias en el alcance del Feed
Las Historias no generan alcance nuevo por sí mismas, pero funcionan como alimento del algoritmo del Feed. Cuando un seguidor responde una encuesta, reacciona o envía un mensaje directo a partir de una Historia, el sistema interpreta esa interacción como una señal de relación activa y posiciona la siguiente publicación de esa cuenta en un lugar más visible del Feed de ese usuario.
Mantener una presencia diaria en Historias se convierte así en una herramienta para sostener lo que podría describirse como una puntuación de relación alta con la audiencia existente, un factor que incide directamente en el rendimiento de los Posts y Reels posteriores.

articles.title: Un écran de 12,7 pouces à 144 Hz : la Lenovo Idea Tab Pro de 256 Go est à 349,99 €
articles.text:
La tablette Lenovo Idea Tab Pro de 12,7 pouces et 256 Go est à 349,99 € (-30 %)
La Lenovo Idea Tab Pro associe un grand écran LCD à 144 Hz, une puce Dimensity 8300 et 256 Go de stockage pour le multimédia et le multitâche.
Boulanger propose la tablette Lenovo Idea Tab Pro de 256 Go à 349,99 €, contre un prix de référence affiché de 499,99 €. L’économie atteint 150 €, soit 30 %. Il s’agit d’un produit neuf vendu et expédié par Boulanger.
Un grand écran et des performances solides
La tablette Lenovo Idea Tab Pro possède un écran LCD de 12,7 pouces affichant 2 944 × 1 840 pixels, jusqu’à 144 Hz. Sa puce MediaTek Dimensity 8300 est accompagnée de 8 Go de mémoire vive. Le stockage peut être complété par une carte microSD.
Lors de notre test, nous avons apprécié sa réactivité et ses performances en multitâche. Les jeux les plus exigeants peuvent toutefois demander des concessions graphiques. Son écran manque aussi de luminosité et reste sensible aux reflets : un usage en intérieur lui convient davantage.
Une autonomie convaincante, un suivi logiciel limité
Nous avons mesuré 18 h 43 min d’autonomie selon notre protocole d’usage mixte. La batterie de 10 200 mAh accepte la recharge jusqu’à 45 W, mais le chargeur secteur n’est pas fourni.
Le suivi logiciel figure parmi les limites relevées dans notre test : Lenovo annonçait des mises à jour système jusqu’à Android 16 et quatre ans de correctifs de sécurité. Un point à considérer pour un achat destiné à durer.

articles.title: Ajman Chamber prepares to launch Thara initiative for entrepreneurs and investors
articles.text: Ajman Chamber will launch the Thara Investment and Entrepreneurship Ecosystem on October 29, 2026, during the inaugural Thara Connect Forum at the Thara Entrepreneurship Centre in Ajman. The initiative aims to develop an integrated ecosystem supporting entrepreneurs and startups at different stages of growth, while facilitating investment opportunities and partnerships between emerging businesses and investors. Held under the patronage of Sheikh Humaid bin Rashid Al Nuaimi, Ruler of Ajman, the forum will bring together investors, business leaders, entrepreneurs and industry experts from the UAE and international markets. The event will feature panel discussions, networking sessions and a startup exhibition, alongside the unveiling of Thara's initiatives and services designed to support entrepreneurship and investment in Ajman. Press release: Ajman Chamber is preparing to launch the Thara Investment and Entrepreneurship Ecosystem during the inaugural Thara Connect Forum, scheduled for Thursday, 29 October 2026, at the Thara Entrepreneurship Centre in Ajman. The event will be held under the patronage of His Highness Sheikh Humaid bin Rashid Al Nuaimi, Supreme Council Member and Ruler of Ajman, and in the presence of His Highness Sheikh Ammar bin Humaid Al Nuaimi, Crown Prince of Ajman and Chairman of the Executive Council. The forum will bring together leading investors, business leaders, entrepreneurs, and industry experts from the UAE and abroad, providing a platform for exchanging knowledge, strengthening connections, and exploring investment and partnership opportunities. H.E. Eng. Abdullah bin Mohammed Al Muwaiji, Chairman of Ajman Chamber, emphasised that the launch of Thara reflects the UAE leadership's vision of building a diversified and competitive economy in which entrepreneurs and startups play a key role in driving economic growth. H.E. Maryam Khalifa Al Nuaimi, Chairperson of the Thara Investment and Entrepreneurship Ecosystem, highlighted that Thara represents a significant step forward in Ajman's approach to the new economy through the development of an integrated environment designed to support entrepreneurs at different stages of their business growth. The forum will feature a series of panel discussions and specialised networking sessions, alongside a startup exhibition showcasing innovative solutions and providing opportunities for entrepreneurs to connect directly with investors and business leaders. The event is also expected to unveil further details about the Thara Investment and Entrepreneurship Ecosystem, including its components, initiatives, and opportunities for supporting investment and entrepreneurship, reinforcing Ajman's position as an attractive destination for innovative businesses and emerging ventures.

articles.title: TSMC Could Charge Up to 20% More for CoWoS Packaging Amid AI Crunch
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
TSMC Could Charge Up to 20% More for CoWoS Packaging Amid AI Crunch
TSMC is reportedly considering raising prices for its CoWoS (Chip on Wafer on Substrate) advanced packaging by as much as 20%, according to supply chain sources cited by Taiwan's Commercial Times. Foundries and outsourced packaging firms are apparently weighing another round of 10% to 20% increases, as CoWoS demand has spread beyond AI GPUs to server CPUs and custom ASICs, leaving a growing backlog of unfilled orders. TSMC hasn't confirmed anything yet.
Testing is turning into a bottleneck of its own. Nomura estimates, via Seoul Economic Daily, that NVIDIA's Blackwell takes roughly four times longer than Hopper in final testing, while Rubin could need seven times as long. Packages keep growing too, with TSMC already mass producing CoWoS-L at 5.5 times the reticle limit. Tool lead times have reportedly stretched from three to six months to as long as eight months. TSMC, which usually negotiates for discounts or extra features, apparently placed this year's equipment orders at existing prices instead, which says a lot about how tight things are.Liberty Times also reports that TSMC has finalized plans for 3% to 6% wafer price increases from January 2027, with 2 nm and 3 nm seeing the steepest hikes. Some packaging relief is coming, just not soon. GlobalFoundries reportedly signed a five-year, $2 billion deal to make CoWoS silicon interposers in New York, with volume production expected to ramp in the first half of 2028. At the moment this is mostly a data center problem, since gaming graphics cards don't use CoWoS, though pricier wafers will probably reach consumer chips eventually.
Sources:

articles.title: Amazon’s new Echo Time wants to be the smartest thing on your nightstand
articles.text:
Amazon’s new Echo Time wants to be the smartest thing on your nightstand
The Time is an intriguing smart display
- Amazon’s Echo Time is a smart clock with Alexa+ and a 3.2-inch display
- A camera-free design and customizable clock faces set it apart
- Sensors and adaptive lighting aim to improve your wake-up routine
Amazon has long offered a wide variety of smart speakers and smart displays, all powered by Alexa, and more recently, many have gotten the upgrade to Alexa+. Now, after several new devices, from Kindles to tablets with a glare-free Nano Matte coating, Amazon has five more, and the most intriguing is the $199 / £184.99 / AU$379 Echo Time.
A device that earns a spot on your bedside table needs to clear a high bar, and the devices team at Amazon, led by Panos Panay, thinks they’ve cracked it with this one. Speaking to press and creators, Panos called the Echo Time the ‘smartest clock in the world,’ and, first and foremost, it's meant to show you the time in a range of ways.
It really presents itself as a more well-thought-out Echo Spot. Rather than a half-circle display, the Echo Time offers a 3.2-inch screen wrapped in what looks like the body of an Echo Dot Max, with woven mesh on the rear, top, and sides. Controls sit at the top, just above the woven mesh, for volume up, volume down, and microphone mute. It does have microphones you can mute, but the Time notably doesn’t have a camera.
That’s a refreshing admission for a device designed for your nightstand and will likely make the Time more popular than the Spot.
Instead, Echo Time aims to mix clock skills with Alexa+. Like the previous Echo Spot and the forthcoming Apple HomeView, you can customize it with a range of clock faces and even add mini widgets. I saw several designs that look like traditional clocks, with or without hands or numbers, as well as digital ones and others that use photos.
There are some collaborative designs pulling from famous characters like Harry Potter or the Powerpuff Girls — I am hoping for some Disney, Star Wars, or Marvel ones one day. You can swipe left or right to adjust the clock face and long-press to swipe between and customize them.
It can, as you might suspect, function as an alarm clock, but Amazon takes this a step further, as it can raise or lower the brightness of the display and glow light at the bottom to help with your wind-down or wake-up routine. For instance, rather than blaring a loud horn as your alarm, it can intelligently raise the display brightness and work with connected smart home gadgets, like a smart bulb, to help ease your wake-up. It can gradually raise the brightness like a sunrise, and at night, it could start to dim things and even cut blue light from the display. At night, the display can drop to as low as 0.3 nits, meaning that the glow won’t keep you up and the screen can be viewed without burning your retinas.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
It will also utilize Omnisense to find the best time to wake you up if you opt in, which is different from Soli on, say, the Google Nest Hub or the Hatch Sleep Clock with sleep tracking. Echo Time isn’t looking to track your sleep but is using these sensors — room temperature, presence detection, ultrasound for breathing, and proximity — to figure out when you’re in a state of lighter sleep and start to wake you up. From there, when an alarm is set, Alexa and the Echo Time can make the call to sound it earlier.
And since it’s running Alexa+, you don’t need to be precise with your asks. You could tell Alexa you have an important meeting at 9 AM, so you need to be up by 7:30 or 7:45 AM, and have it figure out the best routine, potentially setting an alarm but also cueing the lights and hopefully easing you into your day.
With its built-in speakers and screen, you can ask Alexa topical questions and even request music playback, and the Echo Time will happily oblige. It seems like a fully capable Alexa smart display, but it’s unlike the rest of the Echo Show or the standard Echo lineup. Echo Time is squarely built around being a digital clock with Alexa capabilities. And that's a good thing.
Instead of trying to be another smart display that does a little bit of everything, it offers a camera-free design, customizable clock faces, and smart features designed to help you start your day or ease into slumber. It's a more purpose-built Echo, and that could be exactly what makes it worth the space on your nightstand.
At $199.99, it is the same price as the Echo Show 8 and more than the Echo Spot at $109.99. That puts it in an interesting spot in the lineup, and I'm looking forward to spending more time with it soon. Its price puts it firmly in premium smart-clock, smart display territory, so it’ll be interesting to see whether its added features justify the cost over other Echo devices.
Amazon’s also dropping the Amazon Kids Echo Time at $209.99 / £194.99 in Galactic Grape — my favorite — or Cosmic Lime, and it comes bundled with a year of Amazon Kids+. The standard Echo Time comes in Graphite, Glacier White, and Coral Pink for $199.99. Both are available to order now and are shipping now.

Since then Jacob has worked for a plethora of publications including CNN Underscored, TheStreet, Parade, Men’s Journal, Mashable, CNET, and CNBC among others.
