articles.title: Pour ne pas revivre le fiasco de l’IA, Intel s’offre une pépite du quantique à 2,3 milliards
articles.text:
Après avoir pris du retard dans l’intelligence artificielle, Intel ne compte pas laisser passer la prochaine révolution informatique. Le géant américain a annoncé ce lundi 26 octobre le rachat de Classiq, une start-up israélienne spécialisée dans les logiciels quantiques, pour un montant qui atteindrait les 2,3 milliards de dollars.
Intel semble bien décidé à ne pas reproduire les erreurs du passé. Alors que NVIDIA a largement profité de l’explosion de l’intelligence artificielle, le fondeur américain prépare déjà son offensive sur un autre marché prometteur, celui de l’informatique quantique. Pour accélérer, le géant de Santa Clara vient de signer un accord en vue du rachat de Classiq Technologies, une entreprise israélienne dont les logiciels pourraient devenir une pièce maîtresse de sa stratégie.
Selon Reuters et Bloomberg, l’opération atteindrait 2,3 milliards de dollars, un montant qu’Intel n’a pas officiellement confirmé. Le rachat doit encore obtenir les autorisations réglementaires nécessaires, avec une finalisation espérée au premier semestre 2027.
Classiq veut simplifier la programmation des ordinateurs quantiques
Faire fonctionner un ordinateur quantique reste une affaire de spécialistes. Contrairement aux machines traditionnelles, ces systèmes reposent sur des qubits dont le comportement impose des méthodes de programmation particulièrement complexes.
C'est précisément ce problème que cherche à résoudre Classiq. Fondée en 2020, la start-up a développé une plateforme capable de transformer automatiquement des algorithmes de haut niveau en circuits quantiques sans obliger les développeurs à maîtriser les particularités de chaque processeur.
L'autre intérêt de cette technologie est son indépendance vis-à-vis du matériel. Elle peut fonctionner avec différentes architectures quantiques dans un secteur où plusieurs approches se disputent encore la première place. De quoi séduire les entreprises qui souhaitent expérimenter cette informatique sans miser immédiatement sur un fabricant de puces.
Intel veut réunir les puces et les logiciels
Le quantique n’est pas un terrain inconnu pour Intel. Depuis plus de dix ans, le groupe travaille notamment sur des qubits de spin en silicium, une technologie qui pourrait tirer parti de ses compétences historiques dans la fabrication des semi-conducteurs.
Avec Classiq, le fondeur entend désormais réunir ses processeurs expérimentaux, ses systèmes de contrôle et les outils logiciels nécessaires pour les exploiter. Une approche dite full-stack, qui doit lui permettre de proposer à terme une solution complète plutôt qu’une simple collection de composants.
« Notre rapprochement avec Classiq transforme notre division quantique en une activité couvrant l’ensemble de la chaîne technologique », explique Lip-Bu Tan, le patron d'Intel.
L'ambition est claire. Après les CPU, les GPU et les accélérateurs spécialisés, Intel espère pouvoir ajouter les processeurs quantiques, ou QPU, à son catalogue. Encore faudra-t-il que cette technologie trouve des applications commerciales suffisamment convaincantes.
Classiq continuera de travailler avec les concurrents d’Intel
L'acquisition par un fabricant de puces pourrait inquiéter les clients de Classiq qui utilisent d’autres architectures quantiques. Intel assure toutefois que la plateforme conservera sa compatibilité avec les matériels concurrents.
Une promesse essentielle pour préserver l’intérêt de ses logiciels, mais dont la mise en pratique devra être suivie une fois le rachat finalisé. Nir Minerbi, cofondateur et patron de Classiq, estime par ailleurs que cette alliance permettra « d’accélérer l’adoption de l’informatique quantique » en la rendant plus accessible aux développeurs et aux entreprises.
Car, malgré les investissements et les annonces, l’ordinateur quantique capable de transformer réellement les usages industriels reste encore largement à construire.
Un qubit est l’unité de calcul d’un ordinateur quantique, capable de représenter des états quantiques qui ne se limitent pas à 0 ou 1 de façon strictement binaire. Cette particularité permet certains gains théoriques, mais rend les opérations très sensibles au bruit et aux erreurs (décohérence). Programmer un calcul quantique consiste souvent à définir une suite d’opérations (portes quantiques) formant un circuit, puis à composer avec les contraintes du matériel (connectivité entre qubits, taux d’erreur, temps de calcul). À l’inverse, la plupart des développeurs sur CPU/GPU peuvent s’appuyer sur une exécution plus déterministe et sur des abstractions logicielles très stabilisées.
Un circuit quantique est une représentation bas niveau d’un programme quantique, décrite comme une séquence de portes appliquées à des qubits. Partir d’un algorithme haut niveau revient à exprimer l’intention (par exemple une optimisation ou une simulation) sans se lier immédiatement aux détails d’un processeur quantique donné. La conversion automatique implique généralement de la synthèse et de l’optimisation : réduire le nombre d’opérations, respecter la topologie de la machine et limiter l’impact des erreurs. L’enjeu est de rendre la mise au point plus rapide et de diminuer la barrière d’entrée, car écrire des circuits à la main devient vite impraticable dès que la taille du problème augmente.
Une approche full-stack vise à maîtriser toute la chaîne : le processeur quantique (QPU), l’électronique et les systèmes de contrôle, le compilateur/outil de mapping, et les bibliothèques logicielles utilisées par les développeurs. Cette intégration peut améliorer les performances réelles, car le logiciel peut être optimisé pour compenser les limites du matériel (erreurs, connectivité, contraintes de calibration). En parallèle, une plateforme logicielle dite “agnostique” du matériel cherche à fonctionner sur plusieurs types de QPU, ce qui évite d’enfermer les utilisateurs dans une seule technologie. C’est un point clé tant que le secteur n’a pas convergé vers une architecture dominante et que les entreprises veulent tester des cas d’usage sans parier trop tôt sur un unique fournisseur.

articles.title: FBI Seizes Virtualine Domain Over Alleged Criminal Hosting and Bitcoin Money Laundering
articles.text:
The U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) on Tuesday announced the seizure of a domain associated with a bulletproof hosting provider (BPH) named Virtualine.
The move was in response to the service being used to commit and facilitate prolific criminal activity, including "the advertisement of sexually explicit images of minors, the intentional disclosure of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions of adults and minors, and international money laundering designed to conceal and promote criminal conduct," the DoJ said.
Visitors to the "virtualine[.]net" domain are now greeted by a message that states it has been seized by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation as part of a coordinated operation between international law enforcement agencies and private sector entities, including the Hessen State Police, the National Police Corps of the Netherlands, the U.K. National Crime Agency, OverRIPE, and Lumen Technologies.
According to court documents, Virtualine, which also operated as Secury, Massgod, Spamhouse, Lanedo, and Omegatech, advertised its services to criminals on cybercrime forums, claiming that they can be used for phishing, carding, email spam, and port scanning, with the exception of child content and terrorism activities.
In June 2025 on HackForums, the provider is alleged to have boasted that "Virtualine ignored more abuse than your last three therapists." Earlier this March, it also began marketing an "additional protection plan" that promised its customers to move their criminal infrastructure to a shell company unaffiliated with Virtualine when receiving official requests from law enforcement agencies.
Snapshots captured by the Internet Archive show that standard plans cost anywhere between $19.99 per month for one virtual CPU, 2GB memory, and 30 GB storage to $179.99 per month for 24 vCPUs, 64 GB memory, and 130 GB memory. Virtualine also offered plans optimized by CPU, memory, and storage, starting from $21.99 per month to $379.99 per month.
"Despite advertising that it does not allow 'child contents' on its server, Virtualine knowingly hosted a website that did so, identified in court records as Vendor 1," DoJ said. "Vendor 1 is a criminal online forum that allows users to post and sell access to nude, sexually suggestive, and/or sexually explicit images and videos of minors and adults."
"Vendor 1 also promotes a hack-for-hire service in which users can pay hackers to access victims’ online accounts without their consent and illicitly obtain explicit images and videos. In January 2026, about one month after Virtualine assigned an IP address to Vendor 1, Virtualine began receiving notifications about sexually explicit images and videos of minors on that server."
The Justice Department said Virtualine continued to host Vendor 1's services despite receiving numerous notices from law enforcement in Germany, Canada, and Australia; the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) in the United States; and a victim's attorney.
Virtualine has also been accused of working closely with Vendor 1 to create a new website where its clients could upload their illicit content and download it upon completing a purchase. The website continues to be hosted by Virtualine to this day, the department added.
"Virtualine.net included a number of payment options for Virtualine's customers, including Vendor 1," the DoJ said. "Virtualine accepted payment through BTC [NO-AML], specific unhosted bitcoin addresses that allowed customers to direct pay without concern their funds would be flagged as illicit."
"The funds Virtualine's criminal customers paid to Virtualine, some of which can be traced directly to various criminal groups, were received by Virtualine and then further laundered to conceal the origin of the funds."
Blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis, in its own analysis, said Virtualine accepted direct Bitcoin payments through unhosted wallet addresses, allowing criminal customers to pay without triggering compliance checks at hosted exchanges.
"Virtualine's on-chain footprint has direct exposure to a broad cross-section of the cybercrime ecosystem, including ransomware operators, infostealer infrastructure, Russian-language cybercrime forums, illicit shops, and scam and phishing addresses," it said.
Following the site seizure, the operator of Virtualine has published an open letter, refuting allegations that the service knowingly hosted child sexual abuse material (CSAM). The operator also claimed they have taken action on requests for cooperation concerning CSAM within 24 hours. In a post shared on their Telegram channel, they insisted that customer data was safe.
"When we identified prohibited material associated with the customer described as 'Vendor 1,' we ended our relationship with that customer," the individual added, claiming "Virtualine has been part of my life for five years."
"Please do not cast suspicion on me and the tens of thousands of customers who have trusted Virtualine because of the actions attributed to a single customer. I want you to know that I am prepared to respond to your requests concerning 'Vendor 1.'"
In September 2025, the Spamhaus Project revealed that Virtualine had expanded their operations to AS209800. "Thanks to Turkey- and U.S.-based IP address brokers with poor customer vetting procedures, Virtualine keeps obtaining new IPv4 prefixes for enabling internet abuse. AS209800 is currently routed via aurologic GmbH, a hosting provider proliferating several other bulletproof hosting operations."
"A lost ASN does not by itself mean the BPH has stopped," Silent Push said. "The speed of acquiring a new ASN is a crucial part of the problem, and we believe the process for registering an ASN should be tougher."

articles.title: Madica secures $6 million to invest in up to 30 African startups
articles.text: Africa-focused pre-seed investment programme Madica has secured an additional $6 million commitment from Flourish Ventures to extend its investment pilot by three years, targeting 25–30 more early-stage startups across the continent. Launched in 2022 and led by Emmanuel Adegboye, Madica is a sector-agnostic investment programme affiliated with Flourish Ventures, providing early-stage funding and hands-on company-building support to African founders underserved by traditional venture capital networks. Madica has invested in 18 startups across 10 African countries and 12 sectors, including AI, climate technology, semiconductors and biotechnology. Its portfolio companies have subsequently attracted additional funding averaging twice Madica's initial investment, while more than half have at least one female co-founder. The additional capital will support new pre-seed investments, expanded company-building assistance and a longer evaluation period to assess portfolio growth and investment returns. Eligible startups must be headquartered in Africa, have a minimum viable product with paying customers and have received little or no institutional funding. Press release: Madica, a structured pre-seed investment programme for African startups, today announced $6M in additional capital from Flourish Ventures to extend its investment pilot by three years. Building on lessons learned and early signs of traction across its portfolio, Madica will back 25-30 additional companies and deepen its company-building support for exceptional founders who are underserved by established venture capital networks. The extended pilot will build further evidence for Madica’s founding conviction: that these founders can build world-class businesses capable of generating venture returns when equipped with the right capital and support. Launched in 2022, Madica set out to demonstrate that exceptional founders in Africa’s overlooked markets, sectors and networks can build globally competitive businesses with the right capital and support. The sector-agnostic programme has since backed 18 startups across 10 countries and 12 sectors, combining patient pre-seed capital with structured, hands-on company-building support. These companies have attracted, on average, twice Madica’s investment in additional funding, an early signal of investor confidence as they work towards the commercial outcomes needed to challenge prevailing assumptions about where venture-scale businesses can emerge in Africa. The extended pilot will allow Madica to track how companies across a broader portfolio translate early traction into sustained business growth, examining the role of its investment and support model in that progress and assessing the potential to generate venture returns through exits. This continues the pilot’s original purpose: to build tangible evidence that can challenge assumptions about which founders and markets offer venture-scale opportunities in Africa. The findings will help refine Madica’s approach and provide practical lessons that other investors can adapt and apply. “Madica was launched as an experiment to test whether pairing capital with hands-on company-building support could help overlooked founders building world-class businesses generate venture outcomes, and in many ways, our work sits at the intersection of the very many questions that underpin the state of early-stage venture investing in Africa. From the outset, we knew that gathering meaningful evidence would require years of investment, support and learning," said Emmanuel Adegboye, Head of Madica. “Three years have given us valuable lessons and encouraging early signals, but building enduring companies and assessing venture outcomes takes longer. Flourish Ventures’ continued commitment gives us the capital to build on those lessons and test our conviction across a broader portfolio while deepening our company-building support. We want the resulting evidence to give other investors a model they can apply, shaping where funding goes and how founders are backed across Africa, well beyond Madica”, he continued. Today, Madica’s portfolio spans over a dozen sectors, including climate-tech, semiconductors, AI, HR, biotech, mobility and more, reflecting the breadth of innovation emerging across the continent. The diversity is also evident in the volume and reach of applications, which span 28 sectors and 78 countries, with 40% coming from outside Africa’s four largest venture capital markets. This signals both the depth of untapped entrepreneurial potential across Africa and the urgent need for more inclusive funding pathways. Every company in Madica’s portfolio is majority African-owned, more than 50% have at least one female co-founder, and 39% are led by female CEOs, demonstrating a deliberate approach to identifying and backing talent that established investment networks have often overlooked. “We retain our conviction that with the right capital and support, exceptional talent across Africa can build world-class businesses. Madica’s first three years have strengthened that belief, and we are excited to continue backing the team as they help more entrepreneurs achieve that mission,” said Efayomi Carr, Investment Partner at Flourish Ventures and Co-founder of Madica. Madica continues to seek exceptional founders building early-stage startups across Africa. To pitch your startup, visit the Madica website. Eligible startups must have a minimum viable product (MVP) with proven traction from a few paying customers, founder(s) engaged full-time, little or no institutional funding, and be headquartered in Africa.

articles.title: WhatsApp prepara ‘Organizaciones’, la nueva herramienta para gestionar grandes comunidades
articles.text:
WhatsApp prepara una nueva función para ordenar el funcionamiento interno de sus comunidades. Se trata de ‘Organizaciones’, una herramienta pensada para que los administradores controlen con mayor facilidad los subgrupos y los cientos de participantes que puede llegar a reunir una misma comunidad.
El hallazgo lo hizo el medio especializado WaBetaInfo, que detectó la función en la versión beta de WhatsApp para Android 2.26.43.1. Según precisó este medio, el desarrollo aún se encuentra en una etapa inicial.
Qué es la función Organizaciones de WhatsApp
Organizaciones es, en esencia, una nueva pantalla dentro de la aplicación. Permite a los administradores visualizar de un vistazo el número total de miembros que integran una comunidad.
Esa pantalla incorpora un botón con la etiqueta “ver todo”. Al presionarlo, el sistema despliega el listado completo de usuarios junto con el detalle de los grupos específicos en los que cada uno participa.
De esta manera, quienes administran una comunidad podrían dejar de depender de revisar subgrupo por subgrupo para saber quién forma parte de cada espacio. La herramienta centraliza esa información en una sola vista.
Diferencia entre comunidades y la nueva herramienta de gestión
Las comunidades de WhatsApp no son una novedad: la compañía las lanzó en 2022 con el objetivo de agrupar bajo una misma estructura a varios subgrupos que compartieran una temática común.
Organizaciones no reemplaza ni modifica ese esquema. Se trata de una capa adicional, exclusiva para la administración, que convive con el formato ya existente de comunidades.
Por ese motivo, la experiencia de los usuarios que participan en una comunidad no se vería alterada. La función impacta únicamente en el panel de control que utilizan los administradores, sin introducir cambios visibles para el resto de los integrantes.
Cuándo estará disponible la nueva función para administradores
Por el momento, Organizaciones no está disponible ni siquiera para los usuarios inscritos en el programa beta de WhatsApp. WaBetaInfo señaló que el desarrollo se encuentra en una fase muy temprana.
En consecuencia, todavía no existe una fecha estimada de lanzamiento, ni para la versión de prueba ni para su eventual llegada al público general.
WhatsApp prepara un cambio que integrará los canales a la pestaña Chats
WhatsApp evalúa una modificación que trasladará los canales desde la pestaña Novedades hacia la pestaña Chats, con la posibilidad de que cada usuario decida cuáles quiere conservar junto a sus conversaciones. La función, en desarrollo para Android, apunta a reorganizar un espacio que hasta ahora funciona de manera separada dentro de la aplicación.
El cambio afectaría a quienes siguen actualizaciones de medios, artistas, equipos deportivos, empresas u organizaciones a través de canales. En lugar de recibir esos contenidos en una sección independiente, la aplicación permitirá dejarlos visibles en la lista principal de chats, enviarlos al archivo o dejar de seguirlos.
El rediseño de la pestaña Novedades
La propuesta original de WhatsApp planteaba una decisión general para todos los canales: mantenerlos en la lista principal o archivarlos en conjunto. Ese esquema cambió durante el proceso de desarrollo.
La versión beta 2.26.43.2 para Android muestra ahora una alternativa más específica, con una recomendación individual para cada canal seguido. Esto significa que el usuario ya no tendría que elegir una única ubicación para toda su lista de canales, sino definir caso por caso.
Esta modificación se enmarca en una reorganización más amplia de la interfaz. WhatsApp ya prueba, con un grupo de usuarios, que las actualizaciones de estado aparezcan en la parte superior de la pestaña Chats.
Si los estados y los canales terminan compartiendo ese mismo espacio, la pestaña Novedades perdería su razón de ser dentro de la aplicación. En su reemplazo, se prevé la llegada de una sección llamada Contactos, orientada a mostrar quién está en línea y a facilitar la búsqueda de personas guardadas en la agenda.

articles.title: Why 'never trust, always verify - repeatably' security strategy for AI Agents, starts after login
articles.text:
Why 'never trust, always verify - repeatably' security strategy for AI Agents, starts after login
Securing AI agents requires continuous verification of actions after login
Modern digital security frameworks were originally built to correct a flawed historical assumption: the belief that if a user or system was inside the company network, they could be trusted implicitly. Over the past decade, the rapid rise of cloud storage, subscription-based business software, and remote working destroyed that network boundary.
In response, our security models shifted focus. We began verifying the identity of the person trying to log in, inspecting the hygiene of their computer, requiring multiple verification steps during login, and continuously checking that they were who they claimed to be.
Chief Information Officer and Global Chief Information Security Officer at Cato Networks.
This model works well when a human is logging in to perform a task. But with the rise of autonomous AI agents, the real security risk no centralized at the login screen. It starts after access has been granted.
An AI agent does not behave like a standard piece of software. It reads a human instruction, pulls context from company databases, utilizes multiple sets of tools, chooses its own digital tools, connects to external software communication links, and triggers complex automated workflows.
Verifying the initial login simply tells you that the agent is officially recognized by your system. It tells you absolutely nothing about whether the next action the agent plans to take is safe, ethical, or correct, focus has shifted to context.
The evolution of the machine identity problem
IT teams have already experienced a simpler, quieter version of this challenge with non-human identities. For years, companies have used automated service accounts, security tokens, and digital certificates to allow different software programs to talk to one another.
Most security leaders are all too familiar with the risks these credentials present: accounts are created for a temporary project, granted permanent access to database files, and then completely forgotten long after the project has ended. They become silent, unmonitored backdoors into the network.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
However, AI agents complicate this familiar problem by introducing the element of independent judgment.
A traditional service account follows strict, pre-written code. By contrast, an AI agent interprets a high-level goal, analyses real-time context, selects its own tools, and actively decides how to proceed.
As a result, security policies can no longer stop at the front door. We must protect every internal data or compute asset the agent can reach and monitor every single decision it makes.
Matching autonomy with executive control
To manage this risk, security leaders must separate two distinct concepts: how much independence an AI agent has, and what level of file access it holds.
The combination of these two factors dictates the level of control required. For example, a basic agent that merely summarizes long documents only needs limited reading rights and clear activity logs. However, an agent designed to update sensitive, production databases, access code repos, write new types of code, or alter business workflows requires mandatory human approval steps, strict operational boundaries, and a clear path to reverse any mistakes.
We can categorize these digital workers into 3 distinct levels of independence, applying tighter security controls as their autonomy increases:
1. First, there are Conversational AI Agents (GenAI), productivity agents usually built and managed by employees & teams as part of their productivity (e.g. managed agents, self hosted chat bots). When driving security, we must enable proper RBAC authorization, associated with the employee and team, ensuring access to non-sensitive or production-related data, enabling logging, and validating the response to ensure proper integrity.
2. Second, there are Agents Acting with Semi/Full Human Guardrails (AI Agents), such as customer support tools that draft emails or prepare database updates for review. Here, security teams must validate the parameters of the tools being used and require a human to approve any actions involving writing, deleting, spending money, or sending information externally. All above controls apply
3. Finally, there are Fully Autonomous Agents (Agentic AI), which reset passwords or trigger complex workflows on their own. These require the strictest boundaries, from visibility (agent architecture, tool usage, and more) and focus on active set of controls. The controls include strict rate limits, continuous real-time policy checks, network access restrictions, run time security controls (Public/Private Cloud) continuous identity and minimal authorization verification, and finally complete, unalterable audit trails.
The industry is leaning toward autonomous agents seeking human approval upon abnormal behavior, can that be triggered in your agent?
The need for real-time inspection
To enforce these policies, security teams need a dedicated vantage point within the network. They must be able to inspect the human prompt, the agent's response, the digital tools being used, and the movement of data while the work is actually happening.
This requires an architecture that can discover all active agent activity across the business, govern how those agents use internal tools, and maintain complete visibility over data flows and automated workflows.
The true value of this approach lies in context. When the behavior of an AI agent is viewed alongside network traffic, user activity, and cloud database logs, security teams can investigate incidents with clear evidence. They can instantly see which agent ran, who in the organization owns it, what data was moved, and which automated tool was called.
For business leaders, this means cleaner, more consistent governance across human users, software applications, and digital agents alike.
How to begin: Start with a single workflow
Securing this new landscape does not require a complete overhaul of your entire security department overnight.
Start by picking a single AI workflow that is currently in use or close to being launched. Map out its digital identity, its level of independence, the files it can access, the tools it uses, the points where a human must approve an action, and how you would undo a mistake.
This simple mapping exercise will quickly highlight where your security gaps lie. If you cannot see the agent's actions in real-time, approve its decisions, block its access, or explain its behavior after the fact, your security controls are simply too far away.
From there, build a baseline on how your secure your coding agents, AI harness (or AI orchestrator) up to utilizing of tools/skills/MCP and moving forward to data assets access and utilization of identity that will allow you to set the correct foundations and guard rails.
The core principle of a "never trust, always verify" security model must follow the agent into its daily work. The most meaningful decision is no longer who is logging in, but whether their next action should be allowed to happen, under these exact conditions, right now.

articles.title: Avant le Black Friday, ce Dyson Cyclone V10 Fluffy tombe à 329€
articles.text:
Les offres « Black Friday » anticipées se multiplient sur les aspirateurs Dyson depuis ce lundi, un mois avant l’événement. Le Dyson Cyclone V10 Fluffy passe ainsi à 329 € à la Fnac, son prix le plus bas sur trois mois, pour un balai de 2018 pensé d’abord pour les sols durs et dont l’autonomie dépend beaucoup du mode choisi.
Lancé en 2018, le Cyclone V10 a précédé les V11, V12 et V15 dans la gamme de balais sans fil de Dyson. Sa version Fluffy se distingue par sa brosse principale à rouleau doux, conçue pour le parquet, le carrelage et les autres sols durs. La Fnac le vend à 329 € au lieu de 449 €, soit 120 € de moins que son prix barré, qui correspond aussi au plus haut relevé sur trois mois par LeDénicheur.
Ces 329 € sont le tarif le plus bas observé par le comparateur sur la période, et l’offre est vendue par la Fnac elle-même. Elle vise surtout les logements où dominent les sols durs.
Le Dyson Cyclone V10 Fluffy est proposé à 329 € au lieu de 449 € par la Fnac, son prix le plus bas relevé sur trois mois.
Pourquoi choisir le Dyson Cyclone V10 Fluffy ?
- Une brosse pensée pour les sols durs : Son rouleau en nylon doux, garni de fibres de carbone antistatiques, ramasse poussière fine et débris plus gros sur le parquet ou le carrelage, sans abîmer les revêtements délicats selon Dyson.
- Jusqu’à 60 minutes en mode normal : La batterie à sept cellules suffit pour faire le tour d’un appartement à puissance modérée. Comptez environ 3 h 30 de recharge sur la station murale fournie.
- Un balai qui devient aspirateur à main : Le corps se détache du tube pour le canapé, les marches ou la voiture, avec la mini brosse motorisée et le suceur long livrés. Le bac de 0,76 litre se vide d’un geste, sans toucher la poussière.
Du parquet du salon aux sièges de la voiture
Le Cyclone V10 Fluffy se prête surtout à un ménage rapide et fréquent sur sols durs. Son moteur numérique monte à 125 000 tours par minute et ses 14 cyclones séparent la poussière de l’air, pour une aspiration annoncée à 150 AW en mode Boost. Trois modes de puissance permettent de doser l’effort, de l’entretien courant au tapis plus encrassé. La filtration associe HEPA, mousse et technologie multicyclonique pour retenir une grande partie des particules fines.
Le profil type est celui d’un foyer en appartement, avec du parquet ou du carrelage dans la plupart des pièces. Il est moins pertinent pour une maison couverte de moquette, car la brosse principale livrée est la Fluffy, prévue pour les sols durs. L’autonomie annoncée suppose aussi le mode normal : en puissance maximale avec une brosse motorisée, le Journal du Geek n’a mesuré qu’une vingtaine de minutes lors de son test du V10 Absolute. Enfin, à environ 77 dB, il reste bruyant.
Face aux balais sans fil plus récents, à budget proche
Le Cyclone V10 date de 2018 et n’a pas le capteur de détection de poussière des générations plus récentes de Dyson. Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs aspirateurs balais, le Dyson Gen5 Detect Absolute occupe la première place, mais il s’affiche autour de 649 €, soit près du double. À l’opposé, le Dreame V20 Pro y est retenu comme meilleur rapport qualité-prix autour de 299 €, un peu moins cher que cette offre. À 329 €, le V10 Fluffy se défend pour qui privilégie la brosse douce de Dyson sur sols durs plutôt que les fonctions récentes.
✅ Les points forts
- Brosse Fluffy à rouleau doux adaptée au parquet et au carrelage
- Jusqu’à 60 minutes d’autonomie en mode normal
- Conversion rapide en aspirateur à main, avec mini brosse motorisée
- Vidage du bac sans contact avec la poussière
- Prix le plus bas relevé sur trois mois par LeDénicheur
❌ Les limites
- Une vingtaine de minutes en puissance maximale, selon un test indépendant
- Bruyant, autour de 77 dB
- Bac de 0,76 litre à vider souvent sur de grandes surfaces
- Pas de détection de poussière, contrairement aux Dyson récents
Vendu directement par la Fnac, le Cyclone V10 Fluffy revient à 329 €, quand sa marketplace le propose à partir de 408,89 €.
À 329 €, le Dyson Cyclone V10 Fluffy devient une option sérieuse pour un logement surtout en sols durs, avec l’appoint d’un aspirateur à main. La baisse de 120 € est réelle : le prix barré de 449 € a bien été pratiqué ces trois derniers mois, selon l’historique de LeDénicheur. Son âge se voit pourtant : pas de détection de poussière, et une autonomie qui fond vite en mode Boost.
Si votre logement compte surtout de la moquette, ou si le bruit vous gêne, mieux vaut regarder les modèles de notre comparatif. Pour un appartement en parquet ou en carrelage, le V10 Fluffy couvre en revanche l’essentiel du ménage courant. Et avec les offres Dyson anticipées avant le Black Friday, garder un œil sur les prix des prochaines semaines reste un bon réflexe.

articles.title: LattePanda Launches LattePanda Sigma 2: The Embeddable AI Single Board Server
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
LattePanda Launches LattePanda Sigma 2: The Embeddable AI Single Board Server
The LattePanda Team today launched LattePanda Sigma 2, an x86 single-board server designed to bring high-performance local AI computing directly into intelligent products and systems. Built around the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H processor with Intel Arc B390 graphics, LattePanda Sigma 2 delivers up to 180 TOPS of total AI performance at INT8 in a compact form factor.
As "The Embeddable AI Single Board Server," LattePanda Sigma 2 combines high-performance computing, up to 64 GB of memory, high-speed networking, flexible expansion, and real-time hardware control in a single board. Rather than sitting alongside a product, it is designed to be integrated directly into the product itself, supporting applications from autonomous robots and vision systems to professional instruments and private AI appliances.LattePanda Sigma 2 combines the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU, Intel Arc B390 GPU, and integrated NPU to deliver up to 180 TOPS of total AI performance at INT8. It features a 16-core CPU with up to 4.8 GHz clock speed, a 12 Xe-core Intel Arc B390 GPU delivering up to 122 TOPS of INT8 AI performance, and an NPU capable of up to 50 TOPS.
With up to 64 GB of LPDDR5X-8533 RAM and 136.5 GB/s memory bandwidth, LattePanda Sigma 2 provides the capacity and throughput required for demanding local AI workloads. Up to 59 GB of VRAM can be allocated for AI workloads, providing enough room for 35B-class quantized MoE models and the KV cache required by long-context AI agents. With INT4 quantization and OpenVINO, the system can run the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model locally at around 30 tokens per second.
Built for Local AI Systems
LattePanda Sigma 2 is designed to support both individual AI workloads and multi-agent local AI systems. Developers can expand compute capacity through M.2, OCuLink, or Thunderbolt 4, connecting additional AI accelerators as workloads grow. An integrated RP2350 microcontroller adds GPIO connectivity and real-time hardware control, allowing AI applications to interact with sensors and actuators. Preloaded MicroPython firmware provides a programmable interface for intelligent devices and automation systems.
Server-Class Expansion in an Embeddable Form Factor
LattePanda Sigma 2 provides extensive connectivity for storage, networking, and acceleration. It includes three M.2 M-Key slots, one M.2 E-Key slot, PCIe 4.0 x2 via OCuLink, and two Thunderbolt 4 ports. Dual 10GbE Ethernet supports high-bandwidth networking, while USB 3.2 Gen 2, USB 2.0, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 2.1, and eDP 1.5 provide flexible system integration options. These interfaces allow LattePanda Sigma 2 to operate as a compact local AI server or integrate directly into larger intelligent systems.
Ready for Local AI Development and Deployment
LattePanda Sigma 2 supports Windows 11 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, with compatibility for OpenVINO, llama.cpp, and Ollama. It ships with Ubuntu, GPU and NPU drivers, OpenVINO Model Server (OVMS), OpenClaw, and local AI models pre-installed on the onboard SSD, reducing setup time for local AI deployment.
Designed for Product Integration
LattePanda Sigma 2 is designed for product-level integration and long-term deployment, offering a guaranteed 3+ year product lifecycle, custom boot logos and BIOS customization options, and direct engineering support for integration projects. Its combination of local AI compute, high-speed I/O, flexible expansion, and real-time control supports a wide range of applications, including:
- Local AI Appliances—Run private RAG and AI agents while keeping sensitive data on premises.
- All-in-One Homelabs—Combine NAS, virtualization, media services, and local AI in one system.
- Professional Instruments—Capture and process high-speed data streams directly inside compact professional equipment.
- Mobile Autonomous Robots—Unify perception, navigation, planning, and real-time control on one platform.
"Local AI is moving beyond development and into the products and systems people use every day," said Youliang Yu, Product Manager of LattePanda Sigma 2. "With LattePanda Sigma 2, we are combining the computing performance, memory capacity, expansion, and real-time hardware control needed to run AI locally in a compact, embeddable platform. The goal is to give developers a practical way to put local AI directly into the products they build."
Key Specifications
- Processor: Intel Core Ultra X7 358H
- AI Performance: Up to 180 TOPS (CPU + GPU + NPU, INT8)
- NPU: Up to 50 TOPS
- CPU: 16 cores (4P + 8E + 4LPE), up to 4.8 GHz, 18 MB cache
- GPU: Intel Arc B390, 12 Xe-cores, up to 122 TOPS (INT8)
- Memory: Up to 64 GB LPDDR5X-8533 RAM, 136.5 GB/s bandwidth
- Storage & Expansion: 3× M.2 M-Key, 1× M.2 E-Key, OCuLink PCIe 4.0 x2
- Networking: 2× 10GbE RJ45
- Thunderbolt: 2× Thunderbolt 4 Type-C
- USB Type-A: 2× USB 3.2 Gen 2, 2× USB 2.0
- Display: HDMI 2.1, DP 2.1 via USB Type-C, eDP 1.5
- Co-Processor: RP2350
- Operating System: Windows 11, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later
- Dimensions: 146 × 102 mm
For more information about LattePanda Sigma 2, please visit the LattePanda website. During the pre-sale period through mid-November, the LattePanda Sigma 2 is available at a promotional price of $2,599. Following the conclusion of the pre-sale period, the price will return to $2,799.

articles.title: Japan's GMO Offers $1 Million Bounty to Catch Hackers Behind FX Trading Cloud Breach
articles.text:
Japan's GMO Internet Group is offering up to $1 million in total for tips that help catch the attackers who breached its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service, after refusing to pay an extortion demand.
The reward program opened on October 28 and pays only if a tip helps lead to an arrest or an international wanted notice. The service hosts Windows desktops used for FX trading, and a broker has linked unauthorized trades on some of its customers' accounts to logins leaked from the service.
GMO says the attackers took customer information. It received a demand for about $50 million (about ¥8 billion) on October 21 from people it believes carried out the attack. They have also threatened its customers' trading accounts and data.
On October 27, the attackers posted material on their website that they say is information about GMO and its customers. The site's domain, including its mirror sites, was shut down at about 4 a.m. Japan time on October 28, and GMO plans to act against any new site.
How the Reward Works
GMO Internet Group runs and pays for the program, called GMO Cybercrime Bounty. Tips are sent by email to an address listed on a dedicated website, in Japanese, English, or Chinese, and can be anonymous. The program is open until an arrest, an international wanted notice, or October 27, 2027, whichever comes first.
GMO wants information linking people, servers, domains, IP addresses, accounts, or cryptocurrency addresses to the attack, extortion, or movement of money, along with evidence of how the crimes were carried out. Guesses, unsupported accusations and reposts of public information generally do not qualify.
A tip earns money only if it leads to an arrest, including one by police outside Japan, or to an international wanted notice, such as an Interpol Red Notice. GMO decides how much each tip helped, and one tipster can receive the full $1 million or the total can be split. Tipsters must prove their identity before payment, and if no tip qualifies, no payment is made.
Some people cannot be paid, including anyone involved in the crime, anyone who got information illegally, such as by buying leaked data, and GMO staff. GMO tells tipsters not to break into systems, negotiate with or pay the attackers, or send leaked data, credentials, or malware.
Tips are shared with police and other authorities in Japan and abroad as needed. GMO has already given police all its evidence on the threats, including communication records.
GMO will never ask tipsters for passwords, authentication codes or fees, and it writes to them only from addresses ending in @cybercrimebounty.gmo.
The Breach and the Trading Accounts
GMO Internet, the subsidiary that runs the service, found on October 20 that a third party had installed malicious programs on some customers' servers. It shut down the servers on every plan from October 21. It counts 26,739 servers as potentially affected, which is not the number of confirmed break-ins or data thefts.
On October 24, GMO said it had confirmed a security problem in the service's systems, unauthorized access to the service, and the exfiltration of customer information from the company.
Anything customers stored on the servers may have been viewed, including login credentials saved in trading software such as MetaTrader 4 and 5 (MT4/MT5). GMO does not keep customers' payment card data on the servers.
Customers began reporting trades they did not recognize on October 21. A broker, OANDA Japan, has confirmed that a third party logged in to and traded on some of its customers' accounts using ID and password pairs it believes were leaked from the GMO servers. It has restricted trading on accounts that may be affected, and as of October 26 it had not found a break-in or leak in its own core systems.
Another broker, FXTF, warned on October 22 that third parties may have stolen the logins of some customers who use VPS servers, in an attack it believes hit another company's VPS servers. They may also have used the logins to log in and trade. It told customers who had connected to Desktop Cloud to change their FXTF passwords from a device that had never connected to it.
GMO Internet Group said in a stock exchange filing on October 28 that it had not yet confirmed how many customers its payments will cover, how much information was published, or which trades qualify for compensation. It had not confirmed any impact from the breach on its other services.
The Threats and the Leak
GMO says the attackers threatened to keep manipulating customers' accounts at more than 70 securities and FX firms, to publish information about the service and about customers' PCs, to hit those PCs with ransomware, and to publish details of GMO's systems.
They set noon on October 27 for publishing customer information and launching the ransomware attack. No ransomware attack had been confirmed as of 1:55 p.m. Japan time that day.
The material posted on October 27 was what the attackers called one customer's personal information, ITmedia NEWS reported that afternoon. GMO was checking it that day.
The attackers collected information about anyone who visited their site, according to GMO, which tells visitors to run a full antivirus scan. It asks people not to visit the site or any new one, and not to repost or link to the material.
How the Attackers Got In
As of October 28, GMO had not said how the attackers got in.
Masatoshi Kumagai, who heads GMO Internet Group, wrote in an October 25 blog post that the group's own white-hat hackers had warned the team running the service about problems in advance.
The response was neither fast nor thorough enough, he wrote, and the attackers took advantage of the gap.
On their website, the attackers claimed that one administrator account was shared across all the servers and that customers' PC drives were visible from the servers by default when they connected, ITmedia NEWS reported.
They also claimed they used a flaw in the service to reach customers' own PCs. GMO had not publicly confirmed these claims either.
By October 26, GMO had collected PCs from customers who offered them for analysis, as of 11:59 a.m. Japan time on October 27, it had found no malware, including ransomware, on the PCs it had finished checking. That does not confirm that every customer's device is safe, and the analysis is still ongoing.
What Customers Should Do
GMO has told Desktop Cloud customers to take these steps:
- Change trading-account and trading-software passwords from a device not used for FX trading, such as a phone.
- End every logged-in session, through the broker if needed, even after changing the password.
- Check trading history and balances, and report unrecognized trades to the broker first.
- Turn on two-factor authentication where the broker offers it.
- Change passwords reused on other services or saved in the browser.
- Run a full antivirus scan on devices used to connect, and back up data.
- Do not reply to messages from anyone claiming to be behind the attack, or open their links or files.
- Ignore offers to recover lost money for a fee. GMO will never ask for a password or authentication code.
GMO Internet will pay every current user ¥5,000 and cover actual trading losses and fees from trades it confirms were unauthorized and caused by the breach. Customers whose information it confirms was published will also get ¥10,000 to ¥25,000 for each type of information exposed.
GMO will not restart the service on the breached systems as they are. Customers who want a Windows desktop will be offered a move to a separate service, free for six months and only with their consent, with details due by October 30.

articles.title: Singapore's Rently secures $12 million credit facility to expand into UAE
articles.text: Singapore-based proptech startup Rently has secured a $12 million growth credit facility from January Capital to expand its rental payment solutions across Singapore, Hong Kong and the UAE, as well as new markets. Founded by Dominic Schacher, Tarik Stafford, Siebren Khamphorst and Emeric Martin, Rently offers a rental payments platform that allows tenants to pay rent in flexible instalments, earn rewards and manage payment schedules. In the UAE, its Rent Now Pay Later service enables monthly rent payments while landlords receive scheduled payouts. Rently claims to have processed more than AED 100 million in rental contracts in the UAE, where transaction volume has increased more than fivefold year-on-year. Across its three markets, the company reports over $50 million in annualised rental volume and more than 2,400 tenants using its platform. The facility will support rental transaction financing, customer acquisition and geographic expansion. Rently is also preparing to raise $10 million to $15 million in Series A equity funding to develop new products and enter additional markets from 2027. Press release: Rently, the platform that lets tenants choose how and when they pay rent, has secured a $12 million growth credit facility from January Capital, a leading technology investment firm backing high-growth companies across Asia Pacific and beyond. The facility allows Rently to fund more deals, extending Rent Now Pay Later and its broader rent flexibility offering across its existing markets, Singapore, Hong Kong and the UAE, and into new ones, helping the next thousands of tenants on their housing journey. The big picture: one platform, three markets Rent is the largest recurring expense for most households, reaching up to 40% of monthly household income in Rently’s markets¹, yet it is still paid in rigid, upfront and unrewarding ways. Rently is now running at over USD 50 million in annualised rental volume. Year to date, volume is nearly three times the same period of 2025, with more than 2,400 tenants paying rent through Rently. The same platform adapts to how each market rents: monthly payments instead of upfront cheques in the UAE; rewards on rent and flexible payment dates in Singapore and Hong Kong. Zoom in: the UAE Dubai alone registered almost 1.2 million tenancy contracts in 2025. Yet many residents still pay up to a full year of rent upfront in one to four cheques, while earning a monthly salary. Easing that upfront burden has become a policy priority: in June 2026, the Dubai Land Department launched Flexi Rent to let tenants pay rent monthly. Rently’s Rent Now Pay Later (RNPL) closes that gap: tenants pay rent monthly, while landlords continue to receive structured, timely payouts. Rently has already handled more than AED 100 million worth of rental contracts in the UAE. Its rental transaction volume has grown more than fivefold year on year, and growth has kept accelerating quarter after quarter, right through a year of regional conflict. Rently works with real estate agencies like White & Co as well as Co-living firms and property managers in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Taimur Khan, Managing Director, Middle East, said, "People in the UAE earn monthly, but most still pay rent upfront in a handful of cheques. That is the gap we are closing. We now bring on more tenants in a single quarter than we did in the whole of 2025, and this facility means we can say yes to many more tenants and to the agencies and landlords we work with, as demand keeps climbing.” Jason Edwards, Partner, Growth Credit, January Capital, added: “Rently addresses a real financing constraint for tenants across different rental markets. This investment underscores January Capital's commitment to supporting fast-growing companies in the Asia-Pacific region with flexible, non-dilutive credit solutions and we are pleased to partner with Rently through this next phase of growth.” Shiv Mahajan, CEO of Rently, commented, "Rent is the biggest payment most people make and still the least flexible. Our ambition is to triple the number of tenants we serve over the next 12 months and become the leading rental payments platform in every market we operate in. This facility gives us the capital to serve more tenants as we scale, while keeping our equity focused on building new products, investing in technology and expanding into new markets.” The facility strengthens Rently’s capital stack as the company prepares for a $10-15 million Series A equity raise to double down on its core offerings and expand into new markets in 2027 and beyond. Rently is leveraging AI to accelerate its growth and automate much of how it operates, so it can keep scaling efficiently as volumes grow. Rently previously raised $3 million in Pre-Series A funding from investors including Hustle Fund, 5I Ventures, Woh Hup, Orvel, Orange Bloom and Feedback Ventures.

articles.title: Tailscale Patches SSH Flaws That Could Let Hacked Devices Gain Root Access on Other Servers
articles.text:
Tailscale has released version 1.104.4 to fix flaws in its built-in SSH server that could let an attacker reach services and files on other servers that only the root user should be able to touch.
The flaws are in how Tailscale SSH forwards network connections, a job the Tailscale background process carries out with root privileges. To use them, an attacker must already control a device that the network's access rules permit to open an SSH session to the target, with forwarding allowed in that rule.
The flaws come from a report called Tailworm, published days before the fix by Erica Windisch of Cyberdione Labs, who tested released versions of the Tailscale client and the self-hosted headscale control server in a lab.
Tailscale SSH decides who can connect using a device's identity and the network's policy file, not a password or key, so an attacker does not need stolen credentials, only a foothold on a device the policy already trusts.
The flaws "don't allow an unauthenticated attacker to connect to arbitrary Tailscale SSH servers," Tailscale said, and an attacker can still reach only the machines the policy file already allows.
Tailscale SSH's server runs only on Linux and the open-source macOS build; the attacker's own device can be any platform.
The problem is in socket forwarding. When a permitted SSH session forwarded a connection to a Unix socket on the server, the Tailscale process checked the path but then operated as root. A timing trick let an attacker swap in a different path after that check, defeating the safeguard meant to limit which sockets forwarding could reach.
In Windisch's own tests, forwarding to the Docker control socket produced a root shell and read the system password file, /etc/shadow, with no administrator rights. Tailscale's bulletin describes the reach more narrowly, saying an attacker could get to root-only sockets such as the Docker socket or the tailscaled local API.
In 1.104.4, Tailscale changed the server to carry out forwarding as the logged-in user rather than as root, and to rely on the operating system's own file permissions in place of its earlier path check. The release covers 4 security bulletins:
- TS-2026-014: the SSH socket-forwarding flaws above, which let a permitted session reach root-only sockets such as the Docker socket or the tailscaled local API.
- TS-2026-015: a way for a permitted SSH session to use up a server's memory and crash the Tailscale process, cutting all Tailscale networking on that node.
- TS-2026-016: a flaw in tailscale serve where a forward to a Unix socket could reach the tailscaled local API, giving remote control of the node, plus a related socket-swap issue.
- TS-2026-017: a flaw where, with TLS serve and 2 or more mounts, one request could receive another mount's permission headers.
What to Do
Users of Tailscale SSH should update to version 1.104.4 or later. If you cannot update a server yet, you can turn off SSH forwarding on it by setting TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 in the tailscaled service environment and restarting the service, which Tailscale says turns off forwarding without disabling Tailscale SSH and blocks several of the more serious findings.
Tailscale also recommends reviewing SSH access rules so that only the users and devices that need access have it.
Tailscale suggests using SSH check mode, which requires a user to sign in again before a session starts, for sensitive systems. Check mode does not stop these forwarding flaws: it guards the start of a session, whereas the forwarding occurs within a session that has already been approved.
If a server may already have been compromised, Windisch's report says the fix alone is not enough. A stolen device key stays valid until the device is deleted at the control plane, because reimaging the machine does not revoke it. Tailscale's notices do not cover this case.
The picture is worse on headscale, the self-hosted control server. On headscale, SSH forwarding is granted on every accepted session and cannot be turned off in the policy, so Windisch's report says every SSH grant there should be treated as giving root. The newest headscale release, version 0.29.5 from October 13, does not fix the reported issues.
Is It a Worm?
Windisch called the chain "wormable." In her tests, one compromised device could spread to every device the policy allowed, with no passwords, no stolen keys, and no user action, in under a second per step.
Two controls stopped the spread in those tests. Writing access rules as single device-to-device pairs held it back, and binding device keys to hardware such as a TPM kept a stolen identity from being reused elsewhere.
Tailscale rejected the worm description. The findings do not describe self-replicating malware that spreads between machines on its own, the company said, but lateral movement limited to the connections a policy file already allows.
It called the privilege-escalation problems "serious security issues," said it had reproduced the main ones, and added that it is still working out which configurations are affected.
Disclosure and Earlier Fixes
As of publication, the 4 bulletins carry no CVE identifiers or severity scores, and none state the oldest affected version. The report also covered Tailscale's app connectors and its serve and funnel features.
Tailscale said the app-connector finding is in conn25, an experimental feature it has not released, and that the connectors customers use today are not affected. Of 5 serve and funnel findings, it fixed 3 and said the other 2 work as designed.
Windisch published the report without coordinating the release with Tailscale first, which she has described as "reported but not coordinated." Tailscale said it received the report on the morning of Saturday, October 24, about 2 hours before Windisch published it, and that its engineers were already looking at the same parts of the code.
Neither Tailscale nor the report says the flaws have been used in real attacks. The proof-of-concept code is not public, and Windisch said she gave it only to Tailscale's security team.
The report is the latest in a run of fixes in the same part of Tailscale this year. In June, Tailscale fixed a separate flaw in Tailscale SSH's Unix-socket forwarding that let an unprivileged user reach a privileged socket, in version 1.98.9.

articles.title: Estas aplicaciones de Apple acaban de recibir un chatbot de IA: requisitos para aprovechar la actualización
articles.text:
Apple incorpora un asistente de inteligencia artificial a su suite de aplicaciones de productividad, que incluye Keynote, Pages y Numbers. El asistente, construido sobre modelos de IA de Apple y de OpenAI, puede interpretar el contexto de un documento para ejecutar tareas como diseñar, animar y perfeccionar diapositivas en Keynote.
En Pages, la compañía indica que el asistente puede redactar, reestructurar y ajustar contenido escrito. En Numbers, por su parte, la herramienta calcula, visualiza y organiza datos, además de sugerir tipos de gráficos y construir tablas personalizadas.
Keynote, Pages y Numbers son compatibles con el Model Context Protocol en macOS 27 o versiones posteriores, lo que permite que agentes de IA de terceros se conecten a las aplicaciones. El asistente se distribuye en fase beta para los dispositivos compatibles con Apple Intelligence y funciona en equipos con iOS 27, iPadOS 27 o macOS 27 o superior.
La actualización alcanza a otras aplicaciones del ecosistema. Pixelmator Pro incorpora la función Generate Fill, que permite editar una parte de una imagen con solo describir el cambio deseado. Según Apple, la herramienta “automáticamente iguala la iluminación, la perspectiva y la textura del entorno para que las ediciones se integren”.
Logic Pro, disponible para Mac y iPad, recibe un rediseño con Liquid Glass y un asistente de IA capaz de “configurar una pista vocal a partir de un solo comando” y de editar proyectos existentes. La aplicación suma además un Browser rediseñado para Mac que utiliza IA en el dispositivo para analizar, clasificar y etiquetar de forma automática los sonidos agregados.
Final Cut Pro también se actualiza con la incorporación de plantillas, gráficos, títulos y transiciones directamente en la aplicación a través de MotionVFX. A esto se suma el Content Hub, integrado dentro de Final Cut Pro, que ofrece una biblioteca de video, fotos y fondos de stock.
Requisitos para acceder a la actualización
Las nuevas funciones estarán disponibles en noviembre de 2026 únicamente para quienes ya cuentan con una suscripción activa a Creator’s Studio de Apple, sin cargo adicional.
Para acceder a las capacidades de inteligencia artificial en Keynote, Pages y Numbers, además, es necesario contar con un dispositivo compatible con Apple Intelligence que ejecute iOS 27, iPadOS 27 o macOS 27 o una versión posterior. El asistente se encuentra, por el momento, en fase beta.
iOS 27.2 llega con mejoras para Siri AI y nuevas funciones de FaceTime
En paralelo a estas novedades, Apple distribuyó iOS 27.2, que expande las capacidades de Siri AI. El asistente ahora puede recordar conversaciones previas, de modo que el usuario puede consultarle sobre información que ya le había proporcionado, como una recomendación de restaurante dada días atrás.
Siri AI también amplía sus fuentes de datos, con acceso a fotos adjuntas en Mensajes, asistentes a eventos del Calendario, buzón de voz y un mejor aprovechamiento del historial de Safari y la lista de lectura. La actualización suma la función Excluded Apps, que centraliza en un solo ajuste la elección de qué aplicaciones pueden acceder a Siri, la búsqueda y las sugerencias, además de permitir la selección y copia de un fragmento específico dentro de una respuesta del asistente.
iOS 27.2 también incorpora la función Dual Capture para las llamadas grupales de FaceTime, que permite activar simultáneamente la cámara frontal y trasera durante una videollamada, de modo que el interlocutor ve tanto al usuario como aquello que está observando. Esta función requiere un iPhone 17 o modelo posterior y que todos los participantes de la llamada cuenten con iOS 27. La actualización suma, además, la posibilidad de incorporar a un intérprete de lengua de señas o un servicio de subtitulado en vivo de terceros durante una llamada de FaceTime.

articles.title: ‘This is such a game-changer’: the Android Kindle app now has handwriting support — and iPads could be getting it next
articles.text:
Amazon has quietly added handwriting support to the Kindle app for Android, giving you one less reason to buy a Kindle Scribe
And iPads could get this soon too
- The Android Kindle app now supports handwriting
- This means you can use a stylus to annotate books
- A support page suggests similar functionality might soon come to Apple devices
One of the big perks of the Kindle Scribe is being able to add handwritten annotations to your books, but it’s a perk that’s no longer exclusive to Amazon’s hardware, as the Kindle app for Android now supports handwritten notes too.
With this update, you can now use a stylus to write directly onto your Kindle books, selecting from different pen styles, colors, and sizes. You can also use this feature to highlight, circle, and underline text.
This could be especially useful for studying, but if you enjoy annotating fiction books, it’s a helpful update there too. It’s not limited to large-screen devices either, with users on Reddit claiming that various standard phones, such as the Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, gained access to this feature as well — though it appears to only work on devices that have native stylus support.
An ereader upgrade — with iOS support possibly incoming
Still, as confirmed by some users, that also means you can access this update on some Android-powered ereaders like certain Boox models.
It’s a feature that’s largely been received positively, with comments on Reddit including “nice surprise,” “I was so happy to see this,” “this is awesome,” and “this is such a game changer.”
Right now, this feature is only available on the Android app, but an Amazon support page mentions that Active Canvas (the feature that allows you to write directly on a Kindle book) is also available on supported iOS devices — so perhaps the iPad and iPhone Duo app will get this update soon.

articles.title: GTA 6 : une fuite annonce un téléchargement colossal sur PS5, commencez à faire de la place
articles.text:
Une fuite donne une première indication du poids de GTA 6 sur PS5, et votre SSD risque de se sentir à l’étroit. Rockstar n’a pas encore confirmé ce chiffre, mais les joueurs vont peut-être devoir arbitrer entre Vice City et leurs jeux déjà installés.
Les joueurs comptent les jours avant de retrouver Vice City (plus que 22 à l’heure où nous écrivons cet article), mais certains pourraient aussi devoir compter les heures devant une barre de progression. À quelques semaines du lancement, une nouvelle fuite donne une première indication du volume de données à récupérer sur PS5. Et votre connexion aura du travail.
Un téléchargement de 210 Go annoncé sur PS5
Dans une publication du 27 octobre reprise par Insider Gaming, le compte spécialisé PlayStation Game Size annonce un téléchargement de 210 Go pour GTA 6. Le média affirme avoir recoupé cette information, sans détailler sa méthode de vérification.
La prudence reste de mise : ce chiffre ne constitue pas une confirmation officielle de Rockstar. Il concerne la version PS5 et ne permet pas de déduire le poids de celle destinée aux Xbox Series X et Series S.
Autre nuance : la publication parle bien de taille de téléchargement. Cela ne suffit pas à établir précisément l’espace libre nécessaire pendant l’installation, ni la place occupée après celle-ci. Une éventuelle mise à jour au lancement pourrait également ajouter des données à récupérer, mais rien ne permet pour l’heure d’en annoncer le volume.
Le préchargement laissera une semaine pour se préparer
Pour se représenter ce que pèsent ces 210 Go, quelques calculs donnent un ordre d’idée. Avec un débit constant de 100 Mb/s entièrement consacré au téléchargement, il faudrait environ 4 h 40 pour tout récupérer. À 10 Mb/s, l’attente grimperait à 46 h 40, contre 28 minutes avec une connexion maintenant réellement 1 Gb/s.
Ces durées sont théoriques : elles ne prennent en compte ni les autres usages de la connexion, ni les variations de débit, ni les limites éventuelles des serveurs. Même avec la fibre, le débit annoncé par votre opérateur ne garantit pas celui obtenu sur la console.
Rockstar confirme toutefois que le préchargement commencera le 12 novembre à minuit, heure locale, une semaine avant la sortie du 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Les précommandes numériques pourront en profiter, tout comme les acheteurs de la version boîte une fois leur code reçu et activé.
La version boîte ne vous évitera d’ailleurs aucun téléchargement : elle contiendra un code, sans disque. Avec une connexion modeste, le préchargement dès le 12 novembre sera donc précieux. Après des années à attendre GTA 6, autant éviter de passer la soirée du lancement à attendre les derniers gigaoctets.

articles.title: SK hynix Expects Memory Demand to Outpace Supply Through 2030
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
SK hynix Expects Memory Demand to Outpace Supply Through 2030
SK hynix reported its latest Q3 2026 quarterly results with a record $78.129 billion in net revenue. However, the company also shared a market outlook, highlighting its long-term supply agreements and plans for expansion with new fab capacity and facilities under construction. For the consumer market, the outlook is grim as SK hynix expects memory demand to continue outpacing supply through 2030. The main supply constraint is the complexity of leading-edge semiconductor nodes and the lengthy lead times for fab construction, which take years to translate into regular mass production volumes.
Despite sustained demand, pricing is also on an upward trajectory, with the average selling price of memory modules in Q3 increasing by over 20% compared to Q2. This is concerning, as it suggests that the prices of consumer electronics devices might jump by more than 20% once memory inventory is depleted. Although SK hynix expects a decrease in PC and smartphone shipments, this will be offset by a strong rollout of AI data centers. About 14 major customers, including most hyperscalers, have signed 5-year long-term agreements, which will account for over 50% of total capacity sold for 2027 and 2028.SK hynix expects its DRAM business to continue aggressively adopting the 1c nm node. As a reminder, DRAM nodes differ from conventional logic nodes. DRAM manufacturers use variations of 10 nm, scaling them with more EUV layers or advanced features. For SK hynix, the currently dominant 1b node is around 12-13 nm in actual design and involves about 4 layers of EUV patterning, while the most advanced 1c node shrinks to 11-12 nm with 5-6 layers of EUV. SK hynix will use the 1c node to manufacture HBM4E, LPDDR6, and DDR5 memory. For the older 1b node, SK hynix produces DDR5, LPDDR5X, HBM3E, and HBM4.
In the HBM segment, Q4 is expected to see HBM4 surpass HBM3E in shipment and revenue share, and negotiations for 2027 HBM have been finalized. Finally, for NAND, the majority of production output is now 321-layer NAND Flash, and SK hynix continues to work on HBF solutions.
