articles.title: Corsair Warthog case review: A rugged, military-themed chassis with plenty of airflow
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Warthog’s rugged military looks are the standout feature of this mid-tower, but its higher price and noise-normalized cooling performance on the video card keep it from soaring above the rest
Reasons to buy
- + Military theme
- + Rugged construction
- + Roomy interior for components
- + Designed for high airflow
- + Cool-looking front panel IO
- + Built-in GPU support bracket
- + Light over rear IO panel
Reasons to avoid
- - Cost
- - Below average noise-normalized cooling for GPU
- - Can’t mount rads in front and side simultaneously
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Fractal arguably kicked off the wood accent PC trend with the North line, and the company says its new Summit case is built for “...expressive, high-performance systems combining distinctive Scandinavian design and advanced cooling potential.” The chassis sports FSC-certified wood (timber verified to come from responsibly managed, socially beneficial, and economically viable forests) for details like the front surround and solid wood feet. There’s no doubt it’s a good-looking case, but if you want to show off the wood, you’ll want to stick to the Chalk White or Black versions, as it blends in with the Blackout SKU we tested.
Corsair’s latest case, the Warthog, is a military-inspired chassis that resembles a fuel canister (jerry can) you’d see on military vehicles. Based loosely on the Vengeance C70 case from 2012, which looked more like an ammunition container, the new Warthog evolved into a much better-looking, more functional chassis for today’s hardware in either of the two colorways.
The Warthog does resemble its predecessor, and Corsair borrowed some features from the C70 while updating the design with “...even more rugged exterior, significantly more expansion options, and an emphasis on excellent airflow throughout the chassis,” and the company largely succeeded.
The Warthog updates include the InfiniRail Fan Mounting System for flexible fan mounting, a pegboard motherboard tray for custom cable management, room for today’s massive video cards (plus built-in GPU support), and three mounting locations for 360mm radiators and 13 120mm fans. It even has bump guards on the front I/O for that all-in military aesthetic. The fighter jet-style front IO includes USB ports, one fast USB 3.2 Gen2x2 (20 Gbps) Type-C port, plus an on/off button for a unique integrated light on the back of the case that illuminates the rear IO area and down.
If you’re into the military look, the Corsair Warthog ($179) and Warthog RS ($199 with fans) absolutely nails it, with plenty of other features that make it a compelling mid-tower chassis. We'll cover more details inside and outside the chassis, showcasing the features and any issues we encounter during the build. We'll also run the case through thermal and noise testing to show how it performs compared to others and whether it could make our best PC cases list. Below are the case's specifications from Corsair.
Corsair Warthog Product Specifications
| Type | Mid-Tower | 
| Dimensions (H x L x W) | 21.4 x 21 x 11.1-inches (546 x 534 x 284mm) | 
| Motherboard Support | Mini-ITX, Micro ATX, ATX, E-ATX | 
| Back-connect Motherboard Support | Yes | 
| Color | Olive Drab Black | 
| Storage Support | (1) 3.5-inch (2) 2.5-inch | 
| PCIe Expansion Slots | 7 | 
| Fan Support | Top - 3x120/2x140mm Front - 3x120/2x140/2x200mm Bottom - 3x120mm Side: 3x120/2x140mm Rear - 1x120/140mm | 
| Pre-installed fans | (3) RS Series (120mm rear, 2x200mm front) | 
| Radiator Support | Front - 360/280/240mm Top - 360/280/240mm Side - 360/280/240mm Rear - 140/120mm | 
| CPU Cooler Clearance | 190mm | 
| GPU Clearance | 393mm (w/ front fans) 405mm (w/o front fans) | 
| Vertical GPU Support | Yes (requires riser card) | 
| PSU Length | 200mm | 
| Dust Filters | Front, Bottom, and Side | 
| Other features | 3x pre-installed fans, integrated GPU support, Infinrail system, light on rear I/O, Military theme | 
| MSRP | $179.99 (w/o fans) $199.99 (w/pre-installed fans) | 
| Warranty | 2 Years | 
Features of the Warthog
▶️ External Features
Externally, the Warthog doesn’t look like many other cases. Sure, it has the general shape of a classic mid-tower, but the front and windowed panel break up the monotony we’re used to, with bars resembling a fuel tank breaking up the window pane and front of the chassis. The front and side panels also use Corsair’s steel 3D-Y perforations (also found on the 4000) for increased airflow, and they look different from most other cases. It also has a military-inspired front I/O, sturdy built-in steel handles, and the familiar army olive drab color (it also comes in black). It just screams military industrial design.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Looking more closely at the front of the case, we get a better view of the door that covers the front panel fans. We get a close-up of the contrasting black 3D-Y perforations, which not only look better than the typical circular holes, but are said (by Corsair) to allow 12% better airflow. Next to the red handle, Corsair stamps the model WX-01 in white on a thin crossmember in the upper-right corner (it’s WX-02 for the black SKU). Pull the red tab on the left, and it opens via two hinges on the right, revealing the magnetically attached dust filter.
At the bottom of the front panel is the fighter-jet-inspired I/O panel, complete with bump guards and a flip-up cover over the reset button. On flight control panels, the guards prevent accidental activation of critical or dangerous switches. A flip-up toggle would be cool here, too. Port-wise, it has everything you could want. On the left is a 3.5mm audio jack for headphones and a microphone. Next to it is the recessed power light that glows red when powered on. Next to it is the USB 3.2 (20 Gbps) Type-C port. Between the bump guards are a square power button, the cool flip-up reset button, and the light button. All buttons feel solid under my fingers and not wobbly or cheap. On the right are two USB 3.2 (5 Gbps) Type-A ports. What’s here is typical fare, but it looks a lot cooler than most front IOs.
The tempered-glass side panel doesn’t offer a full view inside. Instead, diagonal, crossmember-like ribs break it into one main viewable area, with two smaller triangles at the ends. On military vehicles, this reinforces the weaker glass while still allowing visibility. On the Warthog, it just adds to the rugged look, and maybe lets you get away with a little less time managing cables — I kid, clean up those cables! The panel is secured to the frame with two tabs at the bottom and four ball-and-socket joints at the top, two on each side. Pull toward you at the top to release, then pull up to remove. Simple, and it felt secure.
The other side panel is solid, except for side venting. The venting matches the front and top panels with the 3D-Y pattern, but here it’s olive drab instead of the black we see everywhere else. Inside is another magnetically attached dust filter. The ‘service panel’ (stenciled in the upper-right corner) is secured the same way as the front, using tabs on the bottom and ball-and-socket joints on top.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
At the top of the case, there’s not much to see—just more 3D-Y perforations for airflow. Many cases let you easily remove the top for easier access to the Infinirail fan/radiator mounts, and the Warthog does too. Loosen the thumbscrews on the back, remove both side panels, and pull the nylon strap.
Flipping the case around, we see the power supply sits at the bottom, and Corsair includes two captive screws for tooless mounting. Above it, seven vertical expansion slots offer plenty of room for large graphics cards and other expansion. The Warthog also supports vertical GPUs up to three slots wide, but you need a riser card accessory. Above that is space for up to a 140mm fan (120mm RS fan included for RS model), and to the left is the IO area. Corsair installed a small light above that shines down on the rear of the case, illuminating the rear IO area and back of the case, which is certainly useful when plugging in cables.
On the bottom of the case, there isn’t too much going. The Warthog does have a removable dust filter that slides out from the windowed side of the chassis. I prefer this location because, if the filter pulls out from the rear, you'll likely need to move your heavy case to get it out.
▶️ Internal Features
Inside the case, we see a single-chamber design with visual separation only between the power supply area at the bottom and the rest of the case. You won’t find a fancy air guide to feed the video card, but we do spy the small (but effective) adjustable GPU support strut. Beyond that, there’s nothing special at first glance.
The motherboard tray has plenty of cutouts for wiring, but there isn’t much space to route connectors through. Sometimes you need to flex the frame a bit to get larger ones through, like the ATX connector. That’s not ideal, but it isn’t a big deal, even with a motherboard already mounted. The good news is there are no rubber grommets to pull through the holes. While we’re here, we also get a better look at the pegboard feature, which lets you custom-manage cables on the back side. For those planning to build a PC with rear-connect motherboards, the Warthog supports all of them (Asus BTF, Gigabyte Stealth, MSI Project Zero).
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Looking at the front of the case from the inside, we see the massive pre-installed 200mm RS fans that come with the “RS” version of the chassis. Corsair says the magnetic half-dome-bearing fans spin up to 1,000 RPM and move up to 135 CFM of air at a low 36.5 dBA. They are quiet and move a fair amount of air. The front area supports up to 3x120mm fans or radiators.
Looking up at the ceiling from below, you'll see Corsair’s Infinirail system (also on the front, but hidden by the fans), which lets you slide and position fans and radiators where you need them. Although the case fits up to 3x120mm radiators here, they will protrude into the case and can cover the top of your motherboard in many cases. Be sure to mount your motherboard and connect the EPS plugs before you install a top radiator.
At the bottom rear, you can see the power supply area, along with space to route cables for any headers along the bottom of the motherboard. The bottom chamber is also vented into the rest of the chassis. It won’t radiate much heat, since the power supply draws filtered, cool air from below.
Opening up the other side of the chassis gives a better look at the side fan/rad mounts and the default cable-routing options. There is 50mm between the motherboard tray and the outside panel, which is plenty of room to route cables, even with reckless abandon. The pegboard motherboard tray, part of Corsair’s RapidRoute 2.0 cable management system, gives you plenty of freedom to move the cable-ratcheting strap mounts.
From the back, we can see the motherboard tray mounting for your SSD and HDDs. Corsair uses a combo drive plate connected via a thumbscrew. You can install two 2.5-inch drives and one 3.5-inch drive on the combo plate, which should be enough for most users in 2026. Note that to access the back of your motherboard (to mount a cooler, for example), you need to remove this combo plate.
Overall, I do like the look of this rugged, military-themed case, particularly in the olive drab colorway. The fighter jet-inspired front IO panel and jerry can-like look stand out among the played-out designs we’re used to, without looking like a failed attempt at abstract art. Inside, there’s plenty of room for components, even multiple radiators. That said, it is polarizing. Either you like the look, or you don’t. There isn’t much in between.
Joe Shields is a staff writer at Tom’s Hardware. He reviews motherboards and PC components.

articles.title: Robôs de limpeza fazem bonito durante feira em São Paulo • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Resumo
- A Redroad, marca de soluções inteligentes de limpeza, apresentou três robôs de limpeza durante a HigiExpo 2026, feira em São Paulo.
- Os robôs RD10 Pro, RD55 e RD70 Pro atendem a diferentes portes de espaços, desde pequenos ambientes até grandes áreas.
- Os preços sugeridos são de US$ 14.900, US$ 32.900 e US$ 41.900, respectivamente.
A marca de soluções inteligentes de limpeza Redroad demonstrou três robôs durante a HigiExpo 2026, feira voltada ao setor de limpeza que ocorreu em São Paulo, na última semana. A companhia garante não apenas produtos com altíssima tecnologia, mas também uma solução completa para os clientes – em sua essência, pessoas jurídicas – que optarem por implementá-los em suas localidades nos próximos meses.
O responsável pela marca, Danny Cui, conta ao Tecnoblog quais são os pilares das novidades reveladas na capital paulista:
- Linha para diferentes portes: os três modelos atendem desde espaços pequenos, como academias e casas de repouso, a grandes áreas, como aeroportos e fábricas. “Como na limpeza comercial existem muitos setores diferentes, precisamos oferecer uma linha ampla de produtos”, disse Cui.
- Operação local: a empresa montou um escritório em São Paulo com central de atendimento em português, um centro de serviço e um estoque de peças de reposição. Os planos incluem, no futuro, uma unidade de montagem em Jacareí, no interior de São Paulo, que vai trabalhar com componentes principais importados.
- IA física: o termo delimita os algoritmos que permitem ao robô perceber o ambiente e se adaptar quando algo muda no caminho. Na prática, a equipe escaneia o local do cliente com um aparelho portátil com o objetivo de criar mapas e rotinas de limpeza antes mesmo de enviar o robô.
- Pós-venda em três camadas: a Redroad explica que os clientes obtêm atendimento via telefone, acesso remoto ou com técnicos de campo que visitam a localidade para fazer os reparos. “Respondemos à dúvida em até duas horas, encontramos a causa e a solução em até 24 horas e consertamos em até 48. Se não conseguirmos consertar, fornecemos máquinas substitutas”, afirmou o executivo.
A Redroad aproveitou a feira em São Paulo para reforçar que quer ser mais do que um fornecedor capaz de entregar dispositivos de limpeza comercial; ela se posiciona como uma parceria que estará junto do cliente desde a detecção das necessidades até o fornecimento dos equipamentos e o posterior pós-venda, inclusive com visitas de manutenção preventiva – ou seja, revisões programadas antes que surjam problemas.
“No fim das contas, o cliente final não precisa do equipamento, ele precisa garantir que o piso esteja limpo todos os dias”, disse Cui ao Tecnoblog. O executivo revelou que os contratos com os clientes costumam durar de 12 meses a cinco anos.
Conheça os produtos
Os três modelos demonstrados pela Redroad funcionam em pisos rígidos de vários tipos – mármore, madeira, granito, cimento, epóxi, cerâmica e piso plástico – e podem ser acompanhados à distância por aplicativo, segundo a fabricante. A ideia é que o cliente escolha o robô pelo tamanho e pelas características do espaço, em vez de adaptar o local ao equipamento.
Os dispositivos compartilham o mesmo software e a mesma estrutura de serviço, o que permite combiná-los num mesmo espaço. Cui dá o exemplo de um supermercado: o robô maior poderia cuidar dos corredores largos com eficiência, enquanto o menor chegaria perto das bordas e garantiria a limpeza embaixo das prateleiras. “Isso sim é uma solução”, resumiu o executivo.
RD10 Pro
O RD10 Pro é o modelo compacto da linha atual, pensado para espaços apertados, como os corredores entre prateleiras de lojas de conveniência. Ele mede 52 cm de comprimento, 42 cm de largura e 49 cm de altura, e pesa 26 kg. A Redroad afirma que o corpo de 42 cm é o mais estreito da categoria. O tamanho reduzido também facilita a entrada em elevadores e a passagem por catracas.
O robô tem dois modos de trabalho: lavagem de piso, com até 3 horas de autonomia, e varrição, com até 8 horas. Ele limpa uma faixa de 350 mm a 0,6 m/s, o que rende de 756 a 1.008 m² por hora, e sobe rampas com até 10% de inclinação. Duas escovas de rolo fazem a lavagem com alta pressão, e o sistema separa os resíduos secos dos molhados. A limpeza chega rente a paredes e pilares, pontos que costumam ficar para trás. Os tanques de água limpa e de água suja têm 10 litros cada, com um reservatório auxiliar de 4 litros.
O RD10 Pro combina visão e laser para se orientar melhor no ambiente. Ele usa câmera de profundidade 3D, sensores ultrassônicos, LiDAR – o sensor que mede distâncias com laser, também presente em carros autônomos e tablets de ponta – e um sensor de movimento (IMU), e desvia de obstáculos em 360°. O ruído fica abaixo de 65 dB, e o robô volta sozinho à base para recarregar a bateria de 20 Ah. A estrutura aberta, de desmontagem rápida, simplifica a manutenção diária. A autolimpeza do sistema de sucção vem de série; a do tanque de água suja é opcional.
A fabricante recomenda o modelo para hospitais, escritórios, shoppings, escolas, hotéis, restaurantes, academias e casas de repouso. O preço sugerido é de US$ 14.900, cerca de R$ 80,5 mil na cotação de hoje (26/10).
RD55
O RD55 é o produto intermediário, para áreas médias e grandes. Mede 82 cm de comprimento, 68 cm de largura e 113 cm de altura, e pesa 170 kg. O principal diferencial é a integração com os sistemas de elevadores e de controle de acesso dos prédios, o que permite ao robô trabalhar em vários setores de edifícios comerciais e escritórios.
O aparelho limpa uma faixa de 550 mm e rende até 1.980 m² por hora. Duas escovas de rolo lavam o piso e também recolhem pequenos resíduos secos. O rodo de sucção tem câmara dupla, recurso que, segundo a Redroad, reduz a água que sobra nas frestas do piso. Os tanques têm 45 litros para água limpa e 45 litros para água suja. O próprio robô faz a própria limpeza de tanque, com remoção de 95% dos detritos, e o ventilador do sistema de sucção tem vida útil estimada de 10 mil horas. O modelo pode trabalhar com uma estação-base que faz a recarga, reabastece a água e limpa o tanque.
A navegação combina laser e visão computacional: o robô monta o mapa do ambiente e se localiza nele ao mesmo tempo, com LiDAR, câmeras e sensores de deslocamento das rodas. Para desviar de obstáculos, cruza informações de vários quadros captados pela frente e por trás. O controle pode ser feito no próprio robô, pela nuvem ou pelo celular.
A bateria suporta 8.000 ciclos de recarga e garante cerca de 3 horas de operação. O ruído fica abaixo de 68 dB, e a garantia é de um ano para o equipamento completo. Os cenários indicados são shoppings, hospitais, supermercados, escritórios e fábricas. O preço sugerido é de US$ 32.900, cerca de R$ 177,8 mil.
RD70 Pro
O RD70 Pro é o maior produto da linha, voltado a aeroportos, grandes armazéns e supermercados. Ele tem bastante apelo para “grandes espaços públicos”, segundo Danny Cui. Para se ter uma ideia de sua robustez, o robô pesa 199 kg sem água. Na versão com escovas circulares, usa discos de 20 polegadas, que, segundo a Redroad, cobrem o dobro da área por passada de produtos concorrentes. A pressão de 27 kg sobre o piso ajuda a remover sujeira incrustada.
O robô limpa uma faixa de 560 mm, anda a até 4 km/h e rende até 2.040 m² por hora. Também sobe rampas com até 6% de inclinação. Os tanques têm 70 litros para água limpa e 50 litros para água suja – somados, são os 120 litros. A bateria de lítio de 100 Ah, que pesa 25 kg, dá cerca de 4 horas de operação e pode ser trocada em um minuto, o que evita esperar a recarga para continuar o trabalho. O robô também volta sozinho para recarregar.
O sistema de navegação NeverLost 360° reúne câmera panorâmica, LiDAR, câmera de profundidade, sensores ultrassônicos, sensor de movimento e para-choques, para que o robô se desloque sozinho e desvie de obstáculos. As limpezas podem ser agendadas conforme a rotina de cada estabelecimento, e o equipamento também pode ser operado manualmente, alternando entre os modos de trabalho.
O RD70 Pro gera relatórios automáticos que servem para inspeção de qualidade, comprovação do serviço feito e rastreabilidade das operações. O ruído fica entre 75 e 80 dB. O modelo segue normas da União Europeia e tem garantia de um ano para o equipamento completo. O preço sugerido é de US$ 41.900, cerca de R$ 226,4 mil.
Robô humanoide vista estande
Além dos três robôs de limpeza, o estande da Redroad na HigiExpo recebeu um robô humanoide, que proporcionou experiências interativas aos visitantes durante os três dias de feira, de 20 a 22 de outubro.
O espaço também teve demonstrações ao vivo dos robôs de limpeza, com limpeza rente às bordas, passagem por corredores estreitos, deslocamento entre andares, integração com sistemas de controle de acesso e retorno automático à base para recarga.
Distribuidores, empresas de serviços de limpeza, equipes de gestão predial e grandes redes varejistas puderam conversar com a equipe da Redroad sobre a escolha de equipamentos, condições para projetos-piloto – as chamadas provas de conceito, em que o cliente testa o robô no próprio ambiente antes de fechar contrato –, aplicações práticas e parcerias comerciais. Segundo a empresa, essas conversas levam em conta as características de cada ambiente e as necessidades específicas de cada projeto.
A companhia aproveitou o momento para anunciar sua chegada ao Instagram, por meio do perfil @redroadbrazil.

articles.title: Ghost Rider : Marvel aurait trouvé le grand méchant du film avec Ryan Gosling
articles.text:
Ghost Rider : Marvel aurait trouvé le grand méchant du film avec Ryan Gosling
L'acteur Connor Storrie, vue dans la série Heated Rivalry, est en discussion avec Marvel Studios pour être le grand méchant du prochain film Ghost Rider.
Inconnu il y a encore quelque mois, l'acteur Connor Storrie a vu sa carrière décoller grâce à la série Heated Rivalry et va peut-être bientôt rejoindre l'une des franchises les plus importantes d'Hollywood : Marvel. Il est en effet pressenti pour incarner l'antagoniste du prochain film Ghost Rider face à Ryan Gosling.
De Heated Rivalry au MCU
Et si Connor Storrie faisait des infidélités au hockey sur glace pour venir jouer les méchants chez Marvel ? C'est en tout cas ce que rapporte nos confrères du Hollywoord Reporter en annonçant que l'acteur de 26 ans est en discussion avec Marvel Studios pour jouer dans le prochain film Ghost Rider.
Réalisé par Shawn Levy (Deadpool & Wolverine), ce futur long-métrage est écrit par Jonathan Tropper (Adam à travers le temps) et racontera l'histoire de Johnny Blaze (Gosling), un cascadeur à moto qui a vendu son âme pour sauver un proche de la maladie et devient l'hôte d'un esprit de vengeance appelé Zarathos.
On ne sait pas encore quel méchant de l'univers des comics Ghost Rider Storrie pourrait incarner mais dans les précédents films Ghost Rider, portés par Nicolas Cage, Blaze faisait face à Méphisto et son fils, Blackheart.
Méphisto est déjà apparu dans le MCU sous les traits de Sasha Baron Cohen (Ali G) dans la série Iron Heart, alors reste à savoir s'il pourrait revenir dans ce futur film.
Le tournage de Ghost Rider commencera l'année prochaine à New York et le film sortira en salles le 26 juillet 2028.
En attendant, vous pouvez voir ou revoir les autres productions du MCU sur la plateforme de streaming Disney+.

articles.title: Une erreur cryptographique vieille de 18 mois contraint Microsoft à bannir des certificats de Windows
articles.text:
Une grave erreur cryptographique a compromis huit clés privées appartenant à l'autorité de certification eMudhra. Microsoft a exclu sept certificats des listes de confiance de Windows et d'Edge, et publié des correctifs exceptionnels pour les appareils privés des mises à jour automatiques des certificats.
Un certificat numérique n'est fiable que si l'autorité qui l'a émis conserve le secret de sa clé privée. Chez eMudhra, cette garantie faisait défaut depuis avril 2025. Huit clés pouvaient être reconstituées à partir d'informations publiques, sans aucune intrusion dans les systèmes de l'entreprise. Détectée le 17 octobre, la faille a conduit les principaux éditeurs de navigateurs à bloquer les autorités compromises. Microsoft a depuis étendu ces mesures à une partie de la hiérarchie de certification du groupe indien, au risque de perturber les services qui en dépendent encore.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Des clés privées réduites à moins de 256 possibilités
À l'origine de l'incident, une erreur commise le 30 avril 2025 lors d'une opération de génération de clés cryptographiques chez eMudhra. Huit autorités de certification intermédiaires ont alors hérité de clés privées anormalement faibles. Six étaient destinées à délivrer des certificats TLS, utilisés pour authentifier les sites et sécuriser les communications web. Les deux autres concernaient la signature de code, qui permet notamment de vérifier l'origine d'un logiciel.
La faille se trouvait dans la valeur même de ces clés. Bien qu'elles reposent sur P-384, un algorithme de cryptographie elliptique offrant normalement un espace de recherche gigantesque, leurs valeurs étaient toutes inférieures à 256. Moins de 256 essais permettaient donc de retrouver chacune d'elles à partir de sa clé publique. Un défaut de génération particulièrement grossier, qui ne remet pas en cause la solidité de P-384, mais la manière dont eMudhra l'a utilisé.
L'entreprise reconnaît une erreur de script lors d'une opération de manipulation des clés, qui aurait produit un second jeu de clés vulnérables, ensuite associé aux certificats publics. Plus embarrassant encore, l'anomalie a échappé aux contrôles pendant près de dix-huit mois, malgré deux cycles d'audit indépendants.
eMudhra a révoqué les huit autorités le 18 octobre et affirme qu'aucune n'avait délivré de certificat final. Un attaquant en possession de leurs clés privées aurait néanmoins pu émettre de faux certificats pour des domaines qu'il ne contrôlait pas. Sur un appareil reconnaissant encore les autorités compromises, ces certificats pouvaient faciliter l'usurpation de sites légitimes et l'interception de communications chiffrées. Les clés de signature de code pouvaient également servir à présenter des logiciels malveillants comme provenant d'un éditeur de confiance.
Microsoft exclut sept certificats de confiance et publie des correctifs hors cycle
Microsoft avait pris de premières dispositions le 20 octobre en inscrivant les huit autorités intermédiaires compromises sur la liste des certificats interdits de Windows. Edge et WebView2 avaient reçu une protection équivalente par l'intermédiaire de leurs mises à jour internes, sans nécessiter l'installation d'une nouvelle version du navigateur.
Le 26 octobre, l'éditeur a élargi sa réponse en excluant six certificats racines eMudhra G3 et un certificat de signature croisée AAA Certificate Services de la liste de confiance de Windows. La même mesure a été appliquée à Edge le lendemain.
Pour Windows 11, cette décision s'accompagne de trois mises à jour cumulatives exceptionnelles : KB5134133 pour Windows 11 24H2, 25H2 et 26H2, KB5134134 pour 26H1 et KB5134130 pour 23H2. Windows 10 et Windows Server disposent également de correctifs.
Ces correctifs s'adressent principalement aux machines isolées, privées du service Microsoft de mise à jour des certificats ou configurées pour désactiver les actualisations automatiques des listes de confiance. Les administrateurs peuvent les récupérer dans le Microsoft Update Catalog. Sur les PC qui reçoivent normalement ces listes, les nouvelles règles de confiance s'appliquent sans intervention particulière.
Les entreprises doivent également recenser les sites, applications et services dont la chaîne de certification passe par l'un des sept certificats retirés. Leur remplacement, ou l'utilisation d'une autre chaîne de confiance reconnue, permettra d'éviter les erreurs de validation. Microsoft déconseille de rétablir localement cette confiance sans avoir préalablement évalué les risques.

articles.title: Colombia tiene ahora un centro de ciberseguridad que detecta ataques en menos de 10 minutos y los resuelve 5 veces más rápido
articles.text:
Indra lanzó en Colombia un Centro de Operaciones de Ciberseguridad (SOC) con inteligencia artificial (IA) para detectar incidentes críticos como ciberataques en menos de 10 minutos y reducir hasta cinco veces los tiempos de investigación y resolución.
El centro incorpora automatización y agentes de IA para clasificar alertas, identificar comportamientos anómalos y priorizar los eventos que requieren intervención, con un alcance que cubre a Colombia y Latinoamérica.
La operación mantiene supervisión humana durante el análisis y la contención de incidentes, según explicó Edwin Balteros, director de ciberseguridad de Indra para Colombia, Ecuador, Centroamérica y el Caribe.
Cómo opera el centro de ciberseguridad
El SOC reúne herramientas de monitoreo que reciben señales desde distintos sistemas de una organización. A partir de esos datos, identifica accesos inusuales, intentos de intrusión, movimientos sospechosos dentro de una red y otros indicios que pueden anticipar un ataque.
La operación busca cubrir el ciclo completo de un incidente: detección, análisis, respuesta, contención y recuperación. El modelo contempla la protección de espacios de tecnologías de la información y de tecnologías operativas, que controlan procesos físicos en sectores como energía, transporte, salud e infraestructura.
Cómo la IA potencia la ciberseguridad
La inteligencia artificial permite filtrar un volumen elevado de alertas y entregar a los analistas una primera evaluación sobre el nivel de riesgo. Los agentes automatizados contrastan eventos, identifican patrones y ayudan a diferenciar una actividad rutinaria de una posible amenaza que requiere una intervención inmediata.
Baltero explicó que los tiempos de revisión se redujeron frente a métodos convencionales. “Generalmente, el tiempo promedio de análisis de una alerta se hacía más o menos entre 25 y 30 minutos. Estamos pasando a hablar de una alerta bien validada entre cuatro y cinco minutos”.
Por qué es clave la rapidez al momento de detectar un incidente de ciberseguridad
La velocidad es uno de los factores que determina la dimensión de un incidente. Un atacante que permanece dentro de una red sin ser detectado puede obtener contraseñas, copiar información, desplazarse entre sistemas, alterar procesos o bloquear archivos y servicios.
“Esta es una competencia de tiempo. Entre más rápido logremos detectar, más rápido garantizamos que no se expanda un ataque dentro de una compañía”, dijo Balteros.
El ejecutivo aclaró que la IA participa en el análisis y la priorización de eventos, aunque los especialistas mantienen la supervisión de las decisiones relacionadas con la respuesta.
Cuáles son los ciberataques más comunes que experimentan usuarios y empresas
El phishing continúa entre las técnicas más utilizadas. “El phishing, que es ese correo malicioso, sigue siendo el top en todos los tipos de ataques”, señaló Balteros. El ataque aprovecha un punto vulnerable que no depende exclusivamente de las defensas tecnológicas: la decisión del usuario que recibe el mensaje.
Según explicó Balteros, los avances en inteligencia artificial mejoraron la redacción, la apariencia y la personalización de mensajes fraudulentos, lo que dificulta reconocerlos a simple vista.
Asimismo, el ransomware mantiene presencia entre las amenazas que enfrentan las organizaciones. En estos casos, los atacantes cifran información o bloquean sistemas y luego exigen un pago.
A ello se suman fraudes que utilizan clonación de voz y videos manipulados para suplantar a directivos, empleados o familiares y obtener transferencias, información reservada o autorizaciones internas.
Qué sectores están más expuestos a ciberataques
El sector financiero continúa entre los objetivos más atractivos por el volumen de recursos e información que administra. A la vez, los ataques contra infraestructuras críticas han ampliado el riesgo a sectores como energía, salud y transporte.
“Hoy en día son todos los sectores”, afirmó Balteros al referirse a los objetivos de los ciberdelincuentes. “Paralizar un hospital es una problemática que pasa más allá del mundo digital. No simplemente la pérdida de una información, sino que puede terminar en afectación de vidas humanas”.

articles.title: US Marines join NATO mission in the Baltic Sea to protect undersea cables from sabotage as Russia continues to lurk — 'around four dozen' recon and intel specialists deployed to deter seabed threats
articles.text:
US Marines join NATO mission in the Baltic Sea to protect undersea cables from sabotage as Russia continues to lurk — 'around four dozen' recon and intel specialists deployed to deter seabed threats
The U.S. military is supporting a NATO mission to protect European undersea infrastructure
A team of around four dozen U.S. Marines is joining a NATO-led operation in the Baltic Sea to help protect undersea internet cables and gas pipelines in the area. In a press release, the U.S. Marine Corps shared its plans to deploy a "specialized team" to support NATO's Enhanced Vigilance Activity Baltic Sentry operation. The move comes amid a backdrop of growing undersea cable interest, movements of Russia's shadow fleet, and fears of sabotage.
The U.S. Marines are being sent from Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune in North Carolina to provide "advanced expeditionary surveillance and tactical reconnaissance capabilities" to the region in support of Finnish and other NATO allies. Marines from 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, and the II Marine Expeditionary Force Information Group are joining the mission.
Capt. Johan Tillander, Chief of Operations for the Finnish Navy, explained that the "experience, skills, and systems of the U.S. Marine Corps are perfectly suited" for the operation, including "monitoring of the Baltic Sea."
While the press release stresses that the Marines are serving in a "supportive, enabling capacity," with European nations taking the lead, the Marines are there to provide "highly specialized, agile force multipliers."
Maj. Gen. Daniel Shipley, Commander of U.S. Marine Corps Forces, Europe and Africa, shared that its participation shows its ability to "rapidly project specialized capabilities where they are most effective," and as a result, "ensuring we can operate seamlessly as a cohesive, lethal team to deter hybrid threats" in the area.
The U.S. deployment means that the operation will be able to "leverage... unique capabilities of Reconnaissance Marines, including small Unmanned Aerial Systems and littoral sensors, to feed vital data directly" to NATO.
The Baltic Sea is the frontline in potential assaults against European undersea infrastructure. Several attempts have been made to sabotage cables in the area, and two cables were cut between Finland, Sweden and Europe back in 2024. Meanwhile, Finland's own concerns about shadow fleet operations led it to set up a dedicated maritime surveillance center earlier this year to monitor activity in the Baltic Sea.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Russia isn't mentioned in the U.S. press release, but the authoritarian nation is one of Europe's biggest threats in the region, and has had worsening relations with European nations for several years, particularly since it went to war with Ukraine in 2022. Over 500 incidents of Russian fishing boats loitering near undersea cables in Europe have been seen in the last four and a half years, showing a persistence in mapping and identifying, if not directly interfering, with global data links in the area.

articles.title: OpenAI branche ChatGPT à iCloud, en plein procès contre Apple
articles.text:
Le 27 octobre, un juge fédéral de San José a accordé à Apple un accès élargi aux preuves détenues par OpenAI. La décision tombe dans le procès pour vol de secrets industriels que la firme de Cupertino a engagé cet été. Le même jour, OpenAI annonçait l’arrivée de connecteurs iCloud pour les applications Mail et Calendrier dans ChatGPT. L’assistant pose ainsi un pied dans l’un des services les plus personnels de l’écosystème Apple.
 Much requested, and now yours to connect: iCloud Mail and Calendar plugins are available in ChatGPT.
Ask ChatGPT to find that email, catch up on your inbox, check what’s next, or update a calendar event. Phew.
Available on all ChatGPT plans on web, desktop, and iOS. https://t.co/g68OWoFVg8
— ChatGPT (@ChatGPT) October 27, 2026
Que peut faire ChatGPT dans une boîte iCloud ?
Une fois le connecteur activé, ChatGPT peut rechercher, lire et trier les messages d’une adresse @icloud.com, @me.com ou @mac.com, en préparer des brouillons et les envoyer. Côté agenda, il consulte les rendez-vous, en crée et en déplace, et il pioche dans le carnet d’adresses pour retrouver un destinataire. De quoi lui demander un tri de la boîte du matin, un créneau de libre dans la semaine ou un brouillon de réponse prêt à relire. L’ensemble fonctionne sur le web, dans les applications de bureau et sur iOS, pour tous les forfaits.
La connexion ne réclame jamais le mot de passe du compte Apple. Il faut générer un mot de passe d’application depuis la page de gestion du compte, une clé dédiée que l’utilisateur révoque quand il veut sans toucher à ses autres accès. C’est la porte qu’Apple laisse ouverte depuis des années aux logiciels de messagerie tiers, et qu’OpenAI emprunte à son tour. iCloud rejoint ainsi Gmail et Outlook parmi les services que l’assistant sait piloter, et l’agent Dots, capable d’enchaîner des tâches sans supervision (mais indisponible chez nous), peut lui aussi s’en servir.
Un lancement en pleine bataille judiciaire
En juillet, Apple a porté plainte devant le tribunal fédéral de San José contre un ancien vice-président du design, Tang Tan, un ancien ingénieur, Chang Liu, ainsi que contre OpenAI et io Products. La marque les accuse d’avoir emporté des secrets industriels liés à ses futurs produits, et réclame au passage l’interdiction de les exploiter.
Le 13 octobre, le juge a d’abord accordé à Apple une collecte de preuves accélérée. Le lendemain, OpenAI s’est engagée à ne pas exploiter les secrets en cause pendant l’instruction, et le magistrat a laissé entendre qu’il accorderait très probablement l’injonction réclamée par Apple. Deux semaines plus tard, la décision sur les preuves élargit encore le terrain de jeu des avocats de Cupertino. OpenAI, de son côté, reproche dans ses écritures à Apple d’avoir encouragé ses salariés à travailler depuis leur iCloud personnel, ce même service qu’elle branche aujourd’hui sur ChatGPT.

articles.title: Keystone to Destroy 18,835 Hardware Wallets After Hackers Steal Device Verification Key
articles.text:
An attacker who gained access to Keystone's website obtained the key that its hardware wallets use to prove they are genuine, the company said in a statement on October 26.
Someone with that key could build counterfeit devices that pass the online check owners use to verify a Keystone. A buyer who trusted a counterfeit could have their crypto stolen, but the incident did not involve owners' recovery phrases or wallet private keys.
Keystone will destroy 18,835 unsold devices that carry the key, and all new devices will get a new one.
Keystone found the unauthorized access on October 20, and its advice to owners depends on when a device arrived. For a device received after that date with the old key, the company said: "Even if such a device passes authentication, we cannot completely rule out the possibility that it is counterfeit."
Owners of such a device should contact Keystone support and use it only after the company confirms it is genuine.
A device delivered before October 20 that passes the check can be considered genuine and used normally, according to Keystone. The company has not said when the attacker first got in.
The attacker exploited a vulnerability in a third-party data monitoring tool used by Keystone's website to escalate privileges, according to the company. That let the attacker obtain customer data and the key.
Keystone blocked the attacker's access on October 20 and has since fixed the vulnerability. It has not said where the key was stored.
How the Device Check Works
The owner scans a QR code on Keystone's verification page with the device, then enters the code the device displays on the page.
In Keystone's open-source firmware, the QR code carries that code in encrypted form, and the device decrypts it with its stored key. So a correct code shows that the device holds the key.
The key is used only for this check. It plays no part in creating recovery phrases, deriving private keys, or signing transactions.
Anyone with a copy of the key could produce the right codes, so a counterfeit device carrying it could pass the check. Such devices could be sold or shipped to customers, leading to the theft of their crypto, Keystone said. The company has not reported any counterfeit devices or thefts.
The key is written into each device during manufacturing and cannot be erased or rewritten. The firmware keeps it in memory, which can be written only once, and refuses to accept a second key. So devices already made cannot be switched to the new key.
Customer Records
Keystone first disclosed the breach on October 24, saying a third party had obtained customers' shipping information.
The incident affected 25,964 buyer records from purchases on Keystone's website between 2024 and 2026, the company said on October 26. The records hold names, contact details, shipping addresses, and order details. Keystone's online store runs on Shopify, which stored and managed the records.
Payment card and bank details and government ID numbers were not involved, Keystone said. Purchase records from Amazon and Keystone's other sales channels were not affected.
Keystone has also included 12,873 unpaid checkout records in its response as a precaution. These hold names, contact details, and shipping information from purchases that were never completed.
Some of the affected data should already have been deleted. Keystone had promised to delete shipping information 180 days after each order.
An automated tool Keystone built to erase records in bulk did not work reliably. Some deletions failed, and Keystone did not catch the failures in time.
Keystone is shortening the period it retains customers' personal data from 180 days to 90 days, effective immediately. It has asked Shopify to delete buyers' personal data older than 90 days and expects that to be done on November 3. As of October 27, its privacy policy still listed 180 days.
Keystone is emailing affected customers and plans a page where people can check whether their information was affected.
What Keystone Owners Should Do
Keystone's guidance covers these situations:
- Delivered before October 20: A device that passes the check can be used normally.
- Received after October 20 with the old key: Do not use the device until Keystone support, at support@keyst.one, confirms it is genuine. Keystone told these owners to follow instructions on its device verification page, but the page showed no such instructions as of October 27. Keystone has not said how to tell which key a device carries, or what owners who have already sent crypto to such a device should do.
- Waiting on an order from Keystone's website: Shipping is paused until devices with the new key are ready. As of October 27, the store listed the Keystone 3 Pro as a pre-order expected to ship within 4 to 6 weeks.
- Bought through Amazon or a reseller: The same guidance applies, because it is based on when a device arrived, not where it was bought. Keystone sells through Amazon official stores and authorized resellers. Keystone has not said whether devices with the old key are still on sale there.
- Already holding crypto with a Keystone: Owners do not need to move their crypto just because of the incident, Keystone said. Those with a device received after October 20 with the old key should still follow the steps above.
- Scam messages: Treat any call, text, email, or letter offering a refund, a replacement device, a recall, wallet verification, or help moving crypto as a scam. Keystone will not ask anyone to return a device. Never enter a recovery phrase into a device you did not order, and type keyst.one into your browser instead of following links.

articles.title: SK hynix Announces 3Q26 Financial Results
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
SK hynix Announces 3Q26 Financial Results
SK hynix Inc. announced today that it has recorded 104.6155 trillion won in revenues, 83.3338 trillion won in operating profit (with an operating margin of 80%), and 39.7756 trillion won in net profit (with a net margin of 38%) in the third quarter. In a market environment in which prices of key products have risen on the back of growing demand for AI memory, the company once again posted all-time-high quarterly results in both revenue and operating profit, underpinned by the competitiveness of its high-value-added products. In particular, revenue exceeded 100 trillion won for the first time in the company's history. Revenue and operating profit increased by 32% and 38%, from the previous quarter, respectively.
By product, DRAM results were driven by a significant increase in sales of server DDR5 while HBM4 shipments began in earnest. In NAND, sales of 321-layer TLC eSSD expanded, and high-value-added products for data centers continued to grow across the board. The company's financial structure has also become significantly concrete. At the end of the third quarter, cash and cash equivalents stood at 114.5 trillion won, up 26.5 trillion won from the end of the previous quarter, while borrowings decreased by 2.8 trillion won to 15.8 trillion won. As a result, net cash increased to 98.7 trillion won.Memory supply shortage to persist through 2030
SK hynix analyzed that a virtuous cycle has taken hold in which AI-driven productivity gains and new revenue generation in areas such as software development, customer service, and search lead to greater AI adoption, which in turn drives increased investment in infrastructure. It also projected that, as the drivers of AI investment move beyond the early stage, when a small number of companies accounted for most of it, and broaden to include general enterprises and nation-level initiatives, the global AI data center infrastructure market will continue to grow steadily.
The company likewise expects the memory market to sustain its growth, led in the short term by enterprise and personal AI and, over the mid-to-long term, by physical AI such as autonomous driving and robotics.
The company assessed that supply, on the other hand, is not keeping pace with the growth of the market. Given technical difficulty of leading-edge processes and the long lead time required to build new production facilities, it expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030.
Expanding production capacity and strengthening product competitiveness to achieve a further step up in growth next year
Building on these favorable conditions, the company plans to accelerate the expansion of production capacity and the strengthening of product competitiveness in order to sustain the current growth momentum, and to scale up revenue and profit one step further next year.
First, the company plans to rapidly increase the portion of its 10 nm-class 6th generation (1c) process technology and expand sales of DDR5 and LPDDR5 SOCAMM for AI servers, thereby further strengthening its DRAM portfolio centered on high-value-added products.
To respond to surging HBM demand, the company will ramp up M15X to maximum capacity by the end of the year to increase HBM4 production. Accordingly, the company expects HBM4 to surpass HBM3E in both shipment volume and revenue in the fourth quarter and to establish itself as a mainstream product.
In NAND, the company will raise the ratio of its 321-layer process to more than half of its domestic production capacity in the fourth quarter, and thereby increase the supply of high-performance, high-capacity eSSD. Over the mid-to-long term, the company intends to develop NAND into a core solution that enhances the throughput and economic efficiency of AI services, based on HBF and system optimization technologies.
Long-term agreements secured for more than 50% of 2027~2028 production capacity and the company to drastically expand investment next year
To improve mid-to-long term demand visibility and solidify its growth foundation, SK hynix is expanding long-term agreements (LTAs) with customers. The company has currently signed LTAs with 14 major customers, including leading global cloud service providers (CSPs), and is also proactively discussing with a number of customers the possibility of extending the contract terms, which are typically five years.
The LTA volume secured to date corresponds to more than 50% of total production capacity for 2027 and 2028. In particular, by introducing a mechanism that reflects market conditions within a price range agreed upon with customers, the company has established a structure that secures stable profitability while allowing flexible responses to market changes.
Backed by the demand visibility, the company is also moving to expand its production capabilities. Next year, with the Yongin Phase 1 entering full-scale operation and domestic and overseas infrastructure investment gaining momentum, investment is expected to increase significantly. The company nevertheless plans to adjust the scale and timing of its investment flexibly, after carefully weighing customer demand, product competitiveness, profitability and investment efficiency.
Most of the gains from the Kioxia investment to be shared with shareholders, with approximately 100 trillion won in shareholder returns to be executed this year
As previously indicated in August, SK hynix announced its additional shareholder return plan. For fiscal year 2026, the company will pursue shareholder returns totaling approximately 100 trillion won, comprising cash dividends of 30 trillion won or more and share repurchases and cancellations of 60 trillion won or more in total, including the 40 trillion won announced in August. Through this, the company intends to fulfill its commitment to return 50% or more of free cash flow (FCF). Of this, the 40 trillion won share repurchase announced in August was completed last week, and the shares will be cancelled shortly.
The company also set out its principles: the dividend amount will be determined on the basis of operating results; if significant investment gains arise, they will be returned additionally through special dividends; and share repurchases will continue every quarter.
At today's meeting, the Board of Directors resolved on a third-quarter cash dividend of 14 trillion won and a share repurchase of 20 trillion won. Of the shares to be repurchased, 10 trillion won, earmarked for shareholder returns, will be cancelled in full, while the remaining approximately 10 trillion won will be used for employee compensation and is not included in the shareholder return total.
The third-quarter dividend is 20,000 won per share, consisting of a 10,000-won dividend reflecting improved earnings and a 10,000 won special dividend that shares the gains from the Kioxia investment. The company has decided to return to shareholders most of the gains realized from its Kioxia investment this year.
SK hynix emphasized that it will deliver stable results based on robust memory demand growth and technological competitiveness and the company will consistently share financial achievements with our shareholders.

articles.title: Planet Zoo 2’s coral-bedecked aquariums and leafy aviaries definitely drew me in — but its improved interface and more flexible tools are what make it my new favorite management sim
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
There's a lot to love about Planet Zoo 2. Graphics have had a definite glow-up, while new habitat options like aquariums and aviaries have made zoos feel far more varied and alive. But the biggest upgrade for me is how much more fluid the tools and interfaces feel, making it far easier than ever before to whip up your dream zoo.
Reasons to buy
- + Aquariums and aviaries add huge variety to zoos
- + New animal models look gorgeous
- + Massive improvements to tools make decorating far easier
Reasons to avoid
- - Wildlife reserves slightly lacking in depth
- - Terrain paint tool lacks subtlety
- - Some bugs on release — although they're being quickly patched
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Planet Zoo 2 is the sequel to 2020’s zoo-building management sim. And it’s crammed with more animals, scenery items, and game modes than ever, so you can really let your creativity run wild.
Building zoos is my happy place. Life is stressful, the cost of living is shocking, and politics is so absurd I often feel like I’m being doped with increasing levels of satire to make the world’s first irony-immune man. Playing games like Planet Zoo 2 lets me spend time in a simpler world, where I can spend five hours tweaking the placement of ferns and rocks to make simulated siamangs happy.
As a result, I’ve spent a lot of time playing the original Planet Zoo. More than a lot, actually. Over 1,100 hours. That’s more than 45 days straight — a fact that makes me feel slightly queasy about my priorities in life. I’ve spent more time experiencing its highs and dealing with its limitations than I’ve spent with my extended family. So, naturally, as soon as I heard Planet Zoo 2 was in development, I knew I had to be the person to put it through its paces.
With the addition of aquariums, aviaries, wildlife reserves and more besides, I couldn’t wait to get my teeth into the new game and see what it was capable of. Even if it meant jettisoning a thousand hours of work, binning my old zoo and starting building from scratch, I was eager to see how all the new tools and content upgraded play. So are the two games birds of a feather, or is Planet Zoo 2 of a different stripe entirely?
Wings, fins and fur
Without a doubt, aquariums are my favorite new feature. Not only can you add a fantastic variety of undersea beasties, but you can also decorate tanks with rich-looking reefs, with everything from fronds of seaweed to brightly colored corals.
As a bit (okay, a lot) of a Planet Zoo nerd, when Planet Zoo 2 was announced, I had plenty of things on my mental wishlist of upgrades I’d like to see. But top of my list were the addition of both flying birds and fish, two types of critters that felt conspicuous in their absence from the huge roster of DLCs released for the original game. So honestly, it was pretty pleasing to see both of these kinds of exhibits included when previews of the game dropped.
Flat out my favorite addition has been aquariums. These new piscine enclosures are as pretty as a picture. Aquariums feel really versatile, whether you want huge open-air tanks or to build a wall of fish into your restaurant. Walkthrough tunnels make creating immersive exhibits a breeze, and the need to filter habitats separately depending on whether they require fresh, brackish, or salty water adds an extra layer of — excuse the pun — depth.
Underwater decorations also look fantastic, allowing you to create really richly colored coral reefs and rafts of seaweed and grasses. But naturally, the animals in Planet Zoo are the stars of the show, and there’s a huge variety of sea life on offer to populate your tanks, whether you’re looking for sharks, rays, turtles or schools of fish. Wisely, Frontier has steered away from including many sea mammals like whales and dolphins — a sensible decision in light of the increasing attention that’s been paid to the ethics of keeping highly intelligent, social mammals in small tanks — but the game does include manatees, and there’s still huge potential here for semi-aquatic mammals like seals and walruses.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Leading up to Planet Zoo 2’s release, I was particularly excited about the addition of flying birds, as this adds a whole new dimension to your habitats compared to flightless fowl like ostriches and emus. While aviaries — essentially roof support poles and netting sitting over a classic habitat — don’t feel quite as fresh an experience as creating aquariums, I can still see how I’ll be able to use them to create stunning enclosures. And the variety of feathered friends already on offer is decent, adding everything from toucans to brightly colored long-tailed parakeets.
In fact, animals in general have had a definite glow-up in Planet Zoo 2. Not only have the earliest, lower-definition critters from the base game, like lions and African elephants, received new meshes to bring them in line with sleeker-looking critters from later expansion packs, but fauna in general looks stunning in this game.
There’s also a really solid variety of animals on offer at launch, from gila monsters to giant pandas. Don’t get me wrong: some of my personal favorites from the original game and expansions still aren’t here. Frankly, any zoo that doesn’t have fennec foxes in it is not a zoo I want to spend time in. But all the classics are here, with just enough funky additions — Goodfellow’s tree-kangaroo, anyone? — that I’m already pretty jazzed about additions that might be coming up with future updates.
All told, the variety offered by Planet Zoo 2 makes creating diverse, vibrant zoos feel easier than ever.
Management material
Given that Frontier Developments has launched two more park management games — Planet Coaster 2 and Jurassic World Evolution 3 — in the almost seven years since the OG Planet Zoo’s release, its core gameplay loop has inevitably evolved.
First off, career mode feels the most well-rounded it’s been in a Planet game to date. While you’ve always been able to dip in and out of individual missions on the map to complete objectives and pick up bronze, silver, and gold medals, the progression between them feels increasingly organic.
Functioning as an extended tutorial, career mode leads you through a variety of maps and scenarios throughout the world. As you complete bronze medals at each zoo, you’ll learn new mechanisms and unlock new accreditation tiers, in turn granting you access to higher tiers of animals. While this does mean your progression is somewhat locked to missions, the non-linear connection between maps made me feel much freer to pop in and out of maps than past games.
A big part of this is down to the addition of wildlife reserves. Releasing animals was a relatively shallow mechanic in Planet Zoo — enabling you to offload unneeded creatures in return for dollars or Conservation Points — in its sequel, this has been spun out into a sub-game in its own right.
Wildlife reserves’ core gameplay loop is pretty straightforward. When you arrive in a new reserve, you’ll create ecosystems for released animals by painting one in the landscape, clearing any invasive plant species, and balancing the terrain and plant requirements. Once it’s ready, you’ll be required to release animals from your zoos of the compatible type, balancing the ecosystem, and place research items like camera traps and acoustic monitors to unlock higher levels of research in your zoos.
I’ll be honest here: wildlife reserves are the area that I feel both sound like the most transformative on paper and yet haven’t fully clicked for me in practice. Part of this is because they rely heavily on my least favorite tool: the terrain painter — more on that shortly.
But it’s also just because these mechanics feel relatively shallow. These reserves don’t really require much ongoing management, and given there’s not much more detailed interplay among the flora and fauna once it’s placed, you can basically just set and forget these areas. As a result, I often found myself just rushing to establish ecosystems and dump the required animals in them so I could return to meatier zoo management. I’m hoping that the more I play with them, the more I’ll find to love about these freer locations, but so far they’ve stood out the least to me.
One other factor that's occasionally caused me slight discomfort is the presence of bugs. No, I'm not talking about those tarantula exhibits: at release, there have definitely been some odd issues creeping in.
I've encountered nothing game-breaking, just slightly hinky behavior here and there. At one point, items I was meticulously placing using the advanced move tools would randomly jump to a different position once I clicked place. Meanwhile, I've experienced several well-documented issues where animals ghost through their bars or get boxed up en masse inside their habitats for no clear reason. Fair play to Frontier Developments, though: they promised to patch these issues pretty quickly and, at the time of publishing, I think all of these issues have been fixed.
If you're wanting a freer experience than career mode can offer, Planet Zoo 2 still has all the other game modes you loved from the original. Franchise mode lets you focus on building your global zoo network from scratch as always, adding the ability to create your own wildlife reserves to help you feel like you’re really contributing to global conservation.
But hands-down my favorite gameplay mode is still Sandbox. I’m a bit prone to hyperfixating on small details — I know: the dude with 1,100 hours in the game is a bit obsessive. You don’t say. And that’s why I love this mode. Being able to concentrate on tweaking every last detail and focusing on building the most realistic zoo I can without needing to sweat about profitability or management just speaks to the creative part of my brain.
And, on that front, Planet Zoo 2 is better than ever.
Build baby, build
Given I’m talking about a game crammed with gorgeous wildlife, brand new habitats and new game modes, I’ll admit this makes me sound tiresomely dull. But honestly, what’s gotten me most excited about Planet Zoo 2 is the part that should be the most boring: logistics upgrades.
Rather than management sims, I’ve always felt like the Planet games are fantastically creative park design tools with a fun game on the side. And these tools have been refined across the board.
Let’s start with the placement tools. Not gonna lie, on release the placement tools in Planet Zoo were so rigid I can honestly understand if many people rarely dug into creating detailed scenery. Fortunately, these have been significantly improved — they feel more fluid, while the scale tools from Planet Coaster 2 and mirroring tools have been added, giving each decorative item significantly more versatility and making it much easier to create organic-looking areas like rockfaces.
Frustrating memories of trying to select scenery items in Planet Zoo — with their utterly random-seeming hitboxes — still haunt me to this day, particularly as deselecting items felt super awkward. In its sequel, these tools have been overhauled, not only making it easier to select and deselect items even on controller but also providing a range of toggles that allow you to restrict selection to certain types of objects, from nature objects to pathing.
While creating pathing used to involve an exasperating degree of trial and error in the original, pathing tools have had significant improvements here. Alongside the original’s straight and curved pathing options, upgrades from Planet Coaster 2 and the Jurassic World Evolution series have been introduced, like stamp and draw tools. This makes it trivial to introduce more organic-looking paths than ever and even super-precise circular courtyards and viewing areas.
All of these features contribute to making buildings and decorative items feel far easier and more fluid. But it’s not only placing man-made structures that has been improved. I’d argue that one of the hardest areas of creating your dream zoo in Planet Zoo used to be making natural scenery look organic. A significant proportion of that monumental playtime I clocked in the first game came from meticulously placing bushes piece by piece to make scenery look suitably wild.
Fortunately, Frontier has introduced the scenery brushes first created for Planet Coaster 2 into this game, enabling you to quickly paint scenery across your landscape. Not only does it come with a wide array of pre-created options, but you can also make up your own using any combination of scenery you’d like. While the end result can be slightly random-looking and the brushes still don’t get tight enough for creating really dense-looking foliage, this massively speeds up initial placement and allows you to then manually shift and complement the items for significantly faster decoration.
Similarly, terrain brushes have also had loads of new options added, with attract, repel, and curl brushes adding good variety to the existing toolset available. Terrain painting also comes with a significantly wider array of options, with not only lots of sub-terrain types — such as wild grass, long grass, forest floor or scree — but also brush presets that blend combos of the above.
Sadly, these terrain painting tools are the ones that I feel most lukewarm about. While they should add an enormous amount of extra variety to your landscapes, in practice I found them quite hard to blend subtly, with the intensity slider never quite going low enough to reduce hard borders between terrain types. You can achieve a similar effect by rapidly clicking to feather the brushes, but this is one of the few areas where I feel the tools at your disposal could do with some more refining.
Still, though, the impact of the tool and brush improvements has made the game feel far more fluid in action. They’re all tiny QoL upgrades in isolation, but they’re huge in aggregate. It takes Planet Zoo from a game that’s almost notoriously fiddly and rigid to something that feels more approachable for people who don’t have 1,000 hours to learn all of its tricks.
Should you play Planet Zoo 2?
Play it if…
You want a whole new world of aquatic and avian critters
Aquariums and aviaries add a whole host of flexible new habitats to bring your zoos to life. Watching turtles and toucans explore their new homes is still a magical experience.
You want the best park design tools to date
Honestly, I can’t think of a single clunky tool from the OG Planet Zoo that hasn’t had a QoL improvement here. They’re more usable, flexible, and creative than ever before.
Don’t play it if…
You want to fill a quick 15 minutes
Preset buildings make playing Planet Zoo 2 much quicker, but creating things from scratch can take a long time. If you want to design your own zoo piece by piece, be prepared to invest some serious time.
You want a whole new game
Planet Zoo 2 builds on its predecessor, so it’s more evolution than revolution. You’ll see some duplicate items and animals, but the range is still staggering, feeling much larger than in the original.
Accessibility features
There’s a small range of accessibility features available here. For those with visual impairments, you can scale the in-game font from 60% to 100% and the UI from 70% to 100%. Meanwhile, Planet Zoo 2 caters to most forms of color blindness, allowing you to change the color of subtitles, as well as the positive, warning, and negative UI feedback colors.
How I reviewed Planet Zoo 2
Given its lengthy career mode and how long it can take to build custom enclosures, I wanted to make sure I had a broad experience of the game, so I played Planet Zoo 2 for over 75 hours. While I was reviewing the PC version, I made sure to try it out on a variety of devices, including my desktop gaming PC, the Asus ProArt P16 RTX Spark, and my Steam Deck. I also tried playing it with the SteelSeries Aeon Pro controller to ensure it was as playable on controller as it is on mouse and keyboard.
When in-game, I tried to test out as wide a variety of content as possible. I played a significant chunk of the campaign, started several franchise zoos, and began building my own zoo in sandbox mode. I built aquariums, aviaries, and traditional habitats, as well as other scenery items. And I completed multiple research levels in different wildlife reserves.
As for my own experience, not only do I have that ludicrous 1,100-hour playtime in the original Planet Zoo game, but I’ve been playing management sim games ever since the OG, Theme Park, back in 1994. I’ve been gaming across a wide variety of platforms for at least 35 years and now play principally on my PC, Steam Deck, Nintendo Switch 2, and Xbox Series X.

He’s an expert in a wide range of products from Spatial Audio headphones to gaming handhelds. articles.title: Anatel ordena que clientes de telefonia móvel façam biometria • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Anatel ordena que clientes de telefonia móvel façam biometria
Reconhecimento facial será usado em ativações, troca de chip, portabilidade e mudanças contratuais. Linhas sem cadastro poderão ser suspensas em 2029.
A Anatel tornou obrigatória a validação biométrica para ativar e manter linhas de celular. A nova regra, aprovada pela Superintendência de Planejamento e Regulamentação e divulgada nesta quarta-feira (28/10), vale para pessoas físicas e microempreendedores individuais (MEI) e será implantada gradualmente até o fim de 2028.
Segundo a documentação, o reconhecimento facial será exigido para clientes em novas ativações, portabilidade, troca de chip e alterações cadastrais ou contratuais solicitadas pelo consumidor. Quem já tem uma linha também precisará passar pelo procedimento até 31 de dezembro de 2028. Pessoas jurídicas que não sejam MEI ficam fora da exigência.
O objetivo é dificultar a abertura e a transferência de linhas usando dados falsos ou de terceiros. Uma das fraudes mais conhecidas é o SIM swap, em que criminosos conseguem transferir o número da vítima para outro chip e passam a receber ligações e códigos de autenticação enviados por SMS.
A biometria é mais uma barreira nesse processo. A Anatel já tornou obrigatória a confirmação por SMS nas portabilidades e anunciou o Anatel Protege, ferramenta para impedir a abertura de linhas vinculadas ao CPF do usuário.
O uso de biometria no setor, no entanto, não é novidade. Desde 2021, operadoras já adotam o chamado ID Digital na ativação de algumas linhas pré-pagas, com envio de selfie e documento para validar o cadastro. A nova norma amplia esse tipo de verificação para outras operações.
A norma técnica da Anatel prevê validação do CPF, captura do rosto e uma prova de vida para confirmar que há uma pessoa real diante da câmera. Depois, a imagem será comparada com uma base biométrica já existente, pública ou privada.
Se o reconhecimento não funcionar, haverá alternativas, incluindo nova tentativa, atendimento presencial ou comparação da selfie com a fotografia de um documento oficial.
A Vivo, por exemplo, já utiliza um processo similar em alguns atendimentos. Em solicitações feitas por telefone ou WhatsApp, a operadora pode enviar um SMS com um link para confirmar a identidade. O cliente precisa mostrar o rosto e aguardar alguns segundos pela validação antes que uma alteração de plano, por exemplo, possa prosseguir.
A medida busca dificultar fraudes, mas também cria mais uma situação em que consumidores terão de fornecer dados biométricos para acessar um serviço. As prestadoras também poderão acrescentar outras verificações para identificar fraudes.
A norma determina que a coleta seja limitada ao necessário, exige cumprimento da LGPD e proíbe o compartilhamento irregular com terceiros. Os sistemas também deverão manter registros auditáveis das verificações.

articles.title: SK hynix-owned Solidigm is plotting a new $45 billion flash memory factory for the US, report claims — wants go-ahead to export equipment for China upgrades in return
articles.text:
SK hynix-owned Solidigm is plotting a new $45 billion flash memory factory for the US, report claims — wants go-ahead to export equipment for China upgrades in return
Solidigm's using the potential US investment as leverage in its attempt to export equipment to upgrade an existing plant in China
Solidigm, an American subsidiary of SK hynix, one of the biggest flash chip makers on the planet, is reportedly in talks with the Commerce Department over plans to invest $45 billion in a new plant to be built in the United States. But, Bloomberg reports, there's a catch — Solidigm wants to be given the go-ahead to export equipment to upgrade its existing plant in Dalian, China. The company has purportedly told officials that the upgrades would allow the Chinese plant to then help finance the cost of its U.S.-based counterpart, according to unnamed sources. It's as-yet unclear how the proposal was received, or whether the Commerce Department is inclined to agree to the deal.
The U.S. government has been keen to drive at-home manufacturing wherever possible, including for chips used in its computers and data centers. National security is regularly cited as a key reason behind the move. It's also the reason for the government's stance on exporting technologies to China, including the equipment that Solidigm says will help upgrade its Dalian plant. Similar export restrictions are in place for high-end AI data center components, with a black market having sprung up to take the place of sanctioned sales. Earlier this month, it was reported that some of Nvidia's powerful Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs are being used in China Telecom data centers, with no explanation of how they got there. A 2025 report claimed that a cool $1 billion worth of Nvidia AI chips had been smuggled into China, a figure that is sure to have increased significantly as 2026 draws to a close.
In this case, Solidigm's planned Chinese factory upgrades could be mutually beneficial, allowing funds to be transferred to the new U.S. plant. But that requires the U.S. government to give it permission to ship the machinery in the first place, something that is far from guaranteed. The Dalian factory produces NAND flash memory, the likes of which are used in everything from relatively simple devices to full-blown data centers. It also comes at a time when global NAND production is a hot-button topic. Samsung and SK hynix are upgrading their Chinese factories to produce more of the chips used in AI data centers in an attempt to meet growing demand. Manufacturers have already slashed production of consumer-focused memory in favor of the more lucrative data center-grade components, causing prices to spike globally. This volatility in the market as a whole was given as one of the reasons SK hynix chose to cancel a planned Solidigm IPO earlier this week.
Beyond dangling a $45 billion plant, Solidigm has also allegedly told the Commerce Department that its total investment in U.S. manufacturing could reach $100 billion eventually, with construction in New York penciled in for 2027. The company is fresh from its latest earnings call, where it announced revenues of $75 billion with $60 billion in operating profit, and $28 billion in net. The company made no mention of its Dalian plant or a planned US investment, but did warn that memory shortages are set to last through 2030.
