articles.title: Qué aprendió Jeff Bezos trabajando como cocinero de comida rápida antes de fundar Amazon
articles.text:
Jeff Bezos tenía 16 años cuando consiguió su primer empleo de verano en McDonald’s, en 1980. Antes de convertirse en fundador de Amazon y uno de los hombres más ricos del mundo, el joven pasó varios meses friendo hamburguesas y aprendió lecciones que, según sus propias declaraciones, marcaron su forma de entender los negocios.
Bezos trabajó como cocinero, no como cajero. “No me dejaban acercarme a los clientes. Era mi época de adolescente con acné. Me decían: ‘¿Por qué no trabajas en la cocina?’”, relató el empresario a Fast Company, con un tono de broma sobre su rol en la parrilla.
El desafío de mantener el ritmo en horas pico
Como parrillero, la mayor dificultad para Bezos consistía en sostener la producción al ritmo adecuado durante los momentos de mayor demanda. “Cuando eres cocinero, lo más complicado es que todo salga a tiempo y bien, sobre todo en hora punta”, explicó el empresario, según consta en declaraciones recogidas por el periodista Cody Teets para su libro ‘Golden Opportunity: Remarkable Careers That Began at McDonald’s (2012)’.
Esa experiencia fue, de acuerdo con Wired, el primer contacto directo de Bezos con el sector minorista. Durante el verano, observó de cerca el sistema de automatización que empleaba la cadena de comida rápida: pitidos y señales que indicaban el momento exacto de revolver los huevos, dar la vuelta a las hamburguesas o retirar las papas fritas de la freidora.
Alcanzar esa precisión en las rutinas le permitió comprender, desde joven, que las operaciones a gran escala premian el orden y la disciplina.
El servicio al cliente, una lección aprendida desde la cocina
Aunque no tenía trato directo con el público, Bezos pudo observar de cerca el trabajo de atención al cliente que realizaban sus compañeros en la caja. De esa experiencia extrajo tres lecciones que consideró valiosas: identificar con claridad lo que pide el cliente, asistirlo cuando es necesario y saber disculparse si algo sale mal, según confesó en una entrevista con Wired.
“Aprendí que es realmente difícil”, declaró Bezos a Fast Company sobre el servicio al cliente. Esa noción temprana derivó, años después, en uno de los pilares de su empresa: la obsesión por el cliente, definida como el primero de los principios de liderazgo de Amazon.
Trabajar bajo presión y la importancia del equipo
Bezos también destacó la dificultad de actuar bajo presión ante la cantidad de imprevistos que pueden surgir en un restaurante, un desafío mayor para alguien que recién comenzaba y era muy joven. Con el tiempo, comprobó que un buen desempeño laboral genera confianza de manera progresiva.
A esto sumó otro aprendizaje: la relación con los compañeros de trabajo incide directamente en el ambiente laboral y, en consecuencia, en el resultado final del negocio con los clientes. Ese concepto de colaboración también quedó documentado en el libro de Teets.
Del verano en McDonald’s a su primer proyecto propio
La experiencia en la cadena de comida rápida duró apenas un verano. Al año siguiente, Bezos emprendió uno de sus primeros proyectos empresariales junto a su entonces novia, Ursula “Uschi” Werner: el DREAM Institute, un campamento de verano orientado a enseñar métodos de razonamiento en ciencias y literatura a jóvenes.
La iniciativa logró reunir a seis estudiantes, entre ellos dos hermanos del propio Bezos, que pagaron 600 dólares por participar. Werner afirmó que ese fue solo el comienzo de las aspiraciones del empresario, quien “siempre soñó con amasar una fortuna” a partir de sus ideas.
El consejo de Bezos para los jóvenes
Para Bezos, cualquier trabajo, sin importar cuán sencillo parezca, ofrece una oportunidad de aprendizaje si se lo encara con seriedad. “Se puede aprender lo que es la responsabilidad en cualquier tipo de trabajo, si te lo tomas en serio, incluso si es dando vueltas a unas hamburguesas”, afirmó en el libro de Teets.
El empresario remarcó además que ese tipo de experiencia temprana aporta un aprendizaje distinto al que se adquiere en la educación formal: “Se aprende mucho trabajando de joven en McDonald’s. Es diferente a lo que se puede aprender en el colegio”, sostuvo, y agregó que no debe subestimarse el valor de ese tipo de vivencias.

articles.title: With GTA VI expected to come in at 210GB, here's how long it'll take to download on every NBN speed
articles.text:
With GTA VI expected to come in at 210GB, here's how long it'll take to download on every NBN speed
From almost 19 hours to just 14 minutes, your NBN plan could make all the difference come launch day
The world is expected to come to a standstill in roughly three weeks, when the long-overdue, much-anticipated GTA VI finally, finally launches on November 19.
If you've already preordered the game, or are planning to, you might be wondering whether you've got the best TV to make the most of its sumptuous graphics. But there's something else you'll want to consider before launch day: is your home internet connection up to the task of downloading what could be an absolutely enormous game?
Our friends at GamesRadar have reported that GTA VI could weigh in at a whopping 210GB on PS5, roughly double the size of GTA V. And with Rockstar confirming that even physical copies will contain a download code rather than a disc, there's no escaping the need for a sizeable download, regardless of which version you buy.
That means you'll not only need to make sure you've got enough storage space on your console — one of the best SSDs for PS5 could help if you're running low — but you'll also want to know how long it'll take to download. And with preloading confirmed to start on November 12, there's good reason to start preparing now.
So, I've crunched the numbers to find out how long a 210GB download would take on every NBN speed tier, from NBN 25 all the way up to NBN 2000.
The results make for interesting reading. While the difference between the slowest and fastest plans is enormous, it's the jump from NBN 100 to NBN 500 that could provide the most compelling reason to upgrade.
How long will GTA VI take to download on your NBN plan?
The table below shows the estimated time it would take to download GTA VI on each NBN speed tier. These calculations assume a file size of 210GB, which remains unconfirmed, and that each connection maintains its maximum advertised download speed throughout. Actual download times may vary depending on network congestion, your equipment and the speeds supported by the game servers.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
| NBN plan | Download speed | Time to download | 
| NBN 25 | 25Mbps | 18h 40m | 
| NBN 50 | 50Mbps | 9h 20m | 
| NBN 100 | 100Mbps | 4h 40m | 
| NBN 500 | 500Mbps | 56m | 
| NBN 750 | 750Mbps | 37m 20s | 
| NBN 1000 | 1,000Mbps | 28m | 
| NBN 2000 | 2,000 Mbps | 14m | 
NBN 25 vs NBN 2000
If you're still on an NBN 25 plan, you might want to make yourself comfortable. Based on a 210GB download, you'd be looking at a wait time of approximately 18 hours and 40 minutes before GTA VI is ready to play. And that's assuming your connection can maintain its full 25Mbps download speed throughout.
At the other end of the spectrum, an NBN 2000 connection could theoretically download the same game in just 14 minutes. Clearly, that’s a crazy difference, but there are some important caveats to be aware of before you put an order in for one of the best NBN 2000 plans.
For starters, you'll need a new network termination device (NTD) installed at your premises, along with a compatible router with at least a 2.5Gbps WAN port to take full advantage of the connection. Even with these two taken care of, your console could still be a limiting factor.
The standard PS5 and PS5 Slim support Wi-Fi 6, while the more powerful PS5 Pro supports Wi-Fi 7. The latter is theoretically capable of wireless speeds exceeding 2Gbps when paired with a compatible router, but real-world performance will depend on a variety of factors.
And if you prefer the reliability of a wired connection, all PS5 models have a Gigabit Ethernet port, effectively limiting download speeds to around 1Gbps at best.
So while an NBN 2000 plan might sound like the ultimate solution for downloading GTA VI in record time, there's no guarantee your console will be able to make full use of all that bandwidth.
NBN 500 proves it worth once more
Despite coming to the conclusion that an NBN 1000 plan offers the best value on a cost per mb basis, I still believe that an NBN 500 plan is the sweet spot for most Australian homes. The combination of fast speeds and low-cost monthly fees is a win-win in my book.
And now the best NBN 500 plans are making a solid argument for upgrading, whether that be from an NBN 50 plan, or taking advantage of the free fibre upgrade to get your home connected via fibre-to-the-premises (FTTP) technology.
As the table further up shows, an NBN 100 connection would theoretically take four hours and 40 minutes to download a 210GB game. Step up to NBN 500, and that figure plummets to just 56 minutes — a time saving of almost four hours, and a fivefold increase in download speed.
The benefits become less dramatic as you move further up the speed tiers. An NBN 750 plan would shave another 19 minutes off the download, while NBN 1000 could theoretically have the game ready in just 28 minutes.
Of course, faster is always better when you're impatiently waiting to play one of the most anticipated games in history. But whether those additional minutes are worth paying more for is another question entirely.
And with NBN 500 plans now widely available from Australian internet providers, it could be the most sensible choice for gamers who want significantly faster downloads without necessarily paying for the fastest connection available.
Still on FTTN or FTTC? Now could be the time to upgrade
There's one final consideration, particularly if you're still connected to the NBN via fibre-to-the-node (FTTN) or fibre-to-the-curb (FTTC).
While these connection types can support an NBN 100 plan, you'll generally need an FTTP or hybrid fibre coaxial (HFC) connection to access the faster NBN 500, 750 and 1000 speed tiers.
The good news is that many Australians with FTTN or FTTC connections are eligible to upgrade to FTTP through NBN Co's fibre upgrade program.
If you're eligible, you can arrange the upgrade through your internet provider, although installation timeframes will vary depending on your property and the work required.
With GTA VI preloading scheduled to begin on November 12, it's worth checking your eligibility sooner rather than later if you're considering making the switch.
And while upgrading your internet connection solely for one game might seem a little excessive, the benefits of faster downloads, additional bandwidth and a more capable connection will extend well beyond GTA VI.
The NBN plan to get
If you’re questioning whether your current NBN is going to be up to the task of handling the GTA VI download file, then there’s one plan in particular that I can confidently recommend.
Exetel One | 500Mbps | AU$80p/m
Exetel’s NBN 500 plan could be the goldilocks option for GTA players. Not only does it promise maximum plan speeds during busier evening hours, but customers can boost the speed up to NBN 1000 for AU$1 per 24-hour period. Plus, the telco recorded the quickest ping speeds in the most recent ACCC broadband performance data report of 6.9ms, which could be ideal if you intend to game online. Plus, its low-cost monthly fee makes it the cheapest provider from year two of service.
• AU$80 minimum cost
• AU$960 yearly cost
Ultimately, whichever NBN plan you're on, a little preparation could go a long way towards making sure you're ready for GTA VI's launch.
If you're on a slower connection, taking advantage of the preload period could mean the difference between playing as soon as the game unlocks and spending launch day staring at a download progress bar.
And while upgrading to a faster NBN plan could dramatically reduce your download time, there's no need to rush out and sign up for the fastest connection available. As the figures above demonstrate, even a relatively modest upgrade could make a substantial difference.
After all, you've waited years for GTA VI. What's a few more hours?

articles.title: Taiwan working on autonomous drone swarms to counter China’s increasingly aggressive grey-zone military tactics — island has already completed flight simulations, now working towards flight trials over maritime areas
articles.text:
Taiwan working on autonomous drone swarms to counter China’s increasingly aggressive grey-zone military tactics — island has already completed flight simulations, now working towards flight trials over maritime areas
Taipei has also received its first shipment of U.S.-made V-BAT drones.
Taiwan’s Ocean Affairs Council is working on an autonomous system that would allow drone fleets to coordinate and execute missions without human intervention in response to "grey-zone" activities carried out by China. According to the South China Morning Post, the council is working with the National Cheng Kung University, which has already completed simultaneous flight simulations of two drone fleets, with each fleet comprising 10 units. This is already the second step of the process, which has shifted from individual aircraft control to the coordination of two drone detachments.
This project is designed to help Taiwan’s Coast Guard Administration (CGA) to counter Beijing’s grey-zone tactics in the waters surrounding the island nation. There have already been instances of civilian Chinese ships damaging undersea cables that Taipei relies on, with the CGA increasing its defensive patrols around 24 undersea cables and closely monitoring nearly a hundred China-linked boats. Despite that, Chinese “research vessels” continue to loiter over Taiwan-U.S. undersea cables, mimicking the activities of Russian trawlers in the Atlantic.
“The next stage will involve hardware-in-the-loop testing, prototype integration and flight trials over actual maritime areas to assess reliability under different sea and weather conditions,” the council said. The researchers programmed the drones to have a minimum separation of 100 feet in 3D space, and they’re also incorporating leader-follower formation flying and dynamic obstacle avoidance. This should allow them to respond to quickly changing conditions out in the open sea and even deal with unexpected hazards.
More than that, the autonomous system Taipei is working on would let different types of drones coordinate their movements, divide tasks, and plan routes, primarily for maritime surveillance. This is especially important as it would allow them to use different types of drones to accomplish various missions, much like how different air forces use different aircraft types. 
The project is currently focusing on three Western-made drones — the Jump 20, V-BAT, and Flexrotor. In fact, the Ocean Affairs Council just received the V-BAT, a VTOL drone built by U.S. defense firm Shield AI. This unit can take off vertically from the relatively constrained deck space of non-aircraft carrier ships and offers an endurance of over 12 hours for extended missions, making it ideal for the CGA, as it would not need to make major renovations to its ships to accommodate these drones while extending their reach.

articles.title: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Two PHP2Shell Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday confirmed active exploitation of the recently patched PHP2Shell flaws by adding them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
The PHP vulnerabilities, both rated 9.2 on the CVSS scoring system, facilitate unauthenticated remote code execution on affected deployments -
- CVE-2026-109618 - An out-of-memory corruption vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.
- CVE-2026-109619 - A stale internal request-state vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.
The addition of the two flaws to the KEV catalog comes after Adel Karimi, detection and response lead at Perplexity, confirmed successful instances of remote code execution against honeypot systems on October 24, 2026.
"This is now confirmed RCE with usable memory disclosure, not just a crash followed by a suspicious process," Karimi said. "The response delivered an 800 KiB decoded cookie dump, and a function address derived from that dump using the public exploit's offsets appears in the subsequent execution payload."
"The evidence demonstrates this chain on the intentionally favorable single-worker mod_php profile; it is not a measurement of exploit reliability on other worker counts, PHP builds, or applications."
The issues have been addressed in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 released on October 21, 2026. Federal agencies have time until October 29, 2026, to apply the necessary fixes.
PHP, short for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, is a server-side scripting language used in roughly 70% of all websites on the internet. According to estimates shared by Censys, more than 32.51 million PHP services are still running an affected version.
The severity of the vulnerabilities has prompted numerous advisories from software and security vendors and government agencies across the world, including -
- ABB

- Belden

- Canon
- Citrix
- Craft CMS
- Dell

- Schneider Electric
- Siemens (1), (2)

- WordPress
As of October 26, 2026, the PHP Foundation also released Windows builds 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1 to address CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Brotli decoder library that could also result in privilege escalation and unauthenticated remote code execution.
The vulnerability, also known as Broccoli2Shell, HTTP2Shell, and Node2Shell, affects Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.0.9, 1.1.0, and 1.2.0. It has been patched in versions 1.0.10, 1.1.1, and 1.2.1, along with other projects that include the C library, including Node.js, Bun, Envoy Proxy, Istio, .NET, and Python.
"In PHP Windows builds, the vulnerable decoder can be reached through the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled," the PHP Foundation said. "This is disabled by default in cURL, but applications and HTTP client libraries can enable it."

articles.title: Claude recusa tarefas de engenharia reversa em TVs e jogos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Claude recusa tarefas de engenharia reversa em TVs e jogos
Usuários relatam restrições no Opus 5.5; Anthropic não confirmou mudança nos filtros de segurança.
Usuários do Claude relatam que o assistente de inteligência artificial passou a interromper tarefas de engenharia reversa de softwares e firmwares. As queixas envolvem principalmente o Claude Opus 5.5, lançado em setembro com capacidades aprimoradas de programação, e incluem análises de jogos e tentativas de modificar sistemas de smart TVs.
As reclamações começaram a ganhar força após publicações no Reddit e apontam que o modelo pode iniciar uma tarefa e interrompê-la no meio da resposta após acionar uma verificação de segurança. A Anthropic não confirmou uma mudança voltada para esse tipo de atividade.
A engenharia reversa permite examinar um programa para entender como ele funciona, mesmo sem acesso ao código-fonte original. A técnica é usada em pesquisas de segurança, de compatibilidade e desenvolvimento de modificações.
Parte dos relatos envolve o REA (Reverse Engineer Anything), projeto de código aberto que conecta agentes de IA a ferramentas de análise. A ferramenta automatiza etapas que normalmente exigiriam conhecimento técnico e trabalho manual.
O interesse pela técnica também cresceu com projetos que usam IA para recompilar jogos para rodar em outras plataformas, incluindo até navegadores.
Um caso explicado pelo Decrypt mostra mais detalhes sobre o problema. Um usuário pediu ao Claude Code que instalasse uma interface alternativa em uma TV LG com webOS. Durante o processo, ele encontrou uma barreira de segurança do Opus 5.5. O assistente sugeriu trocar para o Opus 4.8, mas o modelo anterior também interrompeu etapas do procedimento.
O episódio não demonstra que a engenharia reversa de TVs está bloqueada, mas mostra como filtros de segurança podem interferir em algumas tarefas técnicas.
A Anthropic já havia reforçado as proteções de cibersegurança quando lançou o Claude Opus 5.5. No anúncio oficial, a empresa afirma que atividades de desenvolvimento e correção de código continuam permitidas. Até agora, não há evidências de que a Anthropic tenha proibido oficialmente toda a prática.
A empresa também não confirmou uma alteração nos filtros do Opus 5.5.

articles.title: Call of Duty Crosses $40 Billion in Lifetime Revenue, Xbox CEO Confirms
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Call of Duty Crosses $40 Billion in Lifetime Revenue, Xbox CEO Confirms
Call of Duty has crossed $40 billion in lifetime franchise revenue, according to Microsoft Gaming CEO Asha Sharma. She shared the milestone on X on October 26, a few days after Modern Warfare 4's full launch on October 23, calling it one of the most celebrated games in the series' history and thanking both the Activision team and the players. The series debuted in 2003 and has seen a new entry almost every year since, along with Warzone and mobile spin-offs, so that figure covers a lot of ground. PC Gamer's math puts it at a staggering $4,762,472 a day, which is hard to wrap your head around. It's also worth remembering that this is revenue, not profit, and Activision doesn't disclose development or marketing budgets for its games.
Sharma, however, didn't say how Modern Warfare 4 is selling, or whether it was the game that pushed the franchise over the line. Early signs have been good, at least on PC. The game picked up a 90% positive Steam rating during campaign early access, a far cry from the reception Black Ops 7 got, and even climbed the Steam Top's Sellers list rapidly. Activision has also called it the conclusion of the current Modern Warfare series, with a new sub-franchise set to follow. For some context, Microsoft paid $68.7 billion to acquire Activision Blizzard back in 2023, though only some of that $40 billion would have come in under Microsoft's ownership.
Sources:
				Asha Sharma on X, 				via PC Gamer

articles.title: C'est le moment d'acheter un aspirateur robot puisque ce Roborock est bradé par Amazon
articles.text:
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est un aspirateur robot laveur qui aspire les poussières et nettoie vos sols sans que vous n’ayez à intervenir tandis que la station de lavage se charge de l’entretien. En ce moment, le produit de Roborock est disponible pour 330 euros de moins sur Amazon.
Avec des températures qui se rafraîchissent de plus en plus, on a de moins en moins envie de nettoyer nos sols de fond en comble. La solution est donc d’investir dans un aspirateur robot. Justement, Amazon brade le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 avec une réduction de 38 %. Malgré cette remise, il faudra dépenser plus de 500 euros pour s'offrir les services de cet engin.
Sur Amazon, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 passe de 889,99 euros à 549,99 euros
Pourquoi choisir le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 ?
- Une cartographie précise : Grâce à l’intelligence artificielle, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 offre une navigation précise et il pourra éviter la plupart des obstacles. L’engin peut également franchir des seuils pour pouvoir passer d’une pièce à l'autre.
- Un nettoyage intelligent : Sur l’application, il est possible de définir les horaires de passage et les zones où le robot doit passer. En action, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 peut lever ses brosses lorsqu'il arrive à proximité d’un tapis afin de ne pas l'humidifier.
- Une station qui se charge de l’entretien : Pour limiter les interventions humaines, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 s’entretient tout seul. La station d'entretien vide le bac à poussière. Elle nettoie les serpillières à l'eau chaude et les sèche à l'air chaud.
Un aspirateur robot qui n’oublie aucune zone
Roborock a apporté un soin tout particulier au design de son Qrevo Edge 2. D’abord, cet aspirateur robot n'est pas très haut avec seulement 7,98 cm de hauteur. Un détail qui n'est pas anodin puisqu’il permet à l’engin de passer sous la plupart des meubles.
Autre point fort, sa technologie FlexiArm. Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 dispose d’un petit bras extensible pour atteindre les coins ou passer le long des plinthes. Un double système anti-emmêlement est présent pour aspirer les poils et les longs cheveux sans qu’ils ne s’emmêlent autour de la brosse. Côté aspiration, il faut compter une puissance maximale de 25 000 Pa. C’est suffisant pour aspirer tous les éléments qui traînent au sol.
L'aspirateur robot emporte aussi des brosses pour le lavage des sols. Le résultat sera convaincant dans la plupart des situations, même si un second passage sera nécessaire pour les taches les plus tenaces. À noter que ces serpillières peuvent se lever pour ne pas humidifier les tapis.
Une navigation (presque) parfaite
Avant de pouvoir profiter de toutes les qualités de ce Roborock Qrevo Edge 2, il faut qu’il effectue un premier passage afin de cartographier votre intérieur. Une fois cette première étape effectuée, vous pourrez personnaliser le nettoyage. Par exemple, il sera possible de créer des zones interdites ou de définir des heures de passage.
Cet aspirateur robot possède un système de détection des obstacles qui s’appuie sur l’intelligence artificielle. Roborock affirme que son engin peut reconnaître plus de 280 obstacles. Cependant, pour les objets les plus fins comme les câbles, le robot peut présenter quelques difficultés.
Au terme de ses opérations de nettoyage, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 rejoint sa station d’entretien. Elle se charge de vider le bac à poussière et de laver les serpillères à l’eau chaude. Pour éviter les mauvaises odeurs, la station sèche les serpillères à l’air chaud.
✅ Les points forts
- Un robot pas très épais pour passer sous les meubles
- Un bras extensible pour atteindre les zones les plus difficiles d'accès
- Un double système anti-emmêlement contre les cheveux longs et les poils
❌ Les limites
- Une détection par IA qui peut montrer des limites face à des objets fins comme des câbles
- Plusieurs passages peuvent être nécessaires pour éliminer les taches les plus tenaces
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est actuellement disponible pour 549,99 euros au lieu de 889,99 euros
Le prix élevé de ce Roborock Qrevo Edge 2, même après la réduction d’Amazon, se justifie par toutes les qualités offertes par ce robot. Il se charge de nettoyer vos sols et s’entretient seul pour limiter les interventions humaines. Pour trouver des défauts, il faut les chercher et le seul qui peut être dérangeant concerne les faiblesses de l’IA pour détecter des câbles. Hormis sur ce point, le robot nettoiera votre intérieur de fond en comble grâce à son petit format qui lui permet de passer sous les meubles.

articles.title: Felix Mobile’s new true unlimited plan is faster at 80Mbps, but it’s now also cheaper for a limited time
articles.text:
Felix Mobile’s new true unlimited plan is faster at 80Mbps, but it’s now also cheaper for a limited time
The telco’s new Unlimited+ plan was already a bargain at AU$50/m, and you can save 50% for the first 6 months
Felix Mobile has long been the sole provider of truly unlimited mobile data plans in Australia, with the only catch being download speeds are limited. For a time, the telco’s only offering was 40Mbps for AU$40 per month. Earlier this month, though, the telco unveiled a faster Unlimited+ plan that doubles download speeds to 80Mbps, for only AU$10 extra each month.
In my mind, AU$50 a month for truly unlimited data is a bit of a bargain, but now Felix Mobile has taken things a step further by offering 50% off its Unlimited+ plan for the first 6 months — that’s just AU$25 per month for as much mobile data as you need, at speeds up to 80Mbps.
Felix Mobile Unlimited+ | Unlimited data/calls/texts | No lock-in contract | AU$25/m (first 6 months, then AU$50/m)
Felix Mobile is the only mobile provider in Australia with truly unlimited data plans, and it's now offering a much faster Unlimited+ plan with 80Mbps speeds (up from 40Mbps in the existing Felix Unlimited plan) using Vodafone’s 5G and 4G networks. If you sign up anytime before November 30, you’ll only pay AU$25/m for the first 6 months, representing an annual saving of AU$150. The plan also includes unlimited standard calls and texts. Unlimited international calls and texts to 40+ selected countries are also available for an extra AU$5/m.
Most telcos in Australia technically offer unlimited mobile data on their plans, but they almost always throttle the speeds significantly once you’ve used your monthly allowance — usually down to around 2Mbps. Felix Mobile’s Unlimited and Unlimited+ plans forego data caps entirely, and the speeds remain consistent at 40Mbps and 80Mbps, respectively (compared to the minimum 100-150Mbps that most telcos offer).
The 80Mbps speeds of Felix Unlimited+ will be virtually identical to a 100-150Mbps mobile plan for everyday browsing, social media and music streaming, and I’d argue that even streaming 4K video will perform quite similarly, too.
You’d only be able to tell the difference when you’re downloading large files and apps, though you’d be better off using your home internet for those, anyway.
Felix recommends using the Unlimited+ plan for personal mobile use only, with occasional hotspotting to personal devices like laptops or tablets while on the go, and it shouldn’t replace a home or office internet plan or be used for continuous downloading of large files.
If you want to test the data speeds before committing, Felix also offers a 7-day guarantee where you can get a full refund within 7 days of activating if you’re not satisfied.

articles.title: “Tenemos un historial de pérdidas netas”: la frase de Anthropic que pone en alerta a Wall Street
articles.text:
La salida a bolsa de Anthropic, la primera de un laboratorio frontera de inteligencia artificial, revela cifras que combinan crecimiento y alarma en partes iguales. La compañía facturó 16.000 millones de dólares en los primeros seis meses de este año, pero acumuló pérdidas de 80.000 millones en el mismo período.
En medio de ese contraste, su folleto previo a la cotización, el S-1, incluye una advertencia que ya circula entre inversores: “Tenemos un historial de pérdidas netas y es posible que no generemos ingresos suficientes para alcanzar o mantener la rentabilidad en el futuro”.
Ese párrafo, ubicado en la página 64 del documento, detalla que Anthropic registró pérdidas netas de 1.500 millones de dólares en 2023, 8.300 millones en 2024, 42.000 millones en 2025 y 80.700 millones en los seis meses cerrados el 30 de junio de 2026.
La cifra ha circulado en redes como prueba del riesgo que implica invertir en la empresa dirigida por Dario Amodei, aunque el contexto completo del S-1 matiza esa lectura inicial.
Qué significa el historial de pérdidas netas de Anthropic
La frase que alarma a los mercados no es una confesión espontánea, sino una fórmula legal estandarizada en las salidas a bolsa estadounidenses. Su función es advertir a los futuros accionistas que, si la inversión no resulta rentable, la empresa ya lo había anticipado por escrito.
El S-1 de Anthropic dedica 94 páginas a riesgos asociados a la compra de sus acciones, el doble de lo habitual en documentos similares de otras compañías tecnológicas. Ese volumen inusual responde a una misma lógica de protección legal ante eventuales demandas de inversores en caso de pérdidas futuras.
Pese al disclaimer, Anthropic declara por primera vez un margen del 10% en su operativa diaria, positivo desde su fundación en 2021. El verdadero lastre financiero no proviene de los ingresos, sino de dos factores estructurales: la revalorización de los bonos convertibles con los que se financió, en su mayoría en manos de Amazon, y los compromisos de compra firmados con los hiperescaladores, que ascienden a 265.600 millones de dólares a 30 de junio de 2026, con plazos de hasta 20 años.
La pregunta que dominará la cotización de Anthropic es sencilla: ¿se trata de una empresa condenada a la insolvencia o de un negocio en fase de inversión masiva antes de alcanzar rentabilidad plena? El propio historial de pérdidas, lejos de ser excepcional, sigue el mismo patrón que atravesaron otras tecnológicas antes de consolidarse en bolsa.
Por qué los disclaimers de pérdidas son habituales en las tecnológicas
Un repaso a los documentos de salida a bolsa de otras grandes compañías confirma que la fórmula empleada por Anthropic no es nueva. El S-1 de Uber declaraba haber “incurrido en pérdidas significativas desde su creación”. El F-1 de Spotify admitía que quizá “no sería capaz de generar suficientes ingresos para ser rentables”. El S-1 de SpaceX contiene advertencias similares.
Estas tres empresas, de menor capitalización que la prevista para Anthropic (hasta 2 billones de dólares en el escenario más optimista), comparten un rasgo común: operaron a pérdidas durante años, sostenidas por inversores privados, antes de convertirse en referentes de sus sectores.
El caso de Uber resulta ilustrativo. Fundada en 2009, no declaró beneficios operativos hasta 14 años después. Solo en 2023, cuatro años después de su salida a bolsa, la empresa salió de los números rojos. El riesgo existía desde el inicio, pero a largo plazo se convirtió en una apuesta rentable para quienes sostuvieron la inversión.
La naturaleza de las empresas tecnológicas, con modelos de negocio sostenidos durante años por líneas de crédito privadas antes de alcanzar madurez financiera, explica por qué este tipo de advertencias legales forman parte del guion habitual de cualquier salida a bolsa relevante.
La diversificación de ingresos que defienden los entusiastas de la IA
Frente a la lectura pesimista del documento, existe otra narrativa que resalta fortalezas concretas del negocio. Anthropic reporta más de 11.900 clientes con un gasto anual superior a los 100.000 dólares cada uno, una base mucho más diversificada que la concentración de clientes que la empresa reconocía en etapas anteriores.
Según información citada por The New York Times, ningún cliente individual supera el 10% de la facturación anual de Anthropic. Ese dato contrasta con la imagen de una compañía dependiente de pocos contratos grandes y respalda el argumento de quienes consideran que el negocio tiene bases más sólidas de lo que sugiere el párrafo viralizado sobre pérdidas netas.
El peso de los compromisos con los hiperescaladores
Más allá de los bonos convertibles vinculados a Amazon, el segundo gran lastre financiero de Anthropic son los compromisos de compra firmados con los hiperescaladores, proveedores de infraestructura de computación necesaria para entrenar y operar sus modelos de inteligencia artificial.
Esos compromisos alcanzan los 265.600 millones de dólares a 30 de junio de 2026, con plazos contractuales de hasta 20 años. Se trata de obligaciones a largo plazo que condicionan la estructura de costos de la empresa durante las próximas dos décadas, independientemente de cómo evolucione su facturación en el corto plazo.
La combinación de estos compromisos con la revalorización de los bonos convertibles explica por qué las pérdidas contables de Anthropic no reflejan necesariamente un negocio inviable, sino una estructura financiera moldeada por decisiones de inversión en infraestructura a largo plazo.

articles.title: DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite : une station électrique de 2 kWh qui se recharge au soleil comme en voiture
articles.text:
Six mois après la Power 1000 Mini, DJI est de retour sur le segment de l’énergie avec la Power Auro 2000 Elite. Cette station électrique de 2 kWh (2 016 kWh précisément) est présentée par le géant des drones comme la plus compacte de sa gamme à cette capacité. La station électrique s’inspire en effet de ces aînés pour offrir un volume de 25 litres et un poids d’environ 19 kg, ce qui lui permet d’être 24 % moins volumineuse et 14 % plus légère que la DJI Power 2000. Quant à son encombrement, il se veut proche de celui de la Power 1000 V2, qui ne stocke pourtant que 1 kWh.
Avec ses 456 × 225 × 245 mm, elle se montre aussi un peu plus compacte que l’Anker Solix C2000 Gen 2 que nous avons testé (459 × 250 × 257 mm), pour un poids équivalent. DJI précise toutefois qu’elle ne remplace pas la Power 2000, qui reste sa référence pour les usages les plus gourmands.
La Power Auro 2000 Elite délivre jusqu’à 2 000 W en continu sur ses trois prises secteur, avec un signal sinusoïdal pur, et peut alimenter certains appareils d’environ 2 200 W. Elle compte aussi deux ports USB-C de 65 W, deux ports USB-A et, plus original, un câble USB-C rétractable de 140 W. Celui-ci s’enroule automatiquement dans le boîtier, de quoi recharger un ordinateur portable ou un smartphone sans chercher de câble. Dans le but de faciliter l’accès, toutes les prises sont regroupées sur une seule face.
Un chargeur solaire et un chargeur de voiture intégrés
La principale nouveauté avec ce modèle tient à sa conception tout-en-un. DJI a intégré dans le boîtier un régulateur solaire MPPT et un chargeur de voiture, là où la concurrence passe souvent par des accessoires. La station d’Anker demande, par exemple, un chargeur d’alternateur optionnel de 800 W pour se recharger rapidement en voiture.
Le port propriétaire de DJI et bien présent et les deux ports SDC de la Power Auro 2000 Elite acceptent chacun jusqu’à 600 W, pour un total de 1 200 W. Dans ces conditions, DJI évoque une recharge complète en 2,7 heures environ au soleil et 4 heures en voiture. Les câbles nécessaires sont en revanche vendus à part.
Sur secteur, avec un simple câble d’alimentation et le mode de recharge rapide activé dans l’application, la batterie accepte jusqu’à 2 000 W et passerait de 0 à 80 % en une heure, pour une charge complète en 75 minutes. Elle peut aussi combiner le secteur avec le solaire ou la voiture, toujours dans la limite de 2 000 W.
Une batterie qui vise aussi la maison
DJI met également en avant un usage domestique pour les cas de coupure, avec un mode onduleur qui bascule sur la batterie en 0,01 seconde. Cela doit permettre de garder une box internet ou un ordinateur allumés. À faible charge, la station resterait sous les 30 dB, suffisamment discrète pour fonctionner la nuit, et l’application DJI Home permet de suivre en temps réel l’énergie consommée et stockée.
Associée à des panneaux solaires et à un micro-onduleur, vendus séparément, elle peut aussi injecter jusqu’à 800 W dans le circuit électrique de la maison, à la manière d’une batterie solaire domestique, pour consommer le soir l’énergie produite en journée. Cette fonction n’est toutefois proposée que dans certains pays, précise le fabricant. DJI avance qu’avec cinq batteries d’extension, l’ensemble pourrait fournir plus de 1 000 kWh par an, avec un retour sur investissement en 3,5 ans pour l’unité principale seule. Comme toujours, ces estimations sont à prendre avec prudence, puisqu’elles dépendent largement de l’installation solaire, de l’ensoleillement et du prix de l’électricité.
La capacité de la station pourra justement être étendue jusqu’à 12 kWh avec cinq batteries d’extension de 2 kWh, présentées comme les plus compactes de DJI, mais dont la commercialisation n’interviendra que plus tard. Côté sécurité, la Power Auro 2000 Elite repose sur des cellules LFP, réputées plus stables, qui conserveraient plus de 70 % de leur capacité après 6 000 cycles, soit une dizaine d’années d’utilisation quotidienne selon DJI.
Fidèle à son écosystème, le fabricant permet enfin de recharger rapidement ses batteries de drones via les ports SDC, jusqu’à 240 W avec le câble dédié. Une batterie de DJI Air 3 passerait ainsi de 10 à 95 % en 30 minutes. La DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite est disponible dès aujourd’hui au prix de 1 099 euros.

articles.title: Virtana lets its AI agents pull in agents from other vendors to work IT incidents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Virtana lets its AI agents pull in agents from other vendors to work IT incidents
Information technology observability company Virtana today added Agentic Observability Enterprise Management to its platform so its artificial intelligence agents can pull agents from other vendors into an IT incident.
The release goes after a gap left by the way enterprises have adopted AI agents so far. Most enterprise agents have come built into a single vendor’s product, such as an IT service management system. When a failure spreads across systems from several vendors, none of those agents sees the whole outage. Collating the findings still falls to engineers.
With the new capabilities, a Virtana agent that spots trouble can invite other vendors’ agents into the investigation. Any agent that speaks the Model Context Protocol or the open Agent2Agent protocol is eligible, including those bundled with software a company already owns.
Outside agents have been able to query Virtana’s monitoring data since February, when the company released its System-Aware MCP Server. The feed runs to more than 25,000 real-time metrics. Agents called into an incident also get a shared view of how applications depend on the infrastructure beneath them from the System Dependency Graph, which Virtana introduced at the same time. A month later Virtana extended its monitoring to AI workloads.
In Virtana’s illustration, a third-party agent notices an application has slowed down and asks Virtana’s root cause analysis agent, which it locates through Agent2Agent, to investigate. The diagnosis points to a database bottleneck that appeared after a recent software deployment. Follow-up questions can go back to the root cause agent before other specialized agents are lined up for the fix. Virtana’s software then confirms the application is back to normal.
A conventional IT war room takes hours to staff and run, according to Chief Product Officer Amitkumar Rathi, who said a team of agents can get through the same work “in milliseconds.”
That kind of autonomy applies only to incident types a customer has defined in advance. Customers wanting more caution can have engineers carry out whatever fixes the agents recommend, or require sign-off on each agent action before it runs. Policy also decides which outside agents get into an investigation and how many tokens they are allowed to consume once there. Every agent action is written to an audit log.
Virtana, which went by Virtual Instruments until a 2019 rebrand, is a venture capital-backed company that started out selling tools for monitoring the performance of IT infrastructure. Investors put $73 million into the business in 2022, with Atalaya Capital Management LP and Benhamou Global Ventures among them.

articles.title: Nvidia and Oracle bring Vera CPU instances online in multi-gigawatt deployment
articles.text:
Standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs land in Oracle Cloud's multi-gigawatt deployment — our independent benchmarking of a local server reveals Vera's massive memory bandwidth lead over dual Xeon 6 server
Standalone Vera is generally available on OCI Superclusters now.
Nvidia and Oracle have announced general availability of Nvidia’s Vera Rubin NVL72 rack and Vera CPUs on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Superclusters at Oracle AI World on Tuesday. The announcement comes hot on the heels of Google Cloud announcing general availability for Vera Rubin last week, putting two major hyperscaler feathers in Nvidia’s cap. However, Oracle’s announcement is interesting, specifically calling out standalone Vera instances on OCI Superclusters. We've included a few benchmarks we've performed on a Vera server for a forthcoming review to highlight some of the chip's performance characteristics, but do note that these tests were not conducted on OCI infrastructure.
Neoclouds have been banging the drum of Vera for the past several weeks, with instances under way at Nscale, CoreWeave, and Nebius, among others, so it makes sense to see Vera in the GPU-dominant and AI-focused neoclouds. A standalone deployment at a hyperscaler like Oracle sends a different signal, however.
Although hyperscalers maintain large fleets of hardware, sometimes even renting from the neoclouds, the CPU focus is primarily on x86, with OCI Superclusters otherwise offering the Ampere Altra for an Arm-based instance. It’s Nvidia’s first standalone CPU push into the hyperscale data center, placing Vera alongside the x86 competition regardless of the GPU compute.
Vera is not meant to upend the x86 guard, at least in isolation. Ian Buck, Nvidia’s mind behind CUDA and the face of Nvidia’s AI infrastructure buildout, said in March — when the chip was revealed — that the world couldn’t be served by a single, 88-core SKU. However, Vera is opening the door at hyperscalers like Oracle to expand in future CPU generations.
AMD and Intel maintain the lead when it comes to single-socket density, which is only set to expand in the next generation, as AMD’s upcoming EPYC Venice CPUs can pack up to 512 threads in a single socket. However, Vera offers some distinct advantages due to its topology depending on the workload, many of which are becoming increasingly relevant in the agentic AI era.
Memory bandwidth, for instance, is one of Vera’s strong suits, and that’s not just a marketing claim. Nvidia has said the memory system is capable of 1.2 TB/s of bandwidth, but we can see Nvidia’s lead outside of theoretical numbers in our testing below.
Take the industry-standard Stream benchmark as an example. Nvidia’s use of LPDDR5X-9600, along with a monolithic die and distributed mesh for caching, allows it to more than double the bandwidth available on a dual Intel Xeon 6980P system, even when it’s paired with MRDIMMs sporting speeds of 8,800 MT/s. We’re showing triad here, as it’s the most “demanding” of Stream’s operations, but the leads for Vera are similar across add, copy, and scale as well.
This bandwidth is critical for some types of agentic loops, particularly those dealing with large database queries or extensive documentation. You can see the OpenMP “spread” policy offers a massive boost to Vera’s memory bandwidth, as well. Both AMD and Intel maintain centralized memory control and system-level cache, while Vera distributes it in a mesh across the die. The result, at least in OpenMP set properly, is much higher memory bandwidth by binding processes as far away from each other as possible.
Another critical performance vector for agentic AI is Python. The agentic world is expanding, but much of the foundation of the AI software ecosystem is built on Python. Common agentic frameworks like CrewAI and LangGraph are written in Python, and although we’re seeing more frameworks built in languages like Rust and TypeScript, Python performance is still critical to agentic loops.
And, unsurprisingly, it’s an area where Vera is also strong, beating out CPUs that are much more powerful on paper. Popular agentic harnesses are built on Python, but so are many of the applications that also run on Python, including foundational AI libraries like PyTorch and TensorFlow.
Nvidia’s focus on agentic AI makes sense given the times we’re living in, but it can miss the forest for the trees. Oracle bringing Vera standalone instances online shifts the focus onto the broader implications of Vera’s entrance into the data center. There are some aspects of performance that characterize agentic AI workloads, but many agent workloads are regular data center workloads in the first place, just under high concurrency.
For instance, SQLite performance is important for any server querying a large database, regardless of its written by logic, a person, or an AI agent. Nvidia’s second-gen Scalable Coherency Fabric (SCF), which we saw at play in Stream, shows up in a real workload here, with these database queries largely bound by data movement across the system.
And that is what makes Vera so interesting in the context of Oracle’s announcement. It’s a CPU built for agentic AI, says Nvidia, but the crosstalk with general data center workloads is strong. It’s not just a CPU to use because you need access to Nvidia’s accelerators. Depending on the workload, it may even be a better choice than the x86 guard.
Ultimately, we have to see how customers of these hyperscalers use (or don’t use) Vera in production. It’s demonstrated its usefulness in agentic AI loops, but it’s also showing early promise in certain general-purpose workloads. Oracle’s standalone deployment is a sign that there’s some demand for Vera that isn't exclusively tied at the hip of a Rubin GPU.
Oracle is approaching cautiously, however, as any hyperscaler should be when bringing up a multi-gigawatt deployment. The company said it will also offer Nvidia’s HGX NVL8, bringing eight Rubin GPUs together in a cluster, connected to a dual, 64-core Intel Xeon 6 host with 4TB of DDR5 memory.
Our testing of Vera shared in this article is part of a larger benchmarking session we had with the chip, and we'll share the technical details of the test setup in our forthcoming review. We’ll be publishing our full results shortly on Tom’s Hardware.
Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

articles.title: Jedify formally launches Data Agents for building AI analysts in plain language - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Jedify formally launches Data Agents for building AI analysts in plain language
Enterprise artificial intelligence context startup Jedify Inc. today formally launched Data Agents, a product that lets business teams set up autonomous AI analysts by describing the work they want done in plain language.
Data Agents takes on a longstanding limit of business intelligence software, where analysts have to build dashboards ahead of time around the questions they expect people to ask. Generic AI assistants have tried to fill that gap. In Jedify’s telling, those tools end up guessing at what a business means from its raw tables and schemas.
The company’s core product is a context graph that pulls structured data and documents into a single model of how a business works, down to metric definitions and record-level permissions. Data Agents runs on top of it. Because joins and schema mapping are already worked out inside the graph, building an agent comes down to describing the question.
Users decide when an agent runs, whether on request, on a schedule or when a condition they have defined is met. A market that starts to underperform is the kind of anomaly an agent is meant to catch on its own, and Jedify’s deep research engine then works out what most likely drove the change.
Data access is tied to the person asking the question. Anything that user is barred from seeing, even a single row in a table, stays out of the agent’s results. On cost, Jedify claims its agents burn far fewer tokens per question than ones that have to explore raw schema at query time.
Teams can also work with the agents outside Jedify’s own interface. Under the Model Context Protocol, each one appears as a tool that can be called from Claude, ChatGPT, Slack or any agent platform a company runs. Results can go straight to email or Slack too.
Jedify is pitching the product at data teams and the business staff they support, arguing that analysts who keep fielding the same dashboard request can hand it off to an agent. On the business side, people in finance, revenue operations and sales can set up their own agents.
Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Adi Elimelech said enterprises are moving analytics “from answering questions to doing meaningful work.” The goal, he said, is for teams to build “an analytical workforce” matched to how their business operates and reach those agents from the tools employees already use.
Online casino game developer RubyPlay Ltd. is already using the product. Its team set an agent up once and scheduled it to run every day, and the report now arrives without anyone asking for it.
“It even flagged us on its own that not all of our target markets were covered yet, which told us it was reasoning through the task rather than just running a script,” said Avi Baruch, vice president of data and business applications at RubyPlay.
Data Agents is available now through Jedify’s Agents Hub, and companies can start on it for free. Jedify is a venture capital-backed startup that has raised more than $33 million, including a $24 million Series A round led by Norwest in June.

articles.title: Sony Pays $50,000 for the PS5 Hypervisor Bug, Jailbreak Scene Is Not Happy
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Sony Pays $50,000 for the PS5 Hypervisor Bug, Jailbreak Scene Is Not Happy
Sony has seemingly paid a security researcher named Jordy $50,000 for reporting a PS5 hypervisor bug, and it looks like it's the same bug that PS5 Linux developer Andy Nguyen had found earlier and kept to himself. Jordy's HackerOne profile, under the handle 2tonejordy, lists a single resolved PlayStation report worth $50,000, paid through the bug bounty program Sony launched in 2020. He shared the payout on X on October 14, joking that he "can at least buy GTA 6 with this." The jailbreaking community, however, isn't celebrating.
Back in mid-September, Nguyen announced he was walking away from the PS5 scene and his PS5 Linux work, including PS5 Pro support planned for 2027. According to him, he asked the researchers to wait until GTA 6 launched so people could buy the game and still run Linux, and they agreed, only to report it within a day. Jordy's version is a little different. He says he did agree to hold off, but someone else found the same bug with AI a few hours later, so he reported it, and he insists nobody handed him the bug. People were quick to pile on under his post, with one user accusing him of not finding the bug himself.There's no confirmation on whether Sony has patched it yet. Firmware 14.20 rolled out on October 21, though its patch notes only mention usability tweaks. A private exploit for firmware 14.10 also surfaced recently, but the hypervisor still seems to be holding up there. For now, owners who want to keep running Linux are better off staying on older firmware.

articles.title: Oregon city declares state of emergency over data center ban
articles.text:
Oregon city declares 'state of emergency' after statewide ban causes it to lose data center revenue
Umatilla declares emergency over Gov. Tina Kotek's data center ban
- Oregon city declares an emergency over $6 million in threatened revenue
- Statewide data center restrictions threaten more than $5 billion in investments
- Umatilla faces possible delays to its planned new police station
An Oregon municipality has declared an emergency after statewide restrictions on new data centers threatened approximately $6 million in expected municipal revenue.
Umatilla officials warned state Governor Tina Kotek's suspension of environmental permitting could disrupt infrastructure projects, employment opportunities, and billions in private investment.
The emergency declaration addresses anticipated financial losses rather than an existing budget crisis, with municipal reserves remaining at historically high levels.
Revenue losses threaten public infrastructure projects
The city's financial projections include income from planned data center developments, with some proceeds expected to support major public infrastructure improvements.
Among the threatened projects is a proposed police station, alongside several million dollars in planned upgrades to municipal water infrastructure.
City manager Dave Stockdale warned that interruptions to expected payments would force officials to reconsider schedules for improvements already incorporated into financial plans.
Umatilla currently hosts four operational data centers, while another facility is being constructed and two additional developments are awaiting completion.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The local industry includes Amazon Web Services and Sabey Data Centers, whose operations contribute to the area's expanding digital infrastructure sector.
Municipal estimates indicate that the permitting restrictions could jeopardize more than $5 billion in prospective private investment associated with local developments.
The council also identified risks to at least 1,000 construction jobs, alongside hundreds of permanent positions and employment opportunities in supporting industries.
Projects awaiting regulatory approvals could experience delays exceeding two years, while some developers might abandon their investments or move elsewhere.
“These consequences extend far beyond the interests of individual businesses. They threaten the broader economic and financial well-being of the Umatilla community,” said Dave Stockdale, Umatilla city manager.
“I believe the Governor's directive creates precisely the type of human-created circumstance involving threatened widespread financial loss that Oregon law expressly recognizes as a potential emergency.”
Despite these concerns, officials confirmed that existing municipal services and financial obligations remain unaffected because the disputed revenue has not been received.
Statewide restrictions and emergency response
Kotek instructed Oregon's environmental authorities in October to suspend new pollution permits for data centers, effectively restricting development until July 2027.
The governor previously halted transactions involving state-owned land intended for such facilities, allowing officials to examine their potential long-term consequences.
That directive followed an August decision preventing the sale of 32 acres at Salem's Mill Creek Corporate Center for a Verrus development.
Individual municipalities have also introduced restrictions, including Hillsboro, which imposed a 120-day suspension on new data center developments in July 2026.
Umatilla's council approved an emergency resolution requiring reconsideration within 90 days, following a formal request submitted by Stockdale to elected officials.
The resolution authorizes an economic assessment of projected losses and calls upon Kotek to reconsider the restrictions without further delay.
Stockdale claims that the city had not received or spent the expected data center revenue, although it had included the money in future financial plans.
He explained that the declaration was intended to protect future investment plans rather than address an immediate shortage of municipal operating funds.
The assessment will examine potential consequences for municipal financing, employment and infrastructure schedules while officials seek changes to the state's permitting policy.

articles.title: Instagram bien décidé à nous faire regarder des vidéos... de 90 minutes !
articles.text:
Instagram ne veut plus se limiter à ces courtes vidéos que l’on fait tous défiler machinalement (oui, vous aussi) sur notre smartphone. Le réseau social teste un nouveau format horizontal pouvant atteindre 90 minutes, pour nous inciter à regarder toujours plus de contenus, y compris sur notre téléviseur.
Vous pensiez qu’Instagram se résumait à ces photos, à ces Stories et à ces Reels que l’on enchaîne sans jamais voir le temps passer ? Meta a d’autres ambitions pour sa plateforme, et le réseau social expérimente actuellement un nouveau format baptisé « Features », conçu pour accueillir des vidéos horizontales pouvant durer jusqu’à 90 minutes.
Instagram veut passer à la vidéo longue durée
Interviews, podcasts, émissions humoristiques, contenus plus approfondis… Instagram entend s’ouvrir à des formats traditionnellement associés à un certain YouTube. Un changement de cap notable pour la plateforme qui a largement contribué à populariser les vidéos courtes et verticales.
Pour le moment, l’expérimentation reste limitée. Après une phase d’essai au Brésil, Instagram prévoit d’étendre le dispositif à une sélection de créateurs aux États-Unis, notamment des podcasteurs et des humoristes. Il ne s’agit donc pas encore d’une fonctionnalité accessible à tous.
Bien sûr, Instagram ne compte pas pour autant abandonner les vidéos courtes. Au contraire, le groupe souhaite faire cohabiter les deux formats. Dans l’idée, un court Reel peut servir de porte d’entrée vers une vidéo complète, que l’utilisateur pourra ensuite regarder sans quitter la plateforme. De quoi transformer un extrait découvert au hasard d’un énième scroll, en une séance de visionnage beaucoup plus longue.
Derrière cette évolution, la concurrence avec YouTube devient évidente. Instagram cherche à conserver son audience, mais aussi à offrir davantage de possibilités aux créateurs et aux annonceurs. Meta évoque plusieurs pistes de rémunération, sans avoir encore détaillé de modèle définitif pour ces nouveaux contenus.
Le téléviseur, nouvelle cible d’Instagram
Et si l’idée de regarder une vidéo Instagram de 90 minutes sur son téléviseur peut surprendre au premier abord, elle n’a finalement rien de si étrange. Après tout, c’est déjà ce que nous faisons avec YouTube, où podcasts, interviews et émissions occupent une place de choix sur le grand écran du salon. Alors, pourquoi pas Instagram ?
Meta semble en tout cas bien décidé à profiter de ce nouvel espace pour développer ses contenus horizontaux et faire entrer un peu plus son réseau social dans nos habitudes quotidiennes. Les vidéos longues pourraient ainsi devenir un levier supplémentaire pour installer Instagram (aussi) sur la Smart TV du salon.
Ce n’est pas la première tentative de Meta dans ce domaine. Lancée en 2018, l’application IGTV avait déjà tenté de s’imposer sur le terrain de la vidéo longue avant de disparaître en 2022, mais cette fois, Instagram mise sur une intégration directe à son écosystème. Adam Mosseri reconnaît que cette nouvelle orientation « demandera du temps pour trouver la bonne formule », mais assure que Meta est « pleinement engagé sur le long terme ».
- Des interactions faciles par de nombreux canaux (publications, Stories, messagerie, etc.)
- Un réseau social adapté aux préférences des utilisateurs dans la gestion de leur compte
- De nombreux types de contenus à créer, à partager et à consulter

articles.title: IT vendor lists massive $60 million AI supercomputer on eBay with 300 racks of decommissioned GPUs — includes 9,600 Nvidia A100 GPUs and 4,200 AMD EPYC CPUs, plus free shipping
articles.text:
IT vendor lists massive $60 million AI supercomputer on eBay with 9,600 Nvidia A100 GPUs and 4,200 AMD EPYC CPUs, plus free shipping — 300 racks of decommissioned GPUs on offer
If you ever wanted to own your own supercomputer or data center while earning eBay cashback, Core 4 Solutions has the perfect opportunity. The company is selling a 300-rack AI supercomputer on eBay for $59.7 million, complete with $50 overnight shipping, or free shipping if you're willing to go with FedEx Ground. The cluster packs 9,600 Nvidia A100 accelerators and 4,200 AMD EPYC Rome 64-core processors, enough to jump-start your own sovereign AI nation.
Nvidia and AMD have moved to newer architectures like Blackwell, Vera Rubin, and EPYC Turin. Nonetheless, A100 (codenamed Ampere) accelerators and EPYC Rome processors remain highly relevant for many computing tasks, including AI, machine learning, and scientific research. With the modern Blackwell and Vera Rubin racks from Nvidia, like the GB300 NVL72 and VR200 NVL72, costing up to $6.5 million and $7.8 million per unit, respectively, the A100 has turned into a legitimate budget alternative that can also circumvent the long waitlists and supply chain delays on Nvidia's newer AI hardware.
The cluster's sheer specifications are truly jaw-dropping. Each rack has four compute nodes and three management nodes. Each compute node has two AMD EPYC Rome 64-core processors, eight Nvidia A100 40GB SXM4 accelerators, and 1TB of DDR4-2933 memory. The management nodes are no less impressive. Each features two EPYC 64-core chips and 192GB of DDR4 memory.
When you sum it all up, the cluster comprises up to 9,600 A100 accelerators and 4,200 AMD EPYC Rome processors. With 64 Zen 2 execution cores per chip, the entire cluster boasts 268,800 cores. Memory capacity is equally impressive, with up to 1,401.6 TB or 1.4 petabytes for the entire cluster.
At first glance, $59.7 million sounds like a fortune, and it certainly is, but it seems like a reasonable valuation for the cluster. A rough estimate would be about $24 million for the A100S, $3 million for the EPYC Rome chips, and about $1.1 million for the DDR4 memory. That is about $28.1 million in crucial components, before factoring in other hardware like racks, cooling, power supplies, Nvidia Mellanox ConnectX-6 SmartNICs, etc.
Listing a 300-rack supercomputing cluster on eBay sounds absurd, but given today's AI-driven world, it is not as surprising as it may seem. After all, a broker once sold a 405-foot luxury Gigayacht for $168 million on eBay, so there is no reason why Core 4 Solutions cannot move a $59.7 million cluster. As AI farms and data centers expand, some enterprise clients out there will recognize the value and opportunity in the listing.
Shipping that many racks will be a logistics nightmare, and as funny as it sounds, Core 4 Solutions offers free local pickup or FedEx Ground delivery directly to your home. There is even an option to pay for a $25 two-day or $50 overnight delivery. Imagine FedEx casually dropping off 300 server racks at your front porch.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The cluster seems to have already drawn attention, with 11 people reportedly watching the eBay listing and one prospective buyer already letting it sit in their cart. I guess the real question is not whether it will sell, but whether the buyer will choose $50 overnight shipping.

articles.title: iPhone 18e : deux nouveautés majeures se précisent, mais Apple refuse toujours de corriger son plus gros défaut
articles.text:
iPhone 18e : deux nouveautés majeures se précisent, mais Apple refuse toujours de corriger son plus gros défaut
Attendu pour le printemps 2027, l’iPhone 18e n’a presque plus de secrets grâce à une nouvelle fuite. Malgré deux évolutions matérielles bienvenues, Apple maintiendrait une concession technique majeure du côté de l’affichage.
Après les iPhone 18 Pro et iPhone Duo, Apple prévoirait de revenir au printemps pour annoncer de nouveaux modèles. Outre les iPhone 18 et Air 2, l’iPhone 18e ferait son apparition, avec deux changements bien précis par rapport à son prédécesseur, l’iPhone 17e. Cependant, son plus gros défaut face aux autres smartphones milieu de gamme ne serait pas gommé, délivrant un écran figé dans le passé malgré une tarification élevée.
De la puissance à n’en plus finir sur l’iPhone 18e, mais à quel prix ?
Pour séduire les acheteurs au premier trimestre 2027, aux alentours de mars, Apple miserait sur deux améliorations ciblées pour l’iPhone 18e selon l’informateur Digital Chat Station. La première concernerait l’intégration de la puce A20, gravée en 2 nanomètres. De quoi offrir un gain notable en performances et en efficacité énergétique par rapport à la puce A19 de 3 nm embarquée sur l’iPhone 17e, le tout possiblement épaulé par 9 Go de RAM au lieu de 8 Go actuellement.
La seconde évolution toucherait la caméra frontale, qui abandonnerait enfin son vieux capteur de 12 Mpx. Bien que la fuite évoque un passage à 24 Mpx, Apple devrait logiquement opter pour l’objectif de 18 Mpx des iPhone 17, déjà réutilisé sur les iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max et Duo.
Vient ensuite le point qui fâche. La source souligne en effet que l’iPhone 18e conserverait son vieillissant taux de rafraîchissement de 60 Hz, toujours associé à une dalle Oled compacte de 6,12 pouces. Un choix qui priverait de nouveau l’appareil du 120 Hz, pourtant généralisé sur les smartphones d’entrée de gamme de nos jours. Pour espérer un affichage plus fluide sur cette déclinaison, il faudrait patienter jusqu’à l’hypothétique iPhone 19e en 2028, qui adopterait au passage la technologie ProMotion, faisant varier la fréquence d’affichage de manière dynamique en fonction du contenu à l’écran.
Pour le module photo arrière, le statu quo dominerait, avec toujours un seul et unique capteur de 48 Mpx, identique aux iPhone 16e et 17e, là où des rivaux multiplient les optiques polyvalentes entre ultra grand-angle et téléobjectif. Une façon pour Apple de contenir la hausse du coût des composants tout en évitant de cannibaliser l’iPhone 18 standard.

articles.title: El sistema LZB que ha fallado en el accidente de Toledo debería haber sido sustituido en su totalidad por ERTMS-2 en 2026
articles.text:
El 21 de abril de 1992, España asiste al primer viaje comercial en una línea de alta velocidad. Es el Madrid-Sevilla construido, entre otras cosas, para dar servicio a la Expo 1992 que se va a vivir en la ciudad andaluza. Quedan 11 años para que se abra la siguiente línea de alta velocidad española, el tramo Madrid-Zaragoza-Lleida del corredor Madrid-Barcelona.
Durante esa década se produce un cambio clave en la extensión de las líneas de alta velocidad en Europa. Esa segunda línea, llega ya con el sistema de seguridad ERTMS que viene a sustituir el sistema LZB, instalado en la línea Madrid-Sevilla. Un corredor que estaba siendo modernizado con este sistema generalizado en Europa y cuya implantación definitiva se esperaba para abril de 2026. El accidente de Urda (Toledo) se produce justo durante este proceso de renovación y antes de que se complete del todo.
El ERTMS es un sistema de seguridad que utiliza protocolos diferentes que el LZB. Ambos están considerados como de máxima seguridad pero desde hace tiempo se ha dado la orden desde la Unión Europea de modernizar las líneas al primero de ellos y abandonar el LZB para armonizar todos los lenguajes de seguridad.
Con motivo del accidente ferroviario de Adamuz (Córdoba), en La Vanguardia recogían que en Europa hay hasta 25 sistemas de seguridad diferentes, con 227.000 kilómetros de vías no operables porque no utilizan el mismo sistema de seguridad. Aunque debería ofrecer un nivel de seguridad muy similar, este sistema LZB ya se puso en el punto de mira en enero aunque posteriormente se supo (las investigaciones siguen adelante) que la causa principal del accidente se debió a un fallo en la infraestructura de la vía que hizo descarrilar a un tren Iryo y éste fue golpeado por un Alvia de Renfe.
Un buen ejemplo de esa falta de operabilidad entre sistemas la hemos vivido en España. El corredor andaluz es el único en el que se sigue utilizando el sistema LZB, en lugar del ERTMS. Esto hizo que Ouigo retrasara su llegada a Andalucía porque estaba teniendo problemas para homologar los trenes, que hasta entonces sólo funcionaban con este segundo sistema de seguridad más moderno.
Una vía en proceso de renovación
Para evitar este tipo de situaciones, desde la Unión Europea se dio la orden de cambiar al nuevo sistema ERTMS-2, la evolución del ERTMS. En abril de 2025, el Ministerio de Transportes anunciaba que la línea estaba siendo modernizada para adaptarse a este sistema (de hecho, en los mapas de Adif se muestra que la línea está "en proceso de renovación") y que esperaban que al finalizar 2026 la línea estuviera completamente renovada. Es decir, entre otras actuaciones, con el sistema ERTMS-2 activo.
Este sistema ERTMS-2 funciona de manera diferente al LZB. Este último se basa en un cable zigzagueante que envía la información relativa a la posición del tren, su velocidad de paso y los metros que quedan hasta el próximo cambio en el límite de velocidad.
El sistema, además, cuenta con que el tren interrumpe este circuito cerrado, señalando al CRC (el centro de control de Adif) dónde está cada tren para que dos trenes no circulen por un mismo cantón (tramo ferroviario de kilómetros que se utiliza como sistema de seguridad para una frenada de emergencia). El propio sistema puede gestionar una frenada de emergencia para que un tren no "invada" un cantón donde ya hay un tren situado.
Si el sistema sufre cualquier tipo de avería, como se ha indicado con las primeras informaciones del accidente de Urda (Toledo), el maquinista debe prestar atención al sistema ASFA, el cual indica mediante señales físicas situadas a los lados de las vías si tiene o no permitido el paso y la velocidad máxima a la que puede circular.
El sistema ERTMS-2 funciona de manera diferente. Lo que hace, a grandes rasgos, es simplificar el proceso y el equipamiento. La conexión del tren se realiza por GSM-R y las balizas quedan como sistema redundante para localizar el tren.
Con este sistema, se utiliza un equipo de radio que comunica al tren con el Movement Authority o MA (Autoridad de movimiento), explican en Cómo funcionan los trenes. Esa MA es la encargada de decirle al conductor la velocidad máxima a la que puede circular y durante cuántos kilómetros pero incluye una mayor cantidad de información como restricciones de velocidad temporales, lo que facilita cumplir con los límites.
Explican estos expertos que el sistema tiene la ventaja de que si un tren sufre un problema pero ya no puede detenerse, puede pasar por un enclave a una velocidad adecuada sin riesgo a descarrilar y solo aplica el frenado de emergencia cuando la situación es segura. Al contrario, cierra el paso de todos los trenes al instante para que no se produzca un choque. Se considera que el sistema es más seguro porque cuenta con mayor información, sistemas redundantes y las decisiones se toman más rápidamente.
Además, esa simplificación y modernización de los componentes es clave. En 2020, el Consejo de Ministros y Adif autorizaron la renovación de la línea con una adjudicación de 108 millones de euros tal y como se había adelantado meses antes. En los pliegos técnicos se especificaba que se había llegado al final de la vida útil del sistema y que el soporte técnico se había complicado porque Siemens y Thales/Hitachi, los proveedores de componentes, han venido reduciendo la producción de los mismos por lo que se corría el riesgo de no encontrar repuestos en caso de rotura del sistema.
Los plazos de ejecución pasaban por tener lista esta renovación en 2025, recogía elEconomista a principios de la década cuando se hizo público el contrato de renovación. También Cinco Días recogía un plazo similar, necesitándose 52 meses para ejecutar la renovación. Sin embargo, este cambio en el sistema de seguridad se ha ido retrasando ligeramente.
El año pasado, ABC recogía que la renovación completa se esperaba que fuera efectiva "a lo largo de 2026". Explicaban que parte de los retrasos se debían a que aunque la modernización fue anunciada a principios de 2020, no fue hasta noviembre de ese mismo año cuando se dio por bueno el contrato definitivo. Y fue en septiembre de 2021 cuando las obras comenzaron. Estas obras se estaban realizando por la noche para no afectar al tráfico o hacerlo lo menos posible.
A pesar de ello, en abril de 2025, Transportes ponía una fecha más concreta para la renovación de la línea: "el objetivo es que celebre su 34 aniversario completamente renovada y contando con la tecnología más moderna del mercado, como el sistema ERTMS 2". Es decir, el cambio debía haberse producido por completo antes de abril de 2026.
Hay que recordar que el accidente de tren en Adamuz (Córdoba) mantuvo el corredor ferroviario durante meses. Eso sí, el salto a este sistema de seguridad más moderno ya debería haber llegado antes de enero de 2026, cuando éste se produjo. En aquella ocasión se debió a un problema en la infraestructura de la vía pero el sistema debía estar renovado para entonces.
En resumen, la renovación del sistema obedece a varias causas. La Unión Europea busca mayor operabilidad de las compañías en todo el continente para que la liberalización de las vías sea menos costosa y eficiente. Pero también apuesta por un sistema que tiene menor dependencia de componentes físicos y, por tanto, que presentan un desgaste más rápido y un mayor riesgo de rotura.
También por un sistema sensiblemente más seguro aunque, hay que recordar, el sistema LZB está considerado como uno de los más robustos y se utiliza en miles de kilómetros en otros países de Europa.
