articles.title: Resident Evil Requiem, Five Nights at Freddy’s y más: los juegos recomendados por PlayStation para jugar en Halloween
articles.text:
Resident Evil Requiem, Five Nights at Freddy’s: Secret of the Mimic y Until Dawn integran la selección de juegos que PlayStation recomienda para Halloween, con propuestas de supervivencia, terror psicológico y acción.
La lista reúne títulos con mecánicas diferentes: decisiones que alteran el destino de los personajes, investigaciones paranormales cooperativas, exploración, sigilo y combates contra criaturas.
Entre los juegos elegidos también aparecen Phasmophobia, Amnesia: The Bunker, The Midnight Walk, SAROS, The Last of Us Part II Remastered, Valor Mortis, Silent Hill: Townfall y Alan Wake 2.
Cuál es la lista de PlayStation para Halloween
Until Dawn es una historia interactiva de terror en la que un grupo de amigos vuelve a una cabaña aislada en las montañas un año después de la desaparición de dos integrantes del grupo. Las decisiones del jugador determinan quién sobrevive hasta el amanecer.
SAROS sigue a Arjun Devraj, un agente que explora el planeta Carcosa bajo la influencia de un eclipse. El juego propone combates en tercera persona y un mundo que se transforma después de cada recorrido, mientras el protagonista reúne recursos y enfrenta enemigos hostiles.
En Phasmophobia, hasta cuatro jugadores investigan locaciones encantadas para identificar distintos tipos de fantasmas. Para hacerlo, utilizan herramientas como lectores EMF, grabadoras EVP, termómetros y cámaras de visión nocturna.
Resident Evil Requiem, el noveno título principal de la franquicia, sigue las historias de la analista del FBI Grace Ashcroft y el agente Leon S. Kennedy.
La experiencia combina combate, investigación, acertijos y administración de recursos, con la posibilidad de alternar entre primera y tercera persona.
Five Nights at Freddy’s: Secret of the Mimic transcurre en el taller abandonado de la mansión de disfraces de Murray. El objetivo es recuperar tecnología de Fazbear, resolver enigmas y evitar al Mimic, un endoesqueleto que puede adaptarse a distintos trajes y apariencias.
En The Midnight Walk, el jugador acompaña a Potboy, una lámpara perdida, por un mundo de plastilina animado en stop motion. La luz de ese compañero permite distraer a criaturas que se alimentan del fuego mientras el jugador se oculta y avanza por el recorrido.
Amnesia: The Bunker se desarrolla en un búnker abandonado de la Primera Guerra Mundial. El jugador controla al soldado francés Henri Clément, que debe administrar munición y provisiones, mantener encendidas las luces y escapar de una criatura que reacciona a sus ruidos y movimientos.
The Last of Us Part II Remastered retoma la historia de Ellie y Abby cinco años después del viaje de la primera entrega. La versión para PS5 incorpora mejoras gráficas, funciones del control DualSense y Sin retorno, un modo de supervivencia con enfrentamientos aleatorios.
En Valor Mortis, el jugador controla a William, un soldado de la Grande Armée que murió y resucitó en una versión alternativa de la Europa del siglo XIX.
Una plaga misteriosa se extendió por el continente, y el protagonista debe utilizar el poder que adquirió tras su resurrección para enfrentarse a enemigos y descubrir el origen de la enfermedad.
Silent Hill: Townfall presenta a Simon Ordell, quien regresa a St. Amelia para “enmendar las cosas”.
El jugador explora calles y zonas costeras cubiertas por niebla, sigue pistas y utiliza un televisor portátil llamado CRTV para detectar amenazas y hallar fragmentos de la historia. Sus decisiones definen los distintos finales.
Alan Wake 2 es un juego de terror psicológico y supervivencia protagonizado por Saga Anderson y Alan Wake.
Anderson, una agente del FBI, investiga una serie de asesinatos rituales en Bright Falls, mientras Wake intenta escapar del Lugar Oscuro, una realidad alternativa que cambia a partir de sus escritos. Ambos deben utilizar la luz como herramienta de defensa frente a una oscuridad sobrenatural.

articles.title: Info Edge reports steady business growth ahead of leadership transition
articles.text:
Info Edge reports steady business growth ahead of leadership transition
Revenue from operations grew 12% YoY, while net profit was up 87%. Growth was driven by recruitment business, 99acres, and matchmaking services.
Info Edge (India), which owns and operates internet-led businesses, delivered steady business growth in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 12.2% year on year (YoY) to Rs 903.9 crore, while profit after tax was up 87% YoY at Rs 649.8 crore.
Growth was supported by the recruitment business, faster expansion at property portal 99acres, and continued momentum in the matchmaking business. However, the education segment remained under pressure.
Profitability improved as expenses grew more slowly than revenue, although higher other income also contributed to the increase in reported profits.
There is also a leadership transition in the offing. Hitesh Oberoi is due to leave the full-time role of Managing Director and CEO on December 2 this year, after nearly 27 years with the company. Founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani is slated to assume an expanded executive role from December 3, subject to shareholder approval.
Operating growth improves
Info Edge operates the brands Naukri (online recruitment), 99acres (property listings), Jeevansathi and Aisle (matchmaking), and Shiksha (education services). It also invests in other businesses. So its financial results reflect both operating performance and changes in investment values.
Consolidated total income, including other income, increased 37.7% YoY to Rs 1,332.3 crore. Other income rose 164.8% to Rs 428.4 crore from Rs 161.8 crore, while total expenses increased 4.5% to Rs 588.6 crore from Rs 563.5 crore. Profit before tax, before exceptional items, rose 85.2% to Rs 747.7 crore.
Consolidated PAT reached Rs 649.8 crore, up 87% YoY from Rs 347.5 crore. This includes profits attributable to non-controlling interests in subsidiaries. The portion attributable to Info Edge’s shareholders was Rs 479.7 crore, up 51.6% from Rs 316.4 crore.
Based on consolidated revenue, expenses, depreciation and finance costs, operating EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) comes at approximately Rs 354 crore, up 27.4% YoY, with a margin of 39.2%, compared with 34.5% a year earlier.
Standalone revenue from operations rose 12.8% to Rs 841.7 crore, while operating profit before tax increased 29.8% to Rs 347.3 crore. Its margin expanded to 41.3% from approximately 35.9%.
Standalone PAT, however, fell 92.9% to Rs 333.8 crore from Rs 4,720 crore. The previous year’s quarter included an exceptional gain of Rs 5,200 crore arising from an unrealised investment valuation gain following the amalgamation of Makesense Technologies with PB Fintech. The decline therefore does not represent a comparable deterioration in operating performance.
Revenue streams diverge
Recruitment remained the largest revenue contributor. The company's earnings presentation, which includes acquired businesses in its operating-business breakdown, puts recruitment revenue at approximately Rs 682 crore, or 75.4% of the total. Standalone recruitment revenue grew 13.3% YoY to Rs 632 crore, while operating profit before tax increased 19.9% to Rs 374 crore. Its operating margin reached 59.1%.
Recruitment billings grew 12.6% in Q2 and 14.9% in the first half of FY27. Candidate Services billings increased 37%, while AI and data products for recruiters and job seekers accounted for a high single-digit share of recruitment topline.
Real estate contributed approximately Rs 134 crore, or 14.8% of revenue. 99acres revenue grew 16.7% YoY, while billings increased 21.2%. Property enquiries rose over 33% and app daily active users grew 25%. Operating losses narrowed 93% to Rs 1.6 crore, while cash from operations rose to Rs 22 crore from Rs 2.3 crore. These figures indicate improving business economics, although sustained operating profitability remains a test.
Matchmaking contributed around Rs 53 crore, comprising Rs 40 crore from Jeevansathi and Rs 13 crore from Aisle. Jeevansathi revenue grew 16.5% and it reported operating profit of Rs 2 crore. Aisle revenue increased 35.1% and billings rose 40%, but it recorded an operating loss of Rs 3 crore. Combined matchmaking billings grew 23.1% YoY.
Education remained the weakest business. Shiksha generated approximately Rs 35 crore in revenue, down 8.5% YoY, while billings fell 27.2%. The company attributed the pressure to AI-related traffic headwinds, declining Google-referred search traffic and subdued student interest in studying in the US, with preferences shifting towards the UK, Australia and Europe. The business reported negative operating cash flow of Rs 16 crore.
Cash and transition
Standalone cash generated from operations before tax rose 27.4% YoY to Rs 372.8 crore. The company reported a cash balance of approximately Rs 4,976 crore as at September 30, 2026, including balances held by wholly owned subsidiaries.
The company board has declared an interim dividend of Rs 3 per share and approved an investment of approximately Rs 150 crore in wholly owned subsidiary Redstart Labs. It has also approved exits from the stakes in Medcords and Unnati Online, investments that had been fully impaired in earlier years.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Samsung Portable SSD P9 review: speedy USB4 in a slim, pricey package
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
If you’re after fast external storage, you’re going to have to pay a lot for it these days, but Samsung’s P9 is the best USB4 drive we’ve tested to date. If you need speed for video recording or other professional tasks, its performance won’t disappoint.
Reasons to buy
- + Great USB4 performance
- + 16-inch, high-quality braided cable
- + 256-bit hardware encryption
Reasons to avoid
- - Expensive (like all SSDs these days)
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
It’s a tough time to launch an external SSD, with demand for flash and RAM at all-time highs thanks to AI hyperscaler demand. But content creators, videographers, and media collectors need more, faster, and roomier options, so Samsung has launched its first USB4 external drive, the Portable SSD P9.
It’s offered in 1, 2, 4, and 8TB capacities (but currently only in stock at 2TB as of this writing), with rated sequential read speeds up to 4,000 MB/s and write speeds up to 3,800 MB/s, a slim (0.3-inch) but simple boxy solid shell. It also includes one of the nicest-feeling sleeved cables I’ve come across (that’s also long for an external drive, at 16 inches). The Samsung P9 is a premium, pocket-friendly portable drive that’s speedy enough to potentially knock Corsair’s EX400U out of its top USB4 drive spot on our list of the best external SSDs.
It’s also quite expensive, starting at $339 for the 1TB model, $649 for the 2TB version we tested, and commanding a whopping $2,879 for the 8TB model. Those prices might seem extreme, given Corsair’s competing USB4 drive launched at $119 for 1TB in early 2025. But as we’ll see below in our comparison section, Samsung’s pricing isn’t exactly exorbitant compared to the current price of USB4-based competition – and many alternatives that launched last year are tough to find in stock.
Samsung P9 Specifications
| Product | 1TB | 2TB | 4TB | 8TB | 
| Pricing | $339.99 | $649.99 | $1,439.99 | $2,879.99 | 
| Interface / Protocol | USB4 Gen 3x2 (40Gbps) | USB4 Gen 3x2 (40Gbps) | USB4 Gen 3x2 (40Gbps) | USB4 Gen 3x2 (40Gbps) | 
| Sequential Read | Up to 4,000 MB/s | Up to 4,000 MB/s | Up to 4,000 MB/s | Up to 4,000 MB/s | 
| Sequential Write | Up to 3,700 MB/s | Up to 3,800 MB/s | Up to 3,800 MB/s | Up to 3,800 MB/s | 
| Dimensions | 3.5 x 2.6 x 0.3 inches | 3.5 x 2.6 x 0.3 inches | 3.5 x 2.6 x 0.3 inches | 3.5 x 2.6 x 0.3 inches | 
| Weight | 0.21 pounds | 0.21 pounds | 0.21 pounds | 0.21 pounds | 
| Warranty | 5 years | 5 years | 5 years | 5 years | 
Design and accessories
At 3.5 x 2.6 x 0.3 inches and weighing 0.21 pounds, the P9 is neither the smallest external storage drive, nor the lightest. But it’s slimmer than the company’s previous-generation T9 drive (which is 0.55 inches thick and roughly half as fast, at 20 Gbps). It ditches the rubber, textured, dust-collecting coating of the T9 for a metal shell on the P9 that feels very solid. The bottom of the P9 is coated in rubber to keep it in place on your desk.
There are no IP ratings for dust or wind resistance in Samsung’s spec sheet, and I don’t love the visible seam around the subtly rubberized bottom. But the P9 feels rigid and solid, to the point that I am pretty confident it could sustain more than its rated 2-meter drop rating.
There’s also a lot to like about the included cable, which is the only bundled accessory (unless you count paperwork). The cable is roughly 16 inches long, not counting the USB-C plugs on either end, and braided in a way that feels better than even other braided cables in my USB arsenal. There are even two Velcro-like hook-and-loop fasteners on the cable to keep any excess under control. Yes, it is just a cable, but I appreciate the ample length for us desktop PC users, and it is one of the nicest-feeling cables I’ve used.
Samsung Magician Software
Samsung includes a Samsung Magician Launcher link on the drive, but it’s really just a pop-up box that prompts you to download the latest version of the software. The app has widgets and sections for drive health and management, temperature and performance, diagnostics, monitoring, secure erasing or encrypting the drive (256-bit hardware encryption is supported), and more.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
It’s one of the more feature-rich SSD toolboxes, and benefits from Samsung’s long history in the storage realm. But it also has a mobile-app-first design that makes it look big and clunky on a desktop, with rounded corners. On the 65-inch TV that I use as a monitor, the Drive Health gauge defaulted to something close to the size of my head, and toggling to the compact version hides nearly everything but that single gauge widget. While that is of course an extreme example, the software just has a big UI for the information it presents.
Comparison products
Samsung has a fair amount of competition on the USB4 drive front, but much of it is increasingly scarce, likely due to flash availability. Sandisk’s Extreme Pro is the most recent USB4 competitor we’ve tested, with the 2TB version selling for $549, or $100 less than the P9.
LaCie’s Rugged SSD4 launched a little over a year ago and performed very well on both Windows machines and Macs. But it’s listed as sold out or no longer available in many places. As of this writing, it was available at Micro Center and a couple of online outlets, for between $750 and $800 for the 2TB model.
Corsair’s magnetic-backed EX400U has long been our favorite USB4 drive, for its compact size, performance, and value. But Corsair’s drive is also becoming hard to find in stock. And, like everything else in this space, its price has risen as well, with the 2TB version selling for $692 when I wrote this.
For those who don’t absolutely need USB4 speeds, the latest iteration of Crucial’s X10, a 20 Gbps drive with effectively half the bandwidth of these competing USB4 drives, is selling for $399 for the 2TB model. It’s very good for a 20 Gbps drive, but obviously that’s a different performance class than USB4 (40 Gbps).
With all that perspective, the $649 2TB Samsung P9 still feels expensive — if the drive launched a little over a year ago, it would likely have been roughly a third of this price. And it is $100 more than its Sandisk competitor, but it’s still priced a little less than other, older options. Let’s see how it performs.
Storage testbed
In 2025, we updated our external storage testbed to an AMD Ryzen 7600X-based PC with an Asus ROG Crosshair X870E Hero motherboard, installed in Lian Li’s Lancool 217 case. This was done in part because we needed a system with native USB4 support for upcoming drives (like this one).
All the drives in the charts below have been re-tested on the new X870E system, with the exception of the final Iometer sustained sequential test. That benchmark is less about top speed and more about how long a drive can write before depleting any fast cache onboard. We also updated to CrystalDiskMark 8, rather than the older (and non-comparable) version 7 we used on the previous testbed.
Trace Testing - PCMark 10 Storage Benchmark
PCMark 10 is a trace-based benchmark that uses a wide-ranging set of real-world traces from popular applications and everyday tasks to measure the performance of storage devices.
Samsung’s P9 doesn’t start off our test suite looking its best. It (unsurprisingly) falls behind LaCie’s Thunderbolt 5 drive (which is currently priced at $1,999 for the 4TB model we tested), but it also lands behind USB4 drives from LaCie and Sandisk in PCMark 10. It did, though, fare better than Corsair’s USB4 EX400U here.
Transfer Rates — DiskBench
We use the DiskBench storage benchmarking tool to test file transfer performance with a custom 50GB dataset. We copy 4,617 files (images, videos, and software ISO files) to a folder on the test drive (write). Then, after leaving the system idle for five minutes, we run the same test in reverse, moving the test folder to a different location on our PCIe 4.0 testing drive.
Samsung’s P9 led the pack in this real-world write speed test. Although its read speed technically landed it in fourth place, it again easily beat Corsair’s USB4 drive, and was close to Sandisk’s drive, which was less than half as fast when it comes to writes in this test. Note the somewhat odd performance of LaCie’s TB5 drive here, which is capable of being faster on Apple hardware, but did not perform very well on our USB4 testbed in some tests.
Synthetic Testing: CrystalDiskMark
CrystalDiskMark (CDM) is a free and easy-to-run storage benchmarking tool that SSD companies commonly use to assign performance specifications to their products. It gives us insight into how each device handles different file sizes. We run this test at its default settings.
The Samsung P9 looks its best on this synthetic, best-case-scenario benchmark, landing in first place in both reads and writes. Most of the other high-end drives were close, save for SanDisk’s USB4 SSD, which is a few hundred MB/s slower on read speeds, but was still fast.
Sustained Write Performance
A drive's rated write specifications are only a piece of the performance picture. Most external SSDs (just like their internal counterparts) implement a write cache, or a fast area of flash, programmed to perform like faster SLC, that absorbs incoming data.
Sustained write speeds often suffer tremendously when the workload saturates the cache and slips into the "native" TLC or QLC flash. We use Iometer to hammer the SSD with sequential writes for 15 minutes to measure the size of the write cache and performance after the cache is saturated.
Samsung hasn’t disclosed SLC cache size for its P9 drive, whether it’s fixed or dynamic, or if it differs by capacity. In other words, our 2TB P9 drive may be at a disadvantage here, at least compared to the 4TB LaCie and Crucial drives in our chart. But regardless, the Samsung P9’s performance on this test is largely positive, if somewhat complicated.
For roughly the first minute, the P9 wrote close to its max spec, around 3,750 MB/s. It then dropped to a write speed that fluctuated between just below 2,200 MB/s and just above 2,400 MB/s, which is still quite fast. It maintained that speed range for the next 12 minutes of writes, before dropping into the 600-800 MB/s range.
Sandisk’s Extreme Pro USB4 drive maintained its initial speed, around 3,500 MB/s, for roughly three times longer. But when its cache was exhausted, it dropped lower, first to roughly 1,200 MB/s, and then to around 800 MB/s. Looking beyond our usual 15-minute test, the Sandisk drive stayed in the same 800 MB/s range after the 15-minute mark, until we stopped the test at 30 minutes. The Samsung P9, however, recovered a good chunk of its write speed after about 17 minutes, switching back into its “middle” write range of 2,200-2,400 MB/s, from then until the end of the 30-minute test.
Corsair’s EX400U was more consistent in this test, but its write speeds never topped 1,800 MB/s, and it frequently dipped below 1,600 MB/s. Samsung’s P9 is flatly in another class, even though these are both USB4 drives.
Bottom line
As much as $649 for a 2TB external SSD still feels like a lot, the Samsung P9 performed very well in our testing. It wasn’t always at the top of the charts, but it consistently beat Corsair’s EX400U, which costs a little more now, if you can find it.
Sandisk’s Extreme Pro USB4 costs $100 less at 2TB, and $340 less at 4TB (and the P9 wasn’t even in stock at that capacity when this was written). But Sandisk’s drive has been on the market longer, and I would expect the two drives' prices to land close to each other once the P9 has settled into the market — that said, they both very well could go up in price, given recent trends.
Regardless, Samsung’s P9 drive is faster in most scenarios, particularly when it comes to sustained write speeds, which are important to professional users. And Samsung’s drive is about a third smaller, making it more travel-friendly. So while you could easily get by with Sandisk’s drive and save some money, Samsung’s P9 is a better USB4 drive if you want the best, fastest option for serious storage demands.
After a rough start with the Mattel Aquarius as a child, Matt built his first PC in the late 1990s and ventured into mild PC modding in the early 2000s. He’s spent the last 15 years covering emerging technology for Smithsonian, Popular Science, and Consumer Reports, while testing components and PCs for Computer Shopper, PCMag and Digital Trends.

On pense notamment aux 16 Go de mémoire vidéo empruntés au modèle supérieur et aux prestations en jeu de la carte graphique, qui permettent de jouer aisément en 2560 x 1440p, et même de flirter avec la 4K, y compris sur des jeux très récents, notamment grâce à la technologie DLSS4. Sa consommation reste maîtrisée en comparaison aux gains de performances apportés et ce modèle est pour l’instant le plus intéressant de la gamme au regard du prix.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).

articles.title: The US Navy is turning to a portable nuclear microreactor to power a key military base even if the lights go out
articles.text:
The US Navy is turning to a portable nuclear microreactor to power a key military base even if the lights go out
Truck-mounted nuclear microreactor should keep the lights on
- The US Navy has picked Radiant's 1MW Kaleidos microreactor for a prototype plant at Naval Weapons Station Crane in Indiana
- The Pentagon wants it running by September 2028 to keep critical systems powered through potential grid outages
- Kaleidos has not publicly gone critical yet, and one unit will back critical loads, not the whole base
The US Navy wants one of its most important weapons installations to keep running if the commercial grid goes down, so it chose a nuclear reactor that can be trucked in to do the job.
The Navy said it had selected Radiant Industries to design, build, and deliver a prototype microreactor power plant for Naval Weapons Station Crane in southern Indiana, a day after the California startup announced the win.
Brendan Rogers, Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Energy, Installations and Environment, said dedicated reactor power means "our critical naval support systems will never go dark."
A 'portable' nuclear reactor for critical infrastructure
Radiant's reaction to being picked has been jubilant: President and COO Tori Shivanandan said there is "no organization in the world with more experience in nuclear power" than the Navy, and the company now bills itself as the only nuclear firm selected by the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
It has multiple reasons to be proud; Kaleidos is a factory-built, helium-cooled, TRISO-fueled reactor rated at 1MW of electricity. Radiant says it can travel by road, sea, or air; needs no cooling water, major excavation, or extensive on-site construction; and runs for up to five years per fuel load over a 20-year life.
It will not roam around Crane; the whole unit travels in tandem. Radiant handles its own fueling, refueling, and spent-fuel storage, so host sites never keep spent fuel and can be returned to greenfield within two years of removing a unit, per the company.
The US Army's Janus program (which procured this) requires all radiological material to leave a host site within two years of shutdown, meaning either enlisting the US Department of Energy to help with any potential disposals or shuttling it elsewhere, often on public roads. Critics see the flip side: anti-nuclear group Beyond Nuclear argues the model puts reactors loaded with irradiated fuel on public highways on their way back to the factory.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The Navy's announcement gives no output, cost, or schedule; the 1MW figure is Radiant's. That is modest for a sprawling installation, and Army officials have been clear that Janus reactors are not meant to run whole bases. They will stay tied to the grid, and Jeff Waksman, the Army's principal deputy assistant secretary for installations, said they are "not going to provide 100% of the power on any of these installations."
The chosen deployment location is no ordinary one; Crane hosts the Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane Division and the Crane Army Ammunition Activity, which, together, handle weapons development, electromagnetic warfare, strategic missions, advanced manufacturing, and conventional munitions production, according to the Navy.
This isn't the Navy's first onshore reactor play; in March 1962, a portable 1.75MW pressurized water reactor known as PM-3A went critical at McMurdo Station in Antarctica, and a Navy team ran it for a decade.
It suffered a hydrogen fire in its first year, shut down for good in 1972 amid cost and corrosion concerns, and removing it meant shipping thousands of tons of contaminated gravel and soil back to the US, according to the Naval Historical Society of Australia. Waksman has cited Janus' two-year cleanup rule as a key break from how the military ran reactors in the 1950s and 1960s.
None of this means Crane won't get its reactor, but it does create red tape and a cautious environment. On the other side of the equation, the Pentagon has a hard deadline and an eager host state; the Navy's reactor program is lending its expertise; and Radiant has a $750 million Army contract in tow.
However, for now, the Navy has picked a reactor that has never publicly run at power to keep a weapons base lit when the grid fails, and testing at Idaho National Laboratory will decide whether "never go dark" is a plan or a hope once it happens.

articles.title: Red Hat introduces sandbox for OpenClaw agents- SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Red Hat brings OpenShell security to enterprise AI agents
After OpenClaw made a splash — or a tidal wave, depending on who you ask — in the artificial intelligence community, security became paramount.
Ahead of the upcoming KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA event, Red Hat LLC leaders gave more insight into OpenShell, a secure, open runtime for agents that is designed to keep OpenClaw deployments safe and governed. Nvidia Corp. developed OpenShell, which Red Hat is integrating into its AI platform. The architecture, which places agents in isolated sandbox environments.
“OpenClaw came out with a bang,” said Pete Cheslock (pictured, right), principal AI community architect at Red Hat. “This autonomous agent that can just do everything — it was really shocking to see the ecosystem and the community expand around it. As people started to dive into it … you start to ask the questions that everyone should be asking, especially enterprise, which is, what can this access and what can it do? That’s where tools like OpenShell started answering some hard questions.”
Cheslock and Stu Miniman (left), senior director of market insights for hybrid platforms at Red Hat, spoke with theCUBE Research Chief Analyst Dave Vellante ahead of KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive interview on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed the evolution of KubeCon and how Red Hat is addressing AI security concerns with open-source tools. (* Disclosure below.)
Securing OpenClaw with OpenShell
On Nov. 9, Red Hat will host an OpenShift Commons Gathering, an opportunity for open-source practitioners to hear from leaders in the space. Kubernetes is just one part of the cloud ecosystem, and its “heterogeneity” is increasing as AI makes demands on the multicloud, Miniman explained.
“There’s no better way to start your week than going [to OpenShift Commons],” he said. “We’ve got financial services companies, we’ve got companies that are working on AI, working on virtualization, working on some of those key cloud-native pieces, as well as we’ve got two of our Red Hat general managers. We are a clear leading contributor to all of these and have broad customer adoption.”
As organizations reassess agent security following OpenClaw’s rapid adoption, Red Hat and Nvidia are collaborating to bring OpenShell into enterprise AI environments. The idea is to use OpenClaw agents and OpenShell’s architecture in concert, so that agents’ access to potentially vulnerable information is monitored and secured.
“The OpenShell community is obviously new … but it’s growing at pretty incredible clip,” Cheslock said. “We’ve got contributors from a wide variety of companies. It builds on top of some core Kubernetes special interest groups. The agent sandbox is one of them, so that you can deploy these agents in a secure way using Kubernetes native APIs. Engineers who have to deploy these agents, there’s a lot of new stuff that they have to learn but they don’t have to learn the APIs to deploy it.”
Although agents can introduce serious security risks, companies are also deploying them for protection. AI-powered security tools can test for vulnerabilities at greater speed and scale than their human counterparts, helping organizations identify and patch gaps before attackers can find them.
“We’re trying to make sure that customers can feel secure and understand and use these tools,” Miniman said. “That’s front and center. There’s even more effort being put on security than ever, which has always been a focus of Red Hat … it’s that trust, compliance and security. If we make sure that layer is as locked down and reliable and trusted as possible, everything else comes secondary.”

articles.title: Radeon 9070 XT vs. Radeon 7900 XTX: 50+ Game Benchmark
articles.text:
In today's market, the Radeon RX 9070 XT is the best-value high-end GPU you can buy, which is brutal considering that pricing starts at around $900 (against a $600 MSRP). Still, that's about how much you'll pay for an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB in some markets, and the Radeon GPU is on average 70% faster at 4K gaming.
With that kind of performance gap, it's hard to make a case for GeForce right now, at least if you're shopping for something with more than 8GB of VRAM.
So, is it an open-and-shut case for the 9070 XT? Well, not so fast. Many readers have been asking us to revisit the Radeon RX 7900 XTX. Some have cited it as a potentially viable purchase in their region, while others simply want to see how AMD's RDNA 3 flagship has aged, and not just across 10 games, but more like 50+ titles. And that's exactly what we're going to do.
There's a lot of data to go over, after all we did test 51 games in total. However, much of it tells a similar story because the 9070 XT and 7900 XTX often deliver very similar gaming performance. So we'll focus on the games where we found notable results before diving into the overall performance summaries.
Test System
As usual, we're using our Ryzen 7 9800X3D GPU test system, equipped with 32GB of DDR5-6000 memory. The latest available display drivers at the time of testing were also used.
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D | 
| Motherboard | MSI MPG X870E Carbon WiFi [BIOS 7E49v1AA7] | 
| Memory | G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB DDR5-6000 32GB CL30 [CL30-38-38-96] | 
| Graphics Card | Radeon RX 9070 XT, Radeon RX 7900 XTX | 
| ATX Case | MSI Prospect 700R | 
| Power Supply | Kolink Regulator Gold ATX 3.0 1200W | 
| Storage | TeamGroup T-Force Cardea A440 M.2 PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD 4TB | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 26H2 | 
| Display Driver | AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.9.2 (9070 XT) AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.10.1 (7900 XTX) | 
Gaming Benchmarks
Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced
Believe it or not, the margins we're seeing here in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced are on the larger side of what we observed across the 51 games. In this example, the older 7900 XTX was 6-7% faster using the Very High quality preset, but when we enabled Extended Ray Tracing, that margin dropped to just 3-5%, depending on the resolution.
Black Myth: Wukong
Performance in Black Myth: Wukong is also much the same, though we are seeing up to a 6% performance advantage for the 7900 XTX using the High preset at 4K. That margin is reduced to just 3% when using the Cinematic preset.
Arc Raiders
Arc Raiders is more representative of the typical performance margins we saw. Here, the 9070 XT was 2-3% faster at 1440p, while the 7900 XTX nudged ahead at 4K by just 1%.
Borderlands 4
Borderlands 4 is a mixed bag. For example, the 7900 XTX was up to 7% faster at 1440p using the High preset, and 5% faster at 4K. However, switching over to the Badass preset allowed the 9070 XT to pull out a 4% win at 1440p, though the results were tied at 4K.
Crimson Desert
The older 7900 XTX enjoyed Crimson Desert, delivering 11% greater performance at 1440p when using Medium settings. Beyond that, though, we're looking at margins of around 6% or less.
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
The Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 results are very typical. For the most part, we're seeing nearly identical performance between these two GPUs. The only exception was at 1440p using Medium settings, where the 7900 XTX pulled out a 5% win. That's close enough to call a tie, but in this data set, it stands out as a relatively large margin.
Doom: The Dark Ages
The 9070 XT does quite well in Doom: The Dark Ages. At 1440p, we see no real difference between these two GPUs, but at 4K using the Ultra Nightmare settings, the newer Radeon GPU was 10% faster. However, despite the RDNA 4 architecture offering better ray tracing support, that advantage doesn't matter much with path tracing enabled, as both GPUs get smashed.
F1 25
F1 25 saw the 7900 XTX delivering up to 5% greater performance when using the High preset, as seen at 4K. However, enabling ray tracing favors the 9070 XT, though only slightly, with the newer Radeon GPU pulling ahead by 4-6%.
Hell is Us
Performance in Hell is Us is pretty typical of what we saw across most of the 51 games tested, with just a few frames separating these GPUs. In this example, the 9070 XT was generally ahead, but again, we're talking about low single-digit margins here.
Indiana Jones and the Great Circle
Indiana Jones and the Great Circle is another example where performance was largely the same. The 7900 XTX was up to 5% faster at 1440p using the Supreme preset, but that margin quickly shrank to just 2% at 4K. Then, when enabling full ray tracing, the 9070 XT takes the lead, though only just, offering around 5% better performance.
Lego Batman
Lego Batman provided us with more of the same. For the most part, there's little to nothing separating these two GPUs. At most, we saw a 4% margin at 4K using Medium settings, which favored the 9070 XT.
Monster Hunter Wilds
The same is true of Monster Hunter Wilds. Here, we're looking at identical or near-identical performance for the most part. The only somewhat noteworthy results can be seen at 4K using the High ray tracing settings, where the 7900 XTX was actually faster. So the 9070 XT isn't always superior when using RT effects.
Pragmata
Another typical example can be seen in Pragmata. Here, the 7900 XTX and 9070 XT deliver virtually identical performance, with or without ray tracing enabled.
Marvel Rivals
The same is also true of Marvel Rivals. The two GPUs trade blows using Medium settings, with performance swings no larger than 4%. But once we max out the quality settings, performance is virtually identical.
007 First Light
007 First Light gives us a mixed bag of results. Using Medium settings at 1440p, the 7900 XTX was 4% faster, not a big margin, but at 4K the results are flipped, and now it's the 9070 XT that's faster, leading by a slim 6% margin. Back at 1440p, but this time with Ultra settings, the 7900 XTX gets out to a 9% lead, only for that margin to shrink to 2% at 4K.
Cities: Skylines
Cities: Skylines provides us with some unusual results. In this example, the older 7900 XTX is quite a bit faster, delivering 12-13% greater performance using the Medium preset and then 12% at 1440p using High settings, though just 6% at 4K. Still, overall, the 7900 XTX was the faster GPU in this title.
Counter-Strike 2
The 7900 XTX was also dominant in Counter-Strike 2, delivering 18% greater performance at 1440p with Medium settings and 25% at 4K. These gains were maintained using Very High settings, with the older Radeon delivering 22% greater performance at 1440p and then a massive 32% increase at 4K.
Delta Force
In this example, we see that Delta Force favors the newer 9070 XT. Here, the RDNA 4 GPU delivered 14% more performance at 1440p using Ultra settings, though just 5% more at 4K. We also saw similar scaling using the Ultimate preset.
Forza Horizon 6
Forza Horizon 6 provided the kind of data I expected to see more of, that is, competitive rasterized performance with the newer 9070 XT taking the cake once ray tracing is enabled. Using the Extreme preset, the 9070 XT was 3% faster, but when we switched over to ray tracing, that margin grew substantially to 23%.
Fortnite
Testing with Fortnite, we find the limits of our Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor at 1440p using Performance mode, reaching just over 700 fps, which seems like enough to me, for now. Anyway, at 4K, the 7900 XTX delivered 18% stronger performance, and even with ray tracing enabled, the older RDNA 3 GPU still came out on top, offering 14% better performance.
Grand Theft Auto V
Testing with Grand Theft Auto V shows very similar rasterized performance between these two GPUs, but once we enabled ray tracing using the Maximum RT preset, the 9070 XT takes over, crushing the 7900 XTX by 35% at 1440p and 33% at 4K.
Spider-Man 2
The 9070 XT also dominated our Spider-Man 2 testing, well, at least at 1440p, where it was 9% faster using the Very High preset and then 22% faster with the maximum ray tracing settings enabled. At 4K, the margins were much smaller, in the 5-6% range.
Performance Summary
Across the 51 games tested, how do the 9070 XT and 7900 XTX compare?
Well, they're nearly identical in terms of performance. This data doesn't tell us too much, other than the fact that overall, these GPUs deliver very similar performance. So let's take a closer look at the per-game results.
Average Performance by Game
Please note that this data is based on average frame rates, calculated using the geo mean, and combines the two quality configurations tested, as well as both resolutions.
As you can see, the vast majority of games saw less than a 10% difference in performance between these two GPUs. In fact, just five games exceeded 10%. The worst examples for the 9070 XT were Counter-Strike 2 and Red Dead Redemption 2, while its best results came in GTA V, Forza Horizon 6, and Naraka: Bladepoint.
What We Learned
The Radeon RX 9070 XT has continued to age well, and we've seen plenty of evidence of this recently. We've seen it matching and even beating the RTX 5070 Ti in newer titles such as Gears of War: E-Day, The Witcher 3 Remastered, and Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, to name a few, though that will depend on the settings used.
Not only did most early reviews of the 9070 XT find it trailing the 5070 Ti by a reasonable margin, but also the 7900 XTX. Now the 9070 XT and 7900 XTX appear to be pretty much neck and neck.
Looking across all 51 games tested, the performance margins generally fall into three categories: 1) near-parity in standard rasterization, 2) ray tracing and path tracing gives the advantage to the newer RDNA 4 architecture, and 3) specific titles where the older 7900 XTX flagship flexes its memory bandwidth and compute muscle.
Where the GPUs Differ
At native 4K, the Radeon 7900 XTX's additional bandwidth can help, particularly in memory-intensive games. However, that doesn't translate into a 50% increase in FPS simply because it has 50% more memory bandwidth.
The 7900 XTX also has 50% more VRAM: 24GB versus 16GB for the 9070 XT. But right now that only matters when playing heavily modded games with UHD texture packs, running games at extreme settings, working with large 3D scenes, or using local AI models that exceed 16GB.
With ray tracing enabled, particularly in newer games, the 9070 XT generally comes out on top, sometimes by a substantial margin. Both GPUs now support FSR 4.1 upscaling, as AMD extended support to the RX 7000 series back in June. This means the 7900 XTX is no longer restricted to the lower-quality FSR 3.1 upscaler.
The key difference to note here is that the 9070 XT uses FP8 acceleration to run FSR 4.1 more efficiently. It also supports the newer ML frame generation and ray regeneration features in FSR Redstone. The 7900 XTX, on the other hand, runs FSR 4.1 through INT8 processing, which comes with higher overhead. It still supports older FSR frame generation, but not all the RDNA 4-exclusive Redstone features.
As an example, AMD reports roughly 1.3 ms of FSR 4.1 upscaling processing time at 4K on the 9070 XT, compared with 3.1 ms on the 7900 XTX. In short, this means the 9070 XT can deliver better performance when both GPUs use the same upscaling settings, even in games where the 7900 XTX is faster natively.
Both GPUs support AV1 encoding for streaming, though the 9070 XT also gets PCIe 5.0 support, which can be viewed as a modest future-facing benefit. That said, the 7900 XTX's PCIe 4.0 x16 interface really isn't a limitation, especially given that you're far less likely to exceed its VRAM capacity.
Pricing can vary from month to month, sometimes substantially, but as of writing the 9070 XT costs $900 in the US, or $1,250 in Australia, while secondhand 7900 XTX models are selling on eBay for between $800 and $1,100, or around $1,500 in Australia. At those prices, the 9070 XT makes far more sense for most buyers. Obviously, if you already own the 7900 XTX, upgrading to the 9070 XT would be a sidegrade at best, so don't do that.
Bottom line, the 7900 XTX has continued to age well and remains highly competitive with current generation high-end GPUs. Like the 9070 XT, it has only gotten better since release through updated features such as FSR 4.1, even if AMD did take its sweet time rolling out support.

articles.title: Steam Frame Gets Mainline Linux Support, Signalling SteamOS Alternatives for VR Gaming
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Steam Frame Gets Mainline Linux Support, Signalling SteamOS Alternatives for VR Gaming
The Valve Steam Frame has been supported in downstream SteamOS kernel builds since its launch in September, but a new set of patches submitted for inclusion in the mainline Linux kernel 7.4 will officially add support for the new VR headset in the mainline Linux kernel. The patches were submitted by Neil Armstrong on behalf of Valve Software and provide initial support for the Steam Frame. 
The patch notes specifically mention support for system reserved memory, regulators, GPIO keys PMIC functions, PMIC ADC channels, USB gadget, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth, I2C and basic peripherals, and the built-in SD card slot. While support isn't yet feature-complete, it lays the groundwork for further kernel support down the line and should make it significantly easier for other distributions to support the Steam Frame without implementing a bunch of custom code and tools. This is also just one of many Linux 7.4 patches that will improve hardware support in the upcoming Linux kernel version.

articles.title: Samsung launches clip-on Galaxy Buds On that work on either ear
articles.text:
Samsung has released the new Galaxy Buds On earbuds, its first clip-on Galaxy Buds. Though the earbuds are officially only in South Korea, I expect a global release to follow.
Samsung says the Galaxy Buds On lets you listen to what’s going on around you while listening to music or having a conversation. Because of the design, it puts less strain on the ears during extended use. The company said it analyzed data from different ear shapes so that it can optimize the position of the speakers and battery.
The Buds On also sports ‘TwinBoost speakers’ designed to offer better low-frequency performance, along with automatic volume control that adjusts to the environment. There’s also an Audio Leakage Reduction feature to help prevent people from hearing what you’re listening to. And when you’re setting up the earbuds, they don’t have a right and left side. The Buds On can automatically detect which side they’re in and adjust the audio channels accordingly.
Spec-wise, the Buds On use the Snapdragon S7 Gen 1 Sound platform with a high-efficiency Class-D amplifier for up to 9.5 hours of continuous music playback on a single charge.
In addition to three microphones, the Buds On have a bone conduction-based vibration sensor that detects vibration when a person speaks and uses machine learning to separate the user’s voice and reduce background noise.
When you wear the Buds On and say “Hey Google, let’s talk live,” Gemini Live launches, so you can talk to the AI in a natural conversation.
There are also Head Gestures to answer or end calls, dismiss alarms, or read message notifications. On Galaxy devices, you can adjust the volume and equalizer by just heading over to your device’s settings instead of heading to the Galaxy Wearable app.
The earbuds are priced at KRW₩299,000, which converts to roughly C$316.94, so if the Buds On come to Canada, expect them to be in the mid-$300 range.

articles.title: China’s snooping around Pacific undersea cables raises risks for Big Tech
articles.text:
Subsea cable projects owned by US companies such as Google and Meta face some of the greatest risks from the threat of deep-sea sabotage in the Pacific Ocean, according to a new report. That coincides with Chinese research ships spending an extraordinary amount of time apparently surveying undersea cables—not to mention Chinese commercial ships being investigated for cutting cables in both European and Asian waters.
Most damage to the undersea cables that form the Internet’s backbone is the result of accidents involving bottom-trawling fishing nets and ship anchors dragging on the seabed, with storms and undersea landslides also factoring in. But the recent rise in international tensions and open conflicts have placed new scrutiny on more suspicious instances of cable-cutting damage, with analysts warning about Russia and China in particular engaging in cable sabotage or tampering as “gray zone” tactics that fall short of direct military confrontation.
One of the newest risk assessments of China’s gray zone tactics targeting the Internet’s undersea infrastructure comes from a research report published by the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, an independent government commission that advises Congress. The report was contracted to the London-based think tank China Strategic Risks Institute and published in September 2026.
Mapping the risks
The report authors created an interactive Trans-Pacific Cable Gray Zone Vulnerability Index that ranks the undersea cables considered most at risk and displays a map of their routes spanning the Pacific Ocean. Such an index could help identify which cables should get highest priority in terms of placing underwater sensors or setting up patrols to monitor for threats.
Risk factors used in the vulnerability index include the undersea depth of the cable routes, nearby shipping traffic, cable ownership, China’s exclusive economic zone and broader territorial claims, and whether each cable connects to Taiwan. Taiwan is considered a geopolitical hotspot as a self-governing island democracy that is also claimed by China, with the latter ramping up military maneuvers involving warships and aircraft around Taiwan in recent years.

articles.title: 10 000 commandes en 19 heures : Volkswagen fait un carton en Chine avec sa berline électrique à 10 700 €
articles.text:
La nouvelle valait bien un joli communiqué. Alors que l’avenir n’a jamais été aussi incertain chez Volkswagen, leur dernier modèle électrique apporte une belle lueur d’espoir. La Jetta M6 fait en effet un carton inespéré en Chine, avec près de 10 000 commandes en seulement 19 heures. Face aux constructeurs locaux solidement établis, cette surprise intégrale fait bien évidemment les affaires de la marque allemande.
Celle-ci a mis les bouchées doubles pour réussir ce tour de force, puisque la Jetta M6 n’est déjà pas très chère. Jetta étant la branche économique de Volkswagen dédiée au marché chinois, il ne pouvait en être autrement. Dont acte : la M6 débute à 79 800 yuans, soit l’équivalent de 10 700 €. 10 700 € pour une berline de 4,81 mètres plus imposante que la Tesla Model 3, référence des références, ça vaut franchement le détour.
10 000 commandes fermes : un vrai raz-de-marée face aux constructeurs locaux
Et ces 10 000 fameuses commandes ne sont pas de simples déclarations intéressées. Il s’agit de commandes fermes ne pouvant plus être annulées sans perdre un dépôt allant de 3 000 à 5 000 yuans selon la version choisie. C’est un signal extrêmement fort. Et pour attirer encore plus de clients, Volkswagen applique en parallèle une protection canon sur le système de conduite semi-autonome du véhicule.
Tout incident ou collision lié à l’assistance à la conduite survenant la première année suivant l’achat du véhicule sera entièrement indemnisé par la marque. De quoi apporter confiance et sérénité aux acheteurs, qui ne savent plus où se tourner tant le marché chinois du véhicule électrique est saturé. Premier modèle à batterie de la marque Jetta, la M6 mise sur une gamme simplissime contrairement à ses rivales.
Écran géant, IA intégrée et… mode lit double à bord !
Les modèles de base sont ainsi équipés d’un électromoteur de 154 ch associé à une batterie lithium fer phosphate de 42,9 kWh assurant une autonomie de 465 km sur le cycle CLTC. Les versions haut de gamme grattent pour leur part une machine électrique de 197 ch avec un pack plus volumineux de 51,9 kWh. Suffisant pour offrir un rayon d’action de 555 km selon la norme CLTC. La charge rapide est en série, avec un 30 à 80 % de batterie en 25 minutes.
Si le style de l’auto est très anonyme, son équipement convainc. Notons notamment un écran 2,5K de 15,6 pouces avec les intelligences artificielles Doubao, DeepSeek et Qwen, ainsi qu’une mise en tablette possible des deux sièges avant permettant d’installer un lit double. Ce raffinement va de pair avec la recharge bidirectionnelle V2L pour le camping. La nouvelle Jetta M6 n’est bien entendu pas prévue chez nous.

articles.title: 800 euros pour jouer 8 heures à GTA 6, l'offre aberrante mais réelle proposée par une entreprise en Europe
articles.text:
Être payé 100 euros de l’heure pour jouer à GTA 6, c’est l’offre lancée par Virgin Media en Irlande. Sauf que derrière ce « job de rêve », on retrouve un concours très encadré, à l'avantage de l'opérateur.
L’opérateur Virgin Media Ireland, de l'autre côté de la Manche, a lancé un concours assez improbable pour être payé à jouer à… GTA 6, à raison de 100 euros de l’heure pendant huit heures, avec jeu offert s'il vous plaît. Présentée comme une offre d’emploi, l’opération s’adresse aux résidents irlandais majeurs, et les candidatures courent jusqu'à mi-novembre. Le règlement impose toutefois au gagnant de faire valider sa critique par l’opérateur avant de la publier sur les réseaux sociaux.
Payé 800 euros pour jouer 8 heures à GTA 6, sympa comme mission
Sur sa page, Virgin Media parle d'embauche, mais il s'agit bien d'un concours, encadré par un règlement officiel. L'opérateur choisira un seul gagnant parmi les candidats. Celui-ci devra jouer huit heures à GTA 6 au cours d'une semaine, à son rythme, d'une traite ou par petites sessions. À 100 euros de l'heure, cela fait une petite manne de 800 euros, auxquels s'ajoute le jeu, acheté par Virgin Media (79,99 euros en France pour l'édition standard). Inutile d'être abonné chez l'opérateur pour tenter sa chance, mais l'offre est réservée aux personnes majeures qui vivent en République d'Irlande.
Le dossier de candidature nécessite de fournir un nom, une date de naissance, un téléphone, une adresse e-mail, ses comptes Instagram ou TikTok ainsi que quelques lignes de motivation, pour être valide. La date limite des candidatures est le 15 novembre, et le gagnant sera contacté dans les sept jours suivant la clôture.
Le calendrier est plutôt calé sur celui de Rockstar Games. GTA 6 débarque le 19 novembre 2026 à minuit, heure locale, sur PS5 (où il pèsera 210 Go !) et Xbox Series X|S, avec un préchargement possible dès le 12 novembre en version numérique. Aucune version PC n'est annoncée à ce stade, rappelons-le. Virgin s'adresse à ceux qui comptent les jours depuis mai 2025, prêts à rejoindre Jason et Lucia à Vice City, au cœur de Leonida, cette Floride à peine déguisée. Bon, certains se diront peut-être que huit heures de jeu sur GTA ne suffiront pas à explorer ne serait-ce qu'une petite partie de la carte, qui s'annonce gigantesque.
Une critique de GTA 6 sous surveillance, sans l'aval de Rockstar Games
Pour valider la participation à cet essai de GTA VI rémunéré, Virgin Media demande un avis « honnête » sur le jeu tel que découvert jusque-là, c'est-à-dire ses premières heures. Le gagnant devra d'abord soumettre son texte à l'opérateur, qui décidera s'il peut être publié. Une fois approuvée, la critique paraîtra entre le 20 et le 26 novembre en ligne et sur les réseaux sociaux, avec un tag vers Virgin Media Ireland et la mention #Ad bien en évidence. La sincérité, oui, mais avec le visa de l'annonceur.
La contrainte suivante est assez amusante. Dites-vous que l'avis ne pourra contenir aucune séquence de jeu, aucune capture d'écran, aucun son, ni aucun visuel ou logo lié à Rockstar Games ou Take-Two. Vanter GTA 6 sur TikTok sans jamais le montrer, l'exercice a de quoi faire transpirer le plus imaginatif des créateurs. Il laisse surtout deviner une opération menée sans l'aval de l'éditeur, Rockstar Games. Mais comme on dit, à l'impossible nul n'est tenu ! D'ailleurs, hors mis le nom du jeu, la page de Virgin ne contient aucun élément multimédia ni autre contenu qui pourrait être revendiqué par le studio américain.
Ce job de rêve est surtout une jolie opération marketing, qui s'assumera, vous l'avez compris, jusqu'au hashtag.

articles.title: WhatsApp Plus APK Descargar (Oficial) Última Versión 2026: por qué instalar esta app pone en peligro mi dinero
articles.text:
Usar versiones alteradas de WhatsApp, como WhatsApp Plus, representa un riesgo porque estas aplicaciones de terceros violan las Condiciones del servicio de la plataforma y pueden exponer los datos personales del usuario.
La plataforma puede suspender una cuenta de forma temporal o permanente cuando detecta el uso de una aplicación no oficial.
Además, usar aplicaciones alteradas como WhatsApp Plus implica riesgos de seguridad que van más allá de una eventual suspensión de la cuenta.
Al no ser desarrolladas ni supervisadas por WhatsApp, estas versiones pueden incluir virus, programas maliciosos o mecanismos capaces de acceder a información almacenada en el teléfono. Esto puede exponer conversaciones, fotos, contactos, contraseñas y otros datos personales.
El peligro también alcanza al dinero del usuario: si la aplicación obtiene acceso a códigos de verificación, datos bancarios o billeteras digitales, podría facilitar fraudes o robos. Descargar solo la aplicación oficial reduce estos riesgos y protege la privacidad del dispositivo.
Por qué no usar WhatsApp Plus, la versión alterada
WhatsApp clasifica aplicaciones como GB WhatsApp o WhatsApp Plus —la aplicación de terceros, distinta de la suscripción— como versiones alteradas desarrolladas por terceros que violan sus Condiciones del servicio.
La plataforma no puede validar las prácticas de seguridad de esas aplicaciones, lo que expone los datos del usuario a riesgos que la versión oficial no presenta. Además, el uso de estas herramientas activa los sistemas de detección automática de WhatsApp, que pueden suspender la cuenta sin previo aviso.
Ignorar el aviso de suspensión temporal y no instalar la aplicación oficial puede derivar en un bloqueo permanente. La medida preventiva es usar exclusivamente WhatsApp, disponible en las tiendas de Google y Apple.
Cómo actuar ante una suspensión temporal o permanente
Ante una suspensión temporal, el primer paso es desinstalar de inmediato la aplicación no oficial.
Antes de hacerlo, conviene realizar una copia de seguridad de los chats: en el caso de GB WhatsApp, el proceso es manual y requiere renombrar la carpeta de datos; en WhatsApp Plus, el historial se transfiere de forma automática al instalar la versión oficial.
Una vez eliminada la aplicación de terceros, el usuario debe descargar WhatsApp desde Google Play Store o App Store, verificar el número de teléfono y restaurar la copia de seguridad disponible.
Si el bloqueo ya es permanente, WhatsApp habilita el botón “Solicitar revisión” en la misma pantalla donde aparece el aviso. Al pulsarlo, el usuario puede explicar su caso directamente desde la aplicación.
La plataforma recomienda ser claro y honesto: si la suspensión ocurrió por el uso de una aplicación no oficial sin conocer las normas, conviene mencionarlo y comprometerse a cumplir las condiciones del servicio en adelante.
Quienes no puedan acceder a ese botón pueden enviar un correo a support@whatsapp.com con el número de teléfono en formato internacional, el modelo del dispositivo y una descripción del problema.
El tiempo de respuesta habitual oscila entre 24 y 72 horas. Si la apelación es rechazada, WhatsApp notifica que la suspensión es permanente y la única alternativa es registrar una cuenta nueva con un número diferente.
Qué es la suscripción WhatsApp Plus
WhatsApp Plus es el primer plan de suscripción oficial de Meta para WhatsApp. Por USD 2,99 al mes, con un mes de prueba gratuito, los usuarios acceden a un paquete de personalización que no altera las funciones esenciales de la aplicación.
El plan incluye 18 nuevos temas de color para la interfaz, 14 iconos alternativos para el menú del teléfono, 10 tonos de llamada exclusivos, paquetes de stickers premium y la posibilidad de fijar hasta 20 conversaciones en la parte superior de la lista de chats.
Los mensajes, las llamadas, las videollamadas y el cifrado de extremo a extremo permanecen gratuitos para todos los usuarios.

articles.title: Info Edge’s Hitesh Oberoi to step down as MD and CEO; founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani to take over
articles.text:
Info Edge’s Hitesh Oberoi to step down as MD and CEO; founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani to take over
After nearly 27 years with Info Edge, Hitesh Oberoi will step down from his full-time executive role in December 2026. Founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani will take over as MD and Group CEO, subject to shareholder approval, as investors watch how the leadership transition shapes the company's next phase.
Hitesh Oberoi, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Info Edge, will step down from his full-time executive role on December 2, 2026, after nearly 27 years with the company, including more than 16 years as MD. The parent of Naukri.com announced the leadership change alongside its second-quarter FY27 results.
Sanjeev Bikhchandani, the founder of Info Edge, will take over as Executive Vice Chairman, Managing Director and Group CEO from December 3, 2026, subject to shareholder approval. The move will see Bikhchandani return to an active management role after serving as Executive Vice Chairman. According to the company's regulatory filing, his term will run until April 26, 2031.
Oberoi, however, will continue to be associated with the company. Subject to shareholder approval, he will remain on its board as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director. Info Edge said he had chosen to step back from his full-time executive role to devote more time to education, entrepreneurship, institution building, investing and philanthropy, while spending more time with his family.
In a statement, Oberoi said that after nearly 27 years, he felt it was the right time to begin transitioning out of his full-time operating role. He added that he would miss the colleagues and teams who had made those years special. Bikhchandani said the two had built Info Edge together over more than 27 years.
Oberoi's tenure spans much of Info Edge's growth. According to a report citing the company's filing, its market capitalisation increased from Rs 2,500 crore to Rs 80,000 crore during his tenure. Oberoi formally took over as CEO and MD in 2010, when Bikhchandani moved into the role of Executive Vice Chairman. The company said it has a strong institutional foundation, supported by senior leaders who have been with Info Edge for more than 20 years.
Investors will be watching how the leadership change affects Info Edge’s core recruitment business and broader strategy. The move comes after CFO Chintan Thakkar stepped down in November 2025, with co-promoter Ambarish Raghuvanshi taking over as interim CFO.

articles.title: Instagram aposta na competição com o YouTube • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Instagram aposta na competição com o YouTube
Plataforma de Mark Zuckerberg ganha vídeos longos e na horizontal.
O Instagram está avançando nos vídeos horizontais de até 90 minutos em um novo recurso em teste, chamado Features. Ele é voltado a conteúdos mais longos, como podcasts e entrevistas, e já está sendo experimentado com alguns criadores no Brasil e nos Estados Unidos.
Essa não é a estreia de vídeos horizontais na plataforma e nem a primeira vez que o Instagram adapta uma ferramenta ao formato, mas, além do player, a rede deve integrar o formato aos Reels.
Criadores poderão publicar cortes e vinculá-los ao vídeo completo, permitindo que o usuário continue assistindo ao conteúdo sem sair do Instagram. O chefe da rede, Adam Mosseri, mostrou em um post como a ferramenta funciona.
Segundo a vice-presidente de produto Tessa Lyons, a intenção é criar uma porta de entrada para a produção principal. A empresa está testando a possibilidade de vincular até oito Reels a um mesmo vídeo longo.
O Features já vinha sendo testado com alguns criadores brasileiros e começou a chegar nesta semana a um grupo restrito nos Estados Unidos.
A iniciativa representa uma mudança de posição para a rede social, que sempre priorizou vídeos curtos. Segundo Lyons, o medo era de que os vídeos longos reduzissem as interações que a empresa considera centrais para a plataforma, como enviar Reels, fotos e carrosséis para amigos.
A avaliação mudou com a percepção de que os formatos poderiam ser complementares. Podcasts e vídeos de comédia, por exemplo, costumam ser divididos em trechos menores, que viralizam em plataformas como o TikTok e o próprio Instagram e atraem o público para a produção completa.
O YouTube já permite marcar um vídeo longo em Shorts, por exemplo, e ainda é a principal plataforma de vídeos longos. Outro desafio para o Instagram deve ser competir com o programa de divisão de receitas do YouTube, algo que ainda não aparece no horizonte.
Para os participantes iniciais do teste, a plataforma negocia alguns acordos individualmente. Os contratos não exigem exclusividade e criadores podem manter patrocínios próprios incorporados aos vídeos. Outras formas de remuneração ainda estão sendo estudadas, segundo o Hollywood Reporter.
A aposta em conteúdos horizontais também acompanha a expansão do app do Instagram para televisões. Ele foi lançado no fim de 2025, com foco nos Reels. Desde então, chegou à Google TV, televisores Samsung e Apple TV.
O Features faz parte de uma série de experimentos recentes voltados a vídeo. Entre eles está o Series, que permite agrupar Reels relacionados em uma área dedicada no perfil do criador, facilitando a organização de conteúdos divididos em episódios. O recurso está em testes desde junho e deve chegar a mais países.

articles.title: Police reportedly pulling motorists over because AI algorithms deem their driving patterns 'suspicious' — rights group report warns AI surveillance systems will sweep in more innocent people than wrongdoers
articles.text:
Police reportedly pulling motorists over because AI algorithms deem their driving patterns 'suspicious' — rights group report warns AI surveillance systems will sweep in more innocent people than wrongdoers
Officers may look for a minor traffic violation to justify pulling the driver over
Police are increasingly using AI-derived pretext to justify pulling drivers over, claims a report by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) on October 26. According to Jay Stanley, a senior policy analyst with the ACLU Speech, Privacy, and Technology Project, police are using AI algorithms and automated license plate reader (ALPR) surveillance data to flag motorists whose travel histories appear “suspicious,” even without evidence of wrongdoing.
Condemning the approach and the use of mass surveillance in general, Stanley expressed concerns that this approach to law enforcement would lead to an uptick in the controversial “pretextual stops” and that “More and more people will be subject to police encounters as these AI algorithms inevitably sweep in far more innocent people than actual wrongdoers.” The report details several incidents, including one in which a woman claims an officer stopped her during a cross-country road trip because a surveillance system he was using had flagged her movements as suspicious. The system has accessed ALPR data on where she had been driving.
ALPRs installed along roads and highways photograph passing vehicles and record their registration numbers, locations, and timestamps. By combining sightings from different cameras, law enforcement can determine where a vehicle has traveled, which routes it used, and how frequently it visited particular locations. An AI system with access to the surveillance data can quickly analyze huge amounts of data and identify patterns it has been trained to deem as “suspicious,” triggering an alert to law enforcement. Stanley implies officers may receive the alert and look for a minor traffic violation to justify pulling the driver over. In some documented cases, officers have concealed the actual reason for the stop.
The report comes amid growing concerns about the impact of massive mass surveillance camera networks, such as privacy, abuse, and limited regulation. Several officers have been fired for abusing the Flock surveillance system. License plate readers have existed for years and have traditionally helped police track known suspects or locate a vehicle already associated with a crime, such as a stolen car. However, the current scale and blanket surveillance are unprecedented. Security researchers disclosed a network of over 335,000 Flock ALPR cameras across the United States.
Using AI, systems can also now analyze large collections of vehicle movements and generate new suspects based on behavioral patterns. Companies such as Flock Safety have been developing AI-enhanced surveillance systems that can identify “unusual” travel behavior and associations between vehicles, marketing them as effective crime-prevention tools.

articles.title: A 989g laptop with a built-in stylus promises exceptional endurance
articles.text:
This Japanese brand solves the 2-in-1 laptop dilemma with a 989g frame — offering 28.5 hours of battery life and a stylus charging inside the body
Dynabook’s V83/PA convertible laptop stores and charges its stylus
- Dynabook V83/PA packs a rechargeable stylus inside a convertible laptop weighing 989g
- The 13.3-inch touchscreen delivers WUXGA resolution in a lightweight convertible design
- Battery estimates reach 28.5 idle hours and 16 hours during video playback
Dynabook has introduced the V83/PA, a 989g convertible laptop which offers the portability of conventional notebooks.
The device incorporates a stylus that fits into a dedicated compartment within its chassis, allowing users to store and recharge it internally.
Its 13.3-inch LCD touchscreen offers 1920 × 1200 resolution, and its convertible design allows users to switch between regular business laptop and tablet use.
Lightweight construction with extensive connectivity
Measuring approximately 298.8 × 212 × 18.8mm, the laptop features rounded rear edges, a Dark Tech Blue finish and an enlarged touchpad.
The laptop includes two Thunderbolt 4 connections, with one installed on either side to accommodate peripherals without restricting cable placement.
Two additional USB 3.2 Gen 1 connections accompany HDMI, Gigabit Ethernet and a 3.2mm audio socket for attaching conventional computer accessories.
Its wireless connection uses Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4, while optional mobile broadband configurations provide access to either 4G or 5G networks.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The keyboard incorporates spill protection against approximately 30cc of liquid, but for protection, users have to shut down the computer after accidental spillage.
Dynabook has not published the battery capacity, but it estimates 28.5 hours idle and 16 hours of video playback.
Intel processors, AI capabilities, and enterprise security
Under the hood, these laptops offer different Intel chips, including the Core Ultra 7 365, Ultra 7 355, Ultra 5 335 and Ultra 5 325 chips.
The Dynabooks come with a memory capacity of 16GB or 32GB of RAM, accompanied by 512GB or 1TB of SSD storage and Windows 11 Pro.
The V83/PA includes a proprietary AI tool that translates and summarizes onscreen content when users circle the relevant information with a finger or stylus.
Processing takes place locally rather than through external servers, allowing the software to handle selected content without transmitting it for cloud analysis.
For video conferencing, the laptop also supports AI noise cancellation and Windows Studio Effects, which provide additional software capabilities for online meetings.
Its proprietary Empower Technology sustains processor performance during demanding workloads.
Dynabook offers the V83/PA with either a 5MP front sensor that supports facial recognition or a 0.92MP alternative, and the rear camera is rated at about 8MP.
Users can also unlock the device with a fingerprint reader, which sits alongside the face recognition option on the higher-resolution camera.
Business protections include Secured-Core PC conformity, NIST SP800-171 support, and a proprietary security manager that guards the BIOS.
The V83/PA starts at ¥1,057,320, roughly $6,740, and that figure covers only the base configuration, so the 32GB RAM and 1TB SSD version will likely cost considerably more.
Its 989g weight and battery endurance remain manufacturer estimates that no independent test has verified.
Many premium convertibles and ultralight laptops from other brands offer comparable processors and memory for less, although few of them store a charging stylus inside the body.
The V83/PA therefore depends on its low weight and built-in pen to justify a price that is hard to defend for specifications that are otherwise fairly typical.

articles.title: Tesla pauses Model 3 Premium orders after hitting import cap
articles.text:
Tesla could be switching back to U.S.-built Model 3 vehicles for the Canadian market after it hit a cap on Chinese imports.
For context, Tesla previously switched to shipping Shanghai-built Model 3 vehicles to Canada to avoid Canada’s counter-tariff response to U.S. President Donald Trump’s tariffs.
However, a notice on Tesla’s website says the company stopped taking Model 3 Premium orders because “high demand exhausted Tesla’s import quota.”
“Model 3 Premium orders paused after high demand exhausted Tesla’s import quota. Ordering resumes if Govt of Canada issues more quota, expected March 2027.”
Currently, the Canadian configurator for the Model 3 greys out the Premium model so it can’t be selected.
There’s some confusion around how the EV import caps work. The government has said the import cap works on a first-come, first-served basis, but Global Affairs Canada can also set aside “a portion of the available quota for the use of OEMs, including new entrants.”
Further, there was some speculation on social media and from DriveTeslaCanada that the company could switch back to offering the U.S.-built Model 3 Premium in Canada due to changes made to the Tesla Canada website.
According to screenshots from RJTesla, the EPA-estimated range was bumped to 584km, and the 0-100 km/h acceleration improved to 5.2 seconds. These numbers match the range of the U.S.-built Model 3 Premium.
However, when I checked the Model 3 Premium RWD’s specs page, the range changed back to 463 km, and the 0-100 km/h acceleration back to 6.2 seconds. It’s not entirely clear what’s going on with the changes. It seems like maybe Tesla pushed the update before it was ready, but it could also be a simple mistake.
