articles.title: Qué es el LZB, el sistema de seguridad que supuestamente ha fallado en el accidente de un AVE y un Iryo en Toledo
articles.text:
España ha vuelto a sufrir un grave accidente ferroviario. Un tren AVE que había salido de Atocha ha alcanzado un tren de Iryo parado en la vía de la línea andaluza de alta velocidad a la altura de Urda (Toledo). El accidente grave es el segundo que se produce este año en la línea Madrid-Andalucía. En enero, un tren de Renfe chocaba con uno de Iryo en Adamuz (Córdoba) como consecuencia de una rotura en la vía.
En esta ocasión, las primeras investigaciones apuntan a que el choque se ha producido después de una caída del sistema LZB en toda la línea. Las primeras informaciones apuntan a que la circulación se ha detenido por completo en la línea y en ese momento se ha aplicado el sistema de respaldo. Una vez activado el protocolo de emergencia, los trenes se han puesto en marcha.
Ha sido cuando se ha restablecido la circulación cuando el AVE ha alcanzado el tren de Iryo que estaba completamente detenido en la vía porque no había podido retomar la marcha.
El corredor andaluz es la línea de alta velocidad más antigua de nuestro país. Inaugurada en 1992 con la apertura Madrid-Sevilla, utiliza el sistema de seguridad LZB, que también se utiliza en las líneas C-5 de Cercanías en Madrid y toda la red del Euskotren.
Las siglas LZB hacen referencia a la palabra alemana Linienzugbeeinflussung, ya que el sistema también se emplea en Alemania y Austria.
El sistema consta de un cable que se extiende a lo largo de la vía, centrado pero dibujando un ligero zigzag que se cruza cada 100 metros. Este cableado envía la información de marcha del tren, la velocidad máxima de la vía y la distancia que queda antes de llegar a un nuevo cambio de límite de velocidad. Esa información es gestionada por un ordenador central que controla sectores de entre 30 y 40 kilómetros.
El cableado envía señales eléctricas en un circuito cerrado para ir recalculando las variables antes mencionadas a través de balizas. Cuando la vía queda obstaculizada, la transmisión se interrumpe y el sistema ordena automáticamente la detención del tren. Esto se produce con un protocolo que tiene en cuenta una primera advertencia sonora para el maquinista, un frenado del tren automático por parte del sistema de la vía y, en último lugar, un frenado de emergencia para detener el tren por completo.
Qué sabemos del accidente
A lo que se apunta con las primeras informaciones es que este sistema LZB se ha caído en la línea por lo que se ha dado la orden a todos los trenes de detenerse de inmediato. En ese caso, cuando el sistema LZB se detiene lo que sucede es que se activa un protocolo de respaldo. Si esto se produce, el maquinista tiene que prestar información al llamado ASFA Digital (Anuncio de Señales y Frenado Automático). Aquí, la velocidad se reduce automática y este sistema de respaldo es el que aplica un frenado de emergencia si el maquinista hace caso omiso de las señales.
Esas señales son físicas y no se encuentran en la cabina. Es decir, es el maquinista el que debe prestar atención a estas señales y parar o continuar la marcha en unas condiciones de velocidad muy concretas.
En esta ocasión, al caer toda la línea, las informaciones apuntan a que ésta ha estado dirigida desde el CRC (Centro de Regulación y Control), una suerte de "torre de control" de Adif. Desde aquí, utilizando pantallas que muestran los tramos abiertos y cerrados y la posición de cada tren, es desde donde se da la orden de detención o paso a los trenes. En el caso del corredor andaluz, este CRC está situado en Atocha (Madrid).
El CRC cuenta con pantallas que detallan un mapa de las líneas de tren. Esas líneas cuentan con cantones, tramos de varios kilómetros en los que dos trenes no se pueden encontrar en condiciones normales de circulación. Con el sistema activo, dos trenes no pueden encontrarse en un mismo tramo para evitar choques por alcance.
Estos cantones se ven en esa torre de control de Adif. Los trenes, con su posición sobre la vía, envían una señal eléctrica que es la que marca que el cantón está ocupado. De esta manera se puede comprobar, cuando las órdenes se dan desde el CRC, qué tramos y cuáles no están ocupados.
Las primeras informaciones apuntan a que, caída la línea, el CRC ha tomado el mando y ha ordenado que los trenes retomaran la circulación. El maquinista del AVE se habría encontrado con la señalización de paso cerrada (el sistema ASFA) pero desde esa "torre de control" de Adif se habría dado el visto bueno a que retomara la circulación sin ser conscientes de que el tren Iryo alcanzado todavía se encontraba parado en la vía.
Maquinistas han confirmado a Xataka que no es raro que el CRC dé al maquinista la orden de continuar su trayecto pese a que la señalización muestre un semáforo en rojo, siempre y cuando se haya producido una incidencia en la vía. En ese caso, el puesto de control es el que toma el mando porque tiene la fotografía global de todo el mapa de la línea.
En ese caso, el tren puede circular pero en unas condiciones que le permitan frenar con seguridad, siempre a una velocidad muy reducida. El límite máximo fijado para estos casos es de 40 km/h hasta que se supere la incidencia o el sistema LZB vuelva a estar disponible. Se considera que a esta velocidad, el maquinista puede detener el tren con seguridad. Sin embargo, todo indica que la velocidad a la que el tren de Renfe ha alcanzado al Iryo era muy superior.
Lo que no se sabe tampoco es por qué el CRC dio la orden de continuar y de hacer avanzar dos trenes en el mismo tramo o cantón, lo que puede haber provocado el accidente.

articles.title: Oracle brings Google’s TPUs to its cloud, adds ChatGPT integrations - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Oracle brings Google’s TPUs to its cloud, adds ChatGPT integrations
Oracle Corp. today announced plans to make Google LLC’s TPU artificial intelligence accelerators available through its public cloud.
The initiative marks the first time the search giant is supplying the chips to another hyperscaler. According to CNBC, Oracle will also add Cerebras Systems Inc.’s wafer-scale accelerators and OpenAI Group PBC’s Jalapeño inference processor. The latter chip is part of a broader partnership that also encompasses several newly revealed cloud services.
Optical network links
Google’s TPUs exchange data using two technologies called ICI and OCS. ICS transmits data via copper wires, while OCS employs optical links. Sending data over an optical link usually requires servers to turn light signals into electricity and then back into light. Google’s OCS technology skips that step, which lowers power usage. It employs tiny mechanical mirrors to steer light beams in the direction of the recipient servers.
The TPUs in Oracle’s data centers will use OCS and ICI technology to exchange data with one another. They will connect to the rest of the host data center using the database giant’s own Acceleron networking technology. Acceleron is powered by a custom SmartNIC, a chip optimized to perform network management and cybersecurity tasks.
“Acceleron’s SmartNIC with hardware-level tenant isolation, High Performance Fabric, and Zero Trust Packet Routing moves data between Oracle databases, storage, and TPU clusters with high throughput and low latency,” Oracle Senior Vice President Karan Batta and Google Cloud Senior Director Gurmeet Goindi wrote in a blog post.
Oracle will start deploying Google’s chips in its cloud next year. It plans to gradually add more TPU capacity from there. CNBC reported that Oracle also intends to deploy Cerebras’ AI chips, which are the size of a silicon wafer and contain trillions of transistors, as well as OpenAI’s Jalapeño inference accelerator. In August, the ChatGPT developer stated that the chip can run some open-source models 1.5 times faster than competing silicon.
Oracle’s partnership with OpenAI also extends to other areas. The companies today announced integrations that will enable customers to access the former company’s applications through ChatGPT. Additionally, Oracle will use OpenAI models to power a series of new cloud services.
Workflow automation
Oracle offers a portfolio of cloud applications that ease day-to-day business tasks such as managing customer records. The company is rolling out a service called AI Workspace that will integrate those services with ChatGPT. The integrations will enable the chatbot to perform tasks in Oracle applications on workers’ behalf. It can also loop in external applications when necessary.
“Consider a customer order put at risk by a supplier delay,” Oracle product marketing director Michelle Meng wrote in a blog post. “Solving it could require finding an alternative product, checking inventory, understanding customer requirements, validating transportation, assessing financial impact and updating the order. Workspace can maintain the goal throughout the process while coordinating the applications, agents, data and tools needed to address it.”
Companies automate some tasks using off-the-shelf chatbots and others with custom applications. A new Oracle tool called App Composer will ease the task of building and managing such applications. According to the company, it enables non-technical users to write custom software using AI assistants. App Composer scans that software for vulnerabilities and then deploys it on managed cloud infrastructure.
“Oracle manages deployment and operations, while IT controls access, approved data, policies, and costs,” explained Blair Bozada, a senior product marketing manager at Oracle.
App Composer is rolling out alongside a vulnerability remediation tool called AI Security Mesh. It uses OpenAI’s cybersecurity-optimized AI models to find weak points in customers’ applications. It prioritizes vulnerabilities by severity and suggests a fix for each one.
The new services are joined by a new “free-to-start” product suite called the Oracle AI SMB Bundle that is geared toward small businesses. It includes AI Workplace, App Composer, the NetApp QuickStart accounting platform, ChatGPT Business and Codex. Oracle says that customers will receive $12,000 in cloud credits per year.

articles.title: Researchers set a real-time fiber record: 3.2 petabits per second over 10.3 kilometers
articles.text:
So Much Internet P0rn: Demand for data processing is surging, and traditional communication standards are no longer up to the job. Thanks to a novel engineering approach, a Chinese team is developing fiber-optic technology that might solve the data speed problem for a while, and then some.
A joint initiative by Chinese researchers and engineers has set a new record for real-time fiber-optic communications. The team sent 3.2 petabits per second (Pbps) through a single optical fiber, topping the 2.5 Pbps mark the same group set earlier this year. The figure reflects bidirectional transmission, with traffic flowing in both directions at once.
One petabit equals 1,000 terabits, which means a 3.2 Pbps connection could download more than 20,000 4K movies in a single second. The researchers said the feat means one fiber-optic cable could, in theory, serve the gigabit broadband needs of 3.2 million households.
The record comes from researchers at CICT's National Key Laboratory of Optical Communication Technologies and Networks, Peng Cheng Laboratory and FiberHome Fujikura. They reached 3.2 Pbps using a 24-core optical fiber over a distance of 10.3 km.
The optical signal was engineered to use thousands of parallel channels across three wavelength bands. The team relied on optical modules it developed in-house, aiming for real-time transfers that could meet current commercial standards.
Lab tests have previously reached much higher speeds on similar 24-core fiber setups, but those efforts depended on experimental equipment and signal-processing devices.
The researchers said petabit-level data channels may be essential to keeping the AI industry moving forward. Single-mode optical fibers are nearing their capacity limit as new AI data centers drive ever more traffic back and forth.
Beyond AI and data centers, the technology could benefit other high-performance connectivity scenarios, including linking massive computing centers and powering backbone networks for 6G wireless services. The work was selected for the 2026 Optical Fiber Communication Conference, and the researchers have been invited to publish their results in a scientific journal.
Finally, CICT noted that the record arrives in the year that marks the 50th anniversary of China's "practical" optical fiber infrastructure. In 1976, the country's research focused on "glass filaments" just 0.2 millimeters wide. Today, China is setting world-level records as it pursues full self-reliance in the IT business.

articles.title: Meta has a new AI pet app called Waddle World | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Continuing its fast-paced experiments with AI apps, Meta has now launched a new app called Waddle World, which essentially looks like a Tamagotchi clone, but with AI. The might be a test, but it could very well be a precursor to the company’s Tamagotchi-like gadget powered by Muse.
The company has launched Waddle World in the Philippines on both iOS and Android. The app, spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra, lets you pick and grow a virtual pet, feed it, and play with it.
We have reached out to Meta for a comment on wider availability, and will update this piece if we hear back.
Meta’s description of the app indicates that it doesn’t want the app to be a habit builder. The company’s page also says that the app is not a chatbot, and is flagged as suitable for users older than 18.
“Waddle World is a cozy 16-bit world where your pixel pet lives. Hatch a virtual pet, visit whenever you like, and let it get to know you. No pressure, no streaks to protect, no scores to chase — just a warm little escape in the cracks of your day,” the app’s description reads.
“Not a chatbot. Not an assistant. Not a productivity tool. It’s a pet, and a place. Stay two minutes or twenty — it’ll be happy either way.”
The app also doubles as a journal, letting users describe their day through voice or text. The pet listens to the user and writes up the note in its own voice as an entry with a doodle. The app also features mini-games that you can play over a few minutes, and can send you a weekly email based on what it learned about you.
Meta may be wanting to stay away from building companion apps, given companies like Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits that allege their products caused harm to teenagers.
Until now, the social media giant has released AI-centric apps like Pocket, which lets you vibe-code games, and Vibes, which let you quickly generate videos.
Besides virtual pets, some companies have also tried making hardware AI pets.

articles.title: Apple refreshes the iMac, entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip
articles.text:
Apple has announced refreshes for the iMac and the entry-level, 14-inch MacBook Pro. Both machines are getting the M6 chip, which was introduced in the Mac mini several weeks ago.
The M6 is split into two variants for the iMac. Picking the “M6 chip with two Thunderbolt ports” option gets you a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, whereas picking “M6 chip with four Thunderbolt ports” gets you 12 cores for each, instead. The two-port variant maxes out at 24 GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, whereas the four-port one maxes out at 32GB of RAM and 2TB of storage.
There’s only one M6 chip option for the MacBook Pro—the one with the 12-core GPU and CPU. It caps out at 32GB of RAM but can go to 4TB of storage.
It’s a more substantial refresh for the iMac, as its previous update introduced the M4. Apple skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here. In terms of performance gains moving from the M4 to the M6, Apple said with the Mac mini that users can expect up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, up to double graphics performance, and nearly five times faster on-device AI. All that largely matches what we saw when we tested the M6 Mac mini last month, and users of the new iMac should expect similar numbers.

articles.title: XPG Launches Third-Generation Core Reactor III Gold Fully Modular Power Supply
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
XPG Launches Third-Generation Core Reactor III Gold Fully Modular Power Supply
XPG, the gaming brand of ADATA Technology, today announced the launch of the new CORE REACTOR III Gold Fully Modular Power Supply. Building on the strong market reputation of the best-selling CORE REACTOR series, the third-generation model is designed to address the growing power demands of high-performance computing, AI applications, and next-generation gaming platforms. Following the technology showcase at COMPUTEX earlier this year, CORE REACTOR III becomes the first commercially available XPG power supply to feature XTREME Power Guard technology, combining 24/7 current monitoring, real-time abnormality alerts, and active power shutoff protection. It also supports ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1, up to 235% power excursion, and 80 Plus Gold certification, providing enhanced power safety and stability for next-generation high-performance systems.
Growing High-Performance Computing Demands Drive Power Requirements: CORE REACTOR III Evolves for Next-Generation Platforms
From AAA gaming and 4K content creation to generative AI, 3D rendering, and GPU-accelerated computing, today's high-end PCs place greater and more dynamic power demands on graphics cards and processors. For gamers and creators, a power supply must provide sufficient wattage while also handling transient loads, maintaining stability during extended operation, and protecting high-value components. As one of XPG's best-selling power supply product lines, CORE REACTOR now enters its third generation with enhanced GPU power protection while preserving the stability and performance the series is known for. CORE REACTOR III is available in 750 W, 850 W, and 1000 W models for a wide range of high-performance system configurations.XTREME Power Guard Proactively Detects Potential Risks: Enhancing Power Reliability Under High-Load Operation
CORE REACTOR III features XTREME Power Guard technology, which continuously monitors current through the 12V-2x6 connector. When current imbalance is detected, the Power Guard LED flashes orange as an alert. If an overcurrent condition is detected, meaning the current exceeds the safe operating range, the LED flashes red and the system can automatically shut off power through the 12V-2x6 connector, helping reduce the risk of connector overheating, melting, or burning. A highly visible colored connector also helps users verify that the power cable is fully and securely inserted. Together, these features elevate power protection from conventional passive safeguards to a system that can actively monitor, alert, and intervene when abnormal conditions occur.
Full ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 Support: Built for the Power Demands of Future High-Performance Systems
CORE REACTOR III supports Intel ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 standards and includes a 12V-2x6 connector capable of delivering up to 600 W. It can also withstand power excursions of up to 235% of its rated output for 100 microseconds, improving its ability to handle sudden load changes from high-performance hardware. The entire series is 80 Plus Gold certified and incorporates main Japanese 105°C-rated capacitors and a 135 mm FDB (Fluid Dynamic Bearing) fan. Combined with a fully modular cable design, eight industrial-grade protection mechanisms, and a 10-year limited warranty, CORE REACTOR III delivers a balanced combination of performance, durability, and protection for high-end gaming, content creation, and computing platforms.

Les MacBook ont perdu leur logo Apple lumineux en 2015, avec le MacBook 12 pouces. La pomme n’avait pas de LED à elle. Elle était découpée dans la coque et laissait passer la lumière du rétroéclairage, c’est-à-dire les lampes qui éclairent l’écran LCD par l’arrière.

Apple n’a jamais expliqué pourquoi elle l’a retirée. Pourtant, ce MacBook avait un écran Retina de 0,88 millimètre d’épaisseur, et avec un écran aussi fin, la lumière qui traverse la pomme aurait pu faire une zone plus claire au milieu de l’image. Le MacBook Pro a suivi en 2016, puis le MacBook Air en 2018. Depuis, la pomme est en métal poli et elle reflète la lumière sans en produire.
Une pomme qui éclaire un MacBook dans le teaser de John Ternus
John Ternus est CEO d’Apple depuis le 1er septembre 2026. Ce mercredi 28 octobre, il a publié une courte vidéo sur X. On y voit un projecteur en forme de pomme qui éclaire un mur rectangulaire, jusqu’à lui donner la forme d’un MacBook. La vidéo arrive quelques heures avant la présentation d’un MacBook Pro redessiné, attendu avec un écran OLED tactile.
Apple a réuni la presse à Los Angeles pour l’occasion. Pour le site américain 9to5Mac, ce teaser pourrait annoncer le retour du logo lumineux. Surtout, la vidéo de John Ternus avant l’iPhone 18 Pro laissait déjà deviner une vraie nouveauté, l’ouverture variable de l’appareil photo, c’est-à-dire un objectif qui règle lui-même la quantité de lumière qui entre.
Par contre, l’ancienne méthode ne marcherait plus. Un écran OLED n’a pas de rétroéclairage, puisque chaque pixel produit sa propre lumière. Apple devrait donc ajouter un éclairage à part derrière la pomme. Le nouveau MacBook Pro sera présenté ce mercredi à 18 heures, heure de Paris.

articles.title: Énergies fossiles et El Niño « hors norme » : le cocktail climatique que redoute l'OMM pour 2026
articles.text:
La Nasa a prévenu, nous nous dirigeons vraisemblablement vers un épisode d’El Niño « historique » dans l’océan Pacifique. Le phénomène est officiellement de retour depuis l’été, et selon l’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM), El Niño va se maintenir jusqu’en février 2027. Cet épisode s’annonce particulièrement intense. Une étude publiée cet été concluait même qu’El Niño est plus puissant qu’à aucun moment depuis 1 000 ans.
Une « nouvelle flambée » des gaz à effet de serre à craindre à cause d’El Niño
Ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, l’OMM a de nouveau attiré l’attention sur l’impact potentiel de ce phénomène, en lien avec un autre triste record planétaire. « Les concentrations de gaz à effet de serre ont atteint de nouveaux records, scellant ainsi une hausse des températures à long terme. L’intensification du phénomène El Niño pourrait entraîner une nouvelle flambée de ces concentrations », résume l’organisme des Nations unies sur X.
El Niño est un phénomène climatique naturel. Il se manifeste par des anomalies de températures de surface dans l’océan Pacifique équatorial. Ces températures plus chaudes que la normale peuvent entraîner une cascade d’effets sur la planète. Avec le réchauffement planétaire, ces effets peuvent être encore plus dommageables.
Dioxyde de carbone : 53 % de plus qu’en 1750, un niveau sans précédent
Le dioxyde de carbone est le principal gaz à effet de serre lié aux activités humaines, suivi du méthane en deuxième, et de l’oxyde nitreux en troisième (qu’on appelle aussi protoxyde d’azote).
L’OMM vient de présenter un nouveau rapport portant sur les concentrations de gaz à effet de serre dans l’atmosphère. Ce texte « montre que les concentrations de surface moyennes mondiales de dioxyde de carbone (CO2), de méthane (CH4) et d’oxyde nitreux (N2O) ont atteint des niveaux sans précédent en 2025 ».
En 2025, la concentration moyenne de CO2 a atteint 426,8 ppm (parties par million), contre 377,5 ppm en 2004, année du premier bulletin. Celle du méthane a atteint 1 948 ppb (parties par milliard), et celle du N2O 339,1 ppb. Par rapport aux niveaux préindustriels de 1750, cela représente une hausse de 53 % pour le CO2, de 167 % pour le CH4 et de 26 % pour le N2O.
Ko Barrett, secrétaire générale adjointe de l’OMM, a commenté ces conclusions dans le communiqué de l’organisation : « Une nouvelle année, un nouveau record. Les gaz à effet de serre retiennent une quantité de chaleur sans précédent dans l’atmosphère, ce qui alimente l’intensification des phénomènes météorologiques extrêmes et les risques qui en découlent pour nos économies et nos sociétés. »
Ce bulletin arrive à deux semaines de la COP31, qui se tiendra à Antalya, en Turquie, du 9 au 20 novembre. L’OMM le publie chaque année pour fournir des données scientifiques aux négociateurs de la conférence des Nations unies sur le climat, qui doit cette fois traduire les engagements pris en actions concrètes.
Les puits de carbone terrestres face à El Niño
Le renforcement d’El Niño attendu pour la fin 2026 et le début 2027 inquiète l’OMM, qui craint qu’il fasse encore grimper la concentration de CO2 dans l’atmosphère. « Nous pouvons nous attendre à une nouvelle hausse des concentrations en 2026, en raison de l’utilisation de combustibles fossiles et du développement d’un épisode El Niño de forte intensité, qui aura un impact sur les puits de carbone terrestres, comme cela a été le cas en 2023/2024 », selon Oksana Tarasova, responsable scientifique chargée de coordonner la recherche et la surveillance mondiale des gaz à effet de serre à l’OMM, citée dans le communiqué.
Comme le résume Reuters, El Niño devrait favoriser un temps plus sec, ce qui compliquera l’absorption des émissions par les puits de carbone. Ces puits, à savoir les écosystèmes terrestres (forêts, sols, végétation) et les océans, absorbent environ la moitié du CO2 émis chaque année selon l’OMM, le reste s’accumulant dans l’atmosphère.
Les alertes de l’OMM au sujet d’El Niño se multiplient ces derniers temps. Quelques jours plus tôt, le 21 octobre, Celeste Saulo, secrétaire générale de l’OMM, aux côtés de Tom Fletcher, secrétaire général adjoint de l’ONU aux affaires humanitaires et coordonnateur des secours d’urgence, a prévenu que l’épisode en cours pourrait atteindre une intensité sans précédent, « au point de sortir littéralement hors du cadre des graphiques de contrôle que nous utilisons depuis 40 ans ». Tous deux ont encouragé à prendre des mesures préventives, pour protéger les personnes les plus vulnérables face aux pires conséquences du phénomène (sécheresse, inondations, faim).
Et en France, quel sera l’impact d’El Niño ?
En France, le phénomène El Niño ne devrait pas avoir un impact direct sur la météo. Le phénomène réchauffe la planète entière, avec des réactions en chaîne fortes dans les territoires des tropiques. Il n’est cependant pas responsable de tous les événements qui pourraient advenir ces prochains mois en France métropolitaine. Mais, indirectement, il augmente le risque de vagues de chaleur et de douceur anormale chez nous.
Le lien entre le changement climatique et l’intensité d’El Niño reste débattu. Ce que l’on sait, c’est qu’El Niño peut amplifier les effets du changement climatique. D’où les appels de plus en plus fréquents de l’OMM à se préparer à cet épisode d’El Niño hors norme.
Toutes vos questions sur El Niño, Numerama va les poser à un expert : voici comment participer !
El Niño est un phénomène aux conséquences complexes, dont nous allons de plus en plus entendre parler ces prochaines semaines, à mesure que l’on approchera de son pic d’intensité. Pour debunker le vrai du faux, Numerama reçoit bientôt Éric Guilyardi, océanographe et climatologue au CNRS. Il est spécialiste d’El Niño, et vous allez pouvoir lui poser toutes vos questions dans une grande FAQ que nous diffuserons sur notre chaîne YouTube.

articles.title: Des pirates ont trouvé comment voler vos données bancaires au moment de payer en ligne
articles.text:
Au moment de valider leur commande, les clients de dizaines de marques de mode brésiliennes ont livré leur numéro de carte et leur cryptogramme à des pirates. Pour piéger toutes ces caisses d'un coup, les attaquants ont modifié le script de statistiques que chacune chargeait.
Ces marques confient leur boutique en ligne et leur page de paiement à la plateforme brésilienne Convertr. L'entreprise annonce plus de 2 milliards de reais de ventes réalisées par ses marchands, soit environ 320 millions d'euros. Convertr intègre à chacune de ses boutiques un petit programme de mesure d'audience, hébergé sur un serveur Plausible qu'elle administre. Plausible est une alternative open source à Google Analytics. Les pirates ont glissé un code malveillant dans ce programme, et récupéraient à chaque commande les informations de carte saisies dans le formulaire, avec le CPF du client. Les banques brésiliennes identifient leurs clients grâce à ce numéro fiscal. L'entreprise néerlandaise de sécurité Sansec a repéré le code malveillant le 24 octobre, et Convertr ne l'a retiré qu'hier. Les victimes sont brésiliennes, mais n'importe quel commerçant qui ajoute un script extérieur à sa page de paiement court ce risque.
Le serveur de statistiques de Convertr, jamais mis à jour depuis 2025
Convertr a installé en 2025 la version auto-hébergée de Plausible, sans jamais la mettre à jour par la suite. Les versions 3.0.0 à 3.2.0 de ce logiciel contiennent une faille critique référencée CVE-2026-8467. Avec cette faille, n'importe qui peut exécuter des commandes sur le serveur sans se connecter, en passant par une bibliothèque de composants que Plausible laissait ouverte à l'adresse /storybook. L'éditeur a corrigé le problème en mai, et Sansec soupçonne les pirates d'être entrés par cette brèche, sans pouvoir le confirmer faute d'accès aux journaux du serveur de Convertr.
Plausible sert ce script directement depuis un fichier stocké sur le serveur. En modifiant ce seul fichier, un attaquant infecte tous les sites qui l'intègrent, explique Sansec. Chaque page de paiement de Convertr chargeait donc le skimmer. Les pirates l'ont retouché deux jours après l'avoir posé, pour lire exactement les champs de l'interface de paiement de la plateforme.
Sansec suit ce groupe brésilien depuis juillet 2024. Ses membres avaient jusqu'ici infecté des dizaines de boutiques en ligne, presque toutes au Brésil, en les piratant une par une, et certaines ont été infectées pendant près de deux ans. « Convertr est la première attaque de la chaîne d'approvisionnement que nous voyons de leur part », relève l'équipe d'investigation de Sansec.
En France, des numéros volés freinés par le 3-D Secure
Ce groupe attaque aussi directement des boutiques WooCommerce, et 47,4 % des boutiques en ligne françaises fonctionnent sous ce logiciel, d'après une étude de mars 2026 que nous citions à propos d'un skimmer glissé par une extension WooCommerce. Pour payer en Europe avec un numéro de carte française volé, un fraudeur doit toutefois, en général, passer le 3-D Secure et sa validation dans l'application bancaire du titulaire. Les principales banques françaises rejettent même, depuis janvier, les paiements sans 3-D Secure dès qu'ils dépassent un centime en 24 heures chez un même commerçant, quand celui-ci encaisse par un prestataire européen, selon le rapport 2025 de l'Observatoire de la sécurité des moyens de paiement.
D'après l'Observatoire, les fraudeurs utilisent d'ailleurs surtout les cartes copiées sur des terminaux piégés pour payer sur des sites marchands hors d'Europe qui n'exigent pas d'authentification forte. Sur ces paiements internationaux hors Espace économique européen, le taux de fraude est de 0,376 %, contre 0,026 % sur les opérations nationales.
Si vous avez payé une commande sur une boutique brésilienne depuis le 24 octobre, avec « checkout.convertr » dans l'adresse de la page de paiement, Sansec vous conseille de faire bloquer et remplacer votre carte. Le script infecté est conservé jusqu'à 24 heures dans le cache des navigateurs, et un client de Convertr peut donc encore tomber sur le skimmer une journée après le nettoyage. Pour vos achats ailleurs, avec une carte virtuelle à usage unique, vous gardez votre vrai numéro hors de portée d'un site piégé. Nous vous la suggérions contre des skimmers cachés dans Google Tag Manager. Et si un fraudeur réussit malgré tout un paiement sans authentification forte, votre banque doit vous rembourser sans délai, y compris en cas de négligence grave de votre part, rappelle l'Observatoire.
Sansec invite les commerçants qui hébergent Plausible sur leurs serveurs à installer la version 3.2.1 et à chercher dans leurs journaux des requêtes vers /storybook. Convertr indique de son côté prévenir les marchands touchés et les autorités, sans avoir publié le nombre de cartes saisies sur ses caisses pendant ces trois jours.

articles.title: How to get corporate gifting right across multiple cities
articles.text:
How to get corporate gifting right across multiple cities
From managing recipient lists and budgets to coordinating packaging and deliveries, here's how businesses can make large-scale festive gifting more organized and efficient.
Sending Diwali gifts to a handful of employees or clients is relatively simple. Sending hundreds of gifts to recipients spread across different cities is another matter. Addresses need to be verified, budgets finalized, packaging standardized and deliveries timed to arrive before the festival. A missed shipment, incorrect address or last-minute change can quickly complicate the exercise.
For businesses managing large-scale Diwali gifting, the key is to plan early, coordinate the details and ensure that every recipient has a consistent experience, regardless of location.
Start with a detailed recipient list
The first step is to organize all recipient information in one place. This should include names, delivery addresses, contact numbers, and any other information required to complete the delivery. For employee gifting, it may also be useful to group recipients according to city or office location. Client and partner lists can be organized separately so that different gifting requirements are easier to manage. Checking the information before placing the order is important. Incorrect or incomplete addresses can create delivery problems, particularly when gifts are being sent to several cities.
Personalize where it matters
Large-scale gifting does not have to feel completely impersonal. Businesses can add small details that make gifts feel more thoughtful. A personalized greeting card, recipient name or company message can add a sense of occasion without making the process significantly more complicated. For key clients or long-term partners, businesses may choose a more customized gift, based on the relationship. The goal is to find the right level of personalization for each recipient group while keeping the overall process manageable.
Use bulk ordering to simplify the process
When a business is managing a large number of recipients, placing individual orders can quickly become time-consuming. Bulk ordering can make the process more organized, particularly when the same or similar gifts are being sent to multiple locations. A single gifting plan can cover product selection, quantities, packaging, and delivery requirements. This also makes it easier for the internal team to monitor the overall budget and track the progress of the campaign. Businesses planning corporate Diwali gifts can also establish recipient categories in advance, making it easier to decide which gift goes to which group.
Keep packaging consistent
Packaging plays an important role in professional Diwali gifting. When gifts are being sent to different cities, consistent packaging can create a unified brand experience. The same box style, colour scheme, greeting card or branding element can be used across the entire order. This helps ensure that recipients receive gifts that feel like part of the same Diwali campaign, even if they are in different locations. Packaging should also be practical enough to protect the contents during transportation. Fragile products or items sensitive to heat may need additional consideration.
Set a clear budget
Diwali gifting costs can increase quickly when the recipient list is large. Setting a budget before selecting products helps businesses narrow down suitable options. The budget can be divided by recipient category. For example, employee gifts may have one price range, while client or business-partner gifts may have another. It is also useful to account for packaging, delivery, and personalization costs rather than looking only at the product price.
Track every shipment
Once the Diwali gifts are ordered, tracking becomes one of the most important parts of the process. A simple tracking sheet can include the recipient, city, order status, and delivery status. This allows the business team to quickly identify delayed or unsuccessful deliveries and take action where required. For larger gifting programmes, having one person or team responsible for monitoring the campaign can make communication much easier. It also prevents different departments from working with separate or outdated recipient lists.
Decide what the gift should include
The next step is deciding what will go into the Diwali gift. Businesses have several options, from traditional sweets and dry fruits to chocolates, snacks, candles and curated hampers. The choice can depend on the recipient group. Employee gifts may follow one format, while important client or partner gifts may have a different product mix. A consistent selection across cities can make large-scale gifting easier to coordinate. At the same time, businesses can create different categories of gifts based on the relationship with each recipient. This balance can help maintain consistency without making every gift identical.
Plan for different delivery locations
Sending gifts across multiple cities requires attention to delivery coverage and timelines. Businesses should confirm whether the selected gifting provider can deliver to all the required locations and understand how long each delivery may take. This becomes especially important during Diwali because demand for gifting and delivery services can increase significantly around the festival. Businesses can group orders by city and create a delivery schedule before placing them. This makes it easier to track which gifts have been dispatched, which are in transit, and which have already reached the recipients.
Start planning before the festive rush
One of the easiest ways to make multi-city Diwali gifting smoother is to start early. Early planning gives businesses more time to finalize recipient details, compare gifting options, approve designs, and schedule deliveries. It also leaves room to handle unexpected issues, such as an incorrect address or a product becoming unavailable. Waiting until the last few days can limit the available options and put additional pressure on both the business team and the delivery network.
Making multi-city Diwali gifting easier
Diwali gifting across several cities requires more planning than a small personal gifting exercise, but the process becomes manageable when it is treated as a structured campaign. A clear recipient database, suitable gifts, consistent packaging, planned delivery schedules, and proper tracking can help businesses coordinate gifting across locations. The aim is not simply to send gifts to as many people as possible. It is to create a consistent and thoughtful festive experience, even when recipients are spread across different cities.

articles.title: Un millonario pasó 34 años excavando túneles bajo Liverpool sin explicar por qué. Dos siglos después, la respuesta lo convierte en un genio
articles.text:
Durante décadas, un millonario británico dedicó buena parte de su fortuna a contratar trabajadores para excavar un gigantesco laberinto bajo las calles de Liverpool. Nadie sabía qué pretendía conseguir. Los túneles no conducían a ningún lugar concreto, algunos alcanzaban profundidades sorprendentes y su propietario jamás dejó planos ni explicaciones. Tras su muerte, la construcción quedó enterrada bajo toneladas de escombros y el misterio sobrevivió durante casi dos siglos. Ahora, después de 30 años de investigaciones, alguien ha encontrado una respuesta mucho más humana de lo que nadie imaginaba.
El millonario que decidió agujerear Liverpool. Joseph Williamson nació en Yorkshire en 1769 y llegó a Liverpool con apenas 11 años para trabajar en el negocio tabaquero de Richard Tate, cuya hija Elizabeth acabaría convirtiéndose en su esposa. En 1803 asumió el control de la empresa y acumuló una considerable fortuna gracias al comercio y otras inversiones. Tres años después compró terrenos en Edge Hill, entonces una zona poco urbanizada situada a varios kilómetros del centro de Liverpool, con la intención inicial de construir viviendas.
Lo extraordinario llegó después: durante 34 años, hasta su muerte en 1840, mantuvo a numerosos hombres excavando la roca arenisca del subsuelo y levantando túneles, cámaras y estructuras abovedadas. El proyecto fue creciendo hasta convertirse en una construcción cuya verdadera finalidad Williamson nunca explicó públicamente.
Una ciudad subterránea que nadie sabía que existía. Bajo Edge Hill apareció un entramado de pasadizos estrechos, escaleras, sótanos y enormes cámaras distribuidas en varios niveles. Algunas estimaciones sugieren que la red podría extenderse por una superficie de alrededor de 2,6 kilómetros cuadrados, aunque sus límites reales siguen sin conocerse. Entre las estructuras más espectaculares destaca el llamado Banqueting Hall, una sala abovedada de unos 20 metros de longitud y más de ocho metros de altura, cuyo suelo visible descansa sobre una acumulación de escombros que podría alcanzar seis metros de profundidad.
Los investigadores han identificado sectores con dos y tres niveles superpuestos y galerías que descienden al menos 18 metros, mientras que algunos voluntarios sostienen que determinadas estructuras podrían alcanzar los 27 metros. La magnitud de la obra resulta especialmente desconcertante porque fue construida manualmente durante la primera mitad del siglo XIX.
El secreto que Williamson se llevó a la tumba. El comerciante tenía fama de excéntrico y protagonizó numerosas historias cuya autenticidad resulta difícil de comprobar. Se decía que acudió a una reunión con el rey Jorge IV vestido con ropa remendada y botas de trabajo, que organizaba banquetes para poner a prueba la lealtad de sus invitados y que incluso gastó bromas a los obreros que construían el ferrocarril entre Liverpool y Londres. Una de las anécdotas cuenta que ordenó a sus trabajadores esconderse en un túnel para asustar a los ferroviarios cuando atravesaran accidentalmente una de sus galerías.
Su comportamiento alimentó las especulaciones sobre las excavaciones, realizadas sin planos conocidos, registros detallados ni explicaciones públicas. Tras su fallecimiento, las cámaras comenzaron a utilizarse como vertederos improvisados y terminaron selladas bajo los residuos de viviendas, fábricas y comercios. Con el paso de las décadas, buena parte de aquella construcción desapareció de la memoria de la ciudad.
De los contrabandistas al fin del mundo. La ausencia de explicaciones dio lugar a teorías de todo tipo. Algunos investigadores sugirieron que los túneles servían para transportar mercancías de contrabando, mientras que otros imaginaron que Williamson había construido un refugio para sobrevivir a un supuesto apocalipsis. Esta última hipótesis sostenía que Elizabeth, su esposa, había recibido la influencia de un predicador convencido de la proximidad del fin del mundo y persuadido a su marido para preparar habitaciones subterráneas.
También surgieron explicaciones relacionadas con la construcción de viviendas: las galerías y sus grandes arcos de ladrillo podrían haber permitido recuperar antiguas canteras de arenisca y levantar edificios sobre terrenos previamente excavados. Por cierto, esta interpretación encuentra cierto respaldo en las características arquitectónicas del complejo, aunque tampoco explica por completo la extraordinaria duración y profundidad de las obras.
El redescubrimiento de un laberinto olvidado. El interés por los túneles resurgió gracias a los artículos publicados por el historiador Charles Hand durante la década de 1920, que impulsaron investigaciones oficiales en 1926. En 1989 se fundó la Joseph Williamson Society y, una década después, los trabajos realizados junto a una promoción de viviendas para estudiantes permitieron localizar en 1999 una entrada a un antiguo sistema de sótanos. Desde entonces, grupos de voluntarios han dedicado miles de horas a retirar los residuos acumulados durante generaciones y recuperar las estructuras originales.
Los trabajos han permitido extraer más de 120 contenedores de escombros y recuperar objetos tan variados como tinteros escolares, botellas de cerveza y veneno, pipas de arcilla, cerámicas hospitalarias, huesos de animales y juguetes. Actualmente, Friends of Williamson Tunnels y Williamson Tunnels Heritage Centre investigan y muestran al público distintas secciones del complejo, mientras continúan las excavaciones para descubrir nuevas galerías.
La explicación que cambia por completo la historia. Después de tres décadas estudiando las estructuras, los responsables de ambas organizaciones consideran que la hipótesis más convincente no es otra que la filantropía. A comienzos del siglo XIX, Liverpool era una próspera ciudad portuaria cuya riqueza se concentraba principalmente entre los comerciantes, mientras miles de trabajadores sobrevivían gracias a empleos precarios. La mecanización industrial había desplazado a numerosos artesanos y el final de las guerras napoleónicas en 1815 provocó el regreso de soldados que necesitaban encontrar trabajo.
Williamson habría utilizado su fortuna para contratar a hombres sin recursos, proporcionarles ingresos y enseñarles oficios relacionados con la construcción. La profundidad alcanzada por algunas excavaciones resulta fundamental para esta interpretación: los voluntarios han encontrado trabajos cuya utilidad económica parece difícil de justificar, incluidos agujeros que aparentemente fueron excavados para volver a rellenarse. La posibilidad que plantean los investigadores es que el verdadero propósito de aquellas obras fuera mantener a cientos de hombres empleados durante el mayor tiempo posible.
Una obra interminable para que nadie se quedara sin trabajo. Los investigadores también han encontrado indicios sociales que respaldan esa interpretación. Según los voluntarios, los registros bautismales de una iglesia cercana muestran que varias familias pusieron a sus hijos el nombre de Joseph Williamson, un posible reflejo del agradecimiento hacia el comerciante. La hipótesis sigue sin estar demostrada documentalmente y algunas estructuras pudieron tener funciones prácticas relacionadas con la urbanización de Edge Hill.
Aun así, la escala de las excavaciones y la aparente inutilidad de determinados trabajos sugieren que Williamson pudo haber convertido una obra sin final definido en una forma de asistencia social basada en el empleo.
Así, casi dos siglos después de su muerte, los voluntarios siguen excavando aquel laberinto y descubriendo nuevas partes de una construcción que todavía conserva numerosos secretos. Y si la interpretación filantrópica es correcta como parece, el genio de Williamson consiguió que sus túneles siguieran dando trabajo a generaciones de personas mucho después de su muerte.

articles.title: SFR augmente encore ses tarifs : vous risquez de payer jusqu’à 5 € de plus par mois
articles.text:
Nous vous en parlions début octobre, SFR, RED et Prixtel ont décidé d’augmenter certains de leurs forfaits. Peu de temps après, des abonnés de SFR ont bel et bien rapporté une augmentation de prix de 1,49 € à presque 5 €, en fonction de l’abonnement en cours. Le plus dur serait passé pour les clients de SFR ? Il semble que non. Selon AlloForfait, l’opérateur annonce à certains de ses clients, chez SFR, RED by SFR ou Prixtel, de nouvelles augmentations de prix.
De nouvelles augmentations de prix pour les abonnés SFR
Une nouvelle fois, les hausses peuvent aller de 1 euro à 5 euros par mois. Les forfaits mobiles et Internet sont concernés. Par conséquent, la peine peut être double. Une famille peut voir son abonnement Internet augmenter, tout comme ses forfaits mobiles. Un utilisateur du réseau social X fait par exemple état d’une augmentation de 15 euros « en 2 mois pour une box et 3 mobiles ».
Les hausses atteindraient 4,99 euros par mois pour la box et 3,99 euros par mois pour certains forfaits mobiles. Ces augmentations, cumulées au sein d’une famille, peuvent donc sensiblement alourdir la facture globale d’un foyer. Si l’on considère une augmentation totale de 20 euros par mois pour un forfait fixe et trois forfaits mobiles, la facture annuelle d’un foyer augmente donc de 240 €. À l’heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, nous ne pouvons pas dire combien d’abonnés SFR sont concernés, ni lister les offres touchées par ces augmentations de prix.
Comme le souligne BFMTV, SFR pourrait vouloir augmenter ses tarifs avant son rachat, les régulateurs étant susceptibles de limiter les hausses de prix une fois l’opération finalisée.
Il est possible de résilier son abonnement SFR sans frais
Si vous ne consentez pas à une hausse de prix, il est possible de résilier son abonnement en cours sans frais et sans pénalité, grâce à l’article L.224-33 du Code de la consommation. Comme l’opérateur l’explique lui-même : « vous avez la possibilité de résilier votre contrat sans frais et sans pénalité si vous n’acceptez pas ces nouvelles conditions contractuelles. Cette résiliation peut être effectuée dans un délai de 4 mois à compter du présent courriel ». Les personnes concernées disposent donc de 4 mois à partir de la réception du courrier les informant d’une hausse de prix.
SFR précise par ailleurs qu’il existe trois façons de résilier un abonnement concerné par une hausse de prix : par courrier (en indiquant que vous refusez cette modification contractuelle), depuis votre espace client en ligne (en indiquant le motif suivant : « Refus des modifications contractuelles/Motifs légitimes ») et, enfin, en cas de changement d’opérateur avec portabilité du numéro.

articles.title: DoorDash reportedly in talks to acquire Instacart in $17 billion deal
articles.text:
In brief: DoorDash is reportedly in late-stage talks with Instacart to acquire the popular grocery delivery service as part of a deal valued at roughly $17 billion. An announcement could come as early as mid-week, sources said, who also warned that nothing has been finalized and the deal could still fall through.
Instacart was also recently tied to acquisition rumors with Uber, but sources say those talks are no longer active. It is unclear if Uber would try again if DoorDash comes up short.
Shares in DoorDash are up 2.61 percent on the news as of this writing, while Instacart's stock is down about the same percent. For reference, DoorDash has a market cap around $74.7 billion and Instacart is worth roughly $14 billion.
The potential buyout comes at a pivotal time for food delivery platforms. Gone are the boom days of pandemic ordering, and those that have survived this long now have to compete with rising labor costs, stricter regulations as it relates to employees / delivery drivers, and competition from heavyweight players like Amazon and Walmart.
As Reuters highlights, the deal would give Instacart access to DoorDash's vast delivery network and customer base. The outfit would also benefit from existing retail partnerships.
To be clear, the two platforms currently operate in similar but different categories. DoorDash specializes in restaurant/ fast food and convenience store delivery, while Instacart has traditionally focused on grocery delivery. Consolidation in the space could also be a win for consumers, as merging the services could result in one less monthly or annual subscription fee for those currently signed up to both services.
History has shown that consumers are willing to pay to automate and simplify certain aspects of their lives, and getting food delivered to your front door from the grocery store or from your favorite restaurant certainly qualifies. I have relied on grocery delivery service for a few years now, and not once have I missed the crowded aisles and long checkout lines at my local store.

articles.title: Airbnb Cuts Recommendation Staleness from 2 Days to Seconds with Chronon
articles.text:
Airbnb has extended its open source Chronon feature platform with Push Mode and Near Real Time (NRT) Model Transform to update sequence based recommendation embeddings within seconds of guest activity. The change reduced embedding staleness from nearly two days to less than a minute, with typical updates arriving within 10 to 30 seconds. Airbnb also reported a 1.67% improvement in offline NDCG and an approximately 0.33% increase in uncancelled bookings in online A/B testing.
The work builds on Airbnb’s JourneyFormer based sequence recommender, which uses a Transformer encoder to represent a guest’s booking, review and browsing history. Previously, the encoder ran as a daily batch job, generating embeddings that were stored in a low latency store. During a search, the ranking system retrieved the latest embedding and combined it with the live query, keeping the Transformer outside the latency sensitive serving path. However, activity occurring after the daily batch could remain absent from the embedding until the following run, with processing delays bringing effective staleness close to two days.
Airbnb’s initial architecture showing the daily batch sequence encoder, embedding store and online ranking path. (Source : Airbnb Blog Post)
Airbnb addressed the freshness problem by adding two capabilities to Chronon. Push Mode causes a streaming job to publish a notification when a feature value is committed, allowing downstream processing to react to updated guest activity rather than polling or waiting for a scheduled job. NRT Model Transform allows an already deployed model to run inside that streaming pipeline. Airbnb uses the same Transformer sequence encoder for the near real time path, avoiding a separate inference implementation for the streaming workflow.
The resulting pipeline captures events such as searches and listing views, combines them with the guest’s existing short and long-term sequence data, and triggers model inference when the updated feature state is available. The generated embedding is then written to the same low-latency store used by the batch system. Consequently, the online ranking path remains largely unchanged while the representation it retrieves becomes more current.
Pengyu Hou, Senior Software Engineer, Infrastructure at Airbnb, described the platform change as addressing the gap between event-driven data and model inference:
NRT Model Transform lets Chronon call an already deployed model ... directly from within the streaming flow.
The approach follows a broader feature serving pattern in which predictions can be updated when underlying features change rather than computed on every user request. Feast, another open-source feature platform, documents cached prediction architectures where inference is triggered by feature updates, trading additional writes and pipeline complexity for lower serving latency. Chronon instead integrates streaming computation and model transformation into its feature platform and emphasizes consistency between offline and online computation.
Airbnb’s near real-time Chronon architecture (Source: Airbnb Blog Post)
Airbnb has contributed Push Mode and NRT Model Transform to the public Chronon repository. Chronon supports both batch and streaming computation and provides online feature serving designed to maintain consistency between training and production inference.

articles.title: Apple anuncia MacBook Pro e iMac de 24 polegadas com chip M6; veja preços • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple anuncia MacBook Pro e iMac de 24 polegadas com chip M6; veja preços
Novo MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas promete ainda até 24 horas de autonomia. Já novo iMac de 24 polegadas traz sete opções de cores.
A Apple escolheu esta semana para fazer uma série de anúncios de produtos. Começou com o iPad Mini com tela OLED. Agora, nesta terça-feira (27/10), a companhia revelou dois Macs com chip M6: um MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas e um iMac de 24 polegadas. No Brasil, os preços começam em R$ 17.999.
O Apple M6 é um chip com até 12 núcleos de CPU e 12 núcleos de GPU, sendo que estes últimos são complementados com aceleradores de inteligência artificial. Também para lidar com tarefas de IA, o chip conta com uma implementação do Neural Engine com dois blocos de 16 núcleos.
Eis o efeito: o M6 oferece até 30% mais desempenho gráfico, bem como até 25% mais desempenho em IA em relação ao M5. Isso deixa claro que o MacBook Pro continua apto a lidar com tarefas que demandam altas cargas de trabalho.
Isso sem abrir mão da autonomia: ainda de acordo com a Apple, o MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas conta com uma bateria que dura até 24 horas com uma recarga completa. Trata-se do maior tempo de autonomia já registrado na linha. Para completar, a carga pode chegar a 50% de capacidade com apenas 30 minutos de tomada.
Falando dos demais recursos, o novo MacBook Pro também conta com uma tela Liquid Retina XDR (LCD com mini-LED) de 14 polegadas que alcança brilho de pico de 1.600 nits em HDR e, opcionalmente, com vidro “nano-texture”, que reduz os reflexos para melhorar a percepção de qualidade de imagem.
A frente também abriga uma câmera de 12 megapixels com tecnologia Center Stage, que usa IA para manter o usuário centralizado na imagem durante chamadas de vídeo.
Outros atributos de destaque incluem:
O novo iMac de 24 polegadas traz o mesmo chip M6 do novo MacBook Pro, podendo ter dez ou 12 núcleos de CPU e GPU, o que significa que desempenho também é um ponto forte do modelo, principalmente no âmbito da inteligência artificial.
Mas, talvez, o maior destaque fique para a tela, que consiste em um painel Retina (LCD) de 24 polegadas com resolução 4,5K. O componente suporta ainda até 500 nits de brilho e mais de 1 bilhão de cores. A câmera de 12 megapixels com Center Stage está por lá. O vidro “nano-texture” também é uma opção aqui.
Outras características incluem:
O novo MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas já aparece no site brasileiro da Apple, mas ainda não há informação sobre data de disponibilidade. Por lá, o preço parte de R$ 24.999, podendo variar de acordo com a configuração escolhida (o chip pode ser o M6, o M5 Pro ou o M5 Max, por exemplo).
Sobre o novo iMac de 24 polegadas, a novidade também não teve data de lançamento confirmada para o Brasil, mas custará a partir de R$ 17.999 por aqui. Haverá sete opções de cores: azul, roxo, rosa, laranja, amarelo, verde e prateado.
Nos Estados Unidos, ambos os produtos começarão a ser vendidos oficialmente a partir de 6 de novembro, mas a pré-venda terá início amanhã (28/10).
Vale lembrar que, ontem, a Apple anunciou o iPad Mini com tela OLED e chip A20 Pro. Para amanhã, podemos esperar o anúncio de um MacBook com tela touch. Fiquemos de olho.

articles.title: Dell adds identity resilience to cyber recovery tools - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Dell expands cyber recovery tools to protect identity
Restoring data after a cyberattack isn’t enough if the identity systems that control access are compromised. Dell Technologies Inc. is extending its cyber recovery tools to cover those systems, putting identity resilience alongside data protection.
That gap is widening as AI ties data, identity, infrastructure and applications into interdependent systems, making data protection a core layer of enterprise AI. Backup and recovery alone no longer get the business running again, according to Rob Emsley (pictured, left), director of cyber resilience product marketing at Dell.
“Without good identity and trust in identity, your ability to bring the business back is almost impossible,” he said. “Without the identity framework, the identity platform that you rely upon, you may have the data, but you can’t access it.”
Emsley and Adam Miller (right), global lead for security and resilience services marketing at Dell, spoke with theCUBE’s Dave Vellante for the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Dell is extending cyber recovery to identity platforms and AI infrastructure. (* Disclosure below.)
Identity resilience moves into the recovery playbook
Dell is building on its PowerProtect data protection and cyber recovery portfolio to address a critical dependency in the recovery process, according to Emsley.
“We’re introducing identity resilience into the PowerProtect portfolio for the key identity platforms that customers rely upon: Active Directory, Entra ID and Okta,” Emsley said. He added that the goal is to know “when the time comes to recover, you have trust in the identities that you rely upon before you then start bringing back the applications and data.”
Dell is also adding identity threat detection and response capabilities to its managed detection and response service, aiming to spot misuse of legitimate credentials as it happens and shut it down automatically. Miller pointed to the “impossible traveler,” a user who appears to log in from two distant locations faster than anyone could move between them.
“If you’ve got someone who logs in with legitimate credentials, but from an IP address they’ve never used before, we don’t only need to see that; we need to be able to automate response so quickly to either remove that person from the network or produce an outcome that stops that attack in its tracks,” he said. “This only becomes even more important when we start talking about agentic identity and what we’re going to need to do in order to govern those identities the same that we would any human.”
The same thinking now applies to AI infrastructure. Dell is embedding PowerProtect as an option within the Dell AI Factory and extending PowerProtect’s snapshot orchestration to PowerScale storage, with replication to ObjectScale. The moves build on PowerProtect One and Dell Cyber Detect, which Dell introduced in May to simplify cyber resilience across the data center. The company also draws lessons from about 6,500 AI Factory customers, according to Miller.
“Part of those insights include things that we’re learning from them that are making some organizations successful while others’ projects are stalling,” he said. “One of the key things that we’ve realized is that security and resilience really needs to be brought in from the beginning, a core architectural decision, so that we’re not repeating the pitfalls of the cloud transition and trying to bolt it on later.”
Testing is where many resilience plans fall short. Dell’s services teams run tabletop exercises and end-to-end simulations of a ransomware intrusion, its detection and the recovery that follows. One customer that restructured its approach to improve recovery speed saw backup-to-recovery efficiency improve 17 times, according to Miller. Emsley emphasized the importance of knowing that critical operations can be restored.
“Everything you do, you need to test it,” Emsley said. “The concept of assured recovery has never been more important than it is today.”

articles.title: Trump prohibirá el término "inteligencia artificial" porque lo considera inexacto
articles.text:
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, anunció en su red social Truth Social que prohibirá oficialmente el término “inteligencia artificial” en “todos los documentos relevantes” y en “todo lo demás”, porque lo considera inexacto. Prefiere llamarla “superinteligencia”, o SI por sus siglas en inglés.
Trump pregunta cuándo empezará a usar “SI” en lugar de IA, un nombre que calificó de “muy malo e inexacto”, y sostiene que “prácticamente todos” ya usan su término preferido o pronto lo harán. Cerró con un agradecimiento por la atención al tema.
El mensaje no explica cómo se aplicaría la prohibición ni qué documentos alcanzaría. Consultada por Mediaite sobre la libertad de expresión que protege la Primera Enmienda, la oficina de prensa de la Casa Blanca respondió con la frase “remítanse a LA VERDAD”.
Según Forbes, las agencias federales y las bases de datos del Gobierno siguen usando el término. Medios de alcance nacional también lo mantienen, y el manual de estilo de The Associated Press lo considera la denominación correcta.
La orden del 29 de septiembre de 2026 ya obligaba a las agencias
El anuncio amplía una campaña anterior. El 29 de septiembre de 2026, Trump firmó una orden ejecutiva que instruye a los departamentos y agencias federales a usar “superinteligencia” en sus comunicaciones oficiales, según PolitiFact. Ese día, en la Casa Blanca y junto a ejecutivos de las grandes empresas de IA, dijo: “No es artificial. Todos estamos de acuerdo en eso”.
Trump también había publicado encuestas en Truth Social para elegir un nuevo nombre, con opciones como “inteligencia superior”, “inteligencia extrema” e “inteligencia suprema”. A comienzos de octubre escribió que la Casa Blanca considera “EL ENEMIGO” a quien use el término “inteligencia artificial”, según Mediaite.
El cambio tuvo poco eco en el sector. PolitiFact sostiene que, tras la orden, casi nada cambió en cómo los líderes de la industria nombran su tecnología en materiales públicos. Elon Musk dijo que rebautizará su empresa SpaceXAI como SpaceXSI, y el director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, llamó “fábricas de superinteligencia” a los centros de datos.
“Superinteligencia” ya tenía otro significado
El obstáculo conceptual es que el término ya existe. En la industria, “superinteligencia” designa una IA que supera la capacidad cognitiva humana en casi todos los campos, algo que, según PolitiFact, el sector coincide en que ningún sistema logró. El filósofo Nick Bostrom lo definió así en 1998.
Según la orden, “superinteligencia” reemplaza a las tecnologías que la ley estadounidense actual describe como inteligencia artificial. El científico Geoffrey Hinton, profesor de la Universidad de Toronto, criticó el cambio: “No se puede hacer que sea más inteligente que las personas solo llamándola más inteligente que las personas”.
Baobao Zhang, profesora asociada de la Universidad de Syracuse que estudia la política de la IA, dijo a PolitiFact que las definiciones importan para regular la tecnología. Advirtió que sistemas que hoy no encajan en la nueva definición podrían causar daños graves y quedar fuera.
Los límites de la autoridad presidencial
Según Deadline, el poder del presidente para imponer el nombre fuera del Gobierno es limitado. La Casa Blanca ya intentó forzar otro cambio de denominación: excluyó a AP de la sala presidencial por no usar “Golfo de América” para el Golfo de México. Un juez federal dictaminó que probablemente violaba la Primera Enmienda, y la decisión está en apelación. Trump no dio una fecha para la prohibición.

articles.title: South Carolina's measles outbreak jumped to Washington state 5 times in 2 weeks
articles.text:
Since measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, the country’s occasional cases have come mainly from international travelers—visitors from far-flung places where the virus still spreads freely—or unvaccinated US residents who return from abroad with a highly infectious souvenir. But as vaccination rates have slipped nationwide in recent years and outbreaks grow bigger and more frequent, domestic travel now poses a greater risk than international incursions.
In a study published this week in NEJM Evidence, Washington state health officials highlight that risk, detailing how an explosive outbreak in South Carolina reached their distant state through five distinct importation events over two weeks in January. In all, the introductions led to 26 cases among residents before officials stamped out the spread.
South Carolina’s measles outbreak began on October 2, 2025, and was declared over on April 26, 2026. Officials confirmed 997 cases in the state during the outbreak. At the time, it was the largest measles outbreak recorded since the virus was declared eliminated, but Pennsylvania’s ongoing outbreak has since surpassed it.
The study in Washington relied heavily on epidemiological data, linking cases among contacts and exposure sites. But also key to the work was whole-genome sequencing, which made clear that cases didn’t just stem from one single introduction of the virus from South Carolina that then spread among Washington residents; instead, it revealed five separate introductions.
“As public health jurisdictions prepare to respond to increased measles importations linked to domestic measles outbreaks, while remaining vigilant for international importations, timely whole-genome sequencing can supplement epidemiologic information to help differentiate distinct importations from local transmission and inform outbreak response,” the authors conclude.
Importations
In their analysis, health officials identified the first importation in a resident who fell ill with the telltale rash on January 12 after returning from a trip to South Carolina, where they were exposed to a person sick with measles. Genome sequencing found that the virus closely matched sequences from South Carolina cases. One close contact of the Washington case fell ill and was isolated. No other cases were linked to this importation.

articles.title: Free Fire returns to India as Garena launches localized version four years after ban | TechCrunch
articles.text:
More than four years after New Delhi banned Free Fire over national security concerns, Garena has brought the popular battle royale game back to India with a localized version.
On Wednesday, Garena launched the localized version, called Free Fire India, as a standalone game available on Android and iOS. The new version features India-specific content, parental controls, playtime limits, and spending caps, with user data hosted on servers in India, the firm owned by South Asian giant Sea said. The launch comes more than three years after Garena quietly postponed Free Fire India’s earlier release after announcing it in September 2023.
Free Fire was one of India’s most popular mobile games before it was banned in February 2022 alongside 53 other apps over alleged links to China. The game had become more popular after India banned its rival PUBG Mobile in September 2020. Free Fire’s ban, however, sent shares of Singapore-based Sea, Garena’s parent company, tumbling, wiping more than $16 billion off its market value in a single day. Still, Garena remained active in India. Free Fire MAX, an enhanced version of the game, was not among the banned apps and remained available to players.
PUBG Mobile’s South Korean publisher Krafton later introduced Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI), a version similar to PUBG Mobile but made specifically for Indian players. But BGMI has struggled to match the popularity of Garena’s Free Fire franchise. In June, the franchise had about 77.4 million monthly active users in India, compared with 20.8 million for BGMI, according to Sensor Tower data reviewed by TechCrunch.
Vaibhav Das Mundhra, Garena’s head of operations in India, told TechCrunch that Free Fire MAX would remain available alongside Free Fire India. Players will be able to use the same account across both games, play together and take part in the same events, he said.
Garena, Mundhra said, had worked with relevant Indian government authorities and incorporated their feedback while preparing Free Fire India for launch. However, he did not answer questions about why the game’s planned 2023 launch was delayed or what had changed to allow its release now.
While Free Fire India’s launch remained on hold, TechCrunch earlier reported that Garena continued developing games for the Indian market. Through its studios in Pune and Mumbai, the company worked on titles inspired by Hindu mythology, cricket, and the traditional board game Ludo, releasing some of them while the original Free Fire remained banned. One of those titles, Versus, was previously available in early access on Google Play but is no longer listed on the store.
Despite regulatory setbacks, India remains a significant market for mobile gaming companies. Mobile game downloads in the country grew 14.2% quarter-over-quarter to 2 billion in Q2, while revenue rose 3.7% to more than $106 million, per Sensor Tower.
Garena’s Free Fire MAX has also maintained a presence in India’s esports scene, with Indian teams including S8UL Esports, Apex Gaming, and Total Gaming competing at the Esports World Cup 2026.
Animesh Agarwal, co-founder and CEO of S8UL Esports, said Free Fire India’s return could open up more opportunities for players and creators. “For me, the real impact goes beyond the game itself. It’s about the players who dream of building a career in esports, the creators who have built communities around the title, and the opportunities this ecosystem can create for everyone involved,” he said.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2 Multiplayer Looks Likely
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Cyberpunk 2 Multiplayer Looks Likely
Cyberpunk 2 has already been confirmed as being in development by CD Projekt Red, but not all that much has been revealed about the game aside from its massive budget and a potential 2030 launch date. Now, a new job posting by CD Projekt Red has potentially confirmed recent rumors that multiplayer support is being worked on for Cyberpunk 2. This comes after Cyberpunk 2077 was originally meant to have multiplayer support, but that was cancelled ahead of release. 
The job listing is for a lead quest programmer "to join the team working on Cyberpunk 2" and specifically mentions "understanding of multiplayer network architecture and client-server synchronization for game state/quests" in the "nice to have" section. This suggests that, while multiplayer is almost certainly on the cards for Cyberpunk 2, the game will still likely be built with the single-player, narrative-driven gameplay first and foremost—perhaps something similar to the older Borderlands games, whose campaigns can be played in multiplayer or single-player, all within the same playthrough.The full requirements for the Cyberpunk 2 Lead Quest Designer read as follows:
Qualifications
- At least 7 years of professional programming experience within the AAA games industry.
- 1+ years experience in technical leadership, people management, or leading a team of engineers.
- Strong proficiency in C++ programming.
- Demonstrated experience developing custom quest systems, narrative tools, or node-based editor workflows.
- Proven track record of working in a highly collaborative shared technology environment that spans multiple teams or projects.
- Ability to interpret the needs of creative and less technical team members, translating design visions into clear technical requirements.
- Excellent communication and collaboration skills to work effectively across time zones and multicultural environments.
Nice to Have:
(please note these skills are not required to apply)
- Familiarity with Unreal Engine architecture.
- Understanding of multiplayer network architecture and client-server synchronization for game state/quests.
- Shipped AAA game(s) on a bespoke or custom narrative/quest toolset.
- Familiarity with Unreal Engine UI tools or editor scripting for custom content tools.
Source:
				CD Projekt Red

articles.title: Meet the TechRadar Product of the Year 2026 winners — our editors choose their favorite gadgets of the last 12 months
articles.text:
Though 2026 has been a tumultuous time for technology when it comes to price hikes and shortages, the tech that's reached us has been excellent — in fact, it's been a banner year in most areas, just with some downsides for your wallet.
We've already crowned the best tech of the year as chosen by you in our TechRadar Readers' Choice Awards 2026 — but this is where we let our experts have their say.
Our writers and editors chose their favorite products in nearly 100 categories, ranging across all the kinds of products we review. In some cases, we agree with the readers; in lots of cases, we don't. So read on to see which gadgets we rate as being the most impressive of the last 12 months.
Phones & tablets
Phone of the Year
Apple iPhone 18 Pro
Wherever you look, the iPhone 18 Pro excels. It might not have the biggest camera sensor or the longest-lasting battery of any phone on the market, but it does offer a near-unrivaled combination of premium flagship features. From its variable aperture feature and pro-level video capabilities to its phenomenal performance and gorgeous display, the 18 Pro is the Swiss Army knife of 2026 smartphones.
Read our full iPhone 18 Pro review
Phone Brand of the Year
Honor
The Chinese company has brought something competitive to the table at every turn in 2026. The Honor Magic 8 Pro is an extremely capable flagship. The Magic V6 is easily one of the best foldables you can buy. The Honor 600 series offers some serious value for money in the mid-range sector. The MagicPad 4 is an iPad-beating tablet in several ways. And the Robot Phone is, well, the Robot Phone. Honor’s products aren’t globally available in the same way as, say, Apple's or Samsung’s, but those who have tried the brand’s phones and tablets will know about their level of hardware quality.
Phones Innovation of the Year
Honor Robot Phone
Sticking with Honor, it’s hard to see past the Robot Phone as the most exciting Phones Innovation of the Year in 2026. There's been some competition from foldables in this area this year, but Honor deserves credit for bringing something wildly different to the market (in China, at least). Computing
Laptop of the Year
Apple MacBook Neo
If there's one laptop that has made the biggest impact in 2026, then it's the MacBook Neo. Audio Innovation of the Year
Cambridge L/R S speakers
Before I heard these speakers, I thought Cambridge had taken a big risk here. Then, I gave them a thorough listen and I knew they were winners. The L/R S is a genuinely active stereo speaker system, so it does not involve a powered primary speaker and a dumb counterpart to make a pair. OK, only the primary speaker receives power, but there are two channels of amplification for each speaker. Then, there's a full DSP crossover which acts as a PWM signal to each amp — and that's before the bespoke four-conductor cable to connect the primary speaker to the secondary! Might we call them over-engineered? Maybe — or you could simply call Cambridge's work ethic ‘admirable’, as I do.
