articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 28, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 28, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Wednesday, October 28, 2026.
From Jio Platforms making a strong debut on the National Stock Exchange on Wednesday with its shares gaining 21.3% over the issue price of Rs 1,119 apiece, to AI that can generate almost anything we ask for, here are the latest developments across sectors.
Featured Stories
When content becomes infinite, what makes people pay attention?
We are living in a world where content is no longer scarce. There is more news, more videos, more creators, and, AI that can generate almost anything we ask for. But this abundance brings a new challenge: when everyone is creating content, how do you get someone to stop scrolling, pay attention, and come back?
On the sidelines of TechSparks 2026, Avinash Mudaliar, Co-founder and CEO of HT Media Labs and the creator of Saregama Carvaan; Deepit Purkayastha, Co-founder and CEO of Inshorts; and GSN Aditya, COO of Eloelo Group, came together for a discussion titled The Format Is the Product: When Content Becomes Infinite.
Latest News
Jio Platforms makes strong market debut, lists on NSE with a gain of 21.3%
Jio Platforms made a strong debut on the National Stock Exchange on Wednesday with its shares gaining 21.3% over the issue price of Rs 1,119 apiece, resulting in a market capitalisation of Rs 12.5 lakh crore.
The share opened at Rs 1,358 and reached an intraday high of Rs 1,374.50. It was trading at Rs 1,366.60 at 11:41 am with a market capitalisation of Rs 12,58,045.70 crore.
Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213-crore IPO received an overwhelming response from investors. It was oversubscribed in less than two hours on opening day, and closed with a 22X oversubscription.
Funding News
Healthy snack brand Troovy raises Rs 100 Cr in Series B round led by Fireside Ventures
Troovy, a food and snacks brand, has raised Rs 100 crore in a Series B round of funding led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Sharrp Ventures and other investors.
The Gurugram-based brand will use the funding for R&D, expanding its manufacturing capacity, and scaling distribution across quick commerce and offline channels, as it looks to launch a wide range of products.
Troovy was founded in 2023 by Mansi Baranwal and Aditya Mukherjee with the goal of providing nutritious food. Its portfolio spans categories such as snacks, sauces and spreads, and millet pasta. It says its vacuum-cooked potato chips have 10-12% oil and high protein, compared with 35-40% oil in mainstream chips. It also promises clean-label ketchups and seasonings without synthetic additives or preservatives.
Other News
QwikBuild raises $2.3M in pre-seed funding, enters Japan through JV
Bengaluru-based enterprise AI startup QwikBuild has raised $2.3 million in pre-seed funding from Globalway Inc, Blume Ventures, Marsshot, DeVC and angel investors, including Groww founder Lalit Keshre and Cure.fit founder Ankit Nagori.
The company also announced a joint venture with publicly listed Japanese firm Globalway to enter Japan’s enterprise market. QwikBuild uses autonomous AI agents to build bespoke enterprise software in days, enabling businesses to automate workflows, modernise legacy systems and integrate applications with existing platforms such as SAP and Salesforce. The startup currently serves enterprises across India, the US and Singapore.
PhonePe rebrands Indus Appstore, targets digital goods market with 200 million devices
PhonePe has rebranded its homegrown app marketplace, Indus Appstore, as PhonePe Appstore, as it expands into digital goods and services. The platform is available on more than 200 million devices through original equipment manufacturer (OEM) partnerships, with Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Karnataka and Telangana among its top markets.
Alongside apps and games, users can access gift cards and digital top-ups, with gaming top-ups scheduled to launch first. PhonePe has also introduced phonepeappstore.com, a webstore for discovering and purchasing digital products through browsers. The platform aims to offer developers alternative distribution and monetisation opportunities through payments, advertising and digital sales.
ixigo co-founder Rajnish Kumar launches Rs 1 crore fund to back IIT Kanpur startups
ixigo co-founder and Group Co-CEO Rajnish Kumar has launched the Rs 1 crore Made in Fire Fund to support technology-led startups founded by graduating IIT Kanpur students. Beginning with the Class of 2026, the initiative will select 10 startups per batch, offering each Rs 10 lakh in non-dilutive prototype funding.
Beyond capital, founders will receive mentorship from Kumar, ixigo’s leadership team and its wider entrepreneur network, alongside product reviews, go-to-market guidance, hiring support and investor introductions. The fund will prioritise founder conviction, customer understanding and execution over pitch decks, backing ventures across AI, SaaS, deep tech, mobility, healthcare and other technology sectors.
CHOSEN Extends Series A with Backing from Wellbeing Nutrition Founders
CHOSEN, India's first exposome-based dermocosmetic brand, has extended its Series A round with investment from Wellbeing Nutrition founders Avnish Chhabria and Saurabh Kapoor, joining Fireside Ventures, L'Oréal's BOLD, and Alkemi Growth Capital. The fresh capital will strengthen R&D, expand the formulation pipeline across topicals and nutraceuticals, and fund a dermatologist-led Centre of Excellence.
Founded in 2020 by Dr Renita Rajan, the Chennai-based brand formulates melanin-rich Indian skin, targeting pigmentation, texture, contour and hair ageing. It offers over 50 products prescribed by more than 2,000 doctors, and raised a $5 million Series A in May 2026.
Bellatrix Aerospace appoints Kiran U as CFO to drive growth and international expansion
Bengaluru-based in-space mobility company Bellatrix Aerospace has appointed Kiran U as its Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead its financial strategy and support business expansion. A Chartered Accountant and Company Secretary, Kiran brings over 17 years of experience across financial planning, treasury, capital raising, taxation, audit and investor relations.
In his new role, he will focus on capital efficiency, funding diversification, financial discipline and operational scalability as the company pursues international opportunities and expands its commercial pipeline. Bellatrix Aerospace develops in-space propulsion technologies, including Arka Hall Effect Thrusters and Rudra Green Propulsion Systems, for satellite and space missions.
PB Money secures SEBI licence to expand retail access to bonds
PB Money, an investment platform strategically partnered with Paisabazaar, has received a Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) licence as an Online Bond Platform Provider (OBPP). The licence allows the platform to manage the entire bond investment journey, covering investor onboarding, KYC, bond discovery, order placement, payments and post-investment servicing.
Through its partnership with Paisabazaar, PB Money aims to reach a wider consumer base and simplify access to fixed-income products. Investors can compare bonds based on parameters such as yield, credit rating and investment amount, helping them evaluate options and diversify their portfolios."
PhysicsWallah’s School of Startups partners with DPIIT to support 25,000 startups
PhysicsWallah’s School of Startups (PW SoS) has partnered with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under a two-year agreement to support 25,000 early-stage startups across India. The initiative will focus on entrepreneurs in Tier-II and Tier-III cities and rural areas, offering training, mentorship, incubation, seed funding and investor access.
Programmes include PW UDYAMI, a 90-day online course with one year of mentorship, and a six-month DeepTech Accelerator. The partnership will also support prototype development, corporate pilot projects and growth-stage funding readiness, aiming to strengthen regional entrepreneurship and innovation.
Let’s Game Now raises Rs 30 Cr from Anand Mahindra and other investors
Let’s Game Now, an Indian gaming and esports company, has closed a Rs 30 crore investment round backed by Anand Mahindra, Bestvantage Investments and a UAE-based family office. The company will use the funding to accelerate the development of the Indian Super Gaming League (ISGL), a franchise-based competition combining gaming, sports, entertainment and technology.
The league has also received backing from actors Ranveer Singh and Abhishek Bachchan. Let’s Game Now claims a community of over 1.4 million members and has organised more than 2,000 events. Bestvantage Investments advised the company exclusively on the investment round.
Oracle, Snowflake bring AI Data Cloud to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
Oracle and Snowflake have announced that Snowflake AI Data Cloud will be available as a native, first-party service on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), expanding options for enterprises seeking to use their data for artificial intelligence and analytics. Customers will be able to purchase, provision and consume the service directly through Oracle, with unified pricing and billing.
They can also use Oracle Universal Credits, simplifying procurement and enabling them to draw on existing cloud commitments. The integration is designed to bring Snowflake’s analytics and AI capabilities closer to enterprise data held across Oracle services, including Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications, NetSuite and Oracle databases.
HCLTech launches AI-powered nano GCC offering with AWS
HCLTech has launched an AI-powered nano Global Capability Centre (GCC) offering built on Amazon Web Services (AWS), aimed at helping enterprises transition from AI experimentation to business outcomes. Part of its GCC 360 solution suite, the model combines HCLTech’s advisory expertise and AI platforms, including AI Force, with AWS infrastructure and agentic AI services.
The offering targets established GCCs seeking AI-led transformation and mid-market companies looking to enter new geographies with lower risk. It focuses on compact, product-centric teams, AI-enabled workflows, autonomous IT operations, engineering, data analytics and intelligent business operations.
BonV Aero completes high-altitude logistics drone trials
Bhubaneswar-based uncrewed aerial systems manufacturer BonV Aero has completed fleet testing of its logistics drones across remote, high-altitude locations, demonstrating payload transport at elevations ranging from 10,500 to 16,500 feet. The trials involved carrying a 32-kg payload and evaluated the performance of heavy-payload unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in challenging operating conditions.
The latest trials build on the company’s earlier achievement of lifting 30 kg to 19,024 feet at Umling La in Ladakh in 2023. It has also supplied 45 heavy-payload UAVs to the Indian Army’s Eastern Command.
Vashi Integrated Solutions plans 22 solar marts across 10 states
Vashi Integrated Solutions plans to establish 22 Vashi Mart outlets across 10 states by FY 2026-27 to improve access to solar equipment and installation essentials for rooftop solar installers. The initiative aims to address procurement challenges, particularly in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets, by bringing inventory and technical support closer to project locations.
The first phase will cover Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam, Uttarakhand and Odisha. The outlets will primarily serve residential rooftop solar installations, while also supporting smaller commercial and industrial projects.

articles.title: Tesla : la conduite autonome promise par Elon Musk attendra encore
articles.text:
Tesla prend du retard sur son planning de déploiement de la conduite autonome FSD. Alors qu’Elon Musk promettait en 2025 des voitures capables de conduire seules avant la fin de l’année, les cadres de l’entreprise américaine donnent désormais une échéance au deuxième trimestre 2027. Et encore, seulement dans certaines zones prédéfinies. Pourtant, Tesla espère livrer les premiers exemplaires du Cybercab avant la fin de l’année.
Une conduite autonome en retard
Si Tesla fait bien rouler quelques voitures autonomes comme service de taxi dans certaines villes américaines, cela se cantonne à de petites zones précisément cartographiées et parfois avec des superviseurs sur le siège passager pour arrêter le véhicule si nécessaire. On reste encore loin de « l’usage personnel non supervisé d’ici la fin de l’année, dans certaines zones géographiques » promis par Elon Musk en juillet 2025.
Et les investisseurs s’impatientent. Lors de la dernière réunion avec les investisseurs, la question a été soulevée : « Quand pouvons-nous espérer le FSD non supervisé dans les voitures des clients ? » À cette question, Ashok Elluswamy, en charge de l’IA chez Tesla, a donné une nouvelle échéance : le deuxième trimestre 2027.
À partir de cette date, les clients ayant des véhicules compatibles pourront confier leur Tesla au service de Robotaxi de la marque. Il ne s’agit donc pas d’un usage personnel, mais bien d’un usage commercial géré par la marque. Actuellement, seulement six villes américaines ont autorisé l’usage du Robotaxi dans certaines zones, à vitesse réduite, loin des autoroutes, et parfois avec un superviseur, comme à San Francisco. On est encore loin du rêve d’Elon Musk de la conduite totalement autonome des Tesla.
D’autant que les propriétaires de Tesla disposant de la fonction FSD, mais avec l’ordinateur de bord HW3, ne pourront pas bénéficier de la conduite non supervisée sur leur véhicule. Ce qui réduit grandement le nombre d’utilisateurs potentiels de la conduite 100 % autonome lorsqu’elle sera admise par les différents cadres réglementaires.
Tesla veut déjà livrer les Cybercab
Si vous avez visité le hall 7 du Mondial de l’Auto de Paris, vous avez vu le modeste stand Tesla. Le constructeur y présentait au public le Cybercab, sa voiture totalement autonome pensée pour ne pas avoir de conducteur. En effet, cette voiture n’a ni volant ni pédales, ce qui ne laisse pas l’humain reprendre le contrôle sur l’IA de conduite autonome. Le parti pris est fort : Tesla semble montrer qu’il faut davantage faire confiance à l’IA qu’aux humains en ce qui concerne la conduite.
Et Tesla espère livrer ses premiers Cybercab dès cette année, comme l’explique Lars Moravy : « Nous essayons de livrer des Cybercab à des clients d’ici la fin de cette année, 2026 », d’après Reuters. Elon Musk a ensuite nuancé les propos, précisant que ces premiers Cybercab appartiendront à la marque et serviront son service de VTC, qui est actuellement assuré par des Model Y.
Pourtant, les Cybercab ne sont pas encore approuvés par l’organisme de sécurité routière aux États-Unis, la NHTSA. L’agence a ouvert une enquête juste après les premières courses payantes du Cybercab à Austin, au Texas, à proximité de la Gigafactory de Tesla. Dans le pays, un constructeur peut mettre une voiture en circulation avant l’autorisation des organismes, à condition que celle-ci respecte les exigences fédérales, comprenant notamment un volant et des pédales. Or, le Tesla Cybercab se passe de volant et de pédales, et la société ne semble pas disposée à en ajouter, même si cela pourrait faciliter la mise en circulation du véhicule. Tesla n’a pas demandé de dérogation pour son Cybercab et a jusqu’au 30 octobre pour répondre à la NHTSA.

articles.title: CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
articles.text:
On Tuesday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that hackers have begun exploiting a critical Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell, Broccoli2Shell, and HTTP2Shell.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, this critical-severity flaw stems from an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Brotli decoder used to expand data compressed with Google's widely popular Brotli lossless compression algorithm.
Unprivileged attackers can use a maliciously crafted Brotli-compressed stream to trigger crashes or memory leaks and, in some cases, gain remote code execution on devices with vulnerable Brotli libraries or binaries.
The security issue was first identified in the Node.js JavaScript runtime environment, but it also affects HTTP servers and clients that rely on vulnerable Brotli implementations.
On Sunday, Microsoft also pushed an emergency .NET security update, warning that attackers could exploit it to escalate privileges on systems with a vulnerable .NET version.
CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US government agencies to patch their systems within two weeks, by November 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
"Google Brotli contains an unchecked return value vulnerability that allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream," it said.
"These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise."
While CISA's BOD 26-04 applies only to federal agencies, the cybersecurity agency urged all network defenders to prioritize patching this security flaw to block incoming attacks.
Security teams that can't apply the updates immediately should block incoming Brotli-compressed requests at the proxy or firewall level, or disable the Brotli decoding feature until they can update.
After patching, administrators must also restart affected processes and rebuild and redeploy affected container images.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Salir a caminar en vez de ir al gimnasio está muy bien, pero solo funciona si la caminata es a 5 km/h y con cierta constancia
articles.text:
Durante mucho tiempo se pensó que el ejercicio solo era válido si se realizaba en bloques de tiempo bastante largos o combinado con una buena rutina de gimnasio, hasta el punto de que las guías oficiales sugerían un mínimo de 10 minutos seguidos para que la actividad "contara" como válida. Pero esto ha cambiado radicalmente.
No importan los bloques. Las revisiones sistemáticas que se han hecho demostraron que la reducción de la mortalidad es similar tanto si la actividad se acumula esporádicamente como si se hace en bloques. Por ello, las guías de la OMS de 2020 eliminaron cualquier umbral de tiempo a la hora de ejercitarse, por lo que el mensaje actual es bastante claro: cada minuto de actividad cuenta.
Aunque no siempre. Sin embargo, para aquellas personas que son sedentarias o poco activas, hacer caminatas con cierta continuidad si tiene un valor añadido. Aquí, un reciente estudio español liderado por la Universidad Europea de Madrid analizó a más de 33.000 adultos en el UK Biobank que daban 8.000 pasos o menos al día. Y lo que vieron fue que el riesgo de sufrir eventos cardiovasculares disminuía drásticamente según cómo agruparan esos datos.
Lo que se vio fue que la incidencia era del 13% en quienes caminaban en tramos de menos de cinco minutos, y bajaba al 4,4% en quienes acumulaban la mayoría de sus pasos en tramos de 15 minutos o más. Es por ello que, aunque en la mente tengamos que hay que caminar de manera seguida durante 30 minutos para que cuente, la realidad es que para estas personas bastaría con 10-15 minutos, que es mucho más llevadero.
El ritmo importa. Salir a ver escaparates de manera tranquila una tarde no cuenta como un ejercicio cardiovascular, aunque nos tiremos una hora de tienda en tienda. Aquí tenemos como referencia un estudio publicado en 2022 que concluyó que los 5 km/h son el umbral práctico perfecto para identificar una caminata de intensidad moderada en adultos. Y es que caminar adecuadamente puede tener beneficios sobre el colesterol o la hipertensión en el mismo orden que ir al gimnasio, siempre que el esfuerzo sea adecuado.
Es por ello que el ritmo al que caminamos tiene un impacto directo en nuestra esperanza de vida, puesto que un gran estudio británico con más de 50.000 participantes demostró que caminar a un paso rápido, frente a un paso lento, se asocia con un 24% menos de mortalidad general y un 21% menos de mortalidad cardiovascular.
No sustituye al gimnasio del todo. Aunque a nivel puramente cardiovascular y de gasto energético caminar a buen ritmo es extraordinariamente efectivo, la realidad es que hablamos de un ejercicio exclusivamente aeróbico. Aquí los equipos de investigación nos apuntan a que el trabajo de fuerza es un factor protector independiente y no intercambiable.
Por ejemplo, un metaanálisis encontró que las actividades de fortalecimiento muscular se asocian por sí solas a un 10-17% menos de riesgo de mortalidad y enfermedades cardiovasculares. Es por ello que a la recomendación de tener entre 150 y 300 minutos de actividad aeróbica semanal hay que sumarle al menos dos días a la semana de entrenamiento de fuerza.

articles.title: Vos messages Discord bientôt sur Google ? Ce qui va changer pour les utilisateurs
articles.text:
Les réponses publiées dans les salons publics des grandes communautés Discord pourront apparaître dans les résultats des moteurs de recherche à partir de la mi-décembre, sans pseudo ni avatar. En France, cela ne sera valable que pour les membres qui activent l’option.
Ne vous précipitez pas sur vos chats tout de suite. Seuls les serveurs « découvrables » sont concernés. Leurs administrateurs les ont inscrits dans l’annuaire interne de Discord, et n’importe qui peut les rejoindre sans invitation. La plateforme n’admet dans cet annuaire que des communautés d’au moins 1 000 membres et datant d’au moins huit semaines, soit plus de 63 000 serveurs de ce type. Beaucoup de forums de joueurs ont migré vers ces espaces au fil des années, et les internautes ne trouvent plus leurs conseils sur un boss ou un speedrun en passant par un moteur de recherche. Dans son annonce, l’entreprise dit vouloir « ramener ce qui faisait la force des forums ». Les membres pourront refuser la publication de leurs messages, mais pas celle des résumés automatiques de leurs discussions.
En France, des messages publiés seulement avec votre accord
À partir de la mi-décembre, certains messages des salons publics pourront s’afficher sur la page Web de leur serveur et dans les résultats de recherche. Discord retire pseudos et avatars de ces extraits, et ne publiera aucun message envoyé avant cette date. Les membres de l’Union européenne et de cinq autres pays, dont le Royaume-Uni et le Canada, devront activer l’option pour que leurs messages sortent de Discord, car l’entreprise se plie dans ces régions à des contraintes légales. Partout ailleurs, l’option est activée tant que le membre ne la coupe pas. Discord exclut totalement les adolescents, qui ne pourront l’activer qu’à leur majorité.
Le réglage se trouve dans Paramètres utilisateur > Données et confidentialité, et un seul interrupteur vaut pour tous les serveurs découvrables dont vous êtes membre. Si vous changez d’avis, vous pouvez le couper à tout moment. Vos messages suivants ne sortiront plus de Discord, mais ceux publiés pendant que l’option était activée resteront en ligne tant que vous ne les avez pas supprimés.
Côté administrateurs, les salons publics participent par défaut. Ils peuvent retirer certains salons, ou tous, dans les paramètres du serveur, rubrique Web Presence. Discord signalera les salons ouverts aux moteurs de recherche par une étiquette, pour que chacun sache avant d’écrire si son message peut finir sur le Web.
- Chat vocal, visuel et écrit
- Un outil employé à la fois pour les loisirs et le travail
- L’option la plus populaire
Des résumés automatiques inévitables
Dès le 16 novembre, chaque serveur découvrable disposera d’une page Web publique. Discord créera une page par défaut à partir du profil du serveur pour les communautés qui n’ont encore aucune page, et les administrateurs qui refusent cette vitrine devront rétrograder leur serveur au rang de serveur communautaire. Discord pourra publier sur cette page des résumés automatiques des conversations actives dans les salons publics, sans pseudo ni avatar.
Les membres n’ont aucun moyen de bloquer ces résumés, puisque Discord les génère séparément, à partir des grands sujets abordés dans chaque salon. Seuls les administrateurs peuvent choisir les salons résumés ou couper la fonction. Discord teste ces publications sur le Web avec des communautés de jeux vidéo, dont celles de NBA 2K et de Dead by Daylight, mais tous les messages de ce test venaient d’administrateurs ou de modérateurs.
Des utilisateurs ont critiqué l’annonce sur Reddit et sur X, rapporte TechCrunch. Pour une partie d’entre eux, écrire dans un serveur public ne revient pas à accepter d’être lu sur tout le Web. D’autres redoutent que ces conversations servent à entraîner des modèles d’intelligence artificielle. Des utilisateurs de Reddit avaient soulevé cette question lors des accords de partage de données conclus par leur plateforme. Discord n’aborde pas le sujet de l’IA dans son annonce.

articles.title: AI agents need to be replaceable – without losing your work
articles.text:
AI agents need to be replaceable – without losing your work
An agent receives approval to process a partial refund. It sends the request to a payment API, and the process crashes. Maybe the payment service completed the refund. Maybe the request never went through. A replacement agent spins up and finds an operation record marked dispatched with no outcome written.
This kind of ambiguity isn’t unique to agents. Any distributed worker crashing mid-mutation faces the same problem. But a conventional worker resumes a predetermined workflow from the last checkpoint. An agent does something more dangerous: it reasons on its own. Given the same customer request and no outcome record, it might come up with a different plan, pick different parameters, or decide to issue a new refund instead of continuing the one already approved.
“An agent does something more dangerous: it reasons on its own.”
If the original refund went through, a second attempt refunds the customer twice. The charge still has enough remaining balance to cover another partial refund, so nothing stops it.
The replacement must inherit the original operation, not reinterpret it.
The operation must outlive the agent
An agent’s process, its in-memory variables, its transient reasoning context: all disposable. The business operation is not. The refund, its approval, its parameters, its current status. A long-running agent can preserve useful state for as long as it runs. The requirement: no essential operation should depend on the original execution surviving.
Before dispatching the refund, the application commits a durable operation record to a transactional store. That record includes the approved amount, the applicable authorization, the idempotency key the application sends to the payment provider, the application’s operation identifier in the provider’s metadata, and a status.
“An agent’s process, its in-memory variables, its transient reasoning context: all disposable. The business operation is not.”
The status moves from created to dispatched as the request leaves, and to confirmed or failed only on a provider response. If the agent crashes, the replacement retrieves this record and its correlation identifiers. A record stuck in dispatched indicates a call was attempted, but the outcome was never written.
The replacement inherits the approved operation rather than regenerating it.
When the replacement needs to verify the outcome, it can list refunds against the original charge and match the operation identifier in the returned metadata.
But the durable record isn’t just context for the replacement. The application enforces it at the tool boundary: the dispatch layer validates every outbound request against the committed record. The agent can propose a next step, but only authorized operations with their original parameters and identity reach the provider. The model can’t redefine what was approved.
ClickHouse Managed Postgres holds the business data, including the authoritative operation record that defines what the replacement is allowed to do. Native CDC replicates that data into ClickHouse. Application telemetry ships to ClickStack and agent traces to Langfuse, both configured to use the same ClickHouse service as their backend database.
Because business data, application telemetry, and agent traces land in one database, tying an operation to the agent run that dispatched it and the failed HTTP call is a single-identifier query. Not a reconciliation across three tools.
Two conditions. The application has to propagate that identifier. The operation ID must appear in the Postgres row, in the Langfuse trace attributes, and in the service’s log context, because nothing correlates it for you. And the replacement reads the record from Postgres, not from the replicated copy. CDC runs with seconds of latency. The authoritative row is the one the tool boundary enforces.
Restarting execution isn’t safely resuming work
Durable execution frameworks like LangGraph and Temporal record execution progress and resume after a failure. Both recommend making side effects idempotent, because resuming doesn’t resolve one. If the refund completed while the step was still pending, the framework can restart the agent, but it can’t tell the replacement whether the payment provider committed the original request.
The durable operation record implements that idempotency guidance for an agent whose next step isn’t predetermined.
The idempotency key from the durable record connects the replacement to the original request. If the replacement retries with the same key, the provider can recognize the same operation rather than processing an independent refund. This holds even if the original agent’s in-flight request completed after the crash, or a worker assumed dead has resumed. AWS’s Builders’ Library formalizes this pattern: a caller-provided identifier recorded atomically with the mutation.
But retrying isn’t always safe. The outcome might stay unclear. Stripe documents that a 500 response on a mutation can still produce external effects. When the outcome is unknown, the replacement needs evidence to investigate.
Langfuse can show the previous agent’s tool invocation: a refund request dispatched with the recorded idempotency key. ClickStack can fill in the operational side: an outbound HTTP request to the payment service followed by a connection failure, narrowing the failure window.
Both are available to the replacement directly. The Langfuse MCP server lets it query the previous agent’s trace by operation ID, and the ClickStack MCP server lets it search service events in the same window. Give the replacement the read tools only. It can narrow down what happened, but the tool boundary still controls what the replacement can do.
Neither trace proves the provider committed the refund. And an absent trace doesn’t prove the request was never sent, since Langfuse transmits traces asynchronously and a crash can prevent delivery. The payment provider remains the system of record for the external outcome. Execution telemetry narrows the investigation. It doesn’t replace authoritative confirmation.
Continue the work; don’t start over
The replacement has the durable record and, where the outcome was unclear, the execution evidence. Now it needs to act, but not by re-deciding what to do.
The replacement follows the recovery protocol the application defines, not its own judgment about the customer’s situation.
If the provider confirms the refund is complete, the replacement records the outcome and moves on. If the provider shows the refund is still pending or in progress, the replacement waits. Retrying would risk a duplicate. If the refund definitively failed with no external effect, the replacement revalidates preconditions before a new authorized attempt. If the outcome remains unclear, it escalates rather than guessing. A missing provider record doesn’t prove the refund was never processed. The provider may not have finalized the transaction.
“A stored approval is historical evidence, not current authority to act.”
Even after establishing the external outcome, the replacement has to verify that the world hasn’t changed. The refundable balance may have shifted. A human representative might have processed a separate refund through a different interface. The customer’s account status may have changed. Someone may have revoked the original authorization.
A stored approval is historical evidence, not current authority to act.
The real engineering question is whether a new agent can establish the work’s current objective, outstanding obligations, and uncertain effects, then continue safely without treating the predecessor’s recollections as authority.
The agent is disposable. The work isn’t.

articles.title: Core Advanced, 20 milliards de paramètres dans 2 Go : un chercheur a mesuré l'IA de macOS 27 qu'Apple n'a jamais documentée — Frandroid
articles.text:
Julien Simon, ancien évangéliste en chef de Hugging Face, a publié le 25 octobre dans sa newsletter The AI Realist une longue enquête sur Core Advanced, le modèle de langage qu’Apple installe avec macOS 27 sur ses Mac les plus récents. Apple n’a publié aucune model card, la fiche qu’un laboratoire publie d’habitude pour décrire son modèle.
Julien Simon en a donc reconstruit une à partir de ses propres mesures, sur un MacBook Pro M3 Max doté de 48 Go de mémoire. D’après ses relevés, un modèle de 20 milliards de paramètres coûte au Mac, en mémoire comme en énergie, à peu près autant qu’un modèle de 4 milliards. Siri n’est d’ailleurs pas le seul à s’en servir : n’importe quel script peut l’interroger dans un terminal (avec la commande fm respond).
Apple a présenté Core Advanced le 8 juin 2026, pendant la WWDC, sur son blog de recherche en apprentissage automatique. C’est le plus gros de ses deux modèles embarqués, dans une famille de cinq modèles « conçus sur mesure en collaboration avec Google ». Il compte 20 milliards de paramètres, mais seuls 1 à 4 milliards travaillent à la fois. Il fait tourner les nouvelles voix expressives de Siri et la dictée.
Apple le réserve aux Mac M3 ou plus récents qui ont au moins 12 Go de mémoire unifiée ; côté mobile, il équipe les iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro et 17 Pro Max, ainsi que les iPad M4 ou plus récents dotés de 12 Go. Sur PC, l’IA locale demande beaucoup plus de matériel, mais pour des modèles qui visent des tâches plus lourdes, comme le code : on a eu besoin d’une machine comme le PC Nvidia RTX Spark pour remplacer ChatGPT pendant un vol de onze heures, et Microsoft parle de jusqu’à 60 Go de RAM pour ses IA hors ligne, voire de 75 Go pour MAI Code 1.1 Flash.
Le modèle reste dans le SSD
Core Advanced repose sur un mélange d’experts (MoE) : chaque couche est découpée en petits réseaux spécialisés, les experts, et seuls quelques-uns calculent à un moment donné. Dans un MoE classique, le choix des experts change à chaque token (un bout de mot), si bien que tous les experts doivent rester en mémoire vive.
Apple explique sur son blog que le transfert entre la mémoire flash et la RAM est trop lent pour ça. Le modèle complet reste donc dans le stockage, et un petit bloc choisit un jeu d’experts en lisant la requête, puis le renouvelle de temps en temps pendant la réponse. Julien Simon a observé ce mécanisme en direct : pendant une réponse, le Mac lit un seul fichier de 4,95 Go par blocs de 294 912 octets, avec une petite salve de lectures toutes les 32 tokens environ.
Les calculs tournent sur le Neural Engine, le bloc de la puce M3 Max dédié à l’IA. Il consommait autour de 4 watts, pendant que la partie graphique (GPU) restait au repos. Pour Julien Simon, ce Neural Engine explique aussi le choix des experts par requête : le Neural Engine exécute des programmes compilés à l’avance, qui supportent mal des experts qui changent à chaque token.
L’expert estime par ailleurs, en partant de la taille des pages chargées en mémoire, que les poids sont compressés à environ 2 bits chacun. Enfin, deux modèles de sécurité de 300 millions de paramètres tournent dans un processus séparé ; d’après leurs noms dans le journal système, ils filtrent les requêtes. Ils occupent 0,7 Go sur les 2 Go mesurés deux secondes après une longue requête, un total qui montait jusqu’à 3,4 Go pendant son traitement.
Pour comparer, Julien Simon a pris Gemma 4 26B A4B, un modèle ouvert de Google qui suit le même principe : 25,2 milliards de paramètres, dont 3,8 milliards actifs, mais avec des experts choisis à chaque token. Compressé à 4 bits, il occupait environ 15 Go deux secondes après une requête identique de 5 000 tokens, soit sept fois plus que Core Advanced et ses modèles de sécurité.
Pour autant, Julien Simon reconnaît lui-même qu’environ la moitié de l’écart vient de la compression, 4 bits d’un côté et environ 2 bits chez Apple. Ces 2 bits par poids restent proches des compressions les plus poussées du moment : PrismML fait tenir une IA de 27 milliards de paramètres, dérivée de Qwen d’Alibaba, dans 5,9 Go, à 1,76 bit par poids. Apple, lui, ne charge en mémoire vive qu’une petite partie de son modèle et laisse le reste dans le SSD.
Le modèle d’Apple paie cette sobriété en mathématiques. Sur 20 problèmes, il a consommé environ un tiers de l’énergie du meilleur modèle ouvert testé, Qwen3 4B d’Alibaba, mais n’en a résolu que 13, contre 20 pour Qwen3. Sur 100 problèmes de niveau scolaire, il en réussit 78, contre 89 à 94 pour les trois modèles ouverts, et finit dernier sur quatre.
Sur 200 questions de culture générale, en revanche, il se place au milieu, avec 67 % de bonnes réponses, devant Gemma 3 4B (59 %) mais derrière Gemma 4 E4B (69,5 %) et Qwen3 4B (72 %). Apple ne s’en cache pas : sa documentation pour les développeurs déconseille de l’utiliser pour les calculs de base, le code et le raisonnement logique. Elle le réserve au résumé, à l’extraction d’entités (noms, dates, lieux) ou à l’écriture créative.
Apple avait promis sur son blog un rapport technique pour cet été. Au 25 octobre, il n’était toujours pas publié.

articles.title: AI safety expert stops saving for retirement, he believes AI could wipe out humanity within a decade
articles.text:
Crystal ball: Worried about the increasing likelihood that an AI will go rogue and kill us all? It's a depressing thought, but one AI safety leader is looking on the positive side: his concern that the technology will bring about mass extinction in the next decade has led him to stop saving for retirement.
Nate Soares, the president of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI), revealed his pessimistic choice to The Atlantic CEO Nicholas Thompson in a recent interview for the latter's The Most Interesting Thing in AI series.
"I do not save for retirement right now. I have a 401(k) from when I worked at Google, but I haven't contributed for a decade," Soares said.
Apocalyptic warnings about AI are a dime a dozen, but they hit a lot harder when one comes from an expert in the field. Soares has spent 12 years working on AI alignment. Before joining MIRI, a non-profit focused on AI risks, he was an engineer at Google and Microsoft. He also authored a book called, worryingly, If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies.
The problem, in Soares' words, isn't that a superintelligent AI would hate us. It's that it wouldn't particularly care whether we lived or died. Humans could become obstacles to whatever goals it develops, especially if we try to shut it down or build a competing system. It's a warning that other AI experts have also expressed.
"From my perspective, the real question is not how does it kill us? It's how does it become self-sufficient?"
For now, AI still needs us to keep the lights on and the chips coming. Once it can run its own automated economy, that dependency disappears. We might be deliberately eliminated, or simply die as the machines reshape the planet to suit themselves. Neither outcome sounds especially retirement-friendly.
Soares is less certain about the precise route to disaster. He compares it to facing chess champion Magnus Carlsen: you don't need to know which piece will deliver checkmate to suspect you're in trouble.
But he insists there's still an alternative to waiting for the end.
"I don't think it's inevitable. I think we could absolutely still stop this race to the very dangerous sort of AI," Soares said. But his decision not to save for retirement suggests he expects the worst.
The potential existential threat posed by AI has made plenty of headlines in recent times. Following the many incidents of AI agents hacking other companies without being instructed to do so, an Anthropic researcher resigned with a warning that the technology could end the human race.
In 2025, Geoffrey Hinton, one of the so-called Godfathers of AI, said there was a 10% to 20% chance AI could seize control, agreeing with a prediction first made by Elon Musk.

articles.title: VCs will make billions on Anthropic's IPO, but Amazon is set to make much (much) more | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Many investors stand to win big when Anthropic goes public. Stakes held by firms including Menlo Ventures, Sequoia, Sound Ventures, and Spark Capital are expected to return billions.
Yet according to Anthropic’s S-1, none of those VC firms owns 5%, the threshold for being included in the principal stockholders’ table. That’s highly unusual. In a typical tech IPO, lead venture investors hold double-digit-percentage stakes in the startups they backed. The reason is Anthropic’s size. At its $965 billion private valuation, a 1% stake is worth nearly $10 billion, so, for example, Menlo’s roughly $14 billion position is only about 1.5% of the company, according to recently reported Bloomberg figures.
While the venture firms may lack sizable percentage stakes, Anthropic sold large stakes to strategic partners, companies that are also its business partners. Indeed, Amazon is likely the single largest financial beneficiary of the IPO.
Amazon first backed Anthropic in 2023 with a commitment to invest up to $4 billion in the AI company. Since then, Amazon has poured billions more into Anthropic. Instead of taking stock upfront, Amazon structured much of its investment as convertible notes, a type of debt that converts into shares upon an IPO or sale.
According to the S-1, Amazon holds convertible notes with $6.2 billion in principal outstanding as of June 30. That is Anthropic’s entire debt load. But as Anthropic’s valuation soared across successive funding rounds, the shares those notes will convert into became far more valuable. Amazon’s own filings valued its note holdings at $97.9 billion as of June 30.
As the value of Amazon’s convertible notes surged, Anthropic had to record the growing value of what it owes on its books. It reported the adjustments on its income statement under “change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs,” a line that totaled $72.4 billion for the first half of 2026. The charge is non-cash, meaning no money left the company.
Amazon’s notes could convert into as many as 1.84 billion shares, according to the S-1. But a cap limits Amazon to 12% of Anthropic’s “partially diluted” share count, a figure that counts some shares not yet issued, such as stock options. Amazon can waive the cap. Notes that can’t convert will stay outstanding and convert in later quarters, subject to the same limit.
But the notes are only part of Amazon’s holdings. It further invested $10 billion in nonvoting preferred stock (a type of equity), in the second quarter, according to Amazon’s quarterly report for the period ended June 30. Amazon did this by investing $5 billion in each of Anthropic’s last two funding rounds. Combined with the $8 billion it invested in the notes from 2023 through 2025, that brings Amazon’s total investment to about $18 billion.
Beyond its stock gains, Amazon will also continue to earn significant revenue from Anthropic, which has committed to spend at least $110 billion on AWS over the next 10 years.
Google, too, is set for a major windfall from both the listing and its cloud computing deals with Anthropic. The search giant held about 14% of Anthropic as of early last year, according to court filings that were reported by The New York Times, and has invested more since, including $10 billion in April. (Google was likely diluted in subsequent and massive funding rounds, with PitchBook analyst Harrison Rolfes telling TechCrunch he estimates its current stake at closer to 5.6%.) It has also secured at least $114 billion in cloud commitments from the Anthropic through 2033.
While VCs set for massive paydays have little reason to complain, the S-1 makes it clear that the biggest winners of Anthropic’s IPO may well be tech giants like Amazon, which backed a would-be rival early on and now sell it much of the computing power it runs on.
The S-1 itself warns that some of those cloud providers also build rival AI models and that they may not always want the same things that Anthropic does.

articles.title: Galaxy Watch Ultra para esportistas alcança mais de R$ 3 mil OFF na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Watch Ultra para esportistas alcança mais de R$ 3 mil OFF na Amazon
Galaxy Watch Ultra possui corpo de titânio resistente para aventuras; smartwatch da Samsung recebe desconto de 64% sobre o preço original em promoção no Pix
O Galaxy Watch Ultra LTE de 47 mm está saindo por apenas R$ 1.799 no Pix na Amazon. O smartwatch da Samsung lançado em 2025, com sensores que suportam diversas atividades esportivas e corpo de titânio, recebe desconto de 64% sobre o preço original de R$ 4.999.
Um dos melhores smartwatches do mercado, o Galaxy Watch Ultra possui o mesmo kit de sensores do novo Ultra 2 e oferece suporte a diversas modalidades esportivas, como corrida e ciclismo. Ele também conta com funções de saúde, como eletrocardiograma (ECG), monitores do sono e da oxigenação do sangue.
Seu corpo em titânio resistente de 47 mm é reforçado pelas certificações IP68 e militar MIL-STD-810H e resiste a até 10 atmosferas de pressão (10 ATM). Portanto, o smartwatch pode ser usado em atividades de água rasa, como natação. Além disso, ele ainda resiste a altas temperaturas.
O suporte ao 4G/LTE torna este wearable uma ferramenta importante em situações de risco. No caso de uma emergência médica, ele pode disparar alertas para contatos pré-programados e ligar para números como 190 (polícia) e 192 (bombeiros) sem depender de um celular, podendo assim salvar a vida do usuário.
A tela Super AMOLED de 1,5″ do Watch Ultra possui brilho de até 3.000 nits, sendo capaz de reproduzir imagens com cores vibrantes e visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar. O vidro Cristal de Safira protege o display contra arranhões, pancadas e quedas.
Seu chip Exynos W1000, combinado a 2 GB de RAM e 64 GB de espaço interno, permite que o gadget instale e rode apps localmente. Sua bateria de 590 mAh tem autonomia de até 100 horas de uso no modo economia de energia, segundo a fabricante, resistindo por um dia inteiro sem descarregar.
O Galaxy Watch Ultra de 47 mm (apenas R$ 1.799 no Pix) suporta redes Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.3, o já mencionado 4G/LTE e GPS multibanda, que determina a posição do usuário em tempo real, recurso essencial para a prática de esportes e outras aventuras.

articles.title: Cuántos Balones de Oro tiene Harry Kane, cómo se llama su esposa y más preguntas de Google del capitán inglés
articles.text:
Harry Kane, capitán de Inglaterra, ganó el Balón de Oro 2026 y el premio impulsó las búsquedas sobre el deportista en Google. Entre las consultas que registró Google Trends aparecieron preguntas sobre la cantidad de galardones que obtuvo, su edad y su esposa, Kate Kane.
El jugador del Bayern Múnich recibió el premio por primera vez el 26 de octubre, durante la ceremonia celebrada en Londres. Kane, de 33 años, se impuso a Kylian Mbappé y Lamine Yamal en la votación por el reconocimiento individual.
En España, el interés de búsqueda por Harry Kane fue mayor en Melilla, con un índice de 100, seguida por Canarias, Cataluña, Ceuta y la Comunidad de Madrid.
En México, las consultas asociadas combinaron el nombre del inglés con términos como “qué ganó Harry Kane”, “cuántos Balones de Oro tiene Harry Kane” y “esposa Harry Kane”, además de referencias a Alexia Putellas y Charlyn Corral, ganadoras de otros premios en la ceremonia.
Qué pregunta la gente sobre Harry Kane en Google
Una de las preguntas que más se repitió fue si Harry Kane ganó el Balón de Oro 2026 y qué premio recibió. El delantero inglés ganó el Balón de Oro masculino, el principal reconocimiento individual de la gala.
Otra consulta fue cuántos Balones de Oro tiene Harry Kane. La respuesta es uno: el de 2026 fue el primer Balón de Oro de su carrera. Con ese logro, se convirtió en el primer futbolista inglés en ganar el premio desde Michael Owen, en 2001.
Los usuarios también buscaron la edad de Kane y quién es su esposa. El capitán de Inglaterra tiene 33 años y está casado con Kate Kane, cuyo nombre de soltera es Kate Goodland. La pareja se conoce desde la infancia y contrajo matrimonio en 2019.
Durante su discurso, Kane agradeció a sus familiares, a sus compañeros y a los entrenadores que lo acompañaron en su carrera. También le dedicó unas palabras a Kate, a quien definió como su mejor amiga y su mayor apoyo, y destacó los sacrificios que hizo para acompañarlo en el camino hacia el premio.
Qué es Google Trends
Google Trends es una herramienta de Google que permite observar el interés de búsqueda de una palabra, una persona o un tema a lo largo del tiempo y según la ubicación geográfica de los usuarios.
La plataforma no muestra el número absoluto de búsquedas. En cambio, presenta un índice normalizado de cero a 100: el valor 100 representa el punto de mayor interés relativo dentro del período y el lugar seleccionados.
Por eso, que Melilla registre un índice de 100 para Harry Kane no significa que haya acumulado más búsquedas totales que otras regiones de España.
Indica que, en relación con el total de consultas realizadas allí, fue el territorio con mayor interés proporcional por el futbolista.
Google Trends también identifica temas y consultas relacionadas que están en ascenso. En el caso de Kane, esas búsquedas reflejaron la curiosidad de los usuarios por su triunfo en el Balón de Oro, su trayectoria y su vida familiar.
Alexia Putellas y Charlyn Corral, también ganadoras de la jornada
Alexia Putellas y Charlyn Corral fueron dos de las protagonistas de la ceremonia del Balón de Oro 2026, celebrada en Londres. La española ganó el Balón de Oro femenino por tercera vez, tras imponerse en una edición que volvió a reconocer su influencia con la selección de España y el Barcelona.
La mexicana Charlyn Corral, por su parte, recibió el premio a la mejor delantera del año. La atacante de Pachuca fue distinguida durante una gala en la que también se premió a Harry Kane como mejor jugador masculino.
El reconocimiento a Corral llevó su nombre a las búsquedas vinculadas con la ceremonia en México, según Google Trends. Putellas también apareció entre los temas y consultas relacionadas en España y México, donde los usuarios buscaron información sobre sus premios y trayectoria.

articles.title: Dell ties supply chain security to agentic AI risks - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Dell links supply chain security to the challenges of agentic AI
Supply chain security is taking on new importance as enterprises bring AI into core business operations. Those deployments introduce risks that require security teams to examine how infrastructure, data and autonomous systems are protected.
As AI agents gain the ability to act on their own, executives need to rethink where risk lives and who controls it. Dell Technologies Inc. has made AI factory security a central part of that conversation, according to Kamlesh Shah (pictured, right), director of product management, Dell AI Factory Solutions, at Dell.
“With the speed and scale at which the AI systems are growing, the enterprise needs to be ready to be able to actually act at [that] speed and scale,” he said. “And it doesn’t happen overnight.”
Shah and Ash Lakshmanan (left), director of product management, Dell Services, at Dell, spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante for the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how enterprises can secure agentic AI and why legacy tools miss agent identities. (* Disclosure below.)
Supply chain security anchors a layered AI defense
Many of the controls Dell recommends are familiar to security teams. Dell’s approach begins with supply chain security, vetting suppliers before a product is even envisioned and extending protection across the full life cycle of a deployment, according to Shah. Dell has offered those capabilities through the Dell AI Factory while also running them in its own internal IT operations, he noted.
“Dell’s experience in the AI infrastructure as a provider and a very large-scale AI user has created a model that the customers can look at and replicate,” he said. “The goal is to turn these deployment lessons into repeatable patterns … rather than reinvent the control.”
Agents change the threat model because they do more than answer questions. Given a goal, an agent can take multiple steps, find and use tools, call systems of record and communicate with other agents, which makes its behavior less predictable, Shah explained. That puts boundaries at the center: policy enforcement checks, runtime sandboxing and telemetry that records who authorized what.
“The agent itself should have the ability and identity that’s tied to a particular workload, not a broad-based permission to work on all applications,” he said. “The layer at which the agent needs to operate is really delegated, narrowly scoped permissions. Time-based.”
Once customers choose an architecture, Dell Services helps them turn a promising use case into an environment they can operate, govern and iterate on, according to Lakshmanan. That work covers security across a four-layer stack spanning hardware, runtime, data and applications. The piece customers most often underestimate is observability across all four layers, he noted.
“Your old tools just cannot look at AI workloads. Your old tools that could look at human identities and possibly machine identities cannot look at agent identities,” he said.
Some customers that ran Dell’s penetration testing services against chatbots they planned to release learned the bots weren’t ready and could have been exploited by a hacker, Lakshmanan noted. Dell is also working with Nvidia Corp. to bring agentic AI from the deskside to the data center.
“We need new tools, platforms and skills to tackle this,” he said. “But the foundational elements of security have not gone away, which is the layered security approach we talked about. You still need to narrow your attack surface. You still need 24/7 continuous observability, and you need to be prepared as if a breach could happen.”

articles.title: "AI threats are real - it's not some kind of urban myth": Microsoft UK security head on why your business should be prepared for a new generation of AI cyber threats
articles.text:
"AI threats are real - it's not some kind of urban myth": Microsoft UK security head on why your business should be prepared for a new generation of AI cyber threats
Security is everyone’s problem now, Microsoft warns
As AI becomes an increasingly important part of our everyday lives, the role it plays in cybersecurity for both attackers and defenders is coming under rising scrutiny.
Microsoft recently released its Digital Defense Report (DDR) highlighting the role that AI is playing in crafting new and more devious cyberattacks, with businesses being hit with more threats than ever before.
But Microsoft is also using its own AI tools such a Copilot to help support its digital crimes unit, showing that the attackers won’t have all the advantages.
At the recent Microsoft Frontier Tour London event, I spoke to Dr Jon Davies, Chief Security Adviser, Microsoft UK, to find out more.
AI threats are here
“Frontier AI is transforming the threat landscape,” Davies tells me. “Right now, AI threats are real, it's not an urban myth, or something we're going to see in 2030.”
The DDR found that as AI becomes more widely available, the barrier of entry into cybercrime is being lowered, allowing hackers to launch a record number of campaigns against consumers and businesses alike.
The UK was particularly affected, becoming the most targeted country for nation-state and geopolitical cyber activity in Europe, facing 76 observed events in the past year, and ranking fifth in the world for countries where customers are most frequently impacted by cyber threats.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Davies notes that the AI threat has been building for a while, as attackers turn to automation to carry out more advanced attacks - with so-called “swarm attacks" becoming particularly more common as attackers get agents to do their dirty work
“We're getting to the point where the technology, compute, and storage is catching up with the ambition of the attacker,” he says, pointing out that defenders are embracing AI too.
“We've been solving one problem at a time as (threats) have evolved,” he adds, “the opportunity with agentic AI is to elevate the human up into the orchestration.”
But despite all the AI intelligence being funneled into creating new and more complicated attacks, more “basic” forms of scam like phishing are still proving incredibly effective, showing that the human will always remain the weakest link when it comes to cybersecurity.
The DDR found phishing attacks jumped globally from 7% to 23% of incident-response intrusions year-over-year, with attacks using fake meeting invites and calendar markers among the scams on the rise, and Davies highlights how criminals are taking information gathering on specific C-suite individuals to a new high in order to get them to click on a link.
“An attacker has no ethical line,” he points out, “phishing…is still the front door for any organization…(and) I don't think it's going to go away - with AI on its side, it's only going to get more real and harder to detect.”
So where does the responsibility lie when it comes to awareness? Davies says it should be a combination of individual and collective culpability - which means those annoying phishing tests your employer sends you are probably here to stay.
“The whole point of those training exercises is to help educate us, show us what the attackers are doing…I don’t think we should be embarrassed if we’ve clicked a link in one of those exercises, as the point is to educate and train.”
“It’s everyone’s responsibility to put a seat belt on, you are accountable to it, and regardless of who you are in your personal life, you are responsible for cybersecurity. We’re at that step change now where it’s not just the cybersecurity teams responsible for security - it is everyone within the organization.”
Davies notes that “security can be the seatbelt for AI transformation,” likening it to the introduction of the seatbelt in cars - as although they worked from day one, it still took some time to catch on.
“Security is the same way for enterprises - we can buckle up,” he adds, noting that the seatbelt doesn’t slow the car down, and eventually the change happened, making seatbelts (and safety overall) a key reason why we might buy a specific car.
So with the huge amount of threats facing cybersecurity defenders on a daily basis, how can security professionals stay positive?
“It’s really tough,” Davies says, “the threat landscape is evolving extremely, extremely fast at the moment. It has to be embedded from top to bottom - from the board level downwards through the C-suite and down to the employees - but it also then needs to be trained up from frontline staff.”
He adds that given the number of widespread cybersecurity stories hitting the headlines these days, more and more C-suite executives are becoming aware of the need to stay protected - and challenging their CISO about what they plan to do about it, and how they can recover if the worst happens.
“We’re having these conversations quite regularly,” he says, “as a member of the security profession, we’ve asked for a seat at the table for a number of years - and we’ve finally got that.”
Davies points out that the DDR isn’t just a commercial or PR exercise - it is Microsoft’s view from the front lines of the battle against the latest cybersecurity threats.
“We’ve got skin in the game,” he says, “there is no other organization on the planet that can do this at that level, it’s giving back what we’re able to share to help organizations measure their risk and threat.”
“The physics of cyber are changing,” he concludes, “we’ve got variables that we can change - but they (attackers) also have variables they can change on their side…it's a scary place out there...the world that we're living in right now is very dynamic.”

articles.title: Hacker awarded $50k bounty for reporting bug to Sony that allowed PS5 Linux exploit — move sparks backlash from jailbreaking community
articles.text:
Hacker awarded $50k bounty for reporting bug to Sony that allowed PS5 Linux exploit — move sparks backlash from jailbreaking community
The security researcher who originally discovered the hypervisor bug held off reporting it to Sony, intending to disclose it only after the launch of GTA VI.
A hacker used an AI LLM to find a hypervisor bug that allowed security researchers to load Linux on PlayStation 5 consoles, subsequently reported it to Sony, and received a $50,000 bug bounty. IGN reports that the person who discovered the flaw, who goes by Jordy on X, shared the award on the social media platform, drawing significant ire. The biggest driver of the criticism, though, is that Jordy agreed to delay the report until after the launch of GTA VI, but moved forward anyway after someone else discovered the flaw, meaning it would be patched prior to the launch of the game, and possibly denying someone else the payday.
“I can at least buy GTA 6 with this, I think,” Jordy said on their X account. One user called Gille replied to their post, saying, “50k in bank but 0 friends left. Worth it?” Another one named Darth Riker commented, “You did not ‘find this bug yourself’. The flow0 (Andy Nguyen) did that. You, however, didn’t. You’re just a lazy s****** who’s no different to those scammers out there,” while Matthew Cramer added, “The worst thing is not the money grab, it’s the fact that the whole point of exploiting PS5 is freedom, ownership, and control. Sony goes against everything we stand for! If Jordy was in need of money, there are hundreds of bug bounty programs with high paydays… or a better job!”
The ps5-linux-loader GitHub project requires a PS5 Phat, Slim, or Pro running firmware version 3.00 to 13.60 to work as intended. While it’s unclear if Sony had been aware of the flaw that allowed the Linux install on the console before Jordy’s report, it released firmware version 14.20 on Oct. 21, 2026, which patched the flaw. Because the latest games often require the latest firmware on the console before you can install them, the latest update means that users who are experimenting with running Linux on their PlayStation 5 would either have to pick between that and playing GTA VI on launch date.
Another thing that caught the ire of many jailbreaking fans is Jordy’s use of AI. Despite being a useful tool for discovering vulnerabilities when used by professionals, it has also overwhelmed several bug bounty programs with AI submissions. This includes Google, which has frozen its program until 2027, and Linus Torvalds, who switched to a public system as the Linux security mailing list has become “almost entirely unmanageable,” with AI bug hunters finding as many as 2,000 CVEs per release.
“I am stepping away from the PS5 scene and stopping all my work on PS5 Linux. After pouring my heart and months of my life into it, including plans to finish PS5 Pro support and release in 2027, it’s all down the sink,” Nguyen posted on X. He also added, “The scene used to be a group of highly talented researchers, but now it is just a bunch of noobs using LLMs and writing hacks they don’t even understand. Slop kiddies found the only hypervisor bug left, which I had also found a while ago, and decided to report to Sony.”
Jordy told the publication that they agreed with Nguyen to delay the bug report, with the latter asking to only do so after GTA 6 has come out. However, the former admitted to doing it anyway as other researchers using generative AI also found the bug, with Jordy risking losing the $50,000 bounty if somebody else reports the exploit. “I decided I would report it,” Jordy told IGN. “If I and another person can find it with LLM, so can someone else.”
Sony’s PlayStation 5 has been the focus of hacks, emulators, and jailbreaking recently, especially after the company announced that it will end physical game disc production by January 2028. Despite the pushback against this decision, Sony has doubled down on its move and even threatened to cut off customer support and take legal action against harassment from disgruntled customers. This, combined with Jordy’s use of AI and X post sharing the $50,000 award, is what drove the ire of many in the PS5 jailbreaking scene.
