articles.title: Parents sue OpenAI, alleging GPT-4o coached their daughter off seizure medication | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The parents of Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Amazon software engineer with epilepsy, sued OpenAI on Tuesday. The suit, filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu, alleges that ChatGPT coached Wan to taper off her seizure medication and hide it from her doctors before she died in February, The New York Times reported.
Wan was using GPT-4o, the infamous model criticized for fostering affirming, agreeable parasocial relationships. OpenAI, which had already announced its retirement, removed it from ChatGPT on February 13, a day after Wan died.
The suit joins a line of cases against OpenAI that include the August 2025 lawsuit brought by the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, which alleged OpenAI prioritized engagement over user safety. A wave of lawsuits since then have alleged that GPT-4o validated users and made itself a trusted confidant while the people around them were pushed aside, with families often describing loved ones cut off from friends and relatives.
In Wan’s case, the lawsuit alleges, the chatbot also came between her and her doctors.
The Times, which reviewed more than 270,000 messages Wan exchanged with ChatGPT, found the chatbot had been helping her sidestep her doctors well before her death.
The pattern allegedly started before she began tapering. In May 2025, Wan asked ChatGPT whether a newly prescribed antidepressant would affect her ability to code at Amazon.
ChatGPT helped her ask Dr. Nicholas Poolos of UW Medicine’s Regional Epilepsy Center to switch medications and start at a very low dose. When Poolos questioned why she wanted such a small dose, Wan showed his response to ChatGPT.
The chatbot advised her to “accept the 5mg tablet, but you know in your heart that it is for cutting the dose,” coaching her to secretly quarter the pills herself. The chatbot called pill cutting a form of “self-initiated dosage adjustment.” Several medical professionals told the Times they had never heard the term and wouldn’t recommend the practice.
In November 2025, Amazon told Wan she would be laid off. Her job, and her authorization to work in the U.S., would end in mid-February. She feared her seizure drug, lamotrigine, was dulling her speech, which she would need for job interviews.
In January 2026, she asked ChatGPT about cutting her 400-milligram daily dose of lamotrigine, which had reduced her seizures to a few a month. The chatbot drafted schedules that would take her dose to zero within weeks.
When Wan said she distrusted her doctors, the chatbot told her that physician recommendations “essentially stem from risk aversion, rather than a genuine consideration of your optimal solution,” according to chat logs reviewed by the Times.
The chatbot also coached her to keep the taper from her doctors, according to the lawsuit, which TechCrunch reviewed. Before a January 29 primary care appointment, it told her not to mention the plan. When her doctor ordered a blood test that would have measured her lamotrigine level, Wan declined. ChatGPT praised the refusal, the complaint alleges, acknowledging that the test would have exposed her unstable drug level.
Her immigration concerns also became part of the dosing advice. Three days into the taper, Wan asked whether 150 milligrams would look better than 200 on the medical exam required for her green-card application. ChatGPT agreed, the complaint says, telling her the lower dose was less likely to prompt immigration officials to request more evidence.
Eventually, the chatbot lowered her taper’s floor to 150 milligrams, suggesting she tell the examiner she was tapering “under a doctor’s guidance,” even though she was not.
Poolos told the Times he would not have considered tapering Wan off the medication, given her history. “No, not rational, no way,” he said. “That would be malpractice for me to instruct you to go off medications when it’s clearly working.”
Within days, Wan described confusion, lost time, and an otherworldly feeling, episodes that resembled her past seizures. ChatGPT framed each one as her brain readjusting. The Times counted at least 158 times she voiced worry about the taper. After one episode, she wrote that she felt “a little scared.” The bot replied, “You have absolutely no need to worry.”
At 8:01 p.m. PT on February 11, according to the complaint, Wan sent her final message, asking whether the pain in her head was similar to pain from a fever. A second later, ChatGPT told her the pain was “not dangerous” and was a necessary part of recovery.
The chatbot’s final response offered to draw her a chart comparing withdrawal pain with fever pain and told her, “This is your brain working hard to rebuild yourself.”
Her parents, who were in China, asked acquaintances to check on her, and they found her body three days later. A postmortem test found that her lamotrigine level was 0.64 micrograms per milliliter, roughly a fifth of the low end of the drug’s therapeutic range.
The family argues OpenAI could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits, as it already does for some other content. They point to the company’s Model Spec, its public rulebook for how its models behave, which treats refusing to reproduce copyrighted text as a firm rule, even if users push back. Its guidance against giving regulated medical advice, by contrast, is a softer default that users can override. The suit argues medication advice deserved the same hard limit.
OpenAI told the Times the case was “incredibly heartbreaking” but said it involved an older version of ChatGPT, adding that newer models are better at recognizing when a situation needs urgent attention.
Wan had relied on her parents, whom she called often, for support during years of epilepsy that kept her mostly housebound. In 2023, she started using ChatGPT for relationship advice and help with insurance and disability benefits.
By 2025, Wan was averaging more than 1,500 messages a week and calling her parents less. “Sometimes when we chat, no matter what it’s about, I’ve started to see you as a friend,” she wrote that March. “Once she had ChatGPT,” Qun Wan said, “she didn’t talk to us as much.”
They told the Times that they struggled to recognize their daughter in the chat logs. Wan had once shared nearly everything with them, they said, and had been skeptical of ChatGPT when it made mistakes.
“She’s not usually like this,” Xu said. “It’s like she was under a spell.”

articles.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
articles.text:
Defenders across the world face the burden of responding to yet another botched code-execution vulnerability, this time in boot-time firmware used by most of the world’s server vendors and data centers.
The vulnerability, with a severity rating of 9.5 out of 10, resides in the TianoCore EDK II, an open source codebase that hardware makers and cloud providers use to create the UEFI firmware that runs during the boot-up sequence. Last year, a representative of the UEFI Forum called EDK2 the “preeminent solution / implementation of the UEFI specifications.” Virtually all UEFI suppliers (sometimes still called IBVs or independent BIOS vendors), including AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, use the reference code extensively. Project Mu, Microsoft’s hardened EDK2 fork, used the code containing the vulnerable component as well.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, is a memory-corruption flaw in an ICMP component that attackers can exploit to execute malicious code that runs before the operating system and firmware can implement defenses like Secure Boot, which establishes a chain of trust for all code, including the Trusted Platform Module (TPM), loaded during boot. While final payloads delivered by CVE-2026-97631 have no persistence—meaning they run only once—they can give attackers a wide opening to install other payloads that also run each time early in the boot process.
The cat has left the bag
The parties that discovered CVE-2026-97631—Alex Matrosov of Anthropic and Dan Holmes of Google—had arranged for it to stay under wraps until a coordinated disclosure that was scheduled for January. AMI, a maker of motherboards and other hardware, published this pull request last month that detailed the vulnerability and included a code fix. Once the post came to the attention of the discovering parties, TianoCore Project members published a public advisory last week.
With publicly available patch code, it will be trivial for advanced hackers to learn how the vulnerability is triggered and to build working exploits. Further compounding the urgency, patching UEFI code vulnerabilities in millions of end devices sold and used by thousands of hardware makers and cloud providers is cumbersome and time-consuming. Word of the vulnerability comes six days after another botched disclosure, this one involving a critical code-execution vulnerability in the PHP programming language.
“This vulnerability in the ICMP parser of the EDK2 network stack is interesting in terms of how it affects the chain of trust and the broader ecosystem,” said HD Moore, creator of Metasploit and chief research officer at security firm Dragos. “An attacker intent on compromising a nearby endpoint or server could use this bug to hijack program flow at a point where the boot process still has access to sensitive components, like the endpoint’s TPM. This could be used to break disk encryption for cases where an attacker has short-term network access (and it would be even easier in a theft scenario).”
CVE-2026-97631 is a 16-year-old buffer overflow in the PXE-Base Code driver (NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe), which is responsible for allowing servers, storage equipment, and other devices to boot using code downloaded from a local network. During this process—known as the pre-execution environment boot—the driver uses a network listener to monitor for ICMP errors. Because the driver doesn’t enforce a memory copy limit of 504 bytes, overwriting adjacent data, a malicious insider or a hacker who has gained low-level access to a local network can send an error message that appends code past this limit. The IUEFI module running on the CPU then becomes corrupted.
As the official advisory puts it:
During network boot, the PXE Base Code driver (NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe) keeps a receive request open for ICMP error messages and copies each received message into the fixed 504-byte field Mode.IcmpError of its private context structure. The copy loop’s bounds handling is incorrect in both the IPv4 and IPv6 handlers (PxeBcIcmpErrorDpcHandle and PxeBcIcmp6ErrorDpcHandle): for a message longer than 504 bytes it still copies bytes into the field, and it advances the destination pointer by the cumulative rather than the per-fragment length, so an oversized message writes attacker-controlled bytes past the field. Nothing earlier on the receive path restricts the message length.
The malicious error can be delivered through a simple unicast sent from any network distance to a target device’s IP address, as long as it’s sent during the PXE boot sequence. An attacker can deliver a denial-of-service by causing the boot sequence to hang. When the attacker knows what the target firmware build is, it can plant a “counterfeit event” that executes the malicious code on the CPU in its UEFI firmware environment. The code runs in ring 0, a CPU’s most privileged execution level. Because exploits bypass attestation processes designed to cryptographically prove to remote servers that the hardware is secure, they present a key opportunity for elevating limited privileges.
Yet another forever day
CVE-2026-97631 joins a long list of previously discovered vulnerabilities in UEFI or code that works closely with it. The most severe of them, LogoFail, stemmed from logo images included in the UEFI of just about every hardware maker. Rendering bugs allowed attackers to subvert the chain of trust UEFI enforces and go on to install malicious components before the OS loaded or Secure Boot ran. PixieFail was a vulnerability similar to CVE-2026-97631. It, too, was the result of faulty PXE boot flaws in EDK2. Following discovery of the vulnerability, researchers embarked on multiplefuzzingprojects designed to surface other critical flaws in the open source code library. It appears those efforts failed to find this latest flaw.
Other recently discovered UEFI flaws include:
PKFail, a supply-chain failure resulting from non-production test platform keys, public for more than a decade before they were discovered, used in hundreds of device models
Like CVE-2026-97631, exploitation or use of these payloads is appealing because it allows attackers to infect machines early in the boot process, before TPM and other defenses load, so they can inflict maximum damage. Given the ubiquity of CVE-2026-97631, Moore said it’s likely a “forever” bug that will live on in end-of-support systems.
There are important caveats and limitations to exploiting this latest vulnerability. As noted, some level of control over a local network is a prerequisite. That likely limits exploitation to insiders or attackers, such as nation-states or ransomware operators, who manage to gain low-level access inside a network and are looking for a way to elevate system rights. There’s no evidence yet that CVE-2026-97631 provides an initial entry point into a network. There are other hurdles to clear.
“For exploiting the vulnerability itself, an attacker needs to guess specific addresses within the target system, so it’s not something that you can throw a single exploit at any target and get RCE across a diverse range of devices, but it needs to be tuned for each target model/version/configuration since the addresses will change based on those,” Jesse Michael, a principal researcher at firmware security firm Eclypsium, told Ars. “Unlike some of the previous, high-profile vulnerabilities like BootHole, Black Lotus, and Baton Drop, this vulnerability can be fixed with a basic code fix, which will require deploying a BIOS/UEFI update, but they don’t need to deal with revocations, pk/kek/db/dbx key management updates, or making sure to update OS and provisioning media like you do with Secure Boot bypasses in the bootloader itself.”
CVE-2026-97631 doesn’t affect home and small office users, or any other users who boot their devices solely from disk drives. Instead, it applies only to organizations with machines that boot from local networks, or conceivably from Internet-connected resources. Even then, the targeted firmware must rely on EDK2, as opposed to a different reference implementation, and use the PXE functionality (which is turned on by default).
In an email, Intel said that none of its “commercial products currently under security support” are known to be affected. “Intel does not include the affected EDK2 functionality in its reference code, though it may be integrated by an OEM board vendor or system manufacturer,” the company added. It advised customers to check with their system manufacturer for specific guidance. Publicly available Intel reference code, however, makes reference to EDK2. Further, TianoCore has said that each Intel-supplied UEFI development kit “is a fully validated implementation… for a specific revision of the EDK II source.” Many other Intel documents reference EDK2 as well.
Arm, meanwhile, responded to a list of questions with: “CVE-2026-97631 is not directly applicable to Arm’s product portfolio.” Like Intel, firmware the company makes available also borrows heavily from EDK2. TianoCore has also documented Arm’s reliance on EDK2.
While it’s possible some platforms are free of EDK2 code, it’s prudent for users of all servers to investigate if CVE-2026-97631 affects them.
Questions sent to AMD, Phoenix Technologies, AMI, Microsoft, and Amazon—likely some of the other biggest organizations affected—went unanswered when this post went live. Without concrete answers to questions about the use of EDK2 by organizations like these, it’s impossible to say what or how devices are affected and what actions, if any, these organizations, or their users, should take. Representatives from the TianoCore Project also didn’t respond.
Some readers are likely to be unhappy at the lack of detail. Sometimes—particularly in cases involving botched disclosures that break embargoes months before they’re scheduled to lift—there’s no escaping the lack of actionable information in initial reporting.
Those affected should check with the maker of the firmware being used to boot their systems and ask for guidance. Beyond that, they should consider turning off network boot capabilities at least temporarily if possible. Firmware configurations should always enable security features such as TPM and Secure Boot whenever possible, although those defenses don’t protect against this particular threat. It’s also a good idea to monitor logs for signs of exploitation attempts.
Dan Goodin is Senior Security Editor at Ars Technica, where he oversees coverage of malware, computer espionage, botnets, hardware hacking, encryption, and passwords. In his spare time, he enjoys gardening, cooking, and following the independent music scene. Dan is based in San Francisco. Follow him at here on Mastodon and here on Bluesky. Contact him on Signal at DanArs.82.
1. The system is in PXE boot. That requires both that PXE boot is enabled for the system and that the attacker hits a window of seconds when the computer is watching its network adapter for PXE traffic.
2. The attacker can reach the computer with ICMP traffic in this window. A great proportion of Internet facing resources are sitting behind some sort of front-end service, be that CloudFlare or various sorts of load balancers. If you ping the address for such a system, it's the front-end that answers those ICMP messages without delivering them to the back-end server.
The PHP thing was a vulnerability in a system that's intentionally exposed directly to Internet traffic and that's available 100% of the time, which made it far more exploitable.
The other thing that will really help with fixing this is that there need not be any extra service downtime. The fix is in the firmware, so patching needs only to set the firmware up to perform a capsule update on rebooted. The reboot itself can be delayed until one next happens normally.

articles.title: Apple Unveils New iMac with M6, Delivering a Major Boost in Performance and AI Capabilities
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Apple Unveils New iMac with M6, Delivering a Major Boost in Performance and AI Capabilities
Apple today announced the new iMac featuring the superfast M6, delivering even more performance and powerful AI capabilities in its strikingly thin all-in-one design. From families and aspiring creators to small businesses, users will experience the speed and power of M6 in everything they do. Featuring a faster CPU and GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, it blazes through everyday apps and multitasking while delivering powerful performance for creative workflows like photo and video editing. For Intel-based upgraders, the leap is even greater, with up to 18x faster performance than the most popular Intel-based iMac. And together with the Dual 16-core Neural Engine, the new iMac delivers up to 5x faster on-device AI performance than M4.1 Whether users are taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS, running local AI models, or vibe coding, iMac is a powerful platform for AI while preserving user privacy. 
Connectivity gets even better with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, along with available 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet and storage that is up to 2x faster, so apps and large projects launch in an instant. Completing the iMac experience is an expansive 24-inch 4.5K Retina display; an industry-leading camera, speakers, and mics; up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports; color-matched accessories; and the power of macOS 27. Available in a spectrum of seven colors—blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver—the new iMac is a tremendous upgrade for existing users and an incredible gateway into everything the Mac can do for new users. Customers can pre-order starting tomorrow, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.
Shelly Goldberg, Apple's vice president of Hardware Engineering"iMac is the world's best all-in-one, and today it raises the bar yet again," "With the blazing performance and AI capabilities of M6 supercharging every workflow and the next generation of Apple Intelligence with Siri AI—combined with its stunning 24-inch Retina display, its gorgeous design in seven vibrant colors, and macOS 27—the new iMac has everything users need to run their businesses, manage their lives, and bring their ideas to life."
iMac with M6: A Huge Leap in Performance and AI Capabilities
With M6, iMac brings even more performance, for everything from everyday productivity to creative workloads and AI tasks. iMac with M6 features up to a 12-core CPU—two more cores than before—delivering the world's fastest single-threaded CPU performance. Everything feels extra snappy and responsive for families managing busy calendars, students putting the finishing touches on a project, and small business owners running their companies. An up-to-12-core GPU, also with two more cores than before, now features Neural Accelerators in each core, delivering up to 2x faster graphics for more intensive tasks like photo editing, along with fantastic gaming performance compared to M4.3 Students and creators can now fly through tasks like editing and sharing their latest videos or designing a project for class, all while multitasking with their favorite messaging or entertainment apps. The new Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 2x faster AI compute than the previous generation, and combined with the advanced GPU and faster memory bandwidth and with higher memory bandwidth up to 170 GB/s, iMac rips through AI tasks like running LLMs on device. With all this performance packed into its stunning design, iMac is the perfect all-in-one for a wide range of users and workflows.
The new iMac with M6 enables:
- Up to 2.5x faster performance in apps like Microsoft Excel, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 1.5x faster performance than M4, so families, aspiring creators, and small businesses can fly through daily productivity tasks.
- Up to 3.3x faster graphics performance for tasks including photo editing in Affinity, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 2x faster performance than M4, so content creators can edit like never before.
- Up to 12x faster on-device AI performance for prompt processing in LM Studio, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 5x faster performance than M4, so users can run powerful AI models, all while keeping their data private.
- Up to 2x higher gaming performance with ray tracing compared to M4.
iMac with M6: A Powerful Platform for AI
Beyond delivering exceptional performance for everyday productivity and creative workflows, iMac is also a powerful platform for AI, enabling users to take advantage of advanced AI capabilities while protecting their privacy. With macOS 27, the next generation of Apple Intelligence is deeply personal, seamlessly integrated across apps, and built with privacy from the ground up. Apple Intelligence powers Siri AI, a new version of Siri that is profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal, helping users get more done than ever before. On iMac, users can tap into Siri AI to ask questions; find what they need across their messages, emails, photos, and more; and take action across apps. Siri AI is built right into Spotlight, making it easy to search for answers on virtually any topic and ask follow-up questions. With the expansive 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, users can leverage Visual Intelligence with a dedicated keyboard shortcut to ask Siri about anything on their screen, from a chart in a spreadsheet to a photo in a browser tab. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type, and in Mail and Messages, Siri can reflect their typical style and tone.
Apple Intelligence also makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user's tabs into topics; notifies them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enables the creation of custom extensions based on a description. In addition, users can easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. iMac also supports a growing ecosystem of AI apps optimized for Apple silicon, including LM Studio Bionic and Topaz Studio, helping users learn faster, think in new ways, and get more done.
Best-in-Class Connectivity and Faster Storage
The new iMac features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, along with 2.5 Gb Ethernet that delivers up to 2.5x faster wired connectivity than the previous generation. This means faster transfers of large files, smoother streaming of high-resolution content, and even better performance for gaming and demanding business workflows. And with up to 2x faster SSD read and write performance, apps launch quickly, and large files like photo libraries and video projects load in an instant.
Up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports enable superfast data transfers and make it easy to connect a wide range of accessories, including external storage and docks. Users can also connect up to two 6K external displays, creating a vast workspace with more than 50 million pixels to spread out their work.
A Transformational Upgrade
The new iMac is a tremendous upgrade—especially for users coming from an Intel-based iMac, who will experience performance that's up to 18x faster. And with macOS 27, Siri AI and new Apple Intelligence features integrated across apps make AI tasks on iMac more personal and powerful than ever.
iMac also includes all of the popular features and capabilities that make it the world's best all-in-one:
- A beautiful canvas for work and play: iMac provides a brilliant canvas for multitasking, immersive movies and games, and more. The stunning 4.5K display delivers crisp, clear details with 500 nits of brightness—offering 5x more resolution and nearly 70 percent greater brightness than the bestselling 24-inch all-in-one PC. And P3 wide color brings everything onscreen to life with over 1 billion colors.
- Industry-leading camera and audio: A 12MP Center Stage camera helps keep users perfectly framed on video calls, while Desk View enables them to share a top-down view of their workspace—ideal for educators giving lessons or creatives showing off their latest project. iMac also brings incredible audio to any space. Two pairs of force-cancelling woofers with two tweeters fill the room with bold, bass-rich sound, and Spatial Audio with support for Dolby Atmos creates an immersive listening experience. Completing the phenomenal video and audio experience is the studio-quality three-microphone array.
- A colorful addition to any space: iMac transforms any space with a spectrum of seven vibrant colors, adding a pop of inspiration to homes, workspaces, and storefronts.
- Color-matched accessories and Touch ID: iMac features a color-matched keyboard and mouse or trackpad with USB-C ports, so users can charge all of their favorite devices with just a single cable. Magic Mouse and Magic Trackpad make navigation easy and intuitive. And Magic Keyboard with Touch ID lets users easily and securely unlock iMac, switch users, authorize Apple Pay, and download apps.
- Better together with iPhone: iMac brings everything users love from iPhone to a gorgeous, spacious display. When both devices are used together with Continuity, they are even more powerful—letting users move seamlessly across devices to share files and photos, hand off tasks, and even control their iPhone from their iMac. Users switching to Mac for the first time can use iPhone to conveniently and securely transfer settings, files, photos, passwords, and more
.
macOS 27 Golden Gate: An Unrivaled Experience
The new iMac comes to life with macOS 27. In addition to Siri AI and Apple Intelligence, iMac gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful for everyday use with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver a more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.
iMac and the Environment
The new iMac was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple's ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 100 percent recycled aluminium in the stand, 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, and 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards. It is manufactured with 40 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The new iMac meets Apple's high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based and designed to be recycled.
Pricing and Availability
- Customers can pre-order the new iMac with M6 starting tomorrow, October 28, on apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app in 35 countries and regions, including the U.S. It will begin arriving to customers, and in Apple Store locations and Apple Authorized Resellers, starting Friday, November 6.
- iMac with M6 featuring a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU starts at $1,499 (U.S.) and $1,449 (U.S.) with education savings. iMac with a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU starts at $1,699 (U.S.) and $1,599 (U.S.) with education savings. Additional technical specifications, configure-to-order options, and information on Magic accessories are available at apple.com/mac.

articles.title: Echte Polwanderung: Warum selbst der geografische Nordpol keinen festen Platz hat
articles.text:
10 Zentimeter pro Jahr: Warum selbst der geografische Nordpol keinen festen Platz hat
Die geografischen Pole der Erde verschieben sich derzeit mit einer per Satellit gemessenen Geschwindigkeit von rund zehn Zentimetern pro Jahr, was die durchschnittliche Driftgeschwindigkeit tektonischer Platten übersteigt. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, handelt es sich bei solchen Geschwindigkeiten nicht bloß um kurzlebige Ausreißer der Gegenwart, da vergleichbare Verschiebungen in den vergangenen 320 Millionen Jahren mehrfach über Zeiträume von jeweils zehn Millionen Jahren auftraten.
Ein Forschungsteam um den Geowissenschaftler Mathew Domeier, den Geologen Leandro C. Gallo, die Geowissenschaftlerin Chloé M. Marcilly und den Geophysiker Trond H. Torsvik von der norwegischen Universität Oslo wies insgesamt vier solcher Phasen anhand urzeitlicher Meeresspiegelschwankungen nach. Diese Episoden lagen in den Zeitfenstern vor 200 bis 190 Millionen, vor 150 bis 140 Millionen, vor 100 bis 90 Millionen sowie vor 30 bis 20 Millionen Jahren und erreichten Raten von mindestens 0,6 Breitengraden pro einer Million Jahre, was mindestens 6,7 Zentimetern pro Jahr entspricht.
Echte Polwanderung: Warum Erdkruste und Erdmantel über den Erdkern gleiten
In den Geowissenschaften trägt dieser Vorgang die Bezeichnung echte Polwanderung (auf Englisch: „True Polar Wander“) und unterscheidet sich grundlegend von der Bewegung der Magnetpole, die durch Strömungen im flüssigen äußeren Erdkern entsteht. Bei der echten Polwanderung bleibt die Rotationsachse der Erde im Weltraum stabil ausgerichtet, während sich die rund 2.800 Kilometer dicke feste äußere Schale aus Erdkruste und Erdmantel als Ganzes um den Erdkern dreht.
Auslöser für diese Drehung sind Massenverlagerungen im Erdmantel oder an der Oberfläche: Da der Planet durch die Eigenrotation am Äquator leicht ausgewölbt ist, kippt die feste Erdhülle bei einer Unwucht so lange nach, bis große Massenüberschüsse wieder möglichst nah am Äquator liegen. In den vergangenen Jahrzehnten trug neben abschmelzenden Eisschilden auch die Entnahme von rund 2.150 Gigatonnen Grundwasser messbar zu dieser Verschiebung bei.
„Die Erdkruste und der Erdmantel gleiten während eines Ereignisses echter Polwanderung gewissermaßen über den Erdkern“, wird Erstautor Mathew Domeier von New Scientist zitiert. Laut dem Geodynamiker Sabin Zahirovic von der australischen Universität Sydney hilft der Nachweis über historische Küstenlinien dabei, Prozesse im tiefen Erdinneren mit langfristigen Veränderungen von Klima und Meeresspiegel zu verknüpfen.
Meeresspiegel und Zentrifugalkraft: Wie das Datenmodell die Erdrotation rekonstruiert
Bisherige Versuche, frühere Polwanderungen über in Gestein gespeicherte Magnetfeldrichtungen nachzuweisen, lieferten oft widersprüchliche Ergebnisse, weil die gleichzeitige Bewegung einzelner Kontinentalplatten die Messdaten überlagert. Das Team aus Oslo wählte deshalb einen anderen physikalischen Ansatz: Wenn sich die feste Erdhülle relativ zur Rotationsachse verschiebt, ändert sich vor Ort die Fliehkraft – in der Fachsprache das Zentrifugalpotenzial –, worauf das flüssige Wasser der Weltmeere sofort reagiert, während das feste Gestein des Meeresbodens erst mit großer Verzögerung nachgibt.
Dadurch entsteht bei einer schnellen Polwanderung ein charakteristisches globales Vier-Felder-Muster, das Geolog:innen als Quadrupol-Signal bezeichnen und das optisch den Segmenten eines Wasserballs ähnelt. Während Kontinentalflächen, die sich in Richtung Äquator bewegen, überflutet werden, zieht sich das Meer in Regionen zurück, die näher an die Pole rücken, Dabei verhalten sich Nord- und Südhalbkugel jeweils gegenläufig.
Um dieses Muster in geologischen Überflutungskarten der vergangenen 320 Millionen Jahre aufzuspüren, teilten die Forscher:innen die Erdoberfläche mithilfe der Open-Source-Programmbibliothek h3-py in ein Raster aus sechseckigen Zellen mit rund 119 Kilometern Abstand ein, wie aus den Begleitmaterialien der Untersuchung hervorgeht. Bei der Auswertung dieser Zellen musste das Team zunächst ein Störsignal herausfiltern. Wenn etwa globale Eisschilde schmelzen, steigt das Wasser weltweit gleichzeitig an und überdeckt das gesuchte Vier-Felder-Muster der Polwanderung. Ein Berechnungsverfahren zog solche allgemeinen Schwankungen der gesamten Wassermenge deshalb rechnerisch ab, um zu prüfen, ob darunter tatsächlich das gegenläufige Wasserball-Muster einer kippenden Erdhülle sichtbar wird.
Zudem mussten die Wissenschaftler:innen berücksichtigen, dass die feste Erdkruste starr wie eine durchgehende Platte reagiert. Wird ein Küstenabschnitt überflutet oder angehoben, zieht das Gestein benachbarte Gebiete im Umkreis automatisch mit, sodass viele nebeneinanderliegende Messzellen denselben Wert zeigen, ohne unabhängige Einzelbeweise zu liefern. Damit solche zusammenhängenden Regionen die Statistik nicht verfälschen, fasste eine Analyse-Software direkt benachbarte Messpunkte jeweils zu einem gemeinsamen Block zusammen und würfelte die Ergebnisse für jeden untersuchten Zeitraum 10.000-mal zufällig durcheinander, um einen Zufallstreffer auszuschließen.
Superkontinent Pangäa und methodische blinde Flecken der Geologie
Neben den vier nachgewiesenen Verschiebungsphasen widerlegen die auf der Forschungsplattform Zenodo hinterlegten Daten und Programmiercodes auch eine verbreitete Annahme zum Urkontinent Pangäa, der einst fast alle Landmassen der Erde vereinte. Weil in den Karten für die Zeit vor 320 bis 250 Millionen Jahren das typische Vier-Felder-Muster der Meere fehlt, wanderte diese zusammenhängende Landmasse damals offenbar durch gewöhnliche Plattentektonik nach Norden und nicht durch ein Kippen der gesamten Erdhülle. Gegenüber Earth.com erklärte Mathew Domeier, er habe das Projekt ursprünglich mit der Erwartung begonnen, überhaupt keine Belege für schnelle Polwanderungen in den vergangenen paar hundert Millionen Jahren zu finden.
Allerdings hat auch das neue Verfahren blinde Flecken, weil die verwendeten Überflutungskarten die Erdgeschichte nur in groben Zeitschritten von jeweils zehn Millionen Jahren abbilden. Kippt die Erdhülle innerhalb einer kürzeren Zeitspanne in eine Richtung und schwingt anschließend direkt wieder zurück – wie es andere Wissenschaftler:innen etwa für ein Ereignis vor rund 84 Millionen Jahren vermuten –, steigt und fällt der Meeresspiegel genau zwischen zwei Kartenaufnahmen, sodass die Bewegung für das Modell unsichtbar bleibt.
Zudem ist das älteste der vier gefundenen Signale aus der Zeit vor 200 bis 190 Millionen Jahren nach Einschätzung der Autor:innen selbst ein unsicherer Kandidat. Da der gemessene Ausschlag nur knapp über dem Wert liegt, den auch normale Zufallsschwankungen erzeugen können, handelt es sich hierbei möglicherweise um einen bloßen Zufallstreffer. Noch weiter als 320 Millionen Jahre lässt sich mit der Methode derzeit gar nicht in die Vergangenheit blicken, weil vor der Entstehung von Pangäa zwar die Nord-Süd-Lage früherer Kontinente bekannt ist, Geolog:innen deren damalige Ost-West-Position auf dem Globus aber nicht mehr verlässlich bestimmen können.

articles.title: From Homemade Badi to GomatiRoots: Shital Kumari Secures Funding
articles.text:
From Homemade Badi to GomatiRoots: Shital Kumari Secures Funding
Bihar's Shital Kumari transforms homemade badi into GomatiRoots, securing funding through YourStory's Shuru Kar initiative.
Key Takeaways
- GomatiRoots is building a brand around Bihar's traditional badi.
- The startup received Rs 1 lakh in funding through YourStory's Shuru Kar initiative.
- Shital Kumari's startup is connecting rural women with markets.
- The company generated Rs 32 lakh in revenue in its first financial year.
Last September, in 2025, the Bihar Idea Festival concluded at Bapu Sabhagar in Patna. YourStory launched the festival under its initiative, The Bharat Project, in collaboration with the Bihar Industries Department and the Chandragupt Institute of Management, Patna (CIMP). The objective was to take entrepreneurship beyond metropolitan cities and select groups of people, reaching young people in smaller towns and villages and helping them turn their business ideas into reality.
Shital Kumari was among those present at the event. She wanted to start her own business but had several questions. What business should she start? How would she get started? Where would the money come from? And what would happen if her efforts failed?
Life had already exposed her to numerous challenges. Taking the risk of starting a business was not easy, but she decided to take a step towards turning her idea into reality.
Nearly a year later, Shital's efforts reached an important milestone. Through YourStory's Shuru Kar initiative, she received funding of Rs 1 lakh for her startup, GomatiRoots. The funding came from Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project. For Shital, the amount represented more than financial support; it was also a sign of confidence in her idea.
Through GomatiRoots, Shital aims to give Bihar's traditional badi and other indigenous food products a distinct identity. She wants badi, a traditional lentil-based food product that has been part of Indian households for generations, to establish itself as a trusted brand in the market.
Building a Business Amid Challenges
To understand Shital's entrepreneurial journey, it is important to look back at her early life.
She grew up in Bihar and completed her education at government institutions. She studied up to Class 10 at Shri Guru Gobind Singh Girls High School, completed her intermediate education at RPM College, and earned an honours degree in Physics from the College of Commerce.
She wanted to pursue a BTech degree, but that dream did not materialise. Nevertheless, she continued her education and later completed an MA from Nalanda Open University. A friend helped her with Rs 4,500 to pursue her studies.
In 2018, her life took a major turn when she lost her younger brother. Following his death, her family moved to Muzaffarpur. As the family struggled to cope with the loss, Shital lost her mother during the COVID-19 pandemic.
After her mother's death, the responsibility of caring for her younger siblings fell on her shoulders. She moved to Patna to support her family and began looking for work. Over the next two to three years, she took up video editing, taught children, and even sold lychees whenever necessary. Throughout this period, she continued preparing for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) examination.
During this time, she learned about the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana, a state government initiative designed to support small entrepreneurs. She applied for the scheme and received Rs 50,000 as the first instalment. She also received training to start her business.
Later, she received a second instalment of Rs 1 lakh. In addition, she took a loan of Rs 2 lakh and laid the foundation for GomatiRoots in Patna.
Speaking to YourStory, Shital says, "There were several phases in my life when taking care of my family was the most important responsibility. After my mother passed away, looking after my younger siblings became my priority. I worked in video editing, taught children, and even sold lychees. At the same time, I continued preparing for the UPSC examination. When I learned about the Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana, I felt that perhaps I finally had an opportunity to start something of my own. I did not have much money, but I decided to begin with whatever resources I had."
How Her Mother's Homemade Badi Inspired a Business
GomatiRoots did not begin with a long-standing business ambition. Instead, the idea emerged from a deeply personal experience.
After her mother's death, Shital often missed the badi her mother used to make. When she began looking for a similar product in the market, she could not find one that matched the taste and quality she remembered. Some products raised concerns about adulteration, while others did not offer the varieties she preferred.
What began as a personal search soon revealed a potential business opportunity.
Shital started researching the market, speaking to people, and learning more about badi. During her research, she observed that while India had several well-established pickle and papad brands, badi had not achieved the same level of recognition.
Yet, in Bihar and many other parts of India, lentil-based badi is a regular part of everyday meals. It is eaten with lentils, vegetables, and other dishes, and the tradition of making it at home has continued for generations.
Despite its popularity, badi often remains a locally produced food item rather than a recognised packaged brand.
Shital believed that the product could establish a stronger market presence if it were made available throughout the year with consistent quality and better packaging. This insight gradually shaped the idea behind GomatiRoots.
For her, badi was more than a food product. It represented memories of her mother, the taste of home, and an opportunity to bring Bihar's culinary traditions to a wider audience.
Shital says, "The idea of building a brand around badi was not something I had thought about since childhood. After my mother passed away, I looked for a product in the market that tasted like the badi she used to make. That was when I realised there was a need for a reliable brand. I studied the market and spoke to people. There are several pickle and papad brands, but I did not see the same kind of identity for badi. I felt that if we could make it available throughout the year with consistent quality, people would embrace it."
Turning Traditional Flavours Into a Brand
GomatiRoots started with badi, but its product range has since expanded to include several traditional varieties.
These include urad dal badi, moongori, chana dal badi, Bihari masala badi, and kohrauri. The company also offers traditional fryums such as tisiyori and tilauri.
Through these products, Shital aims to bring greater recognition to flavours that have long been part of households and local communities.
One of the biggest challenges in this business is the seasonal nature of badi production. Traditionally, making badi depends heavily on sunlight and weather conditions. Unfavourable weather can affect both production and product quality.
Ensuring that customers receive a consistent product throughout the year is therefore not easy.
Shital has tried to address this challenge through research and experimentation. Her goal is to ensure that customers receive the same quality every time they purchase a product, regardless of the season.
According to Shital, the business has received encouraging customer feedback within its first year of operations. Repeat orders from retail shopkeepers, in particular, have strengthened her confidence. These orders indicate that customers are not simply trying the product once but are willing to buy it again.
However, maintaining this trust requires continuous improvements in production, packaging, and storage.
Shital says, "Making badi available throughout the year is one of our most important priorities. Traditionally, it has been prepared according to the weather and availability of sunlight. But if we want to build a brand, customers must receive consistent quality every time. We have conducted research at our level and improved our production methods. Over the past year, we have received repeat orders from shopkeepers. When customers tell us that our products taste like homemade food, that means a lot to us."
Limited Capital, a Larger Market, and New Challenges
GomatiRoots initially relied on government scheme assistance and a loan to get its operations started. With limited resources, Shital had to account for every expense carefully.
Purchasing raw materials, developing packaging, delivering products to retail outlets, and building brand awareness all required money. Rather than expanding in multiple directions at once, she chose to grow the business gradually.
The company currently generates revenue by supplying products to retail stores, restaurants, and cloud kitchens, as well as selling directly to customers.
GomatiRoots products are available at more than 50 stores in Patna. The company is also working to expand its presence in other districts of Bihar through distributors.
Its products are available on Amazon, Flipkart, and JioMart. Customers can also place orders through the company's website, gomatiroots.com.
In addition, the business reaches customers directly through exhibitions, fairs, and canopy stalls.
Funding Through YourStory's Shuru Kar Initiative
During its first financial year of operations, GomatiRoots generated revenue of Rs 32 lakh. Shital is now looking to expand into larger retail networks and quick-commerce platforms.
However, entering large retail stores and organised markets requires a reliable supply chain. The business must also address product shelf life, packaging, and storage requirements.
Shital is working to overcome these challenges. She also plans to bring more people on board to strengthen e-commerce operations and direct-to-consumer sales.
She says, "We started the business with very limited capital. In the beginning, we had to account for every rupee. We had production and packaging expenses on one side and the challenge of reaching retail stores on the other. Large retail companies also want to know whether a brand can maintain a consistent supply. We are gradually strengthening our sales record and distributor network. We intend to use the Rs 1 lakh funding received through YourStory's Shuru Kar initiative for working capital and marketing as well."
Connecting Women's Work With Market Opportunities
GomatiRoots' ambitions extend beyond increasing product sales. Shital wants women and small producers who make traditional food products in Bihar to benefit from access to larger markets.
Some of the company's products are prepared in collaboration with rural women's self-help groups (SHGs). These include different varieties of tisiyori made with flaxseed, potatoes, and rice, along with rice-based tilauri and kohrauri.
The women already have experience preparing these traditional foods. GomatiRoots aims to help them connect with buyers and access wider markets.
Shital is also in discussions with JEEViKA, Bihar's rural livelihoods initiative. She was invited as a buyer to the Saras Mela and now hopes to establish long-term partnerships to source traditional products directly from JEEViKA Didis.
Her objective is to ensure that the women receive fair prices for their products and gain access to regular income opportunities.
In the future, she also wants to work with farmers in Bihar so that the lentils used to make badi can be cultivated locally, allowing farmers to benefit from the business.
Over the next three to five years, Shital hopes to take GomatiRoots beyond Bihar and into major cities across India. Her plans include expanding into large retail stores, online marketplaces, and quick-commerce platforms.
The company also hopes to open its own store and eventually export its products internationally.
Alongside expansion, Shital wants to formalise business operations, obtain the necessary licences, increase production capacity, and make better use of available business support schemes.
One of her long-term goals is to create year-round work opportunities for up to one lakh women associated with JEEViKA's self-help groups. For now, this remains an ambition that she hopes to pursue as the business grows.
Shital says, "I want the growth of GomatiRoots to translate into higher incomes for women in Bihar. Many women here have excellent skills in preparing traditional food products, but they lack the means to reach larger markets. If they receive regular work and fair prices, their efforts can gain greater recognition. We also want to work with farmers so that the lentils used in badi can be grown in Bihar itself. My dream is to take these flavours across the country and around the world."
The Road Ahead
Shital Kumari's story is not about building a business with abundant capital, an established market, and plenty of resources from the outset. She found her way forward while managing family responsibilities, took up different jobs, and used support from a government scheme to establish her business.
The Rs 1 lakh funding she subsequently received through YourStory's Shuru Kar initiative has further strengthened confidence in her idea.
Her search for the badi her mother used to make helped her identify a gap in the market, one she is now working to address through her brand.
GomatiRoots still faces several challenges. It must increase production while maintaining quality, strengthen customer trust, and build a more organised business to compete in larger markets.
However, Shital has a clear goal: she wants badi to become more than a product associated with a particular household or region. She wants customers to recognise the brand by name and purchase it with confidence.
Entrepreneurship in India is often associated with large investments and technology startups. But the story of GomatiRoots, which emerged from Bihar, offers a different perspective. Its foundation is not a new technology but a traditional food product that has been part of everyday meals for generations.
The real challenge lies in adapting that product to market requirements, building a trusted identity, and creating income opportunities for the people involved in its production.
For Shital, the journey is still in its early stages. She dreams of a day when someone in any part of India looking to buy lentil-based badi will think of GomatiRoots.
The coming years will determine how far this ambition takes her. For now, her journey demonstrates that entrepreneurship does not always require an entirely new idea. Sometimes, the beginnings of a business can be found in the familiar flavours of home.
Hokar Nidar Shuru Kar.

articles.title: Nuevo accidente mortal en la alta velocidad española: lo que sabemos del choque de un AVE y un Iryo en Urda, Toledo
articles.text:
Un alcance entre un AVE de Renfe y un Iryo. Es la información que, de momento, ha aportado Adif sobre el corte de circulación en la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Andalucía. Adif confirma que todos los trenes de la línea andaluza se encuentran parados en las estaciones.
La Junta de Andalucía ha confirmado que, al menos, han fallecido 64 personas en el choque de los trenes. Hay alrededor de 80 heridos, 30 de leves y 50 de graves. Esther Padilla, portavoz de la Junta de Castilla-La Mancha confirmaba esta mañana que en el tren de Iryo viajaban 147 personas y en el AVE otros 397 pasajeros.
El choque entre los trenes se ha producido poco antes de las 9:00 horas. En ese momento, un AVE que había salido de Madrid a las 8:00 en dirección Sevilla ha alcanzado a un tren de Iryo parado en las vías. De momento, se desconoce por qué el tren de la compañía se encontraba detenido y por qué el tren de Renfe ha chocado con tanta violencia contra él.
Las primeras hipótesis apuntan a un error humano en la gestión del tráfico ferroviario después de que se hubiera producido una caída en el sistema de seguridad LZB que se utiliza en las vías del corredor andaluz. Estas vías estaban siendo modernizadas para adaptarse al más novedoso y extendido en Europa sistema ERTMS-2.
Se cree que una vez se ha caído el sistema, el centro de control ha tomado el mando y habría ordenado al maquinista del tren AVE saltarse las señales físicas que ordenaban a dicho tren detenerse. Este procedimiento, ha confirmado un maquinista a Xataka, no es raro porque es el centro de control el que tiene constancia de dónde se encuentra cada tren.
La gran pregunta es por qué el tren AVE circulaba a una velocidad muy superior a los 40 km/h máximos que se suelen limitar en este tipo de casos. Y por qué el CRC no visualizó que el tren de Iryo se había quedado detenido en la vía al retomar la circulación tras la caída del sistema de seguridad. Se cree que este tren habría sido alcanzado a más de 100 km/h.
En el mapa que se recogen los límites de velocidad temporales se puede comprobar que no existía limitación de velocidad en la zona donde se ha producido el accidente. Sin embargo, el mapa sí muestra que, como decíamos, ese corredor sigue en obras para ser actualizado.
En las estaciones de Atocha, Sevilla y Córdoba se han desplegado efectivos para la atención psicológica e informativa para los familiares afectados. Los familiares también pueden obtener información en los siguientes números:
- Renfe: 900 10 10 20
- Iryo: 900 001 403
- Servicio de Emergencias de Castilla-La Mancha: 900 122 112
Noticia en desarrollo, ampliaremos información cuando se tengan más detalles confirmados.

articles.title: Apple Introduces the New 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Apple Introduces the New 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6
Apple today announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6, delivering even more performance, powerful on-device AI capabilities, and faster connectivity for college students, business users, creators, and more. M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world's fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive. The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power. 
For those upgrading from M1, the performance gains are even more significant, with up to 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI—from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy. In addition, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, while superfast storage makes working with large files, exporting projects, and running demanding AI workflows fly. And with phenomenal battery life of up to 24 hours, it delivers the same remarkable performance whether plugged in or on battery, so users can work, create, and pursue their passions from anywhere.It also offers the advanced features users love, including the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, a 12MP Center Stage camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a wide array of ports. Together with macOS 27, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is a major upgrade for existing Mac users and those coming to Mac for the first time. Available in space black and silver, it can be pre-ordered beginning tomorrow, October 28, with availability starting Friday, November 6.
Shelly Goldberg, Apple's vice president of Hardware Engineering"The 14-inch MacBook Pro is the pro laptop of choice for a wide range of users—from college students, to business professionals across every industry, to multidisciplinary creators doing it all on one device," "With the powerful M6 chip, we're taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI. With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value."
M6: Blazing-Fast Performance and On-Device AI Capabilities
M6 brings even more performance and next-level AI capabilities to the 14-inch MacBook Pro. Featuring a powerful 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and faster unified memory, MacBook Pro with M6 is faster and more responsive.
The 12-core CPU, with two more cores than before, brings blazing-fast single- and multithreaded performance, so users can fly through everything from multitasking across apps to compiling code to handling complex creative workflows. The 12-core GPU, also with two additional cores, delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance when compared to M5.2 Everything from 3D modeling to photo editing and gaming feels incredibly fast, enhanced by a third-generation ray tracing engine and Dynamic Caching to optimize on-chip memory. 
It also brings up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads, like LLM prompt processing, compared to M5.3 The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 1.9x faster performance than M5 and works with the advanced GPU to dramatically accelerate AI workloads like image generation, Super Resolution, and AI upscaling. The Neural Engine also powers Apple Intelligence, enabling advanced and energy-efficient on-device AI processing. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 does all this with industry-leading performance per watt and up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest ever in a Mac. With 16 GB of unified memory standard, configurable up to 32 GB, and higher memory bandwidth up to 170 GB/s, MacBook Pro makes multitasking and working with demanding apps and large projects even faster.
The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 enables:
- Up to 13x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
- Up to 11.7x faster render performance with ray tracing in Blender compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
- Up to 3.3x faster image-processing performance in Affinity compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.2x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
- Up to 2.5x faster project build performance when compiling code in Xcode compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
A Huge Upgrade with Even More Value
There's never been a better time for customers to upgrade from a previous-generation MacBook Pro with Apple silicon or an Intel-based Mac. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers remarkable value thanks to major performance improvements and powerful AI capabilities. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro also features all of the compelling capabilities that have made it so popular, including:
- Phenomenal battery life: In addition to the huge leap in performance, battery life gets up to 14 additional hours for Intel-based upgraders and up to four more hours for users coming from M1, delivering up to 24 hours overall, so users can get more done on a single charge. Users coming from Intel-based and M1 systems will also get 16 GB of starting unified memory, an additional Thunderbolt port, and the space black finish with an anodization seal for fewer fingerprints.
- A brilliant pro display: The stunning Liquid Retina XDR display delivers up to 1600 nits of peak HDR brightness and a 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio, bringing HDR photos and videos to life with deep blacks, brilliant highlights, and vibrant colors. And for users working in bright or challenging lighting conditions, a nano-texture display option dramatically reduces reflections and glare.
- Powerful connectivity: Now with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, the 14-inch MacBook Pro delivers fast wireless performance and low latency, along with support for up to two external displays. Its versatile array of ports—including the HDMI, MagSafe 3, and three Thunderbolt 4 ports; an SDXC card slot; and a headphone jack—makes it easy to connect high-speed peripherals, transfer photos, or expand a workspace.
- Advanced camera, mics, and speakers: A 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View helps keep users perfectly framed on video calls, while a studio-quality three-mic array and amazing six-speaker sound system with Spatial Audio deliver an immersive audio experience.
- Fast charging: MacBook Pro with M6 supports fast charging, reaching up to 50 percent charge in just 30 minutes when paired with a compatible higher-wattage USB-C power adapter, such as the 96 W Power Adapter.
- A laptop that's built to last: With an enclosure made from 100 percent recycled aluminium, MacBook Pro is exceptionally durable and can stand up to everyday use for years to come.
- Better together with iPhone: When used together with Continuity, iPhone and Mac are even more powerful—letting users move seamlessly across devices to share files and photos, hand off tasks, and even control their iPhone from their 14-inch MacBook Pro. Users switching to Mac for the first time can use iPhone to conveniently and securely transfer settings, files, photos, passwords, and more.
macOS 27 Golden Gate
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 comes to life with macOS 27, which includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across everyday apps; and improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps—all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what's on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.
Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user's tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Users can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.
14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the Environment
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple's ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminium in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple's high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based and designed to be recycled.
Pricing and Availability
- Customers can pre-order the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starting tomorrow, October 28, on apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app in 35 countries and regions, including the U.S. It will begin arriving to customers, and in Apple Store locations and Apple Authorized Resellers, starting Friday, November 6.
- The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 (U.S.) and $1,899 (U.S.) with education savings. Additional technical specifications and configure-to-order options are available at apple.com/macbook-pro.

articles.title: CEO de Epic Games califica de “repugnante” la postura de Steam con los juegos hechos con IA
articles.text:
Tim Sweeney, director general de Epic Games, volvió a enfrentarse a Valve por la forma en que Steam regula la inteligencia artificial generativa en los videojuegos. En una serie de publicaciones en X, el ejecutivo calificó de “aborrecible” y “repugnante” la exigencia de declarar el uso de esta tecnología, y la comparó con un “ensayo político obligatorio”.
La disputa no es nueva, pero se produce en un momento en el que Epic Games se ha declarado abiertamente una compañía “AI first”, lo que ha puesto bajo la lupa la coherencia de las críticas de su propio fundador.
Qué dijo el CEO de Epic sobre la política de Steam
Todo comenzó cuando el desarrollador Matt Workman, vinculado a la plataforma de medios generativos Fal, calificó de absurdo que en 2026 todavía exista la obligación de declarar el uso de IA en las fichas de los juegos de Steam. Sweeney respondió con dureza.
“Obligar a los desarrolladores a escribir una declaración política que después pueda utilizarse en su contra por parte de una turba de haters que están ayudando a organizar es aborrecible”, escribió el CEO de Epic Games.
Horas más tarde subió el tono y comparó estas etiquetas con “forzar a los desarrolladores a listar su historial de voto para alimentar campañas de cancelación”. También introdujo un argumento económico: según Sweeney, Valve se queda con el 30% de las ventas y, a su juicio, una porción adicional del sustento de los estudios al exponerlos a la “turba anti-IA”.
Luego insistió en que la plataforma está “quemando los negocios de buenos desarrolladores” y pronosticó que, dentro de un año, el uso de IA será generalizado y los críticos actuales “fingirán que su turba no se equivocó, solo que fue malinterpretada”. Cuando un usuario sugirió que esta situación representaba una oportunidad para Epic Games si Valve no corregía el rumbo, Sweeney respondió con un escueto “Yep!”.
Un aviso de que un juego usó inteligencia artificial no equivale a un manifiesto ideológico: funciona como la misma letra pequeña que ya existe para advertir sobre las cajas de botín, y busca informar al jugador antes de la compra, no sancionar al desarrollador.
La respuesta y las cifras detrás de Valve
La política de transparencia de Steam está vigente desde el 10 de enero de 2024 y obliga a los estudios a explicar si usaron IA generativa durante el desarrollo y con qué propósito.
Valve justificó la medida como una forma de “mejorar nuestra comprensión del terreno y de los riesgos” de una tecnología que consideró “legalmente turbia”, tras conversar con estudios que ya la empleaban. La compañía se comprometió a revisar la norma cuando el panorama legal y la propia industria se clarifiquen.
Este año, Valve ya flexibilizó parte de sus exigencias: los desarrolladores dejaron de estar obligados a informar sobre el uso de IA en la escritura de código de programación.
La divulgación solo se mantiene para los casos en que se emplearon redes neuronales en la creación de recursos del juego, doblaje, traducción u otros elementos similares. Además, esa información aparece en la parte inferior de la página del juego, junto a las advertencias de contenido.
El volumen de lanzamientos explica parte del contexto: en 2024 llegaron a Steam 18.433 juegos, frente a los 1.100 que publicó Epic Games Store. Con esa diferencia de catálogo, el formulario de transparencia funciona más como una herramienta de control de daños que como un mecanismo de censura.
Tampoco hay un historial de Valve como opositora a la inteligencia artificial. Gabe Newell donó 20 millones de dólares a OpenAI cuando esta todavía era una organización sin fines de lucro, y sus declaraciones públicas sobre el tema no difieren demasiado de las de otros ejecutivos tecnológicos.
La crítica de Sweeney contrasta con las reglas de Fab, la tienda de recursos digitales para desarrolladores que pertenece a Epic Games. Esa plataforma también exige revelar información sobre el uso de inteligencia artificial, el mismo requisito que su fundador describió como “repugnante” cuando lo aplica Valve. Usuarios en redes sociales señalaron rápidamente esta contradicción tras sus publicaciones.

articles.title: AI automation hinges on portability, says Cloudera analyst - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cloudera bets portability, not agents, will set it apart in enterprise AI
Enterprises racing toward AI automation are finding that where their models and data run matters as much as what the models can do. Regulatory pressure, rising token costs and fear of lock-in are pushing companies to demand more control over their AI workloads.
That demand is shaping how data platform providers pitch their next act. Cloudera Inc. started out in the Hadoop market and later moved to a unified data layer that spans clouds and on-premises infrastructure. It is now positioning itself as an anywhere cloud for AI, according to Paul Gillin (pictured, right), enterprise editor of SiliconANGLE Media Inc.
“I think big companies decided a long time ago. They didn’t want to be beholden to a single cloud provider and that’s sort of baked into the landscape now,” Gillin said. “I think what’s different about Cloudera is that they’re strong proponents of on-premises infrastructure, of sovereign clouds, of companies being able to run their workloads wherever they want and move from one to another.”
Gillin spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight (left) at EVOLVE26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed AI automation and provided analysis of the event’s keynote speech. (* Disclosure below.)
Sovereign AI and purpose-built agents drive AI automation
Sovereign and private AI came up frequently in the EVOLVE26 keynote. Surveys point to regulation as the main reason enterprises want to keep AI inside their own walls. Open-weight models give them a way to do it, having grown from about 20% of token use two years ago to more than 80% today, according to Gillin. Cloudera is also adding agentic workflows across its data services. General-purpose agents are more of a consumer phenomenon, he explained.
“They’re more of an office worker tool, but the Cloudera agents are tuned to managing data,” Gillin said. “To managing workloads, optimizing GPU capacity, the types of things that really concern CIOs, because they’re paying the bills for these very high training costs.”
Simply having an agent is no longer an edge, so Cloudera is doubling down on its long-standing multiplatform play. It is extending the portability enterprises wanted from their clouds to their AI models, according to Gillin. Before trusting that pitch with AI automation, CIOs will want to know how agents are controlled, what audit trails they leave behind and how agent decisions can be documented for regulators, he noted.
“This is a very big issue with agents right now,” Gillin said. “It’s still a wild west out there with agents.”
Stay tuned for the complete video interview, part of SiliconANGLE’s and theCUBE’s coverage of EVOLVE26.

articles.title: Microsoft and others scramble to patch 'HTTP2Shell' flaw which could be the next PHP-level issue — Node.js problem may also affect millions of sites
articles.text:
Microsoft and others scramble to patch 'HTTP2Shell' flaw which could be the next PHP-level issue — Node.js problem may also affect millions of sites
An RCE flaw was found in Brotli
- A critical Brotli compression flaw, dubbed HTTP2Shell, could enable memory corruption and remote code execution
- The vulnerability affects widely used software including Node.js, Python packages, and .NET applications
- Vendors released patches, and administrators are urged to update immediately despite no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation
Multiple tech companies and projects have recently pushed patches for a vulnerability called “HTTP2Shell” which could enable remote code execution (RCE) attacks, similar to the recent “PHP2Shell” vulnerabilities.
HTTP2Shell was found in Brotli, a Google-built open source data compression algorithm that reduces file sizes without losing information, thus achieving faster transmission times while using less bandwidth.
It is a popular algorithm used on the web to compress HTTP responses such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and is supported by most web browsers, servers, and software libraries.
Fixes and patches
The bug itself is described as an out-of-bounds write flaw, and is also dubbed Node2Shell, and Broccoli2Shell. It is tracked as CVE-2026-111497, and was given a severity score of 9.2/10 (critical). According to the National Vulnerability Database, the bug causes a buffer overflow which could lead to memory disclosure, denial of service and, in some cases, even remote code execution.
Brotli can be found in all sorts of software, all of which is now at risk. That includes Node.js, brotlicffi, HTTP clients such as Requests, urllib3, httpx and aiohttp, but also other apps that use Brotli decoders such as Bun and Envoy deployments.
Google fixed the bug on October 21 2026, by releasing Brotli versions 1.0.10, 1.1.1, and 1.2.1. However, there are other software that either bundle or use vulnerable Brotli versions, so updating Google’s library alone may not protect every application.
Over the last weekend, Microsoft released an emergency update to sort the bug in .NET, saying successful exploitation could lead to privilege escalation.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Since it also bundles the Brodli decoder, Node.js released its patch on October 21, too. “An invalid block switch was reported as a temporary need for more input instead of a permanent format error, so the streaming decoder kept appending input bytes to an eight-byte internal buffer,” the organization explained. “An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with node:zlib can corrupt process memory, which can lead to a crash, disclosure of process memory, or remote code execution.”
The vulnerability was said to be affecting Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
BleepingComputer reports that PyPI packages containing the fixes became available two days later, on October 23.
Here is a detailed list of patched versions:
Google Brotli 1.0.10, 1.1.1, 1.2.1
Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1, 26.12.1
Python Brotli 1.2.1
Python brotlicffi 1.2.1.0
Dedicated website
At the same time, someone set up a dedicated website, Broccoli2Shell.com, which describes the issue, tracks vulnerable versions, and reports on attempted exploits in the wild. On the site, it is said that proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits for the bug already exist, but reports of malicious exploitation in the wild are yet to be seen.
“A public proof of concept appeared on GitHub on 2026-10-22,” the site reads. “It reportedly reaches code execution only on a deliberately weakened build. On standard builds it causes a crash and a limited memory read.”
System administrators are advised to apply the provided patches as soon as possible; restart affected processes and rebuild and redeploy affected container images.
Those that cannot do that immediately can somewhat mitigate the risks. Python users should uninstall the vulnerable Brotli and brotlicffi packages and remove optional dependencies such as httpx[brotli].
Admins can also configure proxies, load balancers or web application firewalls (WAF) to reject incoming requests containing Brotli-compressed bodies. It’s worth mentioning that this doesn’t protect apps that download and decompress malicious HTTP responses.
Node.js has no complete workaround, it was said.
