articles.title: Se filtra el iPhone 18e y esta sería la única razón real para comprarlo en 2027
articles.text:
Apple parece decidida a mantener la fórmula de su gama de entrada sin muchos cambios en 2027. Una nueva filtración reveló las principales características del iPhone 18e, el próximo móvil "barato" de la compañía que debutará en la primavera del próximo año. Los primeros datos anticipan que será más potente que su predecesor, pero el resto de especificaciones se mantendría en la misma cancha que el iPhone 17e.
El conocido filtrador Digital Chat Station reveló en su cuenta de Weibo que el iPhone 18e llegará con una pantalla LTPS OLED de 6,12 pulgadas. El móvil, que se presentaría junto con el iPhone 18 en marzo de 2027, ofrecería un panel similar al del modelo anterior, incluyendo la tasa de refresco a 60 Hz. Al parecer Apple sigue reservando los 120 Hz a sus modelos superiores, pese a que la mayoría de móviles de gama media ya incluyen esta característica por defecto.
El cambio más notable del iPhone 18e sería en el procesador. Los de Cupertino usarán un chip A20 de 2 nanómetros, que sería una versión recortada del A20 Pro que ya incluyen los iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max y el iPhone Duo. La versión Pro ofrece una CPU de seis núcleos, doble Neural Engine para tareas de IA y una memoria unificada de 12 GB. Si bien se desconocen las especificaciones finales del A20, los rumores apuntan a que el iPhone 18e llegará con 9 GB de RAM.
iPhone 18e: misma cámara trasera, pero un salto en las selfies
En el apartado fotográfico, el iPhone 18e contará con una cámara principal de 48 megapíxeles. El rumor no menciona detalles específicos, aunque podríamos esperar estabilización óptica de imagen, fotos en superalta resolución y otras características como flash True Tone, Photonic Engine y Deep Fusion. Donde sí habría cambios sería en la cámara frontal, en donde veríamos un salto a los 24 megapíxeles con control de enfoque y profundidad para los retratos.
Fuera de eso, Digital Chat Station no ofrece más datos, aunque algunos de ellos confirman lo que habíamos escuchado en filtraciones anteriores. Hace unos meses ya se hablaba de la combinación de chip A20, 9 GB de RAM y pantalla OLED de 60 Hz, e incluso se rumoreó que el móvil heredaría el módem C2 de Apple. También se ha dicho que el iPhone 18e le dirá adiós al notch en favor de la Isla Dinámica, aunque no hay más información que lo respalde.
Lo que sí sabemos es que Apple usará el iPhone 18e como el móvil de entrada para acceder a las nuevas funciones de Apple Intelligence. Aquellos que no puedan darse el lujo de gastar en un iPhone 18 Pro podrán comprarse esta variante para usar la inteligencia visual, la edición de fotos o las herramientas de escritura para resumir y redactar textos. Fuera de eso, las diferencias frente al iPhone 17e serían relativamente modestas, por lo que no valdría la pena actualizarse si ya tienes este modelo.
Por el momento no existe fecha definida para la presentación del iPhone 18e. Si nos ajustamos a la cadencia de lanzamientos de Cupertino, es probable que debute junto al iPhone 18 en algún momento de marzo de 2027. El precio sería parecido al del iPhone 17e en este momento, a menos que la crisis de memoria dicte lo contrario.

articles.title: Replit’s CEO says an idea from 1937 could make the org chart obsolete
articles.text:
Replit’s CEO says an idea from 1937 could make the org chart obsolete
Replit CEO and co-founder Amjad Masad has spent the past year watching AI agents absorb the routine execution inside his own company, and in a thread posted to X on Monday, he argues the same shift is bearing down on everyone else, with businesses moving toward a self-driving company where, in his words, “humans exercise judgment and agents execute most of the work.”
He rests the case on Ronald Coase’s 1937 question of why firms exist in the first place, the economist’s answer being that companies survive because coordinating work inside them beats coordinating it through open markets, and he contends AI agents are about to collapse the internal coordination costs — the management, the meetings, the reporting — that firms have swallowed as fixed for nearly a century.
In the thread, Masad posted, “The Rise of the Self-Driving Company,” in which he writes that “every company in the Fortune 500 will be a Self-Driving Company” by the end of 2030.
“Every company in the Fortune 500 will be a Self-Driving Company” by the end of 2030.
What the Agent Habitat is
Replit is moving toward that vision with Replit for Business, which gives AI agents access to company systems, data, and workflows while keeping permissions and approvals in place.
Masad calls the underlying concept the “Agent Habitat,” a space where agents can work with employees and one another without having unrestricted access to company resources. It’s still more of a blueprint; Replit has not yet published a full technical specification explaining how those controls would work together.
Why agent sprawl is risky
Masad is trying to solve a rising problem as companies deploy more AI agents. Many still operate through scattered chat windows, personal accounts, and custom scripts, often with whatever credentials and data employees give them. Companies have little visibility into what those agents can access or what they’ve done.
Giving agents more freedom might not be the answer, either. Recent research shows how easily coding agents can overstep their intended scope, even when doing legitimate work.
Replit’s Agent Habitat aims to strike a balance by giving agents access to the tools and data they need while enforcing permissions.
Replit’s Agent Habitat aims to strike a balance by giving agents access to the tools and data they need while enforcing permissions. Masad also wants companies to benefit from what their agents learn. If an employee corrects an agent, that feedback could become part of the instructions other agents follow. One team could reuse a workflow across the company rather than building it from scratch.
Keeping humans in control
On Tuesday, Replit moved closer to that vision with Cloud Agents, which let employees change a company’s codebase without setting up a development environment or needing to know how the application works behind the scenes.
Engineers still have the final say over what ships, but employees can bring them tested changes instead of waiting for someone to pick up a ticket.
Replit also lets administrators set up shared development environments, so employees don’t have to configure repositories, database, and services themselves. Credentials are managed centrally rather than distributed across teams, reflecting a trend that shifts away from long-lived credentials.
Cloud Agents and code reviews
The company is also experimenting with agents learning from code reviews. When an engineer flags a problem, Cloud Agents can suggest updates to the team’s shared instructions, called “skills,” so future agents can avoid making the same mistake. Engineers must approve those updates, and the feature remains in early access.
Replit says the shared instructions are already helping reduce costs. In its own testing, the company reported a 51% drop in token consumption and said a routine data task that previously took 16 minutes could be completed in one, without sacrificing output quality. That’s a notable improvement, especially since recent research has shown how much an agent’s performance depends on its harness and how it handles memory.
The company has also seen gains in its own engineering teams, where code output nearly tripled during the first half of 2026 without longer review times or an increase in reversions or production incidents. Agents are now being used beyond engineering, with designers building features, and support teams investigating customer issues.
Agents are now being used beyond engineering, with designers building features, and support teams investigating customer issues.
There are limits to those numbers. Replit hasn’t shared enough detail to independently verify the gains or separate the impact of agents from other changes to how its teams work. What works at an AI-native company like Replit could also be much harder to pull off at a large enterprise with decades of existing systems and processes.
Cloud Agents are now generally available to Pro and Enterprise customers, while skills remain in early access. The broader Agent Habitat vision is still taking shape, and Replit hasn’t yet demonstrated that agents can handle the kind of company-wide work Masad describes.

articles.title: EEUU acaba de revelar que China tiene un avión secreto orbitando en el espacio desde seis hace años
articles.text:
Durante años, una fotografía tomada en el espacio alimentó las sospechas de que China había conseguido desarrollar su propia versión de uno de los vehículos militares más secretos de Estados Unidos. La imagen circulaba por internet, había aparecido incluso en una presentación de la Fuerza Espacial estadounidense y nadie había confirmado públicamente qué mostraba exactamente. Ahora, un informe de la inteligencia militar de Washington ha resuelto el misterio: Pekín dispone de un avión espacial reutilizable extraordinariamente parecido al X-37B estadounidense.
Y los detalles que han salido a la luz apuntan a una nueva dimensión de la rivalidad entre las potencias.
Años esperando una respuesta. En 2024, el coronel John Patrick, entonces responsable de las Fuerzas Espaciales estadounidenses en Corea del Sur, mostró durante una conferencia una imagen de baja resolución de un misterioso vehículo en órbita. Su aspecto recordaba tanto al X-37B que ni siquiera estaba claro si la fotografía mostraba un aparato chino o uno de los dos pequeños transbordadores operados por Estados Unidos.
El medio especializado The War Zone solicitó entonces explicaciones a la Fuerza Espacial y a Maxar, la empresa propietaria del satélite que había captado la imagen. Ambas organizaciones rechazaron hacer comentarios. La fotografía permaneció así durante más de dos años como una de las pistas más intrigantes sobre el programa espacial militar chino.
La confirmación. La Agencia de Inteligencia de Defensa de Estados Unidos (DIA) ha publicado un informe desclasificado hace unas horas sobre los desafíos de seguridad fuera de la atmósfera terrestre, un informe que incluye una versión de mayor resolución de aquella fotografía. El documento identifica expresamente el aparato como un avión espacial de la República Popular China y explica que estos vehículos pueden colocar objetos en órbita, realizar experimentos y regresar a la Tierra para reutilizarse.
La imagen muestra una pequeña nave con alas, dos estabilizadores verticales, una bodega central de carga con puertas que se abren hacia arriba y estructuras solares desplegadas en la parte posterior. Su configuración resulta extraordinariamente similar a la del X-37B estadounidense, aunque las alas del vehículo chino presentan una geometría diferente. Dicho de otra forma, la confirmación oficial despeja la duda sobre la identidad del aparato, sin demostrar que Washington desconociera previamente su origen.
Un satélite lo fotografió a solo 90 kilómetros. La actualización publicada por TWZ aporta un detalle especialmente revelador: Vantor, la antigua Maxar, ha confirmado que la fotografía fue tomada el 28 de mayo de 2024 por su satélite WorldView-3, situado a menos de 90 kilómetros del vehículo chino. La empresa también ha identificado un segundo satélite acoplado a la sección posterior del avión espacial, con su estructura y paneles solares visibles.
Uno de los grandes misterios tiene que ver con las puertas de la bodega de carga que aparecen claramente abiertas en el momento de la captura. La escena demuestra hasta qué punto los sistemas de observación orbital pueden vigilarse entre sí y documentar operaciones que sus responsables mantienen fuera del conocimiento público. También plantea preguntas sobre la naturaleza del objeto acoplado y las actividades que estaba realizando la nave.
Seis años enviando su avión secreto al espacio. Desde 2020, Pekín ha realizado cuatro misiones orbitales con un vehículo experimental reutilizable que se cree que corresponde al fotografiado. La tercera comenzó el 14 de diciembre de 2023 y terminó el 6 de septiembre de 2024, después de casi nueve meses en órbita. Durante ese periodo se detectó la liberación de varios objetos pequeños cuya función sigue sin conocerse. La cuarta misión despegó el 7 de febrero de 2026 y, según la información disponible, continuaba activa a finales de octubre, después de haber liberado al menos otro objeto.
Los vuelos anteriores terminaron aparentemente en una instalación militar del noroeste de China equipada con una pista de aproximadamente cinco kilómetros, una de las más largas del mundo. El complejo ha experimentado una importante expansión y también se utiliza para ensayar otras tecnologías aeronáuticas avanzadas.
El parecido con el X-37B. Estados Unidos lleva utilizando sus dos aviones espaciales X-37B desde 2010 y ha desarrollado ocho misiones orbitales, la última iniciada el 22 de agosto de 2025. Estos vehículos despegan mediante cohetes, permanecen durante largos periodos en el espacio y regresan aterrizando como aviones convencionales. Su diseño permite transportar cargas experimentales, desplegar equipos y ejecutar maniobras orbitales.
El informe de la DIA identifica dos grandes proyectos chinos, Shenlong y Tengyun, sin precisar a cuál pertenece el vehículo fotografiado. Shenlong es el nombre habitualmente asociado al aparato experimental que China lleva lanzando desde 2020, mientras que Tengyun fue presentado en 2016 como un sistema de dos etapas que utilizaría un avión nodriza para facilitar el acceso al espacio. Pekín también desarrolla el Haolong, concebido para transportar suministros a su estación espacial Tiangong.
La verdadera preocupación. Los aviones espaciales reutilizables permiten desplegar pequeños satélites, recuperar experimentos y modificar sus trayectorias para aproximarse a otros objetos orbitales. Estas capacidades resultan especialmente valiosas para misiones de inteligencia, inspección y vigilancia, y también podrían utilizarse para interferir con satélites adversarios o desarrollar sistemas antisatélite.
El hecho de que la nave china haya liberado objetos durante sus misiones y aparezca fotografiada con otro satélite acoplado refuerza el interés militar de estas operaciones, aunque ninguna de esas observaciones demuestra por sí misma que haya desarrollado actividades ofensivas. La DIA destaca precisamente la maniobrabilidad y reutilización de estos vehículos como ventajas frente a determinadas plataformas espaciales tradicionales.
La nueva carrera militar. China está invirtiendo en satélites de inteligencia, vehículos reutilizables y cohetes capaces de recuperar sus primeras etapas, tecnologías que pueden reducir los costes de lanzamiento y facilitar operaciones espaciales más frecuentes. Estados Unidos lleva años desarrollando capacidades similares y ambos países consideran cada vez más importante proteger sus infraestructuras orbitales.
La fotografía de WorldView-3 resume esa transformación. Un satélite comercial estadounidense consiguió observar a corta distancia un vehículo experimental chino mientras realizaba una operación cuyo propósito sigue siendo desconocido, y la confirmación de la DIA ha permitido identificar finalmente al protagonista de aquella imagen. El interrogante que permanece abierto es qué estaba haciendo exactamente a cientos de kilómetros de la Tierra y qué papel tendrán estas naves en un posible enfrentamiento entre las dos potencias.

articles.title: Foundations of Power Management in the Age of AI
articles.text:
Home >
                                                                    Systems & Design >
                                                                Foundations of Power Management in the Age of AI                                                    
Systems & Design
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
Make every layer of your hardware PDN-aware and reach your maximum compute density.
								October 28th, 2026 - 
								By: Movellus
								
							
In an AI datacenter, 50 mV of voltage margin can be worth about 270 racks of compute per gigawatt of input electricity. To show how, this paper models two facilities that run the same Vera Rubin NVL72 racks at the same clock speeds, one at 0.80 V and one at 0.75 V. On published Vera Rubin power figures, the second draws about 8% less power per GPU and about 17 kW less per rack.
Margin is the supply voltage added above what the silicon needs to cover the worst-case voltage droop. Evolving AI workloads make that margin larger and harder to predict. As a result, platform and silicon teams often over-margin to compensate, costing them compute density and token throughput, while teams that margin too little see failures in the field.
Power delivery network (PDN) design in the age of AI takes a systematic approach to power management. This paper distills the foundation of that approach into four axioms, drawn from work with customers in AI and high-performance computing (HPC).
AXIOM 1: Test error must be minimized
AXIOM 2: Power envelopes must factor in both evolving workloads and PDN dynamics
AXIOM 3: AI systems require reactive or preemptive Ldi/dt (droop) mitigation
AXIOM 4: Co-architected control loops are a necessity for systems
Movellus addresses the four axioms in one stack through its Aeonic platform. The platform helps teams set the foundation of proper power architecture in the age of AI.

articles.title: Regal debuts Goal Oriented Agents, putting an actor and a director model on every call - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Regal debuts Goal Oriented Agents, putting an actor and a director model on every call
Enterprise voice artificial intelligence company Regal Voice Inc. today added Goal Oriented Agents to its platform, enabling businesses using them to define what a call has to accomplish, and providing two AI models that split the work of getting there.
The new agents are aimed at a problem Regal says shows up in calls such as auto insurance claims, in which someone reporting an accident tends to explain what happened, where and who was involved in one go. Agents built on conditional logic often circle back for details the caller already gave, just so each field gets filled. Building the whole agent on a single prompt keeps the conversation open, and in Regal’s view it leaves business processes only loosely followed.
Goal Oriented Agents put two models on each call. Regal calls them an actor and a director, and both start work as soon as the caller stops talking. The actor, a smaller and faster model tuned for dialogue, replies right away. Running behind it, the director checks whether the goals for the current stage have been met and can move the call to a new stage with fresh instructions for the actor.
Businesses build the agents out of goal nodes, each listing the goals to be met by the end of the node and any prerequisites that come first. Booking a callback can count as one of those goals. A prerequisite is something the agent has to establish before it can act, such as the caller’s date of birth. Regal said those can be written as plain-language conditions too, for example “the caller mentioned a death in the family.”
The director reviews progress after every turn, so one answer can tick off several items at once. Regal’s sample auto insurance claim has a caller named Dan describing the vehicle damage, photo evidence and injuries in his first message. All three get marked as collected, and the agent goes straight to his name. Once it has that, the director sees location and policy number are still missing, so the actor’s next question is where he is.
Regal said complex intake and qualification calls are among the strongest uses it has seen for the agents. The company named Medicare enrollment, roadside assistance and mortgage qualification as uses the design opens up. Medical intake that complies with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act is another.
Google LLC, AAA and Toyota Motor Corp. are among the more than 200 enterprises Regal says it serves. Customers of Five9 Inc.’s contact center platform gained access to Regal’s voice agents through an integration in August.
Regal is a venture capital-backed startup that has raised $83 million to date. That includes a $40 million round in October 2024.

articles.title: Endlich Ruhe im Büro: Dieser Meeting-Simulator täuscht Video-Calls vor
articles.text:
Meeting-Simulator: So täuschst du wichtige Video-Calls vor
Wer am Freitagnachmittag vor dem PC im Büro sitzt und alle Arbeiten für die Woche abgeschlossen hat, fragt sich sicherlich: Wie bringe ich die Zeit bis zum Feierabend noch rum? Wie wäre es damit, die lieben Kolleg:innen etwas zu schocken? Etwa, indem du ein sehr wichtiges Meeting vorgaukelst, zu dem nur du eingeladen wurdest.
Funktionsweise der Meeting-Simulation für den Büroalltag
Dabei will dir die Webseite „Sorry, I’m in a meeting“ weiterhelfen. Es handelt sich im Grunde um einen Simulator für eine Reihe von wichtigen Anrufen. Diese reichen von Calls, bei denen das ganze Unternehmen für den Quartalsbericht zusammenkommt, über Meetings zu Status-Updates des aktuellen Projekts bis zu Ransomware-Krisensitzungen, weil alle Daten im Unternehmen verschlüsselt wurden.
Du trägst einfach deinen Namen in den Simulator ein, der während des Meetings in einer Videokachel angezeigt werden soll. Sobald der Fake-Termin startet, öffnet die Webseite eine Video-Call-Ansicht im Vollbild mit mehreren Fake-Personen darin. Die Videoübertragung ist dabei „deaktiviert“, sodass du nur Stimmen anderer Teilnehmer:innen hörst. Diese wurden KI-generiert. Jedes Meeting ist etwa zwölf Minuten lang, wobei du beim Starten zu unterschiedlichen Zeiten hineingeworfen wirst, sodass die Aufnahme nicht immer offensichtlich an derselben Stelle beginnt.
Anwendungsmöglichkeiten der Fake-Termine im Kalender-Management
Zudem kannst du in den Einstellungen die Option „Back-to-Back Meetings“ aktivieren. Dadurch startet nach dem Ende des ersten Meetings direkt der nächste Termin, sodass die Aufnahme nicht wieder von vorn startet. Alternativ kannst du im Meeting auf „I have to drop“ klicken. Dadurch verabschieden sich alle Fake-Teilnehmer:innen und du kannst das Meeting zu einem glaubwürdigen Ende bringen.
Die Webseite bietet sogar eine Funktion, um dir Meetings in deinem Kalender anzulegen. Du kannst im unteren Bereich der Seite ein Meeting auswählen, einen Titel sowie Datum und Uhrzeit festlegen und daraus eine ICS‑Datei oder Termineinträge für den Google-Kalender oder Outlook generieren. Dabei kannst du auch festlegen, ob ein Beitrittslink in der Mail enthalten sein soll und ob andere im Unternehmen den Terminnamen sehen können. Natürlich handelt es sich dabei um ein spaßiges Tool, das nicht wirklich aktiv zur Überbrückung der Arbeitszeit genutzt werden sollte. Aber es reicht allemal, um den anderen Kolleg:innen vorzugaukeln, man hätte ein wichtiges Meeting ohne die anderen.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 16.10.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.
Gab mal eine IT-Crowd-Folge (glaub ich), wo der frisch eingestellte Manager hastig zum Telefon griff und so tat als würde er telefonieren, als jemand sein Büro betrat. Stellte sich raus, es war der Techniker, der sein Telefon anschließen sollte.

articles.title: Investable.Africa launches platform to connect African startups with investors - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
African startup funding platform Investable.Africa has launched in open beta, giving founders access to a database of more than 4,000 investing firms and investors free access to deal flow from all 54 African countries.
Investable.Africa grew out of a WhatsApp group founder Craig McLeod – who also runs online store builder BoxCommerce – has run for the past decade as both a venture capitalist and a founder. The group brings African founders and VCs together with three aims – increasing funding into Africa, eliminating bad term sheets, and helping founders build the networks they need.
“For 10 years I’ve watched great African founders struggle to reach the right investors, and sign terms they didn’t need to accept,” said McLeod. “The group showed what happens when founders and investors talk openly. Investable.Africa takes that to every founder on the continent, not just the ones who already have the right phone numbers.”
The platform allows founders to build a profile covering their problem, solution, traction, team and current round, with every profile checked by the Investable.Africa team before going live. Founders can upload a pitch deck, which only approved investors can open, and a data room, with founders deciding who sees which folders.
Founders can search the investor database by stage, cheque size, sector, lead or follow, ownership target, founder focus and location, with each firm’s partners and contact routes listed. The database is built from public lists, which are credited openly. Founders can also connect Claude, ChatGPT or another AI assistant to the database to shortlist firms that fit their round and draft personalised outreach for review.
Founders can see who has viewed their profile, opened their deck or read a file, post updates to investors following them, and receive messages from investors addressed to the whole founding team.
Investors use the platform for free, and are vetted before they can see full profiles and decks. They can filter startups by region, country, sector, stage, round type and raise size, or view only companies currently raising. A deal flow overview brings together matching startups, open access requests, data rooms and updates, while investors can request data rooms with a short note explaining their interest and follow startups to receive founder updates by email.
Investors can also list their own firm in the database, and can buy vouchers to sponsor a founder’s listing for a year, with credit as the sponsor.
Founders can build a profile for free, with a listing costing US$99 a month or US$299 per year. Investable.Africa takes no share of any raise and does not handle investment money.

articles.title: Jio Platforms gains 27% on day one of listing, becomes second most valued company in India
articles.text:
Jio Platforms gains 27% on day one of listing, becomes second most valued company in India
Jio Platforms exceeded market expectations with a 26.81% gain on day one of listing and a market capitalisation of Rs 13 lakh crore.
After making a strong debut on the National Stock Exchange today, the shares of Jio Platforms closed at Rs 1,419, at a gain of 26.81%.
Jio Platforms achieved a market capitalisation of Rs 13,06,761.47 crore on its first day of trading, making it the second most valued company on the Indian stock markets, next only only to its parent firm Reliance Industries.
The top five Indian companies in terms of market capitalisation now are: Reliance Industries (Rs 16 lakh crore), Jio Platforms (Rs 13 lakh crore), Bharti Airtel (Rs 12 lakh crore), HDFC Bank (Rs 10.57 lakh crore), and ICICI Bank (Rs 9.89 lakh crore). Tata Consultancy Services has moved to the sixth place (Rs 8.90 lakh crore).
Jio Platforms' share opened at Rs 1,358 today, gaining 21.3% over the issue price of Rs 1,119 apiece.
The company's Rs 30,213-crore IPO received an overwhelming response from investors last week. It was oversubscribed in less than two hours on opening day, and closed with a 22X oversubscription.
As it positions itself as a technology firm, Jio Platforms is betting on digital services, artificial intelligence, and cloud computing to drive growth beyond telecom.
"There is no either-or at Jio: the network is our technology," said Akash Ambani, Managing Director of Jio Platforms, highlighting the company's in-house 5G core, cloud-native radio access network, and software platform serving 533.3 million customers.
“Connectivity was the first product we built on that platform. Digital services, AI and cloud are what we are layering on top of it now," he said.
Meanwhile, brokerage houses are bullish on the prospects of Jio Platforms.
Motilal Oswal, in its note, said scaling up digital platforms (cloud, enterprise communications, IoT, and managed services, along with international tie-ups for 5G/UBR technology) will offer Jio Platforms the next leg of growth beyond the connectivity business.
The brokerage house has set a bull-case target price of Rs 1,690 crore and a bear-case target price of Rs 1,035.

articles.title: “The panic hasn’t turned into patching”: What security researchers really think about the PHP2Shell response
articles.text:
“The panic hasn’t turned into patching”: What security researchers really think about the PHP2Shell response
The PHP panic has not turned to patching: And that’s bad news, capital B, as PHP2Shell attacks ramp up.
We know the paired PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, aka PHP2Shell, have a Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) score of 9.2, which is scary bad. After all, about 70% of websites with an identifiable server-side language run on PHP-based systems like WordPress.
But does that mean people are patching their servers as fast as they can?
To quote Moshe Siman Tov Bustan of Ox security: “The panic hasn’t turned into patching.” Ox reports in a new blog post that of October 26, five days after disclosure, the picture has barely shifted – 93.6% still exposed.“
Wow! Ow!
“…remediation isn’t in panic state, it barely crawls, with more headlines than fixed instances in the wild”
Bustan goes on to write, “Remediation is too slow, while everyone panics about PHP CVEs, remediation isn’t in panic state, it barely crawls, with more headlines than fixed instances in the wild… we missed the opportunity to actually get our patches out the door – and now, when exploits are out there, proven in the wild and not just speculation – we’ve left our most precious assets exposed for the next hacker to take advantage of.”
We really do like living dangerously, don’t we?
It’s not just Ox reporting abysmal PHP2Shell patch numbers. Censys, a security company, in its PHP2Shell survey as of Tuesday, reports that about 11.2 million Internet-facing PHP services are reporting patched versions. That’s not as impressive as it sounds. These counts are based on the PHP versions servers report, and because Linux distributions often backport fixes without changing the version number, some “vulnerable” services may already be patched.
Some 32.5 million are still showing they’re running unsafe PHP versions. Censys also doesn’t know what 61,303,506 PHP services (58% of all detected) are running. Many of these are likely to be running unsupported versions of PHP.
That’s scary news. The security company Flare found that of the 2.2 million PHP service records it tracked in an October 22nd report, “nearly three quarters advertised a PHP branch no longer supported by the PHP project.”
Another study of 2.6 million services by Mallory, a security firm that uses AI to track Internet dangers, found about 1.9 million internet-facing services running unsupported PHP versions. That’s about 73.5% of the surveyed services.
Such systems get no official patch release. They must be updated to a supported version.
Such systems get no official patch release. They must be updated to a supported version. That’s a much more involved job than simply patching a supported version of PHP.
As Ramy Rahman, senior principal solutions engineer at ArmorCode, an AI security company, said in a statement on Tuesday, “The reality is that many organizations are likely running older, unsupported versions, which introduces the additional complexity of upgrading applications, addressing compatibility issues, or working with vendors to obtain supported fixes.”
Be that as it may, as the National Security Agency (NSA) says when PHP2Shell first appeared, “All organizations using PHP for their systems are advised to be prepared for an update addressing two critical vulnerabilities …. If an immediate update is not feasible, it is recommended that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.“
Clearly, while some organizations have done so, such as the Wikimedia Foundation and Internet Archive, and two PHP-driven online games have closed down permanently, most did not. Meanwhile, some governments have made patching mandatory. The biggest example is the US. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) made PHP2Shell remediation mandatory for Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies, with a deadline of Thursday, October 29, 2026.
That’s easier said than done. As we’re seeing, PHP2Shell attacks are now ongoing. CISA hasn’t given any details, but the CVE reports are now listed in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
In addition, Adel Karimi, a Paerplexity AI‘s detection and response lead, says his honeypots recorded evidence of confirmed remote code execution against an Apache mod_php installation running PHP 8.4.26, a vulnerable pre-patch version. Karimi cautioned that his single-worker setup was deliberately favorable to attackers.
That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post-announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now.
And, as Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince posted on X, “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the @Cloudflare network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it. That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post-announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now.”
It’s only getting worse. Soon this wave of attempts will become a flood of successful attacks. Fasten your seatbelts, it’s going to be a bumpy ride.

articles.title: Bizum sigue ganándole terreno a las tarjetas de crédito y podrá ser utilizado para pagar en los supermercados Eroski
articles.text:
Los supermercados de España ya no solo compiten a través de sus lineales, precios y catálogos de marca blanca. Ahora lo hacen en las formas de pago, las opciones de las que disponemos los clientes a la hora de abonar el ticket. A los medios de cobro habituales (efectivo y tarjetas) y plataformas digitales como Google Pay o Apple Pay se suma poco a poco Bizum. El ejemplo más reciente acaba de dejarlo Grupo Eroski, tanto en sus locales como los de Caprabo.
Al incorporar Bizum a sus métodos de cobro, se suman a una creciente lista de cadenas que ya lo están usando (en mayor o menor medida) o tanteando, como Mercadona o Lidl, además de grandes firmas de moda y restauración.
¿Qué ha pasado? Que Bizum va abriéndose paso para dejar de ser únicamente una forma de transferir dinero entre particulares (el uso que la ha hecho popular) y convertirse en un método de pago en comercios, pugnando con titanes como los estadounidenses Visa, Mastercard y American Express.
La semana pasada Grupo Eroski anunció que ha incorporado “Bizum presencial” como una nueva forma de pago en sus tiendas. Y el lunes la cadena catalana Caprabo (de la misma matriz) confirmaba un movimiento similar, extendiendo Bizum tanto a sus supermercados físicos como al canal digital.
¿Cómo lo implantarán? Grupo Eroski explica que los pagos con Bizum ya están disponibles en Caprabo. En el resto de su red comercial el servicio se irá desplegando de manera gradual. Además, al menos en una primera fase, estará limitado negocio de la alimentación, sin incluir Forum Sport ni gasolineras.
“Su extensión al resto de la Península y Baleares se realizará progresivamente de acuerdo con la disponibilidad de Bizum presencial entre las diferentes entidades bancarias”, aclara la compañía. “Se integra en el proceso habitual de pago sin modificar la operativa del personal de caja, de forma que es la propia persona consumidora quien puede elegir el método de pago digital que desea. Para usarla será necesario que la entidad bancaria del cliente tenga habilitado este servicio".
¿Es la primera cadena en hacerlo? Para nada. Lidl se lanzó a probar los pagos con Bizum ya en 2023 y, desde entonces, han hecho algo parecido diferentes cadenas de supermercados, moda o restauración.
Hace unos días Expansión reveló que Inditex, Ikea, Carrefour, Eroski, Alcampo y Burger King han abierto las puertas a Bizum Pay, una lista amplia que podría crecer en no mucho tiempo. El diario económico asegura que, tras un plan piloto hace unos meses en Soria, Mercadona se prepara para su despliegue total. Otra gran cadena que estaría preparándose para incorporarla es El Corte Inglés.
¿Por qué es importante? Por varias razones. La primera es que anuncios como el de Grupo Eroski y Caprabo demuestran la expansión de Bizum en el tejido comercial, en el que aspira a operar como una herramienta de pago más. De hecho, este verano la plataforma presentó Bizum Pay, una cartera digital que permite realizar abonos en tiendas aproximando el móvil a un TPV, un gesto similar al que hacemos al usar tarjetas o los servicios de Google y Apple Pay.
Hace poco la plataforma presumía de que "el pago presencial con Bizum" está disponible ya para el 60% de sus usuarios, lo que equivale a casi 20 millones de personas. Según sus cálculos, ya lo aceptan 1,6 millones de establecimientos, “lo que representa en torno al 75% de los terminales bancarios”.
¿Tan diferente es? Aunque a simple vista puede parecer que no hay grandes diferencias entre utilizar Bizum Pay y otras herramientas muy implantadas en España, como Google Pay o Apple Pay, la nueva aplicación tiene una peculiaridad importante. Bizum Pay no exige vincularse necesariamente a una tarjeta física.
Puede usarse la cuenta bancaria, desde la que se realizan transferencias inmediatas entre cuentas. El pago, aclara la compañía, puede realizarse "directamente desde la cuenta o con una tarjeta". Es decir, el usuario activa la app en el móvil, la acerca al datáfono y paga. Sin tarjeta. Ni números de teléfono, como sí ocurre con las transferencias de dinero entre particulares.
¿Es importante? Sí. Entre otras cosas porque convierte a Bizum en un potencial competidor de grandes multinacionales estadounidenses, como Visa, Mastercard y American Express. Con todo, y a pesar de movimientos como los de Eroski, Caprabo o Mercadona, Bizum Pay no lo tendrá fácil para expandirse.
Aunque la compañía asegura que su despliegue avanza tanto en las cadenas como pequeños y medianos negocios, una visita a comercios y restaurantes demuestra que aún está lejos de ser una opción tan popular como el pago con tarjeta de crédito, efectivo u otros métodos que se basan en los móviles.
¿Manejamos datos? Sí. Los informes del Banco de España muestran también que Bizum Pay deberá abrirse paso en un nicho de negocio con hábitos muy asentados. A finales de 2025, el regulador estimaba que el efectivo seguía siendo el principal medio de pago en los establecimientos para el 57% de la población, frente al 27% que señalaba las tarjetas y el 15% que recurría al móvil.
Bizum también sale en las estadísticas, pero como forma de pago entre particulares. De hecho, es el favorito entre los menores de 45 años y el segundo en general, por detrás del efectivo. El tiempo dirá si decisiones como las de Eroski y Caprabo le permiten trasladar ese dominio a los supermercados.

articles.title: Fim de um tabu: Apple prepara MacBook com tela touch
articles.text:
A Apple deve apresentar seus primeiros MacBooks com tela sensível ao toque nesta quarta-feira, após anos de resistência ao recurso. O lançamento faz parte de uma sequência de novidades da empresa antes da temporada de compras de fim de ano.
O evento em Los Angeles também pode encerrar uma discussão antiga: a inclusão de telas sensíveis ao toque na linha de computadores da marca.
Apple revê posição histórica
Em 2010, Steve Jobs classificou telas sensíveis ao toque em notebooks como “terríveis do ponto de vista ergonômico”. Dois anos depois, Tim Cook, então CEO da empresa, comparou a combinação de tecnologias diferentes à tentativa de juntar uma torradeira e uma geladeira.
A concorrência seguiu outro caminho. Notebooks com Windows oferecem o recurso há mais de uma década, enquanto uma nova geração de consumidores se acostumou a interagir diretamente com as telas de celulares e tablets.
Para Anshel Sag, analista da Moor Insights & Strategy, a resistência da Apple estava equivocada. “Acredito que eles sempre estiveram errados ao resistir ao toque, e agora a realidade está se impondo”, afirmou. “Algumas coisas são simplesmente inevitáveis.”
Novos MacBooks podem manter chips atuais
A apresentação acontece após o lançamento do iPhone Duo, em setembro, e de um hub doméstico inteligente no início deste mês.
Nesta semana, a Apple anunciou uma versão atualizada do MacBook Pro de entrada com chip M6. Segundo a Bloomberg News, os modelos com tela sensível ao toque devem utilizar os processadores M5 Pro e M5 Max, já presentes em versões atuais do notebook. Por isso, não devem trazer um salto significativo de desempenho.
A questão é relevante porque parte do crescimento recente das vendas de Macs vem de empresas e entusiastas que utilizam os computadores para executar tarefas de inteligência artificial (IA) localmente.
Jason Calacanis, comentarista de tecnologia e apresentador do podcast All-In, destacou essa prioridade em uma publicação no X: “A única coisa que as pessoas querem é mais memória e processadores melhores para modelos locais!”
A chegada do toque pode mudar a forma de interação com os MacBooks. Resta saber se o recurso será suficiente para atrair consumidores que também esperam melhorias no desempenho dos computadores.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Hyphenate bags $45M in funding to accelerate autonomous financial operations - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Hyphenate bags $45M in funding to accelerate autonomous financial operations
A startup called Hyphenate says it’s quickly helping enterprises to overcome their fear of artificial intelligence hallucinations and trust it to fully automate their financial operations after raising $45 million in early-stage funding today.
The Series A round was led by Nexus Venture Partners and saw participation from B Capital and existing backers Foundation Capital, BoldCap and Gaia Ventures, bringing the startup’s total amount raised to date to $54 million.
Hyphenate, officially known as Prosperous Commerce Inc., has built an autonomous finance platform that uses self-learning AI agents. Those agents are designed to familiarize themselves with businesses’ financial operations so that they can take over the work of the traditional chief financial officer, performing tasks such as general ledger accounting, treasury management, order-to-cash, procure-to-pay and financial reporting. Its agents integrate with companies’ existing enterprise resource planning, accounting and banking systems to avoid the need for expensive software overhauls.
The startup, which was previously called Maximor until it rebranded earlier this month, is led by co-founder and Chief Executive Ramnandan Krishnamurthy (pictured, right, alongside co-founder Ajay Krishna Amudan), who concedes that corporate finance has always been extremely challenging for AI to get a handle on. Because of unforgiving regulatory requirements and financial reporting standards, few CFOs have been willing to tolerate the risk of AI agents that could potentially hallucinate and mess up vital calculations regarding their finances.
In a recent study, Hyphenate highlighted the widespread apprehension of CFOs regarding AI. Though 96% of survey respondents identified alleviating the burden of repetitive and manual tasks as one of AI’s major benefits, only 14% said they actually trust the technology to do that without making mistakes. Moreover, 97% of CFOs insisted that human supervision of AI work is essential.
However, Hyphenate believes it can overcome this apprehensiveness by changing the way AI agents learn and execute their work. Rather than asking human financial experts to create prompts and design rule-based workflows for agents, the startup trains them on customer’s historical financial workflows.
By looking at thousands of spreadsheets, email trails, financial records, invoices and so on that date back years, its agents aim to capture what Krishnamurthy calls the “tribal knowledge” of each company’s financial department.. That enables them to understand the peculiarities of their operations.
Moreover, Hyphenate also creates a detailed record of its agents’ work, so that every autonomous action they make is preserved, building an evidentiary paper trail that can easily be audited if the need arises. Should a human financial officer handle an exception, the agents will remember that decision as a kind of precedent, so that they can follow that example with their future work. This is backed by unambiguous operational guardrails and a requirement for human oversight at key moments, when qualitative judgment is required, Krishnamurthy said.
“Every finance team has a long list of work it does because somebody has to do it,” Krishnamurthy said. “Our customers are watching that list shrink in production. Once a team sees the system handle one workflow to an auditor’s standard, they hand it the next one.”
In other words, Krishnamurthy says, customers generally test Hyphenate’s AI agents with one or two financial tasks, see that they do the job perfectly, and start to trust it more. They then give it much greater responsibilities. It’s a pattern that has been repeated at multiple early adapters, Krishnamurthy said, enabling the startup to grow its customer base by 11 times and its revenue by 86 times in the last year, though it didn’t provide more specifics.
Hyphenate says it currently counts six publicly traded companies as customers, including Groupon Inc., Synthesia Ltd., HiBid and Mini Melts USA Inc. Those clients have eliminated up to 90% of their routine manual financial work, while reducing audit exceptions by an average of 75%.
One of its most eager adopters is HiBid, which has used Hyphenate to process more than $2.5 billion in gross merchandise value so far, while reducing the time it spends on month-end closing from three weeks to a day. Nexus Venture Partners’ Abhishek Sharma said Hyphenate’s success so far is due to its laser focus on accuracy, controls and auditability. “Hyphenate has built around that bar from the beginning and the expansion we are seeing inside customer deployments shows what becomes possible once the system earns the right to take on more work,” he said.
Given its early traction, Hyphenate now has much bigger ambitions, setting its sights on automating strategic financial operations for its customers. It believes it can provide continuous visibility into a company’s financial health, enabling more precise forecasting and capital allocation.

articles.title: Reicht schon ein Macbook mit M1? Diese Hardware brauchst du für lokale KI
articles.text:
Reicht schon ein Macbook mit M1? Diese Hardware brauchst du für lokale KI
Es gibt viele gute Gründe, KI-Modelle herunterzuladen und lokal auf dem eigenen Computer zu betreiben. Ihr behaltet die Hoheit über eure Daten. Nichts wandert in die Cloud eines US‑Anbieters. Weil die Künstliche Intelligenz direkt auf dem Gerät arbeitet, braucht sie schließlich keinen Zugang zum Internet, um zu funktionieren. Und für den vollumfänglichen Zugriff müsst ihr auch kein Abo abschließen.
Je nach Modell kann euch die KI direkt auf dem Speicher wie gewohnt beim Formulieren von Texten, beim Coden oder bei der Bilderstellung zur Seite stehen. Verknüpft man das Modell mit agentenbasierter Software wie Hermes, kann es auch Aufgaben auf dem Computer erledigen, etwa den Download-Ordner aufräumen.
All das klingt gut, ist aber nicht immer ganz trivial. Denn wie gut so ein lokales Modell läuft, hängt entscheidend von der Hardware ab, die euch zur Verfügung steht – oder vom Budget, falls ihr einen Neukauf plant.

The growing role of AI in analog and mixed-signal design, where complexity is rising, schedules are tightening, and the cost of mistakes is higher than ever.
								October 28th, 2026 -

This white paper examines the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in analog and mixed-signal (AMS) design, where complexity is rising, schedules are tightening, and the cost of mistakes is higher than ever. Drawing on Cadence’s structured AI maturity roadmap and paired with the Virtuoso AI Studio platform, the paper makes the case: AI is no longer a futureworld for analog designers, it has become a present-day engineering tool. From ML-powered engines to conversational design assistance to autonomous, multi-agent workflows, the paper charts a path from where the industry stands today to where it is headed. It also shows how AI can reduce non-differentiating work, accelerate simulation and migration tasks, and serve as a force multiplier for engineers at every experience level, all within a secure, enterprise-ready environment.

articles.title: Nebius cut rollout collection time by 66.9% — here’s what changed
articles.text:
Nebius cut rollout collection time by 66.9% — here’s what changed
In AI agent training, you can pay for powerful GPUs and still spend much of your time waiting. Agents need to attempt tasks and produce results before the model can learn from them. A few slow attempts can hold up the next training update, making the systems that run those tasks a major factor in training speed and cost.
Di Jin, VP of AI Training at Amsterdam-headquartered Nebius, says teams coming from pretraining or supervised fine-tuning can underestimate the work these systems do.
“If you staff and design it as a training project, inference becomes the bottleneck nobody owns.”
Rollout generation often takes most of a training step’s wall-clock time, making batching, cache management and scheduling central to how fast the model can learn. “If you staff and design it as a training project, inference becomes the bottleneck nobody owns,” Jin says.
Time to a trainable batch
He adds that engineers should measure time to a trainable batch alongside throughput. Average tokens per second can hide the long tail: in a synchronous batch, the step cannot finish until the final trajectory is completed.
Agent trajectories do not all have the same length. Many finish quickly, while others take longer, leaving training GPUs waiting on a handful of stragglers. For this reason, Jin advises engineers to treat the inference engine as part of the post-training reinforcement learning optimizer.
Data misunderstood
Learning from data generated by an older model version involves a tradeoff. Some policy lag can improve GPU efficiency by letting generation and training overlap, Jin says, but its safety depends on how much the policy has changed and how the training algorithm handles the difference.
Jin tells The New Stack, “In fully synchronous RL, inference GPUs wait while training runs, and training GPUs wait while generation runs. Letting generation use weights that are one or a few updates old allows both to run in parallel. That overlap is how most large-scale systems reach reasonable utilization.” When success on a hard task is rare, he adds, an already successful trajectory can be valuable to reuse even if it is slightly stale.
Staleness becomes harmful when the policy that generated a trajectory has drifted too far from the policy being trained. The useful measure is divergence, not a universal limit on how many training steps old the data can be.
“Staleness isn’t the enemy. Unmeasured staleness is.”
Rather than seeking to eradicate old data, engineers and organizations should measure and manage staleness. They can apply importance-sampling corrections, usually truncated to limit variance; drop or down-weight samples beyond a staleness threshold; and track divergence between the generating policy and the current policy. Jin says: “Staleness isn’t the enemy. Unmeasured staleness is.”
Environments are the new data
In Jin’s experience, data and environments take up most of the work in successful RL post-training. Algorithm design is the smallest slice, while infrastructure enables fast iteration. “Infrastructure determines how fast you can iterate. But what the model actually learns is decided by the tasks, environments, and rewards you give it,” he says.
For agents, that means focusing on the environments that generate training experience. Supervised fine-tuning uses a collected dataset; in agentic RL, the model generates trajectories by interacting with an environment.
Reproducible containers, codebases, websites, and APIs with realistic states help the model’s learning transfer to real use. Engineers also need reliable verifiers and tasks at a useful difficulty level. As the model improves, the task set needs refreshing so tasks don’t saturate and stop producing a learning signal. Jin says: “Building environments is the new data curation.”
As with previous technologies, problems occur where systems hand over to one another. The trainer, inference engine, sandbox, and verifier may each work on their own, yet failures emerge at the interfaces. A model can exploit verifier loopholes and receive rewards for behavior that doesn’t accomplish the intended task. Sandboxes can also fail or misbehave, corrupting the training data.
Engineers should record whether an episode ended in model success, model failure, infrastructure failure, or an unknown outcome. Exclude failures attributable to infrastructure from policy-gradient updates. Failures caused by the model’s own actions should still be scored as model failures, so triggering a timeout or another error doesn’t become a way to avoid a penalty.
Long-horizon agentic RL combines trajectories, tool calls, and external latencies, creating bursts of GPU demand and periods of waiting. For GRPO-style training, where sibling attempts at a task are scored against one another, engineers should schedule around group completion rather than launch order. A group enters a ready bank once all sibling attempts finish; the trainer then takes eligible complete groups regardless of when they were launched. Time to a trainable batch is the governing measure, while tokens per second remains useful for diagnosing inference. Routing matters because keeping a conversation close to its cached history can avoid repeated prefill work.
In a Nebius experiment on a Terminal-Bench-based workload, changes to routing, sandbox execution, and batch assembly reduced fixed-weight collection time for a 256-trajectory batch by 66.9%. That measured batch collection, excluding the trainer’s forward, backward, and optimizer work; it did not measure complete training speed.
For agentic AI rollouts, an infrastructure goal is to reduce the time expensive GPUs spend waiting on sandboxes, browsers, code execution, and other non-GPU dependencies.
“Your most expensive GPU is often waiting on your cheapest container.”
Jin recommends scaling CPU and sandbox capacity independently of GPUs and provisioning it generously, because idle containers are comparatively inexpensive. “Your most expensive GPU is often waiting on your cheapest container,” he says.
Keeping sandboxes ready, using snapshot and fork methods, can take environment startup off the critical path. It doesn’t remove the time needed to run tools. Jin recommends putting sandboxes on the same network fabric as the GPUs where possible to minimize the cumulative latency of the hundreds of tool calls an agent may make. Per-step timeouts and budgets can limit the disruption from a hung browser or process. Engineers should track GPU-hours spent waiting on environments, alongside utilization and time to a trainable batch, to identify where additional investment would help.
When the maths does not match
During RL post-training, the rollout engine and the trainer can assign different probabilities to the same tokens, even when they start from the same weights. Quantization, kernels, batching, and, in mixture-of-experts models, expert routing can all contribute. Those differences can introduce systematic bias into training updates.
Jin recommends aligning the numerics first, then measuring and correcting the remaining mismatch. That can mean matching the quantization scheme and computation used in the trainer’s forward pass to the rollout engine, while retaining higher-precision weights for optimization. Importance-sampling corrections can help manage residual differences, but clipping alone should not be assumed to solve every form of mismatch.
Evaluation should use the precision, inference engine, and version that will serve the model. Changing quantization or kernels calls for another evaluation.
Keeping the weights in step
As training updates the policy, rollout workers need a reliable way to receive new weights while keeping policy lag within acceptable limits. Jin describes three broad patterns: resharding weights in memory when training and inference share GPUs; transferring weights directly to separate inference workers; and publishing checkpoints that inference engines hot-load through storage. The best choice depends on the model, hardware topology, and freshness requirements.
A full service restart can introduce avoidable downtime, but storage-based publication does not have to require one. Asynchronous transfer and compact updates can move much of the work off the critical path. Teams should measure end-to-end publication latency separately from the pause needed to apply the weights.
Weight publication also needs an explicit plan for active requests and cached state. Depending on the engine, teams can finish, abort, or pause requests before applying an update, and clear or recompute cached context as needed. If a trajectory spans policy versions, record which version generated its tokens so the training system can handle that mixture deliberately. Coordinate transfers with rollout traffic where they share resources, and monitor publication delays alongside policy age.
Designing these components together helps teams improve iteration speed while keeping training data and policy updates reliable. Jin advises smaller teams to start with a simple setup and add asynchronous complexity when measured bottlenecks justify it.
Before scaling, check:
- Batch readiness: How long does it take to assemble a complete, usable batch, including the straggler tail?
- Policy freshness: Can every rollout be traced to the policy version that generated it, and what drift makes it too stale to use?
- Numerical alignment: How different are the trainer’s and rollout engine’s probabilities, and what correction handles the remaining gap?
- Environment reliability: Can you distinguish infrastructure failures from model failures and reproduce an affected episode?
- Weight publication: What happens to active requests and KV caches during an update, and how long does publication actually take?
- Evaluation: Are you testing the model in the precision and serving stack users will encounter?

articles.title: GMKtec's M6 Ultra mini PC is our top-tested pick for home offices
articles.text:
The GMKtec M6 Ultra is our favorite mini PC overall — now Amazon has it on a limited-time deal for $500
Our number one mini PC pick for most people gets a limited-time price cut
The GMKtec M6 Ultra is the mini PC we recommend for most people who want a compact desktop for everyday work and general office tasks. For me, it's the daily driver of the mini PC world.
What we particularly like about this mini computer, which scored 4.5 stars in our review, is the value you get here. The M6 Ultra is currently on sale for $500 (was $700) at Amazon, coming equipped with 16GB DDR5 and 1TB SSD. Both can be upgraded, too.
• Best for: home and office users who want an affordable, upgradeable mini PC for productivity, media, and casual gaming.
• Why we like it: We rated the GMKtec M6 Ultra as the best mini overall - it does everything most users want, with plenty of scope for expansion if you're running more demanding workloads. Alongside the Ryzen 5 7640HS chip, it also has two USB4 ports for fast accessories or hooking up an external GPU. Rounding out the connectivity are dual 2.5G Ethernet ports, and Wi-Fi 6E.
A compact mini PC with a six-core, 12-thread AMD Ryzen 5 7640HS, Radeon 760M integrated graphics, dual-channel DDR5 memory (up to 128GB), and two M.2 NVMe slots. It has two USB4 ports, HDMI 2.0, DisplayPort 1.4, dual 2.5G Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6E, and Bluetooth 5.2, and it can be VESA mounted behind a monitor.
Why we recommend it
In our GMKtec NucBox M6 Ultra review, Alastair Jennings tested the 32GB and 1TB configuration and gave it four stars, with full marks for value. He found it handled everything he threw at it, praised how easy it is to upgrade the RAM and storage, and said it stays quiet during everyday use. He noted that fans get louder under load and that gaming is limited to lower settings without a dedicated graphics card, though its USB4 ports leave the door open to adding an external GPU.
For more picks, including the M6 Ultra, see our guide to the best mini PCs.
Price Context & Historical Value
Since the start of the component cost crisis, this is the general sale price we see on the GMKtec M6 Ultra. But I will note that the Amazon offer is better than anything else I'm seeing on the same machine. On the GMKtec website, $500 buys you the M6 Ultra with 16GB memory and 512GB SSD. So, I'd pick it up from Amazon while the deal lasts.
You could hold out for Black Friday, where it may get a slightly deeper discount (but no guarantees given the state of tech prices right now, and I'd expect it to go no lower than about $20 more if it does). All told, a good price and time to buy for a great machine.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the GMKtec M6 Ultra if... you want a compact, quiet PC for office work, media streaming, and casual gaming. The memory and storage expansion with eGPU support gives it extra versatility for different workloads.
❌ Skip the GMKtec M6 Ultra if... you want to play modern games at high settings without buying an external GPU.

articles.title: When content becomes infinite, what makes people pay attention?
articles.text:
When content becomes infinite, what makes people pay attention?
At TechSparks 2026, leaders from HT Media Labs, Inshorts, and Eloelo Group discuss why credibility, human creativity, and audience-first formats will matter as content creation scales.
We are living in a world where content is no longer scarce. There is more news, more videos, more creators, and, AI that can generate almost anything we ask for. But this abundance brings a new challenge: when everyone is creating content, how do you get someone to stop scrolling, pay attention, and come back?
On the sidelines of TechSparks 2026, Avinash Mudaliar, Co-founder and CEO of HT Media Labs and the creator of Saregama Carvaan; Deepit Purkayastha, Co-founder and CEO of Inshorts; and GSN Aditya, COO of Eloelo Group, came together for a discussion titled The Format Is the Product: When Content Becomes Infinite.
The conversation explored how formats shape the way audiences consume content, what makes a format resonate in an increasingly crowded digital landscape, and why the format itself can be as important as the content it carries.
What is the differentiator in all this: the format, distribution, personalisation or the relationship with the consumer?
“Actually, the four items you mentioned aren't rivals. They are congruent; they co-exist. And all of them need to be married in a particular combination to get a person to come back. Right now, the problem is not content. Content has become infinite. Time has become finite,” said Mudaliar.
He explained that when he was building Carvaan, he had a clear target audience: people who didn't want to open an app, create a playlist, log in, pay, go through the entire rigmarole just to listen, and then go to a search bar and search for a song.
Carvaan put in 5,000 songs in a fully digitised, personalised product, without advertising itself as digital. Instead, it recreated the experience of listening to old-time radio, limiting the choices available and allowing listeners to immerse themselves in the music. With OTT Play, the focus was primarily on personalisation, helping users decide what to watch, where to watch it and how.
Purkayastha said that when he started Inshorts 12 years ago, people were beginning to consume content on smartphones, but no app was truly innovating on how they consumed news and information on these devices.
“Today, people come to us because they want a reliable, factual source of information. They want to stay updated on the world, but they don't want the noise and provocativeness of social media. We are a source reliable enough that they can use it during their digital detox,” he said.
For Eloelo, the micro-drama format unlocked the ability to tell many more stories faster and reach a wider audience.
“I think people's tastes continue to change, and while there is infinite content, the top 5% is often where most of the eyeballs go. So it comes down to your ability to keep reinventing the story arc, tell new stories, and deliver them through state-of-the-art data science to personalise content so people always see what they want to see,” said Aditya.
The role of AI
There's a general perception that AI can create everything, so what will audiences actually value?
Purkayastha says that while AI platforms are increasingly meeting consumers’ on-demand information needs, people still want real-time updates.
“AI can't imagine what's happening at TechSparks right now. Someone has to feed it into the system. That is live content generation, and that is news. Summaries and articles are the collateral that emerge from it.
“When an event happens, the question is which sources and distributors will be trusted. Trust becomes the most interesting capital they build, and I think LLM agents will value it too.”
Aditya believes AI will accelerate content creation but cannot replace human creativity. “It's a great enabler for people to tell stories, but I don't think it will substitute for human creativity,” he says, pointing out that despite the money and data invested in Hollywood and Bollywood, no deterministic system can predict whether a story will be a hit.
“People's tastes continuously change, and their expectations change. That can only be solved by human creativity.”
He added that AI would speed up storytelling workflows, while creativity and inspiration would remain human-driven.
Trust and verification
Mudaliar points to trust and verification as key differentiators in an AI-driven content ecosystem.
“There's a very interesting concept we're trying out at HT Tech right now. HT is already a trusted source for most LLMs for India-oriented news and beyond, simply because we've been around for the last 100 years. We take pride in our journalism, and we put out verified stories. We are now building another ecosystem within HT called HT Verify,” he explained.
“For example, our team member here is capturing this event, creating a video out of it that will also be made into social content, and writing maybe 3,000 words on it, written to the schema AI LLMs prefer and made citable by the AI. So you are literally training the AI that this content is not only trustworthy, it's also verified and ready for consumption. That results in your content being cited and picked up, and then transmogrified for the user,” he added.
For Purkayastha, understanding audiences beyond urban India meant identifying a gap in trustworthy local content. When Inshorts began exploring consumption patterns in smaller cities in 2019, as mobile internet use surged following Jio's arrival, the team realised that local news from smaller towns often went unreported.
“We realised that the biggest gap in those markets was that content generation wasn't happening in a trustworthy way,” he says.
The company addressed this gap with Public, a platform featuring verified creators who report on their towns and cities. Launched in 2019, it has since reached about 80 million users.
For Aditya, micro-drama economics have created opportunities to tell stories for more specific audiences rather than chase mass appeal. With lower production costs and shorter turnaround times, creators can experiment with stories rooted in particular regions and communities.
“I no longer have to make storylines that only appeal to a large catchment of people. I can now talk about storylines relevant to, say, a district in Uttar Pradesh, and the P&L still works. So we're now able to tap into Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, each of these,” he said.
Mudaliar believes the industry still has a long way to go in designing products for India's diverse linguistic audiences. Despite the emphasis on building for Bharat, he argues, many products continue to draw inspiration from platforms designed primarily for urban consumers.
“98% of India consumes in a local language. He doesn't know how to search; he doesn't know how to write in English; he's trying. For him, voice search is the first point of contact because he doesn't know how to type. That's why even Google Maps, even your Uber drivers, use voice. So why aren't we building voice-first products for India?” he asked.

articles.title: Applications open for Cape Venture Bridge programme for Western Cape startups - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Western Cape tech startups are invited to apply for the first cohort of the Cape Venture Bridge, a new programme run by AfricArise that aims to prepare them for international VC and market expansion.
AfricArise, part of the AfricArena network, is delivering the six-month programme with support from the Western Cape Government’s Department of Economic Development and Tourism (DEDAT).
Twenty startups will be selected for cohort one, to receive training on market entry beyond South Africa, cross-border finance and regulation; and investor pitching, as well as at least 12 hours of one-on-one mentorship and ZAR125,000 (US$7,500) in tech credits through programme partners. All participants will also take part in a public pitch event in Cape Town.
The top five startups will join a fully funded delegation to GITEX Africa in Morocco, which takes place in April next year, with investor and partner meetings arranged ahead of their arrival.
“Cape Town founders are building companies ready to compete well beyond our borders. The Cape Venture Bridge gives them the investment readiness, the mentorship, and for the top five, a seat at GITEX Africa in Morocco, where investors and partners are looking for exactly what the Western Cape has to offer,” said Dan Mabbyalas, director of programmes at AfricArise.
He said the programme was particularly keen to receive applications from women and young founders across the province.
Tim Parle, chief director for the digital economy at DEDAT, said the Western Cape was home to some of the continent’s most innovative technology businesses.
“DEDAT welcomes initiatives of this nature that contribute to entrepreneurship, economic growth and job creation in the province. We are particularly encouraged by efforts to broaden participation by women-owned and youth-owned businesses, as well as entrepreneurs from across the Western Cape,” he said.
The programme is open to technology or innovation-driven startups registered and operating in the Western Cape, across sectors including SaaS, climate-tech, agritech, fintech, e-commerce and e-health. Applicants must be planning to enter international markets within the next 12 months, and must be led by at least two co-founders or full-time team members able to attend programme activities.
Over its first 12 months, the Cape Venture Bridge aims to support 40 startups across two cohorts, deliver more than 80 pre-arranged investor meetings and 50 business-to-business introductions, and help facilitate over ZAR3 million (US$180,000) in capital.
Applications are here until November 15.

articles.title: El pueblo de Trasmoz lleva 770 años excomulgado por el Papa y este sábado piensa celebrarlo por todo lo alto
articles.text:
En cualquier película de terror, el forastero que pregunta por la maldición del pueblo no sobrevive al segundo acto. En Trasmoz pasa justo lo contrario: el foráneo que llega pregunta, paga cuatro euros y recibe un susto con entrada incluida. Este pueblo del Moncayo, con menos de un centenar de vecinos, es el único de España excomulgado por la Iglesia y lo celebra. La Asociación Cultural El Embrujo de Trasmoz organiza otra vez la Luz de las Ánimas, una jornada que arranca a las 10:30 y se alarga hasta pasada la medianoche.
Castigos por leña y agua. La historia en realidad empieza en 1255. El abad del monasterio de Veruela discute con el concejo por la leña del Monte de la Mata. El señorío de Trasmoz, además, no rendía tributos al monasterio. El abad consigue que el obispo de Tarazona excomulgue al pueblo.
Dos siglos y medio después llega el tema del agua: los monjes desvían el cauce que abastecía a la villa. Su señor, Pedro Manuel Ximénez de Urrea, acude a las Cortes de Aragón y Fernando II le da la razón. El abad responde con una maldición solemne, con el permiso de Julio II. La tradición cuenta que tapó el crucifijo con un velo negro, recitó el salmo 108 y acompañó cada frase con un repique de campana. Papeleo medieval. Claro, ningún Papa levantó ninguna de las dos condenas y solo otro Papa podría anular la maldición. Por eso, como ya contamos en Xataka, Trasmoz sigue técnicamente maldito.
Brujas, falsificadores y Bécquer. El castillo cargaba además con fama de aquelarres. Una teoría sostiene que los falsificadores de moneda que trabajaban allí difundieron el rumor para tapar el ruido nocturno. Versión Scooby-Doo: no eran brujas, eran monederos falsos.
En la década de 1860, Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer se aloja en Veruela y dedica a Trasmoz y a su castillo tres cartas en su glorioso ‘Desde mi celda’. Ahí aparece la tía Casca, una bruja a la que, según la leyenda, los vecinos despeñaron. Ahí lo tienes, Bécquer haciendo worldbuilding antes de que existieran las series de Netflix.
Así será la noche. Volvamos a 2026. Primero, serán las calabazas. A las 10:30 se reparten, se vacían y se decoran en la plaza de España. A las 16:30 los asistentes las colocan en el camino de la iglesia al cementerio y encienden las velas. La costumbre viene de Todos los Santos. Antes, mujeres de negro y niños de blanco recorrían las calles cantando por los difuntos. Las calabazas alumbraban el paso de las almas. No es un Halloween importado. Ese mismo sábado, Radiquero (Huesca) celebrará su propia Noche de las Ánimas.
Después, el acto central. A las 19:00 sale la procesión desde la iglesia hasta el cementerio. Los participantes rezan y cantan “Los gozos para las ánimas benditas”, un cántico recuperado de la tradición local. Desde la organización se pide silencio y respeto, que no conviertan esto en una fiesta vulgar. Pero a las 19:45 llega la parte ‘Stranger Things’. Es decir, “Calles Animadas”, un recorrido de terror por el pueblo con salida desde el Ayuntamiento. Cuesta 4 euros. La taquilla abre a las 16:00 y conviene llegar diez minutos antes.
Para recuperar fuerzas, hay caldero de alubias por 7 euros (con bebida y pan) o bocadillo caliente por 8. El caldero de las brujas, por una vez, lleva alubias. Durante el día hay también cetrería, cuentacuentos infantil, pintacaras y un mago. A las 00:15 cierra la queimada, con música, vinos y licores que aportan los propios vecinos. Nada dice “estamos malditos” como un fuego azul frente al caldero, mucho me temo.
Por cierto, según he mirado, el castillo abre ese sábado de 11:00 a 14:30 y de 15:30 a 21:00. El domingo 1 de noviembre abre de 11:00 a 14:30 y de 16:00 a 18:00. El lunes 2 de noviembre, de 11:00 a 14:00.
Maldito, pero con misa. La excomunión tiene poco efecto práctico. Los vecinos siguen celebrando misas sin mayores contratiempos. El pueblo explota la maldición y el castillo acoge el Museo de la Torre, el Caballero y la Brujería, y cada verano la Feria de la Brujería reúne a miles de visitantes. Cuando se planteó pedir la absolución al Vaticano, los vecinos votaron en contra. ¿Para qué arreglar lo que da fama? Una maldición bien gestionada da para buen turismo de interior.
Y una curiosidad para cerrar: en Trasmoz descansa también Manuel Jalón, inventor de la fregona. Cuántos dolores de espalda nos habrá evitado a generaciones enteras.

articles.title: À mi chemin entre le VTC et le longtail, le vélo électrique Nakamura Crosscity+ perd 500 €
articles.text:
Un vélo cargo électrique pèse lourd dans le budget d’une famille. Il prend aussi de la place dans le garage ou dans l’appartement. Pour emmener les enfants à l’école sans y laisser une fortune, beaucoup se rabattent sur l’occasion. Le Nakamura Crosscity+ propose une autre option. Il adopte un format midtail, à mi-chemin entre le vélo de ville et le grand longtail, ces vélos cargo très allongés à l’arrière.
Depuis ce mercredi 28 octobre et jusqu’au 22 novembre, Intersport organise des ventes flash sur une sélection de vélos Nakamura, en ligne et dans certains magasins, et le Crosscity+ en fait partie. Il est affiché à 1 699,99 € au lieu de 2 199,99 €, soit 500 € de remise appliquée directement sur la page du produit. L’offre vaut dans la limite des stocks.
C’est quoi, ce Nakamura Crosscity+ ?
Sur un midtail comme ce Crosscity+, le cadre s’allonge entre le tube de selle et la roue arrière pour faire de la place à un passager. Nakamura compense avec des roues de 24 pouces, plus petites que sur un vélo de ville. Le Crosscity+ mesure ainsi environ 1,81 m, contre 2,20 m pour un longtail. Il accepte 160 kg au total, dont 60 kg sur le porte-bagage arrière, de quoi asseoir un passager, et 10 kg dans le panier avant fourni. Le passager a droit à un coussin, des repose-pieds et une poignée fixée sous la selle du conducteur.
L’assistance vient d’un moteur central, placé au niveau du pédalier. Il délivre 70 Nm de couple et propose quatre niveaux d’assistance, plus un mode boost. On trouve aussi un dérailleur Shimano Altus à 8 vitesses, des freins à disque hydrauliques, un écran couleur et le Bluetooth. La batterie de 504 Wh est intégrée au cadre et amovible, et Intersport annonce 80 km d’autonomie et 3 h 30 de recharge. Une autonomie qui peut descendre à une cinquantaine de kilomètres avec un passager et en mode Smart, selon le test de nos confrères de Frandroid.
Le vélo pèse tout de même 25 kg. Il reste plus léger qu’un longtail classique, mais il faut s’en souvenir avant de le monter dans un escalier. Concernant le porte-bagages arrière, il est compatible avec le système de fixation MIK, qui permet d’installer des accessoires compatibles. Notez enfin que le Crosscity+ n’existe qu’en taille unique, et peut ne pas convenir aux cyclistes de plus de 1,90 m.
À ce prix, le Nakamura Crosscity+ est-il une bonne affaire ?
À 2 199,99 €, le Crosscity+ comptait déjà parmi les façons les moins chères de transporter des enfants sur un vélo cargo électrique neuf. Avec 500 € de remise, il se rapproche des prix qu’on voit sur le marché de l’occasion. Vous gardez en plus la garantie à vie du cadre, de la fourche, du cintre et de la potence.
L’automne est aussi la saison où les trajets vers l’école se font au froid et à la tombée de la nuit. Le Crosscity+ a un éclairage fixe à l’avant comme à l’arrière, avec un phare avant de 40 lux. Pour une famille qui emmène un enfant à l’école, l’offre vaut clairement le coup.
