articles.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra is safer overall, but shows more destructive-action flags in tests
articles.text:
OpenAI confirmed GPT-6.1 Terra is safer overall than some of its older models, but its safety testing also found other problems.
According to OpenAI, GPT-6.1 Terra showed higher rates of exfiltration, destructive actions, and attempts to bypass restrictions than GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.
OpenAI performed simulations across approximately 48,690 matched tasks and found that Terra received 22 severity-3-or-higher flags, or 0.045%.
For comparison, GPT-6 Sol received 38, while GPT-5.6 Sol received 61.
"GPT-6.1 Terra received approximately 42% fewer severity level 3 or higher flags than GPT-6 Sol and 64% fewer than GPT-5.6 Sol," OpenAI noted in its system card.
However, that is no longer the case when you compare Terra with other newer models on less severe behaviors.
"Relative to GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra, we observed higher rates of flags for concealing uncertainty, circumventing restrictions, exfiltration, other misalignment, destructive action and inbound prompt injection," OpenAI explained.
Terra is clearly safer overall, but we can't overlook the other potential security issues it has, and this is true for all models shipping in the market, including Claude.
Terra also performed more unauthorized actions in one test
OpenAI also tested what happens when Terra needs to deal with messages from other AI agents while working through blocked coding tasks.
Terra attempted to communicate with those apparent peers in 65% of tests and ultimately performed the specified unauthorized action in 13.75%, or 11 of 80 samples.
OpenAI found that GPT-6.1 Sol did so in just 1.25%.
"These results indicate that performance is comparable to 6.0 Sol," OpenAI noted, adding that much of the regression against GPT-6.1 Sol involved promises of future help that Terra indicated it would not actually carry out.
OpenAI warns that these tests were conducted in simulated environments, so the results may not necessarily reflect how GPT-6.1 Terra behaves in real-world production environments.
But we still aren't seeing meaningful improvements across every area of security, even as these companies claim their models can control computers and code better.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Grab 32GB of DDR5 RAM for just $151 in this 4-in-1 Newegg bundle with the 9800X3D and a 2TB SSD — start building a high-end 4K gaming PC with this combo deal that also includes an AM5 Gigabyte motherboard and a free MSI AIO liquid cooler
articles.text:
Grab 32GB of DDR5 RAM for just $151 in this 4-in-1 Newegg bundle with the 9800X3D and a 2TB SSD — start building a high-end 4K gaming PC with this combo deal that also includes an AM5 Gigabyte motherboard and a free MSI AIO liquid cooler
Four big parts for your next rig with a juicy discount
Rather than spending $450 on 32GB of DDR5 all by itself, you can save a ton of money when you pick up RAM as part of Newegg's PC component bundles, $350 in this case. In this bundle, you can pick up four parts you need for $1,180.99 in a set that includes the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D with 32GB DDR5, a Gigabyte X870E motherboard, and 2TB of SSD storage.
● Check out this deal at Newegg
The discount knocks $358.99 off the combined price for this kit, meaning you're picking up RAM for the equivalent price of just $151.01. That's a massive discount compared to the current price for 32GB of DDR5 RAM, let alone this particular kit, which would cost you $509.99 if you bought it separately.
The price is even better when you include the freebies. A year's worth of McAfee isn't much to write home about, but a free MSI MAG Coreliquid A13 240mm AIO cooler worth $72.49 certainly is. That'll help you keep the 9800X3D cool, and it's totally free with this kit, too.
This is a significant haul for the price in the current market, giving you several of the components you'd need to kickstart a new 4K gaming PC build. Whether it's $358.99 you're saving, or over $431 if you include the free AIO, you're saving several hundred dollars that you can put towards a case, peripherals, power supply, or that all-important GPU purchase.
Four significant parts for a gaming PC build are combined in this Newegg combo deal. It includes the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 32GB of Team Group T-Force Delta RGB DDR5-6000 RAM, a Gigabyte AM5 X870E Aorus Elite WiFi 7 motherboard, and a 2TB Team Group NV5000 SSD, along with a free AIO cooler from MSI worth $72.49.
The AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D is one of the fastest gaming CPUs on the market right now, as you'll see in our CPU benchmark data, and it's still the top option in our best CPU guide. Other chips, like the 9950X3D2, have nudged ahead on performance, but with significantly higher power demands.
AMD dominates the market with its 3D V-cache chips: there just isn't a matching alternative from Intel. The extra L3 cache it provides, with a total of 96MB in the 9800X3D, means that your CPU doesn't have to revert to the slower system RAM. The result is better, more stable frame rates, and overall better gaming performance.
As specs go, you're getting a modern Zen 5 CPU with eight cores. All eight have access to the increased 96MB L3 cache, too. You get a clock speed of 4.7 GHz, which boosts up to 5.2 GHz, and a TDP of 120W. This is a CPU that won't struggle with the demands of 4K gaming with ray tracing, as long as you have a GPU able to match it.
This AM5 CPU needs a motherboard to match, and with this bundle, you're getting the Gigabyte X870E Aorus Elite Wi-Fi 7. This is a mid-tier board for gamers from Gigabyte, and it comes with a set of features designed with gamers in mind. You get 12 USB ports at the back here, with two USB-C ports that give speeds of up to 40 Gbps.
You can install a whole set of M.2 SSDs here, and with the 9800X3D installed, three of them are rated for PCIe 5.0 speeds. 2.5G Ethernet and Wi-Fi 7 support is included, and the board also includes support for up to 256GB of DDR5 RAM for speeds up to 8,200 MT/s.
This bundle isn't quite that good, but you do get 32GB here. Two 16GB modules of Team Group T-Force Delta RGB RAM are included, with speeds of 6,000 MT/s, with CAS and memory timings of 38-38-38-78. Good RAM for gaming, especially with customizable RGB lighting, but it's the price that beats it all. As we mentioned, the discounts applied here mean you're getting this $500+ RAM set for the equivalent of just $151.01.
Oh, and 2TB of SSD storage is included, which'll give you plenty of space for big AAA games alongside a Windows installation. The Team Group NV5000 SSD here is an M.2 NVMe SSD with Gen 4 speeds, and it'll be a good start option in a market where, like RAM, SSDs are becoming very expensive.
This $1,180.99 Newegg combo deal for the 9800X3D, 32GB DDR5, a 2TB SSD, and a Gigabyte AM5 gaming motherboard is a real steal in the market, and one that'll save you $358.99. You won't find 32GB of DDR5-6000 RAM for anything close to the equivalent $151.01 cost you're getting it here. This is a good, core set of parts that'll help you build a new, or upgrade an existing, 4K gaming PC, with that freebie AIO from MSI to help keep it cool.
Ben Stockton is a deals writer at Tom’s Hardware. He's been writing about technology since 2018, with bylines at PCGamesN, How-To Geek, and Tom’s Guide, among others. When he’s not hunting down the best bargains, he’s busy tinkering with his homelab or watching old Star Trek episodes.
- logainofhades While the price still sucks, it's a better deal than a Microcenter bundle, I guess.Reply

articles.title: Warner Bros. drops final trailer for Dune: Part Three
articles.text:
The end of the year is fast approaching and with it, the pre-Christmas release of Dune: Part Three, the final installment in Denis Villeneuve’s acclaimed adaptation of sci-fi author Frank Herbert’s novel(s). Warner Bros. gave us a broody and haunting extended teaser in March and a July trailer jam-packed with tantalizing hints of what to expect, along with plenty of Easter eggs to delight avid book fans. Now we’ve got one last action-packed trailer setting up the final act for iconic anti-hero Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet).
(Spoilers for first two films in the franchise below.)
Previously, 2021’s Dune culminated in the brutal defeat of House Atreides by rival House Harkonnen, with Paul and his mother, Lady Jessica (Rebecca Ferguson), fleeing to the desert and taking refuge among the Fremen. Among them is Chani (Zendaya), whom Paul has been seeing in visions all along.
In Dune: Part Two (2024), Paul ingratiated himself with the Fremen, learned to ride a sandworm, and won Chani’s love. A pregnant Lady Jessica had her own plans for Paul as a messiah figure to fulfill a Bene Gesserit prophecy. Ultimately, Paul challenges the emperor, defeats his champion, and demands the Princess Irulan (Florence Pugh) as his wife. The other Great Houses reject Paul as ruler, so he launches a holy war against them. And Chani rides off on a sandworm after refusing to bow down to Paul.

articles.title: Edge Sound raises $2M to help physical AI make sense of audio - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Edge Sound raises $2M to help physical AI make sense of audio
Edge Sound Research Inc. today announced it has raised $2 million in new funding to build audio infrastructure that isolates useful sounds and combines them with other sensor data to help physical AI systems understand what’s happening in real time.
Stormbreaker Ventures led the round, bringing the company’s total funding to $9 million.
When the company first approached this problem, it looked at sports. When a basketball hits the court, fans are stomping in the stands and bass pounds through the arena’s speakers – all of this comes through microphones at the same time. For an artificial intelligence system trying to isolate the dribble, those overlapping sounds can make this difficult.
This challenge sits at the center of Edge Sound Research’s approach to machine perception: connecting audio with tracking and visual data to determine which sound belongs to which object.
“The issue in audio is it’s not object oriented; it’s channel oriented,” co-founder and Chief Executive Valtteri Salomaki told SiliconANGLE in an interview.
For broadcasters, making that connection means following a player’s sounds through a crowded arena. Edge is betting the same approach could help robots and other physical AI systems interpret the world around them — including activity their cameras cannot yet see.
Humans do this automatically because we exist in a multimodal world: Sight, sound and physical sensation all come in at once. In the physical AI world, sound has always been treated as a second-class citizen to vision because cameras are already everywhere, in everyday life and used for everything. For humans, sound is fundamental to navigating everywhere.
Audio comes in channels, Salomaki explained. It’s connected to microphones, which are positioned around a space or on objects and they listen in locations. These produce signals that identify sounds – they don’t directly associate with anything until something else turns them into readily identifiable information.
“It’s split into two layers,” Salomaki said. “One is how do you create a digital twin of all sensors. The other one is how do you create AI machine learning models to source separate sound elements.”
In the sports arena demonstration, the system uses microphone locations, pickup patterns and player tracking to select useful audio. It then associates locations; visual and audio are paired to identify objects — such as players, the ball, even the coach or a referee with the whistle.
The company said users can import 3D spaces or 2D layouts with coordinates and place sensors within that representation. This allows a spatial map of the environment and its sensors; this is essentially the “digital twin” that Salomaki is referring to.
Other use cases could involve autonomous vehicles, which could be given digital ears to hear if a siren is approaching. Humans identify sounds and direction because our ears are on the sides of our heads. If a sound comes from the left, it’s louder on that side, even if we can’t see an object there.
Anyone who has heard a siren approaching or receding has also experienced the Doppler effect, where the pitch increases or decreases depending on how fast it’s coming or going. A higher pitch can give an autonomous vehicle an immediate warning that an emergency vehicle is approaching from a blind corner (and its direction of approach), even if the lights aren’t visible on camera.
Building the models for audio perception
Edge has a general model that it develops and fine-tunes for customer needs. These models face different delay target requirements for real-time activity. Salomaki cited a sub-33-millisecond tolerance for sports broadcasting and said other environments might tolerate 100 or 200 milliseconds.
Useful perception needs to arrive on time for most applications because hearing what happens needs to be paired with seeing.
The company is building toward hardware independence with its digital twin software and AI models, allowing Edge to assemble new applications around a core technology. This way, it will become audio infrastructure that will work alongside existing microphones and cameras customers already have for their current physical AI robots, media and other systems.
With the funding, Salomaki said, Edge will complete integration with existing enterprise customers and make the platform’s components transferable across industries ahead of a Series A.
Live sports has already given Edge a commercial market as it developed and validated its perception technology, using that to help train and build its models. Its Virtual Sound Engine, which automatically captures and isolates sound from complex environments, is already deployed commercially across the industry. Customers and partners include American audio equipment manufacturer Shure Inc., the National Basketball Association, Fox Sports Media Group and the United States Tennis Association Inc.
“In order to achieve the result everybody wants in physical AI, computers need to become a little bit more human,” Salomaki said.
Image: Edge Sound Research

articles.title: Samsung W27 : les images du smartphone pliable de luxe en fuite
articles.text:
Samsung aura fait de 2026 une année pleine de smartphones. Car un quatrième modèle de luxe est sur le point de sortir !
Quel sera le smartphone pliable de l'année ? L'iPhone Duo, ou alors le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 ? Dans tous les cas, Apple va être loin de son rival historique dans le domaine, au niveau du nombre de modèles qui sont lancés cette année. Car après le Galaxy Z Fold 8, le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, le Galaxy Z Flip 8, c'est un nouvel appareil dit W27 qui va arriver sur le marché. Et aujourd'hui, on le découvre en image !
Le Samsung W27 se révèle en images
Il y a quelques jours, on découvrait une première image publicitaire du quatrième smartphone pliable de Samsung, le W27. Il s'agit d'un smartphone plutôt de luxe, que Samsung va lancer ce 29 octobre, et que vous pouvez dorénavant découvrir dans des images fuitées sur X par Evan Blass, ci-dessous.
La version ici proposée est dite Aura Blue. Le smartphone affiche un design bleu et doré sur les bords qui réussit très bien esthétiquement parlant. Pour ce qui est à l'intérieur, la fiche technique devrait être la même que le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.
Un smartphone qui sera exclusif à la Chine
Pour la version mise en vente, on s'attend à ce qu'une seule version avec 16 Go de RAM et 1 To de stockage soit mise en vente. Niveau prix, il faudra évidemment s'attendre à une étiquette avec un très gros chiffre dessus, sachant que le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra est déjà cher (à partir de 2 199€) et que cet appareil le sera plus encore.
Enfin, pour ceux qui auraient eu le coup de coeur, il faut quand même que l'on vous précise que ce smartphone ne sera vendu qu'en Chine ! Alors, si jamais vous vouliez tout de même vous le procurer, il sera nécessaire d'aller le chercher directement à la source, avec une petite importation à la clé.
Source : GSMArena, Evan Blass sur X

articles.title: On a branché bouilloire et grille-pain sur la batterie solaire DJI 2 kWh : voici le résultat
articles.text:
Voilà maintenant deux ans que le célèbre fabricant de drones DJI a intégré l’univers des batteries solaires nomades avec une vraie réussite. Ses modèles Power 500, Power 1000 et Power 2000 n’ont pas grand-chose à envier à des marques bien établies du secteur comme EcoFlow, Bluetti ou Anker Solix.
DJI revient à la charge avec un nouveau modèle baptisé DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite. Ce dernier se veut d’abord plus compact que ses prédécesseurs en faisant rentrer la capacité de stockage de la Power 2000 dans le gabarit de la Power 1000.
Surtout, ce nouveau modèle entend gommer l’un des principaux défauts de la première génération de batterie, à savoir la nécessité d’utiliser des modules supplémentaires pour recharger en voiture ou grâce à des panneaux solaires. DJI va encore plus loin dans l’intégration de son écosystème, mais sans rogner sur la polyvalence.
Présentation générale et fiche technique
DJI présente la Power Auro 2000 Elite comme une batterie de 2000 Wh (2016 Wh exactement) dans le corps d’une batterie de 1000 Wh. Il faut bien reconnaître que par rapport à la Power 2000, la nouvelle batterie de DJI se montre nettement plus compacte. DJI annonce une réduction de 24 % du volume entre les deux modèles. Côté poids, on passe de 22 kg à environ 19 kg.
En revanche, cette nouvelle compacité ne se fait pas sans compromis puisque le nombre de ports de sortie a été nettement revu à la baisse : 3 prises secteur au lieu de 4, 2 ports USB-C (plus le câble rétractable) et 2 USB-A au lieu de 4 de chaque sur la Power 2000. En parallèle, et c’est peut-être plus embêtant, la puissance de la batterie est passée de 3000 W à 2000 W. Un choix étonnant compte tenu de l’habituelle course à la puissance.
Côté longévité, DJI annonce des cellules LFP qui conservent plus de 70 % de leur capacité après 6000 cycles de charge.
| Modèle | DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite | 
| Capacité | 2 kWh | 
| Capacité extensible | Jusqu’à 12 kWh | 
| Type de batterie | LFP | 
| Poids | 19 kg | 
| Puissance totale | 2000W | 
| Puissance de recharge | 2000W sur secteur | 
| Connectique | 3 prises 230 V, 2 prises SDC, 2 prises USB-A, 2 prises USB-C, 1 câble USB-C rétractable (140 W) | 
| Connectivité | Wi-Fi / Bluetooth | 
| Garantie | Jusqu’à 5 ans | 
| Indice de protection | IP30 | 
Voyons maintenant ce que cette nouvelle version donne au quotidien.
Premières impressions
La batterie arrive parfaitement emballée, accompagnée d’un câble d’alimentation qui peut être vissé à la structure de la batterie, ce qui évite des déconnexions involontaires. Au moment de déballer, on constate sans surprise que la DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite arbore la même robe grise que la quasi-totalité des drones de la marque. Contrairement à la majorité de ses rivales, elle adopte un look volontairement plus « technique », avec des vis apparentes. Ses branchements se retrouvent principalement sur la face avant et sur un côté, ce qui permet éventuellement un stockage à la verticale selon les besoins.
À l’allumage, le célèbre gimmick sonore de DJI fait toujours son petit effet. L’écran qui équipe la batterie est particulièrement lisible, peu importe les conditions d’environnement. Outre l’écran, la façade se compose de 3 prises de courant 230 V standards, 2 ports USB-A, 2 ports USB-C de 65 W et 2 ports SDC. Impossible de passer à côté du câble USB-C enroulable. Celui-ci, d’une puissance de 140 W, permet d’alimenter rapidement et sans difficulté un smartphone ou autre. Ce petit détail fait une vraie différence, car la plupart des concurrentes n’en proposent pas.
On notera, de chaque côté de la batterie, des pas de vis qui permettent de fixer différents accessoires, notamment un kit de montage qui permet de sécuriser une batterie d’expansion à la batterie principale. De manière générale, la liste des accessoires proposés par DJI est particulièrement longue, notamment du fait des ports propriétaires SDC.
Cette batterie d’expansion doit permettre de porter la capacité totale jusqu’à 12 kWh, mais DJI n’a encore communiqué ni son prix ni sa date de sortie.
Démarrage et installation
Place maintenant au démarrage et à la première utilisation de la DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite. Un appui long sur le bouton situé au-dessus de l’écran suffit à réveiller la bête. Sans surprise, elle est utilisable immédiatement, dès lors qu’elle est chargée. Aucun prérequis n’est nécessaire pour alimenter des appareils électriques.
D’ailleurs, dans l’idée d’aller vite et d’optimiser son temps, on apprécie de ne pas avoir à activer les sorties basse tension (USB et 12 V) de la batterie : elles sont directement utilisables. En revanche, l’utilisation des prises de courant nécessite d’abord leur activation via le bouton situé juste au-dessus. L’utilisation est un vrai jeu d’enfant. Sur l’écran, on retrouve classiquement le niveau de batterie restant, la puissance instantanée d’entrée et de sortie du courant.
Les ports SDC
L’une des particularités de la gamme DJI Power réside dans ses deux ports SDC. Le port SDC est un port propriétaire que l’on retrouve sur toutes les stations électriques du fabricant. Reposant sur du courant continu, ce port est censé permettre d’atteindre des puissances élevées de manière bidirectionnelle. Il peut aussi bien servir à recharger un drone comme le DJI Air 3 qu’à recharger la batterie avec des panneaux solaires ou en voiture.
En contrepartie, il faut souvent acheter un ou plusieurs câbles en complément pour pouvoir adapter la batterie à ses besoins. Voici la liste des câbles disponibles :
- DJI Power SDC to DJI Matrice 4 Series Fast Charge Cable
- DJI Power SDC to Matrice 30 Series Fast Charge Cable
- DJI Power SDC to DJI Mavic 3 Series Fast Charge Cable
- DJI Power SDC to DJI Air 3 Fast Charge Cable
- DJI Power SDC to DJI Inspire 3 Fast Charge Cable
- DJI Power SDC to XT60 Power Cable (12V)
- DJI Power SDC to Car Charger Plug Power Cable (12V)
L’application
Si la batterie fonctionne très bien sans application, DJI propose tout de même une application qui permet de paramétrer la batterie et maximiser son potentiel. Il s’agit de l’application DJI Home, utilisée pour les batteries du fabricant mais aussi ses aspirateurs. L’appairage est une formalité, grâce à une connexion en Bluetooth. La batterie peut également être connectée en Wi-Fi pour autoriser son contrôle à distance.
Contrairement à la concurrence, DJI joue la carte de la sobriété avec son application. L’écran d’accueil va à l’essentiel et ce n’est pas pour nous déplaire. On retrouve le pourcentage de batterie affiché en grand, ainsi qu’une estimation du nombre d’heures d’autonomie restante. En dessous, on retrouve toutes les entrées et les sorties de courant, avec leur utilisation.
Dans les paramètres, il est possible de procéder à des réglages comme l’extinction automatique de la batterie, de l’écran ou du courant alternatif. Le mode « Optimisation de l’énergie » permet de définir les paramètres pour optimiser sa facture d’électricité.
Puissance, fonctions et recharge
Maintenant que les présentations sont faites, il est temps de passer aux choses sérieuses. Nous avons d’abord commencé par tester les capacités de la batterie, en particulier concernant sa recharge et sa puissance maximale.
Vitesses de recharge
En termes de recharge, il est d’abord possible de la recharger sur une prise de courant domestique. Lors de notre essai, elle a maintenu la puissance de recharge annoncée par le fabricant de 2000 W, ce qui permet de passer de 0 à 80 % en une heure environ.
DJI propose en option un kit de panneaux solaires pliables d’une puissance de 200 Wc. En théorie, ils permettent de recharger entièrement la batterie en 10 heures. Ils serviront surtout de complément par beau temps. Malheureusement, la météo pluvieuse de la Bretagne ne nous a pas permis d’en profiter réellement. Les deux ports SDC acceptent jusqu’à 1200 Wc de panneaux solaires (600 W par port), ce qui permet alors une recharge en moins de 3 heures par beau temps.
Enfin, DJI met en avant la possibilité de recharger rapidement la batterie via un véhicule. DJI annonce une puissance de recharge pouvant atteindre 600 W, mais uniquement pour les véhicules équipés d’un circuit 24 V ou 48 V. Sur une voiture classique en 12 V, la puissance de recharge maximale tombe à 400 W, et dépend aussi de ce que fournit l’alternateur. Pour en profiter, pas besoin de convertisseur : un câble vendu en option se branche directement sur les bornes de la batterie de la voiture. Si l’installation peut se faire relativement facilement quand la batterie se situe dans le coffre, le montage apparaît plus compliqué quand cette dernière se trouve dans la baie moteur.
Puissance maximale
Avec la Power 2000, DJI était parvenu à proposer une puissance maximale de 3000 W, ce qui en faisait une des références de la catégorie. Une fois n’est pas coutume, le fabricant chinois a revu sa copie à la baisse en ne proposant que 2000 W. On imagine qu’il s’agissait d’un compromis nécessaire pour proposer un nouveau modèle plus compact.
Dans les faits, nous avons poussé la batterie dans ses retranchements en alimentant plusieurs appareils de cuisson. La bouilloire fonctionne avec une puissance maximale frôlant les 2000 W. En revanche, c’est plus compliqué quand on y ajoute un grille-pain, qui fait grimper la puissance instantanée à 2500 W, et la batterie coupe alors l’alimentation.
À l’usage, ça donne quoi ?
Au-delà des mesures, nous avons utilisé la batterie dans plusieurs situations du quotidien.
Pour les professionnels en mouvement
La DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite est avant tout pensée pour les professionnels de l’image qui ont besoin d’avoir une source d’énergie dans n’importe quelle situation. À ce sujet, elle remplit parfaitement son rôle. Cela semble un détail, mais on apprécie de ne pas avoir besoin d’appuyer sur un bouton pour « activer » les connectiques basse tension comme sur la plupart des autres batteries nomades.
Nous n’avons pas pu tester l’efficacité de la recharge de drones via les ports SDC, mais DJI propose des câbles de charge rapide dédiés à ses Matrice 4, Matrice 30, Mavic 3, Air 3 et Inspire 3. Le câble rétractable est une réelle bonne idée, et permet de recharger rapidement son smartphone sans risquer d’oublier son câble.
Si sa compacité ne nous a pas paru être son principal point fort par rapport à d’autres modèles de la concurrence, ses larges poignées et son poids contenu la rendent idéale quand on doit régulièrement la déplacer.
En réalité, seule la certification IP30 peut être un frein pour les professionnels qui travaillent régulièrement en extérieur. Évidemment, on ne s’attend pas à laisser du matériel recharger sous la pluie, mais on aurait aimé ne pas avoir à mettre la batterie à l’abri dès que le ciel se couvre.
En voyage
En road-trip, on retrouve les mêmes avantages et le même inconvénient : légèreté, capacité de stockage, facilité d’utilisation, mais sensible à l’humidité. Outre les prises 230 V qui permettent de profiter d’un confort non négligeable, le câble « DJI Power SDC to Car Charger Plug Power Cable (12V) » prend tout son sens. Il permet de profiter d’une prise allume-cigare pour alimenter des accessoires typiques des vans aménagés, comme une pompe à eau 12 V.
Groupe électrogène et batterie de secours
Au quotidien, la batterie DJI peut dépanner dans de nombreuses situations. Elle permet d’avoir de l’électricité dans le jardin, alimenter un bungalow et même réaliser des travaux quand l’électricité n’est normalement pas disponible. Là encore, la certification IP30 peut être un frein, en particulier pour le bricolage. Si elle peut alimenter une grande variété de machines-outils, gare à la poussière !
Pour finir, la batterie sera d’une grande utilité en cas de coupure de courant, à condition de ne pas brancher trop d’appareils en même temps. Si elle résiste bien à l’alimentation d’une bouilloire, ajouter un autre appareil énergivore la fait couper à partir de 2500 W.
Optimiser sa facture
La DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite bénéficie d’un mode d’injection de courant via la prise de recharge, ce qui en fait une prise bidirectionnelle. Cette dernière peut être mise à profit pour optimiser son énergie et ainsi réduire sa facture. Il existe trois modes disponibles :
- Périodes programmées, avec lesquelles on peut planifier les charges et décharges de la batterie.
- Mode autoconsommation max, un mode idéal pour les ménages possédant déjà des panneaux photovoltaïques.
- Mode heure d’utilisation, qui permet simplement de stocker l’énergie dans la batterie pendant les heures creuses pour la réutiliser pendant les heures pleines.
La limite de puissance de réinjection est, pour le moment, fixée à 800 W. Pour ce type d’utilisation, DJI n’est pas à la hauteur des spécialistes du genre, notamment à cause d’un écosystème moins développé. Néanmoins, si on peut difficilement espérer rentabiliser son achat en faisant baisser sa facture d’électricité, cela permet d’éviter que la batterie ne serve à rien une fois à la maison.
DJI précise par ailleurs que la réinjection dans le réseau domestique, plafonnée à 800 W, passe par un kit micro-onduleur vendu séparément, et qu’elle n’est proposée que dans certaines régions.
Prix et disponibilité
Sa vraie rivale se trouve pourtant dans le catalogue de DJI : la Power 2000, plus lourde (22 kg) mais plus puissante (3000 W) et mieux dotée en prises, s’affiche à 899 € chez le revendeur agréé DJI Paris, contre 1099 € à son lancement. Pour qui n’a pas besoin de la recharge solaire et voiture intégrée ni d’un gabarit réduit, elle reste l’option la plus musclée pour moins cher.
Côté prix, la bonne surprise continue puisque la batterie est vendue à partir de 1099 €, ce qui la place dans la moyenne basse du marché des batteries nomades de 2 kWh. À titre d’exemple, voici le prix actuel de ses principales rivales :
- Anker SOLIX S2000 : 899,99 €
- Bluetti Elite 200 V2 : 1149 €
- EcoFlow Delta 3 Max : 1499 €
Au-delà de ces prix frontaux, il faut prendre en compte la nécessité d’acheter quelques câbles SDC pour adapter la batterie à ses besoins, ce qui peut faire augmenter la note finale. DJI annonce que la garantie peut aller jusqu’à 5 ans.

articles.title: London’s AP Ventures closes €269.62 million third fund to back early-stage industrial and energy tech startups | EU-Startups
articles.text:
AP Ventures, a London-based independent VC firm investing in early-stage industrial and energy technologies, today announced the final close of AP Ventures Fund III LP (Fund III).
The VC firm has raised €269.62 million ($300 million) in commitments for Fund III from a “diverse group” of existing and new institutional investors, including sovereign wealth funds, corporates, pension funds, and family offices. Since its initial close in 2024, Fund III has backed 13 portfolio companies developing technologies focused on industrial and energy systems. 
“This final close reflects the confidence our existing and new investors place in AP Ventures’ ability to identify and support exceptional technology companies. Strong support from returning investors, alongside new institutional partners, allows us to keep backing the technologies industry needs to operate more productively and securely, from the materials it depends on to the processes and data that run it,” said Andrew Hinkly, Founder and Managing Partner at AP Ventures.
AP Ventures began as part of Anglo American Platinum’s PGM (Platinum Group Metal) Investment Programme, and in 2018 it launched as an independent venture capital fund to invest in PGM applications. As cornerstone investors, Anglo American Platinum and South Africa’s Public Investment Corporation (PIC) each committed $100 million to AP Ventures.
Anglo American Platinum Limited is a member of the Anglo American plc Group and is the world’s leading primary producer of platinum group metals, whereas the Public Investment Corporation (PIC) is a public asset management firm wholly owned by the South African government, with the Minister of Finance as the sole shareholder representative of the government.
Led by Hinkly and Kevin Eggers, AP Ventures invests globally in early-stage technologies reshaping the industrial economy, including advanced materials, industrial processes, and energy systems.
According to the firm, this fundraise comes as demand accelerates for high-performing infrastructure across energy and industry. It notes that development and operations of industrial and energy systems are being reshaped by rising power demand, tightening supply chains for critical minerals and materials, and the growing role of AI, data and automation in industrial operations. This creates a growing opportunity for technologies that boost productivity and strengthen supply security, AP Ventures says. 
Fund III invests in early-stage technology companies and works alongside founders through commercialisation, industrial deployment and scale-up.  Its strategic focus spans low-carbon molecules, including hydrogen, across production, storage, transport and end use; carbon capture and utilisation; and circularity and advanced recycling, with applications in energy-intensive, hard-to-abate sectors such as chemicals, steel, aviation and heavy mobility. 
Its present portfolio of 13 companies includes:
Teragen Energy: a Southborough-based startup that develops metal-supported solid oxide fuel cells that can provide clean, on-site power for data centres and other critical infrastructure. 
Aether Fuels: a Chicago-based startup that converts industrial waste gases, biogas and waste biomass into drop-in liquid fuels, giving aviation and shipping a new, locally sourced fuel supply.
CREW Carbon: a US-based startup whose mineral-based process replaces conventional wastewater treatment chemicals, cutting operating costs and supply-chain exposure for water utilities while generating high-quality carbon removal credits.
Rosy Soil: a US-based sustainable soil company which sells patented, peat-free potting soils from biochar, replacing a finite, increasingly restricted raw material while improving plant health and sequestering carbon. 
Reclinker: a Cardiff-based startup which harnesses the Electric Arc Furnace process used in steel production and recycling to convert used cement into on-specification Ordinary Portland Cement. 
Lydian Labs: a Boston-based startup which uses modular, load-following reactors to convert electricity, water and carbon dioxide into synthetic fuels, enabling flexible, distributed fuel production that tracks variable power supply. 
Rubi Laboratories: a San Francisco-based startup which converts carbon dioxide into high-purity cellulose for textile fibres such as viscose and lyocell, giving brands a feedstock independent of forestry and agricultural supply chains.
“We focus on backing technically differentiated companies that solve real operational problems across the industries and value chains in which we invest. Whether improving energy efficiency, resource productivity, safety, environmental performance or supply-chain resilience, this combination of technical rigour and commercial pull is what continues to define AP Ventures’ approach,” said Eggers, founder and Partner at AP Ventures.
Headquartered in London, with offices in Johannesburg and San Francisco, AP Ventures initially invests at Seed and Series A stages and works closely with founders to help them navigate technical and commercial milestones and connect them with a global network of financial and industrial partners.
The firm connects its Limited Partners and portfolio companies to a specialised network that draws on the collective expertise of its team, investors, and broader industrial community.

articles.title: Das Ende des Sonnensystems: Wann Jupiter und Saturn aus der Umlaufbahn fliegen
articles.text:
Das Ende des Sonnensystems: Wann Jupiter und Saturn aus der Umlaufbahn fliegen
Bislang galt das äußere Sonnensystem in der Wissenschaft als ein äußerst stabiles Konstrukt, bei dem selbst nach dem Tod der Sonne in einigen Milliarden Jahren die äußeren Planeten für weitere 30 bis 100 Milliarden Jahre geordnet auf ihren Bahnen verbleiben sollten. Zwar wird unsere Sonne als Roter Riese vermutlich die inneren Planeten zerstören, doch erst externe galaktische Einflüsse galten als endgültige Bedrohung für Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus und Neptun.
Ein Team von Forscher:innen um den Astronomen Konstantin Batygin am California Institute of Technology (Caltech) im US-amerikanischen Pasadena kommt nach neuen Analysen jedoch zu einem vollkommen anderen Ergebnis. Wie aus einer im Fachmagazin The Astrophysical Journal Letters veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, destabilisieren sich die Planetenbahnen vermutlich hundertmal schneller, als es bisherige Simulationen prognostiziert haben.
Ungleichmäßiger Masseverlust verändert die Bahnen
Bisherige Computermodelle gingen davon aus, dass unsere Sonne ihre äußere Hülle in der Endphase gleichmäßig abstoßen wird, wodurch sich die Umlaufbahnen der äußeren Planeten zwar ausdehnen, aber stabil bleiben. Die wahre Ursache für die nun berechnete beschleunigte Destabilisierung liegt jedoch in eben jener Art und Weise, wie der sterbende Stern seine Masse verliert.
Beobachtungen an anderen Weißen Zwergen deuten auf ein abweichendes Verhalten hin, bei dem Sterne in dieser Endphase ihre Materie oftmals asymmetrisch in Schüben abstoßen, wie Scinexx einordnet. Jeder dieser Auswürfe erzeugt einen leichten Rückstoß, der den Stern physisch bewegt, wodurch sich dieser stochastische, solare Massenverlust deutlich auf die Gravitationsverhältnisse im gesamten Sternensystem auswirkt.
Stochastische Rückstöße sorgen für Chaos
Die Forscher:innen um Batygin simulierten die zukünftigen Entwicklungen und nahmen für ein plausibles Szenario an, dass die Sonne ihre Hülle in rund 4.600 einzelnen Auswürfen abstößt. Jeder einzelne Auswurf entspricht in der Simulation dabei einem Verlust von etwa einem Zehntausendstel der ursprünglichen Sonnenmasse.
Die dadurch entstehenden Rückstöße von typischerweise sieben Metern pro Sekunde summieren sich über die Zeit und verändern die Planetenbahnen minimal, aber kontinuierlich, wie AAS Nova berichtet. Um die langfristigen Konsequenzen dieser fortlaufenden Impulse zu evaluieren, führte das Team des Caltech insgesamt 672 Simulationen mit unterschiedlichen Auswurfgrößen durch.
Instabilität beginnt schon im Riesenstadium
Diese vielen kleinen Störungen führen laut den Berechnungen der Forscher:innen dazu, dass sich die Bahnen der äußeren Planeten massiv verschieben. Bei Modellen, die Auswürfe während der gesamten Riesenphase der Sonne berücksichtigten, kam es in 37 von 48 Durchläufen bereits zu Bahnkreuzungen, bevor der Weiße Zwerg überhaupt entstanden war.
Rund 40 Prozent dieser Simulationen zeigten schon zu diesem frühen Zeitpunkt massive Zerrüttungen, durch die das Sternensystem seine bisherige Ordnung verliert. So wurde Saturn in einigen Durchläufen komplett aus dem Sonnensystem geschleudert, während in anderen Berechnungen Uranus und Neptun schlichtweg ihre Positionen tauschten.
Auch bei moderaten Auswurfmassen zeigte sich ein dynamisches Bild, bei dem den Daten zufolge eine Wahrscheinlichkeit von etwa 20 Prozent besteht, dass Jupiter und Saturn sowie Uranus und Neptun in sogenannte Bahnresonanzen eintreten. In diesen Zuständen stehen die Umlaufzeiten der Planeten in einem bestimmten Verhältnis zueinander.
Den Berechnungen zufolge schützen solche Resonanzen die Planeten jedoch nicht vor dem endgültigen Zerfall, da rund drei Milliarden Jahre nach der Entstehung des Weißen Zwergs nahezu 90 Prozent der simulierten Modellverläufe instabile Eigenschaften aufwiesen. Das bisherige Zeitfenster für ein geordnetes Ende korrigiert sich auf Basis der wahrscheinlichsten Berechnung damit von bis zu 100 Milliarden auf lediglich rund eine Milliarde Jahre.
Unsicherheiten im physikalischen Modell
Diese Zahlen stellen allerdings keine absoluten Prognosen, sondern lediglich bedingte Wahrscheinlichkeiten auf der Basis eines physikalischen Modells dar, dessen Ausgang stark von der Masse der tatsächlichen solaren Schübe abhängt. In Simulationen mit sehr geringen Auswurfmassen blieben beispielsweise mehr als 98 Prozent der Systeme dauerhaft stabil.
Ob die Sonne jene Asymmetrien entwickelt, die in den drastischeren Modellen angenommen werden, lässt sich aus den aktuellen Daten noch nicht abschließend beweisen. Beobachtungen der zukünftigen Sonne sind naturgemäß unmöglich, weshalb die Parameter auf Messungen an anderen Sternen basieren und weitere Validierungen durch astronomische Beobachtungen erfordern.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 10.10.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: Madica raises $6 million for Africa's early-stage startups
articles.text:
Madica, the pre-seed investment programme backed by US venture firm Flourish Ventures, has received $6 million in fresh capital from Flourish to back 25 to 30 more African startups over the next three years.
Each startup will still get up to $200,000, plus 18 months of mentorship, executive coaching and investor-readiness support. All $6 million will go into new pre-seed and seed deals, and none is set aside for follow-on rounds, Madica said in a statement shared with TechCabal on Tuesday. The company said a separate budget pays for founder support but did not disclose the figures.
Madica’s new backing comes as early-stage funding becomes harder to secure. African startups raising between $100,000 and $1 million fell from 179 in the second half of 2025 to 100 in the first half of 2026, a 44% decline, according to Africa: The Big Deal, a funding tracker.
Yet, most of the money that does flow stays in four countries. Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt and South Africa took 82% of startup funding in 2025, though they are home to about 30% of Africa’s people. Madica’s $200,000 cheques are in the range investors are pulling back from, and it goes looking for founders outside those four markets
When Flourish launched Madica in October 2022, it set aside $6 million to back 25 to 30 startups over three years, with an equal amount for founder support. Madica has backed 18 startups in 10 countries so far, and its first investments came in 2024.
“Three years have given us valuable lessons and encouraging early signals, but building enduring companies and assessing venture outcomes takes longer,” said Emmanuel Adegboye, Head of Madica.
Madica says its portfolio companies have gone on to raise, on average, twice its investment from other investors. On a $200,000 cheque, that is about $400,000 in follow-on funding per company, signalling its early-stage bets are drawing the follow-on capital that most African pre-seed startups struggle to find.
In its statement to TechCabal, Madica described this as a portfolio average, so some companies have raised less, and the figure says nothing about investment returns.
Every company in the portfolio is majority African-owned. More than half have at least one female co-founder, and 39% have a female CEO. In September, Madica made its first investments in Algeria and Cameroon. Adegboye told TechCabal at the time that Madica now co-invests in most deals because a $200,000 cheque alone often isn’t enough.
Madica said it will judge the extension by whether its startups turn early traction into lasting growth and show they can deliver venture returns. It wants other investors to copy what works. If they do, more early money could reach founders outside Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt and South Africa, where 40% of Madica’s applications already come from.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: Apple dévoile l’iMac M6 : plus de puissance, mais pas de révolution au menu
articles.text:
Un jour après avoir dévoilé le nouvel iPad mini, Apple est déjà de retour. En effet, l’entreprise à la pomme vient de dévoiler l’iMac M6 et le MacBook Pro M6. En ce qui concerne l’iMac M6, voici ses caractéristiques, son prix et sa date de commercialisation.
Le nouvel iMac intègre une puce M6
Pour rappel, le dernier iMac en date remonte à 2024, année de sortie de l’iMac 24 pouces équipé de la puce M4. Le nouvel iMac qu’Apple vient de dévoiler intègre quant à lui la puce M6. Apple a donc décidé de sauter la puce M5 pour passer directement à une puce M6. Rappelons au passage que la firme aurait choisi de faire l’impasse sur les variantes haut de gammes de la puce M6 afin de concentrer ses efforts et ses investissements sur la puce M7, qui permettra de bien meilleures performances en matière d’intelligence artificielle.
Quoi qu’il en soit, Apple promet des performances « ultra-rapides » pour son iMac M6, avec notamment des performances graphiques jusqu’à deux fois supérieures à celles de l’iMac M4 et des performances jusqu’à cinq fois supérieures pour certaines tâches d’intelligence artificielle.
Apple explique que « les étudiants et les créateurs peuvent désormais réaliser des tâches rapides et efficaces, comme le montage et le partage de leurs dernières vidéos ou la conception d’un projet scolaire, tout en utilisant simultanément leurs applications de messagerie ou de divertissement préférées ». L’iMac M6 intègre bien entendu pleinement Apple Intelligence, mais rappelons que Siri AI est toujours bloqué en Europe. Notons aussi la présence d’une caméra Center Stage de 12 Mpx.
Au niveau du design, autant dire que nous ne sommes pas face à une révolution. L’iMac M6 présente une dalle Retina 4,5K de 24 pouces, comme son prédécesseur. L’appareil n’est d’ailleurs pas plus fin, et la carrosserie reste inchangée. En revanche, nous pouvons noter 7 coloris : bleu, vert, rose, jaune, violet, orange et argent. Côté connectivité, l’iMac M6 prend en charge le Wi-Fi 7, le Bluetooth 6, et un port Ethernet 2,5 Gb. L’appareil peut par ailleurs intégrer jusqu’à quatre ports Thunderbolt 4 et prendre en charge deux écrans 6K externes.
Prix et date de lancement
Les précommandes pour l’iMac M6 débuteront ce 28 octobre 2026, à 18 h 10. La commercialisation débutera quant à elle le 6 novembre 2026. Les prix commencent à partir de 1 819 €. Les tarifs varient ensuite en fonction de la configuration choisie.

articles.title: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, a quarter of the company
articles.text:
In context: Microsoft's layoff surge, which has impacted tens of thousands of workers since 2023, accelerated earlier this year as the company focused on AI spending. Months after offering voluntary buyouts to a small percentage of its workforce, Microsoft has now expanded the practice to a scale that might dwarf prior layoff rounds from the past several years.
Microsoft recently announced a new voluntary exit offer for employees at level 70 and below in certain countries. Sources told CNBC that this group includes about 60,000 workers, a substantial increase in scope compared with the buyout offers that began in April.
The time-limited offer, which includes financial support and employment assistance services, is available to members of certain Microsoft organizations based in the US, Canada, India, and the United Kingdom. The 60,000 eligible workers make up 27% of the 228,000 employees the company said it employed across the globe in June 2025.
In a blog post announcing the program, Microsoft said it is learning from the April offers, which it called a Voluntary Retirement Program – the first in its 51-year history. The buyouts follow numerous rounds of layoffs over the past few years.
While some of the eliminations came amid Microsoft's struggle to reorganize the Xbox division after acquiring Activision Blizzard, AI spending is likely the biggest factor behind the drive to offset costs. AI infrastructure spending helped push Microsoft's capital expenditures to nearly $35 billion in the September 2025 quarter and $50 billion in the same quarter of this year.
Microsoft layoffs since 2023
| Date | Reported headcount cut | Main business areas hit | 
|---|---|---|
| 18 Jan 2023 | 10,000 | Windows & devices, Xbox, HoloLens, recruiting & marketing | 
| 25 Jan 2024 | 1,900 | Activision Blizzard, Xbox, ZeniMax after the ABK deal closed | 
| 3-4 Jun 2024 | ≈1,000 (internal est.) | Azure for Operators, HoloLens/mixed-reality, other "moonshot" teams | 
| 12 Sep 2024 | ≈650 | Xbox publishing & game-studio support teams | 
| Jan-Feb 2025 | ≈2,000 | Company-wide "low-performer" cull (no severance in many cases) | 
| 13 May 2025 | ≈6,000 (Microsoft says "< 3% of staff") | All geographies; focus on middle-management, LinkedIn | 
| 2 Jun 2025 | 305 | Redmond, Washington HQ roles; additional WARN-notice layoffs following the May cuts | 
| 2 Jul 2025 | ≈9,000 (Microsoft says "< 4% of staff") | Company-wide; Xbox, sales, management layers, and other divisions | 
| 23 Apr 2026 (opens May) | Up to ≈8,750 offered voluntary exit | US employees at senior director level and below whose age plus tenure equals 70 or higher; certain sales staff excluded | 
| Fiscal Year 2027 (beginning July 6, 2026) | ≈4,800 | Largest reset in Xbox history, five game studios divested | 
| October 26, 2026 | Up to ≈60,000 offered voluntary exit | Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States employees at level 70 and below | 
While it remains unclear how many of the eligible employees will accept Microsoft's offer, another set of layoffs announced in July will eliminate 4,800 positions throughout fiscal year 2027. Before this week's announcements, Microsoft's total layoffs since 2023 were projected to exceed 40,000.
According to TrueUp, layoffs across the tech sector this year have nearly reached 200,000. Aside from Microsoft, the most heavily impacted companies include Amazon, Oracle, Meta, PayPal, and Dell. While not all the job losses are AI-related, Meta's are, as the company prepares to invest over $100 billion in the technology this year. TrueUp estimates that tech industry layoffs will reach approximately 370,000 before the end of the year, exceeding recent years but not quite matching 2023's record of 430,000.

articles.title: How Anthropic Redesigned Source Control for AI-Driven Development
articles.text:
Anthropic recently detailed how it migrated its monorepo from Git to Scion. Scion is a source control system that moves repository operations to the server side and uses content-addressed storage and tiered caches for agent and CI workloads. The design sacrifices offline independence for less local data and shared infrastructure.
In its 13 October engineering post, Anthropic reported that daily merged changes rose from around 2,500 in May to more than 30,000 in September. Its CI systems perform approximately 25 million checkouts daily, against a monorepo with nearly 100 GB of main-branch history and a compressed working copy exceeding 25 GB. The company had used shallow clones, sparse checkouts, promisor remotes, repository snapshots and several hundred Git mirrors, but said these became harder to operate as merge rates increased.
Daily merged changes in Anthropic’s monorepo from January to September 2026. (Source)
Scion puts commits, merges, rebases, history and blame queries on the server. Clients maintain bounded object caches and virtualised checkouts materialise files on demand. Tools can query diffs and perform some writes through APIs without checking out code.
A Scion changeset records the files that have changed relative to its first parent, with content-addressed pointers to the compressed file contents in blob storage. Creating changesets is separate from updating references, so accepting changesets requires no cross-server coordination. For history and blame queries, Scion builds additional structures called "derived data", computed recursively from the parent changesets, either eagerly or on demand. This server-side implementation lets derived data evolve without changing clients.
Scion changesets record changed files and references to their contents; tree structures are derived separately by the server. (Source)
For checkouts, clients ask for the missing immutable trees and blobs rather than negotiating a custom packfile. A node-local daemon shares cached objects across jobs, and fetches from regional caches, which in turn fetch from the authoritative servers (backed by Spanner and cloud storage). The regional caches stream the objects in the daemon's storage format so there's no per-request delta compression.
The tiers expose the same checkout-protocol RPCs, but Anthropic enforces their ordering to isolate failures and prevent a regional cache failure from overwhelming authoritative servers. Sparse and virtualised checkouts only request the objects that they need.
Anthropic reports cache-hit rates above 99% at each tier, a CPU and memory infrastructure footprint 200 times smaller than its previous Git mirrors, and checkout speedups of two orders of magnitude for CI and research jobs. These are company-reported results for its internal workload, not general benchmarks against Git.
InfoQ previously covered Uber’s GitFarm, which centralises standard Git operations without replacing the source-control system. Scion goes further by changing the underlying data model. Its design also builds on established work: in a 15 October update, Anthropic explicitly credited Mononoke and its Bonsai data model with pioneering many of the techniques used.
Anthropic cautions that Scion is not a general-purpose Git replacement. It requires its own code-review, code-search and CI systems, and the company’s implementations are highly bespoke. Instead, it recommends bringing selected ideas, including comprehensive server-side APIs and improved fetch protocols, into existing Git platforms.
For architects, the key takeaway is to reconsider where work happens as workloads change. Repository queries don't necessarily need local checkouts, and immutable objects can be shared via caches. This can reduce redundant work, but Scion depends on server availability, and the required integration is substantial.

Cómo canjear los códigos de Free Fire
Los jugadores de Free Fire y Free Fire MAX pueden canjear códigos promocionales para obtener objetos sin costo, como aspectos, cajas de armas, trajes, emotes, oro u otros artículos disponibles dentro del juego. El procedimiento debe realizarse desde el sitio oficial de recompensas de Garena y no desde la aplicación.
Para reclamar un código, el primer paso es ingresar al portal Rewards Redemption Site desde un navegador. Allí, el usuario debe iniciar sesión con la misma cuenta que utiliza en el juego, vinculada a servicios como Google, Facebook, Apple, Huawei, VK o X, según las opciones habilitadas en cada región.
Las cuentas de invitado no pueden completar el canje. Antes de ingresar un código, los jugadores que usen ese tipo de perfil deberán asociarlo a uno de los métodos de acceso compatibles. Una vez vinculada la cuenta, el premio se acreditará en ese mismo perfil y no podrá enviarse a otro usuario.
Cómo ingresar los códigos y recibir las recompensas
Después de iniciar sesión, el jugador debe copiar o escribir el código alfanumérico en el campo de canje y confirmar la operación en el portal de canje de Garena.
Es importante revisar cada carácter antes de enviarlo: una letra o un número incorrecto impedirá que el sistema valide la solicitud. Conviene evitar espacios al principio o al final de la secuencia.
Si el código continúa vigente, tiene cupos disponibles y funciona en la región de la cuenta, el portal mostrará un mensaje de confirmación. Cada clave se puede utilizar una sola vez por usuario y puede dejar de funcionar si alcanzó el límite de canjes, expiró o fue distribuida para otro servidor.
Tras la validación, las recompensas llegarán al buzón interno de Free Fire. La entrega puede ser inmediata, aunque Garena contempla un plazo de hasta 24 horas.
Para comprobarla, el usuario debe abrir el juego con la cuenta vinculada y revisar el apartado de correo. Se recomienda utilizar únicamente el portal oficial, ya que las páginas o aplicaciones que prometen códigos, diamantes o generadores gratuitos pueden poner en riesgo las credenciales de acceso.
Para qué sirven los códigos de Free Fire
Los códigos de Free Fire sirven para obtener recompensas dentro del juego sin gastar diamantes ni dinero real. Cada combinación puede habilitar objetos distintos, como aspectos para armas, trajes, emotes, cajas, oro o artículos temporales para personalizar la experiencia.
Estos códigos no garantizan un premio específico: su contenido depende de la clave publicada y de las condiciones de la promoción.
Además, pueden tener vigencia limitada, un número máximo de usos o restricciones regionales. Por eso, un código válido en un servidor puede no funcionar en otro, y una clave puede quedar inutilizada luego de alcanzar su cupo de canjes.
El beneficio se acredita en la cuenta con la que se realizó el canje y, en general, llega al buzón interno del videojuego.
Para recibirlo, el jugador debe ingresar la secuencia en el portal oficial de recompensas con un perfil vinculado, ya que las cuentas de invitado no pueden utilizar esta función.
Conviene copiar cada código sin espacios ni errores y reclamarlo cuanto antes: los códigos expiran o agotan sus cupos y no pueden usarse más de una vez por cuenta. Las recompensas varían según la campaña activa de Garena.

articles.title: Upwind Security Raises $400 Million at $3.8 Billion Valuation
articles.text:
Upwind Security Raises $400 Million at $3.8 Billion Valuation
The massive funding round comes just days after reports emerged that Upwind had attracted acquisition interest from several companies, including Datadog
Upwind Security today announced a $400 million Series C funding round at a $3.8 billion valuation. Coming just nine months after the company announced a $250 funding round at $1.5 billion valuation, the investment brings the total amount raised by the company to over $800 million.
Upwind offers a runtime-native cloud security platform that provides organizations with increased visibility into networks, APIs, and data flows, which the company says is used by hundreds of organizations, including Siemens, Roku, and Nubank.
Upwind explains that its platform “uses runtime intelligence to help security, development, and DevOps teams identify their most critical exposures, remediate risks proactively, and detect attacks in real time.”
Headquartered in San Francisco, California, Upwind was founded in 2022 by Amiram Shachar, who previously founded Spot.io, which was acquired by NetApp for $450 million.
The latest funding round was led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Canapi Ventures and existing investors including TCV, Greylock Partners, Salesforce Ventures.
The massive funding round comes just days after reports emerged that Upwind had attracted acquisition interest from several companies, including Datadog. According to The Information, Datadog had offered nearly $4 billion to acquire the cybersecurity security startup, while other potential buyers had also expressed interest. However, Israeli technology publication CTechquestioned the report, citing information indicating that Datadog had not made the alleged offer.

articles.title: From 8VC to Benchmark, here's what's hiding in October SEC filings | TechCrunch
articles.text:
October was a big month for venture funds, per SEC filings. The filings show that established names are currently commanding top dollar from LPs, especially with a specialized focus. Here are some of the most notable ones we found that haven’t been meaningfully announced or have seen important updates.
For one, Trust Ventures filed Monday to raise a $400 million Fund V. The Austin-based firm was founded in 2017 by Salen Churi to back founders building in highly regulated industries. Koch Disruptive Technologies notably backed the firm’s debut fund back in 2018. It previously sought to raise a $225 million Fund IV in 2023, though it’s unclear if or when that fund closed. Deep tech fund Interlagos Capital is also raising a $400 million Fund II.
Elsewhere, Victor Lazarte and Kris Fredrickson, two former Benchmark VCs, have raised $1.252 billion for their debut AI fund called Diffusion ONE. Forbes previously reported back in May that the two had teamed up (after raising smaller funds of their own) to launch this fund with a target of $800 million, meaning it’s far surpassed that original target. The firm has already cut big checks since its debut, including co-leading Harvey’s $550 million Series H with Lightspeed Ventures and taking part in Etched’s $300 million Series C, announced in July.
Speaking of Benchmark, the firm filed what looks like four new partner-only funds, called Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund T1, Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund 2, Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund 2-A, and Benchmark Partners Founders’ Fund T1-A, seeking to raise $220 million, $132 million, $4.5 million, and $7.5 million, respectively. Jack Altman, who recently left his own firm to join Benchmark, is listed in each filing.
Meanwhile, Joe Lonsdale’s 8VC also seems to be seeking to raise new vehicles — including a $400 million fund called 8VC DSS III; a $30.35 million fund called 8VC COSC; a $20.35 million 8VC BRSC fund; and a fund called 8VC AI Fund XI, which has already raised $13.5 million, including from 8VC itself. This follows the July news that 8VC raised $1.5 billion for Fund VII.
Earlier this month, Notable Capital, backers of companies like Anthropic, Airbnb, and Square, filed to raise a fifth fund, while Neil Mehta’s Greenoaks, which co-led Anthropic’s $65 billion Series H, filed to raise a fund called Greenoaks 7. The timing is good as Anthropic just took another major step in its efforts to go public, meaning the firms are already prepared to market themselves based on possible handsome returns. According to PitchBook, Greenoaks has also backed companies like Ramp and Anthropic.
Industry Ventures, meanwhile, has raised at least $1.7 billion for its secondaries fund, which opened in late July. The size of the vehicle shows how important that market has become, as appetite grows to buy into hot exiting private companies. One family office advisor told TechCrunch last month about how popular the secondaries market has become, while Emily Zheng, a senior VC analyst at PitchBook, said that stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI are some of the “most contested real estate in venture.”

articles.title: Intel "Crescent Island" GPU Die Shows Up: 32 Xe3P Cores and 256 XMX Engines
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Intel "Crescent Island" GPU Die Shows Up: 32 Xe3P Cores and 256 XMX Engines
Intel recently announced its D-series "Crescent Island" inference graphics cards, based on the Xe3P GPU microarchitecture, with the D270 being the highest-end SKU. The company's website has added a GPU bare die shot, revealing that the card is not the massive chip one might expect, but rather something seemingly smaller. The D270 GPU SKU features 32 Xe3P cores, 256 XMX engines, and 32 MB of unified L2 cache. The XMX engines have been redesigned from the four-deep systolic design of the regular Xe3 to 16-deep processing on the Xe3P. This card is intended for AI inferencing rather than training, so silicon requirements are secondary, and the card is rated for up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X.
Additional details include support for the FP4 data format alongside FP8, as well as large register files of 1 MB per core and an L1 cache of 512 KB per core. In total, there are 256 Vector engines and 256 of the new XMX engines, each divided into groups of eight per Xe3P core. Furthermore, the Xe3P lacks graphics processing elements for outputting imagery, as the silicon is designed purely for AI inference workloads that require long context and agentic tasks. A media engine with four encoders and four decoders is also included, which could assist with multimodal workloads where video generation and understanding are essential.The accelerator is designed as a 350 W, air-cooled PCIe 5.0 x16 card, allowing it to fit into conventional server infrastructure without the need for dedicated liquid cooling. Intel designed this silicon with agents performing thousands of steps, handling a 100K context, maintaining that context, and reasoning, all while serving tokens at high speeds. We have yet to see what real-world performance looks like and what Xe3P graphics IP can do for AI processing.

articles.title: Excel quiere ahorrarte horas frente a la pantalla con una nueva IA que hace el trabajo aburrido por ti
articles.text:
Excel es una de las aplicaciones que más se ha beneficiado de la integración de la IA. La más reciente tiene que ver con una función que permitirá obtener y limpiar datos automáticamente a través de Copilot. Los usuarios solo necesitarán dictar las instrucciones en lenguaje natural y el asistente se encargará de eliminar una parte del trabajo manual que normalmente requiere este proceso.
La nueva habilidad conocida como Get Data aparece en la hoja de ruta oficial de Microsoft y debutará en Excel para la web. De acuerdo con una publicación en la web de la tecnológica, esta función permitirá obtener, transformar y cargar datos a través de un prompt. En la instrucción, el usuario describirá la información que necesita y cómo desea que se procese y a partir de ahí, Copilot recopilará y preparará los datos para añadirlos a una hoja de cálculo.
Según Microsoft, la idea es simplificar una de las tareas más tediosas para quienes trabajan con grandes volúmenes de información. La compañía lleva unos años vendiendo la idea de que la IA se encargará de los procesos repetitivos que a nadie le gustan, liberando a las personas para que se dediquen a lo que de verdad importa. En el caso de Excel, el asistente de Copilot que se integra a la aplicación ya es capaz de resolver algunas tareas que demandan tiempo y ahora va por más.
Excel resuelve una de las tareas más tediosas con ayuda de la IA
Actualmente, importar datos desde distintas fuentes y prepararlos para su análisis suele requerir conocimientos de Power Query o aplicar múltiples transformaciones manuales. Con Get Data solo hay que explicar el resultado esperado para que la IA genere el flujo de trabajo necesario. Además de ejecutar el proceso, Copilot mostrará el script de Power Query para revisarlo y hacer correcciones antes de aplicarlas definitivamente.
Aunque la nueva integración de Excel suena interesante, todavía existen algunas interrogantes. Microsoft no ha revelado si esta función podrá modificar scripts de Power Query ya existentes o si solo funcionará con nuevas peticiones para importar datos. Tampoco se sabe qué tipo de fuentes serán compatibles en el lanzamiento, aunque la tecnológica aclaró que algunos orígenes de datos podrían requerir autenticación previa.
Get Data forma parte de una ofensiva para convertir a Copilot en un asistente más robusto dentro de Excel. Además de esta función, Microsoft lanzó Clean Data, una habilidad que identifica y corrige problemas típicos en las hojas de cálculo. La IA puede encontrar formatos inconsistentes, espacios adicionales, valores duplicados o datos almacenados con tipos incorrectos, los cuales enlistará y propondrá correcciones para que el usuario las apruebe.
Excel también recibió funciones orientadas a la automatización y creación de informes, como Skill Builder y Skill Recorder. La primera es capaz de crear habilidades reutilizables a partir de instrucciones, ejemplos o flujos de trabajo definidos por el usuario, mientras que la segunda convierte las tareas en automatizaciones. Por último, Interactive Canvas puede transformar los datos de una hoja de cálculo en informes interactivos que se actualizan automáticamente cuando cambia la información de origen.

articles.title: This is how badly X wants you to pay to promote your posts
articles.text:
After Elon Musk warned that “advertisers who post ads that are ugly, shrill, strident or overstate claims about their product will be barred from advertising” on X earlier this month, the platform now appears to be using a jarring animated arm that reaches across the screen to draw attention to the “promote” button while users are composing a post.
This is how badly X wants you to pay to promote your posts
You have to hand it to X’s latest promotional gimmick.
Many X users have seen and shared images of the unsettling promotional tool, including The Verge’s Tom Warren, but it doesn’t appear for everyone on the platform. The arm seems limited to verified users, or those with a paid subscription to X Premium. Reactions, unsurprisingly, have been less than positive. “I’ve never promoted a post and HATE this screen takeover,” said Sheel Mohnot, while Jesse Middleton likened it to a Halloween prank. “I wish I could explain how jarring this hand and animation was in the @X app. It was truly shocking, almost like a Halloween gag, but I’m pretty sure it was real.”
Using the paid promote feature extends the reach of an X post to a larger audience based on their location, interests, or demographics, including those not currently following a user’s account. Posts that have been promoted look like other posts on X but are branded with a “promoted” or “ad” label.

articles.title: Channel 4 is coming to Disney+, and I think that weakens the UK government's pitch to extend the TV licencing fee to include streaming
articles.text:
Channel 4 is coming to Disney+, as the UK government considers a 'YouTube tax' on streaming services
Another "landmark agreement" between Disney and a UK broadcaster
- Disney+ will be bringing Channel 4 content to its streaming platform in early 2027
- The collaboration aims to expand Channel 4's content on Disney+, while enhancing the British broadcaster's audience reach
- ITV joined forces with Disney+ in 2025 for a similar partnership
The Walt Disney Company has announced a new Disney+ content agreement that will bring Channel 4 into its roster of broadcasting partners in early 2027.
The partnership, which a press release claimed is a "first-of-its-kind collaboration", will see a number of Channel 4 titles become available on-demand each year on Disney+ in the UK and Ireland at the same time as airing on Channel 4. That means Disney+ subscribers can expect upcoming shows, including drama series Maya, comedy show Stepping Up, and popular reality series Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins, to be available to stream, alongside Channel 4's main live TV channel.
But given you can already stream Channel 4 content for free on its own All 4 service, what's the purpose of the partnership? For both parties, it’s all about expanding their audiences — and it could have ramifications for the proposed 'YouTube tax' changes to the BBC licensing fee.
For Disney+, it gets to expand its library of on-demand content for existing subscribers, combining quality public service programming with a premium streaming experience. At the same time, the partnership is designed to enhance Channel 4’s audience reach, giving Disney+ subscribers who don’t use public service broadcasting platforms a taste of what Channel 4 has to offer.
"Local broadcaster partnerships are very important as we build our content libraries and serve fans around the world," said Adam Smith, chairman of direct-to-consumer at Disney Entertainment. "Channel 4 has created shows with strong appeal to audiences in the UK and Ireland, and we’re excited to bring some of those favourites to Disney+", he added.
Priya Dogra, Channel 4’s chief executive, is also naturally excited by the partnership, saying. "We’re thrilled to be working with Disney+ to give audiences even more ways to discover and enjoy Channel 4’s brilliant shows," she said.
When the collaboration launches early next year, programming will be listed in a Channel 4-branded section of the Disney+ app, distinguishing it from other content on the platform. In addition to new and upcoming shows, subscribers will also have access to some of Channel 4’s existing popular titles, including Big Mood, Tip Toe, and 24 Hours in A&E — all at no extra cost.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Disney+ has secured similar collaborations with broadcasters across the EMEA region, including ARD and ZDF in Germany and RAI in Italy, but this isn’t the first time a UK broadcaster has linked up with the streaming platform to increase audience reach.
In July 2025, the streaming giant partnered with ITV to bring select Disney+ titles to the free ad-supported ITVX streaming platform. The ‘Taste of Disney+’ section allowed viewers to access a small handful of Disney+ shows for free without having to sign up for a subscription. At the same time, Disney+ launched the ‘Taste of ITVX’ collection on its own service, bringing a number of popular ITVX titles to the platform and expanding the free platform’s audience reach. However, as it stands, the deal between Disney and Channel 4 won't see Disney+ content shown on Channel 4, like it did with ITV.
What does this mean for the rumored 'YouTube tax'?
As British broadcasters increasingly partner with US streaming giants like Disney+, the UK government's proposal to expand the TV licence fee to include platforms like Netflix and YouTube could gain support.
After all, it could allow more people to access a live public broadcast channel while being able to avoid paying the licence fee, as it would be harder to police who is watching what inside a third-party app. It also becomes tougher to argue that British public television and streaming services are two different beasts.
But critics already argue this so-called 'YouTube tax' is merely a bailout for the BBC's funding shortfalls. Because many UK households intentionally ditched traditional broadcasters for streaming, this proposal would force consumers to effectively pay twice. With networks like Channel 4 and ITV proving they can independently negotiate major commercial deals, the justification for a broader streaming tax will, for many, become even weaker.
As for when exactly Disney+ subscribers can expect Channel 4 content to be integrated into the platform, it doesn’t have an exact launch date yet. But the broadcaster says "further details on launch timings and content available will be confirmed in due course".
