articles.title: Sony's next PlayStation handheld may get exclusive access to AMD's mobile RDNA 5
articles.text:
Winners & losers: Handheld PC gaming enthusiasts have long speculated that mobile SoCs based on AMD's upcoming RDNA 5 architecture could deliver generational performance gains for the Steam Deck 2 and its rivals from other PC makers. But recent comments, some disputed, suggest that Sony's next handheld may have mobile RDNA 5 all to itself for the foreseeable future.
According to Digital Foundry, Sony might have some kind of exclusive access to the mobile variant of AMD's upcoming RDNA 5 architecture. The nature of that exclusivity remains unclear, however. Sony and AMD may have a formal deal, or Sony may simply be the only manufacturer able to justify a dedicated RDNA 5 chip.
The comment, made in DF's Direct podcast, sparked speculation that competing devices, such as a potential Xbox handheld, the Steam Deck 2, or successors to other handheld gaming PCs, might be forced to settle for RDNA 4m.
Earlier statements from trusted leaker Kepler_L2 also fueled theories that only Sony could meet AMD's shipment requirements for bleeding-edge mobile SoCs, though it remains unconfirmed whether those requirements apply to Valve or other PC makers.
In any case, Sony's previously leaked 15W chipset, codenamed Canis, is the best-documented mobile RDNA 5 design in development. Expected to outperform the Xbox Series S, it reportedly features four Zen 6c CPU cores clocked at up to 2.2GHz, 12 to 20 RDNA 5 GPU compute units, and LPDDR5X-7500 memory on a 128-bit bus.
It's still unclear whether the device will support PlayStation 5 games, PS6 games, or titles from either console that developers could update and optimize manually.
Meanwhile, other reports suggest AMD plans to debut RDNA 4m with a set of SoCs named Ryzen Z3 and Z3 Extreme, possibly in early 2027. The chips would combine RDNA 3.5's GPU architecture with RDNA 4's machine learning capabilities, enabling greater performance gains from FSR 4.1 than RDNA 2. There are reasons to both believe and doubt that a customized Z3 variant codenamed "Gainsborough" might power the Steam Deck 2.
Valve has repeatedly said it won't move forward with a successor to the RDNA 2-powered Steam Deck until an APU arrives that delivers generational performance gains without sacrificing battery life. If the company can't get its hands on RDNA 5, speculation based on Gainsborough's specifications suggests it might double the Steam Deck's performance at the same power draw.

articles.title: Carreteras estrechas y más tráfico: GTA 6 buscará hacer más realista la conducción dentro del juego
articles.text:
GTA 6 tendrá carreteras más estrechas y tráfico más denso que GTA 5, dos decisiones de diseño con las que Rockstar busca que conducir por sus ciudades resulte más realista y exigente. La información procede de Jason Schreier, periodista de Bloomberg, quien la compartió tras hablar con Aaron Garbut, director artístico y codirector de Rockstar North. No se trata de una confirmación sobre todos los detalles del sistema de conducción, sino de una característica del diseño del mundo descrita por el directivo.
La diferencia puede modificar la manera de recorrer Vice City. En GTA 5, muchas vías anchas permiten acelerar, cambiar de carril y adelantar con relativa facilidad. En la nueva entrega, los espacios más reducidos y la presencia de más vehículos podrían obligar a los jugadores a calcular mejor sus maniobras, frenar con más frecuencia y buscar el momento adecuado para adelantar.
Rockstar no ha explicado todavía con detalle cómo responderán los vehículos ni qué reglas seguirá la inteligencia artificial del tráfico. Por eso, el efecto final sobre la conducción dependerá también de la física de los coches, el comportamiento de los personajes controlados por el juego y la forma en que se gestionen los atascos y las colisiones.
Un cambio que afecta al diseño de Vice City
Según Schreier, Garbut explicó que las carreteras de GTA 6 son significativamente más estrechas que las de GTA 5. La decisión se tomó durante el desarrollo del mapa y tuvo consecuencias en otros aspectos del mundo: al reducir el espacio de las vías, Rockstar tuvo que incorporar más edificios y elementos alrededor de ellas para completar el entorno urbano.
El diseño de las calles no es solo una cuestión visual. La anchura de una vía condiciona cuánto espacio hay para los coches, cómo se distribuye el tráfico y qué rutas pueden tomar los jugadores. Una red vial más compacta puede hacer que los desplazamientos por la ciudad se sientan distintos, sobre todo si se combina con una mayor cantidad de vehículos.
El tráfico también podría influir en las persecuciones policiales, una parte habitual de la saga. En calles congestionadas, escapar a toda velocidad podría resultar más difícil y obligar a elegir entre reducir la marcha, buscar una ruta alternativa o arriesgarse a pasar entre otros coches. Sin embargo, esa posibilidad es una consecuencia potencial del diseño, no una mecánica específica que Rockstar haya confirmado.
Una conducción menos arcade
En GTA 5, conducir a gran velocidad por las calles suele permitir maniobras arriesgadas, especialmente en avenidas amplias. El nuevo planteamiento apunta a una experiencia más contenida en las zonas urbanas: si hay menos espacio y más coches, adelantar o esquivar obstáculos puede requerir mayor precisión.
La comparación con Red Dead Redemption 2 surge por la atención de Rockstar al detalle y al realismo en sus mundos. Aun así, no implica que GTA 6 vaya a replicar exactamente sus sistemas. La saga Grand Theft Auto conserva un tono y una jugabilidad propios, y todavía no se conoce hasta qué punto las nuevas carreteras cambiarán el ritmo de las partidas.
El diseño también podría variar entre entornos. La información difundida señala que las zonas rurales mantendrán vías más amplias y menos tráfico, lo que permitiría conservar una mayor sensación de velocidad fuera de la ciudad. Esa diferencia daría espacio a estilos de conducción distintos según el lugar, aunque Rockstar no ha detallado cómo se distribuirán estas características por todo el mapa.
La experiencia real se conocerá al jugar
Las carreteras estrechas y el tráfico denso pueden hacer que los trayectos urbanos sean más inmersivos, pero también podrían reducir la facilidad para conducir a toda velocidad. La respuesta de los jugadores dependerá de cómo se equilibren el desafío, el control de los vehículos y la libertad de movimiento característica de la serie.
Por ahora, Rockstar no ha publicado cifras sobre la densidad del tráfico ni una demostración técnica centrada en la conducción. Los detalles conocidos proceden de las declaraciones de Garbut recogidas por Schreier. Habrá que esperar a que la compañía muestre más del juego para saber cómo se traducirá ese diseño en las calles y en las persecuciones de GTA 6.

articles.title: Chuva avança pelo Brasil e traz risco de temporais em cinco regiões
articles.text:
Áreas de diferentes regiões do Brasil devem receber chuva nesta quarta-feira (28) e quinta-feira (29). A instabilidade também avança sobre o Sudeste e o Sul, com risco de temporais em algumas localidades.
No MATOPIBA, região que abrange partes do Maranhão, Tocantins, Piauí e Bahia, a previsão é de chuva. Já no extremo Norte e em áreas do Nordeste, o calor continua forte, com temperaturas próximas de 40 °C.
Temporais atingem áreas agrícolas
No Norte, as precipitações se concentram principalmente no Acre, Amazonas, Rondônia, Pará e Tocantins. O Centro-Oeste também terá chuva em praticamente toda a região na quarta-feira, com intensificação prevista para partes de Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul e Goiás no dia seguinte.
No Sudeste, a instabilidade ganha força em áreas de São Paulo e Minas Gerais, com possibilidade de chuva também no Rio de Janeiro e no Espírito Santo. Na quinta-feira, as precipitações voltam a avançar pelo Sul, sobretudo no Paraná. O Recôncavo Baiano também está sob atenção devido à previsão de chuvas expressivas.
A mudança no tempo está relacionada ao afastamento de uma área de alta pressão em direção ao oceano Atlântico. Com esse movimento, o ar quente e úmido avança sobre o centro-sul do país, favorecendo a formação de áreas de instabilidade.
Entre os principais destaques da previsão estão:
- MATOPIBA: chuva em áreas agrícolas do Maranhão, Tocantins, Piauí e Bahia, com possibilidade de trovoadas.
- Norte: tempo seco e temperaturas elevadas em áreas de Roraima, Amapá e norte do Pará.
- Centro-Oeste: aviso amarelo de perigo potencial para tempestades em toda a região nos dois dias.
- Sul: risco de temporais no Paraná na quinta-feira, enquanto o extremo sul do Rio Grande do Sul permanece com tempo firme.
- Sudeste: chuva e trovoadas em áreas de São Paulo e Minas Gerais, com possibilidade de precipitações no Rio de Janeiro e no Espírito Santo.
Calor intenso contrasta com frio em São Paulo
Apesar da chuva em parte do país, o calor persiste em áreas do Norte e do Nordeste. Boa Vista (RR) pode registrar máxima de 38 °C nos dois dias. Em Teresina (PI), os termômetros podem chegar a 39 °C, mesmo com previsão de precipitações em áreas do estado.
No Centro-Oeste, as temperaturas ficam mais amenas. Em Cuiabá (MT), a máxima cai de 34 °C na quarta-feira para 30 °C na quinta. Em Brasília (DF), as máximas previstas são de 27 °C e 28 °C, respectivamente.
Na capital paulista, a máxima não passa de 20 °C na quarta-feira e chega a apenas 18 °C na quinta. No Rio de Janeiro, os termômetros atingem 27 °C e 26 °C, respectivamente.
O frio também ganha destaque no Sul. Na quinta-feira, Curitiba (PR) terá temperaturas entre 12 °C e 15 °C. Em Florianópolis (SC), a previsão varia de 16 °C a 20 °C.
Avisos de tempestade continuam em vigor
Os avisos amarelos de perigo potencial para tempestades abrangem áreas de diferentes regiões. No Centro-Oeste, o alerta vale para toda a região durante os dois dias. Na quinta-feira, também inclui Paraná, Santa Catarina e o norte do Rio Grande do Sul. No Recôncavo Baiano, o aviso se refere ao risco de acumulados expressivos de chuva.
Até o fim de quinta-feira, a previsão mantém a possibilidade de precipitações em áreas do Norte, Centro-Oeste, Sudeste, MATOPIBA e Sul. Em partes do Norte e do Nordeste, o tempo seco e as temperaturas elevadas devem persistir.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Tiny magnetic vortices could help computers work more like your brain
articles.text:
Tiny magnetic vortices could help computers work more like your brain
- Date:
- October 26, 2026
- Source:
- Norwegian University of Science and Technology
- Summary:
- Scientists have filmed tiny magnetic vortices called skyrmions melting out of an organized lattice for the first time, revealing new ways to manipulate these unusual structures. The breakthrough could help make brain-like computers a reality, potentially enabling dramatically smaller and more energy-efficient technology.
- Share:
Tiny magnetic structures called skyrmions could help pave the way for a new generation of computers that process information more like the human brain while using far less electricity. Although most people have never heard of skyrmions, these microscopic magnetic vortices may eventually play an important role in how computers store and process data.
A study published in the journal Nature Nanotechnology provides new insights into how skyrmions behave and how scientists can control them. The findings could help researchers develop smaller, more efficient computing systems and advance emerging quantum technologies.
Most of the research was conducted at the Institute of Physics at Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany, with contributions from a professor at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU).
"Skyrmions are small, magnetic vortices that can store information in a completely new way," explained Asle Sudbø, who leads NTNU's Centre for Quantum Spintronics (QuSpin).
Unlike conventional technologies, which require increasing amounts of space and energy to handle growing quantities of data, skyrmions could offer a much more efficient alternative.
"Instead of the current technology, where we constantly need more space and energy to process data, skyrmions could make it possible to build much smaller and more energy-efficient data storage systems," explained Sudbø.
Tiny Magnetic Vortices Could Enable Brain-Like Computers
The potential applications of skyrmions extend well beyond conventional data storage. They are also important to spintronics, which explores ways to use the magnetic properties of electrons in electronic devices, and to research involving topological quantum effects.
One particularly promising possibility is the development of computers that operate in ways similar to biological brains.
"These nanoscale vortices could help develop computers that resemble biological brains," said Sudbø.
Rather than relying on conventional transistor-based computing, such systems could use magnetism to process information. In principle, this approach could dramatically reduce electricity consumption, potentially allowing future computers to perform complex tasks with very little energy.
Turning that possibility into practical technology, however, requires scientists to understand exactly how skyrmions behave and how to manipulate them reliably.
The latest research represents an important advance toward that goal.
Scientists Film Magnetic Skyrmion Lattices Melting for the First Time
Skyrmions do not always exist as isolated magnetic structures. Under certain conditions, they organize themselves into repeating patterns known as lattices, resembling the orderly arrangement of atoms in a crystal, but on a much smaller scale.
Scientists can manipulate these arrangements, a capability that could be essential for using skyrmions in future computing devices.
In the new study, researchers achieved something that had not been demonstrated before. They recorded the melting of a magnetic skyrmion lattice as it happened while simultaneously controlling individual skyrmions.
"For the first time, researchers have managed to film how a magnetic skyrmion lattice melts in real time, while simultaneously being able to manipulate each individual skyrmion directly as they film it. For example, both their shape and size can be changed 'on the fly'," said Sudbø.
The ability to observe this process directly provides a clearer picture of how skyrmions respond when their organized structures break apart. It also allows researchers to study how changing the size and shape of individual magnetic vortices affects their behavior.
A New Step Toward Energy-Efficient Computing
Understanding how skyrmions behave during the breakdown of their lattices could help scientists develop more precise ways to control them. That control is particularly important if these magnetic structures are to become useful components in future computer systems.
The findings therefore offer more than a new way to observe an unusual magnetic phenomenon. They provide information that could help researchers overcome challenges involved in developing practical skyrmion-based technologies.
"The findings give us new insight into how these types of particles behave. This could therefore become important for the development of more energy-efficient computer technology in the future," said Sudbø.
Although substantial development is still needed before skyrmions can be used in everyday computing devices, the research highlights their potential for improving data storage, enabling new computing architectures, and supporting advances in quantum technology.
By learning to observe and manipulate these tiny magnetic vortices in real time, scientists are gaining capabilities that could eventually help reshape the design of computers.
"This could revolutionize the way we think about computers," concluded Sudbø.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Norwegian University of Science and Technology. Original written by Steinar Brandslet. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Raphael Gruber, Jan Rothörl, Simon M. Fröhlich, Maarten A. Brems, Fabian Kammerbauer, Maria-Andromachi Syskaki, Elizabeth M. Jefremovas, Sachin Krishnia, Asle Sudbø, Peter Virnau, Mathias Kläui. Real-time observation of topological defect dynamics mediating two-dimensional skyrmion lattice melting. Nature Nanotechnology, 2025; 20 (10): 1405 DOI: 10.1038/s41565-025-01977-2

articles.title: Bank of America kindly asks that you don't share your banking password with your AI assistant | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Financial giant Bank of America is reminding customers to bank safely by kindly not sharing your banking credentials with your AI agent.
In an email blast to customers titled “Protecting your finances in the Al World,” Bank of America urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, “including an Al-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf.”
You can practically sense the frustration in the person sending the email. Still, customers are increasingly handing over their log-ins as personal AI assistants grow more popular. Sharing your banking username and password with an AI assistant runs the risk that it could do something with your finances without your knowledge, or that your bank thinks someone’s raiding your account and locks you out of it. Worse, a security flaw in the AI assistant could result in it leaking your banking credentials elsewhere, giving financially motivated hackers a way into your bank account.
This latest warning comes as banks are still exploring how AI agents fit into the financial world but are reportedly grappling with unauthorized agents accessing their customers’ money. As we discussed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt, banks, payment providers, and processors are still trying to figure out how to allow customers access to their bank accounts using AI tools, such as for agentic payments, which allow people to set agents to autonomously buy things at the best price or the right time.
A spokesperson for Bank of America confirmed the authenticity of the bank’s email that was posted to social media. But heed the bank’s warning, for if things go wrong, it’s on you. Account agreements at most banks hold customers responsible for anyone they give their log-in to. “If you do share your credentials,” its email reads, “keep in mind that you’re responsible for activity resulting from that access.”
(via Bryan Toporek)

articles.title: ASUS Announces TUF Gaming Radeon RX 9070 XT Onimusha Special Edition
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
ASUS Announces TUF Gaming Radeon RX 9070 XT Onimusha Special Edition
ASUS today announced the TUF Gaming Radeon RX 9070 XT Onimusha Special Edition graphics card, arriving alongside Onimusha: Way of the Sword, which releases on September 4, 2026. More than a performance powerhouse, this card is a collectible piece of artistry—bundled with the game, slashing onto the scene, and ready for action.
A masterpiece of dark artistry
The TUF Gaming Radeon RX 9070 XT Onimusha Special Edition pays visual tribute to the world of Onimusha: Way of the Sword. A dark fantasy set in Edo-period Kyoto, the game invites players to explore the historic Japanese capital on the edge of a blade, battling underworld monstrosities with shadow and steel.The graphics card's custom-designed shroud and backplate draw their aesthetic inspiration from the shadows of the samurai, providing a study in contrasts through the blue-and-gold colorway. Game-inspired design elements that echo the legendary Oni Gauntlet make this graphics card a true showpiece for collectors, a piece of art that brings the spirit of Musashi's journey directly into a gaming rig.
Precision and power for the path of the samurai
Powered by the latest AMD RDNA 4 architecture, the ASUS TUF Gaming Radeon RX 9070 XT offers all the power users need to drive Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and then some. This card is built to handle the high-fidelity, cinematic visuals of the RE Engine with effortless grace. With support for AMD FSR Gaming Technologies, users can instantly unlock great performance with immersive visuals, ensuring every clash of steel is rendered with breathtaking speed and absolute fluidity. When players strike, they do so with the confidence of a master.
With 16 GB of GDDR6 memory on a 256-bit bus, users get ample bandwidth and capacity for high-resolution textures and sprawling game worlds. The RDNA 4 architecture driving the RX 9070 XT delivers enhanced ray tracing acceleration and next-gen rendering features, giving users fluid gameplay and modern lighting effects. Through careful tuning, ASUS delivers rock-solid real-world performance, with boost clocks up to 3080 MHz in OC Mode and 2540 MHz in Game mode.
With PCI Express 5.0 support, this graphics card pairs with today's newest motherboards and upcoming platforms. The added bandwidth helps minimize potential bottlenecks in demanding workloads, including high-resolution gaming and large texture streaming. Combined with support for modern display standards and high-refresh, high-resolution monitors, this card is built to power the gaming ambitions of today and tomorrow.
Built to endure the heat of battle
High-stakes combat requires sustained, unwavering performance. The TUF Gaming Radeon RX 9070 XT Onimusha Special Edition withstands the heat of intense encounters through an uncompromising approach to thermal performance.
The advanced cooling architecture features three Axial-tech fans and a phase-change GPU thermal pad, working in perfect harmony to pull heat away from the core. The vented, die-cast metal exoskeleton protects a 3.125-slot design with a massive fin array optimized for airflow, enabling the card to maintain peak boost clocks even when the action is at its most frantic. This hardware stays cool when the battle heats up, providing the reliability users need for long gaming sessions.
This card is built to go the distance, too. Dual-ball fan bearings last up to twice as long as conventional designs. ASUS GPU Guard applies adhesive to secure all four corners to reduce the effects of thermal stress or physical pressure, while a GPU bracket helps ensure uniform mounting pressure and extra stability. TUF Gaming selects military-grade components for rock-solid power delivery and a long lifespan, and it applies a PCB coating to protect against short circuits caused by moisture, dust, or debris. In addition, the ASUS Auto-Extreme manufacturing process offers robust longevity that lives up to the TUF name, so users can be confident their card will power through games for years to come.
The ultimate arsenal
The TUF Gaming Radeon RX 9070 XT Onimusha Special Edition is the result of three storied legacies: the uncompromising durability of ASUS TUF Gaming, the cutting-edge power of AMD RDNA 4 architecture, and the engrossing combat of Onimusha: The Way of the Sword. It is a cannot-miss opportunity for fans of the series to build a gaming PC that showcases their devotion.

articles.title: DeepMind unveils Genie 4 world model promising more realistic physics and humans
articles.text:
Last year, Google DeepMind sent gaming stocks tumbling with the reveal of its Genie 3 world model. Since then, world models have become a major focus of AI labs around the world, but Google isn’t resting on its laurels. Researchers have been hard at work on an updated model that improves on Genie 3 in almost every way. And if you pay Google enough money, you might actually get to use Genie 4 before too long.
It’s easy to look at the output of Genie 4 and see a video game, which is why Genie 3 caused so much consternation in the gaming industry. DeepMind doesn’t think about it that way, though. According to Google, world models are a key element in the march toward artificial general intelligence (AGI). A world model creates a virtual world, but it doesn’t require pre-rendering environments or programming interactive elements. You simply tell the model what you want, and it generates the experience frame by frame in real time as you explore it.
DeepMind says this technology could create infinite training environments for physical robots or unlock new avenues of rapid prototyping for creative fields. Of course, that requires the model to accurately simulate what you want. Genie 4 has several improvements that make its simulations more useful, and that’s thanks in part to Google’s updated Gemini models.
When you prompt a world into existence in Genie 4, it leverages Gemini 3.8 Flash as a guiding agent to break down goals and evaluate each output frame. This helps keep the simulation on track, letting you move through varying environments without losing the original context. However, DeepMind notes that Genie 4 worlds still only remain consistent for a couple of minutes before they forget how things started.
Like Genie 3, the new version supports changing the parameters midstream. You can change the weather, add elements, or move the camera, and Gemini will help steer the simulation with each update. This is similar to the way reasoning models generate additional internal prompts to zero in on the right output tokens.

articles.title: Inside Amazon’s Echo hardware event
articles.text:
Amazon swapped its usual big fall hardware showcase this year for a series of smaller launches throughout October. So far this month, it has announced new Fire TV devices, new Kindles, the Alexa Tablet Pro 12, Ring’s first smart lock, new hardware from AI-wearable startup Bee, and new Blink 4K cameras.
Inside Amazon’s Echo hardware event
The company’s low-key product launch was designed to give each device more attention, according to Panos Panay.
Then this week, it hosted journalists at a small event in New York City’s financial district to showcase its new Echo hardware.
Panos Panay, senior vice president of devices, Alexa, and Leo at Amazon, kicked off proceedings by explaining the company’s approach this year. “We have so many products we’re launching that are meaningful,” he said. “However, we get to this point when we do everything at once; not all your children get enough attention.” This longer rollout allows for more focus on each launch. He also teased two more launches still to come — from Ring and some “Echo on the Go” news — before explaining that today’s focus is “the most important focus we have, which is the home.”
He then spent about 45 minutes introducing five new Echo smart speakers and displays — the Echo Show 16, Echo Time, Alexa Photo Frame, Echo Studio with Home Camera, and a new Echo Dot — with each product sitting on plinths in the warehouse-like space.
He demoed several new software features for the Echo Show smart displays that will start on the Show 16 and trickle down to existing Show products, including dedicated home screens, an interactive 3D map view for smart home control, and a meal planning feature.
Panay also revealed that they have “opened up Alexa Plus’ brain a little bit more,” unlocking a new layer of understanding in the generative-AI-powered smart assistant. He pointed out that AI in the home is still relatively new, and while it’s everywhere else, from your computer to your phone, the home has been harder to unlock.
Amazon is looking to change that with Alexa’s “new brain” — an updated version of Alexa Plus with new capabilities including the ability to do “deeper research” alongside its usual use cases, such as controlling lights, setting timers, and playing music.
To manage these deeper conversations, a new “Card” interface on Show devices collects each chat. Cards also appear in the Alexa app and on Alexa.com, so you can continue chats with the assistant wherever you are.
The event continued in a selection of small rooms designed to feel like home spaces, where product engineers and designers demoed the new devices and explained their features.
Read our full coverage of all the new products in our story stream.

articles.title: Android Auto vuelve a la pantalla del móvil gracias a esta app gratuita
articles.text:
Hubo un tiempo en el que Android Auto se utilizaba desde la pantalla del móvil. Años antes de que Google centrara la experiencia en la pantalla del coche, solo bastaba con abrir la aplicación para acceder a una interfaz adaptada a la conducción, con navegación, controles multimedia y más. Si bien Google puso fin a esa función en 2022, alguien ha conseguido llevar de vuelta la experiencia de Android Auto al teléfono y sin pagar un céntimo.
PhoneAuto es una nueva app que permite ejecutar la interfaz completa de Android Auto en el teléfono. De acuerdo con su creador, el objetivo es ofrecer una experiencia pensada para la conducción, sin necesidad de contar con una pantalla compatible integrada en el vehículo.
Esto es posible gracias a que la app reproduce la interfaz real de Android Auto, incluyendo los enormes botones que permiten moverse entre las distintas secciones. Los usuarios tendrán acceso a Google Maps, reproducción de música, llamadas, mensajes y compatibilidad con el Asistente de Google. Phone Auto adapta automáticamente el diseño a las dimensiones de tu móvil, de forma similar a lo que vemos en la versión actual de Android Auto que se ajusta al tamaño de la pantalla del coche.
Android Auto ya se puede usar de nuevo en el móvil
De acuerdo con el repositorio de GitHub, Phone Auto se vale de una característica para desarrolladores conocida como head unit server. Esta función de Android Auto se utiliza normalmente para pruebas y ejecutar la interfaz del sistema directamente en el móvil. El usuario solo necesita activar el modo desarrollador y poner en marcha el servidor correspondiente, aunque existe una opción para automatizar el proceso a través de permisos de accesibilidad.
PhoneAuto se encuentra en una fase beta y, según las primeras pruebas, el rendimiento es sólido. 9to5Google reporta que la interfaz responde bien en modo horizontal, aunque si se usa en modo vertical existe un retraso al interactuar con ella. Es probable que ese lag se elimine en las próximas semanas antes de que se lance una versión final que estará disponible para instalarse desde la Google Play Store.
Cómo instalar PhoneAuto paso a paso
Si te interesa instalarla, puedes hacerlo a través de sideloading usando el APK que se distribuye en el repositorio de GitHub. La app es es gratuita y no incluye anuncios ni es necesario crearse una cuenta de usuario. Solo considera que esta versión beta dejará de funcionar el 19 de enero de 2027, por lo que deberás actualizarla a una beta más nueva o instalar la versión definitiva desde Google Play.
- Descarga el archivo APK más reciente de PhoneAuto desde su repositorio oficial.
- Permite la instalación de aplicaciones desde el navegador o gestor de archivos cuando Android lo solicite.
- Instala Android Auto desde Google Play si tu móvil no lo incluye.
- Abre los ajustes de Android Auto, desplázate hasta la sección Versión y tócala diez veces para activar el modo desarrollador.
- Pulsa el menú de tres puntos y selecciona Start head unit server.
- Abre PhoneAuto y pulsa Start Android Auto para iniciar la interfaz. Aquí puedes activar el modo vertical si deseas utilizar esa orientación.
- Cuando termines de usarla, cierra la sesión desde la aplicación.

articles.title: 60,000 Microsoft employees offered voluntary buyouts as AI buildout costs bite — program covers roughly 27% of workforce across US, Canada, India, and the UK
articles.text:
60,000 Microsoft employees offered voluntary buyouts as AI buildout costs bite — program covers roughly 27% of workforce across US, Canada, India, and the UK
27% of the company's total 223,000-strong workforce is affected just months after Microsoft's last, and first, voluntary retirement program.
Microsoft has offered voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees across the United States, Canada, India, and the United Kingdom. The employees, who must have an experience level of 70 or below, make up around 27% of the company's total workforce of 223,000 people, a CNBC report notes. This move comes hot on the heels of a similar move in April when the company announced its first-ever voluntary retirement program. That program was open to around 7% of the company's U.S.-based workforce, but it pales in comparison to this latest move. That time around, more than 30% of those eligible for the program took advantage of it.
The "Voluntary Exit Offer" was announced via a post on the Microsoft blog, penned by Amy Coleman, Microsoft's executive vice president in charge of people. "The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter," Coleman explained, going on to say that the move "builds on what we learned" following the retirement program that was launched earlier in the year. Operationally, Coleman added that those who are eligible for the new program will receive an email with all of the relevant details today.
While the blog post points out that the Voluntary Exit Offer is a time-limited, voluntary program, the fact that it comes so soon after April's retirement program is notable. Companies run programs like this when they are looking for ways to slash their wage bills, something that Microsoft knows all about. The company is in the midst of an Xbox "reset" that includes a plan to cut 3,200 jobs by the end of the year. The company has also seen some studios close, with others merging and yet more being cut adrift to pursue life as independents.
As for why Microsoft has chosen now to make cuts, all fingers point to its ongoing AI data center plans. Last year, it announced plans to open the "world's most powerful" AI data center. Fairwater, in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, is now operational, with Microsoft lauding its closed-loop cooling system amid ongoing concern over the impact of data centers on local communities. Since 2023, Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Meta have spent more than $1 trillion on AI infrastructure. AI data center investment is expected to skyrocket to $32 trillion by 2050, with Microsoft among those spending big.
All of this money has to come from somewhere. For Microsoft, at least some of that looks set to come from global salaries. It's unlikely this will be the last cost-cutting measure put forth by Microsoft execs, with Coleman adding that this voluntary exit program is just one "of the ways we’re trying to meet different business needs while continuing to create opportunities for our own people to grow and contribute."

articles.title: 'This is a wow moment': T-Mobile has made the world's first AI-RAN call, and it could mean huge changes for the next generation of staying in touch
articles.text:
'This is a wow moment': T-Mobile has made the world's first AI-RAN call, and it could mean huge changes for the next generation of staying in touch
It won't arrive on your device any time soon though
- T-Mobile, Nokia, and Nvidia claim the first AI-RAN call through a commercial cell site in Bellevue, Washington
- The call ran Nokia's radio software on Nvidia GPUs, but no AI performance data was provided
- Commercial AI-RAN gear is due in 2027, with 6G networks expected around 2030
T-Mobile, Nokia, and Nvidia say they have completed the world's first AI-RAN (Artificial Intelligence - Radio Access Network) call, routed through a commercial cell site in Bellevue, Washington.
The call ran over T-Mobile's live production network using a Nokia Massive MIMO radio, Nokia's 5G anyRAN software and servers built on Nvidia's Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) platform.
This wasn't a lab rig with test handsets, either, but a real-world setup that held; according to Nvidia's announcement, the site connected to T-Mobile's existing 5G Standalone core and a commercial smartphone.
What is an AI-RAN and why is it relevant now?
The radio access network (RAN) is the part of a mobile network your phone actually talks to: the antennas, radios, and baseband computers that process signals at each cell site. That processing has traditionally run on custom chips.
AI-RAN moves it onto accelerated hardware, in this case Nvidia GPUs running Nokia's CUDA-based radio software, so the same box can run AI models that fine-tune the radio link and, in theory, rent out spare capacity to other AI jobs.
The prize on offer is spectral efficiency, or more data squeezed through the same slice of airwaves. In a blog post about the call, Nokia's chief technology and AI officer Pallavi Mahajan writes, "With AI-RAN, we are on a path to 2x spectral efficiency."
Nokia's July 2026 platform launch claims gains of more than 20% efficiency gains so far, without saying where they were measured, and puts 50% on the calendar for 2027 and more than 100% for 2028.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Interestingly, while the tests worked in principle, details remained limited on actual throughput, latency, or efficiency figures from any of the three major players. Put simply, the call shows Nokia's radio stack can run on Nvidia silicon in a live network without dropping anyone.
It doesn't yet show that the AI makes your calls any better. The most concrete numbers for the Nokia and Nvidia platform, ironically, came from a lab: Deutsche Telekom reported typical uplink throughput gains of 10% to 15% from AI-based channel estimation in initial tests in Bonn and Oulu, with a field trial still to come.
The timing is also awkward for those pushing GPUs as an eventuality here; A day before Nokia's post, T-Mobile chief network officer Ankur Kapoor published results from AI-managed beamforming trials with Ericsson in New York City, with the AI model running on Ericsson's own silicon rather than Nvidia GPUs. At peak hours, T-Mobile reported a 16% improvement in downlink user throughput and 12% better spectral efficiency.
Those figures are company-reported, and when Fierce Network asked how many sites were involved, T-Mobile did not specify a number.
Despite this, Omdia senior principal analyst Gabriel Brown told Light Reading, "This is a wow moment," adding that the gains came from software updates to equipment already in the field. T-Mobile and Ericsson had already reported close to 10% better spectral efficiency from a separate AI scheduler in May, again with no GPUs involved.
T-Mobile is clearly backing both horses, as it opened its AI-RAN Innovation Center with Nvidia, Ericsson, and Nokia in 2024. Kapoor's post argues that "AI-RAN is a continuum, not a single product," and he told Fierce the carrier is developing AI-RAN software with both vendors.
For anyone actually making calls, nothing changes yet. Your voice sounds the same, and any benefit arrives as extra capacity in crowded places rather than as a new feature. Nokia's AI-RAN products enter pilot deployments around the end of this year, with commercial availability slated for 2027.
T-Mobile CTO John Saw, who favored field trials, said they would help the carrier get "a sense of what the total cost of ownership is," and is aiming to keep expectations in check. When asked about Nokia's spectral efficiency claims, he told Fierce that "the proof is going to be in the pudding." The Bellevue test shows the plumbing works, but scale has yet to be played out.
Whether the AI earns its keep is arguably a more crucial test, and it has yet to play out. But that hasn't stopped Jensen Huang from framing it a few days ago: telecom networks were built for conversations, and "Now, they will also carry the world's intelligence."
Every cell site that gets a GPU is a sale for Nvidia as it chases its next multi-billion-dollar growth idea, betting on reprogrammable AI infrastructure and continuing to target custom ASICs in multiple industries.

articles.title: Norton launches new Safe AI tool to stay in control and protect users when using AI - Tech Guide
articles.text:
With the increased use of AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude, Norton has released Safe AI to keep an eye on what AI chat apps can do and access on your device.
According to Gen Threat Labs, there has been a 54 per cent increase in malicious content served through AI chatbots in the last 90 days.
Separate research has also found more than two-thirds of people are concerned about privacy, data breaches, or losing control of AI assistants that can act on their behalf.
Safe AI is a new set of protections within Norton 360 and can block actions you did not intend and let you decide which personal files AI tools can access and open.
It can also help you avoid risky links.
AI assistants are making things easier for many people, from finding information to getting things done, but that convenience can bring with it new risks.
Safe AI can address these emerging issues and risks and quell people’s concern while increasing Norton’s protection in AI experiences people are using every day.
“Most of the AI tools people are using today should really come with a warning label that safety isn’t included,” said Dagim Girma, GM for Norton.
“The tools were designed around how to get the job done and not necessarily how to get the job done right, or even safely, despite the best intentions,
“That’s where we come in. People shouldn’t have to become AI security experts to benefit from AI tools.
“With Safe AI, we’re helping people stay in control of their information and embrace the possibilities of AI with greater confidence.”
Safe AI has been with the foundation of Norton 360’s advanced scam protection.
It introduces three capabilities designed to help make using AI tools safer:
– Protects against unwanted AI actions. As AI tools become more capable of performing tasks, malicious instructions and prompt injections can introduce new security risks. Action Shield helps stop unwanted AI actions and potentially harmful prompt injections before they run.
– Gives people more control over AI file access. As people connect AI tools to their personal files and content, understanding what those tools can access becomes increasingly important. Safe Zone lets you choose which connected files and content AI can access, with options for full, read-only or blocked permissions.
– Spots risky links before you click. AI assistants can surface links that appear useful or trustworthy, even when they lead to unsafe destinations. Safe Links helps identify potentially harmful links shared through ChatGPT and Claude before people open them.

articles.title: Who Qualifies for South Africa Data Licensing Referrals, and Who Doesn’t - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
A connector’s network can span the continent. Supplier eligibility still depends on the company and its records, with South Africa currently on SourceX’s published list.
Consider an illustrative Nairobi founder who knows a Cape Town software CEO, an ex-colleague running a London services firm and a former manager in Austin. Each could be a strong AI data licensing introduction. Each sits under different eligibility rules.
That is the core idea behind South Africa data licensing referrals. What matters is not where the connector lives. It is where the company being introduced is based, what its data looks like and who has authority to decide.
Get that distinction right and a cross-border network becomes an asset. Get it wrong and you promise a founder something nobody can deliver.
Do South African companies qualify?
SourceX’s current supported-company guidance lists the United States, Canada and the European Union. It also lists additional markets, including South Africa, the UK, Australia, New Zealand, India, Singapore, Latin America, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, under a language condition.
For a South African company, as for the other additional markets, that condition is that at least 90% of the data is in English. Other African countries are not on the current list, so a company in Lagos, Nairobi or Kigali should not be promised eligibility just because the connector has an international network.
A supported location is a starting condition, not acceptance. Rights, the actual dataset and the rest of the qualification criteria still need review.
Run a 60-second fit check before you pitch
Before making introductions, obtain an approved partner account and sign the SourceX Channel Partner Agreement. Check any employment, client or professional obligations, disclose your potential reward and ask the company’s permission. Approval to introduce a company never authorizes access to its records.
You do not need a single internal file to know whether a conversation is worth suggesting. Broad facts are enough:
- Where is the company that would actually sign based?
- Has it had at least 50 full-time employees at peak?
- Has it operated for several years?
- Outside the US, Canada and the EU: is at least 90% of its data in English?
- Does it run support, CRM, engineering or documentation systems that hold real work history?
Check every mandatory condition rather than counting yes answers. A company outside the supported footprint does not become eligible because it has a large team or useful records. Where broad fit is plausible, approach an owner or authorized executive; never ask an employee to send internal files as proof.
Multinational structures need one extra step. If the Cape Town office belongs to a parent registered somewhere else, identify which entity actually holds the records and would sign. A convenient address is not the same as the supplier.
How does the referral reward work?
The SourceX referral program offers a standard reward of 25% of Actual Supplier Payout, excluding separately itemized taxes and expense reimbursements, with a cumulative cap of US$100,000 per referred company unless signed terms say otherwise. SourceX pays it separately, so the company’s own agreed payout is never reduced.
Actual Supplier Payout is the compensation actually paid for selected data that reaches Closing and the qualifying completed handoff. It excludes separately itemized taxes and expense reimbursements, the partner reward, SourceX’s fees and the buyer’s full transaction price. Unpaid estimates do not count; rewards accrue as supplier installments are paid.
The $100,000 cap applies cumulatively to each referred company across installments, agreements, repeat licenses and renewals; it never resets. SourceX pays the reward separately, without reducing the supplier’s agreed compensation. The signed Channel Partner Agreement’s Schedule A and agreed addenda control the rate, calculation base and cap.
A hypothetical example shows the arithmetic: a qualifying supplier payout of US$200,000 would produce a US$50,000 reward. It is not a typical payout, a promise in rand or naira, or evidence of a completed African transaction.
A lead, meeting or signed agreement alone earns no payable reward. A qualifying transaction must satisfy these conditions:
- The buyer accepts the dataset.
- The buyer’s payment to SourceX clears.
- SourceX pays the supplier.
- Finance approves the reward, required tax and payment details are complete, and payment is lawful.
The qualifying dataset handoff must also be complete. These payment conditions apply to the reward, not merely to whether the company seemed promising when introduced.
The reward deadline is 60 calendar days after the later of the buyer’s final written, unconditional acceptance and completed handoff of the complete, validated and approved dataset. Payment also requires cleared buyer funds at SourceX, supplier payment, finance approval, the partner’s required payment and tax details, and lawful payment. If a condition is outstanding at the deadline, payment follows promptly once it is met; no new 60-day period starts. The supplier’s invoice timetable is separate.
A convenient address is not the same as the supplier.
Disclose first, then ask permission
The introduction itself can fit in a WhatsApp message, something like this:
“Hi [name], quick one: your company may suit an AI data licensing program I know. If a qualifying deal ever completes, SourceX could pay me a referral reward on top of your payout, never out of it. Want an intro, or shall I drop it?”
Keep customer and employee records out of the first exchange entirely. The company decides what to discuss and controls any later data review.
Check any professional, board or employment duties before accepting a fee. Credit goes to the first valid introduction of a new company when it submits a verified application within the 90-day attribution window. SourceX checks dated introduction evidence, existing applications and prior relationships; an earlier click alone does not secure credit. Earlier leads, accounts or email correspondence can make a company a duplicate. Only one partner is credited per company.
Can a connector outside South Africa participate?
Partners can apply from most countries, subject to account approval and applicable U.S. sanctions and restricted-party checks. Check the connector’s eligibility separately from the supplier’s supported location; neither one establishes the other.
For South Africa data licensing referrals, the useful first action is small. Identify one established company whose owner you can approach naturally, check its location and broad fit, disclose the reward and ask whether a conversation would help.
A cross-border connection is valuable because it reaches the right decision-maker. It is never a way around the company’s authority over its own data.
Check the current company criteria and partner terms through the SourceX referral program. Obtain approval and sign before introducing a leader; explain both the potential reward and its conditions without promising a local payout.
About the founder
Noah Loul is a four-time founder and the founder and CEO of SourceX, which licenses business data directly from companies for AI training and evaluation. He previously founded B2B Rocket, acquired by Blackpearl Group. His work focuses on building permission-based data infrastructure for AI.

articles.title: SAP advances its autonomous enterprise push with smarter, governed Joule agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
SAP advances its autonomous enterprise push with smarter, governed Joule agents
SAP SE today announced a set of artificial intelligence innovations at its annual TechEd conference for developers, enhancing its Joule assistant solutions and Business AI Platform, including tabular data foundation models.
New capabilities in Joule Work will help AI agents become more efficient and interoperate with open protocols. In this case, the Model Context Protocol and Agent 2 Agent allow Joule, the company’s agentic AI assistant, to gather context, make decisions and execute multistep business workflows across the enterprise, while also bringing in third-party data or services.
However, every time an agent goes to work, it needs to be governed by a central authority just like an employee; it needs access and it must execute on tools with permissions. “Open protocols need governed doors,” Ted Way, vice president and chief product officer of SAP business AI product engineering, told SiliconANGLE in an interview.
Way explained that SAP would like customers’ own agents to collaborate with its business agents across company systems. The proposition is that opening those interconnections also requires a controlled entry point where organizations can enforce and oversee activity. This is where a new orchestration layer will come in, enabling assistants and agents to invoke Joule Agents through a governed gateway.
In addition, a recent update will allow agents to trigger n8n workflows, an important connector through Joule Studio. N8n is a node-based workflow automation platform that connects different apps and uses deterministic automation; this means that AI agents can trigger it, but unlike generative AI, n8n uses event-based and trigger-based logic for decision-making. It cannot hallucinate; it is not random and will follow exact rules from start to finish.
That means n8n is suitable for highly regulated or sensitive work that depends on exact needs.
“It needs to do these five steps in this order exactly like this every single time,” Way explained, so in that case, n8n is the go-to.
SAP’s approach combines flexible, natural-language agentic triggers with a prescribed workflow. An agent may help determine when it is needed, while compliance-sensitive procedures can still require an exact sequence of steps.
SAP builds on cloud data to ground the autonomous enterprise
The company today announced the expansion of SAP Business Data Cloud Ontology Manager in SAP Data Cloud, or BDC, to provide an AI-native authoring experience for businesses by giving agents an understanding of how applications relate to one another. It does so by defining relationships between company facts, allowing agents to reason more accurately and make decisions across enterprises.
SAP’s acquisition of Reltio, recently announced at SAP Connect, brings on board multidomain data management to BDC. That helps unify customer, supplier and product records across SAP and third-party systems into trusted data products for applications and agents.
The new product is designed to complement the company’s existing Knowledge Graph, which provides rich business context from SAP data.
Additionally, the company said, it’s expanding its lakehouse capabilities with Dremio, another acquisition, by adding native support for Apache Iceberg and Apache Polaris and a high-performance, federated query engine that enables unified data access without moving or copying data.
Bringing AI models to tables
“Not every enterprise problem is a language problem,” Way said, explaining that although much of the AI approach has focused on natural language, much business data is stored in tables.
To handle this, SAP announced its latest tabular AI model, SAP-RPT-2.0, which expands beyond classification and regression to support anomaly and outlier detection, providing AI-powered analysis through embeddings. It will give multitable capabilities to reduce manual engineering and deliver faster, deeper insights from structured data.
The company also launched a new SAP-RPT-TS model, which will help customers predict values across time-indexed metrics for key forecasting. It uses SAP Business Planning without custom business machine learning, allowing less technical users to deploy the model on their systems.
In a partnership with Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co., SAP announced it’s deploying SAP-RPT on the International Space Station. The aim is to assist with predicting issues before failures escalate, reconstruct missing sensor values from historical data, and generate explainable mission health reports for astronauts and ground teams, all without sending data back to Earth before analysis.

articles.title: AWS named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
AWS named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service
I’m proud to share that Amazon Web Services (AWS) has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) for Amazon Connect for the fourth consecutive year. We believe this recognition reflects years of work pushing on what’s possible in customer experience.
When we launched Amazon Connect Customer, we set out to evolve how businesses serve their customers: to make personalized, intelligent experiences possible without giving up efficiency, flexibility, or control. That belief still drives how we build today.
Customer expectations have shifted. People expect you to recognize them, understand what they need, and stay consistent across every channel. They don’t want to repeat themselves. They don’t want to navigate disconnected systems to solve a simple problem. They want interactions that feel natural, relevant, and genuinely helpful. Meeting that takes more than traditional contact center technology, it takes a comprehensive solution that brings together customer context, AI, and the flexibility to adapt. That’s what we’re building with Amazon Connect Customer.
Customer experience without compromise
What matters most to your customers hasn’t changed: they want to be known, they want their problems fully resolved, and they want to trust you in the moments that matter. Read the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant to know why we are recognized.
Experiences that start with knowing the customer. Connect Customer builds a living picture of every customer: who they are, what they’ve been through, what they need next. Every touchpoint draws on that intelligence. Your customer feels known before a single word is exchanged. That’s what personal actually looks like.
Resolution that carries all the way through.
Most of the industry is still optimizing for deflection: getting customers away from humans as fast as possible. We took a different path. Connect Customer is built for the hard things: the disputed claim, the renegotiated mortgage, the disrupted itinerary that needs real action and can’t go wrong. We carry those interactions all the way through to resolution, and we make them feel natural and personal.
Generative and agentic AI push this further: understanding what a customer needs and acting on it. Every action is auditable. Humans step in when the moment calls for it. You get enterprise scale and the confidence that nothing slips through the cracks.
Building for what’s next
The companies that win the next decade of customer experience won’t be the ones with the most channels or the fastest bot. They’ll be the ones whose customers feel known, whose problems actually get resolved, and whose trust is earned in the moments that matter most. Connect Customer exists to make that real for businesses of every size.
I’m proud of the Connect Customer team for receiving this recognition for the fourth year in a row. Our engineers, product teams, partners, and customers shaped what we’ve built. This is a moment to celebrate how far we’ve come, and a signal of what’s ahead.
Every customer is unique. Every interaction should reflect that.

articles.title: Jobwechsel in unsicheren Zeiten: Für wen er sich lohnt – und für wen nicht
articles.text:
Jobwechsel in unsicheren Zeiten: Für wen er sich lohnt – und für wen nicht
Doch in wirtschaftlich unsicheren Zeiten scheuen viele Beschäftigte einen Arbeitgeberwechsel. Aus einem Sicherheitsbedürfnis heraus halten sie am alten Job fest – Sicherheit wiegt häufig stärker als der Wunsch nach beruflicher Veränderung oder höherem Gehalt.
Dabei lohnt es sich gerade in einer allgemeinen Krisenstimmung, sich aktiv mit seinen beruflichen Vorstellungen und Wünschen auseinanderzusetzen, wie Georg Scheiber von der Beratungsgesellschaft von Rundstedt in Nürnberg sagt. Beschäftigte sollten sich kritisch fragen, welches Standing sie aktuell in ihrem Unternehmen haben und ob sie dort eine Zukunft sehen.
Wer bei dieser Analyse feststellt, dass der eigene Job wackeln könnte, sollte sich aktiv nach einem neuen Arbeitgeber umschauen. „Besser ist es, das Steuer selbst in die Hand zu nehmen, statt es dem Arbeitgeber zu überlassen“, so Scheiber. Für alle, die strategisch vorgehen, könne ein Wechsel gerade in wirtschaftlich unsicheren Zeiten der richtige Schritt sein.
Was für einen Wechsel spricht
Wunsch nach einem sicheren Arbeitsplatz: Ist der aktuelle Arbeitgeber Teil einer schwächelnden Branche wie etwa des traditionellen Einzelhandels, kann ein Wechsel in eine Wachstumsbranche wie beispielsweise die erneuerbaren Energien den Arbeitsplatz langfristig sichern. Einen Branchenwechsel sollten Beschäftigte frühzeitig planen. „Wechselwillige müssen für sich ausloten, welche Weiterbildung oder Umschulung sie brauchen, damit der Übergang in die andere Branche gelingt“, sagt Scheiber.
Mehr Geld: Wer in der bisherigen Branche bleiben möchte, kann bei einem anderen Unternehmen oft eine höhere Gehaltssteigerung erzielen als im Fall einer internen Beförderung. „Voraussetzung ist, dass die eigenen Kompetenzen und Fähigkeiten auf dem Arbeitsmarkt gerade stark nachgefragt sind“, so Scheiber. Das können zum Beispiel technische und digitale Kompetenzen etwa im Bereich Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) und Datensicherheit sein.
Kürzerer Pendelweg: Auch ein im Vergleich zum bisherigen Unternehmen kürzerer Pendelweg ist laut Scheiber oft ein starkes Argument für einen Arbeitgeberwechsel. Denn weniger Zeit auf der Straße im Stau oder in der Bahn sorgt für eine bessere Lebensqualität und spart Geld.
Bessere Konditionen: Auch bessere Karrierechancen oder passendere Aufgaben können für einen Arbeitgeberwechsel sprechen. „Ein Grund für den Wechsel kann etwa auch sein, dass im neuen Unternehmen im Gegensatz zum alten öfter in der Woche Homeoffice möglich ist und sich so Privat- und Berufsleben besser verbinden lassen“, sagt Scheiber.
Was gegen einen Wechsel spricht
Ein Gegenargument ist das Prinzip „Wer zuletzt kommt, geht zuerst“. Das bedeutet, dass neue Mitarbeitende bei Stellenstreichungen oft als Erste die Kündigung bekommen. Weitere Argumente sind:
Geringerer Kündigungsschutz: In den ersten sechs Monaten beim neuen Arbeitgeber gilt zudem der gesetzliche Kündigungsschutz nicht. „Der neue Arbeitgeber kann das Beschäftigungsverhältnis ohne Angaben von Gründen mit einer Frist von zwei Wochen kündigen“, sagt Kathrin Schulze Zumkley, Fachanwältin für Arbeitsrecht in Gütersloh.
Beim bisherigen Arbeitgeber hingegen haben langjährige Beschäftigte in aller Regel einen hohen Kündigungsschutz. „So beträgt die gesetzliche Kündigungsfrist beispielsweise bei einer zehnjährigen Betriebszugehörigkeit vier Monate zum Monatsende“, sagt Schulze Zumkley.
Die Rente ist nah: Scheiber rät Beschäftigten, die nur noch drei bis fünf Jahre bis zur Rente haben, von einem Arbeitgeberwechsel ab. Sollte es im neuen Betrieb auf fachlicher oder menschlicher Ebene nicht passen, drohen kurz vor der Rente unnötiger Stress und eine Sperrzeit beim Arbeitslosengeld I, falls das Arbeitsverhältnis auf eigenen Wunsch endet.
Job ist befristet: Ebenfalls keinen Sinn macht es, von einem Job mit unbefristetem Arbeitsvertrag in einen mit befristetem Vertrag zu wechseln – auch wenn die Tätigkeit noch so verlockend ist.
Lange keine Weiterbildung absolviert: Auch Beschäftigte, die seit Jahren keine Weiterbildung absolviert haben, sollten aus Sicht von Scheiber einen Arbeitgeberwechsel gut überlegen. Denn die Wahrscheinlichkeit sei groß, dass ihre Kenntnisse und Fähigkeiten nicht auf dem neuesten Stand sind und es zu Schwierigkeiten im neuen Job kommt. Besser: Erst weiterbilden, dann bewerben.
Bei einer Wechselabsicht strategisch vorgehen
Wer Pros und Contras abgewogen hat und an der Absicht festhält, den Arbeitgeber in wirtschaftlich unsicheren Zeiten zu wechseln, sollte strategisch vorgehen. „Es ist wichtig, genau für sich auszuloten, was man für sich mit dem Wechsel erreichen will“, sagt Scheiber.
So sei es sinnvoll, eine Liste mit Unternehmen zu erstellen, die zu den eigenen Werten und Karrierezielen passen. Zeichnet sich ein Favorit ab, sollte man sich unbedingt genau mit der Firma auseinandersetzen. Wie sieht das Geschäftsmodell aus – passt es zu meinen Plänen und Wünschen? Wie ist die Kunden- und Auftragsstruktur?
Antworten auf diese Fragen finden sich auf Unternehmenswebsites sowie in Geschäftsberichten, die oft ebenfalls online einsehbar sind. „Auch Arbeitgeber-Bewertungsportale sowie berufliche Netzwerke sind oft hilfreich, um sich ein Bild über ein bestimmtes Unternehmen zu machen“, so Scheiber.

articles.title: AI startup Simplismart raises $14M from Dallas Venture Capital, Nvidia, and others
articles.text:
AI startup Simplismart raises $14M from Dallas Venture Capital, Nvidia, and others
Simplismart said it will use the funding to develop its tech platform, for market expansion, and partnerships.
AI inference infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 million in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax.
The company will use the funds to further develop its AI inference platform, expand its partnerships with cloud providers and sovereign AI initiatives, and strengthen its presence in North America and other global markets.
Simplismart builds software that connects AI models with GPU infrastructure. Its modular inference engine enables businesses to configure models based on their speed, cost and performance requirements, while its orchestration platform manages deployment and scaling across cloud and on-premises infrastructure.
“We have spent four years building the software layer between the model and the GPU, helping customers optimise how their workloads are deployed and operated. This funding will allow us to take that platform to more enterprises and cloud providers globally,” said Amritanshu Jain, Co-founder and CEO, Simplismart.
The company said its annualised revenue run rate has grown 14-fold over the past six months. It counts companies such as HeyGen, Higgsfield, InVideo, Shiprocket, Apna and Ema among its customers, which use its platform to run production workloads across video, voice, multimodal and enterprise AI applications.
For its cloud-provider offering, Simplismart works with NVIDIA to deploy AI infrastructure. Unlike inference providers that purchase or reserve GPU capacity and resell it, Simplismart does not own compute infrastructure. Instead, it provides the software layer that enables third-party GPU fleets to run production AI workloads, positioning itself as a data centre enabler.
The platform allows cloud providers to offer managed AI services under their own brands without having to build the underlying software stack from scratch.
“Simplismart is rapidly emerging as a global player helping enterprises run AI workloads more efficiently, while enabling cloud providers to turn GPU capacity into scalable services. We are backing this fast-growing company because of its proven technical prowess in addressing a critical need in the AI infrastructure ecosystem globally, as well as the strong execution capabilities of its founding team,” said Dayakar Puskoor, Managing Partner, Dallas Venture Capital.

articles.title: From cheap tool to premium subscription: When a beloved app's price skyrockets
articles.text:
How much are you willing to pay to keep using your favorite app?
Maybe you’ve used it for years. Perhaps it performs a function so essential and specific that you couldn’t imagine what you’d do without it. But when the developer announces an extraordinary price hike, you’re forced to consider how much you really value that app.
Earlier this year, Evernote, a note-taking app, changed its subscription tiers, forcing some users to go from paying $130 per year to $250. The highest tier now costs more than 3.3 times as much as the most advanced tier did in 2023 and 10 times more than what Evernote charged for annual subscriptions from its 2008 launch until 2016.
That’s just one example of many longstanding consumer pieces of software that have seen dramatic price hikes in recent years. A lifetime pass to Plex, for example, was $75 in 2012. Today, it’s $250. Individual plans for Quicken, Robokiller, and Inkdrop have each doubled in price.
It’s easy to assume that the developers are miscalculating the value of their app or the loyalty of their users. But an unconventionally honest assessment regarding price hikes from Evernote owner Bending Spoons illustrates how owners of legacy software can apply pressure to loyal customers to extract additional revenue.
Evernote puts a fresh squeeze on old customers
When Bending Spoons bought Evernote in 2023, the app had a sizable customer base. In a June SEC filing, Bending Spoons explained that it was attracted to Evernote’s 200 million accounts and high user engagement.
“We… valued its robust subscriber retention, driven by a rich feature set and a highly engaged and tenured customer base,” the filing says. “Many customers had thousands of notes stored in Evernote and had developed personalized workflows on and around the product. At the time of acquisition, the average customer tenure was 7.2 years.”

articles.title: Moniepoint to cut product, engineering roles in restructuring
articles.text:
Moniepoint, the Nigerian financial services company, is restructuring its engineering and product teams, with some roles set to become redundant. The company is offering affected employees a voluntary exit package and plans to complete the process by the end of December, according to two employees with direct knowledge of the matter.
The restructuring, announced internally to staff on Monday, October 19, introduces smaller teams responsible for building and operating products from end to end, alongside new platform architect roles to oversee shared technology systems.
Moniepoint has grown from a single product into a financial services group spanning payments, banking, credit and business management. It now wants smaller teams with clearer responsibility for delivery and operations, rather than relying on multiple layers of coordination and sign-off.
A Moniepoint spokesperson said the restructuring should not be regarded as a layoff. The company did not disclose how many employees would be affected.
Staff were offered five months’ salary to resign voluntarily. However, Moniepoint can reject applications from employees whose skills it still needs, according to two employees who asked not to be named to speak freely. The voluntary exit window closed on Friday, October 23, and staff will be told whether their roles are affected between November 2 and November 11.
“As part of Moniepoint’s regular strategic review of operations, the management is restructuring the engineering and product functions for the next stage of growth,” the company said in a statement shared with TechCabal on Monday. “The company is moving to a structure of platform groups made up of small, focused product-area teams, each owning what it builds from end to end.”
Moniepoint heavily hired engineers and product managers as it grew to a unicorn valuation, building several financial products and a range of internal tools. As the teams grew, so did the layers of review and sign-off that slow large tech companies down.
The restructuring is Moniepoint’s answer. Small teams will each own a product from build to operation, and new platform architects will design and oversee the shared systems beneath them.
Much of a product manager’s job is coordination: writing specifications, setting priorities, and passing work from design to engineering to quality assurance. When one team owns a product end to end, there are fewer handoffs, and fewer people are needed to manage them.
“This model is designed for a business of the company’s size and ambition, giving teams greater autonomy and clearer accountability, while enabling faster product development, greater operational reliability, more consistent service for a growing customer base, and smoother expansion into new markets,” Moniepoint added in the statement.
Platform ownership
Moniepoint said the new structure requires fewer roles in some areas while creating others. As a result, some existing roles will become redundant. The company said it would consider affected employees for open positions elsewhere in the business and would initiate redundancy consultations only where it cannot identify suitable roles.
Employees in backend, frontend, mobile and quality-assurance engineering, as well as product management, are affected. The changes apply across the countries where Moniepoint operates.
Employees will be assessed against written criteria covering delivery and adaptability, work quality, their track record, and length of service. Engineering leaders will score staff, and the human resources team will review the scores across teams. Before any role is confirmed as redundant, the company will check for open roles that could suit the person.
The restructuring comes as Moniepoint expands its financial services business and decides where to deploy its resources.
Founded in 2015 as TeamApt, Moniepoint became a unicorn in October 2024 after a $110 million Series C round. The company says its subsidiaries process more than $400 billion in digital payments a year. In March, it bought a 78% stake in Kenya’s Sumac Microfinance Bank and, in August, phased out MonieWorld, its UK remittance product, less than 18 months after launch.
The job cuts come as Moniepoint continues to hire. The company hired more than 120 people in October, according to one employee, and brought in several heads of department from outside Nigeria, according to another. In May, Tosin Eniolorunda, Moniepoint’s chief executive officer, said the company was struggling to fill about 500 vacancies, later clarifying that the shortage was in senior technical talent.
Earlier this year, Moniepoint discussed internally how artificial intelligence could streamline product management, according to one employee. While the company did not name AI a driver of the restructuring, the discussion reflects a wider question of whether automation and new ways of organising work will enable technology companies to deliver more with smaller teams. In February, Zap Africa, a Nigerian cryptocurrency startup, cut 44% of its workforce as “part of an AI-driven efficiency shift.”
Wider shift
Moniepoint is not the first technology company to argue that smaller teams and clearer ownership can improve productivity. In February, Block, the parent company of Square and Cash App, cut 4,000 jobs, about 40% of its workforce. Chief executive Jack Dorsey linked the cuts to AI tools and a move towards “smaller and flatter teams.”
Across Africa, companies have also reduced staff while trying to improve profitability or refocus operations. Branch laid off employees in Kenya and Nigeria in May, despite reporting about $30 million in profit in 2025. That same month, Jumia said it would cut about 200 jobs as it incorporated AI into operations, logistics, finance, and marketing.
TechCabal Insights found that restructuring was the most common reason African tech companies gave for layoffs between January 2023 and March 2026, while one cited AI. If smaller teams work for the companies that try them, and AI keeps getting better at the specialised tasks those teams used to share, more African tech companies will hire fewer people to do the same work.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell to Root Firewalls
articles.text:
A China-linked threat actor has been exploiting the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to gain root access to firewalls and deploy webshells for persistent access, cybersecurity firm Dream reports.
The hackers have been chaining an exploit for the two PHP flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, with another for Fragnesia, a privilege escalation bug in the Linux kernel tracked as CVE-2026-46300.
As part of the observed attacks, the hackers used the Chinese internet asset search engine FOFA to identify 19,000 internet-facing firewalls from a specific vendor, and proceeded to exploit 25 of them on October 23-24, Dream says.
After discovery, the hackers first filtered servers in the US, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, then filtered those running newer PHP releases, which gave them a pool of 240 potential targets.
Using an automated tool, the attackers then targeted the firewalls with the full PHP2Shell-Fragnesia exploit chain, dropping a PHP root webshell on 24 devices for persistent access.
While no post-exploitation activity was observed on 22 of the firewalls, the hackers did progress further on two servers belonging to a US government-affiliated environment.
The first rooted server crashed shortly after exploitation, on October 23. The attacker launched a second wave of attacks on October 24, which was successful.
“The attacker monitored [the first firewall] with 240 automated probes over two hours, waiting for it to recover. It didn’t. The second firewall, whose certificate data definitively linked it to the target organization, had timed out during the original batch,” Dream notes.
To maintain access to the firewall, the attackers deployed a reverse SSH tunnel and then used it to target an internal firewall management server with the PHP2Shell-Fragnesia chain, gaining access to the configurations, credentials and settings of every firewall the organization managed.
The hackers then used the management server to access and decrypt the LDAP service account password, enumerate users and groups in the domain, perform password spraying attacks, and attempt to create Active Directory backdoor accounts, among others.
Dream has not attributed the activity to a specific threat actor but believes it is part of a Chinese-nexus operation.
“Since US, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea are the four primary strategic adversaries and intelligence targets for Chinese state-aligned cyber operations in the Pacific theater, this indicates potential nation-state adversary efforts,” Dream notes.
