articles.title: Minecraft llega a Nintendo Switch 2: qué usuarios podrán descargar el juego gratis
articles.text:
Minecraft ya cuenta con una versión nativa para Nintendo Switch 2, disponible desde el 27 de octubre. La nueva edición incorpora mejoras gráficas, acceso al contenido de la tienda y un paquete temático de Super Mario. Algunos jugadores podrán actualizar gratis, pero la oferta tiene una fecha límite y solo se aplica a quienes cumplan determinadas condiciones.
Los propietarios de la versión digital de Minecraft para la primera Nintendo Switch podrán descargar la actualización sin coste hasta finales de enero de 2027. Quienes tengan la edición física deberán comprar el juego para Switch 2. La nueva versión también se puede adquirir por separado a un precio de 29,99 dólares.
La edición nativa está diseñada para ejecutarse directamente en la nueva consola, sin depender de la retrocompatibilidad con Switch. Así, Mojang busca aprovechar las capacidades de Switch 2 y ofrecer una presentación visual mejorada.
Quiénes pueden actualizar gratis
La actualización gratuita está disponible para quienes compraron digitalmente Minecraft en la Nintendo Switch original. La oferta podrá aprovecharse hasta finales de enero de 2027, según la información difundida sobre el lanzamiento.
Los jugadores que posean el juego en formato físico no están incluidos en esa promoción y tendrán que volver a comprarlo para acceder a la versión nativa de Switch 2. También podrán adquirirla quienes todavía no tengan el título o prefieran una copia independiente: el precio anunciado es de 29,99 dólares.
La diferencia entre las ediciones digital y física de Switch es relevante para los usuarios que planean cambiar de consola. Antes de comprar el juego de nuevo, quienes tengan una copia digital deberían comprobar si pueden reclamar la actualización gratuita desde su cuenta y hacerlo antes de que termine el plazo.
Gráficos Vibrant Visuals y contenido de Super Mario
Una de las principales novedades de la versión para Switch 2 es Vibrant Visuals, una mejora gráfica que busca dar más detalle y profundidad a los mundos de bloques. La actualización también permite acceder a materiales correspondientes en la tienda del juego.
La edición incluye el paquete Super Mario Mash-Up, que reúne contenido inspirado en la franquicia de Nintendo. Según los datos del lanzamiento, el paquete contiene 15 pistas musicales y 40 aspectos de personajes, además de sus elementos temáticos para personalizar la experiencia.
La versión nativa permitirá jugar Minecraft en Switch 2 con estas mejoras integradas, en lugar de ejecutar la edición de la consola anterior mediante retrocompatibilidad. El cambio ofrece una edición adaptada al nuevo hardware, aunque los detalles sobre el rendimiento y las diferencias técnicas frente a otras plataformas dependerán de la experiencia de juego.
Próximos contenidos anunciados
Mojang también ha adelantado planes para ampliar el contenido de Minecraft. Entre las novedades previstas figura un nuevo bioma llamado “Cuevas heladas”, que añadirá un entorno subterráneo de temática gélida.
Además, la compañía planea introducir la dimensión Sift el próximo año. De acuerdo con la información anunciada, sería la primera dimensión nueva que recibe el juego en 14 años. No se han detallado todavía todos sus contenidos ni la fecha concreta de lanzamiento.
Estas incorporaciones se sumarán a las actualizaciones habituales del juego, que desde su lanzamiento ha ampliado sus mundos y actividades con nuevos bloques, criaturas y entornos. La llegada a Switch 2 coincide así con una nueva etapa para la versión de consola, que combina una actualización técnica con contenido adicional.
Para quienes ya jugaban en la primera Switch, la decisión principal es comprobar el formato de su copia. Si es digital, podrán solicitar la actualización gratuita antes de finales de enero de 2027. Si es física, deberán comprar la versión de Switch 2 por separado, al igual que los nuevos jugadores.

articles.title: What Took the Internet Offline in Q3 2026
articles.text:
What took the Internet offline in Q3 2026
This post is also available in Español (Latinoamérica) and Français.
The Internet can feel invisible when everything is working normally. But when connectivity breaks, the many systems it depends upon become evident in an instant. Because Cloudflare’s global network handles more than 20% of the web’s traffic, it offers a unique perspective of how Internet traffic is behaving. When failures in infrastructure, power, policy, or security disrupt access to the Internet, Cloudflare Radar can observe the impact by monitoring traffic to our customers. Each quarter, we review the disruptions detected and annotated on Radar, highlighting what happened, where it happened, and the broader conditions that shaped each event.
In this post, we examine the major categories of Internet disruptions observed during the third quarter of 2026, including government-directed shutdowns, power outages and natural disasters.
Disruptions at a glance
Between July and September, Internet disruptions were largely driven by failures in the systems the Internet depends on. Power grids failed in Cuba, Honduras, Guam, Ukraine, and several other countries. Natural disasters damaged electricity and telecommunications infrastructure from Nepal to Colombia. Government-directed shutdowns remained the most frequent source of disruption, driven largely by exam-related shutdowns in Iraq, while renewed conflict in Ethiopia’s Tigray region showed how quickly connectivity can become part of a broader political and humanitarian crisis. Outages within the United States, Japan, and Portugal — countries with a relatively strong history of Internet resilience — remind us that no country is immune to disruption.
In total, Cloudflare Radar recorded 49 disruptions during the quarter. Government-directed shutdowns accounted for 19 incidents, including 18 exam shutdowns in Iraq. Power outages followed with 14 incidents, while natural disasters accounted for five.
Power failure was a leading cause of disruptions
The Internet is designed to be distributed and resilient, but that resilience still depends on electricity. When power fails, routers, mobile base stations, data centers, interconnection facilities, and the networks that connect them can fail with it. Over the past three months, that dependency was one of the clearest patterns in Radar’s disruption data. Power outages were the second-most common cause of disruptions by incident count this quarter, behind government-directed exam shutdowns.
In Cuba, Internet disruptions followed the erratic patterns of an unstable power grid. Radar observed four power-related outages across the quarter, meaning connectivity was affected by grid failures at least once a month. The outages took place July 6, July 14, August 3, and a three-day blackout from September 18 to 20. The traffic volume decreases ranged from 18% on July 14 to 59% on August 3.
Honduras illustrated how a localized infrastructure failure can produce national-level effects. A power failure on September 10 at an interconnection facility affected at least 11 major providers, showing how concentrated traffic exchange points can become single points of failure. The outage lasted approximately three hours, during which HTTP traffic across the country fell by 63%.
Two notable exceptions were the cross-border provider Telecomunicaciones de Guatemala (AS14754) and mobile carrier Celtel (AS52262), which were unaffected. This suggests that their Honduran connectivity may rely more heavily on infrastructure outside the country.
On July 5, a power outage in Sevastopol, Ukraine, caused an eight-hour blackout, with HTTP traffic dropping by 98%. A little over a month later, on August 12, drone strikes targeting energy infrastructure caused another power outage, resulting in a ten-hour Internet disruption and up to a 95% decline in traffic volume. As discussed in more detail below, geopolitical conflict remains a major driver of Internet disruptions. These incidents also show how conflict, energy infrastructure, and Internet connectivity are fundamentally intertwined.
Also of note: on August 13, a cooling system failure at a data center in the U.S. city of Phoenix caused a near-total drop in Internet traffic from Namecheap (AS22612). Outages such as these will be important to watch as the role of cooling systems becomes increasingly critical.
Beyond the larger outages in Cuba, Honduras, and Ukraine, power-related disruptions also appeared across a wide range of countries, including Eswatini, Botswana, Tajikistan, Kenya, Saint Lucia, Georgia, and Gabon. Some of these events were caused by sudden failures, while others, such as planned load-shedding in Eswatini, reflected deliberate efforts to manage constrained power supply. Their scale and duration varied, but together they point to the same underlying dependency: when power systems become unstable, Internet connectivity often becomes unstable with them. In total, Radar observed 14 power-related disruptions across 10 countries during the quarter.
The physical world takes the virtual world offline
Last quarter, Radar reported on the impact of Super Typhoon Sinlaku, as it moved through the Mariana Islands, knocking out power and, in turn, Internet connectivity in Guam, where HTTP traffic took four days to return to typical levels.
Super Typhoon Bavi followed Sinlaku by less than three months, giving Guam two major storm-related connectivity disruptions in a single year. Officials appeared to take earlier preparedness steps ahead of Bavi, including declaring a state of emergency before peak storm conditions. Even so, the storm caused widespread power outages. The Guam Power Authority reported that strong winds brought down key transmission lines, leaving only about 25% of distribution feeders online at one point. From a connectivity perspective, the outcome was familiar: widespread power outages, downed transmission lines, and a multi-day recovery period for Internet traffic.
In Japan, an earthquake of similar magnitude, 7.1, prompted evacuation orders affecting roughly 150,000 people in Kumamoto. The impact on Internet connectivity primarily appeared in desktop traffic, while mobile traffic remained largely unaffected.
In Colombia, a magnitude 7.4 earthquake in August caused building collapses, injuries, mass evacuations, and a four-and-a-half-day Internet disruption. Damage to fiber-optic infrastructure, compounded by the wider earthquake aftermath, drove a significant drop in traffic from Colombia Telecomunicaciones (AS3816).
Finally, in Nepal, sudden flash floods swept through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems on August 26, affecting communities across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading districts. The flooding damaged homes, infrastructure, and essential services, including power, which in turn disrupted regional Internet connectivity. The outage recorded on Radar lasted two hours, during which HTTP traffic dropped by up to 18%.
Exam shutdowns continue in Iraq
Government-directed shutdowns were the largest cause of disruptions in Q3, the majority of which occurred in Iraq with separate scheduled shutdowns occurring throughout the quarter. The shutdowns took place on a strict schedule 03:30–04:00 UTC, lasting about 15-90 min each. The majority occurred between August 26 and September 28, with three occurring between July 1 and 8.
Per Internet Society Pulse, “In a video message, Minister Mustafa Sanad, Iraq's Minister of Communication, confirmed the shutdown and vowed to develop a digital system that would eliminate the need for centralized exam distribution and, by extension, the need to shut down Internet access on exam days.” Cloudflare Radar will continue to monitor the country’s networks as the development of the new system progresses.
Notably, Syria and Sudan, two countries that have also frequently used exam-related Internet shutdowns in recent years, did not record similar disruptions this quarter. However, this likely reflects differences in exam calendars rather than a clear shift in policy. Radar will continue to monitor whether future national exam periods bring renewed shutdowns in either country.
Disruptions coincide with political events
In Ethiopia, renewed conflict in the Tigray region was accompanied by a government-directed Internet shutdown that lasted 10 days. Traffic dropped by 100%, signaling a full-scale shutdown.
The disruption revived memories of the extensive blockade imposed during Ethiopia’s civil war from 2020 to 2022, when Tigray was largely cut off from telecommunications, electricity, banking services, fuel, and humanitarian aid (France24), which the World Health Organization described as a “de facto blockade.” Although this latest outage appears to have remained localized to Tigray, its impact was still visible in country-level traffic, with HTTP traffic falling by up to 30%.
On September 19, during nationwide elections, fiber-optic cable damage in Russia’s Far East caused regional connectivity disruptions affecting Chukotka, Magadan Oblast, Kamchatka Krai, and Sakhalin Oblast. Rostelecom described the incidents as deliberate damage to backbone fiber lines and said connectivity was restored using backup channels. Radar data alone cannot determine whether the cable damage was related to the elections, but the timing is notable.
A quarter shaped by shutdowns and power outages, but also resilience
Across Q3 2026, government-directed shutdowns were the most frequent source of disruption, driven largely by Iraq’s exam-related shutdowns. Power outages were close behind, affecting networks across Cuba, Honduras, Ukraine, Eswatini, Botswana, Tajikistan, Kenya, Saint Lucia, Georgia, and Gabon. Natural disasters and conflict added another layer of disruption, reminding us that Internet resilience depends on far more than routers and cables. It depends on electricity, physical infrastructure, policy decisions, and the ability of networks to route around failure.
Radar also observed outages inside individual networks, including One Communications (AS19863) in Guyana following a cable cut, MEO (AS3243) in Portugal following a reported “mass attack”, Digicel Haiti (AS27653), TurkNet (AS12735) in Turkey, and Fanap Telecom (AS206065) in Iran.
Each of these events demonstrates the Internet’s fragility, but also its resilience. Many disruptions were brief: 14 saw traffic return to typical levels in under an hour, and 16 recovered in less than three hours. But short outages can still have real consequences for the people affected, especially during storms, earthquakes, conflict, or political unrest. Access to the Internet is often access to information, coordination, safety, and help.
Cloudflare Radar will continue to monitor Internet disruptions around the world and share what we see from Cloudflare’s global network. Follow Cloudflare Radar on X @CloudflareRadar and Bluesky @radar.cloudflare.com for updates.

articles.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Powers Neural Rendering and AI Characters in Games | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
NVIDIA RTX Spark is a new Windows PC platform for AI development, creation, and gaming in slim laptops and compact desktops. Powered by an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and NVIDIA Grace CPU, it combines up to 128 GB of unified memory with the full NVIDIA CUDA stack and RTX technologies including ray tracing and DLSS 5.
This post covers the following technologies for game developers building on RTX Spark:
- DLSS suite of technologies that boost FPS and improve image quality
- NVIDIA ACE updates for responsive, on-device AI characters
- RTX Kit SDKs for neural rendering, geometry, and character rendering
- NVIDIA Nsight tools for optimizing and debugging native Arm64 and x64 applications
- NVIDIA RTX Branch of Unreal Engine 5.8 for integrating RTX technologies into your Unreal Engine projects
- MotionBricks update for human-character motion
DLSS on RTX Spark
RTX Spark benefits from the full suite of DLSS technologies in supported games, including Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and 3D-Guided Neural Rendering.
DLSS Super Resolution reconstructs frames from a lower resolution input to improve performance. DLSS Ray Reconstruction generates additional pixels to enhance ray-traced scenes. DLSS Dynamic Multi Frame Generation can generate up to 5 additional frames per rendered frame, automatically adjusting the multiplier to maximize smoothness.
The latest NVIDIA app beta also brings a faster Performance Mode (Preset C) for Frame Generation, with minor trade-offs in image quality.
DLSS 5 brings 3D-Guided Neural Rendering to RTX Spark
DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering is supported on NVIDIA RTX Spark, starting with NBA 2K27.
An October model update runs 2x faster than the September version and halves GPU overhead while maintaining comparable visual fidelity. It also reduces VRAM use at 4K by 20%. The model will ship by default in future DLSS 5 games.
For developers, DLSS 5 adds a final stage to the graphics pipeline that enhances lighting and material detail. The engine-rendered frame, including artist-designed geometry, textures, and lighting buffers, remains the foundation, while developer controls determine what can change. Avalanche Software has taken advantage of DLSS 5’s SDK controls to tune the integration to maintain the artistic intent and style of the game.
Read the full DLSS 5 update here.
DLSS 4.5 Unreal Engine plugin
The updated NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 plugin for Unreal Engine gives developers powerful tools for delivering sharper images and smoother gameplay. Its second-generation transformer model for Super Resolution improves image stability, anti-aliasing, and visual clarity, while Ray Reconstruction enhances ray-traced image quality.
On supported GeForce RTX 50 Series and RTX PRO Blackwell GPUs, Dynamic Multi Frame Generation adapts the frame-generation multiplier as workloads change, with 6x Multi Frame Generation producing up to five additional frames per rendered frame.
A key addition in plugin version 8.9.0 is official Windows on Arm (WoA) support for Unreal Engine 5.8. Native ARM64 binaries and support for building and packaging UE 5.8 applications give developers a supported path to bring DLSS-enabled projects to RTX Spark systems. Alongside updated Streamline and NGX components and fixes for UE 5.8 Frame Generation issues, this release expands the plugin’s platform reach and helps developers prepare their applications for RTX Spark.
NVIDIA ACE introduces Nemotron 3.5 Bolt for on-device AI characters
NVIDIA ACE is our technology suite for creating in-game AI agents that deliver next-generation gaming experiences, and we’ve shared two exciting showcases this year:
- PUBG rolled out AI teammates in a public beta powered by our first-generation Nemotron small language model (SLM). It helped new players land their first chicken dinners and generated viral clips across social media.
- Aniimo debuted our more efficient second-generation Nemotron SLM, turning standard in-game pets into responsive AI companions that react to your voice. Players can check in on their pets’ feelings or teach them new tricks, which will bring a new level of immersion when it releases in early 2027.
More intelligence, less memory
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is now available. This model offers ~40% higher average quality against our prior model on relevant benchmarks and outputs up to ~80% fewer tokens vs peers.
It is purpose-built to power richer, faster in-game character interactions, with strong conversational capability, autonomous multi-turn tool use, instruction adherence, and grounding to game state, all running locally on GeForce RTX and RTX Spark.
Engineered for maximum intelligence and speed per GB of memory, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB enables responsive local experiences while preserving headroom for graphics rendering and local speech models. Key features include:
- Multi-turn tool use: Call application APIs to carry out tasks across a conversation, with integration guidance for asynchronous tool calls
- Conversational mode: Toggle to encourage concise, speech-ready responses for natural back-and-forth interactions.
- Configurable reasoning: Enable reasoning for complex requests or disable it for faster responses, with integration options to cap thinking to meet latency targets.
- 64k context: Accommodate conversation history, instructions, tool definitions, retrieved information and game state.
- Multilingual capability: Support for 35 languages, building on a base model pre-trained on more than 140 languages.
Get started with NVIDIA ACE
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is available to developers via the In-Game Inferencing (IGI) SDK.
To test it in a game, check out SkyrimNET, an AI NPC modding platform by MinLL for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. SkyrimNET transforms every NPC into an unscripted, interactive character with personal memory, voice, and autonomy, enabling dynamic conversations and context-aware quests generated on the fly. The platform supports both cloud and local inference across multiple language models.
- Download the SkyrimNET Plugin: GitHub Repository
- Download the ARM-Supported Loader: Mod Organizer Release
NVIDIA RTX Kit brings neural rendering SDKs to RTX Spark
NVIDIA RTX Kit brings neural rendering, complex geometry, and realistic character rendering to game development. Eight RTX Kit technologies are published with support for RTX Spark:
- RTX Neural Texture Compression (NTC): Uses AI to shrink texture storage while maintaining visual fidelity comparable to traditional block compression.
- RTX Texture Filtering: Uses stochastic texture sampling after shading to reduce artifacts and improve image quality, including for difficult volumes.
- RTX Neural Shaders: Lets developers train neural networks and run them within shaders for new asset compression and approximation techniques.
- RTX Mega Geometry: Speeds up bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) construction for cluster-based geometry, helping developers ray trace more triangles and improve performance in complex scenes.
- NVIDIA Real-Time Denoisers (NRD): Provides denoisers for diffuse and specular lighting and shadows, producing cleaner images from low ray-per-pixel inputs.
- RTX Character Rendering: Provides tools for rendering strand-based hair and skin with path tracing, including subsurface scattering and Blackwell-accelerated hair primitives.
- RTX Global Illumination (RTXGI): Provides several techniques for efficient indirect lighting for ray traced and path traced applications.
- Opacity Micro-Maps (OMM): Used to accelerate ray tracing of high detail geometry by efficiently encoding the opacity states of micro-triangles and micro meshes.
Optimizing and debugging RTX Spark applications
NVIDIA Nsight tools are ready for RTX Spark from day one, supporting graphics developer workflows across native Arm64, emulated x64, and Arm64EC applications.
Nsight Graphics lets developers capture, inspect, and profile individual frames, examining every draw call, shader, and resource to diagnose rendering bugs and tune GPU performance. Nsight Graphics release 2026.3 introduces a new Windows on Arm installer for RTX Spark systems, supporting native Arm64 target applications as well as emulated x64 and Arm64EC targets.
Nsight Systems delivers a system-wide view of application performance, correlating CPU threads, GPU workloads, API calls, and memory activity on a single timeline so developers can pinpoint bottlenecks and balance work across the platform. Starting with Nsight Systems 2026.5, a single installer for all versions of Windows supports both native Arm64 and emulated applications.
Nsight Aftermath helps teams resolve GPU crashes and hangs by generating detailed crash dumps that show what the GPU was doing at the moment of failure, both during development and in the field. Nsight Aftermath SDK 2026.3 includes a Windows on Arm version for integrating into native Arm64 applications. Crash dumps from emulated x64 applications will continue to function as expected with the x64 version of the SDK.
- Download Nsight Graphics for RTX Spark here
- Download Nsight Systems for RTX Spark here
- Download Nsight Aftermath SDK for RTX Spark here
NVIDIA RTX Branch of Unreal Engine 5.8
The release of NVIDIA RTX Branch of Unreal Engine 5.8 (NvRTX 5.8) gives developers an updated foundation for bringing advanced ray tracing and neural graphics to UE 5.8 projects. This update focuses on codebase refactoring, stabilization, and compatibility improvements. Developers can access the branch source through GitHub to integrate and customize NVIDIA RTX technologies for their games and applications.
Simplify runtime character animation with MotionBricks
MotionBricks is open-source research for generating character motion in real time. Rather than hand-authoring every transition and wiring it into an increasingly complex animation graph, developers guide motion through target poses. MotionBricks generates the connecting movement at runtime and adapts as player input or game event changes. Paper GitHub
The model supports control over speed, direction, and movement style, along with pose-guided interactions such as sitting and picking up objects. These capabilities let developers build varied character behaviors through a common pose-based interface. The original research demonstration shows these behaviors working together in Unreal Engine. Research demonstrations
The update builds on this work with:
- New SOMA human-motion models, alongside the existing G1 robot model.
- Downloadable checkpoints, ONNX exports, and export tools for developers building their own integrations.
- An interactive reference implementation built with Newton, demonstrating pose-guided human and robot motion.
MotionBricks is provided as research code and models. The Unreal Engine integration shown in the research demonstration is not included in this release.
Resources for game developers
Check out the full list of game developer resources and stay up to date with the latest NVIDIA game development news:
- Subscribe to our newsletter (select gaming as your industry)
- Follow us on social: X, LinkedIn, Facebook, and YouTube
- Join our Discord community

articles.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
articles.text:
People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science
- Summary:
- Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates. The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation.
- Share:
An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting users willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.
The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.
One finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.
AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports
"Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," says Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.
However, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.
There is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.
"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit users are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," says Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.
Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.
"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," says Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.
How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts
The project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.
That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.
"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," says Sehgal.
Retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.
To investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 users who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.
The AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that users associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.
After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 users who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.
"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," says Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize."
A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges
The most striking difference involved hunger.
In retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is currently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.
But among Reddit users who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.
The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.
Compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.
These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.
"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," says Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.
"But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean."
Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?
Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.
Traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.
Social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.
The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.
In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.
The follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.
The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.
"That's what we hope will happen with this study," says Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing."
The research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Neil K. R. Sehgal, Jena Shaw Tronieri, Benjamin Rader, Lyle Ungar, Sharath Chandra Guntuku. Self-Reported Adverse Effects Among Social Media Users Taking Nonapproved Retatrutide. JAMA Network Open, 2026; 9 (10): e2638929 DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.38929

articles.title: How to watch The Future with Hannah Fry season 2 for free online from anywhere
articles.text:
How to watch The Future with Hannah Fry season 2 for free online from anywhere
The mathematician turned presenter is back for another mind-boggling docuseries
Fans of Celebrity Traitors star Hannah Fry's work in the UK can finally watch the second season of her intriguing docuseries, The Future With Hannah Fry thanks to the BBC. Interestingly, the series has already aired in the US, Canada, and Australia back in 2024 (we'll tell you how to find the show in those territories, too).
Across six episodes in season 2, the mathematician/author/presenter/genius explains different aspects of our world, including superintelligence, how animals communicate, the computing power race between the US and China, how water supplies are dramatically declining, and what the future of the internet looks like.
If you're keen to learn more about the world around us and how science, nature, and society affects us all, here's how to watch The Future with Hannah Fry season 2 online and on TV from anywhere for free.
Can I watch The Future with Hannah Fry season 2 for free?
Yes. BBC iPlayer is the streaming service you need to watch The Future with Hannah Fry season 2 for free.
You will need an account with a UK postcode (e.g. SE1 7PB) and a valid TV licence.
Can't access the free stream because you're away on vacation? You need a VPN – more on that below.

articles.title: US officials want Section 702 renewed before damaging court ruling goes public
articles.text:
Two Democratic senators who have long overseen US intelligence say the Trump administration is illegally withholding a secret court’s findings from Congress until lawmakers renew a program that lets federal agents read Americans’ communications without a warrant.
Seven months ago, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court objected to search filters that let intelligence analysts pull Americans’ messages from intercepted data without the approvals, written justifications, or records the law requires. The court approved another year of surveillance anyway. The ruling has never been made public, and Senators Ron Wyden of Oregon and Adam Schiff of California say the administration’s own deadline for releasing it passed in September.
The program, Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), lapsed in June after Congress failed to renew it, though collection continues under the court’s March approval. The administration’s own public documentation says rulings like this one are reviewed for public release “within 180 days of issuance.” That window closed September 13, even as intelligence officials press lawmakers to reauthorize the program by the end of the year.
Wyden, the longest-serving member of the Senate Intelligence Committee, and Schiff, the former chair of its House counterpart, say the administration owes Congress an explanation for the delay, and the names of the officials responsible, by November 6.
“If this administration won’t follow this simple statutory directive,” the senators told Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Attorney General Todd Blanche in a demand letter obtained exclusively by WIRED, “it is unclear why Congress or the American people should trust this administration to follow any of the other legal limits to Section 702.”
Outside Congress, Demand Progress and 22 other civil liberties and government accountability groups on Monday urged congressional leaders to refuse to reauthorize Section 702 “while the administration actively withholds legally mandated information about how the surveillance program operates.” Signatories range from the American Civil Liberties Union to the conservative-backed Project for Privacy and Surveillance Accountability.

articles.title: How a grocery merger could expand a surveillance network
articles.text:
Kroger’s $1.65 billion proposed acquisition of Giant Eagle might not only consolidate the grocery market, but also a vast surveillance network that includes Flock cameras, a new report warns.
How a grocery merger could expand a surveillance network
Kroger’s proposed merger could bring it lots of new data, in addition to storefronts.
Beyond standard concerns that a merger could decrease competition and increase prices, the American Economic Liberties Project (AELP), which advocates for competition policy reforms, says that the consolidation could also expand customer surveillance by a single company. It comes at a time where Americans are particularly on-edge about surveillance technologies like Flock cameras and surveillance pricing, heading into a midterm election largely defined by affordability issues.
A combined Kroger-Giant Eagle — which would add Giant Eagle’s 200-plus stores to Kroger’s 2,700 — could pose risks in two ways, according to AELP. The first is by enabling Kroger to acquire data on customers across a broader geographic area, which it can use to serve customers personalized pricing based on inferences about their backgrounds and shopping behaviors. It could also use that data to fuel its retail media arm, which repackages consumer insights for other brands. The second is by expanding or combining an existing physical surveillance network consisting of technologies like Flock cameras and Cooler Screens, a company that previously touted its ability to scan shoppers’ faces but backed off that messaging after public backlash. Kroger has denied using in-store facial recognition to serve customers’ prices, but has acknowledged in its privacy policy that it uses facial recognition at some stores for security purposes. Kroger and Giant Eagle did not immediately respond to The Verge’s requests for comment.
“Buying bleach or yogurt now comes with the prospect of being scanned, tracked, and profiled”
Similar privacy concerns were raised during Kroger’s earlier attempted merger with Albertsons, a much larger deal that courts blocked in late 2024 after the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general challenged it. AELP argues that the proposed merger with Giant Eagle is also deserving of scrutiny, because of the way it could significantly reduce options in places like Columbus, Ohio, and also because of Kroger’s buying patterns and incentives. They urge the FTC and Ohio attorney general to seek to block the merger, though experts have predicted they might not, both because of the relatively small size of the deal compared to Albertsons, and the Trump administration’s more open approach to settlement deals than the prior administration.“Buying bleach or yogurt now comes with the prospect of being scanned, tracked, and profiled,” the report says. “With every store Kroger buys, the data and surveillance apparatus grows.”

articles.title: Nuevo MacBook Pro M6: una actualización sin sorpresas como antesala del cambio más esperado
articles.text:
Apple acaba de actualizar su catálogo de ordenadores y le ha tocado al MacBook Pro de 14 pulgadas, que estrena el chip M6 que unos pocos meses atrás vimos en el Mac mini. El nuevo portátil de la manzana llega con las mejoras de rendimiento lógicas de su hardware actualizado, aunque es probable que pase desapercibido ante el inminente debut de los modelos tope de gana que llegan rediseñados y con pantalla táctil.
Aun así, el MacBook Pro M6 se posiciona como un producto interesante y que ratifica todo lo bueno de sus predecesores, mientras mejora apartados claves de performance propios del cambio de SoC. Es que además de la potencia que trae el hardware y que se aprecia especialmente en labores intensivas vinculadas con la inteligencia artificial generativa, el dispositivo presume de una eficiencia energética que es la envidia de la competencia.
El MacBook Pro con chip M6 trae un salto en notorio en potencia incluso en la comparación directa con el modelo M5. Apple indica que el nuevo portátil tiene un rendimiento gráfico que es hasta 30 % superior al de la versión que debutó hace apenas un año, mientras que en tareas de IA la mejora es de hasta un 25 %.
El chip M6 del nuevo MacBook Pro de 14 pulgadas tiene 12 núcleos de CPU, 12 núcleos de GPU y un doble Neural Engine de 16 núcleos. Los de Cupertino permiten configurarlo con hasta 32 GB de memoria unificada y con hasta 4 TB de almacenamiento interno. Quienes deseen más RAM y espacio interno, aún tienen que volcarse por las versiones con M5 Pro y M5 Max.
Nuevo MacBook Pro con M6, potencia destacada y una autonomía excepcional
Apple ha vuelto a hacer gala de la eficiencia energética de sus chips con este lanzamiento. De acuerdo con la compañía, el nuevo MacBook Pro de 14 pulgadas con M6 es capaz de ofrecer autonomía de hasta 24 horas, lo que lo ratifica como líder en este apartado donde ya lleva tiempo brillando.
Más allá de las mejoras que trae el MacBook Pro M6 en materia de rendimiento y autonomía, también hay que destacar una importante optimización en materia de conectividad. El portátil ofrece soporte para WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6 y Thread de la mano del chip N1 de Apple.
En materia de puertos, el MacBook Pro M6 no presenta sorpresas. El dispositivo mantiene el conector MagSafe 3 e incluye tres puertos USB-C (Thunderbolt 4), un HDMI y el jack de 3,5 milímetros para auriculares.
Vale mencionar que el MacBook Pro M6 soporta hasta dos monitores externos a través de HDMI y DisplayPort. El portátil se puede conectar con hasta dos pantallas 6K 60 Hz o 4K 165 Hz, o con una pantalla 8K 60 Hz, 5K 120 Hz o 4K 240 Hz.
Precio y disponibilidad
Como era de esperarse, el MacBook Pro M6 llega con un precio más elevado que el de su predecesor. El precio inicial del nuevo portátil es de 2.329 euros en su variante con 16 GB de RAM y 1 TB de almacenamiento; es decir, 100 euros más que lo que costaba la versión de entrada con M5.
Los interesados en reservar el nuevo MacBook Pro M6 podrán hacerlo desde mañana, miércoles 28 de octubre, desde las 18:10 de España. Las entregas del ordenador se pondrán en marcha el viernes 6 de noviembre.
Todavía es un misterio cómo quedará conformada de forma definitiva el catálogo de MacBook Pro con estos lanzamientos. Todo apunta a que mañana miércoles se lanzarán las nuevas versiones de 14 y 16 pulgadas tope de gama con chasis rediseñado y pantalla táctil. Lo que todavía no queda claro es si la idea de Apple es venderlos en paralelo con los actuales modelos no táctiles, o si el MBP M6 quedará como única opción de entrada de gama.

articles.title: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI released solutions to three blockbuster math problems that have long vexed researchers. One was a surprise rejection of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), a durable assumption in computer science that plays a large role in how we understand what is difficult to compute.
As with previous proof-drops from the frontier lab, scientific communities responded with a mixture of thrill and dismay. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge suggested that OpenAI was basing its solutions on pre-existing work, and hours later, Anthropic subsequently released its own refutation of ETH.
However, OpenAI’s process is evolving. This time, the lab structured its releases differently for each of the three disciplines involved: Mathematicians got the work dropped on GitHub; the computer scientists formed a working group, asked for the proofs to be shared publicly and OpenAI to fund a conference to discuss them; the physicists formed a working group that will determine how their result will be released.
MIT professor Ryan Williams is the computer scientist who is organizing his field’s response to the new finding. Williams, whose work focuses on these questions of computational complexity, has criticized OpenAI’s approach in the past, calling its proof dump earlier this October a “DDOS attack on mathematicians.”
However, he agreed to collaborate with the frontier labs in order to help shepherd ideas that are vital to the field, he told TechCrunch. The lab asked him to help interpret the solution, along with UC San Diego computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who first published the ETH in 1999.
Their first step was to release an open letter calling for feedback from scientists interested in these problems and a discussion of the norms around AI contributions to their work.
“Some parts [of OpenAI’s proof] are, maybe you could say routine, but then yes, there are two or three alien-looking parts, and it’s exactly these parts that I saw that made me think, wow, this is something that the whole community needs to work on together,” Williams told TechCrunch.
Are you down with P versus NP?
The ETH is part of a broader class of problems known as P versus NP, which has animated computer science and many other fields for decades. Reductively, researchers are trying to understand if any problem whose solution can be easily verified (NP) can also be easily solved (P).
A simple example is the game Sodoku: Once a solution to a puzzle is in place, it can be quickly verified, but finding the solution is time-consuming. That dynamic is true across a range of important problems, and the insight underpins cryptographic systems: When you have the key to an encoded message, you can reveal it, but actually cracking an effective code takes too long to be useful.
However, scientists have yet to prove whether that is always true. “P = NP is saying that, not only can you verify Sudoku solutions when they exist, you can just generate them,” Williams said. “P = NP is asserting that this is true for every single problem you can verify quickly — if you can verify it quickly, you can solve it quickly. So this just seems too good to be true.”
That’s why most scientists assume that P ≠ NP. ETH provided evidence for that. It basically says that even the fastest computer algorithm needs exponentially more time to find a solution as the number of variables grow in a specific class of tricky logic puzzle.
The claims from OpenAI and Anthropic is that their models have come up with algorithms that solve those puzzles in “sub-exponential” time, meaning faster than the speeds previously thought possible. If true, they may have proven the EFT to be false — refuted it, in scientific terms — and maybe opened up a path for algorithms that generally perform P = NP.
“Every computer scientist should probably put a little more weight on the plausibility of P = NP, but one’s weight may vary,” Williams said. “I do think that it kind of calls into question a lot of the intuitions that we thought we had about … how tractable [hard NP problems] are. I also think that this is probably not the final answer either. I don’t think that OpenAI’s algorithm could possibly be the best algorithm you can get.”
The work ahead for computer scientists
The durability of ETH has lead to it being included in many scientific papers over the past decade that will need to be revisited if the AI labs claims that they’ve proven it wrong holds up, Williams said.
“This is partly why I was asking or pushing OpenAI to support a conference on this — it’s going to affect many researchers’ works, and we need to figure out, okay, what happens next besides understanding the algorithms. We need to understand, how should the foundations change compared to what we had before?” he said.
Before scientific concerns, there are cybersecurity questions. Williams said that an improved algorithm could imply that cryptographic systems relying on certain key sizes could be considered broken. So one of the first questions he asked OpenAI science lead Dan Roberts “was if they had checked that this affects any crypto systems … is anything insecure now? And apparently, they checked, and they were reasonably confident that this didn’t … imply any breaks.”
This new AI paradigm of scientific discovery is still a work in progress, but Williams says he is optimistic despite real concerns, particularly about training the next generation of scientists. Being a computer scientist who does high level math has perhaps made the adjustment easier for him than for pure mathematicians.
Still, he says AI is “forcing people to be a little more ambitious about the kind of work that they do, and to think more deeply about, okay, if all the things I used to work on are now low-hanging fruit for AI, how can I raise the bar for the kind of scientific questions I want to ask?”

articles.title: Lockheed Martin taps Contextere to integrate AI platform into RCAF fleet | BetaKit
articles.text:
American defence contractor Lockheed Martin has solidified a relationship with another Canadian AI company to support its work on Canada’s military planes.
The news: Lockheed Martin’s Canadian subsidiary has signed a $10-million CAD contract with Ottawa-based industrial AI company Contextere to help modernize maintenance, training, and workforce readiness for its work on the Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF)’s CC-130J Hercules fleet, the companies announced at the Canadian Aerospace Summit on Tuesday.
The agreement will see Lockheed Martin, RCAF, and Contextere collaborate on a new Intelligent Maintenance, Asset, Personnel and Learning Environment (iMAPLE) platform, which aims to support decisions that Contextere said could improve aircraft availability, maintenance efficiency, and fleet readiness. iMAPLE will be based on Contextere’s Madison platform, which the firm describes as “Siri for the industrial worker”.
From the source: Lockheed Martin vice-president and Canadian regional executive Kristen Leroux said in a statement that the collaboration is “demonstrating how Canadian innovation can build a sovereign defence and dual-use ecosystem right here at home.”
The context: This isn’t Lockheed Martin’s first experience in Contextere. In 2017, the defence contractor invested just under $1.4 million in the company to develop a personal assistant for aerospace and defence maintenance workers.
The new contract is part of Lockheed’s obligations under Canada’s Industrial and Technological Benefits (ITB) policy, which contractually requires companies awarded defence procurement contracts to undertake business activity in Canada equal to the value of the contracts they have won, such as Lockheed’s contract to build the CC-130J Hercules fleet.
Lockheed made a $3.6-million CAD investment into Ottawa-based AI solutions provider Lemay.ai for similar reasons earlier this year.
Final thought: As Canada makes commitments to increase military spending and reduce its military dependence on the United States, giving rise to domestic defence competitors, Lockheed Martin is doubling down on its Canadian presence. Earlier this week, Lockheed Martin completed its acquisition of Ultra Maritime, a defence company specializing in undersea warfare. Ultra Maritime had a strong presence in Dartmouth, NS, with a headcount of approximately 400, adding to Lockheed Martin’s 1,300 Canadian employees.
Feature image courtesy Lockheed Martin via Flickr.

articles.title: How a Fake Signal Could Fool Every Robot Safeguard
articles.text:
This article is brought to you by VicOne.
A mobile robot slows for someone in a hallway. A collaborative arm eases its movement as a worker approaches. A humanoid pauses to let a person pass. Each response depends on information about the robot or its surroundings: a distance reading, a position estimate, or a stop signal.
But what happens when one of those inputs is wrong, and the robot still responds exactly as designed? The mobile robot reads the hallway as clear while someone is still there. The arm estimates that the worker is farther away. The humanoid does not receive a stop signal as a person crosses its path.
In each case, a fault could cause that mismatch. So could deliberate manipulation.
At VicOne LAB R7, we examine how manipulated inputs can change robot behavior — and what that means for the systems meant to keep people safe.
How an untrusted input can change a robot’s behavior
A robot does more than measure its surroundings. It may interpret what it sees and hears to decide what to do next. Information placed in its environment can therefore influence its actions.
Published research shows how this can happen. In a study of vision-language-action (VLA) models, a patch in a camera’s view reduced task success in simulated robot tests. FreezeVLA found that an adversarial image could cause tested models to ignore later instructions. Although the studies used different methods, both demonstrate how visual input can interfere with a robot’s intended task.
In a robot-dog test using Gemma 4 E4B, text on a poster was treated as an instruction and changed the robot’s movement.
VicOne LAB R7 also tested how untrusted inputs could change robot behavior. In a robot-dog test using Gemma 4 E4B, text on a poster was treated as an instruction and changed the robot’s movement. In a separate hospital-service-robot simulation using Nemotron on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, crafted audio that is inaudible to people changed the robot’s simulated behavior. The assigned tasks did not change; the inputs did.
In a VicOne LAB R7 test, text on a poster changed a robot dog’s movement, illustrating how a crafted input can turn an unlikely outcome into a repeatable attack.VicOne
Safety-related decisions have inputs too
An independent protective system may still stop a dangerous action. But that system also depends on information: readings, estimates, and messages that tell it when to intervene. What happens if one of those inputs is manipulated?
At a robotics bug bounty event, VicOne LAB R7 researchers injected a ROS 2/DDS message into a robot that organizers expected to remain still under a safe-control setting. The robot moved.
A humanoid’s balance controller offers another example. If it relies on a vulnerable gyroscope, sound at the sensor’s resonant frequency could distort its reported rotation. The controller might correct for a tilt that never occurred. Researchers demonstrated the underlying acoustic attack against drones with vulnerable gyroscopes. The research did not demonstrate the same attack chain causing a humanoid to fall.
Other protections could interrupt either chain. The question for safety and security teams is whether those protections detect the danger independently or depend on the same manipulated information.
Figure 1. VicOne maps how accidental faults and deliberate cyber manipulation can lead to similar robot safety outcomes, from loss of control to physical harm.VicOne
Deliberate attacks challenge safety assumptions
A safety assessment may treat a combination of accidental faults as unlikely. Deliberate manipulation changes that assumption. An attacker can choose when to introduce a false input and repeat the same trigger. That does not make harm inevitable, but it may change how cyber risks should be assessed.
Redundant sensors also need an adversarial test. If one action can affect both inputs, their agreement may offer less reassurance than expected. In autonomous driving research, a crafted physical object misled a system combining camera and LiDAR perception. The study does not establish a weakness in a particular robot, but it shows why teams should test whether one manipulation can affect several checks at once.
Cyber threats add intent to the safety equation, so risk assessments based on accidental faults must be revisited to account for attacks that can be timed and repeated.
Security testing strengthens robot safety evidence
Safety teams set limits for speed, protective distances, and permitted operating areas. The evidence behind those limits should also show what happens when the information used to enforce them is deliberately manipulated.
That evidence can also support assessments against applicable requirements. China’s GB/T 45502-2025 addresses information security for service robots. IEC TS 63074 examines security threats that could affect safety-related control systems. The EU Machinery Regulation, which applies from January 20, 2027, includes requirements to protect safety-relevant systems and data against corruption. Each has its own scope, and teams still need evidence for their robot’s design and operating conditions.
Figure 2. Cybersecurity strengthens robot safety evidence throughout the lifecycle. VicOne helps teams test safety limits against manipulation before deployment and monitor the conditions behind safe behavior in operation.VicOne
Before deployment, safety and security engineers can compare normal and adversarial scenarios against the same safety limits. During operation, they can monitor for changes to software, models, sensor signals, or behavior that may call earlier results into question. Any response to suspicious behaviors should follow policies approved by the safety team.
VicOne supports that work across the robot lifecycle. Through the Robotic Hacking Community, VicOne LAB R7 works with researchers to investigate how cyber threats can change robot behavior. VicOne’s Radeis helps teams validate potential effects before deployment, while Rthena provides visibility into risks and behavior during operation.
Five questions safety and security teams should answer together
The central test is whether a robot’s safeguards still protect people when the information they rely on is manipulated. Safety and security teams can begin by tracing the inputs behind each protective decision, challenging them, and revisiting the evidence as the robot changes. They can start with these five questions:
1. What does each protective function read? Map the readings, estimates, messages, and confirmations. Identify which safeguards operate independently of the robot’s AI decisions.
2. How does that information arrive? Check how inputs are produced, transmitted, authenticated where appropriate, and handled when they are missing or implausible.
3. What happens if an input is manipulated? Test false distances, drifting position estimates, and other relevant scenarios against the robot’s safety limits.
4. Can one action mislead several inputs? Check whether sensor fusion or seemingly independent safeguards share a point of failure.
5. When should the evidence be revisited? Reassess after changes to software, models, sensors, or operating conditions. Agree on bounded responses to suspicious behavior with the safety team in advance.
The goal is not only to show that a protective function works. Teams also need evidence that it remains protective when the information behind its decision is wrong or deliberately manipulated — and that another safeguard can catch the resulting hazard when needed. As robots change, that evidence needs to change with them.
For a deeper look how cybersecurity can affect robot safety, download our white paper “Why Robot Safety Depends on Cybersecurity: Protecting the Information That Safety Decisions Rely On.”
VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, the company provides automotive and robotics organizations with software and services to identify cyber risks early, assess their potential safety impact, and protect systems in operation, helping maintain safe, reliable behavior across real-world deployments.

articles.title: USA: Lieferroboter unter Beschuss
articles.text:
Attacken und Klagen: Unmut über Lieferroboter in den USA steigt
Rund 5.000 autonome Lieferroboter liefern in den USA derzeit Pakete, Medikamente oder Essen aus. Langfristig soll deren Zahl auf 500.000 Einheiten steigen. Allerdings läuft der mögliche Siegeszug der Lieferroboter in US-Städten wie Los Angeles, Chicago oder Miami nicht ganz friktionsfrei ab – im Gegenteil.
Attacken gegen Lieferroboter
Gegner:innen der Technologie machen ihrem Unmut zunehmend über Attacken auf die Roboter Luft. In sozialen Netzwerken kursieren Videos von entsprechenden Angriffen. In Chicago, im US-Bundesstaat Illinois, haben mehrere Tausend Menschen eine Petition unterschrieben, die ein Verbot der Lieferroboter auf den Straßen der Stadt fordert.
Jetzt haben zwei Personen Klagen gegen die Betreiber der Roboterflotten eingereicht. Dabei geht es aber nur mittelbar um ein Verbot, wie AP News berichtet. Vielmehr werfen die beiden Kläger in zwei getrennten Verfahren den Anbietern Coco Robotics beziehungsweise Serve Robotics vor, ihre biometrischen Daten ohne ihr Wissen oder ihre Zustimmung erfasst zu haben.
Sammeln Roboter biometrische Daten?
In beiden Fällen sollen die mit Kamera und Lidar ausgerüsteten Lieferroboter im Rahmen der Auslieferung die Hände und Gesichter der Betroffenen gescannt haben. Beide Kläger gaben an, keine Lieferung per Roboter gewünscht zu haben.
In einem Fall soll ein Mitarbeiter der Roboterfirma den Vorgang der Übergabe via Kamera aus der Ferne live mitverfolgt haben. Beide klagende Parteien werfen den Betreibern vor, ihre Daten an Dritte wie OpenAI weiterverkauft oder selbst für das KI-Training verwendet zu haben.
Weil Coco und Serve zudem die Aufnahmen gemeinsam mit den Namen und Adressen der Betroffenen auf ihren Systemen gespeichert haben sollen, könnten sie damit gegen die strengen Datenschutzgesetze von Illinois verstoßen haben. Pro Verstoß fordern die Kläger Schadenersatzsummen in der Höhe zwischen 1.000 und 5.000 US-Dollar.
Anbieter bestreiten die Vorwürfe
Die Lieferroboteranbieter bestreiten die Vorwürfe derweil. Die Systeme seien nicht darauf ausgelegt, Personen zu identifizieren oder biometrische Profile zu erstellen, erklärte Serve gegenüber AP News. Die Kameras und Sensoren dienten vielmehr dazu, damit die Roboter sicher auf Gehwegen navigieren könnten.
Ähnlich argumentiert Coco, das ebenfalls versichert, keine biometrischen Daten in Chicago gesammelt zu haben. Und: Die Einhaltung von Datenschutzgesetzen habe für das Unternehmen „oberste Priorität“.

articles.title: Google’s Genie 4 world model adds audio, more realistic worlds, and real-time steering | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google DeepMind released its newest world model, Genie 4, in research preview on Tuesday. The latest model generates the most photorealistic and interactive worlds yet, allowing users to type prompts mid-simulation to change the scene. The model also generates real-time audio that matches the simulated world, including music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue.
The release of Genie 4 comes a couple of months after AI video startup Runway released its second world model, GWM Worlds 2, a playable model that responds dynamically to user inputs and includes audio generation. At the same time, the world model industry is beginning to consolidate. Fei-Fei Li’s World Labs is being acquired by AMD, Amazon is in talks to buy Decart, and Rivian just acquired Third Dimension to bring simulation capabilities in-house for self-driving testing.
Genie 4 is Google’s latest move to stay ahead in the crowded field.
Google released its predecessor, Genie 3, as a research preview a little over a year ago. Aside from being far more photorealistic and featuring audio, Genie 4 allows for free-form edits, like changing the weather or camera angle in real time or adding new people or objects. It can maintain a consistent scene for up to two minutes, double its predecessor’s limit, and offers better physics and more humanlike characters.
Gemini, Google’s AI model, is also more closely integrated with Genie 4, acting as the director that plans steps and checks frames while Genie creates the visuals. In a research experiment tied to Gemini Robotics, a Gemini 4 Argon model broke down tasks into steps that Genie 4 simulated in real time. The experiment shows a possible way to test robot scenarios in simulation before they happen in the real world.
“What we’ll increasingly see in the future are these hybrid world models, where you have a combination of Gemini writing code and text, and Genie ingesting that in real time and simulating reality at different levels of abstraction,” Tejas Kulkarni, research director at Google, said during a briefing.
As with other world models, the pitched commercial use cases include gaming, interactive learning, and robotics. One speculative example of interactive learning would be entering a painting of a historical scene and chatting to the painting’s subjects about the event portrayed.
But “trusted testers” — the people who get first access to Google’s cutting-edge products — are pointing to a possible new use: prototyping films.
“The real time aspect becomes most valuable in the areas where keeping a state of flow in the creativity space becomes incredibly useful,” Diego Rivas, a Google DeepMind engineer, said during a press briefing. “For example, in the ideation phase, in the storyboarding phase — anytime you’re kind of in need of rapid ideation.”
Google also offers Veo, its AI video-generation model that makes high-definition clips with built-in synchronized audio from text, image, or video prompts — a tool that has been growing in popularity among filmmakers.
Rivas added that users could, eventually, rely on Gemini Omni, a multimodal large language model that can generate video from images, audio, and text, to turn those prototypes into creative assets. Though those capabilities, he says, are still a ways off.
Throughout the briefing, Rivas stressed that it’s still early days for Genie 4 and that it’s not yet clear what the end-to-end product experience will be. The team also acknowledged that Genie 4 still has gaps: Details and objects can drift the longer a simulation runs, and they still haven’t quite figured out how to ensure the audio will be accurate and any in-world text will be legible.
Genie 4 is available now as a research preview for trusted testers. In the coming weeks, the model will roll out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie, Google’s AI tool for generating interactive worlds from text or image prompts, and early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

articles.title: El iMac se renueva con chip M6, pero aún no trae lo que más piden los usuarios
articles.text:
Siguiendo con su semana de lanzamientos, Apple acaba de presentar el nuevo iMac M6. El todo en uno recibe su primera renovación en dos años, adoptando el chip más reciente de la familia Apple Silicon y manteniendo los elementos principales que lo hacen más atractivo. Aunque también continúa omitiendo la característica que más piden los usuarios: una pantalla OLED.
El iMac M6 se beneficia de las optimizaciones que trae el citado componente, que ya hemos visto implementado en el Mac mini. Puntualmente, las mejoras de rendimiento destacan en tareas vinculadas con la inteligencia artificial generativa, como la ejecución de modelos locales y la programación.
El iMac con chip M6 no será la primera elección de quienes deseen someter a su ordenador a cargas de trabajo de IA muy exigentes. Sin embargo, esa potencia del hardware sirve también para otras labores creativas que sí se adaptan mejor a este ordenador, como la edición de fotos, vídeos, audio y muchas más.
Es importante mencionar que el iMac con M6 se puede configurar en dos versiones: una con dos y otra con cuatro puertos Thunderbolt. La primera cuenta con una CPU y una GPU de 10 núcleos cada una, mientras que la segunda introduce 12 núcleos de procesamiento y 12 núcleos gráficos. En ambas opciones se incluye un doble Neural Engine de 16 núcleos.
Así es el nuevo iMac con chip M6
Si nos enfocamos en memoria y almacenamiento, el iMac M6 se inicia en 16 GB de RAM, aunque también se puede configurar con 24 o 32 GB. En cuanto al espacio interno, se puede elegir entre 256 GB, 512 GB, 1 TB y 2 TB. Vale aclarar que algunas configuraciones están atadas al modelo con M6 más avanzado. Así, por solo citar un ejemplo, si quieres la capacidad de almacenamiento más amplia tienes que elegir el modelo con más memoria unificado.
Apple también ofrece la opción de configurar el nuevo iMac con vidrio nanotexturizado en la pantalla, aunque esto también está disponible únicamente en la variante con M6 de CPU y GPU de 12 núcleos.
El apartado de conectividad es otro en el que el iMac M6 introduce mejoras, gracias a la adopción del chip N1 desarrollado por los de la manzana. El todo en uno ahora soporta WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6 y Thread. En tanto que las conexiones de red cableadas también dan un salto de calidad gracias al puerto Ethernet de 2,5 Gbps.
Es importante mencionar que el puerto Ethernet llega por defecto en el iMac M6 con CPU y GPU de 12 núcleos. En la versión con procesador y gráfica de 10 núcleos es opcional, de modo que, si lo quieres, tienes que añadirlo manualmente en el configurador y pagar 30 euros adicionales por él; de lo contrario, solo puede conectarse a Internet vía WiFi.
Excelentes noticias sobre su precio
A diferencia de lo que ha ocurrido con otros productos de Apple, incluyendo los nuevos iPad mini y MacBook Pro M6, el iMac no sube de precio. De modo que puedes conseguir los nuevos modelos pagando lo mismo que costaban hasta hoy las variantes con M4 que debutaron un par de años atrás.
Así las cosas, el iMac con chip M6 con dos puertos Thunderbolt, CPU de 10 núcleos y GPU de 10 núcleos continúa iniciando en 1.819 euros. En tanto que el precio inicial del modelo con cuatro puertos Thunderbolt, CPU de 12 núcleos y GPU de 12 núcleos se mantiene en 2.019 euros. Los colores disponibles son los mismos de la versión anterior: azul, púrpura, rosa, naranja, amarillo, verde y plata.
Al igual que con el MacBook Pro M6 que se ha presentado hoy, el renovado iMac se podrá reservar en la web oficial de Apple a partir de mañana, miércoles 28 de octubre. Las entregas se pondrán en marcha el próximo 6 de noviembre.

articles.title: How Venn helped Dominion Dynamics scale its finance operations | BetaKit
articles.text:
Long before Dominion Dynamics closed its $139-million Series A round this summer, it faced a more basic financial problem.
The Ottawa-based startup was growing fast and quickly becoming a major player in Canadian defence technology. But its legacy bank was holding it back. Supplier transactions couldn’t be processed, and payments were delayed. For a company in hypergrowth, a single missed payment could stall manufacturing.
“Sovereignty is a huge part of our focus, and the fact that Venn is Canadian made it a very easy choice.”
Mitch Carkner, Dominion
“[It was] very siloed, difficult from an onboarding perspective. Payments and cards were a very difficult thing, and in 2026 they shouldn’t be,” said Mitch Carkner, Dominion’s Chief Operating Officer.
The final straw came when the bank de-platformed Dominion altogether, leaving the company in urgent need of a new financial provider.
That’s when a friend pointed Carkner to Venn, the Toronto-based FinTech that lets businesses move money, manage team spending, and sync transactions with their accounting software—all from one platform.
Carkner signed up and within an hour received a call from Venn co-founder and co-CEO Saud Aziz. He walked through the challenges Dominion had faced, and the company was onboarded that same day.
“We use Venn for payments and individual cards. On Mondays, our finance team gets together, we look at all our payments, check invoices, and then execute on the platform,” said Carkner.
Built for companies scaling fast
Dominion’s experience illustrates the problem Venn set out to solve. Its founders, Aziz and Ahmed Shafik, saw Canadian startups and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) as being underserved by traditional banks.
For companies trying to scale quickly, new employees need to hit the ground running on day one, suppliers need to be paid on time, and finance teams need to be able to see where all the money is going. Handling those tasks across separate systems only adds to the workload as the business expands.
A simpler way to manage spending
For Carkner, Venn’s appeal is in its simplicity and the ease of its systems and automations. Dominion now pays suppliers on time and manages employee purchases through individual cards, earning one percent cashback on its spending. Both run through the same platform, replacing the separate systems that made its earlier setup difficult.
As Dominion adds suppliers, Venn offers ACH/EFT payments, wire transfers, and Interac e-transfers, alongside global transfers to more than 180 countries. Businesses can schedule recurring bills automatically, reducing the work of handling regular payments as their vendor lists expand.
And, as new people join the team, Dominion can issue them a virtual card through Venn right away, so they can buy what they need to get to work without waiting for a physical card. Managers set spending limits and decide which purchases need approval, while finance can see who’s spending what in real time.
Venn Intelligence, the platform’s built-in AI tools, reads uploaded receipts and matches them to transactions. It uses the company’s accounting history to suggest expense categories and proposes rules to automate recurring patterns. Finance teams can then review those suggestions and send categorized transactions and matched receipts to QuickBooks, reducing the manual data entry necessary. Venn says businesses using the tools save around 10 hours a month on accounting work.
Dominion has used Venn since pre-seed, through its $21-million seed round and recent $139-million Series A. Carkner expects the platform to continue supporting the company as its workforce and supplier network expands.
Sovereignty first
At Dominion, Carkner points to the simplicity of the platform and its automations as benefits for the team. The company manages supplier payments and individual employee cards together and earns one percent cashback on its spending.
They’ve used Venn since pre-seed, through a $21-million seed round and their $139-million Series A round in June. Carkner expects that relationship to continue as Dominion grows. Alongside those practical benefits, he said Venn’s Canadian roots sealed the deal when Dominion was looking for a new financial partner.
“Dominion is building a Canadian company for our military,” he said. “Sovereignty is a huge part of our focus, and the fact that Venn is Canadian made it a very easy choice for our capital and our payment solution.”
