articles.title: 3 Ways to Boost MoE Inference on NVIDIA DGX Spark | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
Generating tokens faster starts with identifying what limits inference performance. In the batch-size-1 evaluation of Ling-3.0-flash from Inclusion AI on NVIDIA DGX Spark, profiling showed that decoding was memory-bound: reading model weights drove execution time. Two operations stood out—the mixture-of-experts (MoE) computation and the output-layer projection that produces scores across the model’s vocabulary.
Those findings pointed to two ways to improve performance: reduce the weight traffic in each decode step and generate more tokens per verification round. This post examines three techniques that address those costs:
- Humming MXFP4 MoE kernels to improve execution of the routed-expert computation.
- Online FP8 quantization of the output layer, or LM head, to reduce its weight-read volume.
- Multi-token prediction (MTP) speculative decoding with NEXTN to draft and verify multiple tokens together.
This post explains how each optimization works, measures its effect, and examines an integration issue that can make the combined configuration slower than the baseline. Ling-3.0-flash serves as the implementation example, with code and deployment instructions in the Ling cookbook.
Model and baseline configuration
The evaluation used Ling-3.0-flash-fp4, a mixture-of-experts model with 124 billion total parameters and 5.1 billion active parameters per token. The model has 42 layers: 35 Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) linear-attention layers and seven multi-head latent attention (MLA) layers. Each MoE layer routes each token to eight of 512 routed experts, alongside one shared expert.
For agentic workflows, Ling-3.0-flash provides a native 256K-token context window, expandable to 1M tokens. Compared with the previous Ling flash model, it improves long-horizon task stability, tool-calling accuracy, and harness compatibility. Developers can enable reasoning for complex agent tasks or disable it for latency-sensitive interactions. Improved spatial understanding supports constructing physical-scene grids and reasoning about relative positions in coding tasks.
The baseline followed the official cookbook’s W4A8 configuration: FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE kernels, NVIDIA CUTLASS dense GEMM, and the –enable-fp32-lm-head option. The LM head projects a hidden dimension of 2,560 to a vocabulary of 157,184 tokens.
For standard MXFP4 deployment instructions, follow the MXFP4 deployment notebook.
Optimization 1: Humming MXFP4 MoE backend
The first optimization replaces the flashinfer_mxfp4 MoE execution backend with humming. Humming is an independent kernel library available through the humming-kernels pip package.
Unlike the FlashInfer CUTLASS path, Humming uses NVIDIA CUDA Runtime Compilation (NVRTC) to generate and compile CUBINs at runtime for the actual M/N/K dimensions, data types, and GPU architecture. It caches compiled binaries in ~/.humming/cache. This specializes kernels for Ling-3.0-flash shapes, including its relatively narrow moe_intermediate_size of 768. It also compiles at a finer granularity: an individual kernel completes in seconds, whereas the FlashInfer CUTLASS path uses ninja to compile 97 targets and takes on the order of tens of minutes. Performance is reported as time per output token (TPOT) and decode throughput in tokens per second.
| Configuration | TPOT | Decode throughput | Relative to baseline | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 27.71 ms | 36.09 tok/s | — | 
| + Humming MoE backend | 25.35 ms | 39.45 tok/s | +9.3% | 
Optimization 2: Online FP8 LM head quantization
In the checkpoint, the LM head is stored in BF16 and listed in modules_to_not_convert, so it is not quantized during loading. Its vocabulary GEMM is 157,184 × 2,560, and the entire weight block must be read for each generated token. Under a bandwidth bottleneck, it is therefore a high-value target for compression.
The optimization applies a dynamic FP8 quantization configuration only when constructing the LM head. The rest of the model continues to load with the checkpoint’s FP8/MXFP4 configuration. Moving the LM-head weights from BF16 to FP8 halves the read volume for this layer. The configuration is enabled with SGLANG_ENABLE_FP8_LM_HEAD=1.
This setting is mutually exclusive with the baseline –enable-fp32-lm-head option, which outputs logits in FP32 and uses a slower vocabulary-GEMM path.
| Configuration | TPOT | Decode throughput | Relative to baseline | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 27.71 ms | 36.09 tok/s | — | 
| + Humming MoE backend | 25.35 ms | 39.45 tok/s | +9.3% | 
| + Online FP8 LM head | 22.76 ms | 43.94 tok/s | +21.7% | 
Optimization 3: MTP speculative decoding with NEXTN
The first two optimizations reduce the cost of each decode step. Speculative decoding follows a different path: it reduces the number of decode steps.
Ling-3.0-flash includes a NEXTN prediction layer (num_nextn_predict_layers: 1), which can be used directly as a draft model without additional training or downloads. The configuration uses three draft steps and a four-token verification window. In each round, the draft predicts three tokens in sequence, and the target verifies four positions at once, accepting the correct prefix.
The benefit depends on two quantities: accept length, the average number of accepted tokens per round, and the verification-cost ratio, the cost of one verification step relative to a normal decode step. The measured ratio was approximately 2.26. The principal source of verification cost was not attention computation; at batch size 1, KV reads were small relative to weight reads. Instead, the cost came from MoE expert activation: a normal decode activates eight experts for one token, while verification processes four tokens and can activate up to 32 experts.
Note:
When online FP8 LM-head quantization and MTP are enabled together, the draft model must share the entire LM-head module with the target, rather than only its weight tensor. The original Ling NEXTN implementation didn’t expose this interface. Without it, the framework silently falls back: the draft receives FP8 weights but interprets them as BF16, accept length drops to 1.00, and throughput becomes lower than a configuration with no optimizations. Sharing the full LM-head module through this interface restores normal token acceptance. Follow the Ling cookbook to enable FP8 LM-head quantization and MTP together.
| Configuration | TPOT | Decode throughput | Relative to baseline | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 27.71 ms | 36.09 tok/s | — | 
| + Humming MoE backend | 25.35 ms | 39.45 tok/s | +9.3% | 
| + Online FP8 LM head | 22.76 ms | 43.94 tok/s | +21.7% | 
| + MTP (NEXTN, steps=3 / topk=1 / draft_tokens=4) | 9.72 ms | 102.88 tok/s | +185.1% | 
End-to-end results on GSM8K
The component-level results above use a synthetic 32K-input/2K-output workload. Synthetic workloads help isolate individual gains, but their repetitive outputs and simple sampling systematically overestimate speculative-decoding benefits. The evaluation also included a strict end-to-end comparison across all 1,319 GSM8K questions.
The evaluation used five-shot prompting, with demonstrations from the training set and the complete test set for evaluation, temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 29, max_tokens 32,768, and chain-of-thought enabled. Apart from the three optimizations, both evaluations aligned all variables: sampling parameters, parser, five-shot protocol, random seed, and memory allocation. Time to first token (TTFT) measures the delay before the first output token.
| Metric | Baseline | All three optimizations | Difference | 
|---|---|---|---|
| MoE backend | flashinfer_mxfp4 | humming |  | 
| LM head | FP32 | Online FP8 |  | 
| Speculative decoding | None | MTP3 |  | 
| TPOT | 26.45 ms | 18.56 ms | −29.8% | 
| Decode throughput | 37.81 tok/s | 53.89 tok/s | +42.5% | 
| GSM8K accuracy | 96.89% | 96.82% | −0.08 pt | 
| MTP accept length | — | 2.68 |  | 
| Mean latency | 15.21 s | 11.49 s | −24.5% | 
| Latency P50 / P95 | 8.36 / 50.20 s | 6.11 / 38.60 s | −27% / −23% | 
| Mean TTFT | 0.207 s | 0.214 s |  | 
| Request errors / truncations | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |  | 
Why synthetic and real workloads differ
- Synthetic outputs are more repetitive, making draft predictions easier to accept. Accept length was 3.90 for the synthetic workload, compared with 2.68 for GSM8K.
- Sampling parameters differ. The synthetic test used greedy decoding, while the real evaluation used temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, and top_k=29.
- Output-length distributions differ. The synthetic workload fixes output at 2K tokens, while the GSM8K median output is approximately 310 tokens. This spreads the fixed overhead reductions from the first two optimizations over a shorter output.
When evaluating these optimizations on DGX Spark, use a workload that reflects your intended deployment. The 185.1% throughput gain measured in the synthetic test does not establish the gain for other workloads.
Conclusion
Across the full GSM8K evaluation, the three optimizations increased decode throughput by 42.5%, reduced mean end-to-end latency by 24.5%, and produced no statistically detectable accuracy change. Their mechanisms do not overlap: Humming and the FP8 LM head reduce the cost of each step, while MTP reduces the number of steps, so the techniques can be combined.
Stacking, however, is not automatic. Each optimization worked independently, but enabling all three required the draft model to share the full LM-head module. Otherwise, the system silently degrades to a configuration slower than the unoptimized baseline. During deployment, validate that every optimization is active at startup; this is more reliable than inferring configuration state from later performance numbers.

articles.title: CISA Warns of Node2Shell Exploitation as Honeypots Log Attack Attempts
articles.text:
The US cybersecurity agency CISA has added the Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. Separately, two security firms say they have recorded exploitation attempts against their honeypots.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497 and also known as HTTP2Shell and Broccoli2Shell, the flaw is an out-of-bounds write in the decoder of Brotli, the data compression library developed by Google.
It impacts Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. With specially crafted compressed data, an attacker could crash the application, expose the contents of its memory, and potentially execute arbitrary code.
The bug was reported by researchers at OpenAI, and Node.js and Google released fixes on October 21. Microsoft, the maintainers of two Python packages, Bun, Envoy and Istio have also released fixes, and Palo Alto Networks is rolling out hotfixes for PAN-OS.
Imperva has demonstrated that the vulnerability can be exploited for code execution on an official Node.js image.
CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to the KEV catalog on October 27, but provided no information on the attacks. Federal civilian agencies have been instructed to address the flaw by November 10.
Previdian, which monitors exploitation activity through its own network of sensors, says it recorded one exploitation attempt targeting CVE-2026-111497 on October 27, coming from a US-based IP address. The company rates its confidence in the exploitation as ‘confirmed’.
“Confidence is how strongly the evidence supports treating this as exploitation of this vulnerability. It does not mean the attempt succeeded,” Previdian explains.
ELLIO, a cybersecurity lab that monitors reconnaissance and mass exploitation activity, says its sensors caught a malicious request targeting Node.js 24.22.0 running on x86-64 systems on October 26. The previous day, a publicly available tool had sent Brotli-compressed data to its sensors to determine which hosts process such data.
The exploitation attempt came from an IP address that ELLIO previously saw targeting the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities and probing Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet VPN devices. “This is indicative of the RCE being adopted by an operator focused on mass exploitation,” ELLIO said.
According to ELLIO’s analysis, however, the exploit used in the attack was broken. Its delivery components matched public proof-of-concept code, but the final stage, which the attacker wrote themselves, did not result in a shell in any of the 50 tests ELLIO ran against a vulnerable Node.js instance.
“This was likely a first-generation attempt fired in the wild before the operator fully tested the final stage against a live target – a working framework with a defective last 12 instructions,” ELLIO noted.
The company has itself achieved code execution against four different setups running an official Node.js build on x86-64. It also warns that failed exploitation attempts can crash the targeted process, which means they can be used in denial-of-service (DoS) attacks.
VMware patches pending
Broadcom warned on October 27 that SDDC Manager in VMware Cloud Foundation and vSphere Foundation is affected by CVE-2026-111497 because it uses Node.js.
The company rates the issue critical, with a CVSS score of 9.8, for SDDC Manager 9.1.1. For versions 9.0.x, 9.1.0 and 5.2.x, it rates the bug important, with a CVSS score of 7.5.
“A malicious actor with network access to SDDC Manager may exploit this issue to execute arbitrary code,” Broadcom said.
Patches are pending for all affected versions, and Broadcom has published workarounds in two knowledge base articles. Its advisory does not mention exploitation in the wild.

Related: This is Fine: What NetScaler Zero-Days Tell Us About the New Normal

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.text:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Their findings, published in Nature Physics, demonstrate how this combination could help scientists investigate fundamental interactions between matter and fields that are increasingly difficult to simulate using conventional computers.
A Strange Quantum Effect Predicted in 1959
In everyday physics, a charged particle responds to the electric and magnetic fields it encounters. Quantum mechanics, however, reveals that particles can behave in ways that have no straightforward counterpart in our ordinary experience.
In 1959, physicists Yakir Aharonov and David Bohm predicted that a charged particle could be affected by magnetic flux even if it traveled entirely outside the region containing the magnetic field. Rather than experiencing a conventional magnetic force along its path, the particle would undergo a change in its quantum phase.
Quantum phase describes an aspect of a particle's wave behavior that influences how different possible paths interfere with one another. Although the phase itself is not directly visible, differences in phase can produce measurable effects.
The prediction became known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect and was eventually verified in experiments involving real electrons. It remains one of the clearest demonstrations that the quantum world operates according to rules that go beyond the familiar laws of classical physics.
Researchers are now exploring how this phenomenon behaves in more complex theoretical systems known as lattice gauge theories.
These theories describe how matter interacts with fields associated with fundamental forces. They represent space as a grid, with matter located at individual points and fields associated with the connections between them. Such models are particularly important in particle physics and high-energy physics, where scientists study the basic particles and interactions that make up the universe.
The challenge is that the mathematics becomes extraordinarily demanding as these systems grow more complicated. Even powerful conventional computers can struggle to calculate how all the interacting components evolve.
Quantum computers offer a different approach. Instead of attempting to calculate every aspect of a quantum system using classical computing methods, scientists can construct another quantum system that follows the same underlying rules. They can then observe its behavior directly, an approach known as quantum simulation.
How Scientists Built the Quantum Experiment
The Oxford project began in 2022, when lead author Dr. Sebastian Saner, Dr. Oana Bazavan, and their colleagues started developing a way to simulate lattice gauge theories using a hybrid quantum system. They collaborated with Dr. Alejandro Bermudez of the Instituto de Física Teórica in Madrid.
Their experimental design relied on two different quantum components that performed separate functions.
The first consisted of qubits encoded in the internal states of trapped ions, which are electrically charged atoms held in place using electromagnetic fields. These qubits represented the gauge fields in the theoretical model.
The second component used quantum oscillators, created by the vibrations of those same trapped ions. These oscillators represented matter.
By combining the two, the researchers constructed a simple loop that served as a basic building block of a lattice gauge theory. Two oscillators represented matter at two different locations, while two qubits represented the fields connecting those locations.
Although the arrangement was small, it was sufficient to reproduce an important interaction between matter and magnetic flux.
Quantum Entanglement Creates a Surprising Solution
The researchers next placed the two qubits into an entangled quantum state. Entanglement is a phenomenon in which quantum systems become linked in ways that cannot be fully explained by classical physics.
Within the team's simulated lattice gauge theory, this entangled state represented magnetic flux passing through the center of the loop.
Initially, the researchers had planned to introduce the magnetic flux as a fixed background condition. However, creating the necessary interaction would have required capabilities that their quantum hardware did not possess.
Encoding the flux directly into the qubits provided a practical alternative. More importantly, it allowed the magnetic flux to become part of the evolving quantum system rather than remaining an unchanging external influence.
"For us, the exciting step was to encode the magnetic flux in a gauge field that was itself dynamical," says Dr. Saner. "Rather than having matter evolve in a fixed background, the matter and gauge field become part of the same quantum dynamics."
What began as a technical workaround ultimately enabled the researchers to explore a more interesting version of the phenomenon, one in which matter and the field could participate together in the quantum dynamics.
A Quantum Effect That Stops Particle Motion
With their simulated loop in place, the scientists examined how a matter particle moved between locations through a process known as quantum tunneling.
Quantum tunneling allows particles to move between states in ways that would not be possible under ordinary classical rules.
When the researchers ran their simulation without magnetic flux, the particle could tunnel freely around the loop.
Introducing the simulated flux produced a strikingly different result.
The particle had two possible paths around the loop, but the magnetic flux changed their relative quantum phases. As a result, the two paths interfered destructively, meaning their quantum contributions canceled each other out.
This interference completely suppressed the tunneling, leaving the simulated particle frozen in its original state.
The outcome demonstrated the Aharonov-Bohm effect within a lattice gauge theory containing a dynamical field. Rather than simply reproducing the familiar behavior of a particle moving around a fixed magnetic influence, the experiment showed how the phenomenon can emerge when matter and the field are both represented by interacting quantum components.
A New Tool for Exploring Fundamental Physics
The Oxford findings were published alongside a related study by researchers at the University of Maryland, led by Professor Norbert Linke.
The Maryland team also used a hybrid quantum system, but their experiment focused on simulating the Yukawa potential, a mathematical description of an interaction relevant to nuclear and particle physics.
Although the two research groups developed their methods independently, they later coordinated the submission of their studies to Nature Physics.
Together, the experiments demonstrate how hybrid quantum computers could become valuable tools for investigating fundamental interactions that are difficult to reproduce using classical simulations.
By combining different types of quantum components, researchers can build systems in which matter and fields are represented in ways that more closely reflect the physics they want to study.
The Oxford experiment provides an example of that potential. A phenomenon first predicted in 1959 and later observed with electrons has now been recreated in a quantum simulator where the field itself participates in the dynamics, offering scientists another way to explore the unusual rules governing the quantum world.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Oxford. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal References:
- S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, C. J. Ballance, R. Srinivas, D. M. Lucas, A. Bermúdez. Aharonov–Bohm interference in a $${\\pmb{\\mathbb{Z}}}_{\\bf{2}}$$ lattice gauge theory on a hybrid qubit–oscillator quantum computer. Nature Physics, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41567-026-03400-6
- Anton T. Than, Saurabh V. Kadam, Vinay Vikramaditya, Nhung H. Nguyen, Xingxin Liu, Zohreh Davoudi, Alaina M. Green, Norbert M. Linke. Quantum field theory dynamics on a spin–phonon quantum computer. Nature Physics, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41567-026-03402-4

articles.title: CISA confirms PHP2Shell vulnerabilities now exploited in attacks
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added two critical PHP vulnerabilities collectively tracked as PHP2Shell to its catalog of actively exploited security flaws.
Threat actors without privileges can exploit the two security issues (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) in high-complexity attacks to gain remote code execution (RCE) on unpatched systems.
The PHP security team patched the two flaws on Wednesday, October 21, one day after urging security teams to install the security updates as soon as they became available.
Although details on the PHP2Shell security flaws (including the CVE IDs and mitigation measures shared with critical infrastructure providers) leaked and some proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits were published online before patches went live, the PHP security team said that none were functional.
Multiple cybersecurity firms (including Cloudflare, Amazon, Hadrian, watchTowr, Previdian, and Patchstack) also detected widespread exploitation attempts before public disclosure, but they all tagged them as unsuccessful.
Amazon Threat Intelligence security researchers also said that attackers began targeting the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities four days before security patches were released.
Federal agencies ordered to patch by Thursday
CISA added the vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog on Monday and ordered Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their systems by Thursday, as mandated by Binding Operational Directive 26-04.
"These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise," the cybersecurity agency warned.
"While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities."
While CISA has not yet shared further details about ongoing PHP2Shell attacks, Perplexity detection and response lead Adel Karimi first confirmed in-the-wild exploitation over the weekend after their honeypots recorded evidence of remote code execution against an Apache mod_php installation running PHP 8.4.26.
On Friday, the PHP security team also shared mitigation for a new RCE flaw (CVE-2026-115560) with no patch, exploitable when targeting systems "with an unusual combination of configuration and application code."
PHP powers roughly 70% of all websites, with more than 5.1 million PHP hosts exposed online and around 3.8 million instances with at least one port open to attacks, according to VirusTotal estimates.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: OpenAI lanzó GPT-6.1 Terra, un modelo de IA que usa la computadora y cuesta la mitad
articles.text:
OpenAI lanzó el 26 de octubre GPT-6.1 Terra, un modelo de inteligencia artificial de gama media pensado para trabajo de oficina en la computadora. Sus precios para desarrolladores son un 50% menores que los de GPT-5.6 Terra, su antecesor, y los de GPT-6.1 Sol, un modelo superior de la misma empresa.
Según el anuncio de la compañía, Terra combina razonamiento visual, uso preciso de la computadora y una redacción más natural. Entre las tareas que menciona están redactar propuestas, interpretar planos técnicos, completar formularios y editar videos.
Ya está disponible para los usuarios de los planes Plus, Pro, Enterprise y Edu en ChatGPT Work y en Codex, la herramienta de programación de OpenAI. Los desarrolladores pueden usarlo en la API (la conexión para integrarlo en otras aplicaciones) con el nombre gpt-6.1-terra. El anuncio no menciona el plan gratuito.
USD 1 por millón de unidades de texto de entrada
El precio estándar es de USD 1 por millón de tokens de entrada y USD 5 por millón de salida, según la documentación oficial. Los tokens son las unidades de texto que procesa y cobra un modelo. La firma Artificial Analysis, que mide modelos de IA, informó que GPT-5.6 Terra costaba USD 2 y USD 12, respectivamente.
El modelo acepta texto e imágenes, y responde solo con texto. Tiene una ventana de contexto de 1.050.000 tokens, es decir, la cantidad de información que puede manejar en una sola consulta, y su conocimiento llega hasta el 1 de junio de 2026.
En las pruebas comparativas que publica OpenAI, con esfuerzo de razonamiento medio, Terra obtiene 15 puntos porcentuales más que GPT-5.6 Terra en Agents’ Last Exam, un examen de tareas profesionales, a cerca de un tercio del costo. La empresa afirma que iguala a GPT-6 Astra, su modelo más capaz, con una décima parte del precio por token.
En programación, el modelo resolvió el 50,3% de las tareas de Terminal-Bench 4.0 con el máximo esfuerzo, frente al 21,5% de GPT-5.6 Terra. OpenAI recomienda GPT-6.1 Sol o GPT-6 Astra para los trabajos de programación más complejos.
Cifras que provienen de la propia empresa
OpenAI también comparó el modelo con Claude Opus 5.5, de Anthropic. Con el máximo esfuerzo, dice, Terra es más de tres veces más eficiente en tokens y cobra una cuarta parte por token, lo que supone un costo por tarea unas nueve veces menor.
En una prueba interna con preguntas diseñadas para provocar errores, la tasa de fallos factuales bajó de 53,6% a 16,7% con esfuerzo bajo, y a 4,3% con el máximo. Esas cifras son de la empresa y ningún tercero las confirmó, señalaron Decrypt y Quartz.
Artificial Analysis sí midió el modelo por su cuenta: con el máximo esfuerzo, Terra suma 6 puntos más que GPT-5.6 Terra en su índice de inteligencia, con un costo por tarea de USD 0,40 frente a USD 1,40. En su índice de programación con agentes, que son asistentes de IA que ejecutan tareas por su cuenta, obtuvo 48 puntos, seis menos que GPT-6.1 Sol.
El analista Simon Willison comparó a Terra con Sonnet, el modelo intermedio de Anthropic, y señaló que una opción más barata sirve para tareas repetitivas y automatizadas. Ted Sanders, empleado de OpenAI, escribió en Hacker News que para los suscriptores no es una gran novedad: si alcanzan los límites de uso, les puede rendir un poco más.
Para los planes de ChatGPT, OpenAI indica que la misma cuota de uso cubre más tareas con Terra que con GPT-5.6 Terra, y bastantes más que con Sol o Astra. El anuncio no precisa cuántas más.

articles.title: Firefox roadmap: What's new and what's coming next | The Mozilla Blog
articles.text:
Five Firefox updates you might have missed, and a look ahead
Some of our latest Firefox updates have had big moments of their own, from the launch of our new design and built-in ad blocking on iOS to Firefox Enterprise and our partnership with NVIDIA GeForce NOW. You might’ve even spotted a few familiar internet OGs in our latest campaign. Other improvements might’ve flown under the radar until you open a PDF or move your tabs around.
We wanted to take a moment to highlight some of the features and improvements we’ve been working on, from recent additions you might have missed to a look at what’s coming next.
What’s new in Firefox
- Open PDFs faster. Firefox’s built-in PDF viewer now starts up to 45% faster on desktop, so there’s less waiting when you open a document in your browser.
- Put your Android tabs where you want them. Prefer your tabs at the bottom of the screen? You now have the option to move Firefox’s tab bar there. Go to Settings > Customize to choose.
- Find your spot in a video faster. We’ve made it quicker to jump to a different point in a video on desktop, whether you’re skipping ahead in a tutorial or going back to catch something you missed.
- Keep your favorite wallpapers handy. Firefox now saves a collection of your custom wallpapers under “Your images” on New Tab on desktop, so you can switch between favorites without uploading them again.
- Save time filling out forms and keeping up with page changes. Smart Window can now help fill out online forms using information from your chosen tabs, so you don’t have to copy details back and forth. You can also ask it to watch a page and notify you when something changes, like a price drop or a new job listing, saving you from manually checking for updates. Both capabilities are available in English in the U.S. and Canada as part of the Smart Window beta. Learn more about the new features here.
What’s next on the Firefox roadmap
When we launched our public roadmap in June, we shared plans to make everyday browsing more useful, flexible and private. We’ve now updated it with more of what’s ahead. We’re developing these features in the open, in close partnership with our contributors, and will share more about release timing as each feature gets ready for more people to try.
Here’s a look at what’s in the works:
- Keep what you need in view. We heard your request for a way to keep a page visible while browsing. Mini Window will let you pop a tab, or part of a page, into a small floating window, so recipes or instructions stay in view while you work in another tab.
- Listen to pages. Give your eyes a break. Firefox will soon read articles and other web content aloud on desktop and Android, so you can listen while doing other things – even with your phone’s screen off.
- Take your reading offline. No connection? No problem. Offline mode on Android will let you save articles ahead of time to read or listen to without internet access, perfect for flights and commutes with spotty service.
- Turn speech into text on desktop. We’re bringing speech recognition to Firefox on desktop, so websites that use Firefox’s built-in capability can offer voice input and captions without sending your audio to a server. Those sites receive the text, while your audio stays on your device. After downloading the speech recognition model, transcription will work offline, too.
- Choose how VPN works for each site. Since bringing free built-in VPN to Firefox on desktop and Android (iOS coming soon), we’re now adding the ability to set website rules so you can choose how VPN works on a site-by-site basis.
- Clear browsing data directly from your toolbar. We’re bringing Private Window’s familiar 🔥 button to Classic Window on desktop, so you can quickly choose what browsing data to delete without digging through settings.
Keep shaping Firefox with us
Try the latest updates and explore the Firefox roadmap for more of what we’re working on. If there’s something you’re looking forward to, or something you’d like us to improve, tell us on Mozilla Connect. Your feedback helps shape what comes next.

articles.title: L’application LCL est en panne ce mercredi matin : les signalements se multiplient
articles.text:
Les clients de LCL qui ont tenté de consulter leurs comptes ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026 ont eu une mauvaise surprise.
Depuis le début de la matinée, l’application mobile de la banque rencontre des dysfonctionnements, et de nombreux utilisateurs se plaignent de ne pas pouvoir y accéder normalement.
Une hausse des signalements sur Downdetector
L’ampleur du problème se lit sur Downdetector, où les signalements concernant LCL grimpent depuis ce matin, signe que la panne ne se limite pas à quelques cas isolés et touche un nombre important de clients.
Selon nos observations, l’accès aux comptes via l’application et via le site web est concerné.
Pour l’heure, LCL ne s’est pas exprimée sur l’origine de l’incident ni sur le délai nécessaire pour rétablir le service. Rien à signaler en revanche du côté du Crédit Agricole, qui appartient pourtant au même groupe.

articles.title: French VC Aquiti closes €60 million fund for founders outside of traditional venture hubs | EU-Startups
articles.text:
French VC Aquiti announces the final close of their AVA1 fund at nearly €60 million in order to back founders building across the Greater Southwest of France from pre-Seed onwards.
Through its AVA1 fund, Aquiti invests at pre-Seed and Seed, with initial investments ranging from €100k to €3 million and substantial reserves for follow-on rounds. They intend to build a portfolio of 25 to 30 companies.
“Founders should not have to choose between building where they want to live and accessing the capital, network and ambition they need to go far. With AVA1, our goal is simple: be the first partner for the best founders in the Greater Southwest, and stay alongside them as they scale,” says Jean-François Cochy, General Partner at Aquiti and Head of AVA1.
Aquiti’s AVA1 final close comes amid a series of European early-stage venture fund announcements in 2026.
In France, Paris-based Newfund closed its €60 million HEKA fund to support BrainTech startups, while 360 Capital announced an €85 million close for its Poli360 2 DeepTech fund and Elaia closed its third DeepTech Seed fund at €134 million.
Elsewhere, Germany’s Vanagon Ventures completed a €20 million pre-Seed fund, while Lithuania’s FIRSTPICK launched a €25 million vehicle focused on Baltic founders. Together, these fund announcements represent €324 million in disclosed fund capital, rising to nearly €384 million including AVA1.
Aquiti’s regional approach also builds on earlier investment activity, with EU-Startups previously identifying the firm among the backers of Bordeaux-based TreeFrog Therapeutics and CardNexus.
“We chose Aquiti because the relationship went far beyond capital. From our first discussions, we found a team that combines a genuinely close human relationship with experience in investing and supporting tech companies as they scale. Most importantly, we share the same level of ambition: to make RelaiSanté a category-defining company and transform the way patients access care and support after hospitalisation,” adds Étienne Boix, co-founder and CEO of portfolio company RelaiSanté.
Aquiti Gestion is a French private equity firm that has been supporting businesses across Southwestern France for over 25 years, managing over €230 million in assets across regional SMEs and corporate buyouts. To expand into the fast-growing startup ecosystem, the firm launched a dedicated, modern venture capital arm in 2018, known simply as Aquiti or Aquiti Ventures.
This specialised, five-investor venture team focuses strictly on pre-Seed and Seed-stage investments in breakthrough technology, healthcare, and climate startups, pairing the institutional stability of a 25-year-old asset manager with the agile, tech-focused mindset of a fund founded in 2018.
Aquiti has built a team of five investors and backed 13 companies, from AI-powered materials discovery at Synboli to new models of care coordination at RelaiSanté.
They look to work alongside founders to establish the right governance, make key hires, prepare for future funding, and open doors to potential new customers.

articles.title: 100 nanomètres, 700 fois plus fine qu'un cheveu : le rover Perseverance mesure le danger invisible de la poussière martienne
articles.text:
100 nanomètres, 700 fois plus fine qu'un cheveu : le rover Perseverance mesure le danger invisible de la poussière martienne
L'humanité ambitionne de conquérir un jour la planète rouge. Pourtant, un ennemi aussi discret que redoutable se dresse sur le chemin des futurs explorateurs : la poussière martienne. Actuellement sur le terrain, le rover Perseverance fournit à la NASA des données cruciales pour concevoir et protéger les futures combinaisons et les habitats spatiaux.
Marcher sur la planète Mars constitue un défi encore plus colossal pour notre époque que ne le fut la conquête de la Lune à la fin des années 1960. Le challenge s'annonce presque impossible, tant les obstacles techniques et biologiques à surmonter s'avèrent titanesques.
La NASA, titillée par Elon Musk, croit toutefois dur comme fer à ce voyage habité et s'emploie à lever les barrières l'une après l'autre. Après les récentes annonces concernant un démonstrateur de vaisseau à propulsion nucléaire prévu pour 2028, l'agence spatiale étasunienne s'attaque aujourd'hui à un problème très concret : la survie des futurs “marswalkers”. Celles et ceux qui, à leurs risques et périls, fouleront le sol de notre voisine devront en effet affronter une menace littéralement invisible.
Néanmoins, “la NASA a une longue expérience dans la transformation de défis en solutions concrètes, ainsi que dans la recherche de moyens créatifs d’exploiter les données dont elle dispose”, rappelle Lindsay Hays, directrice par intérim de la Division des sciences planétaires au siège de l’agence spatiale à Washington.
L’instrument PIXL à la loupe : des particules martiennes 700 fois plus fines qu'un cheveu
En première ligne depuis février 2021, le rover Perseverance a ausculté, mesuré et analysé la fine, voire ultrafine poussière omniprésente à la surface de Mars, celle-là même qui se soulève lors des gigantesques tempêtes balayant la planète tous les deux ans. L'astromobile embarque ainsi des échantillons de matériaux destinés aux futures combinaisons spatiales afin d'observer comment ce régolithe s'y accroche. L'enjeu est vital : certains grains s'avèrent assez fins pour s'infiltrer jusque dans les poumons et la circulation sanguine des futurs astronautes.
“Le travail principal de Perseverance est de rechercher des signes de vie microbienne ancienne, mais la mission a aussi été conçue pour aider à se préparer aux explorations humaines, détaille Katie Stack Morgan, scientifique rattachée au projet Perseverance au Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Cet effort comprend des démonstrations technologiques comme MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment) et Ingenuity, ainsi que des échantillons de combinaisons spatiales.”
Les relevés approfondis de l'instrument PIXL démontrent que ce régolithe martien est beaucoup plus fin que prévu, se distinguant nettement de la poussière recouvrant le sol gris de la Lune. Si cette roche concassée se révèle globalement moins abrasive sur Mars, Perseverance a identifié deux catégories de particules d'une finesse inouïe, allant de 2,5 micromètres à 100 nanomètres, soit 700 fois moins que l'épaisseur d'un cheveu.
Moutons de poussière et électrostatique : un danger mortel pour les astronautes
Pour Scott Van Bommel, chercheur travaillant sur la mission Perseverance, le problème est de taille : “Les amas plus volumineux, sortes de ‘moutons’ de poussière martienne, finissent par se détacher avec le temps. Mais les particules les plus fines, elles, restent sur place ; ce sont précisément celles qui posent le plus grand défi aux systèmes de soutien à la vie humaine.”
Particulièrement riches en fer, soufre et sulfates de calcium, ces poussières adhèrent farouchement aux surfaces en raison des charges électrostatiques ambiantes. Pour les futurs équipages, inhaler ces particules abrasives ou les introduire accidentellement dans un habitat pressurisé pourrait s'avérer extrêmement toxique.
Plus grave encore d'un point de vue matériel, cette poussière menace d'endommager irrémédiablement les joints d'étanchéité, les visières et les mécanismes délicats des scaphandres spatiaux.
Un marathon sur la planète rouge : Perseverance affole les compteurs
Loin de se contenter de ces analyses statiques, Perseverance trace sa route. En franchissant récemment la barre des 45,22 km parcourus à la surface de Mars — l'équivalent d'un véritable marathon extraterrestre —, l'astromobile vient de battre le record historique de distance établi par Opportunity.
Qu'il s'agisse de dompter la poussière abrasive ou d'enchaîner les kilomètres dans un environnement hostile, chaque nouvelle étape franchie par le rover rend un peu plus tangible la perspective d'une odyssée humaine vers Mars.

articles.title: Vor dem Start von GTA 6: Mit diesen Controller-Ladestationen für die Playstation 5 kannst du nahtlos weiterzocken
articles.text:
Vor dem Start von GTA 6: Warum sich eine Ladestation für deine Dualsense-Controller lohnt
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Nach mehr als einem Jahrzehnt Wartezeit erscheint am 19. November endlich GTA 6. Wer auf der Playstation 5 zockt, darf sich freuen, denn das Game nutzt die adaptiven Trigger und die haptische Vibration exzessiv – etwa beim Fahren über verschiedene Untergründe, bei Schießereien oder bei dynamischen Wettereffekten. Dadurch werden Hardware und Akku des Dualsense-Controllers allerdings stärker beansprucht als bei anderen Spielen. Wenn du in einer Session nahtlos den Controller wechseln möchtest, lohnt es sich, vor dem Release noch in eine Ladestation zu investieren. Hier erfährst du, worauf du beim Kauf achten solltest und mit welchen Kosten du rechnen musst.
Playstation 5: Warum sich eine Controller-Ladestation lohnt
GTA 6 lädt zu extrem langen Sessions ein. Gleichzeitig ist Rockstar Games dafür bekannt, die Grenzen der Technologie komplett auszureizen. Der Controller könnte deshalb deutlich kürzer durchhalten, als du es von anderen Spielen gewohnt bist. Um deinen Dualsense-Controller aufzuladen, hast du mehrere Optionen. Die Standardlösung ist das mitgelieferte USB-C-Kabel, das du mit einem der USB-Ports der Playstation 5 verbindest. So kannst du während des Ladens theoretisch weiterspielen, bist aber an die Kabellänge gebunden.
Auch deshalb lohnt sich eine separate Ladestation. Hier wird der Controller nicht über den USB-C-Port, sondern über die Metallkontakte an der Unterseite geladen. Das Click-in-Design funktioniert kinderleicht und lässt sich sogar mit einer Hand bedienen. Ladestationen bieten in der Regel Platz für zwei Controller gleichzeitig. Das ist ideal für den schnellen Wechsel, sodass du nahtlos weiterspielen kannst. Das Original von Sony und zertifizierte Drittanbieter bieten außerdem einen Überladungsschutz: Sie schalten den Strom automatisch ab, sobald der Akku voll ist. Das schont die Lebensdauer der Batterie.
So viel kostet eine Ladestation für deine PS5-Controller
Die gute Nachricht ist: Für eine Doppelladestation musst du nicht allzu tief in die Tasche greifen. Das Original von Sony ist bei Mediamarkt regulär für 34,99 Euro erhältlich. Aktuell ist es auf 26,99 Euro reduziert. Die weiße Dualsense-Ladestation lädt deine kabellosen Controller ebenso schnell wie eine direkte Verbindung mit der Playstation 5. So schonst du die Anschlüsse, ohne Leistung einzubüßen. Das vollständige Aufladen eines Controllers dauert typischerweise etwa zwei bis drei Stunden. Die Station verfügt über Gummifüße und ausreichend Gewicht, sodass sie nicht direkt abhebt, wenn du einen Controller herausnimmst.
Power A bietet eine Alternative, die preislich sogar noch attraktiver ist. Die offiziell für die Playstation 5 lizenzierte Ladestation hat ebenfalls zwei Steckplätze zum gleichzeitigen Aufladen von zwei kabellosen Controllern. Das Prinzip funktioniert wie beim Original: Du klickst den Controller nach unten ein, sodass die LED-Basis aufleuchtet und den Ladezustand anzeigt. Nach dem Aufladen klickst du erneut nach unten, um den Kontakt freizugeben und das Spiel zu starten. Käufer:innen schätzen die einfache Bedienung und die gute Passgenauigkeit. Die schwarz-weiße Ladestation ist bei Amazon schon für 19,99 Euro erhältlich.
Neben den beiden genannten Ladestationen gibt es zahlreiche weitere Modelle mit ähnlichem Design und Funktionen. Die Kosten starten hier bei etwa 15 Euro. Um Schäden am Controller zu vermeiden, lohnt es sich allerdings, direkt in die Original-Ladestation von Sony oder eine lizenzierte Alternative zu investieren – zumal die Preisunterschiede nicht groß sind. Die offiziell von Sony beworbenen Ladestationen schützen die empfindlichen Ladekontakte am besten und bieten ein intelligentes Lademanagement. Bei einem Blockbuster wie GTA 6 bist du damit ideal ausgestattet und kannst nahtlos weiterzocken, wenn ein Controller schlappmacht.

articles.title: Tesla Roadster : prix, versions, date de sortie… tout savoir sur la voiture volante d'Elon Musk
articles.text:
Neuf ans après sa première apparition, le Tesla Roadster a fait un retour très remarqué avec des propulseurs hérités de SpaceX et une version capable de décoller. Trois déclinaisons, une quatrième plus abordable qui pourrait débarquer, 50 000 euros pour réserver et une production prévue en 2028 : voici ce que l’on sait vraiment de la voiture.
Qu’a montré Tesla lors de la présentation ?
Tesla a dévoilé son Roadster dans la nuit du 15 au 16 octobre 2026, sur le site d’essais de moteurs de SpaceX à McGregor, au Texas. Devant les caméras, la voiture d’Elon Musk a fait le show et a animé les réseaux sociaux en sautant en vrille au-dessus d’une partie de la gamme Tesla, de la Model 3 au camion Semi en passant par le Cybertruck et le Cybercab.
L’autre temps fort a été l’accélération et, propulseurs allumés, le Roadster a affiché un 0 à 96 km/h en 0,81 seconde. Notons quand même que ce chrono a été mesuré par Tesla, sur son terrain et avec sa propre voiture, sans contrôle indépendant. « Le futur a bien des voitures volantes », a ensuite résumé Elon Musk sur X, tout en reconnaissant sur scène que ce n’était « pas forcément une voiture optimisée pour la sécurité ».
Quelles sont les différentes versions du Roadster ?
Tesla propose pour l’instant trois versions. La Performance, présentée comme « prête pour la route », compte deux places et se contente d’une aérodynamique active et d’un système d’aspiration, avec un 0 à 96 km/h annoncé en moins de 1,6 seconde. La Thrust, produite en série limitée, ajoute des propulseurs à l’arrière et descend sous les 0,9 seconde. La Rocket, enfin, sacrifie le siège passager, reçoit des propulseurs tout autour de la caisse et vise moins de 0,59 seconde, avec une vitesse de pointe de plus de 370 km/h. C’est elle qui peut réellement décoller du sol et Tesla précise qu’elle n’est « pas approuvée pour une utilisation sur la voie publique ». Elle est par ailleurs réservée à des clients invités.
Une quatrième version, plus abordable, devrait rejoindre la gamme. Selon Top Gear, ce Roadster « Standard » développerait environ 800 kW, contre plus de 1 MW pour la Performance, et se passerait du système d’aspiration de sa grande sœur. Encore en développement selon Lars Moravy, il n’a pour l’instant ni prix ni date de sortie.
Certaines caractéristiques sont communes à toute la gamme, à commencer par l’autonomie de plus de 480 km annonhcée par Tesla, qui ne précise pas le cycle d’homologation. Le reste vient des interviews données par Lars Moravy, vice-président de l’ingénierie véhicule, à Top Gear et Hagerty. Le Roadster serait une propulsion à deux moteurs arrière, développant plus de 1 MW (environ 1 360 ch) et plus de 1 400 Nm, chaque roue arrière étant pilotée indépendamment. Sa batterie utiliserait des cellules cylindriques à la chimie lithium-ion au nickel conçue sur mesure, sans que Tesla en communique la capacité, et pourrait se recharger de 15 à 85 % en une dizaine de minutes sur les Superchargeurs V4. La voiture pèserait moins de 1 700 kg. La direction, sans lien mécanique avec les roues, est commandée par un volant de type « yoke ».
Comment fonctionnent ses propulseurs et son système d’aspiration ?
Pour tenir à l’envers sur sa rampe, la Performance mise sur un système d’aspiration. Selon Lars Moravy, quatre ventilateurs placés à l’arrière travaillent avec des jupes déployables sous la batterie pour plaquer la voiture au sol, même à l’arrêt. De quoi offrir plus de 2 g d’adhérence en virage, avant même que l’aérodynamique n’entre en jeu. Passé 80 à 100 km/h environ, les jupes se relèveraient pour laisser place à un effet Venturi sous le plancher, puis l’aileron actif, dont un brevet détaillait déjà le fonctionnement, prendrait le relais. Au-delà de 320 km/h, l’appui atteindrait ainsi deux fois le poids de la voiture.
 Real life, baby https://t.co/3QEqn18wig
— Tesla (@Tesla) October 16, 2026
Les versions Thrust et Rocket vont plus loin avec des propulseurs à gaz froid empruntés à SpaceX. Ici, aucun carburant n’est brûlé : le système expulse simplement un gaz stocké à très haute pression, jusqu’à 10 000 psi (environ 690 bar), dans des réservoirs en fibre de carbone. Tesla a parlé d’air pendant sa présentation, alors que Lars Moravy évoque plutôt de l’azote. La Thrust disposerait d’un réservoir de 200 litres logé dans le coffre et de quatre buses à l’arrière, dont deux orientables pour garder la voiture en ligne droite, pour une poussée de plus de 80 kN, soit à peu près celle d’un avion de chasse. La Rocket, elle, remplacerait le siège passager par un second réservoir de 400 litres, soit 600 litres au total, et ajouterait six buses : une au niveau de chaque roue pour soulever la voiture et deux à l’avant pour contrôler sa rotation. Sa poussée dépasserait elle aussi 80 kN, et pourrait atteindre 90 kN selon Lars Moravy.
Comment la Rocket peut-elle voler ?
« Donc oui, il peut voler », assure Tesla sur la page française du Roadster. Le terme mérite pourtant d’être nuancé, puisque la Rocket ne dispose ni d’ailes ni de rotor et ne vole donc pas comme un avion ou un hélicoptère. Elle se soulève uniquement grâce à la poussée de ses propulseurs, à la manière d’une fusée. Les quatre buses placées au niveau des roues dirigeraient le gaz vers le bas pour la décoller du sol, tandis que les deux buses avant serviraient à contrôler sa rotation. Lors de la démonstration, ces propulseurs ont permis de remettre la voiture à l’endroit en bout de rampe, d’amortir sa réception puis de la faire sauter en vrille au-dessus des autres Tesla. Ses capacités se limiteraient toutefois à des sauts et à de brèves lévitations, bien loin d’un vol au-dessus des embouteillages.
Ce spectacle a d’ailleurs ses limites, puisqu’un plein ne permettrait qu’environ cinq secondes de poussée, de quoi accompagner un départ arrêté sur environ 400 mètres. Il faut ensuite s’armer de patience, car le remplissage prendrait aujourd’hui de 2 à 6 heures, et même 6 à 7 heures pour les 600 litres de la Rocket. Tesla travaillerait sur un nouveau système pour ramener ce délai à une demi-heure environ.
Combien coûte le Tesla Roadster ?
Pour l’instant, Tesla n’a annoncé aucun prix de vente et se contente de prendre des réservations. En France, la Performance demande de verser 5 000 euros par carte bancaire, présentés comme entièrement remboursables, puis 45 000 euros sous 10 jours, sans quoi la réservation peut être annulée. Pour la Thrust, sa disponibilité est « limitée » et si la réservation reste figée à 5 000 euros, le montant dû dans les 10 jours grimpe à 250 000 euros. Enfin, la Rocket est accessible uniquement sur invitation et n’affiche aucun montant.
Notez que ces sommes ne garantissent pas la livraison d’une voiture dont on ne connaît toujours pas le tarif final. Pour se faire une idée, Tesla annonçait en 2017 la version de base à 200 000 dollars, et la série « Founders », limitée à 1 000 exemplaires, à 250 000 dollars payés d’avance.
Quand sortira-t-il ?
Elon Musk annonce une production en 2028, et Tesla disposerait aujourd’hui, selon Lars Moravy, de quatre ou cinq prototypes, avant d’assembler une série plus importante début 2027. Après neuf ans de reports, mieux vaut toutefois rester prudent avec les prévisions de l’homme le plus riche du monde.
En attendant, rappelons que le premier Roadster de Tesla a été produit à 2 680 exemplaires entre 2008 et 2012. Son successeur avait été présenté en novembre 2017 avec des promesses alléchantes et une sortie prévue en 2020. Si le constructeur a pris son temps, il n’a pas manqué de faire parler de lui en envoyant un Roadster de première génération dans l’espace, à bord d’une fusée Falcon Heavy. Quelques mois plus tard, Elon Musk promettait une option « SpaceX » à propulseurs. La production a ensuite été repoussée d’année en année, puis la présentation elle-même a été décalée à plusieurs reprises en 2026, la dernière fois à cause de la météo.
Le projet semble aussi peser assez peu dans la stratégie de Tesla. Lors de la présentation des résultats du troisième trimestre, le 21 octobre, Elon Musk a bien qualifié la démonstration de « sans doute la plus cool de tous les temps », sans que le sujet suscite l’intérêt des investisseurs, bien plus tournés vers la conduite autonome, le Cybercab et le robot Optimus.
Pourra-t-il rouler en France ?
Aucune version n’a pour l’instant le droit d’y circuler, puisque Tesla n’a annoncé aucune démarche d’homologation en Europe. Cette étape est indispensable pour obtenir une carte grise et le modèle Performance, le plus classique des trois, est celui qui a le plus de chances d’arriver un jour sur nos routes. Pour cela, il pourrait éventuellement bénéficier d’une homologation allégée prévue pour les petites séries. La Thrust, que Tesla présente comme « prête pour la course », semble plutôt destinée aux circuits, faute de règles adaptées à ses propulseurs. Quant à la Rocket, elle soulève une question inédite, que nous avons détaillée dans un article consacré à l’homologation du Roadster : relève-t-elle du droit routier ou du droit aérien ?
Aux États-Unis, l’aviation civile a déjà tranché en indiquant à CBS News que « le véhicule de Tesla ne répond pas à la définition d’un aéronef de la FAA ». De son côté, l’autorité de sécurité routière, la NHTSA, a rappelé que le constructeur devait respecter les normes fédérales. En Europe, aucune autorité ne s’est encore prononcée.

articles.title: VW vai trazer tecnologia chinesa para novos carros na América do Sul
articles.text:
A Volkswagen vai levar tecnologias desenvolvidas na China para mercados internacionais, incluindo a América do Sul e a África do Sul. A montadora alemã quer transformar sua operação chinesa em um centro de desenvolvimento e exportação para ampliar a competitividade global e reduzir custos.
A expansão começará pela América do Sul até o fim da década, com uma nova plataforma e uma arquitetura eletrônica desenvolvidas em parceria com empresas chinesas.
Nova plataforma para o Sul Global
A próxima geração de veículos da Volkswagen destinada a mercados emergentes usará a Compact Main Platform e a China Electronic Architecture, desenvolvidas pelo centro de pesquisa da montadora em Hefei, no leste da China.
A mudança amplia a estratégia anterior da empresa, chamada “Na China, para a China”, que priorizava produtos voltados ao público chinês. Agora, a tecnologia desenvolvida no país asiático também será aproveitada em outros mercados.
“A China é um motor de inovação essencial para o Grupo Volkswagen e, cada vez mais, um centro de produtos e tecnologia para nossos mercados globais”, afirmou Oliver Blume, CEO do grupo.
A decisão ocorre enquanto a montadora tenta recuperar espaço na China. Fabricantes locais, como BYD e Geely, avançaram nos segmentos de veículos elétricos, software automotivo e modelos com preços competitivos. A Volkswagen também busca transformar parcerias com empresas como Xpeng e Horizon Robotics em resultados comerciais mais expressivos.
Segundo a empresa, seu modelo de desenvolvimento local pode reduzir em até 30% o tempo necessário para criar novos produtos.
VEGA terá recarga rápida e condução autônoma
A América do Sul foi escolhida como primeiro destino internacional da nova arquitetura por ser um mercado sensível a preços, no qual as fabricantes chinesas já conquistaram espaço. A Volkswagen também planeja ampliar as exportações de carros das marcas Volkswagen e Jetta fabricados na China para a América do Sul e a África nos próximos anos.
Outra novidade é o VEGA, pacote tecnológico previsto para 2027. A solução reunirá recursos voltados à eletrificação e à condução automatizada.
Entre os destaques anunciados pela montadora estão:
- Recarga de 850 volts: tecnologia voltada ao carregamento rápido de veículos elétricos.
- Condução autônoma de nível 3: preparação para sistemas capazes de assumir determinadas tarefas de direção.
- Aplicação em diferentes veículos: a arquitetura eletrônica foi projetada para funcionar com diversas plataformas e sistemas de propulsão.
A expansão também poderá alcançar o Sudeste Asiático e outros mercados africanos. Europa e América do Norte, por enquanto, estão fora dos planos para a adoção da arquitetura chinesa.
Frank Han, chefe da unidade de software CARIAD China, afirmou que a aplicação da tecnologia na Europa seria tecnicamente viável, mas dependeria de uma decisão da sede alemã, que precisaria considerar fatores geopolíticos.
Pressão no mercado chinês
A estratégia acompanha uma mudança mais ampla na indústria automobilística. General Motors, Hyundai e Renault também procuram aproveitar tecnologias desenvolvidas na China para competir em outros países.
O cenário doméstico, porém, continua desafiador para a Volkswagen. Ralf Brandstätter, chefe da operação chinesa da empresa, prevê que o mercado de automóveis de passeio do país encolha 20% neste ano, o equivalente a cerca de 4,5 milhões de veículos.
Levar tecnologias chinesas para outros mercados é uma tentativa de aproveitar a capacidade de desenvolvimento instalada no país e responder à concorrência. O resultado dependerá da aceitação dos veículos pelos consumidores e da capacidade da Volkswagen de recuperar terreno na própria China.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Ford Fathom will be the cheapest American EV capable of powering a house | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ford announced two new EV chargers today that will allow its forthcoming Fathom pickup truck to serve as a battery capable of delivering power to the home or grid.
The new chargers promise to be about half the cost of Ford’s existing equivalent products, which could make the technology available to more households. Ford said the Fathom itself will start at $28,350.
The Fathom will be capable of delivering “over 10 kW” to a home, Ford said. That would allow the electric vehicle to substitute for a small standby generator. For most U.S. homes, it wouldn’t be enough to power everything, but it could keep a refrigerator and air conditioner operational for about half a day.
Such capability has been touted as an advantage EVs have over fossil fuel vehicles, but not many EVs come properly equipped, and the chargers required to make use of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) services tend to be costly.
Ford’s two devices offer similar but differing capabilities.
The Home Power Station device can help customers shave their utility bill by charging the Fathom when power prices are low and sending electricity back to the home when prices are high. The automaker says it will cost around $650, about 50% less than its first-generation bidirectional charger.
The other option, Home Backup Power, is a package that bundles the Home Power Station with a second device, the Home Backup Panel, to allow the Fathom to also power parts or all of a home when the power goes out. Ford says the package will cost around $2,100, about 60% less than its first-generation product.
None of those prices include installation, which for existing V2X chargers can run up to $10,000, depending on how much electrical work needs to be done to prepare the home. Ford did not announce any partnerships with installers, though a spokesperson told TechCrunch that Ford would release more details at a later date.
Which loads the Fathom can power will vary by household and the specifics of each installation. Things like air conditioners and refrigerators, for example, typically require a large surge of power to start up, after which point their load drops. So-called soft-start devices can help mitigate the surge, though they add cost to the installation.
Both chargers will allow Fathom customers to participate in virtual power plants (VPPs), which use software to control a fleet of distributed energy storage devices, such as EVs.
As strain on the grid grows due to AI data centers, utilities have been exploring whether VPPs can help alleviate congestion at the edges.
Fathom owners who enroll and keep their truck plugged in can sell electricity back to the grid, often at a premium. Ford did not say how much Fathom owners can stand to make, but the payouts can be upwards of $1,000 per year, depending on the grid’s needs and the level of participation.
Automakers, including Ford, have been diving deep into energy storage as demand for such services surges. The Fathom-powered VPP is Ford’s latest foray into the market, but it’s unlikely to be its last.

articles.title: Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator : -55 % sur cette trottinette électrique
articles.text:
Acer est surtout connu pour ses PC portables et sa gamme gaming Predator. Le constructeur taïwanais reprend ce nom sur ses trottinettes électriques. C’est un segment plutôt dominé par Segway-Ninebot et Xiaomi, mais avec l’ES Series 5 Advanced Predator, la marque vise les trajets urbains du quotidien. Acer annonce jusqu’à 60 km d’autonomie et une suspension arrière. Cet engin devient encore plus intéressant maintenant que son prix vient de passer sous la barre des 250 euros.
L’Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator, c’est quoi ?
- Une autonomie annoncée jusqu’à 60 km
- Un moteur puissant de 500 W, jusqu’à 833 W en pointe
- Une suspension arrière et un frein à disque à l’avant
Affichée à 552,99 euros, l’Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator chute à 249,99 euros sur la Fnac, soit 55 % de remise. L’offre est également disponible chez Darty.
Une trottinette simple et efficace
Sur le plan du design, l’Acer ES Series 5 Advanced Predator ressemble à la majorité des trottinettes du marché sans vraiment se démarquer. Elle opte pour un look sobre, avec quelques touches de bleu sur les câbles de frein et le contour des roues. Ces dernières affichent un diamètre de 10 pouces et adoptent des pneus pleins. Ils ne crèvent pas, mais ils transmettent davantage les vibrations des pavés. La suspension arrière compense en partie ce manque de confort.
Une fois dépliée, elle affiche des dimensions de 118 x 49 x 120 cm. Son système de pliage ramène sa hauteur à 55 cm, ce qui permet de la glisser facilement sous un bureau ou dans un coffre. En revanche, elle pèse 18,5 kg. Si vous devez la porter dans un escalier ou un métro, c’est un poids à prendre en compte. Elle est aussi certifiée IPX5, ce qui lui permet de supporter les projections d’eau sur une chaussée mouillée. Sachez aussi qu’elle accepte une charge maximale de 120 kg.
Un moteur de 500 W pour les trajets du quotidien
Le moteur est placé dans la roue arrière. Il délivre 500 W en continu et jusqu’à 833 W en pointe, avec une vitesse bridée à 25 km/h, comme l’impose la réglementation. Sur le papier, de quoi démarrer franchement au feu vert et grimper des côtes jusqu’à 22 %, selon Acer. Attendez-vous tout de même à une baisse de puissance…
Pour le freinage, elle associe un frein à disque à l’avant et un frein électronique à l’arrière. On trouve aussi un régulateur de vitesse, un feu stop et une connexion Bluetooth. Elle a aussi des clignotants, un phare avant à LED et se connecte à l’application d’Acer.
Enfin, l’autonomie annoncée est de 60 km, un chiffre qui variera selon votre poids, la route et la météo. Elle s’appuie sur une batterie de 36 V et 16 Ah, soit environ 576 Wh : sur le papier, de quoi enchaîner plusieurs allers-retours domicile-travail entre deux recharges. Comptez environ 6 heures pour une recharge complète.
Si vous souhaitez la comparer à d’autres modèles, notre guide des meilleures trottinettes électriques regroupe celles que nous recommandons.

articles.title: Smart Window adds new form filling and page watching features | The Mozilla Blog
articles.text:
Skip the busywork with Smart Window
The days might be getting shorter, but your to-do list is only getting longer. Whether you’re getting a head start on holiday shopping or planning your next career move, Smart Window’s newest features will help you keep up.
Firefox’s opt-in AI browsing experience can now use information from tabs you choose to help fill out forms. It can also watch web pages and notify you about specific changes you’ve asked it to track.
Let your open tabs fill in the blanks
Job applications ask for your work history; event registrations ask for a professional bio. If those details are already in your open tabs, Smart Window can now use pages you choose to suggest what to enter, saving you extra clicks and some Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V.
For example, Smart Window could use information from your online portfolio or professional profile to fill in your work history, or draw on those details to draft an answer to a question like “Tell me about a time when…” Firefox’s regular autofill still handles saved information such as your name and address, which can be entered directly into forms without relying on AI models.
To get started, click into a form field. If the form has at least four text fields that Smart Window can help fill, you’ll see “Fill from sources” appear in the dropdown, along with a recommended source page. Select “Fill from sources” to continue, or click the pencil icon to open “Edit sources” if you want to change or add tabs. Once you’ve chosen your sources, review the suggestions before filling out the form. You can edit the results before submitting; Smart Window won’t submit the form for you.
When you choose to use this feature, information from your selected source pages is shared with Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, the AI model used for detecting the fields and extracting relevant information from your selected tabs. Your model choice for Smart Window chat stays the same, and saved autofill values stay on your device. Learn more about how form filling works.
This feature currently supports text fields on web forms and does not save any generated form fill data. We’re exploring support for more field types, including dropdown menus, as well as PDF forms and ways to save and manage generated information for future forms.
Give your refresh button a break
A watched pot never boils, and refreshing a web page won’t make an update appear any sooner.
Smart Window can now watch a page for a specific update, whether that’s an item going on sale or a new job listing that includes a job title or company name that you’re following. Each task can follow up to five pages, so you can keep an eye on several stores or job boards at the same time.
Type “/watch” in the Smart Window chat to set up a task. Describe what you’re looking for, add the pages to watch, and choose whether Firefox should check for updates on a daily or weekly basis. Those checks run only while the browser is open.
When there’s a match, you’ll see an update through the Tasks button in the toolbar. With desktop notifications enabled, Firefox can also notify you directly; click the notification to open the watched pages. You can have up to 15 active tasks at a time, and you can edit, pause or delete tasks. Smart Window will automatically pause tasks after 60 days without a matching change. If 90 days pass without a change, it will stop checking altogether.
Page monitoring uses the Qwen AI model to identify changes that match what you’re looking for. Your model choice for Smart Window chat stays the same. Learn more about creating and managing tasks.
Try the latest additions
These two new features are available in the Smart Window beta on desktop, in English in the U.S. and Canada, and will roll out to additional markets in the coming months.
Try Smart Window and share your experience on Mozilla Connect. We’d love to hear how you’re using Smart Window to get things done and what you’d like it to help with next.

articles.title: Tailscale Rushes Patches After Uncoordinated Disclosure of ‘Tailworm’ Flaws
articles.text:
Tailscale is getting ready to ship a client update that addresses privilege escalation weaknesses in Tailscale SSH. Details of the bugs went public over the weekend.
Tailscale provides a mesh VPN service that uses the WireGuard protocol to connect an organization’s devices and services over a private, peer-to-peer network.
The Tailscale vulnerabilities, dubbed Tailworm, are described in a report from Cyberdione Labs. It lists 11 findings affecting version 1.104.2 of the Tailscale client and version 0.29.5 of headscale, an open source control server that organizations can host themselves.
Cyberdione Labs published the report before any patches were available, drawing criticism on social media, though the researchers argued that rapid awareness would speed up remediation.
Six of the findings are rated high severity, and four of them concern Tailscale SSH, which grants access based on device identity and network policy instead of passwords or keys.
According to the Tailworm report, Tailscale SSH performs some forwarding operations with root privileges, and the safeguards meant to restrict them can be bypassed.
An attacker who has compromised one device could exploit this against any server that device is permitted to reach over Tailscale SSH, as long as the access rule allows forwarding. In lab tests, this resulted in root access on target servers and the theft of keys that can be used to add rogue devices to the network.
That initial foothold could come from common methods such as phishing, a vulnerable web application or a malicious software package.
Researchers showed that these SSH flaws are wormable. Since no user credentials are involved, an automated attack chaining these bugs moved from machine to machine across every server the policy granted SSH access to, at under a second per hop and with no user interaction.
The report also describes flaws in an experimental app connector feature, the Serve feature, headscale and the client’s relay component that could be exploited to reach cloud metadata services and internal networks while bypassing access rules, expose a node’s administrative interface to remote peers, or cause denial-of-service (DoS) conditions.
Tailscale says fixes are close
Responding on Reddit, Tailscale VP of Engineering Mike Shaver said the company was already running its own investigation, with input from outside security specialists, when the report came in.
“Most of the issues we’ve identified so far concern what happens after someone has been authorized to connect, particularly how Unix privileges and SSH forwarding are handled. In some cases, a session may be able to do more than the configured local user should be allowed to do,” Shaver said.
“While it’s a serious concern, it isn’t the same as an unauthenticated attacker being able to connect to arbitrary machines, but the potential impact depends on how SSH access is configured,” he added.
In an update shared on Monday, Tailscale said fixes were in place for most of the issues and that it was aiming to release a patched client by the end of Tuesday, October 27, pending testing. A security advisory and a technical write-up will follow once the update is out.
The Tailworm report, updated on Tuesday, says fixes for several findings have landed in Tailscale’s public code repositories. None had made it into a numbered release at that point.
“Based on our current assessment, we’re not recommending that everyone disable Tailscale SSH,” the vendor said.
Until the patch arrives, Tailscale advises organizations to review their SSH access policies and disable SSH forwarding where it isn’t needed, which it says mitigates several of the more serious findings.
Neither Tailscale nor the Tailworm report mentions in-the-wild exploitation.
UPDATE: Tailscale has published its full findings, including details of the vulnerabilities, their impact, and the fixes it has rolled out. The company has also published four security bulletins with the specific findings and remediation guidance.
